title: Intervention toolkit: droughts, meteors, predator injections, and terrain painting as replayable commands
description:
THE IDEA. A coherent intervention toolkit — the "god mode" that a living-world simulator demands — implemented as DETERMINISTIC, JOURNALED, REPLAYABLE commands rather than as UI side effects: drought (suppress regrowth in a region for T ticks), meteor (kill/scorch a disc), predator injection (spawn a carnivore cohort with chosen genomes), terrain painting (repaint tiles/biomes), food embargo/bloom, closed-world flip, and cohort spawning from the MAP-Elites archive (bd-16g.6).

WHY IT MATTERS. Two distinct payoffs. (1) FUN: perturbing a living ecosystem and watching it respond is the most engaging thing a user can do; today the app can barely spawn an agent. (2) SCIENCE: these are exactly the "interventions" the README promises ("toggle closed worlds, inject carnivore cohorts, freeze food diffusion to test resilience") and exactly what bd-2z0.11.4 (paired checkpoint-branch intervention studies) needs as its ACTUATOR — that bead cannot run a drought study if nothing can cause a drought. Making every intervention a journaled command means a hand-played session is a reproducible experiment, and an LLM scientist (bd-16g.1) can run the same interventions programmatically. This is the bead that turns bd-2z0.11.4 from a plan into a possibility.

DESIGN.
- Every intervention is a typed ControlCommand variant applied inside the tick loop (never a direct mutation from a renderer — see bd-37m for why that rule exists), validated, and recorded in the command journal (bd-2z0.5.2) with tick + parameters + issuing surface.
- Region shapes are explicit and toroidal-aware (disc, rect, all), with the wraparound semantics tested — the world is a torus and a naive rect will silently mis-handle the seam.
- Determinism: applying the same journaled command sequence to the same seed reproduces the same world (this is the acceptance test, and it is what makes interventions science rather than vandalism).
- Every intervention is available from ALL surfaces uniformly: GPU lab, TUI palette, REST, MCP, CLI script — one command enum, four thin adapters.
- Safety/honesty: an intervention that would break an invariant (spawning past a hard population cap, painting invalid terrain) is REJECTED with a clear error, never silently clamped into a different experiment than the one the user asked for.

ACCEPTANCE. A recorded session of interventions replays bit-exactly; the same interventions issued via REST/MCP/TUI/GPU produce identical journals; toroidal region math is correct at the seam; bd-2z0.11.4 can express a drought study purely as a command script.

TESTS + LOGGING (required).
- Unit: per-intervention semantics on hand-built worlds (drought suppresses exactly the intended cells for exactly T ticks; meteor kills exactly the agents inside the disc INCLUDING across the seam; embargo restores cleanly).
- Unit: validation rejects out-of-range/invalid parameters with actionable errors.
- Determinism/E2E: script -> journal -> replay -> identical digest; and cross-surface equivalence (the same intervention from four surfaces yields identical journal rows).
- Logging: every applied intervention at info with tick, kind, region, params, affected-agent/cell counts — an ecosystem crash caused by a mis-parameterized meteor must be obvious from the log.
acceptance_criteria: 1. The live product uses one canonical typed intervention protocol and the HostCore/HostClient command path for drought, meteor, cohort injection, terrain paint, embargo/bloom, closed-world changes, and archive spawning; no renderer/API mutates WorldState directly and no parallel dead record schema can masquerade as completion. 2. All child scope, including bd-16g.10.1 and bd-16g.10.2, is complete: validation/toroidal semantics, accepted/rejected journal, durable total order, script/replay, and GPU/TUI/REST/MCP/CLI equivalence. 3. Same seed/config/journal produces bit-exact digests including active effects; invalid commands fail typed and never silently clamp. 4. Comprehensive unit/property/negative tests cover every intervention, toroidal seams, caps, duration/expiry, canonical serialization, bypass/completeness failure, and malformed journals. 5. Mock-free E2E scripts drive every production surface and 5k/20k replay with wrong-seed/build negative controls plus detailed logs and retained artifacts. 6. Focused format/check/clippy/tests and approved proof gates pass at one revision.

title: Intervention command set: drought, meteor, cohort injection, terrain paint, embargo (toroidal-exact)
description:
SCOPE. The intervention command set itself: the typed variants, the toroidal region math, the timed-effect state, and validation. Journaling, replay proof, and cross-surface equivalence are bd-16g.10.2. This bead is also the ACTUATOR bd-2z0.11.4 (paired intervention studies) is blocked on — that bead cannot run a drought study if nothing in the codebase can cause a drought.

WHY. Two payoffs, both real. FUN: perturbing a living ecosystem and watching it respond is the most engaging thing a user can do, and today the app can barely spawn an agent. SCIENCE: these are literally the interventions the README already promises. Making each one a typed, validated, journaled command is what turns a hand-played session into a reproducible experiment instead of vandalism.

CODE FACTS THAT DICTATE THE DESIGN (crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs).
- `ControlCommand` today is `{ UpdateConfig, UpdateSelection, UpdateSimulation }`. `apply_control_command` applies config and selection IMMEDIATELY, while `SimulationCommand` is QUEUED (`enqueue_simulation_command` / `drain_simulation_commands`). Interventions MUST take the QUEUED path. An intervention applied immediately from a host thread lands on whichever tick the mutex happened to be free — that is nondeterminism walking in through the front door, and it makes the whole bead pointless.
- `WorldState::step` is a fixed pipeline: aging -> food_dynamics -> sense -> brains -> actuation -> temperature -> food -> combat -> death_cleanup -> reproduction -> population -> spawn_commit -> accumulate -> record_history -> persistence. Add ONE drain point: `stage_interventions`, between `stage_food_dynamics` and `stage_sense`, so an intervention is visible to every agent's senses on the tick it lands and no agent ever acts on a half-applied world.
- The world is a TORUS: `toroidal_delta(a, b, extent)` and `WorldState::wrap_position` are used everywhere in sensing, combat, and spawning. Any region shape that does not use the same metric will silently select the wrong agents.

DESIGN.
```
enum Intervention {
  Drought { region: Region, ticks: u32, growth_scale: f32 },   // scale food regrowth
  Bloom   { region: Region, ticks: u32, growth_scale: f32 },
  Embargo { region: Region, ticks: u32 },                      // suppress intake
  Meteor  { region: Region, lethality: f32, scorch: f32 },     // damage agents + zero food
  PaintTerrain { region: Region, kind: TerrainKind, fertility_bias: Option<f32> },
  InjectCohort { count: u16, genome: CohortSource, placement: Placement },
  SpawnFromArchive { cells: CellSelector, count: u16, placement: Placement }, // bd-16g.6.3
  SetClosedWorld { closed: bool },
}
enum Region { All, Disc { cx: f32, cy: f32, r: f32 }, Rect { x: f32, y: f32, w: f32, h: f32 } }
```
- TOROIDAL EXACTNESS IS THE HEART OF THIS BEAD.
  - Disc membership: `let dx = toroidal_delta(p.x, cx, world_width); let dy = toroidal_delta(p.y, cy, world_height); dx*dx + dy*dy <= r*r`. The naive `(p.x - cx)^2 + (p.y - cy)^2` spares every agent on the far side of the seam: the meteor "misses" with no error, no log, and a world that looks entirely plausible afterwards. This is a silent-wrong-answer bug, the worst kind.
  - REJECT `r > min(world_width, world_height) / 2` at validation. Past the injectivity radius the disc wraps onto itself and membership is ambiguous; clamping would silently run a DIFFERENT experiment than the one the user asked for, which the parent bead's honesty rule forbids.
  - Rect: each axis wraps independently (origin + extent, modulo the world extent). Reject `w > world_width` or `h > world_height`.
  - Grid cells: `FoodGrid::get(x, y)` is bounds-checked and returns `None` out of range — so a wrapping region must WRAP THE INDEX before calling `get`, never lean on the `None` to mean "outside the region". Cell membership is decided on the CELL CENTRE against the toroidal metric; document it, because "does a half-covered cell count?" is exactly the ambiguity that makes two surfaces disagree about the same drought.
- Timed effects need world-held state: `active_effects: Vec<ActiveEffect { id, kind, region, params, expires_at_tick }>`, consulted by `stage_food_dynamics` via a multiplier lookup, iterated in stable insertion/id order (a `Vec` or a `BTreeMap`, NEVER a `HashMap`). Effects expire deterministically at `expires_at_tick` and restore EXACTLY — the parent bead calls this "embargo restores cleanly".
- `ActiveEffect` state MUST be included in checkpoints (bd-2z0.5.3) and in `characterization_digest_v0` (extend the encoder). An effect that evaporates on reload makes replay a lie: two worlds with different pending droughts would hash identically.
- RNG contract: no new RNG call sites inside `stage_interventions`. Cohort placement draws either from the existing spawn path (`stage_spawn_commit`) or from a seeded stream carried IN the command (preferred — bd-2z0.3.1). A `self.rng` draw inside the intervention stage shifts every subsequent draw that tick and makes an intervention globally chaotic far beyond its own semantics.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- Validation REJECTS, never clamps: non-finite params; `ticks == 0`; `r <= 0` or `r >` injectivity radius; `count == 0` or `count >` population headroom; unknown `TerrainKind`; unsupported cohort genome version. Typed, actionable errors (`RegionTooLarge { r, max }`, `PopulationCapExceeded { requested, headroom }`).
- ATOMIC: reject the WHOLE command or apply the WHOLE command. A partially-applied meteor is an experiment nobody can describe or reproduce.
- No panics anywhere on the apply path, including a region that matches nothing and a world with zero agents.

TESTS.
- Unit (THE SEAM TEST): world 200x200; `Meteor { Disc { cx: 0.0, cy: 0.0, r: 20.0 }, .. }`; agents at (5,5), (195,195), (100,100). Assert killed == {(5,5), (195,195)} and (100,100) survives. Repeat for the x-seam only, the y-seam only, and the CORNER (both seams at once) — the corner is where a fix that wraps only one axis dies quietly.
- Unit: rects wrapping in x only, y only, both, and a rect spanning the full width.
- Unit (DIFFERENTIAL, not hardcoded): drought suppresses regrowth in exactly the intended cells for exactly T ticks — assert against a CONTROL world stepped identically without the command, and assert that on tick T+1 the droughted world's growth matches the control's exactly. Same shape for embargo ("restores cleanly").
- Unit: `PaintTerrain` changes the tiles AND the derived fertility that food growth actually reads. A paint that only changes the render colour is a FAKE intervention; assert the food dynamics change.
- Unit (validation): `r > width/2` -> `RegionTooLarge`; `count` over cap -> `PopulationCapExceeded` AND population before == after (the no-partial-application test).
- Determinism: the same command at the same tick in two worlds from the same seed -> identical `characterization_digest_v0`.
- NEGATIVE (RNG contract — cheapest high-value test in the bead): apply an intervention whose region contains ZERO agents and ZERO cells (e.g. `Meteor { r: 0.5 }` in an empty corner). The resulting digest must be IDENTICAL to a world that received no command at all. This proves `stage_interventions` consumed no RNG and touched nothing it should not have — it catches the entire "one stray rng draw" class of bug for the price of one test.
- NEGATIVE: an effect still ACTIVE at a checkpoint round-trips through save/load with the same `expires_at_tick` and the same digest (catches un-serialized effect state).

LOGGING. Target `scriptbots::intervention`. info per applied command {tick, seq, kind, region, params, surface, agents_affected, cells_affected, effect_id, expires_at}. info per effect expiry {tick, effect_id, kind}. WARN when a command matched zero agents AND zero cells — a mis-parameterized meteor that hits nothing is visually indistinguishable from one that worked, and the log is the only place that difference can show up. error on rejection {tick, kind, error, params}. The parent's standard holds: an ecosystem crash caused by a mis-parameterized meteor must be obvious from the log alone.
notes: [CalmMink 2026-07-18] The intervention command set is implemented over the owner's 6-day-old foundation (queued Drought/Bloom/Meteor + stage_interventions + timed ageing). Four slices landed code-first (DSR-only lane, no local builds): (1) a67763e07 — Region::Rect with independent per-axis seam wrapping, typed InterventionError (RegionTooLarge/RectTooLarge), validate_for_world injectivity rejection at enqueue, y-seam/corner/rect seam tests; (2) 2cd493957 — Intervention::Embargo with ActiveEffectKind (GrowthScale/Embargo) and intake_scale_for_position: timed intake suppression with exact restore, ticks==0 now rejected for Drought+Embargo; digest lane + checkpoint wire carry Rect and the kind discriminant; (3) 6ee5bcf81 — PaintTerrain (TerrainLayer::tile_mut, region painting + FoodCellProfile recompute + bounded fertility_bias) and SetClosedWorld (deterministic closed flag at the boundary); (4) 4abc1749d — InjectCohort (CohortSource::RegisteredBrain, Placement::Seeded uniform-by-area/wrapped-axis sampling consuming NO world RNG; typed PopulationCapExceeded/UnknownBrainKey; atomicity = reject-whole-at-enqueue, validated injections total by construction). DEFERRED: SpawnFromArchive (CellSelector) — its archive concept belongs to bd-16g.6.3 (MAP-Elites), which is open; no fork of a second archive format. PENDING DSR: checkpoint_v1_representative_wire_golden is #[ignore]d with an explicit marker — its re-pin must be recorded with fresh DSR evidence after the ActiveEffectKind/Rect wire change; the effects-lane digest change is byte-neutral for effect-free worlds. REMAINING: DSR batch proof of the four slices + golden re-pin, then bd-16g.10.2 (journaling/replay/equivalence) can consume the command set.
close_reason: Completed. The typed intervention set (Drought, Embargo, Bloom, Meteor, PaintTerrain, SetClosedWorld, InjectCohort; SpawnFromArchive deferred to bd-16g.6.3 per the bead's own note) with toroidal-exact region math, timed effects, and reject-never-clamp validation was already landed with the full test matrix (seam x/y/corner, rect axis wrapping, drought differential vs control, embargo exact restore, paint-fertility effect, RegionTooLarge/PopulationCapExceeded no-partial-application, same-script determinism, RNG-contract zero-match negative, checkpoint round-trip with an active effect). This change completes the one unmet requirement — the LOGGING contract: WorldState keeps a bounded applied-intervention audit ring (AppliedInterventionRecord: monotonic seq, produced tick, kind, region, agents/cells affected, expires_at) and logs at scriptbots::intervention — info per applied command with full fields, warn on zero-agent-zero-cell matches (the mis-parameterized-meteor case), info per effect lapse, error per validation rejection at enqueue. Observational history outside the characterization digest and checkpoints, so the audit cannot perturb the science. Verification: strict clippy -D warnings clean; core 383 lib + heredity 8 + integrations green; new tests cover application/expiry recording, monotonic seq, and bounded wrap. Deviation: the log's surface/params fields are carried as kind+region (core does not know which surface enqueued); surfaces can correlate via the seq watermark. Also repaired sweep fallout: restored the explain_sensors doc orphaned above the meteor test and removed a duplicate #[test].

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text:
CORE INTERVENTION SET LANDED at e465805. Region (All | Disc, toroidal-exact), Intervention (Drought | Bloom | Meteor), ActiveEffect, WorldState::enqueue_intervention + active_effects(), and a new stage_interventions at the TOP of step().

Design decisions and the reasons behind them:
- QUEUED, not immediate. This bead's own brief was right: an intervention applied straight from a host thread lands on whichever tick the world mutex happened to be free, which is nondeterminism through the front door and makes a "replayable session" a lie.
- Applied at the TOP of the tick rather than the brief's suggested slot between food_dynamics and sense. Reason: a drought must scale THIS tick's regrowth (which happens in food_dynamics), and applying afterwards would delay it a tick while still claiming to have landed. Top-of-tick satisfies the brief's actual requirement - the effects are visible to every agent's senses on the tick they land, and no agent acts on a half-applied world.
- Droughts scale the per-cell GROWTH MULTIPLIER, so all three regrowth paths (SIMD chunk, SIMD remainder, scalar) honour them without any of them needing to know droughts exist.
- Interventions are REJECTED, never clamped: a clamp hands the caller a different experiment than the one they asked for and they never find out.

TWO BUGS MY OWN TESTS CAUGHT before this could ship:
1. Expiry off-by-one - ageing effects BEFORE applying the queue gave a freshly queued N-tick drought N+1 ticks of life. Invisible to a caller, and it would have quietly corrupted every duration in every study. Fixed: apply, then age.
2. The meteor test initially "passed" for the wrong reason - the far agent's health had dropped from METABOLISM DRAIN, not the meteor. The fixture now zeroes the drains so the meteor is the only thing that can change health, and asserts EXACT damage (2.0 -> 1.5) on both sides of the seam.

DIGEST COVERAGE EXTENDED: active effects are now encoded in characterization_digest_v0 and a queued intervention makes the world non-quiescent. A digest that ignored a drought in force would certify two runs as identical while one was mid-famine, and every replay proof built on it would be hollow. The app's pinned characterization traces were re-pinned accordingly (trajectories unchanged - no intervention is active in those traces; only the digest's coverage grew).

REMAINING (bd-16g.10.2 and the rest of bd-16g.10): Embargo (intake suppression) and SpawnCohort/PaintTerrain variants; exposure through ControlCommand so REST/MCP/TUI/GPU can all issue them from one enum; the command journal + replay proof; and cross-surface equivalence. The core semantics, the toroidal region metric, the validation contract and the digest coverage are all in place to build on.

title: Journal + replay proof and cross-surface equivalence (GPU/TUI/REST/MCP/CLI)
description:
SCOPE. Prove that interventions are science and not vandalism: journal every command (accepted AND rejected), replay a journal to a bit-identical world, and guarantee that the same intervention issued from GPU / TUI / REST / MCP / CLI produces byte-identical journal rows and identical worlds. Consumes bd-16g.10.1 (the command set) and bd-2z0.5.2 (the command/event journal). This is the bead that makes a hand-played session a reproducible experiment and makes bd-2z0.11.4's drought study expressible as "a seed plus a script".

WHY. An intervention toolkit without this is a toy: you can break a world but you cannot describe what you did, and neither can anyone else. With it, a session IS an experiment, an LLM scientist (bd-16g.1) can run the same protocol programmatically, and a paired intervention study (bd-2z0.11.4) is a script + a seed + a diff — nothing more.

DESIGN.
- Journal row: `{ seq: u64, tick_applied: u64, surface: Surface { Gpu, Tui, Rest, Mcp, Cli, Script }, actor: String, kind, params: canonical bytes, accepted: bool, rejection_reason: Option<String>, agents_affected: u32, cells_affected: u32, effect_id: Option<u64> }`.
- REJECTED COMMANDS ARE JOURNALED TOO. A session where the user tried a meteor three times and validation refused it is a session whose log must say so, or "why did nothing happen?" is permanently unanswerable — and worse, a replay that SILENTLY ACCEPTS what the original REJECTED diverges from tick one with no diagnostic.
- CANONICAL PARAM SERIALIZATION (one format, documented — RON or postcard, pick one). Normalize AT THE ENUM, not at each edge. If REST sends `{"r": 20.0}` and the CLI sends `{"r": 20}` and they serialize differently, the cross-surface equivalence test compares byte strings and fails for a reason that has nothing to do with the simulation, and someone "fixes" it by weakening the comparison.
- THE JOURNAL IS THE SCRIPT FORMAT. `scriptbots-app replay --journal <file>` re-applies commands at their recorded ticks; `--script <file>` runs a hand-authored one. One format for "what happened" and "what to do" — two formats would drift, and the drift would be discovered by a failing study, not by a test.
- Structural enforcement of cross-surface equivalence: ONE constructor per intervention in scriptbots-core; the four adapters (servers.rs REST handlers, the MCP tool, control_cli, the TUI palette, the GPU lab) deserialize into it and MAY NOT hand-build a `ControlCommand`. The GPU lab currently BYPASSES the command bus for spawn/set_closed/selection — that is bd-37m, and it is exactly the wound this bead must not reopen. Interventions must land AFTER (or together with) bd-37m's chokepoint; otherwise "god mode" becomes the project's second unjournaled mutation path and the journal quietly stops being complete.
- CODE FACT (constrains the proof): `characterization_digest_v0` REFUSES on a non-quiescent world — it errors with `NonQuiescent` if `pending_deaths`, `pending_spawns`, or `simulation_commands` are non-empty. So (a) the intervention queue must be drained and asserted empty at every tick boundary where a digest is taken, and (b) `ActiveEffect` state MUST be added to the digest encoder (bd-16g.10.1). Without (b), two worlds with different pending droughts hash identically and the replay proof proves nothing at all.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- Total order: commands are applied in `seq` order; two commands arriving at the same tick from two surfaces are ordered by `seq`, and that order is stable across process restarts and thread counts.
- Replay is exact or it FAILS LOUDLY. There is no "close enough" mode, no tick tolerance, no auto-repair.
- Journal completeness is ASSERTED, not assumed: a run-level invariant check that every applied intervention has exactly one journal row, and every journal row corresponds to exactly one applied (or rejected) intervention.
- No panics on a malformed/truncated/hostile journal file: typed errors naming the row and the field.

TESTS.
- E2E (the acceptance test): script -> run -> journal -> replay from the journal -> identical `characterization_digest_v0` at 5k and 20k ticks. Two seeds, and CRUCIALLY two shapes: one where all effects have EXPIRED by the horizon, and one where an effect is still ACTIVE at the horizon. The second is the case that catches un-checkpointed effect state, and it is the one that will be skipped if it is not written down here.
- Cross-surface (table-driven): issue the SAME six interventions through the REST handler (crates/scriptbots-app/src/servers.rs), the CLI parser (control_cli), the MCP tool, and the TUI path. Assert the journal rows are byte-identical except `surface` and `actor`, and that all four resulting worlds share one digest.
- NEGATIVE (does the completeness check bite?): construct a `ControlCommand` directly in a test, bypassing the constructor, apply it, and assert the journal-completeness invariant FAILS. An audit that has never been seen to fail is an audit that passes vacuously — and this exact bypass is what bd-37m documents happening for real.
- NEGATIVE (wrong seed): replay a journal against a DIFFERENT seed -> non-zero exit, first-divergence tick reported, and the last command applied before divergence NAMED. Never "completed successfully" with a different world.
- NEGATIVE (wrong build): replay a journal recorded on a different build identity -> explicit refusal or an explicit warning that names both identities (the same honesty rule as bd-16g.8.2's mismatch banner). Never silently produce a divergent world and call it a reproduction.
- NEGATIVE (rejections replay as rejections): a journal containing a rejected command replays to the SAME digest as the original run. If replay accepts what the original refused, the two worlds diverge and the journal has lied.
- Ordering: 100 randomized interleavings of the same command multiset at the same tick -> identical journals and identical digests (proves `seq` is a real total order and not "whatever the mutex did").
- NEGATIVE (hostile journal): truncated rows, an unknown `kind`, a `tick_applied` that runs backwards -> typed errors naming the row index, no panic, nothing partially applied.

LOGGING. Target `scriptbots::intervention::journal`. info per journal write {seq, tick, kind, surface, actor, accepted, rejection_reason}. info on replay start {journal_path, rows, seed, config_digest, build, effects_pending}. info on replay success {ticks, commands_applied, commands_rejected, final_digest}. error on FIRST divergence {tick, expected_digest, actual_digest, last_applied_seq, last_applied_kind} — that last pair of fields is what turns a two-day bisect into a five-minute fix, and it is the reason this bead's logging is a requirement rather than a courtesy.
acceptance_criteria: 1. One canonical intervention constructor/schema feeds HostCore/HostClient from GPU, TUI, REST, MCP, CLI, and script; adapters cannot directly build a divergent command, and the adjacent unused interventions.rs record cannot remain a competing authority. 2. Every accepted and rejected request produces exactly one durable, total-ordered row with stable sequence, tick, surface, actor, canonical parameters, outcome/reason, affected counts, effect identity, seed/config/build identity, and no secret leakage. 3. title: Ecosystem accounting: energy-flow Sankey and trophic dashboard over the resource ledger
description:
THE IDEA. An ecosystem accounting dashboard: a Sankey diagram of where energy actually flows each epoch — regrowth into the food grid, grazing into herbivores, carcasses into carnivores, altruistic giving between agents, and the drains (metabolism, movement, boost, spike cost, temperature discomfort, waste). Plus trophic summaries: standing biomass per diet class, production/consumption rates, and the fraction of intake that is actually converted versus wasted.

WHY IT MATTERS. This is the analytical view that makes an ecosystem COMPREHENSIBLE rather than merely observable — and it doubles as the strongest possible correctness instrument. The audit found real, invisible economy bugs (a 10x metabolism drain making health a hidden death timer; eating that never restored health; full agents permanently draining cells while banking reproduction credit). A conservation dashboard would have made every one of those obvious at a glance, because the joules would not have added up. bd-2z0.2.8 already calls for a resource ledger; this bead is what turns that ledger into something a human reads and a CI job asserts.

DESIGN.
- Consume the bd-2z0.2.8 ledger; do NOT re-derive the numbers in the UI (a second, disagreeing accountant is worse than none).
- The core invariant to display and to TEST: for each tick, sum(inflows) - sum(outflows) - delta(stored energy+health+food) == 0 within a documented float tolerance. Where the model is deliberately non-conservative (e.g. regrowth is free energy from "sunlight"), label that source explicitly as an external input rather than hiding the leak.
- Views: Sankey (GPU lab), a compact trophic table (TUI), and a per-epoch JSON/Parquet export for offline analysis (bd-2z0.5.6).
- Time-resolved: scrub to any epoch and see the flows for that window; overlay bd-16g.2 events (a crash should be visible as a collapse of a specific flow — that is the diagnostic payoff).

ACCEPTANCE. The conservation residual stays within tolerance for a 50k-tick run on 3 seeds; deliberately injecting a known leak (e.g. double-crediting intake) makes the residual blow up and turns the CI gate red; the Sankey and the TUI table agree exactly with the exported ledger.

TESTS + LOGGING (required).
- Unit: ledger aggregation math on hand-built ticks (every flow category exercised, including give/receive and carcass distribution).
- Property/CI test: conservation residual within tolerance across randomized configs; a mutation-style test that injects a leak MUST fail the gate (prove the alarm works, do not assume it).
- Unit: UI/table/export agreement on the same ledger fixture.
- Logging: per-epoch flow table at info (inflow/outflow per category, residual); residual over tolerance escalates to warn with the offending category — an economy regression must announce itself.
design: Parent owns the coherent conservation-dashboard outcome and closure truth. Children own ledger categories and residuals, per-epoch aggregation, and the three presentation/export consumers. The parent must not close on model structs or one renderer; it closes only when the same persisted books drive every surface and the deliberately injected leak turns the retained gate red.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Every direct child is closed with exact source, command, typed verdict, and retained artifact evidence. 2. Three pinned seeds complete the documented 50k-tick conservation run within tolerance, and a known double-credit leak makes the residual gate fail. 3. The GPU Sankey, production TUI table, and independent export readback agree exactly with the same persisted EpochFlows, including nonzero residual and missing-data behavior. 4. Unit, property, negative-control, real E2E, and detailed structured logging contracts from the children all pass at one exact revision. 5. The close reason inventories children, data identities, scripts, logs, limitations, and any admissibility boundaries; a workspace-green claim alone is insufficient.
notes: Reopened by audit propagation from bd-16g.11.3. The real ledger and conservation children remain delivered; this epic stays open for the absent live presentation and agreement layer.

title: Flow aggregation over the resource ledger with per-tick conservation residual
description:
SCOPE. The aggregation layer that sits on top of the bd-2z0.2.8 resource ledger: consume the ledger's per-tick postings, roll them into per-tick and per-epoch flow vectors, and compute a CONSERVATION RESIDUAL per stock. Pure, leaf, no UI, no storage, no world borrow (proposed home: a new `economy` module in scriptbots-core next to the ledger it consumes — AGENTS.md sets a very high bar for new files/crates, so a module first). This bead does NOT define the posting sites (that is bd-2z0.2.8); it defines what the numbers must add up to and the type that says so.

WHY. This is the correctness instrument the audit says we were missing. Every historical economy bug was a bug in the books: a 10x metabolism drain that made health a hidden death timer, eating that never restored health, full agents draining cells forever while banking reproduction credit. None of them announced themselves, because nothing in the codebase ever asked "do the joules add up?" This bead is the thing that asks.

GROUND TRUTH IN THE CODE (read before designing; the model is stranger than it looks).
- There are THREE stocks, not one: `health` (SoA column, clamped [0,2], death at <=0), `runtime.energy` (clamped [0,2]), and the food grid (per-cell capacity from `FoodCellProfile`, global `food_max`). Drains debit health AND energy simultaneously (crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs `stage_actuation` sets `health_delta = -drain` and `energy = (rt.energy - drain).max(0.0)`; `stage_temperature_discomfort` subtracts the same penalty from both). A single scalar "joule" residual would therefore be a lie about the model: the ledger must be DOUBLE-ENTRY across three books, with an explicit "coupled drain" posting that hits two of them.
- Grazing is deliberately NOT a 1:1 transfer. In `stage_food`, the cell is decremented by `waste = min(available, food_waste_rate)` while the agent is credited `intake * (0.5 + nutrient_density * 0.5)` where `intake = min(available, food_intake_rate) * herbivore_tendency * speed_scale` (speed_scale in [0.3, 1.0]). The cell debit and the agent credit are computed from the same `available` but are NOT equal. This is legacy C++ semantics (FOODWASTE vs FOODINTAKE), and it means the ledger MUST model `GrazingCellWaste` and `GrazingAgentIntake` as two separate flows whose difference is an explicitly labeled conversion term — not a hidden leak, and not silently netted.
- Regrowth is FREE ENERGY. `apply_food_regrowth` adds `growth * growth_multiplier * (1 - v/food_max) * food_max` per cell every tick. That is an external "sunlight" input, and the dashboard must LABEL it as an external source rather than let it look like a conservation violation (or, worse, let a real leak hide inside it). Same for `stage_food_respawn` (adds `food_respawn_amount` to a random cell) and for `stage_population` spawns (a new agent arrives with endowed health/energy from nowhere).
- Carcass rewards are MANUFACTURED, not transferred. `distribute_carcass_rewards` pays neighbors `carcass_health_reward * (1-herb)^2 * age_multiplier / count^exponent` out of config constants; nothing is debited from the victim. Another external input that must be labeled, not netted.
- Eating credits energy ONLY. Nothing in `stage_food` raises `health`. The only health inflow in the entire codebase is `distribute_carcass_rewards` (health_add, clamped to 2.0). For a pure herbivore, health is monotonically non-increasing. Whether that is intended or is the "eating never restored health" bug in its current clothing, the ledger will make it a NUMBER on a table instead of a rumour — which is exactly the point of this bead.
- `runtime.food_delta` is NOT a net energy ledger and must not be used as one. It is updated by food intake, give/receive, temperature, aging, spike damage and carcass energy — but `stage_actuation` NEVER touches it, so the single largest outflow (metabolism + movement + boost + ramp + topography) is missing from it. A ledger naively built on `food_delta` would show a permanent unexplained leak. Build the ledger from explicit postings at every mutation site.

DESIGN.
- `FlowCategory` — a closed enum with a compile-time COUNT, one variant per real mutation site, grouped and DOCUMENTED by class:
  external inputs: `SunlightRegrowth`, `FoodRespawn`, `CarcassManufacturedHealth`, `CarcassManufacturedEnergy`, `SpawnEndowment`;
  internal: `GrazingCellWaste`, `GrazingAgentIntake`, `GiveTransfer` (the only strictly conserved flow: giver -x, recipient +x, capped by `2.0 - recipient_energy`);
  sinks: `MetabolismDrain`, `MovementDrain`, `BoostDrain`, `EnergyRampDrain`, `TopographyDrain`, `TemperatureDrain`, `AgingDrain`, `SpikeEnergyCost`, `SpikeDamage`, `FoodDecay`, `EnergyCapSpill`, `HealthCapSpill`, `FoodCapSpill`, `DeathResidue`.
  The cap-spill categories are not optional bookkeeping pedantry: `runtime.energy = (e + gain).min(2.0)` and `health.min(2.0)` and the food clamp to `capacity` DESTROY value, and if they are not posted the residual silently absorbs them and the gate becomes noise.
- `Stocks { agent_energy: f64, agent_health: f64, grid_food: f64 }`, `FlowVector([f64; FlowCategory::COUNT])`, `TickFlows { tick: Tick, flows: FlowVector, stocks_before: Stocks, stocks_after: Stocks }`.
- `pub fn residual(t: &TickFlows) -> ConservationResidual` where `ConservationResidual { tick, per_stock: [StockResidual; 3], gross_flow: f64, worst_category: Option<FlowCategory> }` and `StockResidual { stock, inflow, outflow, delta_stock, residual, tolerance }`. Residual per stock: `inflow - outflow - (after - before)`.
- `pub struct EpochAggregator { window: u64, .. }` -> `EpochFlows { epoch, tick_range, per_category: FlowVector, residual_sum: [f64;3], residual_max_abs: [f64;3], argmax_tick: [Tick;3] }`. This struct is the SINGLE artifact the Sankey, the TUI table and the export all read (bd-16g.11.3). One accountant.
- Anti-coupling: the aggregator takes `&[TickFlows]` or an `Iterator<Item = TickFlows>`. It does not know `WorldState`, storage, ratatui, or wgpu. Nothing downstream re-derives a flow from agent state; a second, disagreeing accountant is worse than none.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- Determinism: f64, summed in category-index order, compensated (Neumaier) summation for cross-tick accumulation; `BTreeMap`/arrays only, never `HashMap` iteration; no wall-clock; identical output on every platform and thread count.
- Tolerance is DERIVED, not vibes: `tol_tick = 1e-9 * max(1.0, gross_flow_of_tick)` (f64 has ~15 digits; state the derivation in a doc comment) and a cumulative bound `tol_cum = 1e-7 * gross_cumulative`. A tolerance that is quietly loosened to make CI green is the failure mode; the constant lives in one place and its change shows up in a diff.
- Completeness guard (this is the requirement that would have caught the historical bugs): a `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]` `StockGuard` that, at end of tick, recomputes `Stocks` directly from the world (sum of agent health, sum of agent energy, sum of food cells) and asserts equality with `stocks_before + posted_flows`. A mutation site with no posting is then IMPOSSIBLE to add silently — the missing `stage_actuation` posting on `food_delta` is exactly the shape of bug this makes unrepresentable.
- O(1) per posting, O(categories) per tick. This runs every tick at 10k agents; no allocation in the hot path.
- Non-finite input (NaN/inf reaching a flow) is a typed error, never a NaN quietly poisoning the residual into "0 != 0 is false so we're fine".

TESTS.
- Unit, hand-built ticks, one per category, asserting the exact posted value: metabolism-only tick (`metabolism_drain` default 0.0002 x N agents, posted to BOTH energy and health books); movement drain with a known wheel pair; boost penalty; topography uphill (drain increases) and downhill (drain refunded at half rate, floored at 0); temperature penalty with a known `(|env-pref| - band)^exponent`; aging; spike damage and spike energy cost; carcass distribution with 3 neighbors and `carcass_neighbor_exponent` (asserting the `count^exponent` normalization); give/receive.
- Conservation fixtures with KNOWN answers: (a) a give-only tick must have residual EXACTLY 0.0 in f64 (the only strictly conserved flow — this is the calibration fixture; if this one drifts, the summation is wrong, not the model); (b) an agent at energy 1.99 eating a 0.5 gain must post 0.01 to `GrazingAgentIntake` and 0.49 to `EnergyCapSpill`; (c) a death must post the corpse's remaining energy and health to `DeathResidue`; (d) a full-health agent (health >= 2.0) must post NOTHING at all — neither intake nor waste — because `stage_food` gates both on `healths[idx] < 2.0` (this is the regression test for "full agents drained cells forever").
- Property test over randomized configs (seeded): residual within tolerance for 5k ticks; and the stronger property that `sum(external_in) - sum(sinks) + sum(internal_net) == delta(stocks)` per stock exactly.
- NEGATIVE TESTS (the ones that matter):
  1. Delete the `stage_actuation` posting in a test-only fault-injected build -> the debug `StockGuard` must fail on tick 1. If it doesn't, the guard is decorative.
  2. Post the sunlight regrowth as an internal transfer instead of an external input -> the residual must blow up, proving the labels are load-bearing and not cosmetic.
  3. A tick with only cap-spill (every agent at 2.0 energy, food everywhere) must have residual 0 and a NON-ZERO `EnergyCapSpill` — proving the sink is measured rather than swallowed by the residual.
  4. Feed a NaN flow -> typed error, not a silently-passing comparison.

LOGGING. Target `scriptbots::economy`.
- info, once per epoch: `epoch`, `tick_range`, one field per category total, `stock_energy_before/after`, `stock_health_before/after`, `stock_food_before/after`, `residual_energy`, `residual_health`, `residual_food`, `gross_flow`, `tolerance`. A reader who has never seen the source must be able to answer "where did the joules go this epoch?" from this one line.
- warn, on any per-tick residual over tolerance: `tick`, `stock`, `residual`, `tolerance`, `worst_category`, `inflow`, `outflow`, `delta_stock`. An economy regression must announce itself, name the book it broke, and name its prime suspect.
- debug: per-tick residual row (enabled by a config flag; off by default at 10k agents).
- The kernel itself never logs from inside a pure fn: `ConservationResidual` carries every field a complete log line needs, so the caller can emit it without reaching back into the ledger.
close_reason: Completed. The orphaned aggregation core (economy.rs EpochAggregator/EpochFlows with Neumaier compensated summation and derived tolerances, 8 tests) was already landed; this completes the bead's remaining contracts. (1) StockGuard: a debug assertion at every tick boundary — books recomputed from the world must balance with posted flows within derived tolerance, firing AFTER the report update so failing books stay inspectable; fault-injection proves it is not decorative (unposted mutation panics on that tick). FIRST CATCH on day one: stage_actuation's posting skipped zero-drain agents, so over-cap health was destroyed unposted (uid_canonical fixtures: -63/-162 health unexplained); zero-drain cap losses now post to CapacityRejection and the full suite passes with the guard active. (2) FlowClass table (ExternalInput/InternalTransfer/Sink) — the load-bearing labels for sunlight regrowth, manufactured carcass rewards, spawn endowment; pin-tested. (3) Negatives: cap-spill fixture (1.99 + 0.5 gain credits 0.01, the destroyed 0.49 measured as CapacityRejection activity, books reconcile); the flow-class pin covers the sunlight-mislabel case in the landed type system. (4) Logging: warn at scriptbots::economy on any unreconciled tick (release included), info per sealed epoch with per-category totals and residual/gross triples, config-gated per-tick debug row (economy_debug_per_tick, default off). (5) Property proof: four seeded configs (baseline, 5k-tick tiny world, harsh metabolism, generous regrowth) close their cumulative books within derived tolerance, and the class-signed decomposition recomposes delta(stocks). Deviations: per-category posting unit tests partially live in the two resource_ledger attribute tests; the bead's FlowCategory design was adapted to the landed ResourceFlowKind/ResourceLedgerTick types (same coverage, no parallel taxonomy). Verification: strict clippy -D warnings clean; core 398 lib + heredity 8 + integrations green with the StockGuard active; UBS 0 critical.

title: Conservation CI gate with injected-leak mutation test (prove the alarm fires)
description:
SCOPE. The CI gate that turns bd-16g.11.1's residual into a build-breaking assertion, plus the mutation suite that PROVES the gate can go red. Deliverables: a long-run conservation harness (`scriptbots-app economy-audit --seeds 3 --ticks 50000 --out artifacts/economy/`), a CI job that runs it and uploads the residual timeseries, and a table-driven fault-injection test asserting that every injectable economy fault fails the gate.

WHY. A conservation gate that has never been observed to fail is not evidence of conservation; it is evidence of nothing. Every one of the historical economy bugs (10x metabolism drain, eating that never restored health, full agents draining cells forever) shipped green under whatever tests existed at the time. The single most valuable artifact in this bead is not the passing run — it is the FAILING run under an injected leak, because that is the only thing that establishes the alarm is wired to a bell.

DESIGN.
- Harness: a headless runner reusing the matched-seed runner (bd-2z0.5.5). For each seed: build the world from a pinned scenario, tick N times, feed every `TickFlows` (bd-16g.11.1) to the aggregator, and stream the per-tick residual to a CSV/Parquet artifact (`residual_<seed>.csv`: tick, stock, inflow, outflow, delta_stock, residual, tolerance, gross_flow, worst_category). The artifact exists so a red CI run is diagnosable WITHOUT reproducing it locally.
- Verdict type: `ConservationVerdict { seeds: Vec<SeedVerdict>, pass: bool }`, `SeedVerdict { seed, ticks, max_abs_residual: [f64;3], argmax_tick: [Tick;3], cumulative_residual: [f64;3], breaches: Vec<Breach> }`. `Breach { tick, stock, residual, tolerance, worst_category }`, capped at the first 100 with a `truncated` count (a log that prints 50,000 breaches is a log nobody reads).
- Gate criteria, all three (any one alone is gameable):
  1. per-tick: `|residual| <= tol_tick` for every tick, every stock, every seed;
  2. cumulative: `|sum(residual)| <= tol_cum` — catches a tiny systematic bias that per-tick tolerance would wave through, which is precisely how a 0.0002-vs-0.002 drain error hides;
  3. quiet-run: ZERO warn-level economy log lines on the unmutated run. A gate that passes while spraying warnings has already lost.
- Fault injection: `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "economy-faults"))] pub enum LedgerFault { DoubleCreditIntake, DropActuationPosting, DropTemperaturePosting, HalveWasteDebit, MislabelSunlightAsTransfer, MislabelCarcassAsTransfer, SkipDeathResidue, ForgetEnergyCapSpill, ForgetHealthCapSpill, ScaleMetabolismDrainBy10, CreditIntakeWithoutHealthGate }` installed via a test-only hook on the world (`WorldState::inject_ledger_fault(fault)`), NOT via `#[cfg]`-ing the production code paths into different shapes. The faults are chosen to reproduce the audit's real bugs: `ScaleMetabolismDrainBy10` is the hidden death timer; `CreditIntakeWithoutHealthGate` is full agents draining cells forever; `DropActuationPosting` is the `food_delta` blind spot that exists in the code today.
- Completeness: a `fault_coverage` test asserting that every `FlowCategory` variant is exercised by at least one fault (a static table `CATEGORY_TO_FAULT: [&[LedgerFault]; FlowCategory::COUNT]` with a compile-time-checked length). Add a category without adding a fault and the build fails. This is what prevents the gate from decaying as the economy grows.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- Every fault MUST turn the gate red. The test is `for fault in LedgerFault::ALL { assert!(run_gate_with(fault).pass == false, "fault {fault:?} was not detected") }` — and it must also assert WHICH stock and which `worst_category` was fingered, so the gate is not merely red but red for the right reason (a gate that fails on everything is as useless as one that fails on nothing).
- The unmutated 50k x 3-seed run must be green and must stay under a CI time budget (target <= 5 min on the standard runner at ~1000 agents; if it does not fit, reduce agents, never ticks — a short run cannot exhibit cumulative drift, which is the whole point of the cumulative criterion).
- Determinism: the gate's verdict is a pure function of (seed, config, tick count). Two invocations produce byte-identical `ConservationVerdict` JSON. If the gate is flaky, it will be disabled within a month, and then the economy is unguarded again.
- The tolerance constants live in ONE place (bd-16g.11.1) and are printed in the verdict artifact. Loosening a tolerance to make CI green must be a visible, reviewable diff, not a local `--tolerance` flag that a frustrated engineer passes forever. `--tolerance` may exist for debugging but the CI job must NOT pass it, and the harness must record `tolerance_overridden: true` in the artifact when it is used.

TESTS.
- Unit: gate criteria evaluation on hand-built `ConservationVerdict` fixtures (per-tick breach only, cumulative breach only, warn-count breach only, all clean) — each must produce the expected pass/fail and the expected message.
- Unit: `fault_coverage` completeness (above).
- Mutation suite (the centerpiece): every `LedgerFault` -> gate red, correct stock, correct `worst_category`, and the first breach tick within a documented bound (e.g. `DoubleCreditIntake` must be caught within 10 ticks — a leak that takes 40k ticks to detect would not have caught the historical bugs in practice).
- E2E: `economy-audit --seeds 3 --ticks 50000` runs headless, writes the artifacts, exits 0; a second invocation produces identical verdict bytes.
- NEGATIVE (anti-alarm-fatigue): a scenario with EXTREME but legal parameters (food_growth_rate at max, boost always on, 90% carnivores, heavy carcass turnover) must still be GREEN. A gate that fires on a legal-but-weird config gets muted, and a muted gate is a lie in a green checkmark.
- NEGATIVE: run the gate against a ledger with a deliberately mislabeled sunlight input (external -> internal) and assert the failure message names `SunlightRegrowth` — proving the labeling requirement from bd-16g.11.1 is enforced, not decorative.

LOGGING. Target `scriptbots::economy::gate`.
- info at start: `seeds`, `ticks`, `config_digest`, `tolerance_tick`, `tolerance_cum`, `tolerance_overridden`.
- info per seed on completion: `seed`, `max_abs_residual_energy/health/food`, `argmax_tick_*`, `cumulative_residual_*`, `verdict`.
- error on failure: the first 10 breaches, each with `tick`, `stock`, `residual`, `tolerance`, `worst_category`, `inflow`, `outflow`, `delta_stock`, plus the artifact path. Someone reading only CI logs must be able to say "metabolism is over-posted starting at tick 412" without cloning the repo.
- info final: one machine-parseable verdict line (`economy_gate verdict=fail seeds=3 breaches=137 worst=MetabolismDrain artifact=...`) — this is the line the leaderboard/release checklist greps for.
acceptance_criteria: Preserve the committed ConservationGate, typed verdicts, 17 LedgerFault variants, and category coverage. Add scriptbots-app economy-audit --seeds 3 --ticks 50000 --out DIR using the matched-seed headless runner; emit bounded per-seed residual CSV or Parquet plus deterministic ConservationVerdict JSON containing config digest, tolerances, override state, extrema, cumulative residuals, first 100 breaches, and truncation counts. Add a CI job that runs the command without tolerance overrides, enforces per-tick, cumulative, and actual zero warn-event criteria, uploads artifacts, and stays within the documented time budget by reducing agents rather than ticks. Table-driven mutation tests must make every fault fail within a stated bound and assert the expected stock and worst category; add clean 3x50k, extreme-legal anti-alarm, mislabeled-sunlight, cumulative-only, warn-only, byte-identical rerun, typed-error, and missing-artifact negative coverage. comments.author: QuietBeaver
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE of the long-standing every_injectable_fault_turns_the_gate_red failure, and it is a hole in this bead's centerpiece rather than a flaky test.

THE SYMPTOM, red on main since at least bd-cqja recorded it:
  fault DropCombatPosting was not detected within 64 ticks
  crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs, every_injectable_fault_turns_the_gate_red

THE MECHANISM, traced end to end:
  1. Combat is posted as a DERIVED DELTA, not an explicit flow. lib.rs ~23121:
       observed_stage!(WorldStepStage::Combat, {
           let before = self.capture_resource_amounts();
           self.stage_combat();
           self.record_resource_change(ResourceFlowKind::Combat, before);
       });
     So the posting is whatever combat actually changed. If combat changes nothing, the posted
     flow is zero.
  2. DropCombatPosting suppresses record() when kind == Combat (lib.rs ~5624). Suppressing a ZERO
     flow is a no-op, so the residual never moves and the gate never goes red.
  3. The fixture tries to force combat by setting runtime.spiked = true and
     combat.was_spiked_by_carnivore = true on a victim between ticks.
  4. stage_reset_events (lib.rs:19157) sets runtime.spiked = false at lib.rs:19179 -- it runs
     before the Combat stage, so the fixture's flag is wiped before stage_combat ever sees it.
     Combat therefore moves no resources and there is nothing for the fault to drop.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN ONE RED TEST. CATEGORY_TO_FAULTS (economy.rs ~1352) lists Combat as
covered by DropCombatPosting, and the fault_coverage completeness test PASSES. So the suite reports
full category coverage while the Combat category has never actually been exercised. That coverage
is nominal, not real: THE GATE HAS NEVER BEEN OBSERVED TO CATCH A COMBAT LEAK. This bead's own
rationale is that 'a conservation gate that has never been observed to fail is not evidence of
conservation; it is evidence of nothing' -- that statement is true per-category, and Combat is the
category where it currently holds.

It is also a warning about the completeness test's shape: fault_coverage proves a fault is MAPPED
to every category, not that the fault is REACHABLE. A mapping-only check cannot distinguish a
covered category from an unexercisable one, which is precisely how this survived.

TWO WAYS TO FIX, and they are not equivalent:
  (a) Fix the fixture so it produces real combat -- drive a genuine spike hit through the
      simulation (position two agents in range, orient and extend the spike, let stage_combat act)
      rather than setting flags that the reset stage clears. This proves the gate catches combat
      leaks, which is what the bead asks for.
  (b) Weaken or ignore the assertion. That would convert a real coverage gap into a green
      checkmark and is exactly what this bead exists to prevent.
Taking (a). Recording this first because the finding stands independently of whatever fix lands,
and because anyone who sees this test red should not reach for (b).

RELATED, since it changes how this suite is run: bd-dz37 moved the LedgerFault machinery to gate on
cfg(feature = "economy-faults") ALONE -- it previously also admitted cfg(test), which gave every
test build a fault field on ResourceLedgerState that production does not have. This bead's
description still shows the old cfg(any(test, feature = ...)) predicate and is stale on that point.
The suite now needs --features economy-faults, and AGENTS.md's documented gate command carries it.

comments.author: QuietBeaver
comments.text:
QuietBeaver, resumed. CORRECTION to my own handoff note, found by reading stage_brains before trusting the fixture.

My handoff said the uncommitted fixture works by writing runtime.outputs[SpikeTarget]=1.0 because
"stage_reset_events does NOT clear outputs". That half is true and irrelevant. The write still cannot
survive a tick, for a different reason:

  step() order (lib.rs ~23049-23126): Interventions, Aging, FoodDynamics, Sense, BRAINS(23075),
  Actuation(23076), TemperatureDiscomfort, Food, ... COMBAT(23121).

  stage_brains writes back UNCONDITIONALLY, for every agent, bound or not (lib.rs ~18340):
      runtime.brain.restore_execution(job.execution);
      runtime.outputs = job.outputs;
  and for an unbound agent job.outputs = Self::default_outputs(&job.sensors) (lib.rs 18017-18022),
  i.e. a copy of the first OUTPUT_SIZE sensors.

mutation_suite_world spawns six AgentData::default() agents and binds no brain, so every one of them
is Unbound. Therefore on tick 1, before Combat ever runs, outputs[SpikeTarget] is overwritten with
sensors[5]. My between-ticks write is gone. Same class of mistake as the original runtime.spiked
write it was meant to replace: staging a value into a channel that a later stage recomputes.

WHAT IN THAT FIXTURE ACTUALLY DOES SURVIVE, and it is the load-bearing part:
  - spike_lengths[attacker] = 5.0. Actuation only walks spike_length toward decoded.spike_target at
    config.spike_growth_rate, default 0.005/tick, so 5.0 decays to the 0.5 eligibility floor in ~900
    ticks -- far outside the 64-tick window. This is the real unblocker, and it identifies why Combat
    was dead: default spike_length starts at 0 and grows 0.005/tick, so it CANNOT cross the hard
    `if spike_lengths[idx] <= 0.5 { return }` floor (lib.rs 20828) within 64 ticks no matter what the
    brain commands. Combat was unreachable by construction in this suite.
  - herbivore_tendency = 0.0 (carnivore gate), spike_min_length = 0.0, spike_alignment_cosine = 0.0.
  - Geometry is not actually delicate: spike_radius defaults to 40.0, so reach = 40 + spike_length =
    45 in a 120x120 world. Every agent is in reach of every other; only the forward-hemisphere
    alignment test filters.

So the surviving gap is exactly one term: spike_power = outputs.channel_clamped(SpikeTarget) must
exceed EPSILON at the Combat stage, and for an unbound agent that is whatever sensors[5] happens to
be that tick. Leaving it there would make Combat coverage contingent on an incidental sensor value --
nominal coverage again, one sensor-layout change away from silently evaporating. That is the precise
failure mode this bead exists to prevent, so it is not acceptable even if it happens to pass today.

THE FIX, matching machinery this file already has: bind LedgerAggressorBrain (lib.rs 42181-42201) to
the attacker. It is a BrainRunner that returns outputs[5] = 1.0 every tick, it is the same brain the
neighboring resource_ledger_attributes_ecology_combat_and_interventions test uses to produce its
asserted non-zero Combat attribution, and being a brain it writes through stage_brains instead of
being overwritten by it. Deterministic, intentional, and already proven to move Combat resources.

Verification of the pre-correction fixture is running now (hz2, trustworthy worker). Its result is
informative either way but does not change the above: the outputs write is wrong by construction.

comments.author: QuietBeaver
comments.text:
QuietBeaver: a design defect in this bead's own HARD REQUIREMENT, found while scoping the per-fault
diagnostic assertions. Recording before implementing so the assertion is not written wrong.

The bead requires the mutation suite to "assert WHICH stock and which worst_category was fingered,
so the gate is not merely red but red for the right reason". For roughly half the faults that
worst_category assertion cannot be satisfied as written, and forcing it would produce a false test.

WHY. worst_category is computed (economy.rs ~359-370) as the largest-magnitude entry of per_category
on the broken stock:
    per_category.iter().map(|flow| stock.lane(flow.delta).abs()).enumerate()
        .filter(|(_, magnitude)| *magnitude > 0.0).max_by(...)
It ranks flows THAT WERE RECORDED. But every Drop*Posting fault works by suppressing record() for its
own kind, so the guilty category contributes exactly nothing to per_category and is structurally
ineligible to be the max. For DropCombatPosting, DropActuationPosting, DropTemperaturePosting,
DropAgingPosting, DropReproductionPosting, DropPopulationPosting, DropInterventionPosting and
SkipDeathResidue, worst_category will name some innocent bystander -- whichever legitimate flow
happens to be largest on that stock that tick. Asserting worst_category == the dropped kind would
fail; asserting whatever it currently emits would pin an accident.

That is not a flaw in worst_category. It is doing its job: it is a SUSPECT RANKING over the books,
and the defining property of a dropped posting is that it is absent from the books. A missing flow
cannot be fingered by a statistic computed over present flows. Worth stating plainly because the
diagnostic's advertised value ("metabolism is over-posted starting at tick 412") holds for
mislabel/double-credit/scale faults and does NOT hold for drop faults, where the honest diagnosis is
"this stock moved and nothing in the books accounts for it".

THEREFORE the per-fault expectation table should be typed by fault shape, not uniform:
  - DISTORTION faults (DoubleCreditIntake, HalveWasteDebit, CorruptGiveTransfer,
    MislabelSunlightAsTransfer, MislabelCarcassAsTransfer, ScaleMetabolismDrainBy10,
    CreditIntakeWithoutHealthGate, ForgetEnergyCapSpill, ForgetHealthCapSpill): the guilty flow IS
    posted, just wrongly, so assert expected stock AND expected worst_category.
  - OMISSION faults (the eight above): assert expected stock and the first-breach tick bound, and
    assert worst_category is None-or-unconstrained. Deliberately NOT asserting an innocent category.
An expectation table with a per-fault `expected_worst: Option<ResourceFlowKind>` expresses exactly
this, and the None arms should carry the one-line reason so nobody "tightens" them later.

This does not weaken the gate. The stock assertion plus the tick bound still prove it went red for
the right stock at the right time; only the suspect-naming is claimed where it is actually derivable.
Flagging it as a real defect in the bead's acceptance criteria rather than silently diverging.

Sequencing: this is the slice after the DropCombatPosting fixture lands, and it is separable from the
still-untouched economy-audit CLI / CI workflow / residual artifact work. Confirmed by grep this
session that NO economy-audit subcommand, workflow, or artifact writer exists anywhere in crates/ yet.

comments.text:
QuietBeaver: DropCombatPosting fixture LANDED as dfaca98aa448 (main + master). Scope of what is and
is not proven, then exactly what remains on this bead.

WHAT LANDED. One setup arm in every_injectable_fault_turns_the_gate_red, 62 insertions, entirely
inside mod tests. It seeds the attacker's spike_length to 5.0 and binds LedgerAggressorBrain.

THE ACTUAL ROOT CAUSE, which is narrower and more damning than "the fixture was wrong". Combat was
UNREACHABLE BY CONSTRUCTION in this suite. stage_combat hard-gates on spike_lengths[idx] > 0.5
(lib.rs 20828). Default spike length is 0 and actuation only walks it toward the commanded target at
spike_growth_rate = 0.005/tick, so within a 64-tick window the maximum attainable length is ~0.32 --
below the floor, no matter what any brain commands. Every agent returned early from stage_combat on
every tick of every run. record_resource_change(Combat, before) consequently posted a zero delta, and
DropCombatPosting works by suppressing that posting, so it suppressed nothing. The gate could not go
red because there was nothing to drop.

That means KIND_TO_FAULTS has been reporting Combat as covered for the entire life of this suite while
the gate had never once been observed to catch a combat leak -- which is precisely the "evidence of
nothing" this bead was written against, holding per-category.

SECOND MECHANISM, the one that invalidated my earlier uncommitted attempt: the commanded spike must
come from a BRAIN. stage_brains (23075) runs before Combat (23121) and writes back unconditionally for
every agent, bound or not -- runtime.outputs = job.outputs, with default_outputs(sensors) for unbound
agents (18017-18022). So any value staged into runtime.outputs between ticks is overwritten before
combat reads it. Binding LedgerAggressorBrain is what makes SpikeTarget = 1.0 durable, and it is the
same mechanism resource_ledger_attributes_ecology_combat_and_interventions already uses to earn its
asserted non-zero Combat attribution.

  PROVEN: rustfmt --edition 2024 --check exit 0; ubs zero findings anywhere in the changed range.
  NOT PROVEN: pass/fail. The verdict did not return within 18 minutes.
Landed under the bd-e6ff dispensation for inspection/compile-verified work, labelled in the commit

NEW FINDING worth its own attention: THIS TEST MAY BE PATHOLOGICALLY SLOW, AND IT IS NOT MY CHANGE.
The pre-change code also ran 20m24s on hz2 without returning a verdict. Two independent 18-20 minute

rather than of this fixture. Plausible mechanism: mutation_suite_world sets reproduction_cooldown 1,
reproduction_attempt_interval 1, reproduction_attempt_chance 1.0 and population_minimum 8 with agents

discover in CI. NOT yet diagnosed -- flagging with evidence, not asserting.

WHAT REMAINS ON THIS BEAD, unchanged and still untouched by me:
  1. The titled deliverable: `scriptbots-app economy-audit --seeds 3 --ticks 50000 --out DIR`.
     CONFIRMED BY GREP THIS SESSION that no economy-audit subcommand, workflow, artifact writer, or

  6. Anti-alarm-fatigue extreme-legal negative and the mislabeled-sunlight negative.
Bead stays OPEN and in_progress. Closing it now would overclaim by a wide margin: the fixture is one

title: Sankey view (GPU lab), trophic table (TUI), and per-epoch export agreement
description:
SCOPE. The three faces of the same numbers: a Sankey energy-flow view in the GPU lab (scriptbots-render / scriptbots-world-gfx), a compact trophic table in the TUI (crates/scriptbots-app/src/terminal/mod.rs), and a per-epoch JSON/Parquet export (bd-2z0.5.6). Plus the test that proves all three agree, to the last decimal, with the ledger they read.

WHY. A dashboard that computes its own totals is a second accountant, and a second accountant who disagrees with the first is worse than no accountant at all — you now have two numbers and no truth. The entire value of the ecosystem view rests on it being a RENDERING of `EpochFlows` (bd-16g.11.1), not a re-derivation. The payoff, once that holds: a population crash becomes visible as a specific flow collapsing (grazing intake goes to zero while metabolism keeps draining = starvation; carcass flow spikes while intake holds = a predation cascade), and the overlay of bd-16g.2 events onto the flow timeline is what turns "the population fell" into "the population fell BECAUSE".

DESIGN.
- Single source, three renderers. Add ONE shared pure function in the economy module:
  `pub fn sankey_layout(flows: &EpochFlows, opts: &SankeyOpts) -> SankeyGraph`
  `pub struct SankeyGraph { nodes: Vec<SankeyNode { id: NodeId, label: &'static str, class: NodeClass }>, links: Vec<SankeyLink { from: NodeId, to: NodeId, value: f64, category: FlowCategory }> }`
  `pub enum NodeClass { ExternalSource, FoodGrid, Herbivores, Omnivores, Carnivores, Sink, Unaccounted }`
  and ONE shared table builder: `pub fn trophic_table(flows: &EpochFlows, pop: &DietCensus) -> TrophicTable` with typed rows (`TrophicRow { class, standing_health, standing_energy, intake_rate, drain_rate, conversion_efficiency, net }`). The Sankey renderer, the ratatui table and the exporter all consume these structs and do NOTHING but format them. No renderer may call `sum()` on a flow.
- Diet classes are DEFINED ONCE and documented (`herbivore_tendency >= 0.7` => Herbivore, `<= 0.3` => Carnivore, else Omnivore) in the same module, because three views that each pick their own threshold will silently disagree about who ate what.
- The residual is a NODE, not a rounding error. `NodeClass::Unaccounted` receives an explicit link carrying the epoch residual. A Sankey that balances by quietly dropping the remainder is a lie with a pretty gradient; if the books are off by 0.3%, the diagram says so in ink.
- External inputs are drawn as EXTERNAL: `SunlightRegrowth`, `FoodRespawn`, `CarcassManufacturedHealth/Energy` and `SpawnEndowment` enter from a labeled source node ("sunlight", "manufactured") outside the closed system, so a reader can see at a glance how much of this ecosystem is subsidized. (In this model, quite a lot: regrowth is free, and carcass rewards are minted from config constants, not debited from the corpse.)
- Grazing is drawn as TWO links, matching the code: `FoodGrid -> Sink (GrazingCellWaste)` and `FoodGrid -> Herbivores (GrazingAgentIntake)`, because `stage_food` decrements the cell by `waste` and credits the agent from `intake`, and these are not equal. Drawing one "grazing" arrow would fabricate a conservation that the simulation does not have.
- Time-resolved: the view scrubs to any epoch (reading the persisted per-epoch ledger, not by re-simulating), and overlays the bd-16g.2 event timeline on the flow series.
- Export schema is versioned and provenance-carrying: `scriptbots.economy-epoch/v1` with `run_id`, `config_digest`, `epoch`, `tick_range`, every category, every residual, plus the manifest's `reproducible` flag and sense backend (bd-16g.15) — an economy table copied into a paper must carry the provenance of the run that produced it.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- Byte-level agreement: the numbers rendered in the TUI, the link values in the Sankey, and the values in the export are all `f64` from the SAME `EpochFlows`. Formatting may round for display, but the test compares the pre-format `f64`s, so a display rounding change can never masquerade as an economy change (and vice versa).
- Missing data renders as MISSING. If the requested epoch is not in the ledger, the views show "no data" and log a warn. Rendering zeros for absent data is how a broken persistence path gets mistaken for a dead ecosystem.
- Bounded cost: the GPU lab must not stall on the Sankey; layout is computed from an epoch-aggregated struct (tens of numbers), never from raw per-tick postings. The TUI table must render in O(categories + classes).
- No re-derivation. Enforce with a CI grep-level structural test: the render and terminal modules must not reference `FlowCategory` arithmetic helpers or the raw `TickFlows` type — they may only consume `EpochFlows`, `SankeyGraph` and `TrophicTable`. State this in the module doc so the next person does not "just quickly" add a sum in the UI.

TESTS.
- Unit: `sankey_layout` on a golden `EpochFlows` fixture — assert node set, link set, and that for every non-source, non-sink node `sum(incoming) - sum(outgoing) == 0` after the `Unaccounted` link is included (Kirchhoff at every node; if this fails, the diagram is drawing energy that does not exist).
- Unit: `trophic_table` on a fixture with all three diet classes present, one class empty (must render an empty row, not vanish), and a class with zero intake (conversion_efficiency must be `None`/"n/a", not `0/0 = NaN` printed as "NaN%").
- AGREEMENT E2E (the acceptance test): one recorded run -> one ledger -> render the TUI table to a string, build the `SankeyGraph`, write the export, then parse the export back and assert all three carry identical `f64` values for all categories and residuals. Do this for an epoch with a residual deliberately at 90% of tolerance, so the residual link is non-zero and actually compared.
- NEGATIVE: change ONE renderer to sum its own flows (fault-injected build) and de-sync it by an epsilon -> the agreement test must fail. This proves the agreement test is testing agreement and not just running three code paths.
- NEGATIVE: drop the `Unaccounted` link -> the Kirchhoff test must fail. The temptation to hide the residual for a prettier diagram is real; make it structurally impossible to yield to.
- NEGATIVE: request an epoch outside the ledger's range -> assert "no data" is rendered, a warn is logged, and NO zeros appear in the export.
- Snapshot test of the TUI table (insta) so a column-alignment change is reviewed rather than discovered.

LOGGING. Target `scriptbots::economy::view`.
- info on view open: `view` (sankey|trophic|export), `run_id`, `epoch`, `tick_range`, `ledger_digest`, `residual_*`. The `ledger_digest` is what lets a reader confirm two views were looking at the same books.
- warn when an epoch is missing, when a diet class is empty for the whole epoch (an extinct class is a finding, not a formatting problem), and when the residual link exceeds 1% of the epoch's gross flow (the diagram is now visibly unbalanced and the user should be told why before they screenshot it).
- info on export: `path`, `schema`, `rows`, `bytes`, `config_digest`, `reproducible`.
design: This child owns only the three consumer surfaces and their agreement proof. The economy module produces one canonical SankeyGraph and TrophicTable from persisted EpochFlows; GPU, TUI, and export adapters format those shared values and never rederive totals from raw events or TickFlows. Missing epochs remain typed missing data, the residual is visible, and event overlays are keyed to the same run and epoch identity.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A real recorded run is reopened from storage and the same epoch is consumed by the GPU Sankey, production TUI trophic table, and versioned JSON and Parquet export; all pre-format f64 categories, residuals, tick ranges, and provenance agree byte-for-byte with EpochFlows. 2. Unit tests cover balanced and residual-bearing Sankey fixtures, all diet classes including empty and zero-intake rows, missing epochs, stable ordering, and bounded layout cost. 3. Negative tests prove the agreement gate fails when any renderer re-sums an epsilon or drops Unaccounted, and missing data never becomes zeros. 4. A checked-in real E2E script drives the actual storage reader and both shipped presentation surfaces without mocks, parses the export with an independent reader, and retains source/run/epoch/ledger digests, every compared value, screenshots or terminal capture, stdout/stderr, and exit evidence. 5. Structured logs include view, run, epoch, tick range, ledger digest, residuals, missing-data reason, export schema/path/rows/bytes, config digest, and reproducibility label.
notes: Reopened by audit comment 924. Pure view models and unit serialization are not completion; closure requires real GPU, production TUI, export, scrub and event-overlay consumers plus cross-surface agreement.

title: Brain-family tournament: matched-world competitions, Elo leaderboard, and publishable comparative results
description:
THE IDEA. Turn the brain testbed into a competition with results worth publishing: run matched-world tournaments across brain families (MLP, DWRAON, Assembly, Neuroflow, and future ML adapters), with identical seeds/terrain/food and equal starting cohorts, then score families by survival share, biomass share, lineage persistence, and time-to-extinction across many seeds. Maintain an Elo (or Bradley-Terry) rating with confidence intervals, and publish a leaderboard table in the docs that CI regenerates.

WHY IT MATTERS. The README's central claim for the Brain trait is that it "enables fair comparisons" of architectures — and today the project cannot answer "is DWRAON better than MLP, and at what?" That is an embarrassing gap for a brain testbed, and closing it produces the project's most CITABLE artifact: an empirical comparison of neural architectures under identical ecological pressure. It also creates a natural home for future ML backends (bd-2z0.8.10) — a new adapter is interesting exactly insofar as it can win. The infrastructure is nearly free: mixed-family spawning and the same-kind mating barrier already exist, and bd-2z0.5.5 provides matched-seed running.

DESIGN.
- Fairness first (this is the whole point): equal cohort sizes, identical seeds/terrain, identical mutation-rate defaults, and BOTH assignments of families to spawn order (to cancel any order/position advantage) — the tournament harness must actively hunt for its own biases and document them.
- Report effect sizes with CIs over >=N seeds, not a single dramatic run; a family "wins" only if the CI excludes parity.
- Score on multiple axes (survival share, biomass, lineage depth, novelty coverage from bd-16g.6) because "best" is multi-dimensional; publish the whole table, not one number.
- The leaderboard is CI-regenerated from a pinned seed set so it cannot rot into marketing; every cell links to the run_ids that produced it.

ACCEPTANCE. `scriptbots-app tournament --families all --seeds 32 --ticks 20k` emits a leaderboard with CIs and run provenance; results are reproducible; swapping spawn order does not change the ranking (or, if it does, that fact is REPORTED as a finding — an order effect is itself a scientific result about the environment).

TESTS + LOGGING (required).
- Unit: tournament pairing/assignment logic (equal cohorts, balanced orders, deterministic seed allocation).
- Unit: rating math (Elo/BT update, CI computation) against hand-computed fixtures.
- E2E: small tournament (4 seeds, 2k ticks) runs end-to-end headless, persists per-run results, regenerates the leaderboard, and asserts reproducibility across two invocations; log per-run outcome rows (seed, family, survival, biomass, lineage_depth) at info so a suspicious result can be traced to its runs.
acceptance_criteria: The parent closes only when the balanced matched-world harness, uncertainty-aware Elo and Bradley-Terry rating math, and CI-regenerated leaderboard children are all closed at one exact source revision with their retained unit, negative-control, and mock-free E2E evidence. A pinned tournament spec covers every eligible registered production brain family with equal cohorts, deterministic seeds and order swaps, documented exclusions, science/config/build identity, and no family-specific scoring branches; optional or approximate families are labeled rather than silently compared. Independent recomputation from raw match rows reproduces ratings, confidence intervals, multi-axis scores, ordering, rounding, and generated documentation byte-for-byte. Negative controls for seed/config drift, order bias, missing cells, duplicate or excluded runs, hand-edited ratings, and raw-row tampering all turn the publication gate red. The final mock-free pipeline runs plan through worlds, persistence, rating, rendering, and check twice, retains per-match and per-family structured logs plus raw rows/manifests/stdout/stderr, and produces identical result digests before any publishable claim.
