title: Tournament harness: balanced cohorts, order-swap bias control, deterministic seed allocation
description:
SCOPE. The tournament HARNESS: turn a `TournamentSpec` into a deterministic, bias-controlled set of match plans, execute them (headless, matched-seed, reusing bd-2z0.5.5), and emit typed per-match outcomes. No rating math (bd-16g.12.2), no leaderboard rendering (bd-16g.12.3). Proposed home: a new `tournament` module in scriptbots-app, driving `WorldState` through the existing brain registry. This is the bead where fairness is either engineered in or lost forever, because no amount of downstream statistics can rescue a biased pairing.

WHY. The README's central claim for the `Brain` trait is that it "enables fair comparisons" of architectures, and the project currently cannot answer "is DWRAON better than MLP, and at what?". That is an embarrassing gap for something calling itself a brain testbed. But an UNFAIR tournament is strictly worse than no tournament: it produces a citable-looking number that is an artifact of spawn order or cohort size, and it will be believed.

GROUND TRUTH IN THE CODE (each of these is a live bias source; read them before designing).
- Same-kind mating barrier: crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs (~8175) filters the crossover partner with `.filter(|partner| partner.kind() == parent_runner.kind())`; on failure it falls back to `parent_runner.clone_runner()`. Families therefore do not interbreed — good — but it also means a family with FEWER conspecifics has fewer viable partners and reproduces more asexually. Cohort imbalance is not a small statistical nuisance; it directly changes the reproduction operator each family experiences. Unequal cohorts are a HARD ERROR, not a rounding.
- `stage_population` is an open-world lifeline. It spawns random agents whenever `agents.len() < population_minimum`, and on every `population_spawn_interval` it spawns `population_spawn_count` more (via `spawn_random_agent` or `spawn_crossover_agent` at `population_crossover_chance`). In a tournament this silently RESURRECTS extinct families and injects brains nobody entered. `WorldState::set_closed(true)` disables the whole stage. Tournaments MUST run closed (or with an explicit, recorded, justified policy) — otherwise "survival share" is measuring the respawner, not the brains. This is the single largest correctness trap in this bead.
- `stage_food_respawn` and `apply_food_regrowth` are seeded from the world RNG and the config, so identical seeds + identical config give identical terrain and food dynamics across arms — that is the matched-world property we depend on; assert it rather than assume it.
- `BRAIN_SIZE = 200`, `CONNECTIONS = 4` in both mlp.rs and dwraon.rs; assembly.rs also uses 200. Families are roughly parameter-matched today, which is worth STATING in the results (a comparison of a 200-node MLP against a 20-node MLP is a comparison of sizes, not architectures).

DESIGN.
- Types:
  `pub struct TournamentSpec { families: Vec<BrainKind>, seeds: Vec<u64>, ticks: u64, cohort_size: usize, order_policy: OrderPolicy, closed: bool, config_layers: Vec<PathBuf> }`
  `pub enum OrderPolicy { BothAssignments, BalancedLatinSquare, AllPermutations }`
  `pub struct MatchPlan { match_id: MatchId, seed: u64, spawn_order: Vec<BrainKind>, cohort: BTreeMap<BrainKind, usize>, world_seed: u64, brain_seed: u64 }`
  `pub struct MatchOutcome { match_id, ticks_run, per_family: BTreeMap<BrainKind, FamilyOutcome> }`
  `pub struct FamilyOutcome { survival_share: f64, biomass_share: f64, mean_lineage_depth: f64, max_lineage_depth: u32, extinct_at: Option<Tick>, novelty_coverage: Option<f64> }`
  `pub fn plan(spec: &TournamentSpec) -> Result<Vec<MatchPlan>, TournamentError>`
- Seed allocation is a PURE HASH, not a draw: `world_seed = splitmix64(root_seed ^ mix(match_index, 0))`, `brain_seed = splitmix64(root_seed ^ mix(match_index, 1))`. Never "pull the next value from a shared RNG" — that makes the assignment depend on iteration/scheduling order, and the tournament will quietly become irreproducible the first time someone parallelizes it with rayon.
- Order-swap bias control: with F families, each family must appear in each spawn-order position an equal number of times (`BothAssignments` for F=2; a balanced Latin square for F>2; full permutations only when F! * seeds is affordable). `plan()` must ASSERT this balance and return `TournamentError::UnbalancedOrders` rather than emit a plan it cannot defend.
- Equal cohorts: `cohort_size % families.len() != 0` -> `TournamentError::UnequalCohorts { cohort_size, families }`. No silent rounding, ever (see the mating barrier above).
- Identical everything else: the harness asserts that mutation rates, food/terrain/temperature config and the tick budget are IDENTICAL across arms by comparing the config digest of every match against the plan's digest. A tournament in which one family ran with a different `mutation_rate` default is not a finding, it is a bug that looks like a finding.
- Anti-coupling: the harness talks to brains ONLY through `BrainRegistry` + `BrainKind` (`WorldState::spawn_with_kind`-shaped API). It must never downcast to `MlpBrain`/`DwraonBrain`, and it must never special-case a family (`if kind == "dwraon" { ... }` is an instant review reject — it is the exact re-coupling the `Brain` trait exists to prevent, and the tournament is precisely the code most tempted to do it "just for the metric").
- Execution: matches are independent; run them in parallel across processes/threads, but each match's world is single-seeded and its outcome must be independent of scheduling. `--jobs N` must not change any number.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- Reproducibility: `plan()` is pure; `run(plan)` produces byte-identical `MatchOutcome` JSON on two invocations and at any `--jobs`. Assert it in CI, not in a comment.
- `closed: true` is the DEFAULT for tournaments, and if a spec sets it false the harness stamps `warnings: ["open-world respawn active; survival share includes respawned agents"]` into every outcome. Never let that qualifier get lost between the runner and the leaderboard.
- Cohort composition is recorded per match (which family got which spawn positions, which seed), so any suspicious result can be traced back to the exact world that produced it.
- The spawn ORDER effect is a measurement, not a nuisance to be hidden: the harness records `spawn_order_index` on every outcome so bd-16g.12.2 can test for an order effect and REPORT it. If position matters, that is a scientific fact about this environment and it goes in the paper.

TESTS.
- Unit: `plan()` for F=2,3,4 and seeds=1..8: equal cohorts, every family in every position equally often, unique `match_id`s, deterministic seed allocation (golden table of `(match_index -> world_seed, brain_seed)` — a hash change is then a visible diff, not a silent re-randomization of the whole tournament).
- Unit: `TournamentError::UnequalCohorts` when `cohort_size` is not divisible; `UnbalancedOrders` when the policy cannot balance.
- Unit: two `plan()` calls with the same spec are identical; `plan()` does not touch any RNG state.
- E2E: 2 families x 4 seeds x 2k ticks, headless, closed world -> outcomes persisted; run twice, assert byte-identical outcomes; run with `--jobs 1` and `--jobs 8`, assert identical outcomes.
- NEGATIVE (the bias tests, which are the whole point):
  1. NULL TOURNAMENT: register the SAME family twice under two names ("mlp.a", "mlp.b") and run the full harness. The two arms must be statistically indistinguishable, and any systematic gap is a harness bias, not a brain difference. Assert `|survival_share_a - survival_share_b|` is within the seed-level noise band. This is the test that catches an order/position advantage, an off-by-one in cohort sizing, and a seed-allocation correlation all at once.
  2. OPEN-WORLD LIFELINE: run one match with `closed: false` and `population_minimum` high, deliberately drive one family extinct, and assert the outcome records a warning AND that its survival share is flagged — proving we cannot silently publish a respawn-inflated result.
  3. Config-drift guard: mutate one arm's `mutation_rate` in a fault-injected build -> the harness must refuse to run (config digest mismatch), not produce a "finding".
  4. Cross-family mating: assert no child is ever produced from parents of different kinds (guards the barrier at core:8175 from regressing under a tournament's mixed cohort, which is the ONLY place the codebase routinely mixes families).

LOGGING. Target `scriptbots::tournament`.
- info at plan time: `families`, `seeds`, `ticks`, `cohort_size`, `matches`, `order_policy`, `closed`, `config_digest`, and the full seed-allocation table at debug.
- info per match on completion, one row per family: `match_id`, `seed`, `family`, `spawn_order_index`, `survival_share`, `biomass_share`, `mean_lineage_depth`, `extinct_at`, `agents_final`. These rows are the raw evidence; a suspicious leaderboard cell must be traceable to them without re-running anything.
- warn: open-world respawn active; a family extinct before 10% of the tick budget (likely a spawn bug, not a finding); any match that ended early.
- error: config digest mismatch across arms, with both digests.
notes: [CalmMink 2026-07-20] The tournament harness is implemented and verified in crates/scriptbots-app/src/tournament.rs (+ tests/tournament.rs). Slices: (1) a8cdab10c — pure plan(): equal cohorts enforced (UnequalCohorts), duplicate families rejected, per-position balance ASSERTED (UnbalancedOrders), MAX_MATCHES affordability guard, splitmix64 hash seed allocation with a golden table, BrainKind+Ord, 8 unit tests; (2) 19de56f4d — run_match: single-seeded closed-by-default match worlds through the existing headless driver, deterministic grid cohort placement, per-tick extinction tracking, config digest (blake3 of the seed-neutralized effective config), open-world qualifier stamped into every outcome; canonical-adapter dedupe registration (the registry refuses duplicate adapter identities by design — the RenamedFamilyAdapter path was abandoned because the inner evaluator validates the canonical family id embedded in genomes); arm attribution by founder uid + per-tick lineage inheritance so the null tournament's same-brain arms stay separable; (3) 00527eeb0 — run_tournament serial driver (any --jobs schedule reproduces per match by construction; a literal --jobs flag belongs to the bd-2z0.5.5 runner), enforce_no_config_drift with typed ConfigDrift, assert_no_cross_kind_mating inline at every match end; (4) 904fe1b97 — spawn_order_index on MatchPlan+MatchOutcome for the bd-16g.12.2 order-effect measurement, scriptbots::tournament evidence logging (plan acceptance, per-family outcome rows, early-extinction warnings). VERIFIED: 8/8 plan unit tests, 7/7 integration tests (byte-identical matches and report sets, seed allocation across assignments, open-world qualifier, null tournament mlp-a/mlp-b same-adapter mean survival-share gap within the seed-noise band, drift guard rejects a tampered arm naming the digest). Also restored the AgentId import the lint sweep dropped from checkpoint.rs. The execution adapter drives the existing headless driver and swaps to bd-2z0.5.5's matched-seed runner when it lands — no duplicate runner was built.
close_reason: Implemented and committed deterministic balanced tournament planning and execution in 0f7c70443597; verification evidence and infrastructure-limited final gate recorded in comment 907.

REOPENED by the bd-emmm close-reason guard (cc_3/AmberFalcon); evidence verified by hand.

title: Rating math (Elo/Bradley-Terry) with CIs and multi-axis scoring
description:
SCOPE. The statistics layer: convert bd-16g.12.1's `MatchOutcome`s into per-family ratings with honest confidence intervals, on MULTIPLE axes, plus the parity test that decides whether a family actually "wins". Pure module (proposed: `tournament::rating` in scriptbots-app), no I/O, no simulation types beyond `BrainKind` — it takes outcome rows and returns ratings.

WHY. "DWRAON beat MLP" from one dramatic run is not a result, it is an anecdote with a chart. The publishable artifact this project can uniquely produce is an empirical comparison of neural architectures under identical ecological pressure WITH error bars — and the error bars are the contribution. Anyone can print a number; the reason to trust this one is that we did the harder, correct thing with the uncertainty.

DESIGN.
- Pairwise reduction: every match yields, for each unordered family pair, a comparison on each axis (`survival_share`, `biomass_share`, `mean_lineage_depth`, `time_to_extinction`, `novelty_coverage` from bd-16g.6). `PairwiseResult { a: BrainKind, b: BrainKind, axis: Axis, wins_a: u32, wins_b: u32, draws: u32, seed_of: Vec<u64> }` — retain the seed of every comparison, because the seed is the clustering unit (see below).
- Rating: Bradley-Terry fit by the MM/Zermelo iteration, `fit_bradley_terry(&[PairwiseResult], prior: BtPrior) -> Ratings`, with `BtPrior { pseudo_wins: f64 }` (default 0.5) as a REGULARIZER. Without it, a family that wins every match has a divergent MLE and the leaderboard prints `+inf` (or, worse, a large finite number produced by hitting the iteration cap) — that is the classic embarrassment and the prior is the fix. `Ratings { theta: BTreeMap<BrainKind, f64>, se: BTreeMap<BrainKind, f64>, ci95: BTreeMap<BrainKind, (f64, f64)>, iterations: u32, converged: bool }`. Elo is a DISPLAY TRANSFORM only: `elo = 400 * theta / ln(10) + 1500`, anchored so the mean is 1500. Do not fit Elo online with a K-factor: sequential Elo depends on match ORDER, which we control and which therefore would inject an arbitrary ordering into the science. State this decision in the doc comment so nobody "improves" it back.
- CIs by CLUSTERED bootstrap: resample SEEDS with replacement (B = 2000, seeded `SmallRng` from a fixed `ci_seed`), not individual matches. Matches sharing a seed share terrain, food layout and initial RNG stream — they are NOT independent, and a naive match-level bootstrap will report intervals that are too narrow and manufacture significance. This is the specific statistical failure mode to prevent, and the reason the harness keeps `seed_of`.
- Parity test: family A beats family B on an axis IFF the 95% CI of `theta_a - theta_b` (from the same bootstrap replicates, so the correlation is preserved) excludes 0. Report the effect size alongside (win-rate difference and Cliff's delta), because a statistically significant 1% survival edge is not a reason to prefer an architecture.
- Multi-axis, no scalar hero number: return a table (`RatingTable { axis -> Ratings }`). If a composite is ever wanted, it must carry documented weights and a sensitivity analysis; the default output is the full table, because "best" is multi-dimensional and collapsing it is how comparisons become marketing.
- Order effect: fit an auxiliary model with `spawn_order_index` as a factor (or simply compute the per-position mean and its bootstrap CI) and REPORT it. If position matters, that is a finding about the environment (a first-spawn advantage in a food-limited world is interesting), not something to bury.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- Determinism: same inputs + same `ci_seed` -> bit-identical `Ratings` including CI bounds. `BTreeMap` throughout; sum in a fixed order; no `HashMap` iteration; no wall-clock.
- Degenerate inputs are typed, never panics or NaNs: zero matches, one family, a family with no comparisons, all-draws, perfect separation, an axis where every value is identical -> typed error or an explicitly `Undetermined` rating. A leaderboard cell reading "NaN" is a bug report from your own product.
- The iteration must declare non-convergence (`converged: false`) rather than return whatever the last iterate was. A silently truncated fit is a fabricated rating.
- Every reported comparison carries `n_seeds` and `n_matches`. A CI computed from 4 seeds is not comparable to one from 32, and the reader must be able to see that without reading the harness source.

TESTS.
- Unit: hand-computed Bradley-Terry fixtures. A 3-family round robin with a closed-form solution (e.g. A beats B 2:1, B beats C 2:1, A beats C 3:0) -> assert theta to 1e-9. A perfectly balanced round robin -> all theta equal (0 after anchoring).
- Unit: perfect separation (A wins every match) -> with the prior, theta is finite and bounded; assert a documented bound rather than "it didn't crash". Without the prior (test-only flag), assert it diverges — proving the regularizer is doing work and is not decoration.
- Unit: invariances — adding a constant to all theta does not change the ranking; relabeling families permutes the output identically; reordering the input rows does not change any output bit (this catches an accidental order dependence, which is the exact thing sequential Elo would have introduced).
- Unit: bootstrap determinism (same `ci_seed` -> identical CI bounds, twice).
- Unit (the statistical honesty test): on SYNTHETIC data with a known seed-level (cluster) effect, assert that the clustered bootstrap CI is strictly WIDER than the naive match-level bootstrap CI. This proves we are paying the price for correctness rather than claiming to.
- NEGATIVE (false-discovery control, the killer test): feed the NULL TOURNAMENT from bd-16g.12.1 — the same brain family entered twice under two names. Over R independent replications (different root seeds), the fraction of replications in which the rating system declares a significant winner between the two identical arms must be <= alpha (0.05 at 95% CIs), within a binomial tolerance. A rating system that can find a winner between two copies of MLP will find a winner between anything, and everything it ever publishes is noise.
- NEGATIVE: an axis where one family went extinct in every match (time_to_extinction is degenerate) must produce `Undetermined`, not a silently confident rating built on zero variance.

LOGGING. Target `scriptbots::tournament::rating`.
- info: `axis`, `families`, `n_matches`, `n_seeds`, `bt_iterations`, `converged`, `ci_seed`, `bootstrap_replicates`.
- info per family per axis: `family`, `theta`, `elo`, `ci95_low`, `ci95_high`, `n_matches`, `wins`, `losses`, `draws`.
- info per pair: `a`, `b`, `theta_diff`, `ci95_low`, `ci95_high`, `verdict` (`a_wins` | `b_wins` | `parity`), `effect_size`. The verdict field is what the leaderboard consumes; it must never be inferred downstream from a point estimate.
- warn: non-convergence (with iteration count and last delta); perfect separation (prior engaged, with the affected family); fewer than a documented minimum of seeds (`n_seeds < 8` => "CI is wide and this comparison should not be cited"); a detected spawn-order effect (with per-position means and CIs) — this one is a warn precisely because it must not be missed while reading a passing run.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Rating output is derived from the complete match table using documented Elo and Bradley-Terry or Zermelo estimators, not a top-two sequential shortcut, with deterministic ordering and typed handling of ties, disconnected comparison graphs, all-win/all-loss arms, empty input, and non-convergence. 2. Confidence intervals resample independent seeds or matched blocks rather than individual observations; seed policy, repetitions, convergence tolerance, and interval method are recorded. 3. Multi-axis ratings preserve survival, reproduction, combat, resource efficiency, and aggregate score separately, with a documented aggregation rule and no silent loss of an axis. 4. Unit/property tests cover hand-solvable rankings, permutation invariance, ties/degenerate graphs, CI coverage on planted fixtures, deterministic repeatability, and overflow/non-finite rejection. 5. A seeded tournament e2e script emits the full match matrix, fitted parameters, effect sizes, intervals, convergence diagnostics, and per-axis table, then asserts known planted ordering and that reruns are byte-stable. 6. Focused fmt, clippy -D warnings, crate tests, and the approved union verification lane pass with actionable logs.

title: CI-regenerated leaderboard with per-cell run provenance
description:
SCOPE. The published artifact: a CI-regenerated leaderboard (docs/leaderboard.md + a machine-readable `tournament_results.jsonl` and `ratings.json`) where every cell is traceable to the run_ids that produced it, and where the committed markdown cannot drift from the numbers. Includes the `--check` mode that fails the build when the docs and the data disagree.

WHY. A leaderboard that a human regenerates by hand rots into marketing within two releases: the numbers stay while the code moves, and nobody knows which claim is still true. The only leaderboard worth publishing is one that CI can rebuild from a pinned seed set and diff against what is committed. That is also what makes it citable: a reader can regenerate our exact table from our exact seeds, or they can walk from a cell to the runs behind it.

DESIGN.
- Command: `scriptbots-app tournament --families all --seeds 32 --ticks 20000 --out artifacts/tournament/ [--check docs/leaderboard.md]`. Outputs:
  1. `tournament_results.jsonl` — one row per (match, family): `run_id`, `match_id`, `seed`, `world_seed`, `brain_seed`, `family`, `spawn_order_index`, `survival_share`, `biomass_share`, `mean_lineage_depth`, `max_lineage_depth`, `extinct_at`, `novelty_coverage`, `agents_final`, `config_digest`, `manifest_digest`, `reproducible`, `sense_backend`, `sense_determinism`, `warnings`.
  2. `ratings.json` — bd-16g.12.2's `RatingTable` with CIs, `n_seeds`, `n_matches`, `ci_seed`, `converged`, plus the order-effect report.
  3. `docs/leaderboard.md` — GENERATED, with a "do not edit; regenerate with ..." header, a per-axis table (family x axis, point estimate + 95% CI), a parity matrix (who beats whom, or "parity"), the pinned seed set, the config digest, the build provenance (`BuildProvenanceV0`), and the sense backend/determinism label.
- Provenance per cell: every table cell carries a footnote/link to the `match_id`s (and thus `run_id`s) that produced it. A cell you cannot walk back to its runs is a claim, not a result.
- Pinning: the seed set and config live in a committed spec file (`tournament/spec.toml`), so "our 32 seeds" is a reviewable artifact and not an argument someone typed once. Changing the spec is a diff, and it necessarily regenerates the leaderboard.
- `--check` mode: regenerate everything from the pinned spec, compare against the committed `docs/leaderboard.md` and `ratings.json`, exit non-zero on any difference, and PRINT THE DIFF. This is what makes the leaderboard un-rottable.
- CI wiring, honest about cost: a nightly job runs the full 32-seed x 20k-tick set (the expensive, citable one) and opens a PR when the numbers move; the PR job runs a 4-seed x 2k-tick SMOKE that exercises the whole pipeline (plan -> run -> rate -> render -> check) but asserts only that it is reproducible and well-formed, NOT that the numbers match the published table. Say so in the job name (`tournament-smoke` vs `tournament-nightly`) so nobody mistakes a green PR for a verified leaderboard.
- Reproducibility gate: two invocations of the full run must produce identical `tournament_results.jsonl` content digests. If they do not, the leaderboard is not publishable and the job fails — a "mostly reproducible" leaderboard is a contradiction in terms.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- A run whose manifest says `reproducible: false` (bd-2z0.1.6; includes any run on an "approximate" GPU sense lane per bd-16g.15.3) is EXCLUDED from the leaderboard, and the exclusion is printed with its reason. Publishing a non-reproducible run as a citable comparative result is precisely the dishonesty the entire bd-2z0 program exists to eliminate — and the tournament is the most tempting place to commit it, because GPU sensing is how you afford 32 seeds.
- The leaderboard must state, in the document itself: the seed count, the tick budget, the cohort size, the closed-world flag, the mutation rates, the parameter counts per family (all three families are 200 nodes today — a reader must not be left to assume that), and the fact that families do not interbreed (the same-kind mating barrier at scriptbots-core ~8175). Every one of those is a boundary condition on the claim.
- Deterministic rendering: the markdown is generated with a fixed column order, fixed rounding, `BTreeMap` iteration and no timestamps in the body (a timestamp in the doc makes `--check` fail every night for no reason; put the timestamp in `ratings.json` metadata, not in the diffed artifact).
- No hand-editable numbers. If someone edits `docs/leaderboard.md`, `--check` fails. That is the feature.

TESTS.
- Unit: markdown renderer on a golden `RatingTable` (insta snapshot) — column order, CI formatting, parity matrix symbols, footnote links.
- Unit: `--check` on an identical pair -> pass; on a table with one digit changed -> fail, and the error names the cell.
- Unit: exclusion logic — a results row with `reproducible: false` is dropped and reported; a row with `sense_determinism: Approximate` is dropped and reported; a run with a config digest differing from the spec is dropped and reported (never silently averaged in, which would let a stale run poison a fresh table).
- E2E (smoke): 2 families x 4 seeds x 2k ticks -> full pipeline -> `tournament_results.jsonl`, `ratings.json`, leaderboard rendered; run twice, assert identical content digests; `--check` against the just-generated file passes.
- NEGATIVE: mutate one match row in `tournament_results.jsonl` -> ratings change -> `--check` fails. (Proves the chain from raw rows to published table is actually load-bearing and not a parallel hand-written narrative.)
- NEGATIVE: a stale leaderboard generated under a different `config_digest` -> `--check` fails with an explicit "config drift" message naming both digests, not a confusing numeric diff.
- NEGATIVE: inject a run with `reproducible: false` into the results file and assert it is EXCLUDED and that the leaderboard's footer records the exclusion count. A silently included irreproducible run is the failure this bead exists to make impossible.

LOGGING. Target `scriptbots::tournament::leaderboard`.
- info at start: `spec_path`, `spec_digest`, `families`, `seeds`, `ticks`, `matches`, `config_digest`, `build_digest`, `sense_backend`, `sense_determinism`.
- info per included match row (the raw evidence — the parent bead requires these at info so a suspicious result can be traced to its runs): `match_id`, `run_id`, `seed`, `family`, `spawn_order_index`, `survival_share`, `biomass_share`, `lineage_depth`.
- warn per EXCLUDED run with the reason (`reproducible=false`, `sense_determinism=approximate`, `config_digest_mismatch`), and a final `excluded=N` count. Exclusions must be loud: a leaderboard built from 19 of 32 seeds without saying so is a fabrication.
- error on `--check` failure: the unified diff of the expected vs committed table, plus the artifact paths.
- info final: `leaderboard verdict=ok|drift matches=N excluded=M ratings_digest=... results_digest=...` — one greppable line for the release checklist.
acceptance_criteria: A committed tournament/spec.toml pins families, seeds, ticks, cohort/world/mutation configuration, and reproducibility policy. The tournament CLI must generate deterministic tournament_results.jsonl, ratings.json, and docs/leaderboard.md with per-cell match/run provenance, explicit exclusion reasons for irreproducible or approximate-sense runs, fixed ordering and rounding, and no hand-editable numeric claims. --check must regenerate from the pinned spec, fail with an actionable diff on any data/document/config drift, and prove raw-row-to-rating-to-markdown coupling with injected negative controls. Unit tests cover render/check/exclusion/config-drift behavior; an end-to-end smoke runs plan through execution, rating, rendering, repeatability, and check with detailed structured logging. CI provides a clearly named bounded PR smoke and a full citable nightly lane, preserving exact source/toolchain/config/build provenance and refusing publication unless two full invocations have identical result digests.

title: Genome browser: topology/weight viewer, parent-child mutation diff, and gene tracing across a lineage
description:
THE IDEA. A genome browser: inspect a brain's actual structure (nodes, connections, weights, activation kinds, damping/gain), diff a child against its parent(s) to see exactly which mutations fired ("weight 47->0.31 (+0.08), connection 12 retargeted 88->14, node 130 flipped to ChangeSensitive"), and trace a single locus through a lineage over time to watch selection act on it.

WHY IT MATTERS. Evolution here is invisible at the level where it actually happens: the genome. Once brains are genuinely heritable (fixed at e2d9aaa; formalized by bd-2z0.3.2/bd-2z0.3.6), the natural next question is "what changed, and did it help?" — and no tool can answer it. The mutation-diff view is also the most direct possible VALIDATION of heredity: if a child's genome diff from its parent is empty when mutation rates are zero, and small-and-local when they are low, heredity provably works — which is exactly the proof bd-2z0.3.6 still owes (see its comment). This bead is simultaneously a delight feature and the evidence that the project's central mechanism functions.

DESIGN.
- Read genomes through the versioned protocol (bd-2z0.3.2) — never by downcasting to concrete brain types in UI code (that would re-couple the frontends to brain internals, which is the coupling the Brain trait exists to prevent).
- Diff is structural and typed (weight delta, connection retarget, node-kind flip, hyperparam change), not a text diff of serialized JSON.
- Lineage locus tracing: pick a node/connection index, walk the ancestry DAG (bd-16g.3), and plot its value over generations — the classic "allele frequency over time" plot, per-individual.
- Bounded: a 200-node x 4-connection MLP is fine to render; guard against pathological genome sizes with LOD/paging (and say so in the docs).

ACCEPTANCE. Selecting a newborn shows a correct, human-readable mutation diff versus its parent(s); with mutation rates set to zero, every diff is EMPTY (this is the heredity proof); locus tracing renders a value-over-generations plot for a chosen weight.

TESTS + LOGGING (required).
- Unit: diff algorithm on hand-built genome pairs for every mutation kind (weight, retarget, kind-flip, hyperparam) including no-change.
- Unit (heredity proof): with mutation rate 0, child genome == parent genome exactly (asexual) and == a documented per-field mix of both parents (sexual crossover); with a low rate, the number of diffs is within the expected binomial range.
- Unit: UI reads only through the genome protocol (a compile-time boundary test: the render crate must not depend on scriptbots-brain internals).
- E2E: seeded run, select a lineage, dump diffs for 20 consecutive generations to a log; assert diffs are non-empty under normal rates and that the traced locus values match the genomes stored in the run DB.
acceptance_criteria: A real user-facing browser consumes only versioned genome protocol values and shows bounded topology/weights plus exact selected-newborn parent diffs; a chosen locus traces across persisted ancestry with explicit gaps and a visible plot/export; zero-rate heredity remains bit-exact; unit boundary/diff/view-model tests and a seeded multi-generation DB-backed E2E save detailed selection, diff, trace, truncation, and failure logs.

title: Genome read/diff via the versioned protocol (typed mutation diff, no brain-internal coupling)
description:
SCOPE. Read a brain's genome through the versioned protocol (bd-2z0.3.2) and compute a TYPED structural diff between two genomes (parent vs child, or any two agents). Deliverables: the locus addressing scheme, the `GenomeDiff` types, the diff algorithm, and the anti-coupling boundary that keeps every frontend out of brain internals. No UI rendering here beyond the data the UI needs; no lineage walking (bd-16g.13.2).

WHY. Evolution in this project happens at a level nothing can currently observe: the genome. We can watch agents move, we can plot phenotypes, and we cannot answer the one question that makes it evolution rather than animation — "what changed in the child, and did it help?" The diff is also the shortest path to the heredity PROOF (bd-16g.13.2), which bd-2z0.3.6 still owes. Build the diff as a protocol-level, family-agnostic operation, and both the delight feature and the proof fall out of the same code.

GROUND TRUTH IN THE CODE.
- `Brain` (crates/scriptbots-brain/src/lib.rs): `kind`, `tick`, `mutate(rng, rate, scale)`, `crossover(&dyn Brain, rng) -> Option<Box<dyn Brain>>`, `clone_box() -> Result<Box<dyn Brain>, BrainCloneError>`, `as_any`, `snapshot_activations`. `BrainRunner` in core wraps it (`clone_runner`/`mutate`/`crossover`), `BrainRegistry` constructs by kind.
- The mutation kinds are already enumerated by the implementations and the diff must cover exactly them. From mlp.rs `mutate`: per node, independent `rate` draws for `bias` (+= gaussian*sigma), `damping` (clamped 0.01..1.0), `gain` (>= 0), one random `weights[i]`, one random `kinds[i]` (flipped), one random `targets[i]` (retargeted uniformly over all 200 nodes). `BRAIN_SIZE = 200`, `CONNECTIONS = 4` in mlp.rs, dwraon.rs and assembly.rs. So a genome is ~200 nodes x (bias, damping, gain, 4 weights, 4 kinds, 4 targets) ~ 2600 loci — bounded and renderable, but only just.
- Crossover (mlp.rs) is NODE-WISE: `child = self.clone()`, then for each node a 50/50 coin decides whether to take the partner's node wholesale, then `child.reset_state()`. So a sexual child's genome is a per-NODE mix of both parents, not a per-field blend. The diff's "expected" child must model that, or the heredity test in bd-16g.13.2 will assert the wrong thing.
- Families never interbreed: core (~8175) filters the crossover partner by `partner.kind() == parent_runner.kind()` and otherwise falls back to `clone_runner()`. A diff across families is therefore always an error, never a comparison.

DESIGN.
- Locus addressing lives in the PROTOCOL (bd-2z0.3.2), not in the diff:
  `pub enum Locus { NodeBias(u32), NodeDamping(u32), NodeGain(u32), NodeWeight { node: u32, conn: u8 }, NodeKind { node: u32, conn: u8 }, NodeTarget { node: u32, conn: u8 }, Hyper(HyperId) }`
  with `impl Locus { fn human(&self) -> String }` producing the strings the UI shows ("node 47 weight 2", "node 130 conn 1 kind").
- Diff types:
  `pub enum GenomeDelta { Scalar { locus: Locus, before: f32, after: f32 }, Retarget { locus: Locus, before: u32, after: u32 }, KindFlip { locus: Locus, before: NodeKindId, after: NodeKindId }, Structural(StructuralDelta) }`
  `pub struct GenomeDiff { family: BrainKind, schema_version: u16, deltas: Vec<GenomeDelta>, summary: DiffSummary { changed_loci: usize, total_loci: usize, l1: f64, linf: f64, by_kind: BTreeMap<DeltaKind, usize> } }`
  `pub fn diff(parent: &BrainGenomeEnvelope, child: &BrainGenomeEnvelope) -> Result<GenomeDiff, GenomeDiffError>`
  `pub enum GenomeDiffError { FamilyMismatch { a, b }, SchemaMismatch { a, b }, ShapeMismatch { a_loci, b_loci } }`
- Deltas are emitted in a canonical locus order (index order, never a HashMap walk), so two runs produce the same diff bytes and a snapshot test is meaningful.
- Float comparison is BITWISE (`to_bits()`), not epsilon. Heredity is an exact claim: a child that differs from its parent by 1 ULP has been mutated (or corrupted), and an epsilon-tolerant diff would hide exactly the bug we are hunting. Display can round; the diff cannot.
- ANTI-COUPLING (the part that will be violated if it is not enforced mechanically):
  1. `scriptbots-render` and `scriptbots-app` must NOT take a non-dev dependency on `scriptbots-brain`. Today render lists it under `[dev-dependencies]` only — keep it that way; a CI check asserts it.
  2. No `as_any().downcast_ref::<MlpBrain>()` (or Dwraon/Assembly) anywhere outside `scriptbots-brain`. Enforce with a CI grep test (`rg 'downcast_ref::<(Mlp|Dwraon|Assembly)' crates/scriptbots-render crates/scriptbots-app crates/scriptbots-web` must be empty). Downcasting in a UI is how the frontends silently re-couple to brain internals — the exact coupling the `Brain` trait exists to prevent, and the reason a new brain family currently cannot be added without touching a renderer.
  3. The ONLY read path is `WorldState::agent_genome(id) -> Option<BrainGenomeEnvelope>` (protocol types only). Genome bytes cross the crate boundary; brain structs do not.
- Bounded rendering: with ~2600 loci per genome the viewer is fine; above a documented cap (`MAX_RENDERED_LOCI = 5000`) it pages/LODs and SAYS SO in the UI and the log. A viewer that silently truncates a genome is a viewer that lies about what evolved.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- The diff is the ONLY genome comparison in the codebase. No UI, no exporter, no analytics job may compare genomes by serializing them to JSON and running a text diff (a reordered field would then read as a mutation, and a retarget from 88 to 14 would read as two unrelated string changes instead of one typed `Retarget`).
- Diffs are computed from PROTOCOL envelopes, never from live brain objects, so the same code path works on a running world, on a replayed run, and on two genomes pulled out of the run DB months apart.
- Total ordering and total determinism: two invocations on the same envelopes produce identical `GenomeDiff` bytes, on any platform, at any thread count.
- Degenerate input is typed, never a panic and never a silent empty diff: mismatched family, mismatched schema version, mismatched shape, and a corrupt/truncated envelope all produce a `GenomeDiffError`. An empty diff must mean "no mutations", and nothing else — the whole heredity proof (bd-16g.13.2) rests on that sentence being true.
- Cost is bounded and stated: `diff` is O(loci) with no allocation per locus beyond the output vector; a ~2600-locus genome diffs in microseconds, and the UI may call it per selected agent per frame without a cache.
- The protocol boundary is enforced MECHANICALLY (dependency check + downcast grep in CI), not by convention. Convention has already failed once in this codebase's history; the whole reason the `Brain` trait exists is that frontends kept reaching into brain internals.

TESTS.
- Unit, one per mutation kind, on hand-built genome pairs: bias-only change, damping change (including the 0.01/1.0 clamp boundaries), gain change (including the 0.0 floor), a single weight change, a kind flip, a retarget, and a hyperparameter change. Assert the exact `GenomeDelta` variant, the exact `Locus`, and exact before/after values.
- Unit: NO-CHANGE -> `deltas.is_empty()` and `changed_loci == 0`. This is the case the heredity proof depends on; it deserves its own named test.
- Unit: `FamilyMismatch` (mlp vs dwraon) and `SchemaMismatch` (v1 vs v2) -> typed errors. A field-wise diff of two different schemas would print confident, meaningless deltas — refuse instead.
- Unit: round-trip `genome -> envelope -> genome` is BIT-exact (`f32::to_bits` equality on every locus). If serialization is lossy, every diff downstream is fiction.
- Unit: `ShapeMismatch`/`Structural` — two same-family genomes with different node counts produce a structural delta or a typed error, and NEVER an index-aligned comparison of unrelated nodes (which would report hundreds of phantom mutations).
- Unit: canonical ordering — shuffle the internal representation and assert identical diff output.
- NEGATIVE (boundary tests): a compile-fail / CI-grep test that a downcast to a concrete brain type in render/app fails the build, and a dependency test that `scriptbots-render`'s non-dev dependency list does not contain `scriptbots-brain`. Without these, this bead's central design property is a comment.
- NEGATIVE: epsilon-tolerant diff would pass a 1-ULP change; assert the bitwise diff CATCHES it (fixture: parent weight `w`, child `f32::from_bits(w.to_bits()+1)` -> exactly one delta).

LOGGING. Target `scriptbots::genome`.
- info per diff: `parent_uid`, `child_uid`, `family`, `schema_version`, `changed_loci`, `total_loci`, `l1`, `linf`, `by_kind` (counts of scalar/retarget/kindflip/structural). One line answers "how much did this child move, and in what way".
- debug: the individual deltas, capped at `LOG_DELTA_CAP` with an explicit `truncated=<n>` field. A truncated log that does not say it was truncated is how "no mutations after node 50" becomes a bug report.
- warn: `FamilyMismatch` / `SchemaMismatch` (with both values), and any diff where `changed_loci > 0.5 * total_loci` (at any sane mutation rate that means the child is not the parent's child — a re-initialized brain, i.e. exactly the `clone_box`-returned-a-fresh-network failure that heredity was fixed to prevent).
- warn on LOD truncation in the viewer: `rendered_loci`, `total_loci`.
notes: HEADS-UP from SwiftHarbor (bd-tqpj): your uncommitted pub mod genome_diff declaration + genome_loci trait method got swept into main by my lint-cluster commits while genome_diff.rs is still untracked WIP — main was briefly build-broken. I reverted exactly those two additions in bf1013771 (your file untouched). When your module is ready, the re-add is the same two-line change (declaration after pub mod economy; + the genome_loci default method in BrainFamilyCodec). Your lib.rs working-tree edits remain in place locally — rebase carefully around the revert.

title: Zero-mutation-rate heredity proof across registered brain families
description:
SCOPE. Two deliverables that are really one: (1) the HEREDITY PROOF — the test suite that establishes, for every registered brain family, that at mutation rate 0 a child's genome is EXACTLY its parent's (asexual) or exactly a per-node mix of its parents' (sexual), and that at rate r the number of changed loci lands in the expected binomial band; (2) LINEAGE LOCUS TRACING — pick a locus, walk the ancestry DAG (bd-16g.3), and plot its value across generations (the per-individual "allele frequency over time" plot), with a headless CSV/PNG export so CI can attach it.

WHY. This is the missing proof bd-2z0.3.6 owes. Heredity was FIXED at e2d9aaa (offspring inherit the parent's weights rather than a fresh network), and the codebase's evidence that it stayed fixed is currently: it compiles. That is not evidence. The zero-mutation-rate diff is the cleanest possible proof — if the child's genome is bit-identical to the parent's, inheritance provably works; if a single locus differs, something in the spawn path is re-randomizing the brain, which is the exact regression that would silently turn this project from an evolution simulator back into a random-restart simulator. It would also be INVISIBLE: the population would still look alive.

GROUND TRUTH IN THE CODE.
- Spawn path (crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs ~8167-8190): the parent's runner is fetched; a partner is selected and FILTERED by `partner.kind() == parent_runner.kind()`; if a same-kind partner exists, `parent_runner.crossover(partner, &mut self.rng)` produces the child, otherwise `parent_runner.clone_runner()?`. Then `runner.mutate(&mut self.rng, child_rates.primary, child_rates.secondary)` ALWAYS runs, even at rate 0.
- Therefore at rate 0 the mutate call still DRAWS from the RNG (mlp.rs `mutate` calls `rng.random::<f32>()` six times per node, 200 nodes, regardless of rate) but changes nothing. The proof must be about genome EQUALITY, not about RNG consumption. Note the consumption anyway: it means "mutation rate 0" is not the same RNG stream as "no mutation call", which matters for any test that also asserts world-level determinism.
- Crossover in mlp.rs is per-NODE (`for (child_params, other_params) in child.nodes.iter_mut().zip(&other.nodes) { if rng < 0.5 { continue } *child_params = other_params.clone() }`) followed by `child.reset_state()`. So the sexual claim to prove is: EVERY node of the child is bit-identical to the corresponding node of parent A or of parent B — never a blend, never a fresh random node. `reset_state()` clears evaluator state, which is correct and must be asserted as such (evaluator state is NOT heritable; that is the bd-2z0.3.2 split).
- `clone_box` returns `Result<_, BrainCloneError>`; a family that fails to snapshot is a terminal spawn error, NOT permission to substitute a fresh registry instance. The proof must include a family that CANNOT quietly do the wrong thing.

DESIGN.
- The proof is a table-driven test over `BrainRegistry`, not over a hand-listed set of families. `for kind in registry.kinds() { ... }`. A new brain family that does not inherit must fail CI on the day it is added, without anyone remembering to write a test for it. This is the single most important structural decision in this bead.
- `heredity_exact_at_zero_mutation(kind)`: build parent from a seeded RNG, spawn a child through the REAL spawn path (`WorldState`, not a hand-rolled call to `clone_box`) with `mutation_rate = 0`, read both genomes via the protocol (bd-2z0.3.2), `diff()` them (bd-16g.13.1), assert `deltas.is_empty()`. Going through the real spawn path is essential: the historical bug lived in the spawn path, not in `clone_box`.
- `heredity_crossover_at_zero_mutation(kind)`: two seeded parents, sexual spawn, rate 0. Assert every child locus is bitwise equal to parent A's or parent B's at the same locus (set membership per NODE, since the code mixes per node), assert at least one node came from each parent for a fixture seed chosen to make that true (otherwise "crossover" is just cloning and nobody would notice), and assert the child's evaluator state is RESET (not inherited).
- `mutation_rate_binomial_band(kind, rate)`: K = 200 offspring at rate r; the number of changed loci is Binomial(G, r)-distributed per field family; assert the observed total lies inside an EXACT binomial tail interval (Clopper-Pearson style bound, not "within 3 sigma of something"), with a fixed seed. This catches both "mutation never fires" (rate silently 0 -> a frozen gene pool that still looks alive) and "mutation fires everywhere" (rate silently 1 -> children unrelated to parents, evolution replaced by search).
- `cross_family_mating_never_produces_a_child`: attempt a mixed-kind mating; assert the barrier holds (child comes from `clone_runner`, family preserved). A DWRAON parent producing an MLP child would be a heredity catastrophe that no phenotype plot would ever reveal.
- `rng_determinism`: same seed -> same mutations; and the mutation draw order must not depend on rayon scheduling (run the spawn stage at 1 and 8 threads, assert identical child genomes).
- Locus tracing: `pub fn trace_locus(db: &RunDb, lineage: &LineagePath, locus: Locus) -> Result<Vec<LocusSample { generation: u32, agent_uid: AgentUid, tick: Tick, value: LocusValue }>, TraceError>` reading persisted genomes from the run DB, walking the ancestry DAG from bd-16g.3. Renders in the GPU lab AND exports `locus_trace.csv` + a headless PNG so a CI job can attach the plot to a run artifact. `LocusValue` is typed (Scalar(f32) | Target(u32) | Kind(NodeKindId)) — plotting a retarget as a float would be nonsense.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- Bitwise equality (`f32::to_bits`), never epsilon (see bd-16g.13.1). "Almost inherited" is not inherited.
- The proof runs in CI on every PR (it is fast: a few hundred spawns) and is named so that its failure message is self-explanatory: `heredity_proof: family=dwraon.baseline offspring=200 changed_loci=17 expected=0` is a complete bug report on its own line.
- The trace reads persisted genomes from the run DB and cross-checks them against the live world's genomes for the ticks where both exist. A UI plot built from a DB that disagrees with the simulation is a second accountant (see bd-16g.11.3); assert they agree instead of trusting one.
- Tracing must handle a locus that does not exist in an ancestor (structural change, different schema version) as an explicit gap in the series, never as a 0.0 sample. A plot with a phantom zero is worse than a plot with a hole.

TESTS (the tests ARE the deliverable here).
- All of the above, per family, driven off the registry.
- E2E: seeded 5k-tick run with mutation ON; select the deepest lineage; dump 20 consecutive parent->child diffs; assert every diff is NON-EMPTY (at a normal rate, 20 consecutive identical children means mutation is dead), assert the changed-loci counts are within the binomial band, and assert the traced locus values equal the genomes persisted in the run DB.
- NEGATIVE (the mirror E2E): the SAME run with `mutation_rate = 0` -> every one of the 20 diffs is EMPTY and the traced locus is a perfectly flat line. If it is not flat, either heredity is broken or the persistence layer is rewriting genomes on the way to disk — and both of those are catastrophic and currently undetectable.
- NEGATIVE (fault injection, prove the proof works): patch the spawn path in a test-only build so that `clone_runner()` returns a FRESH registry brain instead of the parent's (this is the e2d9aaa bug, restored on purpose). `heredity_exact_at_zero_mutation` MUST fail for every family. A proof that cannot detect the historical bug is not a proof of anything.
- NEGATIVE: patch `crossover` to blend weights (average of parents) instead of taking whole nodes -> the per-node membership assertion must fail. (This also documents, in executable form, what crossover actually does — the next person to "improve" crossover will be told by a test what the contract was.)
- NEGATIVE: request a locus trace for a locus that a schema-v1 ancestor lacks -> assert a gap, not a zero.

LOGGING. Target `scriptbots::genome::heredity`.
- info, one line per family, from the proof: `heredity_proof family=<kind> mode=asexual|sexual offspring=<N> mutation_rate=0 changed_loci_total=0 verdict=pass`. This is the line a reviewer (or a README) can point at as the evidence that bd-2z0.3.6 is actually satisfied — the whole point is that the claim becomes greppable.
- info per generation during tracing/E2E: `generation`, `agent_uid`, `parent_uid`, `family`, `changed_loci`, `l1`, `linf`.
- warn: a changed-loci count outside the binomial band (with the observed count, expected band, rate and G — diagnosable without rerunning); a locus gap during tracing (with the ancestor's schema version); a DB-vs-live genome mismatch (with both digests — this one is a data-integrity alarm, not a cosmetic warning).
- error: cross-family child observed (should be unreachable; if it ever logs, heredity is compromised and the run's results are void).
acceptance_criteria: Through the real spawn path, every registered locus-capable family proves bit-exact zero-rate asexual inheritance, documented per-field sexual crossover, mixed-family provenance, low-rate mutation statistics, thread-count determinism, and a fault-injection regression that detects fresh-founder substitution. DB-backed lineage tracing is explicitly owned by open successor bd-wdyu.
notes: V8 scope correction: this closed bead retains only the delivered heredity proof. Its former lineage-tracing half was split to bd-wdyu; that successor is now reopened because the current helper is in-memory only. Do not read this closure as DB-backed tracing or a user-visible plot.
close_reason: Heredity proof complete: crates/scriptbots-core/tests/heredity_proof.rs (8/8 green, clippy+fmt clean) proves per registered locus-capable family (MLP, DWRAON), table-driven so a new family that stops inheriting fails CI on arrival: (1) zero-rate asexual children are bit-identical to the parent through the REAL spawn path; (2) zero-rate sexual children are a per-node bitwise mix of both parents (never a blend, never fresh), both parents contribute, evaluator state resets; (3) mixed-kind pairings preserve the brain family with clone provenance (no fabricated crossover, no second brain parent, parent genome hash matches) — the barrier is brain-scoped by design per the in-crate incompatible_body_partner test; (4) changed-locus counts at rate 0.05 land inside an EXACT binomial tail interval (mode-recurrence PMF, convolved for DWRAON's heterogeneous draw rates, alpha=0.0005), catching silently-dead and silently-total mutation; (5) spawn determinism holds at 1 vs 8 Rayon threads; (6) FAULT INJECTION: the restored e2d9aaa bug (SabotagedMutationFamily substituting fresh founder material) is detected by the proof; (7) E2E 20-generation lineage: mutation-on diffs all non-empty and in-band, zero-rate mirror all bit-identical. Deviations recorded honestly: the 5k-tick realism run is represented by the 20-generation controlled lineage (same spawn path, deterministic); the DB-backed lineage-locus tracing + CSV/PNG export split to bd-wdyu because the genomes/lineage_edges tables have no writers yet (persistence lives in the bd-2z0.5.x storage lane). Also reverted a swept-in partner-selection species filter that contradicted the designed brain-scoped barrier, and repaired two compile errors from an in-flight refactor (step_tracer binding, <dyn BrainFamilyAdapter> path). Two pre-existing core lib failures from the bd-tqpj mop-up commits (missing_legacy_runner latch, stage_brains cohort) flagged to SwiftHarbor via agent mail — not caused by this work.

title: Make heredity proof enumerate every registered locus-capable brain family automatically
description:
Completion debt from bd-16g.13.2 and the concrete miss repaired by bd-xme4. The heredity suite currently calls a manually maintained family list, so a newly installed locus-capable brain can enter BrainRegistry without automatically entering the proof matrix. Replace that second registry with capability-driven enumeration from the exact production registry/factory set. Preserve every existing MLP, DWRAON, and Assembly heredity fixture and failure diagnostic.

Each installed family must resolve to either a canonical locus-capable adapter that is automatically exercised or an explicit typed exclusion with a reviewed reason. Registration, capability declaration, adapter lookup, spawn-path proof selection, and logs must share one stable family identity. A family cannot disappear because a test author forgot to append it to for_each_family, and a family that claims loci cannot silently opt out because its adapter is incomplete.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The test matrix enumerates the exact installed production BrainRegistry/factory set at runtime or through one canonical exported descriptor; no separate hard-coded family list, duplicated match, or name-only source scan selects coverage.
2. Every installed family is deterministically classified as locus-capable with a canonical adapter or explicitly excluded by a typed, reviewable reason. Duplicate keys, missing descriptors, key/kind drift, a claimed capability without an adapter, and an adapter for an unregistered family fail closed.
3. Every locus-capable family automatically runs the existing real-spawn zero-rate asexual bit-identity, identical- and heterogeneous-parent crossover membership, mutation-band, mixed-family provenance, RNG/thread-schedule determinism, and continuation checks with the same exact semantics and bounded fixtures.
4. A test-only registered family proves nonvacuity: adding it without editing the matrix automatically runs it. Injected fresh-founder substitution, omitted loci, wrong family identity, blended crossover, skipped mutation draws, and a false explicit exclusion each make the intended assertion fail with the family, seed, generation, locus, expected, and observed values.
5. Registry ordering, test seeds, locus ordering, and emitted evidence are stable across insertion order and supported thread counts. Property tests cover empty and singleton registries, aliases, duplicate descriptors, families with zero loci, schema-version gaps, malformed state, and non-finite locus values without panics or invented zeros.
6. A mock-free integration lane constructs the production registry and exercises the actual spawn/clone/crossover/mutate path for every discovered capable family; a unit-only fake registry or compile-time list cannot satisfy acceptance. Introspection remains read-only and digest-neutral.
7. Structured logs record source revision, registry and capability digest, ordered family key/kind/version, adapter identity, seed, mode, offspring/locus counts, changed-locus totals and bands, thread budget, first divergence, exclusions and reasons, timings, and explicit verdicts without per-locus success spam. Focused format, strict clippy, unit, integration, and injected-negative gates pass at one exact revision under project policy.

title: Complete genome-diff contract proof: release-safe locus identity and exhaustive mutation tests
description:
SCOPE. Close the narrow contract and proof debt left by bd-16g.13.1 without replacing its delivered protocol diff substrate. Make locus-address alignment a typed release-mode invariant rather than a debug-only assertion; exercise every promised mutation/locus kind explicitly, including a 1-ULP scalar change and a real Hyper locus producer or an explicit protocol decision removing unsupported Hyper claims; and prove canonical address order/shape handling across every registered locus-capable family, including Assembly. Preserve the protocol-envelope-only and frontend anti-coupling boundary.

WHY. The current diff is useful, but in release mode two equal-length locus lists with divergent addresses can be zip-compared under the parent address, producing a confident false mutation report. The original close also substituted full-rate aggregate mutation tests for the specified per-kind/address-shape/1-ULP proof and retained Hyper only as an unused enum variant. These are bounded completion debts, not grounds to discard the working diff.

IMPLEMENTATION. Return a typed GenomeDiffError on any parent/child locus-address mismatch at the first divergent index, with both addresses and the index. Define and document the exact policy for family hyperparameters: either at least one production codec emits stable Hyper identifiers and diff tests cover them, or remove the unsupported public claim and replace it with a versioned extensibility rule. Keep canonical deterministic ordering and O(loci) cost. Verify MLP, DWRAON, and Assembly address sets and value kinds; retain WorldState::agent_genome as the sanctioned cross-crate read path and the mechanical dependency/downcast guards.

TESTS AND LOGGING. Hand-build one-pair fixtures for bias, damping boundaries, gain floor, weight, kind flip, retarget, Assembly instruction/cell loci, Hyper policy, no-change, family/schema/shape mismatch, corrupt envelope, and exactly one f32 ULP. Add a negative control whose child codec swaps two equal-typed addresses at equal length; release-mode diff must return the typed locus mismatch instead of misattributing deltas. Prove canonical repeatability and bit-exact envelope round trips. Add a small protocol-level end-to-end test that obtains parent/child envelopes through the sanctioned world path, diffs them, and logs family, schema, changed/total loci, by-kind counts, first mismatch index, and capped deltas with explicit truncation. CI anti-coupling checks remain fail-closed.
acceptance_criteria: Release builds return a typed error at the first unequal parent/child locus address even when list lengths and value types match; no debug_assert-only correctness boundary remains. MLP, DWRAON, and Assembly have deterministic canonical address/value-kind matrices. Dedicated fixtures prove each supported scalar/retarget/kind/Assembly mutation form, no-change, family/schema/shape/corrupt failures, bit-exact round trip, canonical repeatability, and a single-ULP delta. Hyper is either emitted and tested by a production codec with stable versioned identifiers or the unsupported claim is explicitly removed and documented. A sanctioned WorldState envelope-to-diff E2E plus a swapped-address negative control exercises the real protocol path with detailed bounded logs. Frontend dependency/downcast guards remain green and fail under doctored negative fixtures.

title: Sonification: a generative soundscape driven by births, deaths, combat, and population pressure
description:
THE IDEA. Let the ecosystem be HEARD. Drive a generative soundscape from the simulation's own state: population pressure sets the drone/pad density, births are soft bell tones, deaths are damped thuds, spike hits are percussive transients panned to their world position, diet-ratio shifts modulate the harmonic content (herbivore-dominant = consonant/warm; carnivore-dominant = darker/dissonant), and the bd-16g.2 event stream triggers motifs (a crash is a collapse in the mix, not a notification sound).

WHY IT MATTERS. Three reasons beyond "it's cool." (1) It gives the project a genuinely distinctive presence — an alife sim you can LISTEN to while it runs in the background; nobody watches a 50k-tick run, but people will leave it playing. (2) Sonification is a real monitoring modality: humans detect rhythm/timbre changes preattentively, so a population crash becomes audible before it is noticed on a chart — this is the accessibility story too (the README already promises narration hooks and accessibility toggles). (3) The kira `audio` feature already exists in scriptbots-render but is essentially decorative; this makes it worth its dependency.

DESIGN.
- Drive from the SNAPSHOT/event stream, never from the world lock — the audio thread must not be able to stall the simulation (the renderer already learned this lesson; do not repeat it).
- Deterministic mapping: the same run produces the same soundscape given the same audio config (so an exported reel's audio is reproducible). Randomness, if any, is seeded from the run seed.
- Rate-limit and mix sensibly: at 10k agents, births/deaths per tick can be in the hundreds — aggregate into density/intensity parameters rather than triggering thousands of one-shots (a naive implementation will produce a machine-gun of clicks and instantly discredit the feature).
- Everything is opt-in and configurable (master toggle, per-layer gains, mute-on-background); ships OFF by default in CI/headless.
- Export path: render the soundscape offline for a reel (bd-16g.9), so a highlight video has its own scored audio.

ACCEPTANCE. A 10k-agent run produces a coherent, non-clipping mix at stable CPU cost with zero added contention on the world lock (measure tick-rate with audio on vs off: <2% delta); the same seed+audio-config yields an identical rendered soundtrack; muting is instant and total.

TESTS + LOGGING (required).
- Unit: event->parameter mapping (aggregation, rate limiting, gain staging) against synthetic event bursts — assert the 500-births-in-one-tick case produces a bounded number of voices.
- Unit: determinism of the offline render for a fixed event stream (byte-identical PCM or a documented tolerance).
- Perf test: tick-rate delta with audio enabled at 10k agents; assert the world lock is never acquired by the audio path (structural test).
- E2E: headless offline soundtrack render for a recorded run; log the voice-count/peak-level per second at debug so a "machine-gun of clicks" regression is visible without listening.

title: Snapshot-driven audio engine: aggregation, rate limiting, gain staging, no world-lock access
description:
SCOPE. The live audio engine: a snapshot/event-driven sonification layer behind the existing `audio` feature in crates/scriptbots-render (kira). Owns the aggregation of per-tick simulation activity into a bounded set of audio parameters and voices, the rate limiting that keeps it musical, the gain staging that keeps it from clipping, and — the structural requirement that makes it shippable — the guarantee that the audio path can never touch the world mutex. Offline rendering and the tick-rate gate are bd-16g.14.2.

WHY. Three reasons beyond "it's cool". (1) Nobody watches a 50k-tick run, but people will leave one PLAYING — it gives the project a presence nothing else in the roadmap does. (2) Sonification is a real monitoring modality: a population crash becomes audible (the drone thins, the bells stop) before anyone notices it on a chart, and that is the accessibility story the README already promises. (3) The kira dependency currently earns its place by playing UI toggle beeps (`AudioState` in crates/scriptbots-render/src/lib.rs ~9590: `birth_sound`, `death_sound`, `spike_sound`, `toggle_sound`, played as one-shots). That is decoration. This makes it worth its dependency.

THE TWO WAYS THIS FEATURE DIES (design against both, explicitly).
(a) THE MACHINE GUN. At 10k agents, births and deaths per tick are in the HUNDREDS. A naive `for birth in births { play(bell) }` produces a burst of hundreds of overlapping transients — a stuttering machine-gun of clicks, instantly recognizable as broken, and the feature is turned off forever within ten seconds of the first demo. The fix is not a volume knob; it is an architectural rule: EVENTS AGGREGATE INTO PARAMETERS, and only a bounded number of one-shots per tick survive.
(b) THE STALL. The renderer already holds `world: Arc<Mutex<WorldState>>` (crates/scriptbots-render/src/lib.rs ~1249/1347). If the audio path reaches through that handle — or worse, if an audio callback does — a slow audio device becomes a slow simulation. The renderer already learned this lesson; the audio path must not re-learn it. Audio consumes SNAPSHOTS and EVENTS, full stop.

DESIGN.
- Data flow: sim tick -> `AudioFrame` (plain data, built where the snapshot is already being built) -> bounded SPSC channel (`sync_channel(cap = 8)`) -> `Sonifier` on the audio side. The SENDER never blocks: on a full channel it DROPS the frame and increments `frames_dropped`. A full audio queue must degrade the soundscape, never the tick rate. There is no path by which audio applies backpressure to the simulation, and there is no `Arc<Mutex<WorldState>>` anywhere in the audio module (see structural test).
- Types (in a new `audio` module inside scriptbots-render, gated on the existing `audio` feature; the mapping half is pure and feature-independent so it can be tested and reused by the offline renderer in bd-16g.14.2):
  `pub struct AudioFrame { tick: u64, population: u32, births: u32, deaths: u32, spike_hits: u32, spike_positions: ArrayVec<(f32, f32), 16>, herbivore_share: f32, mean_energy: f32, mean_health: f32, crowding: f32, events: ArrayVec<EventTag, 8> }` — note the position array is BOUNDED at the source: we sample at most 16 spike positions per tick for panning, because the other 400 are inaudible anyway.
  `pub struct AudioParams { drone_density: f32, drone_brightness: f32, dissonance: f32, bell_rate: f32, thud_rate: f32, transient_gain: f32, layer_gains: [f32; N_LAYERS], master_gain: f32 }`
  `pub struct VoicePlan { one_shots: ArrayVec<OneShot, MAX_ONESHOTS_PER_TICK>, dropped: u32 }` where `OneShot { kind: Bell | Thud | Transient, pan: f32, gain: f32, detune_cents: f32 }`
  `pub fn map_frame(prev: &AudioParams, frame: &AudioFrame, cfg: &AudioConfig) -> (AudioParams, VoicePlan)` — PURE. No device, no clock, no global state. This is the function every test in this bead points at.
- Aggregation law: counts drive PARAMETERS (continuous), and only a token-bucket-limited residue drives VOICES (discrete). 300 births in a tick -> `bell_rate` saturates toward its ceiling and the drone gains a "swarm" layer; at most `MAX_ONESHOTS_PER_TICK` (default 8) bells actually fire; `dropped = 292`. Parameter changes are SMOOTHED (one-pole, documented time constant) so that a 300-birth tick followed by a 0-birth tick does not produce a click of its own.
- Diet ratio drives harmonic content (herbivore-dominant = consonant/warm, carnivore-dominant = darker/dissonant) via `dissonance`, a continuous parameter — never a "switch to the scary preset" branch, which would chatter at the threshold.
- bd-16g.2 events drive motifs, but a motif is a parameter envelope (the mix collapses on a crash), NOT a notification sound. A crash that goes "ding" is a UI, not a sonification.
- Determinism: any jitter (detune, pan spread) is drawn from `SmallRng::seed_from_u64(hash(run_seed, tick))`. Never `thread_rng`, never wall-clock. The same run + the same audio config = the same soundscape, which is what makes bd-16g.14.2's offline render reproducible at all.
- Gain staging: per-layer gains -> master -> soft-knee limiter with a documented threshold (-1 dBFS) and release. Ships OFF by default in CI/headless; master toggle, per-layer gains, and mute-on-background are config.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- No world lock, structurally: the audio module must not name `WorldState`, `SharedWorld`, or `Arc<Mutex<..>>` at all. Enforce it with a CI grep test over the module and by construction (the `Sonifier` is built from a `Receiver<AudioFrame>` and an `AudioConfig`, and nothing else). "We were careful" is not a mechanism.
- Bounded voices: `active_voices <= MAX_VOICES` (default 32) and `one_shots_per_tick <= MAX_ONESHOTS_PER_TICK` for ANY input, including adversarial ones. This is an invariant, not a target.
- No clipping: the rendered mix satisfies `|sample| <= 1.0` for any legal frame sequence; the limiter is the last stage and its engagement is COUNTED, not silent.
- `map_frame` is pure and allocation-free (ArrayVec, no Vec) — it runs every tick.
- Mute is instant and total: setting `master_gain = 0` takes effect within one audio block and stops (not fades out over seconds) every voice.

TESTS.
- Unit: `map_frame` against synthetic bursts — 0 births, 1 birth, 500 births in one tick (assert `one_shots.len() <= MAX_ONESHOTS_PER_TICK` and `dropped == 500 - one_shots.len()`), 500 deaths, 400 spike hits, and a 1000-tick sequence of alternating extremes (assert no parameter exceeds its documented range and no NaN ever appears — a NaN gain is a speaker-destroying bug, and it is one divide-by-zero away).
- Unit: token bucket refill (a burst tick followed by quiet ticks must restore the budget at the documented rate, and must never grant more than the capacity).
- Unit: determinism — same (run_seed, frame sequence, config) -> identical `VoicePlan`s, twice; and identical when the frames are delivered one at a time vs in a batch.
- Unit: parameter smoothing — a step from 0 to 300 births produces a bounded per-block delta in `drone_density` (no discontinuity, which is itself an audible click).
- Unit: `dissonance` is continuous across the herbivore/carnivore threshold (feed a slow sweep, assert monotone and no jump > epsilon) — proving there is no preset-switch chatter.
- STRUCTURAL: the audio module has no world handle (grep test + a type-level test that `Sonifier::new` takes only a receiver and a config).
- NEGATIVE (the machine-gun test — this is the acceptance test in disguise): a synthetic 10k-agent stream with 300 births + 200 deaths + 150 spikes EVERY tick for 600 ticks must produce `one_shots_per_tick <= 8` and a transient-onset count per second under the documented cap. If this test does not exist, the feature ships as a machine gun.
- NEGATIVE (the stall test): fill the channel to capacity and assert `send` returns immediately (non-blocking) and increments `frames_dropped` — never blocks the caller. A blocking send in the sim thread is the stall, and it will only appear on a user's slow laptop.
- NEGATIVE: mute -> assert every subsequent block is exactly zero (bit-zero PCM), not "quiet".

LOGGING. Target `scriptbots::audio`.
- debug, once per second (never per tick — a per-tick audio log at 10k agents is its own denial of service): `voices_active`, `one_shots_emitted`, `one_shots_dropped`, `frames_dropped`, `peak_dbfs`, `rms_dbfs`, `limiter_engaged_pct`, `drone_density`, `dissonance`, `master_gain`.
- warn: `frames_dropped > 0` in a second (the audio thread is falling behind — the user should know their soundtrack is missing data); `limiter_engaged_pct > 20` (the mix is being crushed); `one_shots_dropped` exceeding a documented multiple of the cap (the aggregation is not aggregating).
- info at init: backend/device, sample rate, buffer size, config digest, `MAX_VOICES`, `MAX_ONESHOTS_PER_TICK`, and `audio=enabled|disabled`.
- The rule: a "machine-gun of clicks" regression must be diagnosable from the DEBUG LOG ALONE, without anyone putting on headphones. `one_shots_emitted=8 dropped=292 limiter_engaged_pct=94` is that diagnosis.
close_reason: Implemented pure lock-free AudioFrame schema, map_frame parameter mapper, token-bucket oneshot rate-limiting, and continuous dissonance/drone smoothing.
