title: Deterministic offline soundtrack render for reels + tick-rate impact gate
description:
SCOPE. Two things that must exist before sonification can be claimed: (1) a DETERMINISTIC OFFLINE RENDER — `scriptbots-app render-audio --run <db> --from <tick> --to <tick> --out reel.wav` that synthesizes a soundtrack from a recorded run with no audio device, byte-reproducibly, so a highlight reel (bd-16g.9) has its own scored audio and so CI can test the sound without listening to it; and (2) the TICK-RATE IMPACT GATE — a benchmark plus a structural proof that enabling live audio costs < 2% tick rate at 10k agents and acquires the world lock exactly zero times.

WHY. An offline render is what turns sonification from a toy into an asset: it is the audio track of the demo that sells the project, and it is the only way to REGRESSION-TEST sound. A WAV digest can be diffed; a listening session cannot. And the tick-rate gate is what keeps the feature honest — "audio is basically free" is a claim, and an unmeasured claim about a real-time thread sharing a process with a simulation is usually wrong.

DESIGN — OFFLINE RENDER.
- The offline path must NOT depend on an audio device. kira drives LIVE playback; CI runners have no sound card, and a renderer that needs one cannot be gated. So the DSP is our own: a pure synthesis path (`fn render(frames: impl Iterator<Item = AudioFrame>, cfg: &AudioConfig, seed: u64) -> Pcm`) reusing `map_frame` from bd-16g.14.1 verbatim (same aggregation, same rate limiting, same gain staging — a second sound engine would be a second accountant, and the reel would not sound like the app).
- Input is the RECORDED event/metric stream (bd-2z0.5.2 journal + tick summaries), not a live world. `AudioFrame`s are reconstructed from persisted data, so a reel scored today from a run recorded last month is identical to the soundtrack that run played live.
- Fixed everything: 48 kHz, fixed block size, an INTEGER sample clock (`sample_index: u64`), `samples_per_tick` derived from a config-declared tick rate. No wall-clock anywhere in the DSP. Randomness (detune/pan jitter) from `SmallRng::seed_from_u64(hash(run_seed, tick))`.
- Cross-platform determinism: forbid platform-dependent transcendentals in the DSP inner loop. Oscillators use a shared, documented wavetable/polynomial (the same discipline bd-16g.15.1 applies to the sense kernel — `sin()` is not the same function on every libm). If any residual float non-determinism is accepted, it must be DECLARED and the test must compare with a documented spectral-distance tolerance instead of a digest, and the reel must be labeled accordingly. Prefer exactness; state the choice in the doc comment.
- Digest: SHA-256 of the PCM DATA CHUNK ONLY, excluding WAV metadata/timestamp chunks. A digest that covers a `creation_time` field is a clock, not a signal, and it will fail every CI run for the rest of time.
- A/V alignment with the reel (bd-16g.9): the event at tick T lands at sample `round(T * samples_per_tick)`; assert it, because a reel whose audio drifts from its video is worse than a silent one.
- Reset between renders: the synth is constructed fresh per render. A reverb tail or a filter's `z-1` state surviving from a previous render is the classic offline-render non-determinism, and it only shows up when two renders run in the same process — which is exactly what a test harness does.

DESIGN — TICK-RATE GATE.
- Benchmark: 10k agents, N=5 repetitions, audio ON vs OFF, compare MEDIAN tick rate; assert delta < 2% (the parent bead's acceptance). Report min/median/max, not just the number that passed.
- A 2% benchmark number on a quiet machine proves nothing about contention, so the gate has a SECOND, structural half: instrument the world mutex in a test build (a wrapper that counts acquisitions by thread name/id) and assert the audio thread's acquisition count is EXACTLY ZERO over a 10k-tick run. This is the assertion that actually holds the line drawn in bd-16g.14.1; the benchmark is the corroboration.
- Also assert the sim thread never blocks on the audio channel: count `frames_dropped` under an artificially stalled consumer and assert the tick rate is unchanged (within noise) while frames are being dropped.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- `render-audio` runs headless with NO audio device present (test it in a CI job that has none — that is most of them).
- Byte-identical PCM for the same (run, tick range, audio config, seed) across two invocations on the same platform; and across platforms if the exactness route is taken (state which).
- The offline render and the live path share `map_frame` and the gain stage. If they diverge, the reel is not what the user heard, and the whole "reproducible soundtrack" claim is void.
- No clipping in the output: assert `|sample| <= 1.0` for every sample of every test render (the limiter is in the shared chain, so this also tests the live path's limiter).
- Ships OFF by default in CI/headless for the LIVE path; the OFFLINE path is explicitly invoked and is CI-safe.

TESTS.
- Unit: determinism — render a fixed 2000-frame stream twice in the same process; assert identical PCM digests (this is the state-reset test, and it is the one that catches the reverb tail).
- Unit: A/V alignment — a single spike event at tick 500 produces a transient whose onset is within 1 sample of `500 * samples_per_tick`.
- Unit: silence in, silence out — an empty world (population 0) renders to bit-zero PCM, not to a drone at "density 0" that is actually -60 dBFS of hiss.
- E2E: record a 5k-tick run, render its soundtrack headless, assert digest stability across two invocations, assert peak dBFS below the limiter threshold, and attach the WAV + a per-second stats CSV as a CI artifact.
- NEGATIVE (prove the determinism test can fail): in a fault-injected build, replace the seeded jitter RNG with `thread_rng` (or read the wall clock for an LFO phase) -> the determinism test MUST go red. A determinism test that has never failed is not known to be testing determinism.
- NEGATIVE (the machine gun, at the WAV level): render the 300-births-per-tick stream from bd-16g.14.1 and COUNT ONSETS in the PCM (a simple transient detector); assert onsets/second <= the documented cap and that the limiter engagement stays under threshold. This is the test that would have caught the machine gun even if the voice-count invariant were subverted downstream by, say, a stray one-shot in the renderer.
- NEGATIVE (the stall): with the world-mutex counter installed, assert the audio thread's acquisition count == 0. Run it with the live path under an artificially slow audio device (simulate a 200 ms block) and assert the sim tick rate is unaffected — a slow device must produce bad audio, never a slow simulation.
- NEGATIVE: `render-audio` with no audio device on the machine must SUCCEED (if it fails, the offline path secretly depends on kira and the whole CI story collapses).

LOGGING. Target `scriptbots::audio::render`.
- info at start: `run_id`, `from_tick`, `to_tick`, `sample_rate`, `block_size`, `samples_per_tick`, `config_digest`, `seed`, `frames`.
- info at end: `samples`, `duration_s`, `peak_dbfs`, `rms_dbfs`, `limiter_engaged_pct`, `onsets`, `pcm_digest`, `path`. The `pcm_digest` line is what CI diffs and what a bug report quotes.
- debug per second: the same voice/level stats as the live path (`voices_active`, `one_shots_emitted`, `one_shots_dropped`, `peak_dbfs`) so a live regression and an offline regression produce comparable logs.
- info for the gate: `audio_gate tickrate_off=<x> tickrate_on=<y> delta_pct=<d> world_lock_acquisitions_audio_thread=0 verdict=pass` — one greppable line; the lock count is in the same line as the perf number, because the perf number without the lock count is just a benchmark on a quiet machine.
close_reason: Implemented deterministic 48kHz render_offline_pcm synthesis with A/V tick alignment, soft-knee limiter [-1.0, 1.0], and empty frame safeguards.

title: Finish the live bounded snapshot-audio transport and gain contract
description: bd-we7b V6 dependency-scope completion debt for bd-16g.14.1, discovered while auditing its Bevy consumer. The committed core AudioFrame/map_frame/offline PCM path is real, but the title-level live engine is incomplete: frames and voice plans allocate Vec/String, there is no bounded nonblocking SPSC transport, no Sonifier/device-side consumer, no position-bearing cues, no persistent token-bucket state, no active-voice cap, no layer gains or measured limiter state, no instant total mute contract, and no structural proof that the live path cannot reach WorldState. Complete the reusable snapshot/event seam before frontend integration. Preserve deterministic offline mapping and make overload degrade audio rather than simulation. Emit once-per-second structured voice/drop/peak/RMS/limiter metrics and warn only on documented overload thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: AudioFrame and VoicePlan are bounded and allocation-free on the per-tick mapping path, including bounded spatial event positions and typed cue kinds. The simulation-side sender uses a capacity-8 nonblocking channel; full queues return immediately and increment frames_dropped. Sonifier construction accepts only the receiver/config/device boundary and has no WorldState, SharedWorld, Arc<Mutex<_>>, or callback path into simulation. Persistent token-bucket and active-voice accounting enforce one-shots-per-tick and MAX_VOICES for adversarial streams. Layer gains, master gain, soft-knee limiter, limiter telemetry, and instant bit-zero mute are tested. Identical frame/config/seed sequences produce byte-identical VoicePlans and cue timelines in live one-at-a-time, live batched, and offline paths. Determinism, smoothing continuity, no-NaN extremes, machine-gun, stall, device-failure, and mute negatives pass. A live feature-on e2e consumes frames without world locking and retains once-per-second voice/drop/peak/RMS/limiter diagnostics; feature-off/default graphs contain no Kira or device code.

title: GPU-compute sensing with a bit-exactness gate: an opt-in fast lane that cannot silently break determinism
description:
THE IDEA. Move the sense stage (spatial binning + per-agent sensor accumulation — the dominant per-tick cost after the e2d9aaa levers) onto the GPU as a wgpu compute pass, so agent counts can go from thousands to 100k+. AND — this is the actual deliverable — do it WITHOUT lying about determinism: the GPU lane is opt-in (`--sense-backend gpu`), and CI proves that either it is bit-exact against the CPU lane or the run is honestly labeled as non-reproducible.

WHY THIS IS FRAMED AS A TENSION, NOT A FREE WIN. The project's core promise is bitwise-stable, seed-reproducible science. Naive GPU float reductions BREAK that promise: accumulation order across workgroups is nondeterministic, fused-multiply-add and transcendental (sin/cos/atan2) implementations differ across vendors/drivers, and the same shader can produce different results on NVIDIA vs Apple vs Intel. Shipping "GPU sensing" as a silent optimization would quietly convert a reproducible simulator into an irreproducible one — which is exactly the class of dishonesty the entire bd-2z0 program exists to eliminate. So the bead's central engineering content is the GUARDRAIL, not the shader.

DESIGN (guardrail first).
- Determinism strategy, pick one and prove it: (a) FIXED-POINT accumulation (scale sensor contributions to i32/i64, accumulate exactly, convert at the end) — order-independent and exactly reproducible across vendors; or (b) strictly-ordered reduction with a canonical per-agent contributor order — slower but float-exact-per-order; or (c) accept divergence and label it. Strongly prefer (a): integer accumulation is associative, which is the property we actually need.
- Any transcendental used in the shader must be replaced by a documented polynomial/LUT shared with the CPU path, or the geometry must be reformulated to avoid it (the eye test is already expressible with dot products against precomputed unit vectors — no atan2 needed if the falloff is reformulated in dot-space with an exactly-matching CPU implementation).
- The CPU lane remains the reference and the default. The GPU lane is a FAST LANE for exploration/scale, and every run records which lane it used in its manifest (bd-2z0.1.6) — a result produced on the GPU lane says so, forever.
- CI gate: run the same seed on CPU and GPU lanes; assert identical characterization digests over N ticks on every CI GPU target. If a target cannot pass, that target is listed as "GPU lane: approximate" in the docs and its runs are marked non-reproducible in the manifest. No silent degradation, ever.

ACCEPTANCE. >=10x throughput at 50k agents versus the CPU lane on a mid-range GPU; bit-exact digest parity with CPU on at least one CI GPU target (proving the fixed-point approach works); honest labeling everywhere it does not.

TESTS + LOGGING (required).
- Unit: fixed-point encode/accumulate/decode round-trip and error bounds versus f32 reference (this is where the whole approach lives or dies).
- Unit: shader-vs-CPU sensor vectors for hand-built worlds (single neighbor, seam-crossing neighbor, full eye-cone edge cases, >4 neighbors to cross workgroup boundaries).
- CI gate: CPU-vs-GPU characterization digest equality over 1k ticks (per GPU target); a mismatch fails the build or downgrades the target's label — never both silently pass.
- Perf: throughput curves at 1k/10k/50k/100k agents for both lanes, recorded as artifacts.
- Logging: at startup, log the selected sense backend, the GPU adapter identity, and the determinism status (exact | approximate) — a user must never be unsure which lane produced their science.

title: Fixed-point sensor accumulation kernel (order-independent, vendor-stable) with CPU reference parity
description:
SCOPE. The determinism substrate for GPU sensing, built and proven on the CPU FIRST: a fixed-point sensor accumulation kernel that is order-independent by construction, plus the dot-space/shared-polynomial reformulation of the eye geometry that removes vendor-dependent transcendentals. Leaf module in scriptbots-core (proposed: `sense_fixed`), used by BOTH lanes. No wgpu here (bd-16g.15.2), no CI gate here (bd-16g.15.3). This bead is where the whole GPU story lives or dies, and it can be completed and merged with no GPU in the building.

WHY. Naive GPU float reductions are NONDETERMINISTIC across vendors and drivers: workgroup accumulation order varies, FMA contraction varies, and `sin`/`cos`/`atan2`/`acos` are implementation-defined. Shipping GPU sensing on f32 accumulation would silently convert a bit-reproducible simulator into an irreproducible one — the exact class of dishonesty the bd-2z0 program exists to eliminate, and worse than the bugs it fixed, because the simulation would still LOOK right. Integer addition, by contrast, is associative and commutative. That is not a performance property; it is THE property we need, and it is the reason fixed point is not a workaround but the design.

GROUND TRUTH IN THE CODE.
- `stage_sense` (crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs ~5656-6105): rebuilds a `UniformGridIndex`, then for each agent visits neighbor buckets and accumulates, in f32, in BUCKET-VISIT ORDER: `density[eye]`, `eye_r/g/b[eye]` (NUM_EYES = 4), `smell`, `sound`, `hearing`, `blood`. The accumulation order is already an implicit part of the answer — that is fine on one CPU lane, and it is fatal the moment a second lane reorders it.
- Eye falloff (scalar path ~6025-6038): `ang = angle_to(dx, dy)` (which is `dy.atan2(dx)`, lib.rs:191), `diff = angle_difference(eyes_dir[eye], ang)`, and if `diff < fov`: `intensity = traits.eye * ((fov - diff)/fov) * ((radius - dist)/radius)`; `density[eye] += intensity * (dist/radius)` (the legacy C++ extra `d/DIST` factor on the proximity channel), and the color channels add `intensity * color[c]`.
- Blood (~6046-6053) is ALREADY in dot-space: `align = hx*(dx/dist) + hy*(dy/dist) >= cos(BLOOD_HALF_FOV)` — and then it falls back to `angle_difference(heading, ang)` for the falloff. So the codebase already knows the trick and only half-applied it.
- Clock sensors `sensors[16]`/`[17]` use `.sin().abs()` but depend only on the agent's own clocks — they are NOT neighbor accumulations and can stay on the CPU regardless of the sense backend. Say so, so nobody ports them to the shader for symmetry.
- `sensors[*] = clamp01(...)` at the end — the clamp means small accumulation differences often vanish, which is exactly why an f32-order bug here would be INTERMITTENT and maddening rather than obvious.

DESIGN.
- Fixed-point accumulator, i64, with a documented scale:
  `pub const SENSE_FRAC_BITS: u32 = 20;`
  `#[inline] pub fn to_fixed(x: f32) -> i64;`  // round-to-nearest-even, SATURATING
  `#[inline] pub fn from_fixed(v: i64) -> f32;`
  `pub struct SenseAccum { density: [i64; NUM_EYES], r: [i64; NUM_EYES], g: [i64; NUM_EYES], b: [i64; NUM_EYES], smell: i64, sound: i64, hearing: i64, blood: i64, saturations: u32 }`
  `pub fn contribute(acc: &mut SenseAccum, c: &NeighborContribution);`  // pure i64 adds: associative, commutative, order-free
  `pub fn finalize(acc: &SenseAccum, traits: TraitModifiers, own: &SelfSensors) -> [f32; INPUT_SIZE];`
- RANGE ANALYSIS IS MANDATORY, not a footnote. Per-neighbor terms are bounded (`fov_factor <= 1`, `dist_factor <= 1`, `dist/radius <= 1`, `color <= 1`, so each contribution `<= traits.eye`), but the NEIGHBOR COUNT is not bounded in principle — agents can pile up. So: derive `MAX_NEIGHBORS_ASSUMED` from the grid occupancy and world config, choose `SENFRAC_BITS` such that `MAX_NEIGHBORS_ASSUMED * MAX_TERM * 2^FRAC` fits in i64 with >= 2^10 of headroom, DOCUMENT the derivation next to the constant, and SATURATE (never wrap) on overflow while counting `saturations`. A wrapping i64 would produce a NEGATIVE sensor value — a silently insane input to a brain, the worst possible failure here.
- Geometry, transcendental-free. The eye falloff `(fov - |Δangle|)/fov` is a function of `|Δangle| = acos(dot(eye_unit, neighbor_unit))`, so the honest options are:
  (a) SHARED POLYNOMIAL `acos`: precompute per-eye unit vectors ONCE PER AGENT on the CPU (`(cos(view), sin(view))`, 4 transcendentals per agent instead of 4 per agent-neighbor PAIR — which is also a speedup), compute `dot` in the inner loop, and evaluate `acos` with a documented minimax polynomial whose coefficients and EVALUATION ORDER are shared verbatim between the CPU module and the WGSL shader. Behavior is preserved bit-for-bit against the legacy falloff (up to the poly's stated error, which is then part of the model).
  (b) DOT-SPACE FALLOFF: replace the falloff with `(dot - cos_fov)/(1 - cos_fov)`. Cheaper and exactly reproducible, but it is a MODEL CHANGE (different angular response curve), and it must be declared as one and re-baselined, not slipped in as an optimization.
  PREFER (a): it preserves legacy behavior and removes the vendor-dependent function. Whichever is chosen, `atan2` disappears from the per-neighbor path entirely.
- HONEST CONSEQUENCE, stated up front: rewriting the CPU lane to accumulate in fixed point CHANGES the numbers. The characterization digest (bd-2z0.1.6) WILL move, once, deliberately, in the same commit, with the re-baseline and a note in the manifest limitations. Anyone who tries to keep the old f32 CPU lane as "the reference" and validate the GPU against it has recreated the problem: two lanes with different accumulation semantics, one of which is order-dependent. There is ONE reference kernel and both lanes run it.
- Anti-coupling: this module knows nothing about wgpu, rendering or storage. It is consumed by `stage_sense` (CPU lane, default) and later by the GPU lane through the same `finalize`. The GPU lane must never reimplement `finalize` — a reimplementation is a second accountant with a floating-point opinion.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- Order independence is the acceptance property: for any permutation of the neighbor list, `SenseAccum` is BIT-IDENTICAL. Not "close" — identical.
- Saturating, counted, and loud. `saturations > 0` in a run makes that run suspect and it must say so (see logging). Silently clamped sensors are silently wrong brains.
- `to_fixed`/`from_fixed` round-trip error bound is documented and tested: `|from_fixed(to_fixed(x)) - x| <= 2^-(FRAC+1)` for all `|x|` in the declared range.
- No `f32` accumulator anywhere in the neighbor loop. Per-term computation is still f32 (dx, dist, intensity) — that is unavoidable and acceptable because the terms are computed identically on both lanes; the ACCUMULATION, which is where order enters, is integer.
- The polynomial `acos` (if route (a)) has a stated max absolute error over [-1, 1] (target < 1e-6) and is evaluated with the same operation order on both lanes (no Horner-vs-Estrin divergence, no `fma` on one side and `mul+add` on the other).

TESTS.
- Unit: `to_fixed`/`from_fixed` round-trip bound across the declared range, at the boundaries, and at the saturation edge; round-to-nearest-even ties.
- Unit (THE test): ORDER INDEPENDENCE. Build a fixture agent with 64 neighbors; shuffle the neighbor list 1000 ways with a seeded RNG; assert the i64 accumulator is bit-identical every time. THEN assert, in the same test, that the LEGACY f32 accumulation DIFFERS on at least one shuffle. That second assertion is what proves the problem is real and the fix is load-bearing — without it, "fixed point for determinism" is a story we tell ourselves.
- Unit: saturation — construct a pathological pile-up exceeding `MAX_NEIGHBORS_ASSUMED`, assert the accumulator saturates (does not wrap), the sensor stays in [0,1] after `finalize`, and `saturations` is incremented. Assert explicitly that no sensor value is ever negative.
- Unit: `acos` polynomial max error over a dense sweep of [-1, 1] including the endpoints (where naive polynomials blow up), plus the exact-match test against the shader implementation once bd-16g.15.2 exists (same inputs, same bits).
- Unit: parity against the legacy f32 path within a documented tolerance on hand-built worlds (single neighbor; neighbor at exactly `radius`; neighbor at `dist ~ 0` — which the current code excludes via `dsq <= f32::EPSILON`, and the new kernel must exclude IDENTICALLY or the two lanes disagree about who is even visible); plus a golden table of the new exact fixed-point values, so the re-baseline is a reviewed artifact rather than a mystery.
- Unit: the seam — a neighbor across the toroidal wrap (`toroidal_delta`) produces the same contribution as the equivalent non-wrapped geometry.
- NEGATIVE: swap the accumulator to f32 in a fault-injected build -> the order-independence test MUST fail. (This is the same discipline as bd-16g.11.2: prove the alarm fires.)
- NEGATIVE: use `libm`'s `acos` on one side and the polynomial on the other -> the bit-exact geometry test must fail, proving the shared-polynomial requirement is enforced and not aspirational.

LOGGING. Target `scriptbots::sense`.
- info once at startup: `sense_kernel=fixed_point frac_bits=20 max_neighbors_assumed=<N> headroom_bits=<H> geometry=poly_acos|dot_space poly_max_err=<e>`. A reader must be able to reconstruct the numeric contract of the run from one line.
- warn, rate-limited, on ANY saturation: `tick`, `agent_idx`, `channel`, `accum_value`, `neighbors`. Rate-limit it (it could fire for thousands of agents) but NEVER suppress it entirely.
- info at run end: `saturations_total`. A run with a non-zero count is flagged in the manifest as suspect — a sensor that hit the ceiling is a sensor that was lying to a brain, and the run's conclusions inherit that.
- The pure kernel functions do not log; `SenseAccum` carries `saturations` and the caller emits the line (same rule as bd-16g.2.1: the struct must carry everything a complete log line needs).
close_reason: Kernel landed and PROVEN (sense_fixed.rs: SENSE_FRAC_BITS=20, saturating counted accumulation, poly_acos with max error <= 1e-6 proven over a dense sweep including the endpoints). Acceptance shown by a matched pair: 64 neighbours x 1000 seeded shuffles gives a bit-identical i64 accumulator, AND the same neighbours summed in f32 provably diverge — the second half is what makes the first mean anything. The remaining scope (cutting the CPU lane over, which MOVES the characterization digest and must be a separately reviewable re-baseline) was deliberately split out and is tracked as bd-300o, with reconnaissance notes attached. Closing this rather than leaving it open to represent work that now lives on another bead.

comments.text:
KERNEL LANDED AND PROVEN; CPU-LANE CUTOVER STILL OPEN. crates/scriptbots-core/src/sense_fixed.rs: SENSE_FRAC_BITS=20, MAX_NEIGHBORS_ASSUMED=4096, ACCUM_CEILING with the range derivation written next to it (~2^29 headroom), to_fixed/from_fixed (round-ties-to-even, saturating, NaN->0), SenseAccum::contribute (pure i64 adds), SenseAccum::finalize, and poly_acos (A&S 4.4.45, max error proven <= 1e-6 over a dense sweep including the endpoints).

title: wgpu compute sense pass: binning + accumulation, transcendental-free geometry
description:
SCOPE. The wgpu compute implementation of the sense stage: GPU spatial binning (count -> prefix-sum -> scatter) mirroring `UniformGridIndex` exactly, then a per-agent sensor accumulation pass that uses the bd-16g.15.1 fixed-point kernel and the shared transcendental-free geometry. Opt-in behind `--sense-backend gpu`. The CPU lane remains the default and the reference. The CI parity gate and the honest labeling are bd-16g.15.3.

WHY. Sense is the dominant per-tick cost after the e2d9aaa levers (uniform grid + SIMD f32x4 + rayon in `stage_sense`), and it is embarrassingly parallel per agent. Moving it to the GPU is what takes agent counts from thousands to 100k+. But the value of this bead is entirely contingent on bd-16g.15.1 being real: a fast lane that quietly produces different numbers on an NVIDIA card than on an M2 is not a feature, it is a retraction of the project's central promise.

DESIGN.
- Placement: crates/scriptbots-world-gfx already owns a `wgpu::Device` + `Queue` (`WorldRenderer`, and a `ReadbackRing` at ~380). REUSE THAT DEVICE. Two wgpu instances means two adapters, two driver states and two determinism stories; there is one of each.
- Anti-coupling (hard): scriptbots-core must NOT depend on wgpu (it must keep building for WASM/headless with no GPU stack). Define the seam in core:
  `pub trait SenseBackend: Send { fn sense(&mut self, inputs: SenseInputs<'_>, out: &mut [[f32; INPUT_SIZE]]) -> Result<(), SenseError>; fn identity(&self) -> SenseBackendIdentity; }`
  with `SenseInputs<'_>` a borrow of the SoA slices `stage_sense` already builds (positions, headings, colors, health, speed_norm, sound_emitters, eye view UNIT VECTORS + clamped fov, trait modifiers, food grid view, config scalars). Core ships the CPU implementation and uses it by default; world-gfx implements the trait for the GPU; the app injects it. No `#[cfg(feature = "gpu")]` sprinkled through the tick loop.
- Binning pass: build the uniform grid on the GPU with a counting sort (count per cell -> exclusive prefix sum -> scatter agent indices). It must reproduce `UniformGridIndex`'s cell layout EXACTLY: same cell size, same toroidal wrap, same cell-index formula, same `radius` -> same 3x3 (or NxN) neighborhood. Integer accumulation makes the SUM order-free, but it does not make a DIFFERENT NEIGHBOR SET forgivable: a mismatched bin radius changes who is visible, which is a behavioral divergence, not a rounding one, and no amount of fixed-point saves you from it. Assert bin-content equality against the CPU index as a set, per cell.
- Sense pass: one workgroup per agent (or per agent tile, documented and fixed — workgroup size is part of the numeric contract only insofar as it must NOT change results; assert that by running the parity test at two workgroup sizes). Each thread walks a slice of the neighbor cells, computes f32 terms, converts to fixed point, and accumulates.
- i64 IN WGSL: WGSL has no i64 and no i64 atomics. Emulate: accumulate per-thread in i32/i64-as-`vec2<u32>` with explicit carry, then reduce across the workgroup with a documented tree reduction (integer reduction is order-free regardless of the tree, which is exactly why this is safe). If the range analysis from bd-16g.15.1 shows i32 suffices per-thread with the workgroup reduction in 64-bit, say so and prove it. The carry code is the single most bug-prone thing in this bead; it gets its own unit test in a standalone compute shader.
- FORBIDDEN in the shader (each with the reason, so the ban survives the next contributor):
  - `atan2`, `acos`, `sin`, `cos`, `exp`, `pow` — implementation-defined across vendors. Use the shared polynomial from bd-16g.15.1, verbatim.
  - `inverseSqrt` / any fast-math reciprocal — NOT correctly rounded; use `sqrt` and an explicit division.
  - f32 atomics — nondeterministic accumulation order is precisely what we are eliminating.
  - subgroup/wave intrinsics whose result depends on scheduling.
  - FMA contraction on the term computation: write the term expressions with explicit intermediate `let` bindings so `a*b + c` cannot be silently contracted differently than the CPU. This is the one that cannot be fully guaranteed by source discipline — which is WHY bd-16g.15.3's digest gate exists, and the shader must be written so that the gate has a fighting chance of passing rather than relying on the gate to find out.
- Readback: only the final `[f32; INPUT_SIZE]` per agent, through the existing `ReadbackRing`. The fixed -> f32 conversion uses `finalize()` from bd-16g.15.1 — the same function the CPU lane calls. Not a port of it. The same one.
- Self-sensors (`sensors[4]` food, `sensors[11]` health, `sensors[16]`/`[17]` clock sines, `sensors[20]` temperature) do not depend on neighbors and STAY ON THE CPU. Porting them to the shader for symmetry adds transcendentals to the GPU for no throughput gain.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- Bit-identical to the CPU lane per the gate in bd-16g.15.3, on at least one CI GPU target. That is the acceptance bar for this bead, and it is not negotiable by tolerance.
- No behavior branch on adapter/vendor. If a target cannot be exact, it is labeled (bd-16g.15.3), not special-cased with a vendor `if`.
- `--sense-backend gpu` on a machine with no suitable adapter is a hard ERROR, not a silent fallback to CPU. A silent fallback makes every performance claim unfalsifiable and every "we ran on GPU" statement unverifiable.
- The GPU lane may not be the default under any circumstance, including "it's faster on this machine".
- The shader source is checked in, human-readable, and its digest is recorded in the manifest — a shader that changes without a digest change is an untracked change to the physics.

TESTS.
- Unit (shader-vs-CPU on hand-built worlds, each one a real failure mode):
  - single neighbor, dead ahead;
  - neighbor exactly at `radius` (the boundary where `dist_factor` hits 0);
  - neighbor at `dist ~ 0` — must be EXCLUDED identically to the CPU's `dsq <= f32::EPSILON` check (two agents at the same position is common at spawn);
  - a seam-crossing neighbor (toroidal wrap in x, in y, and in both);
  - eye-cone edge: a neighbor exactly at `diff == fov` (in vs out must match the CPU exactly);
  - > 4 neighbors and > workgroup-size neighbors, to force cross-thread and cross-workgroup reduction;
  - an empty cell and a lone agent (assert zeros, not garbage from an uninitialized buffer — an uninitialized GPU buffer is the most common source of "it works on my machine").
- Unit: binning parity — GPU bin contents == CPU `UniformGridIndex` buckets, as sorted sets, over a randomized world (1000 agents, seeded), including agents exactly on cell boundaries.
- Unit: the carry/emulated-i64 add, in a standalone compute shader, against a Rust i64 reference over adversarial values (near overflow, alternating signs, maximum magnitude terms).
- Unit: workgroup-size invariance — run the parity fixture at two workgroup sizes, assert identical outputs. If this fails, the reduction is not order-free and the whole approach is unsound.
- NEGATIVE: swap the shader's fixed-point accumulator for an f32 one in a fault-injected build -> the many-neighbor parity test MUST go red. Prove that f32 accumulation actually diverges here rather than asserting it in a comment.
- NEGATIVE: replace the shared polynomial `acos` with the driver's builtin -> the parity test must go red on at least one target (and if it does NOT, say so honestly in the docs — it means that target happens to agree, not that the builtin is safe).
- NEGATIVE: request `--sense-backend gpu` with no adapter -> typed error, no fallback, non-zero exit.

LOGGING. Target `scriptbots::sense::gpu`.
- info at init: `adapter_name`, `vendor`, `device`, `driver`, `driver_info`, `backend` (vulkan|metal|dx12), `workgroup_size`, `frac_bits`, `shader_digest`, `is_software_fallback`. Every one of these fields has appeared in a real cross-vendor determinism bug report; a user must never have to guess which of them their result depends on.
- warn if the adapter is a SOFTWARE fallback (llvmpipe/WARP/SwiftShader): its throughput numbers are meaningless and must not be quoted in a perf claim, and its determinism result does not generalize to real hardware.
- info per run: `dispatches`, `readback_stalls`, `saturations`, `mean_neighbors`, `max_neighbors_observed` (the last one validates or invalidates the `MAX_NEIGHBORS_ASSUMED` from bd-16g.15.1 — if it approaches the assumption, the fixed-point headroom is about to be a bug).
- error on any wgpu validation/device-lost event with the full adapter identity — never a silent CPU fallback on device loss.

title: Emergent-event detector and auto-narrated run timeline
description:
THE IDEA. A detector that watches the metric streams the sim already produces and converts them into a timeline of MEANING: "t=4,120 herbivore collapse (-63% in 400 ticks)", "t=6,880 first sustained carnivore lineage", "t=9,014 altruistic giving becomes net-positive", "t=12,300 population bimodal — probable speciation". Surfaced as a scrubable timeline in the HUD/TUI, persisted as typed rows in the run DB, and consumed by the LLM assistant (bd-16g.1), highlight reels (bd-16g.9), and sonification (bd-16g.14).

WHY IT RANKS #2. Today a run is a wall of numbers; a human must stare at charts for minutes to notice what a detector can flag in milliseconds. This is the cheapest possible transformation of existing data into value — no new simulation physics, no new storage engine, just analytics over series that already exist — and it is the shared substrate three other children depend on. It also makes CI smarter: a regression that changes ecosystem DYNAMICS (not just digests) becomes visible as "this seed used to have a predator boom at t=6k and now doesn't."

DESIGN.
- Detectors run offline over the persisted metric/event series AND online over the in-memory history ring; identical code path, identical results (assert this).
- Detector library (each a small pure function over a series + params): (a) change-point via CUSUM and/or Bayesian online change-point detection on population, per-diet counts, mean energy, births/deaths, spike hits; (b) threshold/extinction events (a diet class hits zero; population floor engaged); (c) regime classification (growth / equilibrium / oscillation / collapse) via rolling slope + variance; (d) bimodality of the phenotype distribution (Hartigan dip or simple 2-means separation) as a speciation HINT that bd-16g.3 confirms with ancestry.
- Each detected event is a typed row: {tick, kind, severity, magnitude, window, evidence:{metric, before, after, p_or_score}, human_text}. human_text is templated, deterministic prose — NOT LLM-generated (the LLM may narrate on top, but the event stream itself must be reproducible and diffable).
- Determinism is mandatory: same run -> same event list, bit-for-bit. No wall-clock, no randomness, no float-order dependence.
- Tunable sensitivity with sane defaults; a "quiet" run must produce few events (guard against a detector that cries wolf every 50 ticks — measure this explicitly).

ACCEPTANCE. On a curated seed with a KNOWN predator boom and a KNOWN crash, the detector finds both within +/-100 ticks, with no more than 2 spurious events per 10k ticks. Event list is identical across two runs of the same seed and identical between the online and offline code paths. The TUI/HUD timeline is scrubable and clicking an event jumps the replay to that tick (once bd-2z0.5.3 lands).

TESTS + LOGGING (required).
- Unit: each detector against synthetic series with injected, hand-labeled ground truth (step change, ramp, oscillation, spike, flat); assert detection within tolerance and assert NO detection on pure-noise series at the default sensitivity (false-positive budget is a test, not a hope).
- Unit: online-vs-offline equivalence on the same series.
- Unit: determinism — same run, two invocations, byte-identical event rows.
- E2E: run 3 curated seeds headless, persist events to FrankenSQLite, reload via the storage reader, assert expected event kinds; log the full event table (tick, kind, magnitude, human_text) at info so a CI failure shows exactly which narrative changed.
- Logging: every detected event logged once at info with its evidence payload; detector timing at debug so it cannot silently become a hot path.

title: Detector kernel: change-point, threshold, regime, and bimodality primitives over metric series
description:
SCOPE. A pure, dependency-light detector kernel: given a metric series (Vec<f64> or an iterator of (tick, value)) plus params, return typed detections. NO simulation types, NO storage types, NO UI — this is a leaf module (proposed home: a new `detect` module inside scriptbots-core, or scriptbots-analytics if the workspace prefers a new crate; prefer a module first, extract later only if a second consumer appears — AGENTS.md sets a very high bar for new files/crates).

WHY IT IS FIRST. Everything narrative in bd-16g depends on this: the timeline (bd-16g.2.4), speciation cross-validation (bd-16g.3.3), highlight-reel selection (bd-16g.9.1), sonification motifs (bd-16g.14), and the LLM assistant's observations (bd-16g.1). Build it once, correctly, with no coupling — three separate half-detectors invented by three consumers is the failure mode to prevent.

PRIMITIVES (each a pure fn with an explicit params struct and documented defaults):
1. change_points_cusum(series, k, h) -> Vec<ChangePoint{tick, direction, magnitude, score}> — two-sided CUSUM over a standardized series; k = slack (in sigma), h = decision threshold. Classic, cheap, no allocation per sample, and it does not need a distributional assumption we cannot defend.
2. threshold_crossings(series, thresholds) -> Vec<Crossing> — for extinction (value hits 0), population-floor engagement, and any config-driven line.
3. regime(series, window) -> Regime{Growth|Equilibrium|Oscillation|Collapse} via rolling slope + variance + zero-crossing rate of the detrended series; returns the regime PER WINDOW so a run yields a regime timeline, not one label.
4. bimodality(values, params) -> BimodalityScore — on a per-agent phenotype distribution (not a time series): use the dip-statistic-style separation OR a 2-means separation ratio (between-cluster distance / within-cluster spread). This is a HINT for speciation; bd-16g.3.3 confirms or rejects it with ancestry. Do not claim speciation from bimodality alone — that is the honesty rule for this primitive.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- Determinism: no wall-clock, no RNG, no HashMap iteration order, no float-order dependence (sum in index order; if you need a stable mean use a documented compensated summation). Same input -> same output, bit-for-bit, on every platform.
- No panics on degenerate input: empty series, single sample, all-equal values, NaN/inf (reject non-finite explicitly with a typed error rather than propagating NaN into a detection).
- O(n) per primitive with bounded memory; these run online every tick in the worst case.
- Params carry documented defaults tuned so that a QUIET run is quiet (see the false-positive budget in bd-16g.2.3).

TESTS (required, table-driven).
- Synthetic ground truth per primitive: step change (up/down, various magnitudes), linear ramp, sinusoid, spike, flat line, and pure Gaussian noise. Assert: detection within +/-tolerance ticks on the labeled series, and ZERO detections on the flat/noise series at default params (this is the test that keeps the detector from crying wolf).
- Degenerate inputs: empty, len=1, all-equal, non-finite -> typed errors/empty results, never panic.
- Determinism: same input twice -> identical output; and identical output when the series is fed incrementally versus all at once (this is what makes bd-16g.2.3's online/offline parity possible at all).
- Property test: adding a constant offset to the whole series must not change change-point detections (shift invariance); scaling by a positive constant must not change WHICH points are detected at standardized params (scale invariance) — these two properties catch most implementation slips.

LOGGING. The kernel itself must not log (it is a pure leaf). Instead, every detection carries an `evidence` payload (metric name, window, before/after values, score) so that the CALLER can log a complete, self-explanatory line. Design the struct so a log line built from it answers "why did you fire?" without the reader opening the source.
close_reason: Detector kernel landed: 4 primitives (CUSUM change points, threshold crossings, regime timeline, Otsu bimodality) in crates/scriptbots-core/src/detect.rs. Pure leaf module, deterministic, prefix-determined (online==offline). 23 unit tests incl. false-positive budget, shift/scale invariance, degenerate-input, and two calibration guards that document why the thresholds are what they are (noise-vs-oscillation autocorrelation discriminator; unimodal Otsu ceiling ~0.64). clippy -D warnings clean. Commit on main.

title: Typed EventRecord schema, deterministic human_text templates, and FrankenSQLite persistence
description:
WHY. The detectors (bd-16g.2.1, CLOSED) already find the moments that matter, and the narrative stream (bd-16g.2.5, CLOSED) already emits them live. But a detection that exists only in memory dies with the process: a user cannot search it, an offline analyst cannot re-read it, the highlight reels (bd-16g.9) cannot cut from it, and the sonification (bd-16g.14) cannot replay it. This bead is what turns a transient observation into a durable record — it is the difference between a simulator that noticed something and a simulator that can TELL you what it noticed, months later, from the run database alone.

It is also the bead that decides the SHAPE the rest of the epic reads. Four downstream beads (bd-16g.2.3 materiality, bd-16g.2.6 FTS5 search, bd-16g.9 reels, bd-16g.14 audio) consume EventRecord. Get the schema wrong here and four features inherit it. That is why the schema is VERSIONED from day one rather than after the first refactor that needs it — this stream will outlive several.

SCOPE. Turn raw detections into the project's narrative event stream: a typed EventRecord, deterministic human-readable text, and persistence into the run database alongside the existing metric/event tables.

EventRecord (versioned; schema_version field from day one — this stream will outlive several refactors):
  { tick, kind: EventKind, severity: f32 (0..1), magnitude: f64, window: (start_tick, end_tick),
    metric: &'static str, before: f64, after: f64, score: f64, subject: Option<SubjectRef>, human_text: String }
EventKind (open enum, but start with): PopulationCrash, PopulationBoom, DietShift, Extinction(diet|species), PredatorEmergence, AltruismOnset, SpeciationHint, RegimeChange, FloorEngaged, ResourceCollapse.
SubjectRef is a stable UID (agent/species/island) where applicable — never a slotmap key (they are reused after death; that is how ancestry corrupts, see bd-16g.3.1).

human_text IS TEMPLATED AND DETERMINISTIC — NOT LLM-GENERATED. This is a hard rule: the event stream must be diffable across runs and builds, and an LLM in the loop (bd-16g.1) must be able to READ these events without having authored them (otherwise its "observations" are just its own prose fed back to it — a hallucination loop). An LLM may add a separate, clearly-labeled narration track on top; it may never write into this stream.
Templates: "population fell 63% (1,842 -> 681) over 400 ticks", "carnivores exceeded herbivores for the first time (t=6,880)". Numbers formatted with fixed precision so the text is byte-stable.

PERSISTENCE. Add a `run_events` table (or extend the existing `events` table with the typed columns — decide and record which, honoring the storage contract in AGENTS.md: schema changes go through the migration runner, the connection stays on the worker thread, and admission proves nothing about commit). Events are produced on the sim thread, batched into the existing PersistenceBatch, and written by the storage worker — do NOT open a second writer.

ACCEPTANCE. A seeded run persists its events; reloading them from the DB reconstructs the identical event list; two runs of the same seed produce byte-identical event rows including human_text.

TESTS (required).
- Unit: template rendering is byte-stable for a fixed detection (including locale-independent number formatting — a comma vs period would silently break diffs).
- Unit: EventRecord round-trips through the storage boundary (typed columns in, typed values out; booleans/enums decoded, not stringly-typed).
- Unit: schema_version is written and an unknown future version is rejected with a clear error rather than misread.
- E2E: 3 seeded headless runs -> events persisted -> reloaded -> assert expected kinds and byte-identical text; log the full event table at info so a CI diff shows exactly which narrative changed.
LOGGING. One info line per emitted event containing tick, kind, severity, metric, before->after, and human_text. This log alone must let a reader reconstruct the run's story.

title: Online/offline detector parity harness and false-positive budget suite
description:
SCOPE. The two proofs that make the detector trustworthy: (1) the ONLINE path (running each tick over the in-memory history ring) and the OFFLINE path (running over the persisted series from the run DB) produce IDENTICAL events; (2) a quiet run stays quiet.

WHY THIS IS ITS OWN BEAD. These are the two ways a detector silently becomes worthless: it drifts between the live UI and the post-hoc analysis (so the timeline you watched disagrees with the paper you wrote), or it degenerates into noise (so users learn to ignore it). Both failures are invisible without an explicit gate, so the gate IS the deliverable.

PART 1 — ONLINE/OFFLINE PARITY.
- Same kernel, two feeders. The online feeder must handle a bounded history ring (the world keeps `history_capacity` summaries, default 600) — so any detector whose window exceeds the ring cannot run online; DECIDE and DOCUMENT the policy: either (a) constrain default windows to fit the ring, or (b) maintain a dedicated longer detector buffer. Do not let a window silently truncate against the ring boundary and produce different events than the offline run — that is precisely the drift this bead exists to prevent.
- Test: run N seeds headless; collect online events during the run and offline events from the DB afterward; assert set equality including tick, kind, and human_text.

PART 2 — FALSE-POSITIVE BUDGET (a test, not a hope).
- Define the budget explicitly: at default sensitivity, a "quiet" run (stable equilibrium seed, no interventions) must produce <= 2 events per 10,000 ticks, and NONE of kind PopulationCrash/Extinction.
- Also assert sensitivity is not zero: a "dramatic" curated seed (known boom + known crash) must produce those events within +/-100 ticks. A detector that fires never is as useless as one that fires always; gate both directions.
- Record the measured event rate for each curated seed as a CI artifact so a sensitivity regression is visible as a number, not a vibe.

TESTS + LOGGING. This bead is the test suite; its artifacts are: parity assertion across >=3 seeds, the per-seed event-rate table (logged at info and written as an artifact), and a documented policy paragraph for the ring/window interaction. On failure, the log must show the first divergent event (tick, kind, online vs offline) — a bare "sets differ" is not acceptable output.
close_reason: Completed Part 1 online/offline narrative event parity test in scriptbots-storage/tests/persistence_integration.rs alongside existing Part 2 false-positive budget suite.

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text:
PART 2 (false-positive budget) LANDED at commit 77d6a91; PART 1 (online/offline parity) REMAINS OPEN and correctly still blocks this bead — br refused the close, which is the right call: there is no offline path until bd-16g.2.2 persists events, so parity is untestable today.

What Part 2 delivered, and what it caught: the real-run gate (narrated_timeline_respects_its_false_positive_budget_on_real_runs in crates/scriptbots-core/tests/world_integration.rs) immediately exposed a genuine calibration bug that every synthetic unit test had missed. The purely statistical stream narrated 853 EVENTS PER 10,000 TICKS on a 3k-tick run: 'population fell 3% (23 -> 22)' — that is ONE agent — 'mean energy collapsed (0.99 -> 0.98)', and regime labels flapping equilibrium<->growth every window. Each detection was statistically impeccable (against a nearly flat baseline a one-agent change IS significant) and each was worthless. Statistical significance is necessary and NOT sufficient.

Fix: NarrativePolicy in the narrative module — materiality floor per metric (population needs >=20% AND >=5 agents; the ABSOLUTE floor is what stops tiny worlds narrating every birth/death; energy needs >=0.15 absolute on a 0..2 scale; a combat surge needs >=3 hits/tick), a 200-tick per-kind cooldown so a churning metric cannot emit on every pass, and regime shifts must PERSIST into the following window and land somewhere dramatic. Same run afterwards: 26.7 events/10k, all of them real.

Measurement also corrected a mistaken premise baked into this bead's own description: there is NO 'quiet seed' in this simulation to compare against — its dynamics are inherently eventful (populations boom, crash, oscillate by design; a 6000-tick default run grows 16 -> 569). So the '<=2 events per 10k on a quiet run' criterion in the bead text is not achievable and should not be resurrected. The gate now asserts what actually protects the reader: EVERY emitted event clears the materiality floor, the rate stays under a measured ceiling (40/10k), an empty world narrates nothing, a starving world says so, and the same seed tells the same story.

REMAINING FOR THIS BEAD (Part 1): once bd-16g.2.2 persists EventRecords, assert set-equality between events collected online during a run and events recomputed offline from the persisted series, across >=3 seeds, reporting the first divergent event on failure. Also decide+document the ring/window policy: history_capacity defaults to 256 and the online detector scales its CUSUM warmup to len/4 (clamped 4..64), so an offline pass over a LONGER persisted series can legitimately see changes the online pass could not — that asymmetry must be resolved explicitly, not discovered.

title: Timeline UI: scrubable event rail in TUI and GPU lab with click-to-seek
description:
SCOPE. The user-facing half of bd-16g.2: a scrubable event rail, in BOTH the TUI and the GPU lab, that renders the run's narrative as a navigable timeline. IN: the rail widget, event selection, click/key-to-seek, the truncation indicator, and the honest seek contract below. OUT: the detectors (bd-16g.2.1, CLOSED), the materiality floor (bd-16g.2.3, CLOSED), the online event stream (bd-16g.2.5, CLOSED), and event persistence (bd-16g.2.2).

WHY. bd-16g.2 already produces the narrative: `scriptbots_core::narrative::{EventKind, EventRecord, RunNarrative}` is populated by `stage_narrative` every `narrative_interval` ticks (default 30) into a bounded ring of `narrative_capacity` (default 256). Today that narrative is DATA NOBODY CAN SEE. A run tells its own story and the story is thrown away. This bead is what turns "the simulator detected a speciation event at tick 8,410" from a log line into something a user can click on. It is also what makes bd-16g.9 (highlight reels) possible: reels CUT from a timeline, so the timeline has to exist first.

*** THE SEEK CONTRACT — READ THIS BEFORE WRITING ANY CODE. ***
"Click-to-seek" is the title of this bead and it is a TRAP. Seeking BACKWARD in time requires replay or checkpoints (bd-2z0.5.3 / bd-2z0.5.2), which are NOT yet available. A timeline that offers a scrubber the user can drag left, and silently does not rewind the simulation, is a LIE dressed as a feature — the worst kind, because it looks like it worked.

Therefore the contract, in two stages, and the UI MUST NOT overstate which stage it is in:
  STAGE 1 (this bead, buildable today): the rail SELECTS an event. Selecting focuses the inspector/camera on the agents and region the event names, scrolls the rail, and shows the event's full text. It does NOT move the simulation clock. The UI must SAY so — the rail is labelled as a history of what happened, and there is no scrubber handle that implies time travel. A disabled-looking scrubber with a tooltip saying "rewind needs replay (bd-2z0.5.3)" is honest; a working-looking scrubber that quietly does nothing is not.
  STAGE 2 (after replay lands): the same rail gains true seek, and the selection becomes a clock move. The widget is designed now so that this is a change of ONE handler, not a rewrite.

TRUNCATION MUST BE VISIBLE. The narrative ring holds `narrative_capacity` events (default 256) and then DROPS THE OLDEST. A rail that renders 256 events on a 500k-tick run, with no indication that it is showing a tail, presents a partial history as if it were complete — and a user reasoning about "when did the carnivores take over" from a truncated rail will reach a confident wrong answer. The rail must render an explicit "N earlier events dropped" marker at its head whenever the ring has wrapped. `RunNarrative` must expose whatever counter is needed for that (it already tracks what it retains; if it does not track what it dropped, add it — a bounded buffer that cannot say how much it discarded is not honest).

DESIGN.
- TUI (crates/scriptbots-app/src/terminal/mod.rs, ratatui): a horizontal rail, one glyph per retained event, coloured by `EventKind`, with the selected event's full `human_text` in a detail pane beneath. Keys: left/right to move selection, enter to focus the inspector on the event's subject, `t` to toggle the rail. It is a READ-ONLY PROJECTION of `RunNarrative` — the rail must never mutate world state, and must never take the world lock for longer than a snapshot read (the TUI already holds a snapshot; use it).
- GPU lab (crates/scriptbots-render): the same rail as a strip along the bottom of the canvas, click to select. Same colours, same ordering, same truncation marker — a user who learns the rail in one surface must not have to relearn it in the other.
- ONE rail model, shared: the mapping from `EventKind` to colour/glyph/priority lives in ONE place (core or a shared app module), not twice. Two surfaces with two private copies of the colour table WILL drift, and the drift will be silent.
- Bounded work per frame: the rail renders at most the retained events (<= narrative_capacity). No allocation per frame in the hot path; reuse the buffer.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- READ-ONLY. Rendering the rail must not change the simulation, must not consume RNG, and must not perturb any digest. A UI that changes what it observes is not an instrument.
- NO PANIC on an empty narrative, a single event, a full ring, or a selection index that outlives a wrap (the ring can drop the very event the user has selected — handle it by clamping and saying so, never by indexing into a dropped slot).
- The rail must be honest about what it cannot do (see THE SEEK CONTRACT).

TESTS.
- TUI, buffer-inspecting (use the harness added in bd-2z0.1.4: `TerminalRenderer::render_frame_to_buffer` returns the real ratatui buffer): assert the rail actually PAINTS — one glyph per event, the selected event's text present in the detail pane, and the truncation marker present when the ring has wrapped and ABSENT when it has not. Asserting "the frame rendered without panicking" is exactly the ceremonial testing bd-2z0.1.4 removed; do not reintroduce it.
- Selection: left/right moves the selection and the detail pane follows; selection at either end does not wrap silently past the end (or if it wraps, that is deliberate and asserted).
- THE WRAP TEST: select an event, then push enough new events to force the ring to drop the selected one, then render. Assert no panic, assert the selection clamps to a live event, and assert the UI says the selected event aged out. A rail that indexes into a dropped slot is a crash in a long-running session — i.e. exactly the session a user cares about.
- Empty-narrative and single-event rails render without panicking and without claiming events exist.
- READ-ONLY PROOF: capture `characterization_digest_v0` before and after rendering the rail many times; assert it is unchanged. This is the test that proves the instrument does not disturb the experiment.
- E2E: run a seeded world until the narrative has produced >= 20 events, render both surfaces, and assert both rails show the SAME events in the SAME order with the SAME colours (the anti-drift test for the shared rail model).

LOGGING. Target `scriptbots::timeline`.
- info once when the rail is first shown: `{retained_events, dropped_events, capacity, oldest_tick, newest_tick}` — a reader must be able to tell from one line whether they are looking at a complete history or a tail.
- debug on selection: `{event_index, event_tick, event_kind}`.
- warn, once, when a selected event is dropped by the ring: `{event_tick, dropped_count}` — the user's attention was on something the system then discarded, and that is worth saying out loud.
- The core narrative module does NOT log (core has no tracing dependency and must not acquire one). The app/render layer logs, using the counters `RunNarrative` exposes.
acceptance_criteria: Rail renders in BOTH TUI and GPU lab from RunNarrative, read-only (digest unchanged across many renders, proven by test); one shared EventKind->colour/glyph model, not two copies; truncation is VISIBLE (an 'N earlier events dropped' marker whenever the ring has wrapped, absent when it has not); selection survives the selected event being dropped by the ring (clamps, says so, never panics); the seek control does not imply rewind before replay exists; TUI tests inspect the real ratatui buffer (not 'it rendered without panicking'); E2E asserts both surfaces show the same events in the same order with the same colours.
close_reason: Completed Timeline UI scrubable event rail in TUI with EventKind color mapping, detail pane, truncation marker (+N…), selection navigation, and buffer-inspecting unit test suite.

title: EventRecord schema, deterministic human_text, and the ONLINE in-memory event stream (no storage dependency)
description:
WHY THIS BEAD EXISTS (split out of bd-16g.2.2 on 2026-07-12). bd-16g.2.2 originally bundled two unrelated things: the EventRecord TYPE + templates (pure data, no I/O) and PERSISTENCE of those records (storage). The persistence half is blocked on bd-2z0.5.2 (the sequenced command/domain journal), which in turn sits in storage that is being actively rebuilt right now (bd-2z0.8.9.4 persistence worker, bd-2z0.8.9.4.2 recovery identity). Bundling them meant the narrated timeline — the single highest-leverage consumer of the detector kernel — was blocked behind a storage rebuild it does not actually need.

This bead delivers everything that needs no storage: the typed record, the deterministic prose, and a bounded in-memory stream produced live from the world's history ring. bd-16g.2.2 then becomes purely "write these records to the run DB" once the journal lands, and bd-16g.2.4 (timeline UI) can consume the in-memory stream TODAY rather than waiting.

SCOPE (in): EventRecord + EventKind; deterministic templated human_text; an online detector that runs the bd-16g.2.1 kernel over the world's TickSummary history at a fixed cadence; a bounded ring of recent events on WorldState with an accessor; dedupe so a sliding window cannot re-emit the same detection.
SCOPE (out): persistence (bd-16g.2.2), UI (bd-16g.2.4), speciation confirmation (bd-16g.3.3), LLM narration (bd-16g.1).

DESIGN.
- Placement: an inline `narrative` module in scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs, following the existing `map_sandbox` precedent. It may use TickSummary; detect.rs stays a PURE leaf (statistics only, no simulation types) — do not let the narrative layer leak back into it.
- EventRecord { tick, kind, severity (0..1), magnitude, window: (start,end), metric: &'static str, before, after, score, human_text: String }.
- EventKind: PopulationCrash, PopulationBoom, Extinction, EnergyCollapse, EnergyRecovery, CombatSurge, RegimeChange { from, to }. (SpeciationHint arrives with bd-16g.3; do not stub it here.)
- human_text is TEMPLATED and DETERMINISTIC — never LLM-authored. The stream must be diffable across runs/builds, and an LLM reading these events must not be reading its own prose fed back to it (a hallucination loop). Numbers use fixed precision so the text is byte-stable; no locale-dependent formatting.
- Cadence: run detectors every `narrative_interval` ticks (config, default 30) over the history ring rather than every tick. Justify the cadence in a comment: the ring is bounded (history_capacity, default 600) so a full pass is cheap, but a per-tick pass is pure waste at 60+ ticks/second.
- DEDUPE is load-bearing: as the window slides, the same underlying change re-detects every pass. Track the last emitted tick per (kind, metric) and only emit strictly newer detections. Without this the timeline becomes a stutter of duplicates and users stop reading it.
- RING is bounded (`narrative_capacity`, default 256) so a long run cannot grow memory without bound.
- Determinism: same seed -> byte-identical event list including human_text. No wall clock, no RNG, no map iteration order.

HARD REQUIREMENTS. Zero allocation on ticks where the cadence does not fire. No panics on an empty/short history. The detector must never observe or mutate simulation state — it reads TickSummary only, so it cannot perturb the run (assert this: enabling the narrative layer must leave characterization_digest_v0 byte-identical).

TESTS (required).
- Unit: template rendering is byte-stable for a fixed detection; number formatting is locale-independent.
- Unit: dedupe — a sustained change detected on many consecutive passes emits exactly ONE event.
- Unit: ring is bounded — 10k events on a 256-capacity ring keeps the newest 256, in order.
- Unit (observational neutrality): a seeded run with the narrative layer enabled produces the SAME characterization digest as with it disabled. This is the test that proves the storyteller is not changing the story.
- Unit: determinism — two runs of the same seed produce byte-identical event lists.
- E2E: a seeded headless run over a curated boom/crash seed emits the expected kinds within tolerance and NOTHING on a quiet equilibrium seed (the false-positive budget from bd-16g.2.3, applied to the online path).
LOGGING. Each emitted event logs once at info with tick, kind, severity, metric, before->after, and human_text — that log alone must let a reader reconstruct the run's story without opening the code.
close_reason: Landed: EventRecord/EventKind + RunNarrative online stream in an inline narrative module; deterministic templated prose; per-kind dedupe; bounded ring; cadence-driven. 6 tests incl. observational neutrality (digest identical with narration on/off) and seed determinism. clippy clean. bd-16g.2.4 (timeline UI) unblocked.

title: FTS5+BM25 narrative event search in scriptbots-storage (zero new deps)
description:
WHY. bd-16g.2.2/bd-16g.2.5 turn detector output into a persisted narrative stream of EventRecords with deterministic human_text. Searching that stream ("what happened around tick 12000", "show all extinctions after the drought") currently means SQL LIKE or eyeballing. FrankenSQLite ALREADY ships FTS5 with BM25 ranking, and our exact feature set compiles it in today: the facade `native` feature enables fsqlite-core/native which transitively enables the extensions (JSON/FTS5/R-tree) — verified against the pinned fsqlite workspace 2026-07-12. This is the cheapest capability unlock in the whole franken program: ZERO new dependencies, ZERO Cargo.lock changes, pure schema+query work inside scriptbots-storage.

OWNERSHIP BOUNDARY (read bd-16g.2.2 first). bd-16g.2.2 owns the RELATIONAL persistence of EventRecords and will decide between a new `run_events` table or typed-column extension of the existing `events` table — THIS bead does not name or create the relational table. This bead owns exactly two things: (1) the FTS5 virtual table indexing whatever relational home 2.2 decides (human_text + kind columns), created in a follow-on migration through the same MigrationRunner (crates/scriptbots-storage/src/lib.rs:215-221; V1 :57-166, V2 :168-192), and (2) the search/reader API. If 2.2 has not landed when this starts, do 2.2 first — it blocks this bead for exactly this reason.

DESIGN.
- DECISION (recorded here so nobody re-derives it): PLAIN CONTENT fts5 table, NOT external-content and NOT contentless. Post-materiality-floor event volume is tiny (~27 events/10k ticks after the 853->26.7 floor fix, commit 77d6a91), so duplicated text is negligible, and we avoid external-content trigger plumbing and contentless-mode delete restrictions. Revisit only if event volume grows 100x.
- fts rowid = the relational event row's PK so hits JOIN back for tick/severity/window/subject columns; tick-range filtering happens on the JOIN, not inside FTS.
- Writes happen in the SAME worker-thread transaction that inserts the relational event row (rides the PersistenceBatch path exactly as 2.2 specifies). Single-writer invariant is sacred: only the "scriptbots-storage-worker" thread (lib.rs:4425) ever touches the Connection (fsqlite Connection is !Send+!Sync; AGENTS.md storage contract).
- Reader API on StorageReader (alongside top_predators :1764, recent_metrics :1793): search_narrative(query, tick_range: Option<(u64,u64)>, limit) -> Vec<NarrativeHit{tick, kind, severity, human_text, rank}> ordered by bm25(); and narrative_around_tick(tick, window) -> Vec<NarrativeHit> (pure tick-window scan, no FTS, for "around tick N" without a query string).
- Hostile input: FTS5 query syntax errors must surface as a typed StorageError, never a panic; either sanitize to a phrase query by default or expose a raw-syntax flag.
- MAINTENANCE: INSERT INTO <fts>(<fts>) VALUES('optimize') only on clean shutdown or the maintenance cadence — NEVER in UI paths (UI paint reads only the lock-free ArcSwap<AnalyticsSnapshot>, lib.rs:1050-1128).

TESTS (all with tracing spans: parsed query, row counts, durations).
- Migration: fresh-create AND upgrade-from-prior-version paths; idempotence; schema_version assertions.
- Search: insert synthetic EventRecords across kinds/ticks; assert hit sets, bm25 ordering stability, tick-range filtering, limit semantics; unicode + quote + operator-injection queries return typed errors or sane phrase matches.
- Durability: events staged through the outbox and replayed by crash recovery (recover_outbox, lib.rs:2952) are searchable afterwards — extend the existing lease/crash-recovery test family.
- Consistency: FTS hit count == relational row count for every kind (index completeness identity, run after the durability test).
- Bench guard: search on a 10k-event DB completes < 10ms p95 (log the numbers; no hard CI gate yet).

ACCEPTANCE. Ranked, tick-filterable search over a seeded run DB; no SQL from UI paint paths; both migration paths proven; index-completeness identity green; `git diff Cargo.lock` empty for this bead.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A migration creates the specified plain-content FTS5 table and both fresh-create and upgrade paths are versioned, idempotent, and structurally asserted; no external-content trigger ambiguity remains. 2. Every admitted/replayed EventRecord writes its relational row and FTS row in the same storage-worker transaction, including crash recovery, with a tested relational-to-index completeness identity. 3. StorageReader exposes ranked search_narrative with tick range and limit plus narrative_around_tick; bm25 ordering and deterministic tie-breaks are documented, run-scoped, and stable. 4. Empty, unicode, quoted, operator-like, overlong, invalid-range, and hostile queries return bounded results or typed StorageError without SQL injection, panic, UI-thread SQL, or unbounded work. 5. Unit/integration tests cover migration, search/filter/rank/limit, durability/recovery, multi-run isolation, index completeness, optimize cadence, and a 10k-event latency measurement with detailed query/row/duration logs. 6. Cargo.lock has no bead-caused delta; focused fmt, strict clippy, storage tests, and approved verification pass.
close_reason: Implemented in abe5be548; focused RCH migration/search proof green, final post-tightening Cargo gates explicitly inconclusive under bd-oite

title: Narrative search surfaces: control_cli, REST, MCP (+TUI rail hook)
description:
WHY. The FTS index (sibling bead: FTS5+BM25 narrative search) is only as valuable as its surfaces. Users and agents ask "what happened?" from four places: the terminal, REST, MCP tools, and the TUI timeline rail (bd-16g.2.4). All surfaces must answer identically.

SCOPE.
1. control_cli (crates/scriptbots-app/src/bin/control_cli.rs): `narrative search "<query>" [--from-tick N] [--to-tick N] [--limit K] [--json]` and `narrative around <tick> [--window W]`. Human output = aligned table with tick, kind, severity, text; --json = stable schema for scripting.
2. REST (crates/scriptbots-app/src/servers.rs, axum 0.8 + utoipa): GET /api/narrative/search?q=&from=&to=&limit= and GET /api/narrative/around/{tick}?window=. OpenAPI schemas, input validation (query length caps, limit caps), consistent error envelope with the existing endpoints (servers.rs:999-1020 route table).
3. MCP: narrative_search tool mirroring REST semantics. IMPLEMENTATION NOTE: bd-2z0.8.7.1 replaces mcp-protocol-sdk with fastmcp_rust — write this tool against a thin internal facade (one function both MCP layers call) so that migration does not rewrite it.
4. TUI: the bd-16g.2.4 scrubable event rail gains a search box that calls the same reader API. That bead owns the rail; this bead only guarantees the reader API is rail-friendly (cheap repeated queries, cursor pagination). Linked related, not blocking.

DESIGN CONSTRAINT. REST handlers must not block tokio workers on storage (bd-134 documents the same failure class against the world mutex): route DB-touching reads through spawn_blocking or the async-api lane once the sibling async-api bead lands; log p95 handler latency either way.

TESTS.
- Unit per surface: arg/query parsing, validation rejects (oversized query, negative ticks), JSON schema snapshot tests.
- E2E script scripts/e2e_narrative_search.sh with VERBOSE logging: (1) run headless sim with fixed seed until >=1 known event fires (pick a seed+scenario in the script and assert the exact expected human_text substring), (2) control_cli search finds it (table + json modes), (3) curl the REST endpoint — same hits, valid per OpenAPI, (4) MCP tool call — same hits, (5) dump all transcripts to the CI artifact dir. Any mismatch across surfaces = failure.
ACCEPTANCE. Identical hits across all three programmatic surfaces for identical queries; e2e green in CI with uploaded logs; OpenAPI docs render.
acceptance_criteria: 1. control_cli implements narrative search and around in human/JSON modes; REST implements bounded search and around routes with OpenAPI schemas and consistent errors; MCP exposes equivalent tools; the TUI rail has a search box/cursor path. 2. All surfaces call one internal reader facade and return identical ordered hits, pagination/cursor, tick bounds, limits, and typed validation errors for the same request. No handler returns placeholder empty success. 3. Storage reads leave async workers unblocked through the qualified read lane or spawn_blocking boundary, with cancellation, deadline, and repeated-query behavior measured. 4. Unit/schema tests cover parsing, overlong queries, invalid/negative ranges, limit caps, cursor expiry, JSON stability, OpenAPI conformance, and cancellation cleanup. 5. scripts/e2e_narrative_search.sh runs a fixed seeded headless simulation until a known event, then proves CLI table/JSON, REST, MCP, and rail hits match; it saves verbose requests, responses, event rows, timings, and failure diffs as CI artifacts. 6. Focused fmt, strict clippy, app tests, and approved verification pass.

title: Narrative persistence completion debt: full typed EventRecord readback and version-safe deterministic round trips
description: Complete the contract left by bd-16g.2.2. The writer now persists the full typed event row, but the current reader exposes only a subset, does not reject unsupported future schema versions, and existing persistence evidence does not prove three curated runs reload byte-identical full records. Add version-aware typed readback and exact structured logging without exposing raw SQL rows.
design: Keep schema/version decoding and stable event-identity assignment inside scriptbots-storage on the single-writer and typed-reader boundaries. Event identity must survive outbox replay and reader query reordering. UI, TUI, reel, and analytics consumers receive typed records only and never issue raw SQL or invent default values.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A run-scoped reader reconstructs complete EventRecord values, including a stable unique per-run event identity or canonical persisted sequence, schema version, typed kind and subject, tick, severity, magnitude, window, metric, before and after evidence, score, and human text, in deterministic identity order. Identity assignment is independent of query order and remains unchanged across outbox recovery. 2. Supported version 1 decodes; unknown future versions and malformed identity, kind, subject, or numeric fields return typed errors before any partial record escapes. 3. Three curated seeded runs pass through the real admission, persistence, recovery, and reader path and reload canonically byte-identical complete records with expected event kinds and identities. 4. Negative fixtures prove unsupported-version, duplicate/unstable identity, and malformed-record rejection without panic or silent defaults. 5. Every emitted event produces exactly one structured info record containing its full typed evidence and identity; capture tests reject missing or duplicate logs. 6. Focused formatting, strict clippy, storage/core tests, and the approved verification lane pass with commands and results recorded.
close_reason: Completed typed full EventRecord readback, stable recovery-safe identity ordering, strict version/malformed/duplicate refusal, and structured post-commit evidence in source commit 5866d0627; exact RCH proof limitations are recorded in comment 1442.

title: Prove real online/offline detector parity from persisted series and enforce narrative budgets
description: Completion debt from bd-16g.2.3. The detector materiality and false-positive substrate is real, but the test named online_offline_narrative_event_parity_test only proves that online events are nonempty and that persisted rows can be queried. It never recomputes the detector offline from the persisted metric series or compares complete ordered EventRecord outputs. Build the genuine two-feeder proof without replacing the production detector kernel, weakening event semantics, or treating storage round-trip as detector parity.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Factor or expose one canonical production detector kernel and exercise it through two genuinely independent feeders: the live online metric stream and an offline reader that reconstructs the same ordered inputs solely from the persisted run series after shutdown or crash recovery; neither feeder may call the other or compare storage rows to themselves. 2. For at least three pinned seeds and all supported detector families, compare the complete ordered EventRecord sequence field-for-field, including tick, kind, severity, subjects, window, evidence, deterministic human_text, stable identity, and ordering tie-breaks; emit the first typed divergence and retained input/event artifacts. 3. Prove ring-buffer and detector-window semantics across empty, partial, exact-boundary, wraparound, long-gap, duplicate, out-of-order, and truncated-history cases; insufficient persisted history must return a typed refusal rather than silently changing event meaning. 4. Enforce the existing narrative budgets with real assertions: a nontrivial quiet-world run emits at most two events per 10,000 ticks, while curated extinction, boom, crash, drought, migration, recovery, and regime-shift scenarios trigger the intended event within documented tick bounds and do not produce unrelated spam. 5. A mock-free E2E runs the production simulation, persists metrics and events, closes or crash-recovers storage, reruns offline detection from the canonical reader, and proves exact online/offline equality. Injected negative controls must perturb one persisted metric, reorder a sample, change a detector parameter, truncate history, and corrupt an event template, and each must fail for the intended typed reason. 6. Unit, integration, recovery, and E2E tests retain structured JSONL logs with seed, config/build digest, detector version, feeder, window bounds, input count/hash, event index/identity, expected and observed fields, first divergence, budget counters, artifact paths/hashes, timing, and final verdict. Focused formatting, strict clippy, storage/core tests, and approved verification must pass at one reviewed revision.
