title: Novelty score (k-NN in behavior space) and selection modes with inert-when-off proof
description:
SCOPE. The novelty score (k-NN in behavior space), the selection-mode plumbing that lets novelty actually influence who reproduces, and the "provably inert when off" proof. Consumes bd-16g.6.1's descriptors/archive. Does not own QD metrics or resurrection (bd-16g.6.3).

WHY. Without this, bd-16g.6.1 is a passive scrapbook. The parent bead's whole claim — "evolution that goes somewhere instead of converging" — lives or dies here. It is also the bead with the highest blast radius in the epic: it is the only one that reaches into `stage_reproduction`, i.e. into the RNG-ordered heart of the deterministic kernel. Every hard requirement below exists because that edit is the most dangerous one in bd-16g.6.

TWO CODE FACTS THAT CHANGE THE DESIGN (read before writing a line):
1. There is NO selection operator in ScriptBots. There is no generational GA, no tournament, no population-level fitness sort. Reproduction is a per-agent gate in `stage_reproduction`: energy above `reproduction_energy_threshold`, cooldown expired, attempt cadence fires, then a single RNG draw against `reproduction_attempt_chance` (clamped [0,1]). "selection_mode" therefore CANNOT be a selection operator — it must be a modulation of that gate. Writing it as a GA selection step would mean rewriting the kernel, which this bead must not do.
2. `SelectionMode` ALREADY EXISTS in scriptbots-core as the UI selection enum (Replace/Add/Clear, used by `SelectionUpdate`/`ControlCommand::UpdateSelection`). Naming a new evolution enum `SelectionMode` guarantees a confusing collision in every import list. Name it `EvolutionSelectionMode` and put it at `config.evolution.selection_mode`.

DESIGN.
- Pure scoring fn, no WorldState: `fn novelty_scores(pop: &[BehaviorDescriptor], archive: &[BehaviorDescriptor], k: usize) -> Vec<f32>` in the same `qd` module. Score = mean Euclidean distance to the k nearest neighbours among (population ∪ archive), self excluded, ties broken by index. Distances are computed in NORMALIZED descriptor space (each axis mapped to [0,1] by its declared domain). Failure mode prevented: an axis with domain [0, 1000] otherwise dominates every distance and "novelty" silently becomes "unusual speed" — the classic novelty-search implementation bug.
- `EvolutionSelectionMode { Fitness, Novelty, Curiosity { w: f32 } }` (default `Fitness`). Curiosity score = `w * novelty_norm + (1 - w) * fitness_norm`, both normalized per-tick against the population's own range (documented; a raw mix of a distance and an energy is meaningless).
- Coupling into the kernel: in `stage_reproduction`, the compared probability becomes `p = clamp01(config.reproduction_attempt_chance * modulator(agent))`, where `modulator(..) == 1.0` IDENTICALLY under `Fitness`. You may change the value the draw is compared against. You may NEVER change the NUMBER of RNG draws, their order, or their position in the tick. That invariant is the whole game.
- Cadence: novelty is recomputed every `archive_interval` ticks (default 100), not per tick — naive k-NN is O(N^2). Document the budget (N <= 8k, k = 15, D <= 8). Scores live in `Option<NoveltyState>` on the world, indexed by agent slot, and are reused between recomputes.
- Anti-coupling: the scorer sees only descriptors. It does not see WorldState, storage, or config beyond `k`. bd-16g.6.3 consumes its output; nothing else does.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- Zero additional RNG draws in `Fitness` mode; in any mode, exactly ONE draw per eligible agent per attempt, in the same order as today. (In `Novelty`/`Curiosity` the downstream RNG stream will legitimately diverge because a different set of agents reproduces — that is the feature. The bug is a diverging DRAW COUNT, not a diverging world.)
- No panics: k > population-1 clamps to what exists; a single agent with an empty archive scores 0.0 with no division by zero; a degenerate all-identical population scores 0.0 everywhere (and logs — see LOGGING).
- Determinism: index-order accumulation, stable ties, no HashMap, no wall-clock.

TESTS.
- Unit (k-NN fixture): five hand-placed points on a line, k=2, exact expected mean distances. A second fixture in 3-D with a hand-computed answer.
- Unit (NEGATIVE — normalization): two candidates that rank one way under raw Euclidean distance and the OTHER way under domain-normalized distance. Assert the implementation produces the normalized ranking. This is the test that catches the dominant-axis bug, and nothing else does.
- Unit (INERT-WHEN-OFF, the headline): a 10k-tick pinned-seed, pinned-config run with the qd/novelty code COMPILED IN and the archive ENABLED, under `selection_mode = fitness`, produces a `characterization_digest_v0` byte-identical to the checked-in pre-feature fixture — including the RNG probe words. The RNG probe is what catches an extra draw hidden behind a disabled branch; assert it explicitly rather than trusting the aggregate digest to notice.
- Unit (draw-count contract): using bd-2z0.3.1's RandomStream (or a counting wrapper in the test harness), assert that a single tick over a fixed population consumes an IDENTICAL number of draws under Fitness, Novelty, and Curiosity. Divergent worlds are fine; a divergent draw count is a bug.
- Unit (degenerate): k=0 -> typed error; k > N -> clamps; empty population -> empty result; all-identical descriptors -> all zeros, no NaN.
- E2E (acceptance): two 20k-tick runs on the same seed, `fitness` vs `novelty`. The fitness arm must be SHOWN to converge (behavior-space coverage plateaus — plot/assert the curve; do not assume it), and the novelty arm must reach materially higher coverage and QD-score at the same tick budget (metrics from bd-16g.6.3). Report both arms even if the result is negative.

LOGGING. Target `scriptbots::qd::novelty`. info every recompute {tick, mode, k, population, archive_size, mean_novelty, p50, p95, max}. debug: the five most novel uids with their descriptors and scores. warn when `mean_novelty == 0.0` for three consecutive samples — that is the silent failure where novelty search is "on" and scoring nothing (collapsed descriptor, empty archive, or a mis-scaled axis), and it looks exactly like a boring world from the outside. warn once at startup when mode != Fitness, naming the mode and the digest consequence ("world trajectories will not match fitness-mode fixtures"), so nobody files a determinism bug against an opt-in feature they forgot they enabled.
design: Use EvolutionSelectionMode to avoid collision with the UI SelectionMode. Score typed descriptors in normalized declared domains, exclude self, use deterministic index and UID tie-breaking, and bound k, dimensions, and population. Recompute at bd-16g.6.1 cadence and cache typed NoveltyState. Integrate by modulating the existing reproduction probability without adding, removing, or reordering RNG draws. Curiosity validates finite w in [0,1] and combines normalized fitness and novelty with documented degenerate-range semantics. Metrics, export, and resurrection remain in bd-16g.6.3.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Unit fixtures cover 1-D and 3-D k-NN, self-exclusion, population-plus-archive membership, normalized-rank inversion, distance ties, empty, singleton, all-identical, k=0, k>N, dimension mismatch, nonfinite input, and curiosity weights 0, 1, and out of range. 2. Counting-RandomStream tests prove identical draw count and order for equivalent eligible populations in every mode. 3. Fitness mode with QD compiled and the archive enabled is byte-identical to the pinned fixture, including RNG probe words. 4. Novelty and curiosity alter reproduction probability and trajectories without bypassing eligibility or cooldown. 5. A checked-in real E2E selection script runs matched-seed fitness and novelty arms, validates a predeclared convergence and coverage envelope, retains both positive and negative outcomes, and records source/config/digest/metric/log/exit artifacts. 6. Structured logs include tick, mode, k, population and archive sizes, descriptor and space digests, novelty p50/p95/max, top UIDs and descriptors, reproduction modulators, draw counts, and zero-novelty warnings.
notes: Audit comment 929 is the baseline. An enum or archive-only distance helper is not selection integration or inert proof.

title: QD metrics (coverage, QD-score), archive export, and resurrect-from-archive spawning
description:
SCOPE. Quality-diversity metrics over the archive (coverage, QD-score, archive-diff), provenance-rich export, and resurrect-from-archive spawning. Consumes bd-16g.6.1 (archive) and bd-16g.6.2 (novelty). This is the bead that turns the archive from an internal data structure into a shareable scientific artifact and a reusable behavior library. WHY. Two payoffs the parent bead is explicit about. (1) The archive is the durable result: "here are the 400 distinct viable lifestyles this world produced" beats "here is a champion" — but only if the numbers are comparable across runs and the file is readable without the build that wrote it. (2) Resurrection makes the archive an ACTUATOR: cross-run transfer experiments, seeding a new world with proven lifestyles, and the LLM scientist (bd-16g.1) asking for "the top 20 carnivore elites, injected into a fresh world." DESIGN. - Metrics, pure fn: `fn qd_metrics(&MapElitesArchive) -> QdMetrics { filled, total, coverage, qd_score_raw, qd_score_norm, max_quality, mean_quality, occupancy_entropy }`. Report BOTH raw and normalized QD-score, and state in the struct docs which one is comparable across configs (raw sums are not: they scale with the quality function and the cell count). An unlabeled QD-score in a plot is a number nobody can interpret six months later. - Float order: sum qualities in CellId order with a documented compensated (Kahan/Neumaier) summation. Summing 4,000 f32s in a different order gives a different number, and this number goes into a comparison table. The test below enforces it. - Archive-diff: `fn archive_diff(a, b) -> ArchiveDiff { only_in_a, only_in_b, improved_in_b, regressed_in_b }` keyed by CellId, requiring IDENTICAL `space_version` on both sides — comparing archives across different behavior spaces is a category error and must be a typed error, not a silent join. - Export through bd-2z0.5.6 (Arrow/Parquet/CSV), with provenance columns on every row: run_id, root_seed, config_digest, build identity, space_version, quality_fn_version, genome_version. An export without the axis definitions and the quality function version is scientifically useless — self-describing or nothing. - CLI (subcommands under scriptbots-app): `archive stats --run `, `archive export --run --format parquet --out

`, `archive diff `. - Resurrection is NOT a bespoke API. It is `Intervention::SpawnFromArchive { cells: CellSelector, count, placement }` routed through bd-16g.10's ControlCommand path, validated, journaled, and replayable. `CellSelector { All | TopKByQuality(u16) | AxisRange(Vec<(axis, lo, hi)>) | Explicit(Vec) }`. - Genome decode goes through bd-2z0.3.2's versioned protocol. An archive genome the running build cannot decode is REJECTED with a typed error naming both versions — NEVER silently replaced with a fresh random brain. A silently-random resurrection turns a transfer experiment into noise that looks like a result, and nobody would ever notice. - Placement draws from the existing spawn RNG at the existing point (`stage_spawn_commit`) or from a seeded stream carried in the command (preferred, bd-2z0.3.1). Do not open a new RNG call site inside the intervention stage. HARD REQUIREMENTS. - Determinism: same archive + same command -> same digest; same archive -> byte-identical export bytes (pin Parquet compression/row-group settings, or the "same file" hashes differently on two machines). - Atomicity: a resurrect that would exceed the population cap is rejected WHOLE. No half-cohorts. A partially-applied cohort is an experiment nobody can describe. - No panics on: empty archive (coverage 0, qd 0, no NaN — 0/0 is the obvious trap), all-zero qualities, a CellSelector matching nothing. TESTS. - Unit: metrics on hand-built archives — empty -> {coverage 0.0, qd 0.0} with no NaN; a full archive of quality 1.0 -> {coverage 1.0, qd_raw == total}; a half-full archive -> exact expected values. - Unit (NEGATIVE — float order): build the same archive by inserting entries in 20 different permutations; assert `qd_score_raw` is bit-identical across all of them. This is the test that forces the compensated sum; a naive f32 fold fails it. - Unit: archive_diff across mismatched space_versions -> typed error, not a join. - E2E: export -> read back with an independent reader -> recompute metrics -> identical to the in-process values; two exports of the same archive are byte-identical. - E2E (NEGATIVE — the one that matters): resurrect from an archive whose genome_version the build does not support -> typed error, ZERO agents spawned, population count before == after, journal row records the rejection with both versions. This test is the only thing standing between us and a silent fallback to random brains. - NEGATIVE: a resurrect of 500 agents into a world with 30 slots of headroom is rejected wholesale (population unchanged), with the error naming requested vs headroom. - NEGATIVE: `CellSelector::Explicit` naming cells that do not exist -> spawns only the matched cells, logs the shortfall, and reports matched vs requested in the journal row (silently spawning fewer agents than asked is how a transfer study loses half its treatment arm). - Determinism: resurrect at tick T in two worlds from the same seed -> identical `characterization_digest_v0`. LOGGING. Target `scriptbots::qd`. info on export {run_id, rows, path, bytes, coverage, qd_score_raw, qd_score_norm, space_version, quality_version, config_digest, build}. info on resurrect {tick, selector, cells_requested, cells_matched, agents_spawned, agents_rejected, reason}. warn when cells_matched < cells_requested. info on `archive stats` printing the full QdMetrics as structured fields so a CI job can grep the exploration curve out of the log without opening the DB.
design: Compute raw and normalized QD scores, occupancy entropy, mean and maximum quality, and coverage in CellId order with compensated accumulation. Refuse archive comparisons across differing space or quality-function versions. Reuse bd-2z0.5.6 export infrastructure with deterministic writer settings and no wall-clock metadata. Implement archive-specific CLI commands. Route SpawnFromArchive through the existing versioned intervention, journal, and replay path; decode only through the versioned genome protocol and reject cap or version failures atomically. Storage and generic transport primitives remain with their owners.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Unit tests cover empty/full/partial/all-zero archives, compensated-order invariance over permutations, normalized-score semantics, entropy, and typed version-mismatch diff refusal. 2. CSV, Arrow, and Parquet exports are self-describing, independently readable, canonically ordered, and byte-identical under pinned settings; readback recomputes identical metrics. 3. CLI stats, export, and diff commands cover success, invalid-version, missing-run, and bounded-output cases. 4. Resurrection tests cover every selector, unsupported genome, missing cells, population cap, deterministic placement, duplicate command and replay, and wholesale rejection without partial mutation. 5. A checked-in real E2E export-and-resurrect script runs a world, exports/reloads/diffs the archive, resurrects through a real control surface, replays the command, and compares population, journal, archive, and science digests with retained detailed evidence. 6. Structured logs include run/config/space/quality/genome versions, export rows/bytes/digest/path, metric values, selector/request/match counts, spawned/rejected counts, command/journal IDs, and typed refusal reasons.
notes: Audit comment 930 is the baseline. bd-16g.6.1 owns archive persistence; this bead consumes it. General export and intervention transport remain with their existing owners.

title: Emergent communication laboratory: evolvable signaling channel with information-theoretic instrumentation
description:
THE IDEA. Turn the existing-but-vestigial sound channel into a real emergent-communication laboratory. Agents already EMIT sound (output 7, sound_level, scaled by an evolvable sound_multiplier) and HEAR it (input 18, hearing; input 9, sound). Today that loop is decorative: nothing measures whether signals carry information, and there is no pressure that would make them. Add (a) an evolvable, multi-band signaling channel (a small vector of emitted values rather than one scalar), (b) instrumentation that measures information transfer between emitted signals and receiver behavior / world state (mutual information, transfer entropy), and (c) scenario presets that CREATE selective pressure for communication (e.g. food visible only to a stationary "sentinel" role; predator alarm scenarios).

WHY IT MATTERS. Emergent communication is one of the most captivating results in all of artificial life — and ScriptBots is one line of pressure away from being able to produce it, with the channel already wired end-to-end. This is genuinely NOVEL science for this codebase (not a port of legacy behavior), it is a magnet for attention, and it gives the brain testbed a task where architectures differ dramatically (recurrent/DWRAON should crush stateless MLP at signaling). The instrumentation is what makes it a LAB rather than a demo: a claim like "signals became informative at t=30k" must be backed by a number.

DESIGN.
- Channel: extend outputs/inputs by a configurable number of signal bands (default 1 = exactly legacy behavior; N>1 is opt-in). This touches INPUT_SIZE/OUTPUT_SIZE, so it MUST go through the versioned genome/evaluator protocol (bd-2z0.3.2) and the centralized output map (bd-2z0.2.4) — a naive index shuffle would silently break every brain, which is precisely the failure class we already had (boost read the green channel for months).
- Metrics: mutual information I(signal_emitted ; food_nearby) and I(signal_heard ; receiver_turn_toward_food), plus transfer entropy emitter->receiver; computed offline from the event stream at a fixed cadence with a documented estimator and bias correction (small-sample MI is dangerously biased — the estimator choice is part of the deliverable, not an afterthought).
- Pressure scenarios (reuse bd-2z0.10.1 schema): "sentinel" (food only sensed within a small radius; sharing pays), "alarm" (predators approach from one side; early warning saves the group).
- Honesty guard: publishing "communication emerged" requires the MI to exceed a SHUFFLED-CONTROL baseline (permute emitter/receiver pairings) — implement the control as part of the metric, not as an optional extra.

ACCEPTANCE. On the sentinel scenario, a lineage with signal-conditioned behavior arises and its MI exceeds the shuffled control by a documented margin with CIs; with N=1 band and the feature at defaults, digests are identical to pre-feature runs.

TESTS + LOGGING (required).
- Unit: MI/transfer-entropy estimators against analytically known distributions (independent -> ~0 after bias correction; deterministic copy channel -> ~1 bit); shuffled-control baseline behaves as expected.
- Unit: signal band plumbing — a brain emitting a known pattern produces exactly those values at the listener's inputs at the documented attenuation.
- Unit: default config (1 band) is digest-identical to pre-feature builds.
- E2E: run the sentinel scenario for 100k ticks on a pinned seed; persist per-tick signal/behavior series; compute MI + control offline; assert the pipeline runs end-to-end and log the MI trajectory (tick, MI, control_MI, CI) at info so "did it emerge?" is answerable from the log.

title: Multi-band signal channel behind the versioned genome protocol (default=legacy)
description:
SCOPE. Turn the single scalar sound emission into a configurable N-band signal channel, behind the versioned genome/evaluator protocol (bd-2z0.3.2) and the centralized output map (bd-2z0.2.4). Default `bands = 1` must be BYTE-IDENTICAL to the pre-feature build. Instrumentation is bd-16g.7.2; pressure scenarios are bd-16g.7.3.

THREE CODE FACTS THAT CORRECT THE PARENT BEAD (verify them yourself in crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs before designing):
1. `sound_multiplier` IS NOT AN EVOLVABLE GENE. It is a per-tick latch: `stage_actuation` writes `runtime.sound_multiplier = results[idx].sound_level` (i.e. `outputs[7]`) every tick. There is no heritable amplitude gene, no mutation on it, nothing evolvable about it. Any design (or paper) that says "an evolvable sound_multiplier scales the emission" is describing code that does not exist. Either introduce a real heritable amplitude gene as an EXPLICIT, digest-affecting change in this bead, or stop calling it evolvable. Do not perpetuate the fiction.
2. `sensors[9]` ("sound") IS NOT THE SIGNAL CHANNEL. It accumulates `dist_factor * speed_norm[other]` — it is LOCOMOTION NOISE (how fast your neighbours are moving). The emitted signal is heard ONLY at `sensors[18]` ("hearing"), which accumulates `dist_factor * sound_emitters[other]` where `sound_emitters[idx] == runtime.sound_multiplier`. This distinction is load-bearing for bd-16g.7.2: computing MI against `sensors[9]` would "discover communication" that is nothing but correlated movement.
3. NEWBORNS INHERIT AN EMISSION. `build_child_runtime` clones the parent runtime and resets `sound_output` but NOT `sound_multiplier` — so a newborn broadcasts its parent's last emitted level during its first sensed tick, before its own brain has ever run. Initially-spawned agents use `AgentRuntime::default()`, i.e. `sound_multiplier = 1.0`: every founder screams at full volume on tick 1. Document this. If you fix it, the fix CHANGES DIGESTS and therefore belongs in the bands>1 lane behind the version gate, never as a drive-by.

WHY. The channel is wired end to end and nobody has ever studied it; one scalar band is barely a channel. This bead is the only structural change in bd-16g.7 — .2 and .3 are pure analysis and pure config on top of it. It is also the single riskiest edit in the epic: it changes INPUT_SIZE/OUTPUT_SIZE, and the historical precedent is ugly (combat read `outputs[3]` — the GREEN colour channel — as "boost" for months, and nothing caught it). Index shuffles in this codebase are silent.

DESIGN.
- `INPUT_SIZE = 25` and `OUTPUT_SIZE = 9` are `pub const`s, and the `Brain` trait is `fn tick(&mut self, inputs: &[f32; INPUT_SIZE]) -> [f32; OUTPUT_SIZE]` — FIXED-SIZE ARRAYS. bands>1 therefore cannot be bolted on. The trait must become slice-based (`fn tick(&mut self, inputs: &[f32]) -> &[f32]`, or const-generic over the layout) with a `WorldIoLayout { version: u16, bands: u8, inputs: usize, outputs: usize }` validated at brain-registration time. That touches scriptbots-brain, -brain-ml, -brain-neuro. This is exactly why the parent bead insists it go through bd-2z0.3.2: there is no cheap version of this change, and pretending otherwise produces the boost/green bug at scale.
- Band 0 MUST map to the existing indices: emit at `outputs[7]`, hear at `sensors[18]`. Extra bands are APPENDED at the end (`outputs[9..9+n-1]`, `sensors[25..25+n-1]`). Append, never insert — an insertion renumbers `give_intent` and every brain in every checkpoint silently means something else.
- Emitter buffer: today `work_sound_emitters: Vec<f32>` is one f32 per agent. It becomes `agent_idx * bands + band` (agent-major, documented). A stride bug here is SILENT — it just mixes bands together and the MI analysis reports a channel that carries information it does not carry. The band-isolation test below is the only thing that catches it.
- Attenuation must reproduce today's semantics for band 0 exactly: `heard[b] += dist_factor * emitted[other][b]` where `dist_factor = (radius - dist) / radius` (LINEAR, not inverse-square), summed over all neighbours inside `sense_radius`, then `clamp01`. Note the consequences and document them for bd-16g.7.2: hearing SATURATES at 1.0 in a crowd, and it is a SUM, so an agent cannot distinguish one loud neighbour from four quiet ones. That is a channel property, not a bug — but an MI estimate that ignores saturation will under-report capacity.
- All output decoding goes through bd-2z0.2.4's centralized map. No new raw index literals anywhere; the map is the single source of truth.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- `bands = 1` is provably inert: byte-identical digests, identical RNG draw counts, identical brain I/O sizes.
- Layout mismatch is a typed error at registration (`IoLayoutMismatch { expected, actual, brain_kind }`), never a runtime slice panic and never a silent truncation.
- No panics: a brain returning the wrong number of outputs is rejected; a `bands` value of 0 or > 8 is rejected at `validate()`.
- Determinism: band accumulation in agent-index order, clamped identically on every target.

TESTS.
- Unit (INERT-WHEN-OFF, headline): `bands = 1`, 10k-tick pinned seed -> `characterization_digest_v0` byte-identical to the checked-in pre-feature fixture. Assert the RNG probe words too.
- Unit (BAND ISOLATION — the stride test): three agents at known distances; A emits [1.0, 0.0, 0.0], B emits [0.0, 1.0, 0.0]. Assert the listener's `heard` vector equals the hand-computed per-band sums with the documented linear attenuation, and that band 2 is EXACTLY 0.0. A stride bug fails this and passes everything else.
- Unit (band-0 equivalence): with bands=3, an agent emitting only on band 0 produces exactly the `sensors[18]` value the pre-feature build produced for the same emission and geometry.
- Unit (saturation): five loud neighbours -> heard clamps to 1.0, does not overflow, does not go negative.
- Unit (layout): registering an MLP brain built for the old 25/9 layout against a bands=3 world -> typed error naming expected vs actual sizes. NEGATIVE: assert it does NOT silently zero-pad — a zero-padded brain runs, produces plausible garbage, and is undebuggable.
- Unit (newborn emission): pin the documented behaviour from code fact 3 in a test, so that whichever way we decide, a future change to it is a deliberate, visible, digest-affecting decision.

LOGGING. Target `scriptbots::comms::channel`. info once at world construction {io_layout_version, bands, inputs, outputs, band0_emit_index, band0_hear_index} — the layout must be recoverable from any run's log, because six months from now the only way to interpret an archived series is to know which index was which. warn once when bands > 1 ("world digests will not match legacy fixtures; io_layout_version=N"). error on layout mismatch with brain kind, expected, and actual. debug (sampled, rate-limited) per-tick per-band emission histogram so a dead channel (every agent emitting 0.0, or every agent saturated at 1.0) is visible in the log before someone spends a week computing MI on a constant.
notes: 2026-07-20 (VioletHawk, claimed then honestly de-scoped): assessed the IO-layout wiring before touching code. INPUT_SIZE=25 / OUTPUT_SIZE=9 are COMPILE-TIME arrays ([f32; INPUT_SIZE]/[f32; OUTPUT_SIZE]) baked into the Brain trait signature (fn tick(&mut self, inputs: &[f32; INPUT_SIZE]) -> [f32; OUTPUT_SIZE]), AgentData sensor/output arrays, every brain family, genome envelopes, digest encoders, checkpoints, and the WASM snapshot ABI. A real N-band channel brains can consume requires runtime-sized IO (Vec or MAX_BANDS-masked arrays), which is a trait-wide refactor with workspace-wide blast radius — and 4+ agents are actively editing core/brain files daily. The inert-when-off digest-parity requirement is achievable only if the Vec migration preserves exact 25/9 layout and digest encoding for bands=1 (postcard lengths must match). RECOMMENDED SEQUENCING: land this AFTER the de-monolith brain_runtime seam (SEAM-005, bd-2z0.9.2 lane) so the IO contract lives in one owned module, and after the active core churn (bd-2z0.3.x/16g.10.x) settles. Leaving open with this assessment; the spec's code-fact corrections (sound latch vs gene; sensors[9] locomotion noise vs sensors[18] hearing) are verified accurate as of this tree.

title: Information-theoretic instrumentation: MI/transfer-entropy with bias correction and shuffled control
description:
SCOPE. The estimators: mutual information and transfer entropy between agent signal channels and behaviour/world variables, WITH bias correction and a surrogate (shuffled-control) null. Pure, offline, no WorldState. This bead owns the numbers; bd-16g.7.3 owns the claim.

WHY. "Communication emerged at t=30k" is a scientific claim, and the difference between a claim and a press release is a number with a null and a confidence interval. Small-sample MI is not slightly biased — the naive plug-in estimator is POSITIVELY biased, always, and the bias grows with the number of bins and shrinks only as 1/N. Two independent random series will hand you a confidently positive MI. That is the failure mode this bead exists to prevent, and it is a failure mode that produces a publishable-looking result, which is why it must be engineered rather than trusted.

DESIGN (proposed home: an `infotheory` module next to bd-16g.2.1's detector kernel — same discipline: pure leaf, no simulation types, no storage types, no UI).
- Discretization: fixed, documented bin edges (default B=8 uniform bins over the channel's declared domain [0,1]). Bin edges are part of the estimate's identity and are reported with it — an MI computed with 4 bins and one computed with 16 are not comparable, and someone WILL compare them unless the number carries its bins.
- MI: discrete plug-in with MILLER-MADOW bias correction (subtract (K̂ - 1) / (2N ln2) bits, K̂ = number of non-empty joint cells). Offer KSG (Kraskov) as an alternative for continuous data behind an enum, but ship MM as the default because it is auditable in 20 lines and its failure mode is understood.
- Transfer entropy: `TE(E -> R) = I(R_{t+1} ; E_t | R_t)` — a CONDITIONAL MI, same binning, same correction. TE needs far more samples than MI; compute the effective sample size and REFUSE below a documented minimum: return `Insufficient { have, need }`, never a number. A TE value computed from 300 samples across 512 joint cells is noise wearing a lab coat.
- Surrogate null — get this right or the whole bead is decorative. Do NOT use an i.i.d. shuffle of the emitter series: both signals and behaviour are strongly autocorrelated, and destroying autocorrelation makes the null far too easy to beat, so an i.i.d.-shuffle control will certify communication between two independent random walks. Use a CIRCULAR TIME-SHIFT: rotate the emitter series by a random offset (min offset >> the autocorrelation time) relative to the receiver, R times (default R=200). This preserves each series' marginal distribution AND its autocorrelation, and destroys only the cross-relationship. Also support the pairing permutation (permute which emitter is matched to which receiver) for the multi-agent case.
- Report: `MiEstimate { bits_plugin, bits_corrected, n, bins, estimator, surrogate: SurrogateStats { r, mean, sd, q95 }, p_value, ci_lo, ci_hi, sufficient: bool }`. p = (1 + #{surrogate >= observed}) / (R + 1) — the +1 is not optional; a p of exactly 0 is a lie about a finite permutation test. CI on the observed value by bootstrap (default 1000 resamples) or a documented asymptotic.
- RNG: surrogates need randomness. Use a dedicated SEEDED stream (bd-2z0.3.1's RandomStream), NEVER the world RNG — this code runs offline over a persisted series and must not be able to touch a simulation even by accident. The surrogate seed is recorded in the estimate so the null is reproducible.
- Input: aligned sample pairs pulled from the persisted series (bd-2z0.5.2 / bd-16g.2.2 event+metric stream) by the caller. The estimator takes `&[(f64, f64)]` or two aligned slices. It never opens a database.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- Determinism: same samples + same surrogate seed -> bit-identical estimate. Sum in index order; no HashMap iteration in the joint-histogram pass (use a dense array indexed by (bx * B + by)).
- No panics: empty input, N=1, all-constant series (MI is exactly 0, not NaN — the 0*log0 trap), non-finite values (typed error, never propagate NaN into a p-value).
- Bounds: joint histogram is B^2 (or B^3 for TE) dense cells; reject B > 32 at param validation rather than allocating 32k cells per pair per window.
- Honesty: the estimator NEVER returns a bare number. Every result carries n, bins, the correction applied, the surrogate stats, and `sufficient`. A caller must not be able to print an MI without the context that says whether to believe it.

TESTS (this is the bead where the tests ARE the deliverable).
- Analytic: deterministic copy channel R_t = E_t with 2 symbols -> 1.000 bit ± tol; 8 symbols -> 3.000 bits.
- Analytic: binary symmetric channel with crossover p -> MI = 1 - H(p), swept over p ∈ {0, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5}; at p=0.5, MI ≈ 0.
- NEGATIVE (bias correction does something): two independent uniform streams, N=200, B=8, over 100 seeds. Assert (a) the mean UNCORRECTED plug-in MI is provably POSITIVE (this proves the bias is real and the test is exercising it), and (b) the mean CORRECTED MI is within ±0.02 bits of 0. If the corrected and uncorrected values are equal, the correction is not wired in.
- NEGATIVE (the autocorrelation trap — the most important test in bd-16g.7): two INDEPENDENT AR(1) series with rho = 0.95, N = 5000. Assert that an i.i.d.-shuffle null yields p < 0.001 (i.e. it FALSELY certifies communication — assert this, so the trap is documented in code), and that the CIRCULAR-SHIFT null yields p > 0.05. This single test is the entire justification for specifying the surrogate method instead of leaving it to the implementer.
- NEGATIVE (directionality): a lagged copy R_{t+1} = E_t. Assert TE(E->R) is large and TE(R->E) ≈ 0. A transposed-argument bug is invisible in every other test and would let us publish a backwards causal claim.
- NEGATIVE (small-N refusal): N below the documented minimum -> `Insufficient { have, need }`, not a number.
- Degenerate: all-constant emitter -> MI exactly 0.0, no NaN, no panic. Saturated channel (every value in the top bin) -> MI ≈ 0 AND the `saturated_fraction` field warns (see LOGGING) — a saturated channel and a silent channel produce the same MI and must be distinguishable.
- Determinism: same input twice -> identical bytes, including the surrogate distribution.
- E2E: 100k-tick sentinel run (bd-16g.7.3), persist (tick, uid, emitted[b], heard[b], turn_toward_food, food_nearby, predator_near), compute MI + TE per window, write a report table. Assert the pipeline completes and every row carries observed/surrogate/CI/p/sufficient.

LOGGING. Target `scriptbots::comms::mi`. info per window: {tick_lo, tick_hi, pair, estimator, n, bins, mi_plugin, mi_corrected, surrogate_mean, surrogate_sd, surrogate_q95, p_value, ci_lo, ci_hi, sufficient, surrogate_seed}. warn when sufficient == false, with have/need. warn when > 5% of samples land in the extreme bins (saturation — see the channel's summing/clamping behaviour documented in bd-16g.7.1). This module MUST NOT log the word "emerged", ever: it emits numbers; the claim belongs to bd-16g.7.3's pre-registered study. A log line that editorializes is a log line that will end up in a README as evidence.

title: Communication-pressure scenarios (sentinel, alarm) and emergence acceptance study
description:
SCOPE. The selective pressure (scenarios that make signalling PAY) and the pre-registered acceptance study that decides whether communication actually emerged. Consumes bd-16g.7.1 (channel) and bd-16g.7.2 (estimators), bd-2z0.10.1 (scenario schema), and bd-16g.10 (cohort injection, as the alarm scenario's actuator).

WHY. A channel with no pressure evolves into noise, and 15 years of alife papers exist because someone found the right pressure. This is the bead where ScriptBots stops being a port of a 2009 toy and produces a result nobody has produced with this codebase. It is also the bead where the project is most likely to fool itself — "we ran it and MI went up" is not a finding — so the study protocol, including its stopping rule and its negative-result path, is part of the deliverable.

DESIGN — PRESSURE.
- Scenarios are CONFIG + a command script, expressed in bd-2z0.10.1's schema. They are NOT `if scenario == "sentinel"` branches inside `step()`. Any step-time rule a scenario needs must be a NAMED, VERSIONED, config-gated rule with a default of OFF and its own inertness test.
- `sentinel`: the world's only food sensor is `sensors[4]` (the food value at the agent's own cell) — there is no distal food sense to disable. So the pressure is a gated food sensor: `sense.food_requires_stillness = true` zeroes `sensors[4]` unless the agent's speed is below `sense.stillness_threshold`. A moving forager is blind; a stationary sentinel can see. The only channel from sentinel to forager is the signal band. That is a real, implementable, minimal pressure built from sensors that already exist.
- `alarm`: a carnivore cohort is injected periodically from one edge via `Intervention::InjectCohort` (bd-16g.10.1) on a deterministic schedule from the command script. Ground truth for the MI analysis is `predator_within_radius(agent, r)`, persisted per tick.
- Every scenario ships with the ground-truth series it needs, persisted alongside the signal series — otherwise the analysis in bd-16g.7.2 has nothing honest to correlate against.

DESIGN — THE STUDY (pre-register it in this bead's acceptance criteria BEFORE running it).
- Three arms, N = 10 seeds each, identical tick budget:
  (a) LEGACY: bands = 1 (the existing scalar channel).
  (b) SIGNAL: bands = 3.
  (c) SCRAMBLED CONTROL: bands = 3, but the channel is permuted between emission and hearing every tick with a seeded, agent-independent permutation — the channel exists, costs exactly what the signal arm's channel costs, and carries ZERO information.
- Arm (c) is the crux and it is what separates this from the usual alife hand-wave. Without it, "communication emerged" is indistinguishable from "we gave the brains two extra outputs to fiddle with and the population did better." If the scrambled arm matches the signal arm, we have found NOTHING, and the study must say so.
- The claim "communication emerged" requires ALL THREE of:
  (1) MI(emitted ; food_nearby) and/or MI(heard ; receiver_turn_toward_food) exceeds the circular-shift surrogate at p < 0.01 with a reported CI, in the SIGNAL arm;
  (2) the same MI in the SCRAMBLED arm is indistinguishable from its surrogate;
  (3) a behavioural effect: receivers' turn-toward-food is conditioned on the heard signal in the signal arm and is not in the scrambled arm.
  Anything less gets written up as a negative result. State this up front so it cannot be relitigated after seeing the data.
- Stopping rule, fixed in advance: 10 seeds per arm, 100k ticks, no peeking-and-extending. A study that runs until it gets the answer it wants is not a study.
- Output: a machine-readable report (JSON) with every arm, every seed, every window's MiEstimate, plus config_digest, root_seed, io_layout_version, and build identity per run. Irreproducible numbers are not results.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- Inertness: `sense.food_requires_stillness = false` (default) -> `characterization_digest_v0` byte-identical to pre-feature fixtures. Same for the scramble hook when disabled.
- Determinism: same scenario id + seed -> identical initial digest and identical trajectory; the scramble permutation uses a dedicated seeded stream, never the world RNG at an ad-hoc point (a permutation drawn from `self.rng` inside the sense stage would shift every downstream draw and make the control arm differ from the signal arm for reasons that have nothing to do with the control).
- The scrambled arm must cost EXACTLY what the signal arm costs (same output count, same energy accounting) — if the control is cheaper, it is not a control.

TESTS.
- Unit: scenario construction determinism (same scenario id + seed -> same initial digest; config_digest recorded).
- Unit (INERTNESS): the stillness-gated food sensor and the scramble hook, both OFF -> digest-identical to pre-feature build.
- Unit (the gate works): an agent above the stillness threshold reads `sensors[4] == 0.0`; below it, reads the true cell food value. Boundary exactly at the threshold is specified and tested.
- Unit (NEGATIVE — the control actually controls): feed a KNOWN copy channel (emitter -> hearer, MI = 1 bit) through the scrambler and assert the measured MI collapses to ≈ 0. If the scrambler does not destroy information, the control arm is not a control and every conclusion from the study is void.
- Unit: the alarm scenario's predator schedule is fully determined by the command script (same script + seed -> identical injection ticks, positions, and cohort genomes).
- E2E (CI): 5k-tick smoke of both scenarios — pipeline runs, series persist, estimators produce rows, no panics. The 100k, 30-run study is a nightly/manual job with pinned seeds that publishes its report as an artifact.
- NEGATIVE (anti-p-hacking): the report generator refuses to emit a "communication emerged" verdict unless all three criteria above are met, and emits an explicit NEGATIVE verdict otherwise. Test both paths with synthetic estimate tables — including the tempting case where criterion (1) passes and (2) fails, which must produce a NEGATIVE verdict.

LOGGING. Target `scriptbots::comms::study`. info at construction {scenario_id, arm, config_digest, io_layout_version, bands, gate_rule, scramble, seed, build}. info per completed run {arm, seed, ticks, final_population, mi_best_window, p_value}. info the verdict as structured fields {criterion_1: bool, criterion_2: bool, criterion_3: bool, verdict}. The entire study must be reconstructible from the logs of its 30 runs, and a reader must be able to see a NEGATIVE verdict as clearly as a positive one.
design: Own the versioned selective-pressure scenarios and the pre-registered communication-emergence study, not the signal channel or estimators. Sentinel and alarm remain scenario config plus deterministic command scripts; any step-time rule is named, versioned, default-off, and inertness-tested. The three matched-cost arms use fixed seeds and tick budgets, a dedicated deterministic scramble stream, persisted ground-truth and signal series, and an immutable report schema. The verdict is positive only if every predeclared information and behavioral criterion passes; otherwise it is an equally visible negative result.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Unit tests prove scenario construction determinism, default-off digest inertness, exact stillness-threshold behavior, deterministic alarm injections, equal signal/scramble cost, and a copy-channel scrambler that collapses known one-bit information. 2. Report tests refuse a positive verdict unless all three predeclared criteria pass, including the tempting case where signal MI passes but the scrambled control also carries information. 3. A real 5k-tick E2E smoke for sentinel and alarm persists ground-truth and signal series and produces estimator rows with no direct model calls; detailed artifacts retain scenario, arm, seed, config and layout digests, commands, series identity, logs, and exits. 4. The pinned 30-run study uses exactly 10 seeds per arm and 100k ticks with no peeking or extension, publishes every window and confidence interval, and reports negative results as prominently as positive ones. 5. Same scenario and seed reproduce initial and trajectory digests; disabled gates and scramble hooks preserve pre-feature fixtures and world RNG ordering. 6. Structured logs reconstruct all arms and include scenario, arm, gate and scramble rules, seed/build/config/layout identity, completed ticks and population, MI windows, p-values and intervals, each criterion, and the final typed verdict.

title: Shareable worlds: seed+config permalinks, browser fork-this-world, and a curated gallery
description:
THE IDEA. Make a world a SHAREABLE ARTIFACT. A run is fully determined by (scenario config + seed + build identity), so encode that into a compact permalink: scriptbots.dev/w/<base64(scenario_hash,seed)> opens the WASM build, reconstructs the exact world, and plays it in the browser. Add "fork this world" (tweak a knob -> new permalink), an embeddable iframe/GIF for READMEs and posts, and a curated gallery of worlds worth seeing (each entry: a permalink, a one-line story, and the event timeline from bd-16g.2).

WHY IT MATTERS. Reach and versatility. Today, showing someone an interesting run means "clone this repo, install a nightly toolchain, build for ten minutes." That is a wall. A permalink turns every interesting run into a link a researcher can put in a paper, a teacher can put in a lesson, and a stranger can click. It also makes the determinism promise TANGIBLE and publicly falsifiable: the URL is a claim that anyone can re-run and check — which is exactly the reproducible-research pitch, delivered as a user experience rather than a paragraph.

DESIGN.
- The permalink payload is a scenario reference (hash + optional inline diff) + seed + the build identity/digest version from bd-2z0.1.6 — NOT a snapshot blob. Small, human-inspectable, and it makes the "same link, different build => honest mismatch warning" case explicit rather than silently divergent.
- Build identity mismatch must be SURFACED, not hidden: if the running WASM build's digest version differs from the link's, show "this world was recorded on build X; you are on build Y; trajectories may differ" — never fake reproducibility.
- The gallery is a static, versioned manifest in-repo (no server, no database): each entry is a permalink + title + story + expected event timeline; CI RE-RUNS every gallery world headless and asserts its event timeline still matches. A gallery entry that silently stops being interesting is a regression, and this is how we catch it.
- Fork = edit knobs in the browser -> new hash -> new link; the diff from the parent scenario is displayed (this is a teaching device: "what did you change?").

ACCEPTANCE. A permalink opens in a cold browser and reproduces the recorded event timeline exactly on the matching build; a build mismatch produces an honest warning; every gallery world is CI-verified each run; the payload stays under a documented size (a URL, not a file).

TESTS + LOGGING (required).
- Unit: permalink encode/decode round-trip incl. inline knob diffs; malformed/hostile payloads rejected cleanly (no panic from a URL — this is untrusted input reaching a parser).
- Unit: build-identity mismatch detection triggers the warning path.
- E2E (CI, headless browser): load N gallery permalinks in the wasm build, run to the recorded horizon, assert the bd-16g.2 event timelines match the manifest; on mismatch, log the first divergent event with tick/kind/expected/actual.
- E2E (native): the same permalinks reproduce the same timelines natively (cross-target consistency, coordinating with bd-2wj's native-vs-wasm fixture policy).

title: Permalink codec: scenario hash + seed + build identity, hostile-input hardening
description:
SCOPE. The permalink codec and its hardening. A permalink is (scenario reference + inline knob diff + seed + build identity) — NOT a snapshot blob. Encode, decode, canonicalize, validate, and detect build mismatch as a pure predicate. The browser UX that SURFACES the mismatch is bd-16g.8.2; the gallery that consumes links is bd-16g.8.3.

WHY. This is the bead that makes the determinism promise publicly falsifiable. A URL that says "this exact world" is a claim a stranger can check, which is the reproducible-research pitch delivered as a user experience instead of a paragraph. It is also the ONLY place in the project where untrusted, attacker-controlled bytes reach a parser — inside a WASM module, where a panic does not throw, it kills the page. The hardening requirements below are not ceremony.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS (build on it, do not reinvent it).
- `RunManifestV0` (crates/scriptbots-app/src/lib.rs) already carries exactly the fields a permalink needs: `root_seed`, `scenario: ScenarioIdentityV0 { id, schema_version, ordered_config_layer_digests, population_recipe, bootstrap_ticks }`, `config_digest` + `config_digest_encoding` ("ron-0.8-struct-order-v0"), and `build: BuildProvenanceV0 { package_version, source_revision, core: CoreBuildIdentityV0 { parallel, simd_wide, rayon_threads, target_arch/os/family/endian, pointer_width }, ... }`. The permalink is a projection of the manifest, not a parallel universe.
- CODE FACT: `manifest_digest` is FNV-1a 64 with a domain-separation tag. It is a fast, NON-cryptographic hash. It is fine as an identifier and it is NOT tamper-evident. A decoded permalink's `config_digest` is therefore a CLAIM to be checked against the locally reconstructed config — never a trusted cache key, never a substitute for validating the knob diff. Say this in the module docs, because the next person will assume "digest" means "secure".

DESIGN.
- Payload (postcard-encoded, then URL-safe unpadded base64):
  `struct PermalinkV1 { magic: [u8; 2] = b"SB", version: u8 = 1, scenario_id: String (<= 64 bytes, [a-z0-9_-]), config_digest: u64, seed: u64, build: BuildIdent { core_digest: u64, package_version: String }, knob_diff: Vec<(KnobId, KnobValue)> (<= 32 entries), crc: u32 }`.
- `KnobId` is a stable u16 from the EXISTING knob registry (scriptbots-app's `list_knobs`/`apply_updates` path already enumerates config knobs) — reuse it; a second knob-naming scheme guarantees the two drift and a link means different things to the CLI and the browser.
- Size budget: <= 512 bytes of base64, enforced at ENCODE time with a hard error. A link that does not survive a chat client is not a link. Assert the budget with a 32-knob worst case.
- Placement/anti-coupling: a pure `permalink` module with NO WorldState dependency, no filesystem, no clock, compiling cleanly for `wasm32-unknown-unknown` (this rules out `std::time`, `std::fs`, and anything that panics on the web). `encode(&ScenarioIdentityV0, seed, &BuildIdent, &[KnobDiff]) -> Result<String, PermalinkError>` / `decode(&str) -> Result<PermalinkV1, PermalinkError>`. Both scriptbots-app and scriptbots-web depend on it; neither owns it.
- `fn build_match(link: &BuildIdent, running: &BuildIdent) -> BuildMatch { Exact, Compatible { note }, Mismatch { link, running } }` — a pure predicate here; the banner is .2's problem.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- DECODE IS TOTAL. No `unwrap`, no `expect`, no `panic!`, no raw slice indexing, no `as` truncation on a length field, anywhere in the decode path. Typed errors only: `BadBase64 { at }`, `TooLong { bytes, max }`, `BadMagic`, `UnsupportedVersion { got, supported }`, `CrcMismatch { expected, actual }`, `TooManyKnobs { got, max }`, `UnknownKnob { id }`, `KnobOutOfRange { id, value, min, max }`, `TrailingBytes { n }`.
- NO ATTACKER-CONTROLLED ALLOCATION. Postcard length prefixes are attacker-supplied: decode through a byte-budgeted reader that refuses to allocate more than the declared max. The "4-billion-element Vec" is the classic wasm OOM and it is one `Vec::with_capacity(len)` away.
- Every knob value from a link goes through `ScriptBotsConfig::validate()` BEFORE a world is constructed. A knob diff carrying NaN, a negative population, or `world_width = 4_000_000_000` must be rejected by validation, not by the allocator.
- CANONICAL ENCODING: `encode(decode(s)) == s` for every valid `s`. A non-canonical encoding means one world has two links, and the gallery's cache keys and CI's expectations silently diverge.
- Determinism: encoding is a pure function of its inputs — no map iteration order in the knob diff (sort by KnobId), no float formatting locale dependence (encode f32 bit patterns, not decimal strings).

TESTS.
- Property (proptest): arbitrary valid payload -> encode -> decode == original; and canonicality (`encode(decode(s)) == s`).
- Size: a 32-knob worst-case payload is under the documented cap.
- NEGATIVE (FUZZ — required, not a nice-to-have): `cargo fuzz` (or a proptest byte-string harness) over arbitrary input. Decode must NEVER panic, NEVER OOM, and always return `Ok` or a typed `Err`. Seed the corpus with: truncated payloads at every byte offset; a declared length of `0xFFFF_FFFF`; 10 MB of 'A'; valid base64 of random bytes; `version = 255`; a payload whose CRC is correct but whose knob id is unknown; a scenario_id of 64 KB; deeply nested/duplicated knob entries.
- NEGATIVE: a link whose `config_digest` does not match the config actually reconstructed from (scenario + knob diff) is REJECTED with `DigestMismatch`, not run anyway. This is the test that keeps the digest from being decorative.
- NEGATIVE: a knob diff with NaN / out-of-range values is rejected by `validate()` with the KNOB NAMED in the error, before any world allocation.
- Build mismatch: `build_match` returns Exact / Compatible / Mismatch on hand-built identities, including the case where only `core_digest` differs (different `simd_wide`/`parallel` feature set — the most likely real-world mismatch and the one most likely to actually change trajectories).

LOGGING. The codec is a pure leaf: it does NOT log. Instead every `PermalinkError` variant carries enough context (byte offset, field, declared length, knob id, both digests) that the CALLER can emit one complete, self-explanatory line. Design the errors so that the caller's `warn!` on a rejected link — {kind, reason, payload_len, first_16_bytes_hex, scenario_id_if_parsed} — is enough to diagnose "my link doesn't work" WITHOUT asking the user to re-send the link. That constraint is the design review for this bead's error types.
notes:
2026-07-20 (VioletHawk): permalink codec implemented in crates/scriptbots-core/src/permalink.rs (pure leaf, no logging). Binary form + base64url sbw1. string form; binds scenario reference + inline knob diff + seed + build identity (toolchain/lockfile/core digests). Canonical by construction: ascending knob order, exact f64 bit patterns, CRC32 integrity, duplicate/out-of-order rejection. Total decode with per-field length bounds BEFORE any allocation (MAX_PAYLOAD 12_288 bytes covering 64 worst-case knobs). Errors carry byte offset/field/declared length/knob path/both digests for one-line diagnosis. verify_config_digest recomputes the reconstruction digest (scenario config + diff) and rejects tampering as DigestMismatch. validate_knobs checks the live KNOB_RANGES registry naming offenders; non-finite values rejected pre-allocation. build_match returns Exact/Compatible/Mismatch including the core-feature-drift case (most likely to change trajectories). Tests (10/10 green): round-trip binary+URL, construction-order independence, worst-case size cap, every truncation offset, 50k arbitrary-byte fuzz (never panics, bounded), seeded adversarial corpus (bad magic, version 255, CRC corruption, 0xFFFF declared lengths, 10MB, random base64, 64KB scenario id), DigestMismatch, NaN/out-of-range naming, build_match tri-state, duplicate knob rejection. title: Browser fork-this-world UX with parent-diff display and honest build-mismatch warning
description:
SCOPE. The browser experience: open a permalink into the WASM build, show what world you are in, fork it by editing knobs (producing a new link), display the diff against the parent scenario, and surface a build mismatch HONESTLY. Consumes bd-16g.8.1's codec. The gallery page's contents come from bd-16g.8.3's manifest.

WHY. This is the reach bead. Today, showing someone an interesting run means "clone the repo, install a nightly toolchain, build for ten minutes." A link removes that wall. Fork-with-diff is also the best teaching device the project has: "you changed food_growth_rate from 0.02 to 0.05, here is what happened" is a lesson, where a fork button with no diff is just a slot machine.

WHAT EXISTS (crates/scriptbots-web/src/lib.rs). `init_sim(config: JsValue) -> SimHandle`, `SimHandle::tick_js(steps)`, `snapshot_js()`, `reset_js(seed)`, `register_brain_js(kind)`, `version()`, `default_init_options()`, `decode_snapshot_binary(bytes)` (postcard), plus a `wasm_bindgen_test(run_in_browser)` harness that already works. Extend this surface; do not build a second one.

DESIGN.
- New bindings: `init_from_permalink(link: &str) -> Result<SimHandle, JsValue>`; `permalink_of(&SimHandle) -> String`; `fork(&SimHandle, knob_patch: JsValue) -> Result<String, JsValue>` (returns the CHILD link, does not mutate the running world); `permalink_diff(link: &str) -> Result<JsValue, JsValue>` returning `[{ knob, parent_value, this_value }]`; `build_identity() -> JsValue`.
- THE ANTI-COUPLING RULE THAT MATTERS: the config that a permalink reconstructs must come from the SAME composition path as native `compose_config` (crates/scriptbots-app/src/main.rs: defaults -> ordered config layers -> env overrides -> explicit seed -> `validate()`). Factor that layering into a shared function used by BOTH `scriptbots-app::compose_config` and `scriptbots-web::init_from_permalink`. If wasm re-implements the layering and one default drifts, the same link produces two different worlds on two targets — and the project's central promise becomes a lie told by its own front page. This is the single most important line in this bead.
- Build mismatch UX, three states from `build_match` (bd-16g.8.1): Exact -> silent. Compatible -> a quiet note. Mismatch -> a banner: "This world was recorded on build X (core digest 0x…, v1.2.3); you are on build Y. Trajectories may diverge after tick 0." The banner must be a real DOM node (assertable in a test) and must NOT be dismissible before it has been rendered. A warning that exists only as a `console.log` is not a warning; it is plausible deniability.
- We WARN, we do not BLOCK, and we never silently "fix up" a stale link: no auto-migration of knob ids across versions, no substituting a default for an `UnknownKnob`. An unknown knob is a hard, explained error.
- Fork produces a new link from (parent scenario + merged knob diff + seed). The diff view is computed against the PARENT SCENARIO's config, not against the running world's mutated state — a fork of a fork must show the full path, not just the last edit.
- Cross-target honesty: wasm-vs-native float behaviour is a KNOWN open risk (bd-2wj). This bead's promise is "same build, same trajectory." It must NOT claim native/wasm equivalence — that claim is bd-2wj's to prove or deny. If bd-2wj finds divergence, the honest UX is to say so in the banner, not to quietly stop mentioning it.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- NO PANICS IN WASM. A panic aborts the module instance: the page dies, the user gets a blank canvas, and we get no diagnostics. Every binding returns `Result<_, JsValue>`. Install a panic hook that surfaces the message, but treat any FIRED hook as a P0 bug, not as a safety net — CI asserts zero panics across bd-16g.8.1's fuzz corpus.
- The wasm module must survive a bad link: after a rejected permalink, the SAME instance must still be able to `init_sim` successfully. This is the test that proves nothing was poisoned.
- Bounded work: `init_from_permalink` must not run ticks; a link that names a 4096x4096 world with 100k agents must fail `validate()` before allocation, not after the tab freezes.

TESTS.
- wasm-bindgen-test (run_in_browser, using the existing harness): fixture link -> `init_from_permalink` -> tick 100 -> snapshot summary equals a checked-in expectation (population, tick, food total).
- Fork: patch exactly one knob -> the child link decodes with exactly that one diff -> `permalink_diff` returns exactly one row with the correct parent/child values. Fork the fork: two rows, in stable knob order.
- PARITY (the drift test): reconstruct the same link natively via the shared composition path and in wasm; assert both produce the same `config_digest`. This is what catches the config-layering divergence described above, and it should run in CI on every commit that touches either path.
- NEGATIVE (mismatch is surfaced): a link with a doctored `core_digest` produces the Mismatch banner in the DOM AND still runs (assert both — we warn, we do not block, and we do not lie).
- NEGATIVE (no poison): feed the 8.1 fuzz corpus through `init_from_permalink` in a live browser instance; assert every one returns a typed JS error, no panic hook fires, and a subsequent valid `init_sim` in the SAME instance still works.
- NEGATIVE (no silent repair): a link with an unknown knob id -> explicit error naming the id; assert the world is NOT constructed with a default substituted in.

LOGGING. Web-side `tracing` to the console. info on load: {link_len, scenario_id, seed, config_digest, link_build, running_build, match_state, knob_diff_count}. warn on Mismatch with BOTH build identities in full. warn on every rejected link with the typed error and the first 16 payload bytes in hex. error on any fired panic hook with the payload. Standard: a user complaint of "the link is broken" must be fully diagnosable from that one info/warn line without the user re-sending anything.

title: Curated gallery manifest with CI re-run verification of every world's event timeline
description:
SCOPE. The curated gallery: an in-repo, versioned manifest of worlds worth seeing, plus the CI job that RE-RUNS every one of them headless and asserts its event timeline still matches. No server, no database. One manifest, two consumers (the CI verifier and the wasm gallery page from bd-16g.8.2).

WHY. A gallery that is not verified rots. Worlds are curated because something interesting happens in them; a physics fix, a mutation-rate tweak, or a brain refactor can quietly make that something stop happening — and then the project's shop window is showing worlds whose captions are lies. Re-running the gallery in CI turns "this is interesting" from a claim someone made once into an assertion the build defends. It is also, incidentally, the broadest end-to-end determinism test the project will have: N real worlds, run to horizon, compared against a recorded timeline.

DESIGN.
- `gallery/manifest.toml`, versioned in-repo:
  `[[world]] id, title, story (<= 200 chars), permalink, horizon_ticks, expected_timeline = [{ tick, kind, key_fields }], added_by, added_at, blessed_on_build`.
- The timeline comes from bd-16g.2.2's `EventRecord` stream. Comparison is SEMANTIC on (tick, kind, key fields) — NOT a string compare of `human_text`. Template wording will change; the event will not. A gallery that fails because someone improved a caption is a gallery that gets disabled within a month.
- Tick tolerance is ZERO. Same build, same seed, same config -> the event fires on the same tick or determinism is already broken and we want to hear about it LOUDLY, not smooth it over with a ±5 window. If a tolerance knob ever appears in this comparator, it is a bug being hidden.
- COST BUDGET, enforced at review: `horizon_ticks <= 50_000` per world and the whole `gallery-verify` job under 10 minutes wall clock. Entries that blow the budget are rejected. Otherwise the gallery becomes the slowest job in CI, someone marks it `continue-on-error`, and it is dead — which is precisely how galleries rot in every project that has one.
- RE-BLESSING: when a legitimate change (a real physics fix) makes a world diverge, the fix is to re-bless the entry in the SAME PR: `cargo xtask gallery bless --id <id>` rewrites that entry's expected timeline and records `blessed_on_build`. NEVER auto-bless in CI. An auto-blessing regression test is a rubber stamp — that is exactly what made the old DuckDB replay baseline worthless (see bd-2z0.8.9.9, which dropped it), and we are not doing it twice.
- The bless command must produce a MINIMAL diff (stable field order, stable event order) so a reviewer can see what changed about the world, which is the whole point of making them look.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- Manifest validation is strict: unknown fields rejected (a typo in a field name must not silently disable a check), ids unique, every permalink decodes (bd-16g.8.1) and validates, horizon within cap.
- The verifier is deterministic and hermetic: no network, no clock, no ambient env (the run must pin `RAYON_NUM_THREADS`/`SCRIPTBOTS_MAX_THREADS`, which are part of `CoreBuildIdentityV0` and therefore part of the trajectory's identity — a gallery that passes on 8 threads and fails on 4 is a gallery that will fail on someone's laptop).
- Failure output must be actionable WITHOUT a local repro: the first divergent event with entry id, index, expected vs actual (tick, kind, fields), plus the permalink, plus the full actual timeline uploaded as a CI artifact.
- No panics: a malformed manifest fails at parse with a line number; it does not fail at tick 40,000.

TESTS.
- Unit: manifest parse/validate — unknown field rejected; duplicate id rejected; undecodable permalink rejected AT PARSE TIME, not at run time; horizon over cap rejected.
- Unit: `bless` rewrites only the targeted entry and produces a byte-stable, minimal diff (run it twice -> no-op the second time).
- E2E (the job): at least three worlds, chosen to exercise the comparator rather than to look pretty — one QUIET world (expected_timeline is nearly empty; proves the verifier does not hallucinate events), one with a mass-extinction event, one with a speciation event.
- NEGATIVE (THE test — does the verifier ever fail?): a fixture manifest with one event's tick shifted by exactly 1 must make the job FAIL with the first-divergence report. A verifier nobody has watched fail is a verifier that passes vacuously, and this is the only test that proves it can bite.
- NEGATIVE: an entry whose expected_timeline lists an event kind that no longer exists -> hard error naming the kind (catches a rename that silently dropped a check).
- NEGATIVE: run the verifier with a different thread count than the blessed one and assert it either reproduces exactly or fails loudly with the thread count named — never a silent pass on a different lane.
- Cross-target: the same gallery links, loaded in the wasm build (bd-16g.8.2), reproduce the same timelines — coordinated with bd-2wj's native-vs-wasm fixture policy. If native and wasm disagree, the gallery reports it rather than picking a winner.

LOGGING. Target `scriptbots::gallery`. info per entry {id, permalink, horizon, threads, events_expected, events_actual, elapsed_ms, result}. error on first divergence {id, index, tick_expected, tick_actual, kind_expected, kind_actual, permalink}. info summary {entries, passed, failed, total_elapsed_ms} — and the summary line is what the budget above is enforced against, so it must always be emitted, including on failure.
acceptance_criteria: 1. gallery/manifest.toml strictly rejects unknown fields, duplicate/invalid ids, overlong stories, invalid dates/build ids, undecodable or invalid permalinks, horizons above 50,000, unknown event kinds, and malformed/unsorted timelines with line-aware errors. 2. At least three curated entries include nonvacuous semantic expected timelines: quiet, mass-extinction, and speciation worlds. The hermetic verifier decodes each permalink, pins thread/science identity, runs headless to horizon, and compares zero-tolerance tick/kind/key fields. 3. CI runs every entry under ten minutes total, never auto-blesses, uploads full actual timelines/logs, and reports first divergence with id/index/expected/actual/permalink plus an always-emitted summary. 4. The bless command rewrites only one targeted entry in stable field/event order, records build identity, and is byte-idempotent on a second run. 5. Unit/negative tests cover strict parsing, duplicate ids, invalid permalinks, horizon cap, one-tick shift, removed kind, wrong thread count, empty-vacuity prevention, bless minimality/idempotence, and actionable failure logs. 6. The wasm gallery consumer loads the same links and native-versus-wasm parity reports divergence rather than choosing a winner; focused fmt, strict clippy, tests, and approved CI/DSR verification pass.

title: Evolution theater: auto-clipped, annotated highlight reels exported as GIF/MP4/asciinema
description:
THE IDEA. Auto-produce the highlight reel. Take the event timeline (bd-16g.2), select the K most significant moments of a run, cut a clip around each from the replay (bd-2z0.5.3), annotate it with the templated event text ("t=6,880: first sustained carnivore lineage"), and export the montage as an animated GIF / MP4 (GPU lab) or asciinema/GIF (TUI). One command: `scriptbots-app reel --run <id> --top 6 --out evolution.mp4`.

WHY IT MATTERS. A 50,000-tick run is unwatchable; its six interesting minutes are riveting. This is the artifact that gets the project SEEN — in a README, a talk, a tweet, a paper's supplementary material — and it costs almost nothing once replay and the event detector exist, because both hard parts (knowing WHEN something interesting happened, and being able to re-render any tick exactly) are already paid for by other beads. It is also a genuine debugging tool: "show me the 200 ticks around every mass-extinction event in this regression" is a better bug report than any log.

DESIGN.
- Selection is deterministic and explainable: rank events by severity/magnitude with a documented scoring function; ties by tick. The reel's contents must be reproducible from (run, top-K, scoring version) — a reel is evidence, so it must be re-derivable.
- Rendering reuses the existing offscreen paths (the GPU lab's offscreen PNG rendering and the TUI's ASCII snapshot) — no new renderer. Frames -> encoder (gif/mp4 via an existing crate; asciinema cast for the terminal).
- Annotations come from the event's deterministic human_text, NOT free-form LLM prose (the LLM may optionally add a narration track, clearly labeled as generated).
- Must run headless in CI (no GPU required for at least the TUI/ASCII path) so the reel of a nightly seed can be attached as a CI artifact.

ACCEPTANCE. `reel --run <id> --top 6` produces a montage whose clips correspond exactly to the top-6 scored events, is byte-reproducible for the same inputs, runs headless, and completes within a documented time/memory budget for a 50k-tick run.

TESTS + LOGGING (required).
- Unit: event scoring + selection determinism (same events -> same picks, same order).
- Unit: clip window math (start/end clamped at run boundaries; overlapping clips merged rather than duplicated).
- E2E: headless run -> events -> reel (ASCII path) -> assert frame count, annotation text, and byte-reproducibility across two invocations; log the selected events with scores at info so the reel's editorial choices are auditable.
acceptance_criteria: 1. One documented reel command loads a persisted run, deterministically selects top-K events under an explicit scoring version, seeks exact replay ticks, annotates deterministic human text, and exports requested ASCII cast or GIF plus the documented optional MP4 behavior. 2. Identical run, top-K, scoring version, format, and render options produce byte-identical non-empty artifacts; empty reels create no file and every wrong-tick or encoder failure is typed and leaves no partial output. 3. The headless default lane requires no GPU, display, network, or live mutable world and completes a 50k-tick top-six reel within documented time and memory budgets. 4. Unit tests pin scoring, total ordering, clip bounds, merging, and versioning; end-to-end tests assert event selection, exact frame ticks, captions, frame counts, byte identity, format failures, and detailed editorial/render logs. 5. Every parent-child bead is complete and focused formatting, strict clippy, tests, and approved CI/replay gates pass with retained commands and results.

title: Deterministic event scoring/selection and clip-window math
description:
SCOPE. The editorial brain of the highlight reel: score the events of a run, select the top K, and turn the picks into merged, clamped clip windows. Pure module, no renderer, no encoder, no storage — bd-16g.9.2 consumes the `Vec<Clip>` this bead produces. Input is the persisted `EventRecord` stream from bd-16g.2.2 plus the run's tick bounds.

WHY. "Which 6 of these 4,000 events are worth watching?" is the only interesting question in bd-16g.9, and it is a question about ranking, not about video. Isolating it here means it can be tested exhaustively with a table of synthetic events and zero frames rendered, and it means a reel is EVIDENCE: reproducible from (run, top_k, scoring_version) alone. A reel whose contents depend on when you ran it, or on a config knob someone tweaked, cannot be cited in a bug report or a paper — and both are things the parent bead explicitly promises.

DESIGN.
- `fn score_event(&EventRecord, &RunStats, ScoringVersion) -> f32`, pure and versioned. Score = `kind_weight[kind] * normalize(magnitude) * rarity(kind)`.
- The weight table lives in CODE and is VERSIONED, not in config. A config-tweakable score means two people's "top 6" for the same run differ and neither is wrong — which destroys the reel's evidentiary value. `ScoringVersion` is bumped deliberately; old versions remain reproducible (see tests).
- RARITY TERM (do not skip it): down-weight by `1 / log2(2 + count_of_kind_in_run)`. Failure mode prevented: a run with 400 "population dipped" events and one "first sustained carnivore lineage" produces a reel of six identical population dips. The rare event is the interesting one; a raw magnitude ranking will never show it to you.
- `normalize(magnitude)` is per-kind, against that kind's distribution WITHIN THIS RUN (e.g. a robust z-score or a rank), because magnitudes across kinds are not commensurable — an extinction's "magnitude" and a speciation's "magnitude" have different units, and multiplying them by a shared weight without normalizing is numerology.
- Selection: sort by `(score DESC, tick ASC, event_id ASC)` — a TOTAL order in which ties are impossible. No RNG, ever. Take top K, then apply diversity: at most `max_per_kind` (default 2) clips of any one kind.
- Clip windows: `fn clip_window(tick, pre, post, bounds) -> Range<u64>` clamped to `[0, last_tick]`; then `fn merge_overlaps(Vec<Range>) -> Vec<Clip>` — overlapping OR adjacent windows MERGE into a single clip carrying BOTH annotations in tick order. Failure mode prevented: two events 10 ticks apart producing two near-identical clips, so the reel stutters and looks broken.
- A merged clip's score is the MAX of its members, never the sum. Summing lets a cluster of trivia outrank a mass extinction, which is the one thing the reel exists to show.
- `Clip { rank, start, end, events: Vec<EventRef>, score, merged_from: usize }` — the clip carries its provenance so bd-16g.9.2 can caption it and the log can justify it.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- Determinism: no RNG, no HashMap iteration, no wall-clock, index-order float accumulation. Same events -> same picks, same order, same windows.
- Order-independence: the output must not depend on the INPUT order of the event list (they arrive from a DB query; a `LIMIT`/`ORDER BY` change upstream must not silently re-cut the reel). The total order above guarantees this; the test below proves it.
- No panics: empty event list, K = 0, K > event count, a run with a single tick, `pre`/`post` larger than the whole run.
- Versioned scoring is genuinely versioned: `ScoringVersion::V1` must keep producing V1's picks forever, even after V2 lands.

TESTS.
- Table-driven fixture (checked in, and it IS the spec): ~50 synthetic events across 6 kinds with hand-computed scores -> expected top-6 with exact ranks and scores.
- Determinism: two invocations identical; and — the important one — SHUFFLE the input event order 100 ways and assert byte-identical output every time. That is what proves the total order has no ties left to break by accident.
- Rarity (the anti-monotony test): a run with 400 events of kind X and exactly 1 of kind Y puts Y in the reel. Assert it explicitly; this is the behaviour most likely to be "optimized away" by someone simplifying the score.
- Clip math: an event at tick 0 clamps `start` to 0 while keeping the full `post`; an event at the last tick clamps `end`; two events 5 ticks apart merge into one clip with both annotations in tick order; two events 5,000 apart do not merge; three chained overlapping windows merge into exactly one clip (not two).
- Merged score: a cluster of five trivial events does NOT outrank one high-magnitude rare event (the max-not-sum test).
- NEGATIVE: an empty event list -> an EMPTY reel, exit 0, with an explicit "no events scored above threshold" result — never a zero-clip "success" that bd-16g.9.2 then renders into a 0-frame video file. The failure must happen here, with an explanation, not downstream with a corrupt artifact.
- NEGATIVE: K > event count -> returns what exists; K = 0 -> empty; no panic in either.
- NEGATIVE (versioning is real): bump to `ScoringVersion::V2` with different weights and assert the V1 fixture STILL reproduces the V1 picks. If it does not, the version field is decoration and every old reel is unreproducible.

LOGGING. Target `scriptbots::reel::select`. info ONE structured record of the full editorial decision: {run_id, scoring_version, events_considered, events_scored, max_per_kind, selected: [{rank, tick, kind, score, magnitude_norm, rarity, merged_from, start, end}]}. debug every event's individual score components (kind_weight, magnitude_norm, rarity, total) so the ranking can be recomputed by hand from the log. Standard: "why is this clip in my reel, and why is THAT one not?" must be answerable from the log without opening the database.
close_reason: Implemented deterministic event scoring with ScoringVersion::V1, logarithmic rarity term, input-order-independent selection, clamped window math, and clip merging in scriptbots-core/src/reel.rs.

comments.text: bd-we7b Draw10 verdict D at immutable anchor f380ad5d47a7692bc6181fa3c2186f5c098debfd. Source 604efdfe delivers a real versioned reel/scoring/clip substrate, so the title-level implementation remains closed. The close overclaimed completion: score_event uses raw magnitude, equal score/tick/kind events retain input order, non-finite values collapse through partial_cmp, V2 is absent, and the promised permutation/golden/log matrix is missing.
