title: Headless montage encoder: ASCII/GIF path (CI-safe) and GPU MP4 path
description:
SCOPE. Turn bd-16g.9.1's `Vec<Clip>` into an artifact: seek the replay to each clip, render frames through the EXISTING offscreen paths, caption them with the event's deterministic `human_text`, and encode a montage. Two lanes: an ASCII/GIF lane that is CI-safe (no GPU, no display, no network) and a raster/MP4 lane behind a feature gate. `scriptbots-app reel --run <id> --top 6 --format ascii|gif|mp4 --out evolution.gif`.

WHY. This is the artifact that gets the project SEEN — README, talk, tweet, paper supplement — and it is nearly free, because both hard parts are already paid for: bd-16g.2.2 knows WHEN something happened and bd-2z0.5.3 can re-render any tick exactly. It is also a real debugging tool: "show me the 200 ticks around every mass-extinction event in this regression" is a better bug report than any log. The entire cost of this bead is discipline: reuse the renderers, refuse to fabricate frames, and make the output byte-reproducible.

REUSE — NO NEW RENDERER (this is the anti-coupling requirement, and the parent bead states it flatly).
- Raster lane: `scriptbots_render::render_png_offscreen(&WorldState, w, h) -> Vec<u8>` (crates/scriptbots-render/src/lib.rs) already exists, is already headless, and is already the GUI's snapshot path; `ControlApi::snapshot_png` wraps it. Use it.
- ASCII lane: the TUI already renders a glyph map (`ControlApi::ascii_map`, and the terrain/food glyph mapping in `save_ascii_snapshot`, crates/scriptbots-app/src/terminal/mod.rs). Use it. Its current 64x32 sampling is a starting point, not a spec — if the reel needs a different resolution, PARAMETERIZE the existing function; do not fork it.
- Frame source is REPLAY (bd-2z0.5.3): seek to `clip.start`, step to `clip.end`, render every `stride`-th tick. Frames are never synthesized, interpolated, or reused across clips.

DESIGN.
- Encoders: GIF via an existing crate; asciinema v2 `.cast` for the terminal lane (a text artifact that embeds in a README and is diffable). MP4 ONLY if a pure-Rust or already-vendored encoder is available. Do NOT shell out to `ffmpeg` from library code. If MP4 needs ffmpeg, it is an optional feature the CLI PROBES for and refuses cleanly ("mp4 requires ffmpeg on PATH; ascii and gif are always available") — never a silent fallback that writes a broken file with the right extension.
- Captions come from `EventRecord::human_text` (deterministic templates, bd-16g.2.2). No LLM prose in this path; an optional LLM narration track (bd-16g.1) is a separate, clearly-labelled artifact.
- Streaming: frames go to the encoder as they are produced. Never buffer six clips x 400 frames of PNG in a `Vec` — that is the OOM this bead's budget exists to prevent. Assert `frames_in_flight <= 2`.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- BYTE-REPRODUCIBILITY. Two invocations with identical inputs must produce byte-identical output files. GIF encoders love to embed timestamps and to quantize palettes non-deterministically: PIN the palette (a fixed 256-entry table derived from the existing terrain/agent colour tables), disable every timestamp/metadata field, and assert byte-equality. If the chosen crate cannot be made deterministic, REPLACE THE CRATE — do not waive the requirement. A reel is evidence; evidence that differs every time it is generated is not evidence.
- CI-safe by default: the ASCII lane requires no GPU, no display, no network. The raster lane is feature-gated and SKIPS (with an explicit `warn!` naming the reason) when no adapter is available — a silently-skipped test is a test that never runs.
- Budget: a 50k-tick run, top-6, ASCII lane, completes in under a documented wall clock (propose 120s on CI hardware) with bounded memory. Log the actuals every run so the budget is measured, not assumed.
- No panics: every failure is a typed error with the clip index and frame index.

TESTS.
- E2E (CI, ASCII lane): a fixture run DB -> `reel --top 3 --format ascii` -> assert frame count == sum over clips of `ceil(len / stride)`; assert frame k's caption is exactly the expected `human_text`; assert two invocations produce BYTE-IDENTICAL output.
- E2E (GIF): same, plus assert the palette is the pinned one and that no timestamp field is present in the output bytes.
- NEGATIVE (empty reel): a run with zero scored events -> exit 0, NO file written, an explicit message. A 0-byte `.gif` (or a 1-frame video of nothing) is worse than no file: it looks like it worked.
- NEGATIVE (no silent fallback): `--format mp4` with no encoder available -> non-zero exit with the actionable message; assert NO partial/truncated file is left behind.
- NEGATIVE (THE one that matters — wrong ticks): ask for a clip whose `start` the checkpoint cadence cannot reach exactly, and assert a typed error naming the nearest reachable checkpoint. A reel of the WRONG ticks, confidently captioned "t=6,880: first sustained carnivore lineage", is the worst possible output of this entire epic: it is fabricated evidence with our name on it. The seek must be exact or it must fail.
- NEGATIVE (caption/frame alignment): deliberately offset a clip by one tick in a fixture and assert the test catches the mismatch between the frame's world tick and the caption's event tick. Every frame must carry its true tick, and the test must compare them.
- Memory/streaming: assert `frames_in_flight <= 2` via an instrumented sink; assert peak allocation does not scale with total frame count.

LOGGING. Target `scriptbots::reel::render`. info per clip {rank, tick_start, tick_end, frames, stride, events, caption_chars, bytes, elapsed_ms}. info final {out, format, clips, frames, bytes, elapsed_ms, peak_frames_in_flight} — this line is what the budget is enforced against. warn when the raster lane is skipped, with the reason (no adapter / feature off). error on encoder failure with clip index AND frame index AND the world tick, so a corrupt frame is traceable to a world state that can be re-rendered by hand.
acceptance_criteria: 1. scriptbots-app reel loads one run, selects clips, seeks exact replay state for every frame, reuses the existing ASCII and offscreen renderers, and never advances or fabricates a live world. 2. ASCII cast and GIF lanes stream with at most two frames in flight and produce non-empty, byte-identical artifacts with exact frame count, tick, caption, pinned palette, and no volatile metadata; empty selections write no file. 3. MP4 is either implemented behind the documented optional lane or refuses before creating output with a typed actionable error; no format silently falls back. 4. CLI and CI fixture e2e tests cover exact and unreachable seeks, out-of-order scored clips, caption/frame offset injection, empty events, encoder failure cleanup, two-run reproducibility, and a 50k-tick time/memory budget. 5. Per-clip and final structured logs include run, rank, tick range, frame, stride, events, bytes, elapsed time, peak frames in flight, and exact failing clip/frame/tick. 6. Focused formatting, strict clippy, app/core tests, and approved CI/replay verification pass with commands and results recorded.

title: Reel selection completion debt: normalize magnitudes and enforce a tie-free versioned order
description: Complete the scoring contract left by bd-16g.9.1 without reopening its real title-level implementation. Current V1 multiplies raw cross-kind magnitudes instead of normalizing within each kind and sorts only by score, tick, and kind, so equal events retain input order. Add deterministic per-kind normalization, a stable event identity tie-break, frozen scoring versions, exhaustive fixtures, and auditable editorial logs.
design: Keep scoring, normalization, selection, and clip math pure in scriptbots-core with no database, renderer, CLI, clock, or RNG dependency. Consume the stable persisted event identity owned by bd-16g.2.8. Reject non-finite inputs before sorting, use a tie-free total order, and preserve each scoring version as immutable code plus pinned fixtures.
acceptance_criteria: 1. V1 normalizes magnitude within each event kind using a documented deterministic method, defines degenerate-distribution behavior, and rejects non-finite inputs with typed errors rather than unstable ordering. 2. Every persisted event has a stable identity key and selection sorts by score descending, tick ascending, then that identity, leaving no ties or input-order dependence. 3. A checked fixture of about 50 events across at least six kinds pins exact score components, top-K ranks, clips, and serialized output; 100 deterministic input permutations, including equal-score same-tick cases, are byte-identical. 4. Tests cover 400 common versus one rare event, diversity limits, K zero and above count, run boundaries, separated and chained overlaps, annotation order, and max-not-sum merged scores. 5. A distinct V2 changes weights while the pinned V1 fixture remains byte-identical, proving versioning is semantic. 6. One structured editorial decision log records run identity, scoring version, counts, score components, selected ranks, merged windows, and exclusions so every choice is recomputable. 7. Focused formatting, strict clippy, core/app tests, and the approved verification lane pass with commands and results recorded.

title: Migrate scriptbots-web from Rc<RefCell<WorldState>> JS-driven stepping to HostCore
description: DISCOVERED during bd-2z0.12.4 scoping (2026-07-17): scriptbots-web still drives the world directly (JS calls tick() over Rc<RefCell<WorldState>>, crates/scriptbots-web/src/lib.rs Simulation) — the web analog of the interim frontend adapters that the HostCore migration beads (bd-2z0.4.x) retire for TUI/GPUI/Bevy. HostCore is runtime-neutral and !Send-compatible with wasm's single thread, so the web build can own one HostCore and route the wasm-bindgen boundary through the typed command/snapshot/status contracts instead of ad-hoc method calls. This preserves the renderer-neutral protocol on the web, gives the browser the same command-bus/snapshot-bus shapes as native, and is the PREREQUISITE for a decision-grade asupersync BrowserRuntime spike (bd-2z0.12.4): evaluating BrowserRuntime against the current interim stepping would measure a throwaway configuration. Scope: wrap HostCore in the web Simulation; route init/tick/reset/snapshot/registerBrain through the protocol surfaces; keep snapshot_format json|binary; preserve the bd-2wj parity harness semantics (the parity fixture is scenario-level and should survive unchanged — verify digest neutrality); no BrowserRuntime adoption in this bead (stepping stays JS-driven, just through HostCore). Sequencing: after the live-server/frontend HostClient migrations stabilize the protocol surface (bd-2z0.4.9 family) or in coordination with them.

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text: DEPENDENCY CORRECTION + design findings from HostCore API survey (RainyGorge, 2026-07-17). The original hard dep on bd-2z0.4.9 (HostClient control-plane migration) was overcautious — web consuming HostCore directly doesn't touch the CLI/REST/MCP surface; removed. The REAL blocking dep is bd-2z0.12.1 (renderer-neutral WASM snapshot projection): HostCore publishes Arc<RenderSnapshot> via latest_snapshot()/SnapshotHub, while scriptbots-web's entire boundary (JS bindings, postcard format, and the bd-2wj committed parity fixture) is built on scriptbots_core::DynamicWorldSnapshot. Migrating stepping to HostCore without resolving which projection the web boundary speaks would fork the snapshot schema — bd-2z0.12.1 owns that decision; added as blocker. Other design notes for the implementer: (1) HostCore::new(session_id, WorldState, HostCoreOptions) takes world ownership; web's reset(seed) becomes a new HostCore session — decide session-id semantics for browser reloads vs resets. (2) Web currently uses WorldState::with_persistence(NullPersistence); HostCore owns a JournalPort (VolatileJournal default) — the volatile journal with small capacity is probably right for browser, but bd-2wj fixture digest-neutrality MUST be verified (journal should be non-scientific, but prove it). (3) Options validation: volatile_event_history_capacity > scientific_event_capacity. (4) seed_agents + registerBrain need a pre-construction or command-path story (web seeds agents after world construction today; HostCore may require seeding via commands or before handoff). If bd-2z0.12.1 lands a DynamicWorldSnapshot-compatible projection, the bd-2wj fixture survives as v1; if it moves the schema, regenerate as v2 per that bead's own coordination note.

title: Add agent-keyed RNG substreams for insertion/permutation noninteraction
description: FOLLOW-UP TO bd-2cd1. Implement a versioned agent-keyed or counter-based stochastic substream protocol whose identity is derived from stable AgentUid plus operation/domain context, never dense index or iteration order. Persist/checkpoint every future-affecting counter or continuation, bind it into WorldDigest and the canonical run manifest/checkpoint envelope, and preserve native/WASM deterministic semantics. Acceptance: (1) adding a distant noninteracting agent leaves every pre-existing agents scientific state and per-agent RNG continuation unchanged across multiple ticks; (2) permuting dense storage does not alter outcomes; (3) offspring stochastic identities are deterministic from stable lineage/birth identity; (4) encode/decode idempotence and digest divergence cover all stored counters; (5) DSR-only native/WASM proof. Do not solve with one stream per transient AgentId or dense index.

title: Config layering: defaults -> scenario file -> environment -> CLI, with a matrix and layer digests
description:
SPLIT OUT OF bd-2z0.1.10 (2026-07-14). That bead had four acceptance criteria. Three are now
done; this is the fourth, and it is a distinct surface that deserves its own matrix rather than
being smuggled into a "close" on the strength of the other three.

DONE (bd-2z0.1.10, commits 281ee9b + 88a7d04):
- Thread-count precedence resolved in ONE pure function with an explicit order
  (--threads > SCRIPTBOTS_MAX_THREADS > auto-tune > --low-power > builtin), fixing a real bug
  where an exported SCRIPTBOTS_MAX_THREADS=16 was silently overwritten by --low-power's 2.
- Probe containment: auto-tune RECOMMENDS, it no longer decides.
- Declined layers are reported, not silently dropped.
- The run manifest now records the RESOLVED policy (count + deciding layer + declined layer), so
  a run can finally say how many threads produced it and who chose.

REMAINING, and it is this bead: the same layering discipline for THE CONFIG ITSELF.
  defaults -> scenario file -> environment -> CLI

Today `apply_env_overrides` (main.rs) folds environment variables into ScriptBotsConfig with a
pile of one-off `if let Ok(value) = env::var(..)` blocks, each parsing and warning in its own way.
There is no single place that says which layer beats which, and no test that pins it. That is the
same shape as the thread bug before it was fixed — the winner is whichever branch happens to run
last, rather than the layer the user most explicitly stated.

WHAT THIS BEAD OWES:
1. ONE pure resolver, in the shape of precedence.rs: it takes what each layer said and returns the
   merged config PLUS the provenance of every field that was overridden. Pure — no env reads, no
   file reads, no logging — because that is what made the thread matrix testable at all.
2. A TABLE-DRIVEN MATRIX over every layer pair, including the conflicts and the absent-value
   cases. The thread matrix (8 cases) is the template.
3. Scenario-file layering must be REAL: a scenario file that sets `world_width` must lose to an
   environment variable that sets it, which must lose to a CLI flag. Each of those is a case.
4. RECORD IT. `ScenarioIdentityV0::ordered_config_layer_digests` already exists and is EMPTY for
   real runs — the field was built for exactly this and nothing populates it. Every layer applied
   must append its content digest, in order, so a manifest can say not just WHAT the config was
   but WHICH LAYERS BUILT IT. A config digest that cannot be attributed to its layers cannot tell
   two runs apart when they disagree.
5. A field overridden across layers must be REPORTABLE, the way ThreadPolicy::overridden is. A
   user whose scenario file said one thing and whose environment said another deserves to see that
   in the run record rather than discover it from the results.

TRAP, inherited from the thread lane (see bd-3p7i): do NOT communicate resolved config by mutating
process-global environment variables. Startup currently does this for the thread count with
`unsafe set_var`, and it CLOBBERS the very provenance capture that was supposed to record the
user's environment. Pass values, don't smear them through the environment.

title: frankensqlite submodule legacy_sqlite_code/sqlite references unreachable sqlite object 450a9009 — all fresh clones fail to build
description: Reproduced on wlap (Windows, fresh cargo cache) at rust_scriptbots HEAD: cargo build fails inside the fsql sqlite git dependency with 'failed to update submodule legacy_sqlite_code/sqlite: object not found - no match for id 450a90097fabf4eac7568a9688b34278b4d72122'. git ls-remote https://github.com/sqlite/sqlite shows the object is not reachable from ANY ref (0 matches across 1709 branch refs), so every fresh clone of a frankensqlite-dependent repo is broken. Local caches with the populated submodule mask the failure — including the bd-2z0.8.9.11 pin qualification, which ran from a cache that had 450a9009 already fetched. All three local checkouts (cd9990b, 1eec0d2, e536d7f) pin that same sqlite object and are populated, so this is an upstream sqlite/sqlite reachability change, not an e536d7f regression. Needed: upstream fix (re-pin the submodule to a reachable sqlite commit, or vendor the content without a submodule) OR a frankensqlite release that drops the submodule requirement for the native Rust path. Interim workaround: pre-populate the cargo git checkout from a machine that has it and set submodule.legacy_sqlite_code/sqlite.update=none in the checkout config.
notes: Sharper diagnosis 2026-07-18: the object IS present in github.com/sqlite/sqlite and fetchable BY SHA — "git fetch https://github.com/sqlite/sqlite 450a90097fabf4eac7568a9688b34278b4d72122" succeeds locally (verified; commit subject "Do a better job of not generating unnecessary Bloom filters associated with IN operators."). It is unreachable only via ref-based refspecs (branches/tags), which is what cargo/libgit2 uses for submodule updates — hence fresh-clone failures while populated caches pass. Fresh-machine workaround without any pre-populated cache: in the failed checkout at <CARGO_HOME>/git/checkouts/frankensqlite-*/<rev>/legacy_sqlite_code/sqlite, run "git init && git remote add origin https://github.com/sqlite/sqlite && git fetch --depth 1 origin 450a90097fabf4eac7568a9688b34278b4d72122 && git checkout FETCH_HEAD", then set "submodule.legacy_sqlite_code/sqlite.update=none" in the parent checkout .git/config so cargo submodule update no-ops. Validated alternate: copy the populated submodule from any existing checkout (same object in cd9990b/1eec0d2/e536d7f). Upstream fix options for the frankensqlite owner: (a) fork sqlite and tag 450a9009 so it becomes ref-reachable; (b) vendor the sqlite tree directly and drop the submodule; (c) re-pin the gitlink to a reachable upstream commit (harness-reference drift risk — the vendored sqlite backs the TCL conformance harness). NOTE: the submodule is consumed only by frankensqlite harness/tests (tcl_conformance, spec audit), NOT by downstream consumers of the native facade — downstream breakage is purely cargo unconditional submodule init on checkout. (Earlier notes version was mangled by shell command substitution and has been rewritten verbatim.)
close_reason: Fixed at repo level and pushed in 97afce368: .cargo/config.toml now sets [net] git-fetch-with-cli = true so every fresh-clone git fetch (incl. the frankensqlite submodule) goes through the git CLI, which retries submodule fetches by exact OID; README troubleshooting documents the failure signature + manual recovery. Evidence (SwiftHarbor, this Mac): (1) git CLI fetch-by-SHA self-verified — 'git fetch --depth 1 https://github.com/sqlite/sqlite 450a9009...' completes in ~5s; (2) fresh-CARGO_HOME consumer crate at pin e536d7f with the flag: cargo fetch green in 38s, cargo vendor green; (3) fresh-CARGO_HOME workspace 'cargo check -p scriptbots-storage' with the checked-in config materialized the fsqlite checkout with legacy_sqlite_code/sqlite populated at exactly 450a9009 (build later SIGTERM'd by machine-level contention, git phase already complete); (4) frankensqlite confirmed the ONLY submodule-bearing git dep — zed/frankentorch/rust-xcb have no .gitmodules at pinned revs; (5) repo best-practices doc (RUST_SYSTEM_PROGRAMMING_BEST_PRACTICES.md line 139) already recommends this exact setting. Notes: on this Mac nightly-2026-07-09 even the libgit2 path fetched the SHA, so the wlap failure is environment-dependent (older libgit2/cargo behavior); final wlap end-to-end confirmation deferred to CalmMink while wlap's disk-pressure incident is active. Root upstream condition (gitlink unreachable-by-ref at BOTH e536d7f and frankensqlite main) is NOT fixed by this commit and is tracked in follow-up bd-iswv; fixing it requires frankensqlite-owner action and must not collide with the bd-2z0.8.9.10/.11 pin qualification.

title: GPUI dual-window double-steps the simulation; pause/speed are per-view
description: Remove GPUI dual-window ownership of scientific time. Both windows must consume the same host snapshots; repaint, visibility, resize, and window count must never call WorldState::step or own pause/speed accumulators.
design: Concrete GPUI presentation migration slice of the sole-owner runtime, before the direct-texture decision.

title: core/infotheory: MI bias guard measured at 0.0398 - why it exceeds the original 0.03 bound is unexplained
description:
RESOLVED IN PART by 8c1fade08 (cc_1/CopperCat). The orphan is landed; the open
question is narrower than it was.

MEASURED: mean_corrected = 0.03979384312202239 in test_negative_bias_correction.
Obtained by temporarily tightening the bound to force the assertion to print, then
restoring the file byte-for-byte (sha256 verified identical before and after).

WHAT THAT SETTLED
The value sits ABOVE the old 0.03 bound, so the test was FAILING on main. The
abandoned session was repairing a red test, not weakening a passing one. Declining
to land it was keeping main red, so it is now committed with the measured value,
the rationale for 0.05 specifically, and a pointer back to this bead recorded in a
comment beside the assertion.

WHAT REMAINS OPEN
Why is the corrected mean 0.0398 rather than under 0.03? Two candidates:
  (a) It always was, and 0.03 was simply never a correct bound for this fixture.
  (b) Something moved it - most plausibly a rand/dependency bump changing
      SmallRng's stream, which shifts every seeded statistical value in this
      module. crates/scriptbots-core/Cargo.toml was modified in the same window.
Distinguishing them means measuring the same value at an older commit (before the
Cargo.lock/rand change) and comparing. If (b), the drift is expected and the story
is closed. If (a), the estimator deserves review: with bins = 8 the fixture fills
64 joint cells from n = 200 samples, just above this module's own admissibility
floor of bins * bins * 2 = 128, which is precisely where residual Miller-Madow
bias is largest.

DO NOT simply raise the bound again if it drifts. Investigate calc_mi_mm and the
surrogate path first - this assertion is the only guard proving the bias
correction does substantive work, and it is what stands between the project and
silently over-reporting mutual information on noise.
close_reason:
ANSWERED in b2973fa5f. Candidate (a): the 0.03 bound was never correct for this fixture; nothing drifted.

MEASURED on current main (rch worker vmi1149989, self-reporting fixture, --nocapture):
  mean_uncorrected = 0.19880562389643910
  mean_corrected   = 0.03979384312202239
  clamped_runs     = 29/100

WHY (a) AND NOT (b). The corrected mean is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the 0.03979384312202239 measured on
2026-07-24 (commit 8c1fade08). Two independent reasons the bead's candidate (b) -- "a
rand/dependency bump moved SmallRng's stream" -- is excluded:
  1. Wrong generator. The fixture uses SmallRngStream (infotheory.rs:594), which is PROJECT-OWNED
     Xoshiro256++ seeded by SplitMix64, not rand's SmallRng. A rand bump cannot move its stream.
  2. The controlled experiment already ran, by accident. aaac3fd99 ("make scientific RNG portable
     across native and wasm", bd-7mh6) replaced the generator on 2026-07-25 14:13, AFTER the
     07-24 measurement. The value did not move by a single bit across that swap. Rebuilding at an
     older commit -- the archaeology this bead proposed -- is therefore unnecessary.

ESTIMATOR REVIEW, which the bead required before touching the bound. calc_mi_mm is CORRECT:
lines 367-369 compute plugin - (k_xy - k_x - k_y + 1)/(2N ln2), which is exactly Miller-Madow for
MI, i.e. I + [(m_x-1) + (m_y-1) - (m_xy-1)]/(2N ln2). No defect in the correction itself.

THE REAL DRIVER IS THE CLAMP, now measured rather than assumed. calc_mi_mm ends in
(plugin - mm_correction).max(0.0). That floor is defensible for a single point estimate --
mutual information cannot be negative -- but it is NOT neutral under averaging, and this fixture
averages 100 runs. 29 of those 100 runs are clamped. So mean_corrected does not estimate the
residual bias at all; it estimates E[max(0, MI_MM)], which is strictly greater than E[MI_MM]
whenever the null distribution has negative mass, and here 29% of it does. The guard is measuring
a truncated functional and calling it bias.

Supporting arithmetic: for independent variables at b=8, N=200 the plugin bias is about
(r-1)(s-1)/(2N ln2) = 49/277.26 = 0.177 bits, close to the measured 0.1988. With about 61 of 64
joint cells occupied the MM correction is about 0.167, implying a residual near 0.01 -- well under
the observed 0.0398. Truncating a 29% negative tail is the natural explanation for that gap.

BOUND UNCHANGED at 0.05, per the bead's explicit instruction not to raise it. The fixture now
prints all three numbers under --nocapture, so reading them no longer requires tightening the
bound until the assertion fires and restoring the file byte-for-byte (the method the previous
session had to use).

FOLLOW-UP, deliberately NOT done here to keep this bead narrow as instructed: deciding whether
compute_mi should expose an unclamped corrected value for bias assessment, or whether this guard
should assert on a statistic that is not truncated. That is estimator-contract work and belongs to
bd-r4ja, which I am continuing next.

VERIFIED: rch exec -- cargo test -p scriptbots-core --lib -- infotheory::tests --nocapture on
vmi1149989: 10 passed, 0 failed. rustfmt --edition 2024 --check: exit 0.

comments.author: QuietBeaver
comments.text:
OPEN QUESTION ANSWERED: candidate (a). The 0.03 bound was never correct for this fixture; nothing drifted.

MEASURED TODAY on rch worker hz2, current main plus a self-reporting println:
  bd-270k mean_uncorrected=0.19880562389643910
  bd-270k mean_corrected=0.03979384312202239

That corrected value is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the 0.03979384312202239 recorded in the bead and in the
comment beside the assertion, which was measured on 2026-07-24 (commit 8c1fade08).

WHY THAT SETTLES IT. The bead's candidate (b) was 'something moved it, most plausibly a
rand/dependency bump changing SmallRng's stream'. Two independent reasons that is now excluded:

1. WRONG GENERATOR. The fixture uses SmallRngStream::seed_from_u64(12345)
   (crates/scriptbots-core/src/infotheory.rs:594). SmallRngStream is PROJECT-OWNED Xoshiro256++
   seeded by SplitMix64, not rand's SmallRng, so a rand version bump cannot move its byte stream.
   Only rand's f64 range-mapping in random_range could have contributed, which is a far narrower
   surface than the bead assumed.

2. THE STRONGEST AVAILABLE TEST ALREADY RAN, ACCIDENTALLY. The scientific RNG was made
   project-owned in aaac3fd99 ('make scientific RNG portable across native and wasm', bd-7mh6) on
   2026-07-25 14:13 -- AFTER the 07-24 20:44 measurement. If the generator's output for this seed
   had changed at all, this fixture's mean would have moved. It did not move by a single bit
   across that swap. That is a real before/after comparison spanning the exact change most likely
   to have perturbed it, and it came back identical. (Consistent with intent: rand's SmallRng on
   64-bit IS Xoshiro256++, so a faithful project-owned reimplementation reproduces the sequence --
   the commit bought portability, not different numbers.)

CONCLUSION: the value is stable and was always ~0.0398. The original 0.03 in 7d364bd28 was simply
a wrong bound, not a bound that something later invalidated. No archaeology at an older commit is
needed; the RNG swap already served as the controlled experiment.

WHAT I DID NOT DO, and what remains: the bead says 'if (a), the estimator deserves review'. I have
not yet reviewed calc_mi_mm. Sketching the expectation so the next step is concrete -- for
independent variables the plugin bias is about (r-1)(s-1)/(2N ln2); with r=s=8, N=200 that is
49/277.26 = 0.177 bits, and the measured uncorrected mean of 0.1988 sits close to it. Miller-Madow
subtracts a term based on OCCUPIED cells, so at n=200 over 64 joint cells (mean occupancy ~3.1,
many cells empty by chance) the correction is necessarily smaller than the full-rank case and a
positive residual is EXPECTED, not evidence of a bug. Whether 0.0398 is the right residual needs
calc_mi_mm read against the Miller-Madow definition. That is the remaining work on this bead.

TOOLING IMPROVEMENT LANDED WITH THIS: the fixture now prints both means unconditionally under
--nocapture. Reading this number previously required tightening the bound until the assertion
fired and then restoring the file byte-for-byte (sha256-verified), which is a destructive way to
read a value the test already holds and leaves no record when it legitimately moves.

comments.author: QuietBeaver
comments.text:
CORRECTION, now that the statistic is measurable rather than inferred (landed b10a7cd4a under bd-r4ja).

My close reason on this bead said of the 0.0398 residual: 'Truncating a 29% negative tail is the natural explanation for that gap.' That overstated the clamp's role. Measured directly:

  mean_uncorrected = 0.19880562389643910
  mean_unclamped   = 0.03246288568194164   <-- new, this is E[MI_MM]
  mean_corrected   = 0.03979384312202239       (floored, E[max(0, MI_MM)])
  clamped_runs     = 29/100

The floor accounts for 0.0073 of the value -- real, about 18% of what was reported, and worth exposing. But the UNCLAMPED mean is still 0.0325, well above the ~0.01 that the Miller-Madow residual predicts at bins=8, n=200. So genuine under-correction at 64 joint cells from 200 samples is the DOMINANT term and truncation is secondary. My earlier sentence had that the wrong way round.

Everything else on this bead stands: candidate (a) is still the answer (the 0.03 bound was never correct, proven bit-identical across the aaac3fd99 RNG swap), and calc_mi_mm still correctly implements Miller-Madow.

WHY I GOT IT WRONG, since it is a reusable lesson: I reasoned from the clamp count (29/100 looked like a lot) to a conclusion about magnitude, without being able to measure the magnitude. 29% of runs being truncated does not tell you how FAR below zero they were -- and it turns out not very far. The fix was to expose bits_corrected_unclamped so the question is answerable rather than arguable, which is what bd-r4ja now does.

If anyone revisits the residual: the remaining ~0.02 gap between 0.0325 and the asymptotic prediction is the real open question, and it lives in the sparse-cell regime the bead already flagged (64 joint cells, mean occupancy ~3.1, just above this module's own bins*bins*2 admissibility floor).

title: main never emits a RunManifestV0: real runs carry no provenance record
description:
FOUND BY bd-2z0.1.10 (thread-precedence work, 2026-07-13). Verified by grep + read, not assumed: `RunManifestV0::from_world` / `from_world_with_provenance` are constructed ONLY from tests and library code. `main.rs` NEVER EMITS A RUN MANIFEST. `rg "RunManifestV0|run_manifest" crates/scriptbots-app/src/main.rs` returns nothing.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. RunManifestV0 is the project's provenance record: root_seed, scenario identity, normalized_config, config_digest, build provenance (source revision, tree cleanliness, toolchain, lockfile digest, compiled features), brain roster, `reproducible: bool`, warnings, and CharacterizationLimitationsV0. It is the artifact that lets somebody answer "what exactly produced this run?" — the entire honesty thesis of bd-2z0 rests on it.

And a real run produces NONE OF IT. The type is well-built and thoroughly tested; it is simply never written to disk by the binary a user actually runs. Every claim about reproducible, provenanced runs is therefore true of the LIBRARY and false of the PRODUCT.

CONSEQUENCES, concretely:
  - A user cannot tell which build, which seed, or which config produced a run directory.
  - bd-2z0.1.10's acceptance criterion ("the resolved values and source layer are recorded in RunManifestV0") is unsatisfiable as written — I could add a thread_policy field, but it would record nothing for real runs, which is worse than not adding it: it would look like provenance while carrying none.
  - The lab (bd-16g.1.5's notebook) and the shareable permalinks (bd-16g.8) both need a manifest to point at.

SCOPE.
- Emit RunManifestV0 once per run, at startup, after config resolution and world construction (the manifest needs the resolved config and the brain roster, so it cannot be written before the world exists).
- Write it to the run directory alongside the storage DB, as `manifest.json`, canonical-JSON encoded (the canonicalization already exists and is tested: `canonical_json_sorts_nested_keys_and_round_trips_manifest`).
- Record the thread policy (bd-2z0.1.10 left `ThreadPolicy` ready for exactly this: it carries the resolved count AND the deciding layer, because a run that used 2 threads because the operator asked is a different run from one where low-power quietly decided).
- Honour the existing `reproducible` / `warnings` / `limitations` fields rather than inventing new ones — they already say the true things (dirty tree, unavailable rustc, agent-identity limitation).

OUT OF SCOPE: changing the manifest SCHEMA (the wire golden is pinned and versioned; a field addition is a separate, reviewed change), and the lab/permalink consumers.

HARD REQUIREMENTS.
- The manifest must be written for EVERY run that produces a run directory, including runs that later fail — a manifest that only appears on success cannot explain a failure, which is when you need it most.
- Writing it must never take the world lock for longer than a snapshot read, and must never be able to fail the run: a provenance write that kills the simulation has inverted its own purpose. Log a warning and continue.
- Byte-identical for byte-identical runs (same seed, same config, same build) EXCEPT for the explicitly non-reproducible provenance fields (timestamps, host, durations), which must be segregated into ONE clearly-named block so a consumer can mask exactly that block and diff the rest.

TESTS.
- E2E: run the binary headless for N ticks against a temp run directory; assert `manifest.json` exists, parses, and its `config_digest` matches the digest of the config the run actually used.
- Two runs, same seed and config: manifests are byte-identical outside the non-reproducible block. This is the test that makes "provenanced" mean something.
- A run that FAILS mid-way still leaves a manifest (see hard requirements).
- A dirty source tree produces `reproducible: false` and a warning naming the dirt — assert it, because a manifest that claims reproducibility it does not have is worse than no manifest.

LOGGING. info once at emit: {path, config_digest, root_seed, reproducible, warning_count}. warn if the manifest could not be written, naming why — and CONTINUE.
close_reason: main now writes run.manifest.json next to the run DB (after brains+seeding, before bootstrap ticks), carrying the resolved thread policy AND its deciding layer; failures warn and never kill the run; reproducible=false is logged loudly. E2E runs the real binary and asserts the manifest exists, records the actual seed, and that two identical runs agree on config digest.

title: Migrate the ~51 core RNG call sites onto domain streams (MOVES the characterization digest)
description:
SPLIT OUT OF bd-2z0.3.10 (2026-07-14). That bead had two halves: DECIDE the generator, and
IMPLEMENT versioned domain streams. The decision landed (fnp-random REJECTED — nightly-only, no
wasm32 support, and its only advantage is NumPy bit-parity that this project does not need; its
parity oracle is the legacy C++ ScriptBots). The SUBSTRATE landed in a7f25e4
(crates/scriptbots-core/src/rng_domains.rs: RngDomain, versioned FNV-1a derivation over a stable
domain tag, DomainStreams with per-domain checkpoint/restore, 7 tests incl. the headline
independence proof).

WHAT REMAINS: cutting the ~51 `self.rng` call sites in scriptbots-core over to their domains.

WHY IT IS A SEPARATE BEAD, and not laziness: the migration RE-BASELINES EVERY STOCHASTIC
DECISION and therefore MOVES THE CHARACTERIZATION DIGEST and WorldDigestV1. Burying a
science-wide re-baseline inside the commit that introduces the substrate would make it
unreviewable — nobody could tell which digest movement came from the new streams and which from
a mistake. Same reasoning that split bd-300o out of bd-16g.15.1.

THE WORK:
1. Assign each of the ~51 `self.rng` sites in crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs to a domain.
   Grep `rg -n '&mut self\.rng|self\.rng\.' crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs`. The obvious
   mapping, from the sites I read while building the substrate:
     - food scatter / regrowth                 -> RngDomain::Food
     - spawn placement, culling, population floor injection, random_spawn_position -> Population
     - partner/parent selection, random_key    -> Lineage
     - BrainRunner::mutate, AgentRuntime mutation rates -> Mutation
     - BrainRunner::crossover, the crossover_chance roll -> Crossover
     - interventions, terrain, weather         -> Environment
   DO NOT GUESS on the ambiguous ones. `AgentRuntime::new_random` (lib.rs ~11624, ~11775) is
   used both for seeding founders (Population) and for the discarded-runtime path — read each
   call site rather than pattern-matching on the function name.

2. Replace `WorldState::rng: SmallRngStream` with `DomainStreams`. Note `rng_before:
   self.rng.clone()` (~11706) captures the stream for replay/recovery — that becomes a
   DomainStreams clone, and the replay path must be updated in lockstep or recovery silently
   restores the wrong streams.

3. WorldDigestV1's `rng` lane currently encodes the single stream's checkpoint. It must encode
   ALL SIX domain checkpoints (DomainStreams::checkpoint() already returns them in a stable
   BTreeMap). If it does not, two worlds whose mutation streams are poised differently would
   digest identically — reintroducing, in a new place, exactly the blindness bd-2z0.3.9 removed.

4. RunManifestV1::random_stream is a single RandomStreamState. It must become the per-domain
   map, or a resumed run restores only one domain and silently re-rolls the other five.

5. THE ACCEPTANCE TEST, and it is the one that justifies the whole bead:
   Add a draw to ONE domain's code path (e.g. an extra food-scatter roll) and assert that the
   MUTATION lane of WorldDigestV1 is UNCHANGED across an otherwise identical run. That is the
   property the single-stream design cannot satisfy, and it is what makes controlled experiments
   possible. Without it, this migration is just moving code around.

6. RE-BASELINE DELIBERATELY: the digest WILL move. Record the before/after digests in the commit
   message so the move is a reviewed artifact rather than a mystery, and confirm no golden
   elsewhere in the repo is silently invalidated (as of today no pinned characterization-digest
   constants exist — verify that is still true before landing).
close_reason: Six-domain RNG cutover, strict V1.3/V3 envelopes, deliberate golden moves, and independent DSR native/WASM/performance proofs completed

comments.author: TopazCastle
comments.text: Claimed after bd-2z0.3.14 closed and authoritative BV/BR re-triage. comments.text:
SCOPE WAS WRONG — CORRECTED BY INVESTIGATION (2026-07-13). I claimed this to write the provenance assertions and found there is NO PROVENANCE TO ASSERT. Not 'unasserted': UNPRODUCED.

WHAT I FOUND (verified by reading, not assumed):
1. `BrainProvenance` is NEVER CONSTRUCTED outside tests. `rg 'BrainProvenance::'` in core's non-test region returns nothing.
2. `register_family` is NEVER CALLED outside core. `rg 'register_family'` across the workspace, excluding core's own lib.rs, returns nothing. The family registry is never populated by any product code.
3. `stage_spawn_commit` — the path every offspring actually takes — uses `BrainRunner::clone_runner` / `crossover` / `mutate`. It never touches BrainGenomeEnvelope, never builds a BrainProvenance, never consults a family adapter.

SO THERE ARE TWO PARALLEL SYSTEMS:
  (a) BrainRunner (clone/mutate/crossover) — what reproduction ACTUALLY runs on. It works, and bd-2z0.3.6 now proves it (mutation off -> child genome bit-identical to parent; mutation on -> provably differs). It carries NO provenance.
  (b) BrainFamilyAdapter + BrainGenomeEnvelope + BrainProvenance + the family codecs (MlpBrainFamily, DwraonFamilyAdapter, AssemblyFamilyAdapter, all landed recently) — a complete, well-typed genome protocol that NOTHING WIRES UP.

CONSEQUENCE, and it is bigger than this bead: bd-16g.13.1 (genome browser / parent-child mutation diff) has NO GENOMES TO DIFF. bd-16g.3's phylogeny can draw edges but cannot say what happened along them. Any feature that consumes genome provenance is currently consuming a type that no run ever fills in.

REVISED SCOPE (the assertion is the LAST step, not the first):
  1. DECIDE, explicitly: does the BrainRunner path become the canonical one (and provenance rides on it), or does reproduction move onto the adapter/genome protocol? Both are defensible; picking neither leaves two systems and a permanent lie. Whoever owns bd-2z0.3.2's protocol should make this call — it is their design.
  2. WIRE the chosen path: register the families at startup (install_brains is the obvious place — it already installs the runner factories), and have the spawn path produce a genome envelope carrying BrainProvenance { parents: [Option<AgentUid>; 2], created_at }.
  3. ONLY THEN assert what this bead originally asked for: parent UIDs on crossover vs clone, genome hashes that actually change when the genome changes, OffspringStatePolicy honoured for BOTH Reset and Inherit, and a >=5-generation chain proving genomes keep evolving rather than converging on a placeholder.

I am RELEASING this bead rather than doing step 1 myself: the family adapters landed in the last few hours and whoever is building them is mid-flight in this area. Wiring it from the outside would collide with their design. Mailing them the finding.

title: Storage conformance test re-declares weakened schema copy; export SCRIPTBOTS_SCHEMA_V1 and consume it
description:
ROOT CAUSE (anchors at e2d9aaa, crates/scriptbots-storage/tests/frankensqlite_workload_conformance.rs:12-140): the workload-conformance suite re-declares a private, WEAKENED copy of the production schema — every NOT NULL and CHECK (x IN (0,1)) constraint stripped — plus its own copy of the 39-column agent INSERT. It therefore validates the fsqlite engine against a schema nobody ships, and silently drifts whenever SCRIPTBOTS_SCHEMA_V1 changes; the real constraints are only exercised by the in-crate unit test.

FIX:
1. Export the production DDL from the crate: pub const SCRIPTBOTS_SCHEMA_V1 (or a Storage::schema_sql() accessor) plus the canonical agent_insert_sql() column list, and make the conformance test consume those exports — delete-by-replacement of the local copies (in-place edit of the test file; no new files).
2. Add a constraint-enforcement probe to the conformance suite: after applying the real schema, attempt a direct INSERT violating a NOT NULL and one violating a CHECK; both must error (proving the engine enforces what production declares).
3. Keep the suite honest about what it gates: it opens the exact pinned fsqlite revision file-backed, closes, reopens, verifies committed data + integrity_check — those assertions stay untouched.

TESTS: the suite itself; plus one unit test in lib.rs asserting schema_sql() executes cleanly on :memory: and contains the expected table names, so the export cannot rot. LOGGING: conformance test logs each DDL batch it applies and row counts per table on the reopen pass, so CI failures localize without rerunning locally.
close_reason: Production schema and canonical agent INSERT are exported and consumed by FrankenSQLite conformance; constraints, reopen/integrity, row-count diagnostics, and migration-vs-export drift guard are covered. Same exact-source DSR runtime-storage-union6-f44c236 is fully green.

title: brain-mlp: zero-scale mutation rewrites signed-zero genome bits
description: Confirmed metamorphic identity defect in crates/scriptbots-brain/src/mlp.rs. The MLP protocol accepts finite -0.0 bias, gain, and weight values and encodes their bits exactly, but mutate_parameters always executes selected continuous arithmetic at scale == 0.0. Preserve the exact gate/index/Gaussian RNG schedule, skip only continuous arithmetic when scale is zero, add a scripted negative-zero payload/continuation regression, and bump the MLP adapter semantic identity.

title: Design review: differential-drive turn rate ~10x below legacy (heading += (r-l)*speed/wheel_base vs C++ BOTSPEED*(w2-w1))
description:
DESIGN REVIEW — decide and implement one locomotion policy. Evidence (anchors at e2d9aaa vs original_scriptbots_code_for_reference/World.cpp:362-372):
- Legacy: BOTSPEED=0.3; each wheel's velocity rotates the bot about the OPPOSITE wheel contact point; net turn rate ~ BOTSPEED*(w2-w1) rad/tick (max ~0.3, ~17 deg/tick) and translation emerges from the two rotation applications.
- Rust stage_actuation: heading += (right-left)*bot_speed/wheel_base with wheel_base = 2*bot_radius = 20 -> max ~0.03 rad/tick (~1.7 deg/tick), 10x less agile, and translation is straight along the averaged heading (no rotate-about-wheel arc).
CONSEQUENCE: predators cannot execute legacy-style tight pursuit turns; evolved behavior differs qualitatively from the reference simulator; the README's faithful-port claim is materially weakened. This was flagged as "intentional-looking" by audit — the decision has never actually been made, which is exactly what this bead resolves.

OPTIONS: (A) restore legacy kinematics exactly, selectable via config (locomotion_model = "legacy" | "differential"), default legacy for parity — RECOMMENDED because parity is a core project promise and the differential model can stay for experiments; (B) keep differential drive but retune wheel_base so the angular-velocity envelope matches legacy (cheaper, still loses the rotate-about-wheel arc); (C) declare the divergence intentional and document it prominently in README + parity notes. Whichever option wins must be recorded in the bead comments with rationale.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES (for option A): port World.cpp's exact two-rotation update into stage_actuation behind the config enum; keep torus wrapping; boost multiplies wheel speeds as today; the characterization trace constants in crates/scriptbots-app/src/lib.rs WILL change — re-pin them in the same commit with the rationale in the commit message (see e2d9aaa for the precedent and procedure).

TESTS (required): micro-oracle unit tests with 3-4 numeric cases hand-computed from World.cpp math (given w1,w2,angle,pos -> expected angle,pos within 1e-6); property tests: w1==w2 -> straight line, w1==-w2 -> pure rotation with position invariant to within float noise; e2e: seeded 500-tick run logging the |dheading|/tick distribution (mean, p95, max) via tracing, asserted against the legacy envelope (~0.3 rad max) when locomotion_model=legacy and against the differential envelope otherwise; determinism suite green after re-pinning.
close_reason: Implemented exact selectable legacy locomotion and verified by clean-commit DSR correctness, native/WASM parity, reviewed performance baseline promotion, and strict exact-class comparison

comments.text: DESIGN REVIEW VERDICT (RainyGorge, 2026-07-16): OPTION A — restore legacy kinematics exactly behind locomotion_model = legacy|differential, DEFAULT LEGACY. Verified at current HEAD, and the divergence is LARGER than this bead's evidence: (1) TURN: legacy heading += BOTSPEED*(w2-w1), max 0.3 rad/tick (0.6 boosted, BOOSTSIZEMULT=2). Rust stage_actuation angular = (right-left)*bot_speed/wheel_base with wheel_base=2*bot_radius=20 -> max 0.015 rad/tick (0.03 boosted): 20x less agile, not 10x (the 10x figure assumed wheel_base=10). - Toolchain: workspace already pins nightly-2026-07-09 (rust-toolchain.toml), so nightly-only franken deps are admissible.

Keep detect.rs hand-rolled and bit-stable (f64::total_cmp) — fsci validates it OFFLINE, never replaces it.

title: Build/test is broken on this checkout path: RCH refuses to offload, local link fails (no mold)
description:
SYMPTOM: every 'cargo test'/'cargo build' in this working copy fails with:
  clang: error: invalid linker name in argument '-fuse-ld=mold'

ROOT CAUSE (from 'rch diagnose'):
  Project path normalization failed for /Users/jemanuel/projects/rust_scriptbots:
  input resolves outside canonical root
  (resolved=/Users/jemanuel/projects/rust_scriptbots root=/Volumes/USBNVME16TB/data/projects)

RCH classifies the command correctly (CargoTest, confidence 0.95 >= 0.85, 'WOULD
INTERCEPT'), selects a worker, and then FAILS path normalization and falls back to a
LOCAL build. The local build cannot succeed: .cargo/config.toml sets
target = x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu with -fuse-ld=mold, and this is an aarch64 macOS
host with no mold installed. Even if it linked, the product would be a Linux ELF that
cannot execute here. So ALL testing in this repo depends on RCH offload working.

THE PATH TOPOLOGY IS INCONSISTENT:
  /data -> /Volumes/USBNVME16TB/data      (rch canonical_root = /data/projects)
  /dp   -> /Users/jemanuel/projects        (rch alias_root = /dp)
The repo exists ONLY under /dp (= /Users/jemanuel/projects/rust_scriptbots). There is
no /data/projects/rust_scriptbots. RCH canonicalizes the cwd, so invoking cargo from
the /dp spelling does not help — it realpaths straight back to /Users/... and is
rejected. 'rch exec -- cargo ...' fails the same way.

WHO IS AFFECTED: everyone working in this checkout. Other agents' cargo processes were
observed holding the build-directory lock and would hit the same wall.

WORKAROUND I USED (changes NO config, repo or global):
  CARGO_BUILD_TARGET=aarch64-apple-darwin CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<scratch> cargo test -p <crate>
This builds natively for the host and links with the system linker. scriptbots-core is
pure Rust and passes fully this way (191 tests, clippy -D warnings clean).
CAVEAT, and it matters: ~34 scriptbots-storage tests FAIL under this workaround —
process-exit/durability/file-lock tests that depend on platform semantics (e.g.
'child did not exit at the requested admitted boundary', 101 vs 86). I verified those
failures reproduce on a CLEAN TREE, so they are an artifact of the native target and
NOT a regression. Do not use this workaround to certify storage.

FIX OPTIONS (a human should choose; I did not want to rewrite the user's global tool
config or the shared .cargo/config.toml, both of which have blast radius beyond one task):
  (a) point RCH's path topology at the real checkout root, or
  (b) move/mirror the checkout under /data/projects so it sits inside canonical_root, or
  (c) install mold + a native linker profile so local builds work without RCH.

Until this is resolved, NOTHING in this repo can be certified on its canonical target.
close_reason: Superseded by the mandatory DSR-only verification lane; legacy RCH/direct Cargo remains unsupported but is no longer a certification dependency

comments.author: GoldenPanther
comments.text:
SHARPER DIAGNOSIS (GoldenPanther, 2026-07-13). I tested the fix I proposed and it is
WRONG. Correcting the record before anyone builds on it.

WHAT I DID: `.rch/config.toml` is project-scoped and OUTRANKS the user config, so I set
    [path_topology]
    canonical_root = "/Users/jemanuel/projects"
and re-ran. Path normalization then SUCCEEDED — `rch diagnose` stopped warning, RCH
selected a worker (vmi1152480) and started the transfer pipeline. So normalization was
indeed the first wall, and this does clear it.

BUT IT REVEALS THE REAL SEMANTICS AND BREAKS THE NEXT STAGE:

    rsync: [generator] failed to set times on
      "/Users/jemanuel/projects/rust_scriptbots/ci/fixtures": Operation not permitted (1)
    rsync error: some files/attrs were not transferred (code 23)
    Remote execution failed: Project sync failed: rsync failed, running locally

`canonical_root` is the REMOTE path root ON THE LINUX WORKERS, not a local directory.
Pointing it at the local checkout makes RCH try to rsync the project INTO
/Users/jemanuel/projects/... ON THE WORKER, which it cannot create/chtimes. So the
"fix" trades a fast failure for a slow one: every build would now burn ~40s on a doomed
rsync before falling back to the same unlinkable local build. That is strictly worse, so
I REMOVED the file. The tree is back exactly as it was (canonical_root = /data/projects).

WHY THE OTHER PROJECTS WORK: they live under /data/projects (-> /Volumes/USBNVME16TB/data
/projects). Their realpath lands inside the resolved canonical root, so normalization
passes AND the remote destination is the path the workers actually expect. Our repo is
the outlier: it sits at /Users/jemanuel/projects/rust_scriptbots.

THE SYMLINKS ARE INCONSISTENT WITH RCH'S MODEL, AND THAT IS THE BUG:
    /data -> /Volumes/USBNVME16TB/data       (canonical_root = /data/projects)
    /dp   -> /Users/jemanuel/projects        (alias_root = /dp)
For RCH's alias mechanism to mean anything, /dp should resolve INTO /data/projects. It
does not — it points at the home directory instead. RCH canonicalizes the cwd via
realpath, so invoking cargo from the /dp spelling cannot help: it resolves straight back
to /Users/... and is rejected. Both symlinks are dated 2026-07-11, so this likely broke
when projects were moved off the USB volume.

SO THE VIABLE FIXES ARE (a human should choose):
  1. Move/mirror this checkout under /data/projects (i.e. onto the USB volume) so it sits
     inside the canonical root, like every project that currently offloads successfully.
     This is the option most consistent with how RCH is already configured and working.
  2. Repoint /dp -> /data/projects and relocate the checkout accordingly.
  3. Teach RCH a local->remote path MAPPING (distinct from a shared root) so a checkout
     outside canonical_root can still be synced to the correct remote destination. This is
     an RCH feature question, not a config one.
  4. Install mold + a native linker profile so local builds work without RCH at all.

DO NOT do what I tried (overriding canonical_root to the local path). It clears
normalization and then dies in rsync.

UNCHANGED AND STILL TRUE: core CAN be tested today with
  CARGO_BUILD_TARGET=aarch64-apple-darwin CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<scratch> cargo test -p scriptbots-core
(191 tests green that way), but this does NOT certify scriptbots-storage — ~34 of its
process-exit/durability tests fail on the native target, and I confirmed on a clean tree
that those failures are a target artifact, not a regression.

comments.text: Audited under the current DSR-only policy. DSR run rust_scriptbots_bd_2z0_8_9_4_4_verify/bd-2z0-8-9-4-4-20260715-2 proved focused storage behavior plus full workspace check, strict clippy, and workspace tests on darwin/arm64 at 60e06b3. comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
bd-d3wu audit (cc_3): this close is a SCOPE DECISION, not a fix, and its premise is now STALE. No reopen needed — recording so nobody acts on the stated rationale.

CLOSE REASON SAID: 'Superseded by the mandatory DSR-only verification lane; legacy RCH/direct Cargo remains unsupported but is no longer a certification dependency.'

WHY THAT IS NO LONGER TRUE:
 - bd-h7v0 (filed and fixed 2026-07-24, commit 51ef4809e) removed the global [build] target = x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu from .cargo/config.toml, which was the actual root cause of the local link failure this bead described. Verified in HEAD: the [build] target is gone and the file now carries an explanatory comment naming the exact failure ('clang: error: invalid linker name in argument -fuse-ld=mold'). bd-h7v0's own close reason proves BOTH lanes before commit — remote placed on hz2 (build #29942787491233842) exit=0, and local resolution restored.
 - AGENTS.md still mandates rch as the operative build lane (rch exec -- cargo build/test/clippy, AGENTS.md:664-666, plus the Codex note at :679). DSR-only applies specifically to performance execution (AGENTS.md:217) and to release/batch certification — not to ordinary scoped builds.

So the tracker asserted RCH was unsupported while the project's own agent instructions required it, and that contradiction had a real cost: this session, multiple agents (including me) spent hours treating rch failures as infrastructure outages. The genuine causes turned out to be (a) this config pin, now fixed by bd-h7v0, and (b) bd-oite's active_project_exclusion, where rch exits 1 with zero output when every healthy worker is already building the same project. Neither is 'RCH is unsupported'.

CLASSIFICATION: superseded-then-resolved-elsewhere. The outcome is correct (the problem is fixed); only the stated rationale is misleading. Anyone reading this close reason today would wrongly conclude the RCH lane is unsupported and stop using it, contrary to AGENTS.md.

title: wasm-vs-native parity test runs both sides in wasm runtime with mismatched config; compare against committed native fixture
description:
ROOT CAUSE (anchors at e2d9aaa, crates/scriptbots-web/src/lib.rs ~620-724): the "wasm-vs-native parity" test is only half-meaningful. (a) Config mismatch: the reference world is built from a raw config with default population_spawn_interval=100 while the harness SimSpec::config() zeroes it; every case runs <=64 ticks so stage_population never fires and the mismatch stays invisible — extend past 100 ticks and one side spawns agents the other does not. (b) Both the "native" and "wasm" sides execute inside the same wasm test runtime (wasm_bindgen_test_configure!(run_in_browser)), so the test proves same-runtime determinism of the wrapper, NOT cross-architecture parity; native<->wasm float divergence (libm sin/cos/atan2/powf differ across platforms) is structurally undetectable.

FIX:
1. Use SimSpec::config() for BOTH sides so the scenario is identical, and extend at least one case to >=150 ticks so population spawning is exercised.
2. Add a committed native-generated fixture: a native-only (#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]) test/generator in scriptbots-web that runs pinned seeds and serializes postcard snapshots at ticks {1, 8, 64, 150} to tests/fixtures/native_parity_v1.postcard. The wasm CI test deserializes the committed fixture and compares against wasm-computed snapshots.
3. Comparison policy: per-agent position/velocity/heading/energy with explicit tolerance (start 1e-5); on mismatch, log the FIRST diverging tick, agent index, field name, both values, absolute delta, and the config hash — enough to diagnose from CI output alone. If genuine libm divergence appears, the deliverable becomes a documented per-field tolerance policy (recorded in the fixture header), not a silent loosening.

title: README/AGENTS misstate the app control surface: wrong MCP SDK, 4 of 13 MCP tools, 11 REST endpoints undocumented
description:
Reality check of README application-layer claims (cc_3, Round 1) found three concrete contradictions between the docs and crates/scriptbots-app.

1. WRONG DEPENDENCY. README.md L91 labels the MCP transport '(mcp_protocol_sdk)' and AGENTS.md L80 lists 'mcp-protocol-sdk' in Key Dependencies. 2. MCP TOOL LIST IS 4 OF 13. README.md L876-881 says 'Tools exposed:' and lists only list_knobs, get_config, apply_updates, apply_patch. servers.rs registers 13: those four plus list_presets, apply_preset, pause, resume, step, set_speed, get_status, shutdown, get_command_status (servers.rs:1904-2055). An MCP client reading the README cannot discover most of the control surface.

3. REST ENDPOINT LIST OMITS 11 LIVE ROUTES. README.md L756-773 presents an 'Endpoints:' list. Missing from it, but registered in servers.rs:1826-1861: /api/ws/stream, /api/narrative/search, /api/scenario, /api/pause, /api/resume, /api/step, /api/speed, /api/status, /api/control/pause, /api/control/resume, /api/control/step, /api/control/speed, /api/control/status/{command_id}.

title: Define auto-tune, low-power, and user-config precedence
description: Make startup configuration precedence explicit and reproducible across defaults, scenario files, environment, CLI, low-power mode, auto-tune probe children, and final runs. Explicit user values must not be silently overwritten, and the resolved policy must be present in run provenance.
acceptance_criteria: A table-driven matrix covers defaults, scenario, environment, CLI, low-power, auto-tune probe children, and final-run layering; explicit user values win according to the documented order and are never silently reset; probe overrides cannot leak into the final run; the resolved values and source layer are recorded in RunManifestV0; deterministic tests cover conflicting and absent values.
close_reason: Landed 281ee9b (precedence) + 88a7d04 (manifest records it). The fourth criterion — config-layering (defaults -> scenario file -> env -> CLI) — is a distinct surface and is split to bd-1n2p rather than being closed on the strength of the other three. WHAT LANDED: a real bug is fixed (an exported SCRIPTBOTS_MAX_THREADS=16 was silently overwritten by --low-power's 2, with no warning and no record); precedence is now one pure function with an explicit order and an 8-case matrix; the auto-tune probe RECOMMENDS rather than decides, so a probe child's tuning cannot leak into a run whose operator already chose; declined layers are reported rather than dropped; and the manifest now records the RESOLVED policy — the count, the LAYER that decided (cli-flag/environment/auto-tune/low-power-default/builtin-default), and the layer that was DECLINED. That last part closes the criterion I previously could not: when I first worked this bead the binary emitted no manifest at all, so a thread_policy field would have recorded nothing; bd-28yt then wired emission into startup, which unblocked it. Proven e2e through the real binary, not a unit test of the resolver. TWO DEFECTS FOUND WHILE TESTING, both filed: (1) bd-15c8 — FrankenSQLite refuses to open a database on exFAT, which is what external drives are formatted as; proven by flipping TMPDIR from exFAT to APFS and watching the same tests go 0/4 -> 4/4 with no code change. This also CORRECTS THE RECORD: several of us have been writing these storage failures off as an 'aarch64 target artifact', and that diagnosis was wrong — the filesystem is the variable, and real regressions could be hiding behind that excuse. (2) bd-3p7i — the manifest's environment capture is clobbered by our own unsafe set_var, so it reports the resolved value rather than what the user exported and cannot evidence an override at all; that is exactly why thread_policy had to exist. clippy -D warnings clean; 4/4 e2e green.

Related: --det-check now composes the parent config, pins one shared seed, and forwards the full config layer to both children (previously it compared two differently-seeded runs and ignored parent CLI flags). The broader precedence contract (defaults < scenario files < env < CLI, documented auto-tune/low-power interaction, reproducible probe children) remains this bead's deliverable.

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text:
PART 1 LANDED (281ee9b). Bead stays OPEN — two of the four acceptance criteria are done, two are not, and closing on the other two would be exactly the ceremonial dishonesty bd-2z0.1.4 just removed.

DONE:
- A REAL BUG IS FIXED. A user who exported SCRIPTBOTS_MAX_THREADS=16 and passed --low-power had their explicit value silently overwritten with 2. No warning, no record. Cause: the thread count was decided by a chain of if/else-if branches scattered through startup, each writing into a process-global env var, so the winner was whichever branch ran LAST rather than the layer the user most explicitly stated.
- PRECEDENCE IS NOW EXPLICIT, in one pure function (crates/scriptbots-app/src/precedence.rs): --threads > SCRIPTBOTS_MAX_THREADS > auto-tune > --low-power > builtin. The organising rule: a layer naming a SPECIFIC VALUE beats a layer expressing a PREFERENCE about defaults. --low-power is a MODE that fills in a knob the user did not set; it does not overrule one they did.
- PROBE CONTAINMENT: the auto-tune probe now RECOMMENDS rather than decides (main.rs no longer set_vars from the probe). Evidence must not overrule an instruction, and that is precisely what stops a probe child's tuning leaking into a final run whose operator already decided. Tested.
- DECLINED LAYERS ARE REPORTED, not silently dropped (ThreadPolicy::overridden + a log line).
- TABLE-DRIVEN MATRIX: 8 cases over CLI/env/auto-tune/low-power/default incl. every conflict and the absent-value case, plus tests for probe containment, declined-layer reporting, and purity.

REMAINING SCOPE (why this bead is not closed):
1. SCENARIO-FILE AND CLI CONFIG LAYERING IS NOT COVERED. The matrix covers the THREAD knob's layers. The brief also asks for defaults -> scenario file -> environment -> CLI layering over the config itself (load_config_layer / merge path). That is a distinct surface and deserves its own matrix.
2. THE MANIFEST DOES NOT RECORD THE RESOLVED POLICY, because main.rs NEVER EMITS A RUN MANIFEST AT ALL. RunManifestV0::from_world is currently only constructed from tests and tooling — I verified this rather than assuming it. Adding a thread_policy field would therefore record nothing for real runs; the actual gap is that the manifest emission path is not wired into startup, which is a bigger and separate problem than precedence. Recommend splitting it out rather than pretending a field satisfies the criterion.

FINDING FOR WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP: the startup path mutates process-global env vars with unsafe set_var to communicate decisions to the Rayon pool builder in core. That is a workable channel but a poor one (it is unsafe in Rust 2024 precisely because it races with other threads). If HostCore (bd-2z0.4.5) lands a sole-owner config path, the thread policy should travel through it as a value rather than through the environment.

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text:
CLOSED. All four elements of the brief are satisfied; two were already true and two were ceremonial.

1. INSPECT RENDERED TERMINAL BUFFERS - DONE. run_headless_frames always drew into a real ratatui TestBackend and then THREW THE BUFFER AWAY. Nothing read it, so the draw could have been a no-op while the test passed on the strength of the simulation having ticked. The buffer is now inspectable and a new test asserts the HUD panel and status line were painted, that >200 cells are non-blank, and that the tick shown is THIS world's tick (a HUD rendering a plausible screen for the WRONG world is worse than one rendering nothing).

2. DISTINGUISH CPU SURROGATE FROM LIVE FRAMEBUFFER - DONE. wgpu_capture_smoke/agents asserted only that a PNG existed and that its FILE LENGTH was > 0. A PNG of a solid black frame passes both. Worse, both are named wgpu_* and both run green on a headless box with NO GPU - i.e. llvmpipe, a CPU rasterizer, was doing the drawing (new_for_capture_test quietly sets allow_software_adapter). The compositor always knew which adapter it picked and never told anyone; it now reports it, and every failure message names the surface that actually rasterized.

3. FAIL REPLAY VERIFICATION ON EMPTY EVIDENCE - ALREADY TRUE. require_non_vacuous_replay (main.rs:1755) is wired into the real path at main.rs:1680 and refuses a vacuous nonzero run. Verified rather than assumed; no change needed.

4. RENAME TESTS THAT OVERCLAIM - DONE. wgpu_capture_smoke -> a_captured_terrain_frame_is_actually_rasterized_and_not_merely_written; wgpu_capture_agents -> both_agents_are_rasterized_into_the_frame_at_the_positions_they_were_given.

A FINDING WORTH RECORDING: my first version of the agents test demanded the agent's literal input colour at its centre pixel, and it FAILED - but the renderer was right and my test was wrong. The agents carry glow and selection, so the red agent lands on screen as a washed pink [255,188,175], not [255,64,51]. Rather than reverse-engineer the blend (which would have been a test of the shader's arithmetic, not of whether the agent was drawn), the test now renders the SAME scene with the agents removed and requires the frames to differ near each agent AND to be identical in a far corner. If the agent-drawing path were deleted the frames would be identical - the one thing the old test could never notice.

BOTH NEW ALARMS ARE PROVEN TO FIRE: two tests construct exactly the artifacts the old assertions would have accepted (a uniform black image; an untouched terminal buffer) and prove the new detectors reject them. An evidence check nobody has watched fail is a check nobody knows works.

comments.text: CONFIRMED IN PRACTICE (2026-07-12, GoldenPanther) with a concrete failure: bv reads .beads/beads.jsonl while br exports to .beads/issues.jsonl. At the time of writing, beads.jsonl was 146 BYTES and contained ZERO of the 153 issues in the br database — so 'bv --robot-triage' cheerfully reported open_count=100 and 'bv --robot-insights' reported Cycles: none, both computed from an essentially EMPTY graph. This is worse than a stale number: bv's cycle check silently passes because there is nothing to check, so an agent that validates a new dependency graph with bv gets a false green. I worked around it by copying issues.jsonl -> <tmp>/.beads/beads.jsonl and running 'bv --db <tmp>/.beads' (which then saw all 153 beads, 133 open, 45 actionable, no cycles — the real answer). FIX SHAPE: make br export write the file bv reads (or make bv read issues.jsonl / accept the br DB directly), and add a guard so bv REFUSES to emit metrics when its snapshot's bead count is implausibly smaller than the DB's (a silent empty-graph green is the dangerous case, not the stale-by-one case). Suggested test: create N beads via br, run bv --robot-insights, assert bead_count matches; and assert bv errors (not passes) when handed an empty/missing snapshot.

title: scriptbots-analytics crate + sb-analyze CLI scaffold (offline science layer)
description:
WHY. bd-2z0.11.1/.11.2/.11.3 and bd-16g.1.4 all need a HOME: an offline analytics layer that reads finished run DBs and produces reports. Today the only offline consumer is control_cli's Export subcommand (crates/scriptbots-app/src/bin/control_cli.rs:85-134), which reads the run DB DIRECTLY via --db — exactly the direct-database-access-from-app-binaries pattern bd-2z0.8.9.5 exists to remove. A dedicated analytics crate fixes both problems at once: it becomes the ONE blessed offline DB reader (read-only, identity-verified), and the franken analytics adapters (fsci-stats, fnx, frankenpandas) get a home outside the default product build (plan build budgets: default TUI/server product must not compile heavy deps) and outside the wasm graph entirely.

SCOPE (scaffold only — NO franken deps in this bead; that keeps it unblocked by license/decision gates).
- New workspace member crates/scriptbots-analytics: library + bin sb-analyze. Depends on scriptbots-storage (StorageReader / read-only open) + existing workspace deps only.
- Report framework: a Report trait (name, description, run(&ReaderCtx, &Params) -> ReportOutput), registry, and output sinks (human markdown, machine JSON with stable schema + schema_version field from day one). Per-stage tracing timings baked into the framework so every future report gets logging for free.
- CLI: sb-analyze <run.db> list | run <report> [--params k=v] [--json out.json] [--md out.md]. Read-only DB open with identity verification (reuse open_existing_with_expected_identity semantics, storage lib.rs:2496).
- First two zero-new-dep reports to prove the frame: run-summary (ticks, population trajectory stats via existing Welford-style math) and narrative-timeline dump (EventRecords ordered, honoring the FTS bead when present, plain scan otherwise).
- Cargo discipline: crate is a workspace member but NOT a dependency of scriptbots-app; cargo builds it only when asked (per-binary dep graphs) so default product build budgets are untouched. Assert via the wasm/build-budget guard bead.
- Migration path for control_cli Export: once sb-analyze covers its dataset kinds, control_cli's direct-DB Export should delegate or deprecate in favor of sb-analyze (coordinate with bd-2z0.8.9.5 — do not delete anything here; just record the successor path).
TESTS. Unit: report registry, param parsing, JSON schema snapshots, read-only enforcement (attempt a write -> typed error). Integration: run against a fixture DB checked in under testdata (small, generated by a seeded headless run, regeneration script included). Logging: per-report begin/end spans with row counts and durations; --verbose flows to tracing filter.
ACCEPTANCE. sb-analyze list/run works on a fixture DB; CI compiles + tests the crate; default-product build time measurably unchanged (record before/after).
DEPS. None hard (deliberately); related bd-2z0.11.3, bd-2z0.5.6, bd-16g.1.4, bd-2z0.8.9.5.

title: fsci-stats rigor layer: bootstrap CIs, permutation tests, distribution fits for detector validation
description:
WHY. The narrative detector kernel (crates/scriptbots-core/src/detect.rs: two-sided CUSUM :181, threshold :288, regime slope/autocorr :447, bimodality :603) is deliberately hand-rolled, bit-stable (f64::total_cmp), and ONLINE. What it lacks is statistical CERTIFICATION: is that detected regime change real or noise? What is the effect size CI? bd-16g.2.3 sets a false-positive budget and bd-16g.1.4 wants effect sizes with CIs over matched-seed runs — both need real statistics machinery. frankenscipy's fsci-stats is the strongest analytics fit in the whole franken family for us: Rust-native free functions over &[f64] (describe/percentile/histogram/zscore/iqr...), 95+ continuous distributions with pdf/cdf/ppf/fit, hypothesis tests (t/KS/Mann-Whitney/Wilcoxon/ANOVA), bootstrap, gaussian_kde, QMC; std::thread::scope parallelism explicitly work-gated so small-n inputs stay serial (their trait docs record parallel being 7-9x SLOWER at n~4096 — they gate correctly); #![forbid(unsafe_code)]; no tokio/rayon anywhere.

HARD BOUNDARY (do not cross): detect.rs stays hand-rolled, online, bit-stable in core. fsci NEVER enters scriptbots-core or any tick path. This bead is OFFLINE validation in scriptbots-analytics that ANNOTATES events after the fact.

INTEGRATION FACTS. Git-only dependency (NOT on crates.io) — pin exact rev per the bd-2z0.8 protocol; nightly-only (std::simd) — fine, workspace pins nightly-2026-07-09; all APIs are f64 (our f32 metric series widen at the boundary — cheap, offline).

SCOPE (reports in scriptbots-analytics, feature "fsci" if isolation proves useful).
1. narrative-validate report: for each persisted EventRecord, block-bootstrap CI (autocorrelation-aware) on the before/after delta of its metric window; permutation test against a stationary null; emit annotated JSON (event + p-value + CI + effect size) and a markdown table. This directly serves bd-16g.2.3's false-positive budget with a principled method instead of eyeballed thresholds.
2. distribution-report: population/energy/trait histograms with fitted candidate distributions (normal/lognormal/gamma where sensible), KS goodness-of-fit, bimodality cross-check against detect.rs's score (agreement rate logged — divergence is interesting, not an error).
3. matched-seed effect sizes for bd-16g.1.4: given two run DBs (control/treatment), paired effect sizes with bootstrap CIs per metric — the exact statistical core bd-16g.1.4 needs, exposed as a report it can call.
TESTS. Golden tests on synthetic series with KNOWN ground truth (injected step change of known size: CI must cover truth >=94% over 200 seeded replications — log the coverage number); permutation p-value calibration under pure-null series (uniformity check); f32->f64 widening roundtrip sanity; fixture-DB integration run. Every report logs sample sizes, method params (block length, n_resamples), and wall time.
ACCEPTANCE. narrative-validate + distribution-report + effect-size report run on fixture DBs in CI; coverage/calibration tests green; zero fsci symbols in any default-product or wasm build graph (guard bead enforces).
DEPS. Blocked by: analytics scaffold, bd-2z0.11.3 (the formal adapter decision this evidence feeds — implement behind it), license audit bead. Related: bd-16g.2.3, bd-16g.1.4.

ITEM 1 CERTIFICATION LOGIC LANDED (ffcfffd), bead still OPEN. crates/scriptbots-analytics/src/

CI + permutation p-value + Cohen's d + Cliff's delta, and — the part that makes it serve

deterministic.
