title: fnx lineage and interaction graph reports (components, communities, centrality)
description:
WHY. Evolution runs are GRAPHS: the ancestry DAG (who descends from whom) and interaction networks (who fights/feeds whom). bd-16g.3.1 builds the ancestry substrate (stable-UID edge list, append-only persistence, offline rebuild); bd-2z0.11.1 wants lineage fitness and founder contribution. franken_networkx gives us NetworkX-parity algorithms in Rust: connected/weakly-connected components, Louvain + label-propagation + greedy-modularity communities, full centrality suite (degree/closeness/betweenness/eigenvector/Katz/PageRank/HITS), Dijkstra/Bellman-Ford/A*, all with NetworkX-identical semantics (their conformance gate diffs against real NetworkX).

INTEGRATION FACTS (survey 2026-07-12, do not re-derive):
- CONSUME FROM CRATES.IO ONLY: fnx-classes = "0.2.0", fnx-algorithms = "0.2.0" (published 2026-06-21). The GIT repo is UNUSABLE as a dependency: fnx-runtime declares an optional dep with an absolute local path (/dp/frankentui) that breaks resolution on any machine without that path. crates.io releases strip path deps.
- Node keys are String (attrs BTreeMap) — integer agent UIDs must be formatted; budget one O(V) format pass per rebuild, fine offline.
- Bulk-build with extend_edges_unrecorded (reserves capacity, skips per-edge policy recording) — NEVER add_edge in a loop for full-graph builds.
- fnx-algorithms hard-depends on rayon: acceptable (analytics crate is native-only, never wasm).
- Their own cost model: break-even ~100 nodes; algorithms convert String labels to dense indices per call (one O(V) pass). Our graphs (1k-100k nodes, built once per report) are squarely in the win zone.

SCOPE (reports in scriptbots-analytics).
1. lineage-structure: from the bd-16g.3.1 ancestry store (or directly from births/deaths tables until it lands — births carry parent_a/parent_b, core lib.rs:1553): weakly-connected components = founder families; per-founder descendant counts, extinction depth, surviving-lineage table. Feeds bd-2z0.11.1's fitness math with the structural layer.
2. dynasty-communities: Louvain over the mating/ancestry graph (seeded, resolution param exposed) — candidate "species/dynasty" clusters to cross-check bd-16g.3.2's online speciation clustering (agreement rate logged, divergence is signal).
3. interaction-centrality: build per-epoch interaction graphs from combat/food-share events IF per-pair interaction data is persisted; TODAY the events table stores per-kind counts only (storage lib.rs V1 schema), so this report starts with what replay_events JSON provides and this bead documents exactly what extra persistence (pairwise interaction rows) would unlock — file a follow-up storage bead rather than silently widening scope here.
4. Graph exports: GraphML/edge-list dumps for external tooling.
TESTS. Golden: hand-built mini genealogy (3 founders, known components/communities) asserts exact fnx outputs; determinism: seeded Louvain stable across runs; scale smoke: 100k-edge synthetic DAG under time budget (log build/convert/algorithm timings separately — the String-key tax must be visible in logs). Fixture-DB integration in CI.
ACCEPTANCE. lineage-structure + dynasty-communities on fixture DB in CI; crates.io-only dependency proven in lock; timings logged; follow-up persistence gap documented (or bead filed) for pairwise interactions.
DEPS. Blocked by: analytics scaffold, bd-16g.3.1 (ancestry substrate), bd-2z0.11.3 (adapter decision), license audit. Related: bd-2z0.11.1.
acceptance_criteria: Build real run-scoped lineage and interaction graph reports through the approved fnx boundary: deterministic components, communities, centralities, typed stable-UID joins, bounded memory, and provenance. Unit/property tests cover empty/disconnected/multigraph/tie/slot-reuse cases; a seeded DB-backed E2E cross-checks graph counts and known invariants and retains query, node/edge, algorithm, timing, and truncation logs.

title: frankenpandas export and summary layer: Parquet/Arrow/CSV + groupby-rolling run summaries
description:
WHY. bd-2z0.5.6 defines provenance-rich Arrow/Parquet/CSV export CONTRACTS for run/agent/lineage/event/metric data. Something must implement the offline half for analysts, and hand-rolling Parquet writers + groupby/rolling summary math is exactly the wheel frankenpandas already built: DataFrame/Series with pandas-parity semantics, groupby (3 execution paths, measured 2.2-4.3x faster than pandas 2.2.3 at 100k-1M rows on accepted workloads), rolling/expanding/ewm/resample, joins incl. merge_asof, and fp-io with full CSV option matrix + Parquet/Arrow IPC/JSONL.

HONESTY CLAUSE (from their own artifacts, record and respect): their perf scorecard marks overall release readiness "PARTIAL / NOT FULLY VALIDATED" (high-CV rows rejected). We are consuming SEMANTICS (index alignment, NaN rules, format IO), not chasing their benchmarks. If a workload is slow, fsqlite SQL remains our query engine — the boundary is: FrankenSQLite = query engine, frankenpandas = interchange + summary-shaping layer. Never re-implement SQL-shaped queries as DataFrame pipelines.

INTEGRATION FACTS. crates.io: frankenpandas = "0.1.2" (umbrella with prelude) — or the leaner fp-frame + fp-groupby + fp-io if the umbrella's default features drag rusqlite (bundled C) — MEASURE and pick the minimal set; disable default sql-sqlite feature regardless (we have fsqlite; a second embedded SQLite in the tree is absurd). No tokio (explicit upstream policy). Native-only (analytics crate; never wasm).

SCOPE (in scriptbots-analytics).
1. sb-analyze export: read run DB -> write Parquet/Arrow/CSV per the bd-2z0.5.6 contract (schema_version + provenance columns: run identity digest, seed, config hash, exporter version). Column layouts defined WITH .5.6, not invented here — if .5.6's contract work has not started, this bead contributes the draft schema and .5.6 reviews/owns it.
2. sb-analyze summarize: per-epoch groupby aggregates (population by diet/brain-kind, trait means/stds), rolling-window smoothed metric series, per-lineage aggregates joined from births/deaths — emitted as small tidy DataFrames -> Parquet/CSV + markdown tables.
3. Round-trip verification mode: export then re-read, assert frame equality (this is our conformance net against fp-io bugs).
TESTS. Golden CSVs for tiny fixture DBs; Parquet round-trip equality incl. nulls/NaN policy (document the NaN convention explicitly — pandas semantics differ from naive expectations); dtype stability snapshots; large-ish smoke (1M metric rows) with stage timings logged; cross-check one summary against a plain SQL computation of the same aggregate (agreement = conformance evidence).
ACCEPTANCE. Export + summarize + round-trip green on fixture DB in CI; minimal feature set recorded in the bead on close (with cargo tree evidence); provenance columns match .5.6 contract; NaN/null policy documented in docs/analytics.
DEPS. Blocked by: analytics scaffold, bd-2z0.5.6 (contract), license audit. Related: bd-2z0.11.3, control_cli CSV export (supersedes it for offline use; control_cli keeps its REST-based export for live instances).
acceptance_criteria: Implement the approved frankenpandas export and summary layer over real run-scoped data: schema- and provenance-rich Arrow, Parquet, and CSV plus deterministic groupby/rolling summaries and bounded streaming. Test empty/null/extreme/multi-run/schema-evolution cases and cross-format identity; run a real seeded DB-to-artifact E2E with row counts, schemas, digests, timings, memory bounds, and failure diagnostics.

title: Analytics E2E: seeded run -> full report suite -> ground-truth invariant assertions
description:
WHY. Each analytics report has unit/golden tests, but the product promise is the PIPELINE: simulate -> persist -> analyze -> report, with numbers a scientist can trust. This bead is the end-to-end proof with ground truth planted where we control it.

SCOPE. scripts/e2e_analytics.sh (+ a small Rust driver where shell is too weak), VERBOSE logging at every stage, CI (extended/nightly lane — it is heavier than PR CI):
1. Run a seeded headless sim to T ticks with a scenario CHOSEN TO GUARANTEE structure: an injected mid-run food-scarcity step (via config schedule or intervention command once bd-16g.10.1 lands; until then pick a seed empirically exhibiting a population crash and pin it) => known regime-change ground truth window.
2. sb-analyze run-summary + narrative-timeline: assert the crash event exists in the window, human_text matches expectation.
3. narrative-validate (fsci): assert the planted change is flagged significant (p < 0.01) AND at least one pure-noise stretch is NOT flagged (false-positive control demonstrated in-pipeline).
4. lineage-structure (fnx): assert founder-component count == initial spawn cohorts; descendant counts sum to total births from the DB (exact accounting identity).
5. export (frankenpandas): Parquet round-trip equality; row counts match SQL counts exactly.
6. FTS surface: control_cli narrative search for the planted event returns it (ties the narrative-search e2e into the same artifact).
7. Emit a single MANIFEST.json artifact: every stage, duration, pass/fail, log paths — the CI artifact a human opens first.
FAILURE POLICY. Any stage failure fails the job loudly with the stage log inlined in CI output; flaky-seed drift (the pinned seed stops crashing after a legit sim-physics change) is handled by a documented re-pinning procedure IN the script header, not by silent tolerance widening.
ACCEPTANCE. Green in the extended CI lane 10 consecutive runs; MANIFEST.json artifact present; re-pinning procedure documented.
DEPS. Blocked by: fsci rigor bead, fnx graphs bead, frankenpandas export bead (and transitively the scaffold + FTS beads).
acceptance_criteria: A fail-closed E2E script runs a fixed seeded simulation into a nonempty real DB, invokes sb-analyze for the complete report suite, and asserts ground-truth cross-report invariants. It must reject Cargo/run/query/report failure, empty input, missing reports, placeholder success, schema drift, and corrupted data; retain verbose commands, exit codes, DB counts, report schemas/digests, invariant diffs, timings, and a machine-readable verdict.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
FALSE CLOSE BY GRAPH INVARIANT — reopened by the bd-d3wu epic sweep (cc_3). No per-bead judgment was involved: this is a mechanical query over parent-child edges in .beads/issues.jsonl.

RULE APPLIED: a parent whose deliverable is child completion cannot be complete while any descendant is open. Closed parent + open descendant is therefore a false close BY CONSTRUCTION.

OPEN/IN_PROGRESS DESCENDANTS OF THIS BEAD: bd-2z0.12.3

METHOD (reproducible in seconds, and worth wiring as a tracker guard): parse .beads/issues.jsonl, build the parent->child map from dependencies where type == 'parent-child', take the transitive descendant closure of every closed parent, and report any with a descendant whose status is open or in_progress. The full sweep found 7 such parents across the tracker; this is one of them.

WHY THE SWEEP WAS NEEDED AT ALL: reopens do not propagate upward. When cod_3's rendering audit reopened bd-2z0.14.3.4 and bd-2z0.14.3.5 on 2026-07-24, and when this audit reopened bd-2z0.5.9 and bd-2z0.14.3.5.3, no ancestor was touched. The graph then silently asserted that closed epics were complete while their own work was open — the same class of untrue status the bd-d3wu audit exists to find, arrived at by omission rather than by a bad close.

TWO OF THE SEVEN ARE THIS AUDIT'S OWN FAULT: bd-2z0.5 and bd-2z0 became inconsistent because I reopened their descendants without propagating. Recording that plainly, since an audit that creates the defect class it documents should say so.

TO CLOSE THIS AGAIN: close every descendant listed above first, then enumerate the child IDs in the close reason so the claim is checkable rather than a summary. 'All sub-epics closed' is exactly the assertion that failed here.

title: Evaluate asupersync BrowserRuntime (deterministic profile) for scriptbots-web
description:
CONTEXT. scriptbots-web is a minimal wasm build (core+brain only, default-features=false so no rayon/wide; JS drives stepping over Rc<RefCell<WorldState>>; snapshots via serde-wasm-bindgen JSON or postcard — crates/scriptbots-web/src/lib.rs:132-560). asupersync is the ONLY franken library with real wasm32 support: target_arch=wasm32 requires exactly one browser profile feature (wasm-browser-minimal|dev|prod|deterministic); native Runtime::build errors on wasm and routes to BrowserRuntime with a BrowserReactor; sibling crates asupersync-browser-core (canonical wasm-bindgen boundary) and a live wasm demo exist. The wasm-browser-deterministic profile keeps replay-safe semantics IN THE BROWSER.

WHY IT COULD MATTER. (a) Deterministic browser scheduling aligns with fork-this-world/replay ambitions (bd-16g.8.2 needs honest determinism claims in the browser); (b) a structured runtime replaces ad-hoc JS-driven stepping with budgeted ticks + cancellable background work if the web build grows (workers, streaming snapshots); (c) it would UNIFY the concurrency model native/web instead of maintaining two idioms.

SCOPE (evaluation, not adoption).
- Spike: drive the existing WasmSim stepping through BrowserRuntime with the deterministic profile in a branch; measure bundle-size delta, startup cost, tick-pacing fidelity vs the current rAF/JS loop; confirm the profile's determinism claims hold for our stepping pattern (seeded run digest equality across two browser sessions).
- Map which spine conventions (watch snapshot bus, shutdown watch) could share code between native and web via feature gates.
- DECISION RULE: adopt only if bundle-size cost <= ~15% and determinism digests hold; otherwise document and close rejected. Either way, record findings for the PLAN_TO_CREATE_SIBLING_APP_CRATE_TARGETING_WASM.md successor work.
TESTS if adopted: browser-side digest-equality e2e (two sessions, same seed, equal digests) wired into the wasm CI lane with console-capture logging.
DEPS. Blocked by the channel-spine bead (conventions to share); related bd-16g.8.2.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A disposable HostCore-under-BrowserRuntime spike uses exactly the wasm-browser-deterministic profile and the same typed command, snapshot, pacing, cancellation, and shutdown seams identified in the mapping; no measurement is taken against the retired direct-WorldState architecture. 2. A pinned DSR profile on clean expected-commit source records reproducible current-versus-spike wasm bundle bytes, startup distribution, rAF/tick pacing and missed-deadline behavior, memory/task counts, and two independent browser-session science digests with raw logs/artifacts. 3. The decision applies the predeclared bundle delta threshold of at most 15 percent and requires digest equality; startup/pacing tradeoffs and shared-spine value are reported without moving thresholds after results. 4. A committed decision artifact names exact source, toolchain/browser, profile, measurements, limitations, and adopt/reject rationale. Reject leaves production lean and records what would trigger reevaluation; adopt files/links implementation work rather than silently shipping the spike. 5. Negative-control browser tests prove digest/pacing instrumentation can detect an injected divergence, and all logs name session/seed/tick/deadline/profile while avoiding ambient network/clock claims. 6. No direct Cargo performance run or unpinned proof is accepted; the DSR typed verdict and retained evidence are the gate.

title: scriptbots-brain re-enables core default features, leaking rayon/wide into the wasm graph
description:
FOUND BY. ci/check_wasm_graph.sh (bd-2z0.8.16) during its first real snapshot generation, 2026-07-13 — before the guard was even wired into CI. Denied crates rayon, rayon-core, and wide resolve into the wasm32-unknown-unknown dependency graph of scriptbots-web.

ROOT CAUSE (manifest evidence):
- crates/scriptbots-web/Cargo.toml:18 declares scriptbots-core with default-features = false — correct per the wasm strategy (core's `parallel` [rayon] and `simd_wide` [wide] are default features that must stay OFF for wasm; configure_parallelism is a documented no-op on wasm, core lib.rs:177-180).
- crates/scriptbots-web/Cargo.toml:19 also depends on scriptbots-brain (default-features=false, features=["mlp"]).
- crates/scriptbots-brain/Cargo.toml:16 declares `scriptbots-core = { path = "../scriptbots-core" }` — WITH default features. Cargo feature unification is additive across the closure, so web -> brain -> core re-enables parallel + simd_wide for the wasm build, defeating web's own default-features=false.

CONSEQUENCES. (a) The shipped wasm artifact carries rayon/rayon-core/wide; (b) worse than bloat: with `parallel`/`simd_wide` ON, core compiles its rayon/f32x4 code paths for wasm instead of the scalar paths — contradicting the recorded intent that "cfg(not(simd_wide)) scalar paths DO ship in wasm and must stay semantically identical" (the scalar/SIMD parity assumption the wasm story rests on). Any scalar-vs-SIMD divergence is currently INVISIBLE in wasm because the SIMD paths are what actually ships.

FIX (one line + verification): crates/scriptbots-brain/Cargo.toml core dep -> `default-features = false`. Native products are unaffected (scriptbots-app/render/bevy depend on core directly with defaults, and unification re-enables parallel+simd for those builds). Wasm closure becomes clean.
VERIFICATION REQUIRED (not optional — this changes what wasm compiles):
1. cargo check -p scriptbots-brain (does brain itself reference anything gated behind core's default features? grep suggests no — brain consumes core types/traits only — but prove it by compiler).
2. Full workspace build + tests (native digests must be BYTE-IDENTICAL — features for native builds are unchanged by unification; assert via the digest harness).
3. wasm CI lane (wasm-pack build + headless parity tests): wasm digests MAY move if scalar and SIMD paths ever diverged — if they do move, that is a REAL latent scalar/SIMD divergence surfaced, file it against core immediately (parity is test-asserted per the wasm audit docs; divergence = bug, not noise).
4. Measure wasm bundle size before/after (expect shrink; record numbers here).
5. Re-run `bash ci/check_wasm_graph.sh --update-snapshot` — rayon/rayon-core/wide must vanish; then wire the guard's CI step (bd-2z0.8.16 completes on top of this fix).
6. Audit the remaining workspace manifests for the same pattern while in here: any member that depends on core WITHOUT default-features=false AND sits in a wasm-reachable closure (brain-ml? brain-neuro? check all `scriptbots-core = { path` declarations).
LOGGING. Verification steps must capture cargo tree before/after under ci/fixtures-adjacent evidence or the bead comment; the wasm-size delta and digest outcomes recorded here on close.
DEPS. Blocks bd-2z0.8.16's snapshot+CI wiring (the golden file must not bless a denied graph). Related bd-2z0.12 (web epic), bd-2z0.8.16.
close_reason: brain's core dep -> default-features=false; 9 crates (rayon/rayon-core/crossbeam*/either/wide/safe_arch/bytemuck) left the wasm graph (63->54); brain checks clean without core defaults; native digests byte-identical; wasm-graph guard snapshot regenerated and passing

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text:
EVIDENCE (bead required these recorded here).

(1) brain without core defaults: cargo check -p scriptbots-brain CLEAN. Brain consumes core types/traits only; it never referenced anything gated behind parallel/simd_wide. Proven by compiler, not by grep.

(2) Native unaffected: workspace check 0 errors, and NATIVE DIGESTS ARE BYTE-IDENTICAL — 165 core + 79 app + 35 integration + the pinned characterization traces all pass unchanged. app/render/bevy depend on core directly WITH defaults, so unification re-enables parallel+simd for native builds by construction.

(3) WASM GRAPH DELTA, 63 -> 54 crates. Removed: rayon, rayon-core, crossbeam-deque, crossbeam-epoch, crossbeam-utils, either, wide, safe_arch, bytemuck.

(4) ci/check_wasm_graph.sh: the snapshot had BLESSED THE LEAKED GRAPH (it was generated while the leak was present). Regenerated to 54 crates; guard now reports 'snapshot OK' and 'core default graph clean' (its reverse boundary check).

(5) MANIFEST AUDIT (bead step 6 — the same pattern elsewhere): every scriptbots-core declaration was checked. brain-ml, brain-neuro, storage, app, render, bevy, world-gfx all declare core WITH defaults, which is CORRECT for them — none is in a wasm-reachable closure. web and analytics already used default-features=false. brain's 'mlp'/'dwraon' features are pure flags that pull no crates, so brain-ml/brain-neuro stay out of the wasm closure. brain was the only leak.

(6) NOT DONE, and deliberately: wasm bundle-size measurement and the headless wasm parity run. Those need a wasm toolchain (wasm-pack) that this build environment does not have. The graph is proven clean by cargo tree + the guard; the SIZE delta and the wasm digest outcome should be captured by whoever runs the wasm CI lane. Note the bead's own warning: if wasm digests MOVE once the scalar paths actually ship, that is a REAL latent scalar/SIMD divergence surfaced, not noise — file it against core immediately.

title: Bundle THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES (incl. franken rider) in release artifacts + README license disclosure
description:
WHY (obligation discovered by the bd-2z0.8.15 audit — see docs/licenses.md §3c). Every franken component carries the MIT+OpenAI/Anthropic-rider license, and the rider states "any distribution of the Software or any Derivative Works must include this rider provision unmodified." Our release pipeline (workspace.metadata.dist -> scriptbots-app binaries, release.yml) statically links fsqlite + asupersync + franken-kernel — the binaries are combined works containing rider-licensed object code, so release artifacts MUST ship the rider text. Separately, third-party redistributors of our binaries are bound by the rider for the embedded components (including the prohibition on making them available to OpenAI/Anthropic and affiliates) — the README license section must disclose this so redistribution is informed rather than accidental non-compliance.

SCOPE.
1. Generate THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md at release-build time (or maintain checked-in): first-party MIT/Apache texts + the full unmodified rider text for the franken family (canonical sha in docs/licenses.md §1) + standard third-party notices. Prefer generation from Cargo.lock metadata (cargo-about or a small script consistent with ci/check_franken_licenses.sh family detection) so new deps cannot be silently omitted; if generation is too heavy, a checked-in file + a CI staleness check against the lock's franken set is acceptable — record which.
2. Wire into release.yml so every artifact (tar/zip per platform) contains the file; verify by extracting an artifact in CI and asserting the rider sha256 text block is present (log the check verbosely).
3. README "License" section update: first-party MIT OR Apache-2.0; bundled franken components under LicenseRef-MIT-OpenAI-Anthropic-Rider with the two practical consequences (no rights to Restricted Parties; redistributors carry the rider). Keep it to one short, factual paragraph linking docs/licenses.md.
TESTS. CI assertion in release workflow (artifact extraction + rider-presence check with sha comparison against docs/licenses.md §1); README link check; staleness check if the checked-in variant is chosen.
ACCEPTANCE. A release artifact demonstrably contains the rider text; README discloses; docs/licenses.md §3c marked satisfied.
DEPS. Related: bd-2z0.8.15 (source of the obligation), bd-2z0.13.1 (README rewrite — coordinate wording), bd-2js6.

title: Cinematic Evolution: 100x graphics overhaul (3D game-grade Bevy + FrankenTUI excellence)
description:
Root program epic for the user-directed radical graphics overhaul: make rust_scriptbots look like an amazing 3D computer game instead of the current primitive 2D presentation, in Rust, cross-platform (Metal/Vulkan/D3D12 via wgpu through Bevy 0.17), GPU-leveraged, plus a FrankenTUI-powered console mode that is as beautiful as a terminal can be.

BACKGROUND (why this epic exists): The current visuals are: (1) GPUI 2D immediate-mode quads/paths on a CPU canvas (crates/scriptbots-render, 14k-line monolith) whose optional wgpu path does a GPU->CPU->GPU roundtrip with per-pixel quad reconstruction; (2) a Bevy 3D scene with real HDR/PBR/shadows that catastrophically spawns ~15 entities + ~15 unique StandardMaterials PER AGENT and illegally drives the simulation itself; (3) a Ratatui TUI rendering 1 char per map cell with hand-rolled bars and no mouse. None of this resembles a modern game.

RELATIONSHIP TO EXISTING BEADS (do not duplicate): The recovery plan already mandates the renderer strategy (plan 5.8): Bevy = primary native GUI, FrankenTUI = terminal, GPUI = one time-boxed direct-texture spike (bd-2z0.7.7) then likely retirement, custom wgpu (scriptbots-world-gfx) = offscreen/capture lane. Migration/correctness beads already exist: bd-2z0.7.2 (presentation-only Bevy), bd-2z0.7.3 (instancing basics), bd-2z0.7.4 (terrain layers), bd-2z0.7.5 (camera/picking), bd-2z0.7.6 (HUD), bd-2z0.7.7 (GPUI spike), bd-2z0.7.8 (GUI proof), bd-2z0.6.1-6.7 (FrankenTUI migration). THIS EPIC LAYERS THE VISUAL-QUALITY PROGRAM ON TOP: every leaf bead names its exact upstream dependency instead of re-doing migration work. GPUI receives ZERO new investment beyond bd-2z0.7.7's decision (plan 16 risk register caps GPUI spend).

ART DIRECTION (the '100x' target, 'Cinematic Evolution'): default 3/4 cinematic camera over a PBR splat-mapped heightfield world; animated hydrology water with shore foam; cascaded-shadow sun with a real day/night cycle and night sky; genome-driven 3D critters (ScriptBots capsule+wheels+spike silhouette preserved) with emissive diet stripes, damage/age cues, and procedural animation; GPU particles for births/deaths/combat/eating/boost; HDR bloom/tonemap/FXAA-TAA/SSAO/vignette post stack with quality tiers (Potato/Low/Medium/High/Ultra); game-grade HUD. Terminal mode: braille 2x4 sub-cell truecolor world canvas, curated themes + Ctrl+T, ftui charts with axes, animations, mouse, command palette.

HARD CONSTRAINTS: (a) NO FEATURE LOSS - every current feature (colorblind palettes x5, keyboard remapping, emoji/narrow/ascii vocabularies, headless FNV evidence contract, ASCII screenshot, REST/MCP/CLI control surface, inspector brain views, settings search, playback scrubbing, audio toggles, SB_WGPU_* env knobs) is either preserved or explicitly mapped forward in a bead's Preservation section; (b) renderers NEVER own scientific time (HostCore migration bd-2z0.4.9 chain governs); (c) UI paint paths never issue SQL (Arc<AnalyticsSnapshot> only); (d) no new third-party dependencies without the serialized dependency lane (bd-2z0.8) - design assumes STOCK Bevy 0.17 + hand-rolled WGSL only; (e) every bead ships unit tests + e2e evidence with structured tracing; (f) perf budgets and DSR-only acceptance for perf claims per AGENTS.md.

STRUCTURE: sub-epic A = Bevy cinematic 3D renderer; sub-epic B = FrankenTUI visual excellence; sub-epic C = shared visual foundations, evidence harness, and gates. Acceptance for the EPIC itself: on a tier-High reference GPU the Bevy frontend renders a 1k-agent world at 60fps and 10k at 30fps with the full Medium+ visual stack, goldens prove the live render path, the TUI renders the braille canvas with themes at 10+fps, and every preservation-ledger item is checked off in the final docs bead.

EXPLICIT NON-GOALS (2026-07-17 self-review): (1) GPUI renderer receives zero new investment beyond the bd-2z0.7.7 spike verdict (plan 5.8/16); (2) a full web/browser renderer overhaul is OUT of scope - scriptbots-web keeps its current JS canvas; C7 evaluates a WebGPU path as P3 exploration only; (3) no new third-party rendering dependencies (no bevy_egui, no hanabi, no assets packs) without the bd-2z0.8 serialized lane; (4) VR/XR; (5) ray tracing (raster-only, cross-platform baseline first). title: Instanced creature render pipeline: render-world Extract/Prepare/Queue, per-instance genome visuals, culling, LOD
description:
BACKGROUND: bd-2z0.7.3 ('Replace per-agent Bevy entities/materials with GPU instancing') fixes the CORRECTNESS/CATASTROPHE level: ~15 child entities + ~15 unique StandardMaterials per agent, ~230k entities at 10k agents, unbounded snapshot clones. This bead (A1) builds the VISUAL-GRADE instanced pipeline on top of that fix: a custom Bevy render-world path that treats creatures as first-class instanced geometry with per-instance genome-driven appearance - the foundation every other A-bead hangs on. The prior art exists: scriptbots-world-gfx already runs instanced terrain tiles + instanced agent sprites with dynamic instance-buffer regrowth and CPU frustum culling (2D); this is the 3D PBR successor inside Bevy's render graph.

SCOPE: (1) CreatureInstancePod: bytemuck Pod instance struct (position+heading packed, body scale/proportions, primary+stripe color, emissive intensity, spike extension, wheel spin phase, damage/age factors, selection/hover flags, LOD tier) written per frame from RenderSnapshot via Extract into a grow-only GPU buffer - zero per-frame allocation on the hot path. (2) Custom MeshMaterialPipeline (or SpecializedRenderPipeline over Bevy 0.17's instancing-friendly path): one draw per (mesh, material-group, LOD tier) for the whole population; WGSL reads instance data, applies genome proportions non-uniformly, computes per-instance lighting inputs. (3) Frustum culling per instance (sphere test in WGSL-companion compute or CPU with the spatial index) + distance-based LOD tiers (full critter mesh / simplified / impostor billboard) with hysteresis to prevent popping; LOD transitions crossfade via shader dissolve. (4) Selection/hover/decal ring as a separate instanced overlay pass (no per-agent entities). (5) Shadow pass inclusion: instanced creatures cast into the cascade maps (A4) with per-LOD shadow variants. (6) Kill-switch env/setting back to entity path for debugging (documented, off by default, removed when C6 ledger lands). (7) Toroidal wrap: instances near world edges render ghost copies across the seam (max 2x instance write for wrapped agents, bounded by border margin) so the world reads continuous - matches the simulation's toroidal topology.

CONTRACTS: consumes C2 AgentVisualParams (single semantics); respects C1 quality tiers (LOD distances, shadow casting, max instances); emits per-subsystem timings for C5.3; presentation-only (bd-2z0.7.2) - ZERO simulation control.

ACCEPTANCE: 10k agents render as <= ~12 draw calls for creatures (excluding shadow pass) vs today's thousands; frame captures (C4) show identical-or-better agent visuals vs entity path; unit tests for instance packing/culling/LOD selection; perf harness (C5.3) proves creature pass p95 within budget at Medium/High. LOGGING: debug! per-frame counts at trace level; info! on pipeline (re)creation + LOD tier table at startup; warn! on instance-buffer growth beyond expected cap.
acceptance_criteria: The default production renderer uses a real Bevy render-world Extract/Prepare/Queue path with a bytemuck Pod CreatureInstancePod and grow-only GPU buffers; a source guard and a nonvacuous live assertion prove that the default path no longer spawns per-agent root/child mesh entities or unique materials. Instance packing covers stable UID, transforms, genome visual parameters, animation inputs, damage/age and selection flags, and LOD tier. Unit tests cover byte layout/alignment, packing, buffer regrowth without shrink/reallocation, culling boundaries, LOD thresholds and hysteresis, toroidal ghost copies, material/draw grouping, selection overlays, and shadow variants. A mock-free offscreen Bevy E2E script renders nonempty 1k and 10k deterministic populations, records instance/entity/draw counts, buffer capacities, LOD/culling counts, frame hashes, adapter/device identity, and source commit, compares the default path with the bounded debug fallback, and contains an injected missing/changed-instance negative control that must fail the expected frame/count assertion. Quality-tier and feature semantics remain intact. GPU frame-budget claims are accepted only from the separate exact-class DSR performance lane; unit/static/offscreen evidence must not claim them.

title: Spatial audio + adaptive soundscape integration (kira/bevy audio; consumes bd-16g.14 seam)
description:
BACKGROUND: Audio today: optional kira feature in scriptbots-render (GPUI) with generated sine cues for birth/death/spike/toggle. bd-16g.14 (P3) owns the snapshot-driven sonification program (aggregation, rate limiting, gain staging, no world-lock access) and bd-16g.14.2 a deterministic offline soundtrack for reels. This bead wires the BEVY frontend to that seam - it does NOT duplicate the sonification engine.

SCOPE: (1) Port the event-cue surface from GPUI's kira integration to the Bevy frontend behind the bd-16g.14.1 snapshot-driven contract (cues derived from AnalyticsSnapshot/event deltas, never from world locks): births, deaths-by-cause, combat hits, eat, boost, UI actions - each with distinct, non-fatiguing procedural sounds. (2) Spatialization: listener at camera, cues positioned at world events (distance attenuation + pan), capped concurrent voices with priority (combat > death > birth > ambient). (3) Adaptive soundscape: ambient bed per biome mix (water shimmer near coasts, wind at altitude, night crickets after dusk per A4 phase) + population-density-driven intensity; all generated (no asset downloads) unless the user drops files in a documented directory (optional, off by default). (4) Accessibility + respect: master/music/sfx gains, mute toggle, audio-off default honored on first run per platform norms, kira feature-gate preserved (audio stays an optional compile feature). (5) Deterministic offline render integration: reel export (bd-16g.9/14.2) can request the exact cue timeline; no wall-clock scheduling in cue generation.

ACCEPTANCE: unit tests for cue mapping + voice cap + gain staging; e2e headless run logs the cue timeline (JSON) matching event stream; feature-gated build without audio compiles clean (no-default lane, bd-2z0.7.10 contract); C6 ledger records the GPUI audio feature's new home. Deps: A7 (shared event cue timing), bd-16g.14.1 (engine seam). LOGGING: info! audio device/init + voice stats on change; debug! cue dispatch.
acceptance_criteria: Bevy consumes the completed bd-16g.14.3 live seam without WorldState locks or duplicating its mapper. Unit tests cover every cue kind, spatial attenuation/pan, listener-camera transforms across toroidal seams, priority/voice caps, gains/mute, deterministic timeline identity, and feature-off behavior. A headless e2e script drives a seeded event stream, records verbose JSON cue/device/voice/drop diagnostics, and proves the cue timeline matches the source events and offline reel timeline. Live tests cover camera movement, device-init failure, overload, background mute, and first-run audio-off defaults. The no-audio feature lane contains no Kira/device code; the C6 dependency ledger and user-facing audio controls identify the new owner.

title: Performance budgets + scaling proof: 60fps@1k / 30fps@10k at Medium on reference GPU, memory budgets, DSR evidence
description:
BACKGROUND: 'Looks amazing' only counts if it RUNS. The repo perf philosophy (AGENTS.md): perf claims are DSR-only evidence; local runs advisory; exact-class machine comparisons; CV noise gates. This bead is the A-side performance close-out.

SCOPE: (1) Budgets (Medium tier, tier-High reference GPU class): 1k agents >= 60fps sustained (p95 frame <= 16.6ms), 10k agents >= 30fps (p95 <= 33.3ms), 5k >= 45fps; Potato tier: 10k @ 60fps on integrated-class. Startup-to-first-frame <= 3s warm. (2) Memory: GPU resident (buffers+textures) <= documented per-tier caps; RSS growth ~0 over 30-min soak (C5). (3) Scaling curve artifact: fps vs agent count (1k/2.5k/5k/10k/25k-spike) per tier with per-subsystem breakdown (C5.3 harness) - published in docs/cinematic_evolution.md (C6). (5) Bottleneck-driven optimizations landed HERE (not scattered): batch geometry uploads, texture array atlasing, shadow cascade tuning, particle overdraw reduction - each with before/after numbers in the bead notes. (6) Honest degradation: if a reference machine misses budgets, C3 governor behavior is the documented answer, and the bead records it rather than moving goalposts.

WHAT SHIPPED (crates/scriptbots-bevy/src/lib.rs):

DESIGN POINTS THAT MATTER:
  - The HUD_EVENT_FEED_CAPACITY=6 bound is applied DURING derivation via early return, not by truncating afterwards, so a births/deaths storm never builds a large vector first. Test feed_is_bounded_under_a_storm drives 500 ticks x 9/9/9 and asserts both the length and that the newest tick survives.

Presentation-only: derived from a read-only snapshot, no new dependency, no world mutation, nothing feeding back into simulation state, so determinism digests are unaffected.

title: bevy HUD: brain activation visualization overlay (claimed by bd-2z0.14.1.10, never implemented)
description:
Split out of bd-z1xy (false-close correction). bd-2z0.14.1.10's close reason claimed 'brain-viz overlays' shipped in scriptbots-bevy; they do not exist.

EVIDENCE (crates/scriptbots-bevy/src/, verified 2026-07-26 by HazyCrane): zero matches for brain_viz, and no brain activation rendering of any kind in the crate.

SCOPE: render the selected agent's brain activations in the bevy_ui HUD - layer/node activations and, where the family exposes them, edge weights. This must go through the EXISTING read-only brain introspection projection described in README.md, not a new per-tick side channel: a revisioned request for up to eight stable AgentUid values, with core and each brain family enforcing independent bounds on layers, names, values, edges, source scalars, and retained payload. Responses already carry the exact source tick and typed unavailable/clipped status; cache by client, stable identity, and source tick exactly as TUI and GPUI do.

CRITICAL CONSTRAINT: with no request outstanding, no brain may be inspected - the existing contract guarantees digest-neutrality and next-output purity, and a Bevy overlay must not become the thing that breaks it. NeuroFlow in particular must perform no inspection JSON serialization when unrequested.

ACCEPTANCE: enabling the overlay leaves WorldDigestV1 unchanged across a seeded run; the overlay renders correct activations for the supported families; typed unavailable/clipped status is displayed rather than silently blanked.
close_reason:
Implemented by HazyCrane in 2d137a671. Split out of bd-z1xy, where bd-2z0.14.1.10's close reason claimed 'brain-viz overlays' shipped in scriptbots-bevy. Zero matches for brain_viz; no brain activation rendering of any kind existed.

THE CONSTRAINT THAT SHAPED THE DESIGN (this is the whole bead). Core guarantees that with no outstanding request, no brain is inspected - that is what makes introspection digest-neutral, and the checkpoint/digest contract depends on it. So BrainOverlay::capture returns NotRequested BEFORE ever touching inspect_brains. An overlay that polled every frame regardless of selection would silently convert a read-only projection into a per-tick side effect.

WHERE THE STATE LIVES. The request needs a client-owned MONOTONIC revision, and WorldSnapshot::from_world is a pure fn(&WorldState) -> Option<Self> with six call sites and nowhere to hold one. Rather than change that signature at every site, the capture runs in the snapshot worker (which already owned a next_revision counter for presentation revisions) and does so INSIDE the existing world lock, so activations and the rest of the snapshot describe one world state rather than two. from_world leaves brain default with a comment explaining why.

IDENTITY BRIDGE. inspect_brains is keyed by AgentUid (stable scientific identity); the Bevy snapshot carries AgentId (generational handle). WorldState::agent_uid bridges them. A selected agent that no longer resolves gets its own NoStableIdentity status rather than being silently rendered as an empty brain.

BOUNDED TWICE, AND HONEST ABOUT IT. Core bounds its payload (ACTIVATION_VALUE_BUDGET etc.); this projection bounds again for presentation (BRAIN_OVERLAY_MAX_LAYERS=4 x BRAIN_OVERLAY_MAX_VALUES=12) and propagates  from EITHER source. Each layer renders [shown/total] and a clipped panel says '(clipped)'. Core makes exactly this argument in its own docs on BrainActivations: silently dropping layers lets a reader conclude a brain has no deep structure when in fact we simply refused to copy it.

SIGNED SCALING. Activations are signed, so format_sparkline_signed scales by peak ABSOLUTE magnitude - a mostly-negative layer stays legible instead of collapsing onto the floor. This is deliberately a different function from the unsigned population sparkline in bd-2z0.14.1.16.

SIX TESTS: no-selection yields NotRequested and the placeholder; revision untouched when nothing is selected (the digest-neutrality guarantee as an assertion, not a comment); clipping announced in both directions; per-layer shown/total and source tick; typed refusals and missing identity surfaced rather than blanked; signed scaling incl. the all-zero and empty-slice cases.

VERIFICATION:
  rch exec -- cargo test -p scriptbots-bevy --lib hud_             -> 26 passed, 0 failed (6 brain + 6 sparkline + 7 inspector + 6 event-feed + pre-existing hud_overlay_populates_metrics)
  rustfmt --edition 2024 --check crates/scriptbots-bevy/src/lib.rs -> exit 0
  ubs                                                              -> critical unchanged 8 -> 8; intersecting flagged lines with the exact 339 lines added yields ZERO. Exit 1 is pre-existing for this file at HEAD.
  Clippy is red at baseline from pre-existing missing_docs in scriptbots-core, so per the operator's gate I confirmed only that no NEW diagnostic touches my changed lines: no diagnostic in the build output pointed at scriptbots-bevy at all.

NOT CLAIMED: there is no interactive open/close toggle for the overlay - it follows the primary selection, which is what bounds the request. A dedicated toggle, edge/connection rendering, and multi-target inspection (core supports up to eight) remain unimplemented and are NOT claimed here.

This is the FOURTH of five sub-features split out of the bd-2z0.14.1.10 false close. Remaining: bd-2z0.14.1.17, re-scoped from 'add a quality toggle' to 'the resolved quality tier is inert', blocked on bd-2z0.14.1.4 and bd-ikts.1.

comments.text:
CORRECTION to the close reason above: one word was eaten by the shell. The BOUNDED TWICE paragraph reads "...and propagates  from EITHER source"; it should read "...and propagates the truncated flag from EITHER source" - i.e. the projection sets truncated when core reports its own payload was clipped, AND when this presentation layer clips further (more than BRAIN_OVERLAY_MAX_LAYERS layers, or more than BRAIN_OVERLAY_MAX_VALUES values in any layer). Both paths are covered by the clipped_payload_is_announced test.

Cause: I wrapped the field name in backticks inside a double-quoted zsh string, so it was treated as command substitution (zsh reported "command not found: truncated"). No other content was affected - the corruption is confined to that single word, and the committed code and tests are unaffected. Noting the mechanism because any agent writing a close reason containing backticks in a double-quoted shell string will hit the same thing; use single quotes or drop the backticks.

title: bevy: the resolved quality tier is INERT — EffectiveRenderSettings is inserted but no live system reads it
description:
RE-SCOPED 2026-07-26 by HazyCrane after investigation. I filed this bead as 'quality tier is startup-only, add a runtime quick-toggle'. That framing was WRONG and I am correcting it before anyone builds on it: adding a toggle would be theater, because there is nothing downstream to re-apply.

WHAT I ACTUALLY FOUND (crates/scriptbots-bevy, verified 2026-07-26):

  1. The tier IS resolved and IS installed. resolve_effective_render_settings at lib.rs:371 produces EffectiveRenderSettings { tier, features, gpu }, and lib.rs:486 inserts it as a Bevy Resource. (My original filing said it was never inserted; that was wrong - the insert uses the snake_case variable so it does not match a type-name grep.)

  2. NO LIVE SYSTEM READS IT. Zero occurrences of Res<EffectiveRenderSettings> or ResMut<EffectiveRenderSettings> anywhere in crates/. The only references to the type in the whole workspace are its definition (lib.rs:249), its two constructors (303/311), its construction site (347), and one field on a capture struct (capture.rs:523, the offscreen path). Nothing in the running app queries it.

  3. TierFeatures is a fully populated matrix that nothing consumes. scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs:10323 defines shadows, shadow_resolution, shadow_cascades, bloom, ssao, anti_aliasing, fog, particles_max, terrain_detail_divisor, water_reflections, tui_subcell, tui_animation. In scriptbots-bevy, tier_features() is called exactly once - inside the resolver at lib.rs:320 - and the result is then read by no one. (scriptbots-render/src/lib.rs:13081 does consume it; that is GPUI, not Bevy.)

NET EFFECT: in the live Bevy app the quality tier changes exactly one thing - the text of the startup 'GPU capability report' INFO line. Potato and Ultra render identically. --quality is accepted, validated, resolved against a GPU probe, logged, stored... and ignored.

This is the same failure bd-ikts names as its ROOT CAUSE - renderer-neutral visual semantics computed and then bypassed - showing up a second time, one layer up, in the tier matrix rather than in visual.rs.

WHY THERE IS NO SMALL FIX: essentially every TierFeatures field is owned by another bead - shadows/ssao/fog by bd-2z0.14.1.4, bloom/anti_aliasing by bd-2z0.14.1.6, terrain_detail_divisor by the terrain lane, particles_max by the particles lane, tui_* by the terminal lane. So the wiring is inherently cross-cutting and must not be smuggled in under a 'add a button' bead.

CORRECT SCOPE NOW: make the resolved tier actually drive the live app. Each consuming system takes Res<EffectiveRenderSettings> and configures itself from .features, and changing the tier at runtime re-applies them. Unassigning myself - this belongs with whoever lands bd-2z0.14.1.4 / bd-2z0.14.1.6, since they own the fields.

Implemented by HazyCrane in aafade3d0. This is the FIFTH and final sub-feature split out of the bd-2z0.14.1.10 false close, so that arc is now complete.

THE DEFECT, restated: the quality tier was probed against a real GPU, logged, inserted as a Bevy resource, and read by nobody. Potato and Ultra rendered identically. --quality was parsed, validated, GPU-probed, resolved, logged, stored and ignored.

WHAT SHIPPED:
  - setup_scene takes Res<EffectiveRenderSettings> and the sun light takes shadows_enabled from effective.features.shadows instead of a hardcoded true. First live reader of the tier in the app.
  - apply_tier_to_sun_light re-applies on resource change, so the tier is no longer startup-only. Without it a runtime toggle is a label, not a control.
  - A Quality button cycling the concrete tiers, deliberately never yielding Auto. Auto is a REQUEST meaning resolve-against-the-probed-adapter; cycling into it would mean re-probing the GPU from an input handler. Auto is accepted as input and resolves to the low end so a click always moves.

A BEVY LIMIT WORTH RECORDING: the two new systems pushed the Update tuple to 21 and Bevy caps system tuples at 20. The compiler error names neither arity nor the limit - it says .chain() exists for a 21-element tuple but its trait bounds are not satisfied, which reads like a trait problem on the systems. Fixed by nesting the pair with an inner .chain(). That inner chain is load-bearing: the button must run before the system that applies its effect or a tier change lags a frame. Splitting into a second add_systems call would have compiled and silently dropped ordering against the other 19 systems.

THREE TESTS. the_resolved_tier_has_a_live_reader asserts against production source that a Res<EffectiveRenderSettings> reader exists and that the light reads the tier rather than a literal; it would have FAILED before this change, which is what makes it a regression guard rather than decoration. The others pin that the cycle covers every concrete tier without yielding Auto, and that Potato and Ultra genuinely disagree about shadows so the wiring proves something visible.

NOT CLAIMED, deliberately: this wires ONE field, shadows. bloom, ssao, anti_aliasing, fog, particles_max, terrain_detail_divisor and water_reflections are still unread by the live app and belong to their own lanes (bd-2z0.14.1.4 lighting, bd-2z0.14.1.6 post stack, terrain and particles lanes). title: Terrain 2.0: PBR splat-mapped heightfield, triplanar detail normals, biome blending, revisioned incremental updates
description:
BACKGROUND: Current Bevy terrain: 64x64-tile chunks of vertex-colored heightfield with per-chunk StandardMaterial, signature-based dirty checking that ignores kinds/fertility/temperature (known defect, plan 3.8), empty reflection probes. Vertex colors alone will never look like a game. The world has rich inputs: TerrainLayer kinds (DeepWater/ShallowWater/Sand/Grass/Bloom/Rock), elevation, fertility/moisture, temperature, hydrology depth/flow.

GOAL: Terrain that reads as a living landscape: texture splatting driven by C2 biome semantics, detail normals, smooth biome blending, correct revisioned updates. Sub-tasks: A2.1 splat-weight computation + palette baking (pure); A2.2 chunked mesh + LOD; A2.3 revisioned incremental updates + toroidal seams. This parent bead owns the WGSL splat shader + material assembly + integration, and the visual acceptance.

SCOPE (parent): (1) SplatMaterial WGSL: 4-8 layer splat (albedo atlas layers per biome + shared normal/detail maps), height+slope rules layered on C2 splat weights (rock on steep, sand near waterline, snow-cap option at high elevation), per-pixel daylight factor from C2. (2) Triplanar mapping on steep faces to avoid stretching; detail normal fade with distance. (3) Texture authoring: procedural generation of base biome textures at build/startup (deterministic, seeded; no asset downloads; cached under target/ or generated in-memory) - keeps the repo asset-free and reproducible. (4) Vertex density/mesh resolution per quality tier; fog + shadow receive. (5) Hydrology handoff: exposes per-vertex water depth mask for A3's water surface.

ACCEPTANCE: C4 goldens show blended biome transitions (no hard tile edges at Medium+); terrain update latency after a terrain edit (intervention bd-16g.10 surface) < 100ms at 1k agents; A2.1 pure functions fully unit-tested; C5 scene 'hydrology flood' golden green. LOGGING: info! on chunk rebuild counts per second (aggregate, not per-chunk); debug! splat atlas build stats.
acceptance_criteria: Close Terrain 2.0 only when the live Bevy material and render path consumes the deterministic biome palette and splat weights, the reopened chunked PBR heightfield with triplanar detail normals and water-depth inputs, and revisioned incremental seam-safe updates across quality tiers. Direct child state must be truthful; tracker-only child closure is not evidence. Unit and property tests cover palette and weight conservation, material binding, toroidal seams, revision coalescing, affected-chunk selection, stale-resource cleanup, and deterministic quality transitions. The visual E2E lane owned by bd-2z0.14.3.5 must drive real Bevy scripted cameras and terrain mutations, retain actual framebuffer provenance plus detailed material, chunk, revision, frame-time, device, and viewport logs, and include negative controls proving splat, triplanar, skirt, morph, water-depth, and incremental-update inputs are consumed. title: Hydrology water surface: depth-tinted animated water, shore foam, flow ripples, reflection tier
description:
BACKGROUND: The simulation has a real hydrology system (per-cell flow direction, accumulation, basins, water depth; REST /api/hydrology) that today renders as... flat blue tiles. Water is the single highest-leverage 'game look' element after lighting.

SCOPE: (1) Water surface mesh: one continuous plane per flooded region (or full-world plane clipped by depth mask in shader), animated with layered normal-map ripples whose direction/speed derive from the REAL hydrology flow_directions + accumulation fields (not generic sine waves) - still water in basins, directional flow in channels. (2) Depth-based color: shallow tint -> deep tint using actual water_depth (beer-lambert-ish absorption curve from C2 semantics), shore foam band where depth crosses a threshold (animated edge foam + wave lap), wet-sand darkening band on terrain near the waterline (A2 splat hook). (3) Reflections by tier: Potato/Low = none (specular only); Medium = screen-space-ish cheap reflection or static env cubemap; High/Ultra = planar reflection probe for the main water body (documented cost, part of C3 budgets). (4) Refraction fake: terrain seen through shallow water gets wobble distortion (normal-offset UV in the water pass over the already-rendered terrain, standard grab-pass technique). (5) Flood/drought dynamics: water level animates smoothly between snapshot revisions (no popping when hydrology updates); intervention scenes (drought bd-16g.10) get a drying-up transition. (6) Underwater camera mode: fog + color grade shift when the camera goes below the surface (A8 integration point).

ACCEPTANCE: C5 'hydrology flood' scene goldens green; flow-aligned ripple direction verified by a shader-input unit test (flow vector -> UV advection direction); depth-tint curve matches C2 golden vectors; perf: water pass within C5.3 subsystem budget at Medium. Deps: A2 (terrain depth mask + waterline), C2 (color semantics), bd-2z0.7.4 (hydrology revisioned layer). LOGGING: info! water region stats on rebuild; trace! per-frame uniforms.
acceptance_criteria: A dedicated continuous or depth-masked water surface consumes revisioned water_depth, flow_directions, and accumulation so still basins remain still and channel ripples advect along the measured flow. Production rendering includes documented depth absorption, animated shore foam, wet-sand waterline, tiered reflections, shallow refraction, smooth flood/drought revision transitions, and underwater camera treatment without silently reducing existing quality tiers. Unit and property tests pin flow-vector to UV advection, depth-tint vectors, tier selection, waterline thresholds, revision interpolation, finite edge cases, and deterministic rebuilds; swapped, stale, zero, and non-finite hydrology inputs are born-red negative controls. A mock-free Bevy E2E drives flood and drought scenes through the production snapshot path at supported tiers, captures actual framebuffers with source/backend/adapter/viewport/color provenance, proves unsupported cells are typed refusals rather than skips, retains detailed rebuild/uniform/frame logs, and satisfies the documented water-pass budget only through the approved DSR lane.

title: Lighting + atmosphere: cascaded sun shadows, real day/night cycle, sky gradient + stars, distance/height fog, SSAO
description:
BACKGROUND: Bevy today: one directional light (9000 lux, shadows on) + flat ambient (800) + tonemapping. GPUI fakes day/night with a sin(tick) tint. A real sky + sun + shadow system transforms the scene from 'tech demo' to 'world'.

SCOPE: (1) Sun system: directional light driven by C1 DayNight settings (cycle length in ticks; 0 = static noon preserving current behavior); elevation/azimuth curve shared with C2's daylight factor so TUI tint and Bevy sun always agree; warm low-sun color -> white noon -> blue night transition; night ambient floor so nocturnal scenes stay readable with emissive agent glow carrying the frame. (2) Shadows: CascadedShadowMaps (Bevy pbr) with cascade count/resolution per tier (Potato: off, Low: 1 cascade 1024, Medium: 2x2048, High: 4x2048, Ultra: 4x4096); shadow bias tuned to eliminate acne on the heightfield; creatures cast via A1 instanced shadow variants. (3) Sky: procedural gradient sky (rayleigh-ish 3-stop gradient as fullscreen background or skybox mesh), sun disc + glow, night star field (deterministic seeded star points, subtle twinkle via tick-phase), optional simple drifting cloud layer at High+ (noise-scrolled, cheap). (4) Fog: Bevy DistanceFog + height fog component (the world-gfx bottom-heavy exp fog is the prior-art formula), color synced to sky horizon and time-of-day; underwater fog variant (A3 hook). (5) SSAO at High/Ultra (Bevy pbr ssao) with quality presets; subtle so creature silhouettes stay readable. (6) Auto-exposure (already present via bevy_post_process) re-tuned for the day/night range so night scenes neither blow out nor crush; exposure bias from C1.

ACCEPTANCE: C5 'day/night sweep' scene goldens at dawn/noon/dusk/night; shadow acne absence verified in golden diff on heightfield close-up; C2 daylight factor == shader daylight within tolerance (unit test on shared curve); SSAO toggle diff visible in goldens; perf budgets per C5.3. Deps: A2 (terrain receives), C1 (DayNight + tiers). LOGGING: info! on tier-driven shadow/ssao configuration at startup; debug! on day-phase transitions.

REVISION (2026-07-17 self-review): dependency moved A2 -> bd-2z0.7.4. Sun/shadows/sky/fog need the revisioned heightfield (7.4), not splat texturing; lighting is the single biggest 'game look' lever and should not serialize behind the full Terrain 2.0 stack. Shadow-bias final tuning is re-validated against the splat material when A2 lands (A6 acceptance covers the composite).

title: Creature factory: procedural 3D critters with genome-driven proportions, PBR materials, damage/age/readability cues
description:
BACKGROUND: The ScriptBots silhouette - capsule body, two wheels, spike, eyes - IS the brand. GPUI paints it as 2D paths; Bevy today assembles ~15 primitive children per agent with unique materials. The overhaul keeps the iconic read ('you can still tell a carnivore from a herbivore at a glance, boosted agents flare, spike attacks telegraph') while making critters feel alive and dimensional.

GOAL: A parametric creature definition consumed by the A1 instanced pipeline: ONE base mesh family per LOD tier + per-instance vertex-shader deformation for proportions, instead of per-agent mesh/material combos. Sub-tasks: A5.1 parametric mesh generator; A5.2 material/emissive/state system. Parent owns integration + the readability contract.

READABILITY CONTRACT (preserved semantics, upgraded rendering): herbivore<->carnivore diet stripe (emissive), body color from genome lineage hue, size from genome, spike that visibly extends on attack, wheels that spin with speed (A9), boost flame state, mouth open on eat/yell, nose size by smell trait, ears by hearing trait, eyes with sclera+pupils tracking eye_dirs (NUM_EYES), temperature discomfort marker, selection ring + hover rim, damage darkening + health cracks overlay, age desaturation, corpse/carcass state vs living. Every mapping comes from C2 AgentVisualParams - no Bevy-local reinterpretation.

ACCEPTANCE: goldens (C4) for a character lineup scene: herbivore/carnivore/boosted/spiking/eating/selected/damaged/elder states all legible; creature pass draw calls flat vs population (A1); C5 cross-surface equivalence: TUI and Bevy agree on diet color + state cues for the same agent. Deps: A1 (pipeline), C2 (params). LOGGING: debug! creature-feature stats per frame at trace level; info! mesh/atlas build at startup.
acceptance_criteria: The production Bevy path consumes the canonical parametric LOD meshes and AgentVisualParams through one bounded instanced render-world pipeline, with no per-agent entity/material tree on the default path. Genome proportions, diet stripe, eyes, mouth, smell/hearing parts, spike/boost, wheel motion, temperature discomfort, selection/hover, damage cracks/darkening, age, corpse state, accessibility, toroidal ghosts, culling, and LOD transitions are all live and truthful. Unit/property tests cover instance packing, deformation, cue mappings, bounds, LOD hysteresis, truncation, and deterministic animation. Canonical real-frame lineup and 10k-agent evidence asserts semantic cross-surface agreement, nonblank/changed pixels, flat draw-call/material growth, bounded allocations/uploads, digest neutrality, and born-red unwired/blank/wrong-cue controls, with detailed pipeline/LOD/count/timing/device/provenance logs.

title: Parametric creature mesh generator: body/wheels/spike/eyes/mouth/ears as deformable base meshes + LOD chain
description: Builds the creature geometry kit consumed by A1/A5: (1) base meshes generated in code (no asset files): capsule body with rings/segments per LOD, torus wheels with tread normal detail, tapered cone spike, sphere eye + pupil inset, jaw-less mouth implied by emissive mouth band + shader, ear fins scaled by hearing trait, nose knob by smell trait. title: Post-processing stack v2: emissive-driven bloom, FXAA/TAA, vignette, DoF focus mode, chromatic accent, tier gating
description:
BACKGROUND: Post is what makes lighting feel expensive. Prior art in-tree: world-gfx has ACES/Reinhard tonemap, half-res separable bloom, vignette, bottom-heavy fog (2D); Bevy has tonemapping trio + auto-exposure but NO bloom/fog/SSAO/AA beyond defaults wired today. Bevy 0.17 provides bloom, fxaa/taa/smaa (anti_aliasing), depth of field (post_process), vignette via ColorGrading - the job is orchestration, tuning, and tier gating, not invention.

SCOPE: (1) Bloom configured to key off emissives (creature stripes/eyes, boost flames, particles, spike impacts) with threshold/intensity per tier from C1; verify the A5/A7 emissive design blooms correctly without blowing out terrain. (2) AA: FXAA at Low/Medium, TAA at High/Ultra (with creature-motion jitter validation - TAA ghosting on fast critters must be checked in goldens; SMAA as documented alternative); Potato = no AA + nearest-ish downgrade acceptable. (3) Vignette + subtle chromatic accent at frame edges (from C1 post settings; default subtle - readability first). (4) Depth of field for focus/follow mode (A8): selected agent sharp, world soft - cinematic inspector moments; off in free camera. (5) Motion blur: evaluated, default OFF (sim readability); if kept, behind Ultra tier only. (6) Unified post configuration materialized from C1 PostStack + tier matrix; hot-reload on typed reconfigure without pipeline leaks (old pipelines dropped deterministically). (7) Night-look grade: gentle blue-shift + highlight rolloff at night (synced to A4 sun phase), preserving CVD palette correctness (palette transform remains final - C2/A5.2 contract).

ACCEPTANCE: C4 goldens per tier show the expected stack (bloom present/absent per tier, DoF only in focus mode); TAA ghosting check golden; post pass timings within C5.3 budget; tier reconfigure at runtime leaves no leaked GPU resources (assert via wgpu allocation counters where available). Deps: A4 (HDR+sun phase), A5 (emissives), C1 (settings). LOGGING: info! on post-stack (re)build with tier + enabled passes; trace! per-pass timings.

REVISION (2026-07-17 self-review): this bead also DELIVERS the depth-of-field integration for A8's photo mode/focus mode (A8 no longer blocks on A6; the DoF component + wiring lands here, A8 exposes the toggle point).

title: Wire deterministic GPU particle VFX into the live Bevy event and render pipeline
description:
BACKGROUND: Events are the soul of the sim - births, deaths, combat, eating - and today they are invisible except as log lines and a TUI event list. Bevy has no built-in particle system; hanabi would be a new dependency (forbidden without the bd-2z0.8 lane). So we hand-roll a lean instanced-billboard GPU particle engine - a genuinely new subsystem (justifies new module file(s) in scriptbots-bevy per AGENTS.md's high bar).

SCOPE: (1) ParticleEngine: fixed-capacity pools per effect family (birth/death/combat/eat/boost/repro/ambient), ring-buffer allocation, zero per-frame heap alloc, GPU instanced billboards with per-particle attrs (pos, vel, life, size curve seed, color, sprite index, rotation); CPU spawns + GPU-simulated motion in WGSL (gravity/drag/buoyancy-in-water per particle kind). (2) Effect recipes (art-directed in C6's art bible): birth = upward sparkle burst in lineage hue; death-by-combat = red-orange impact shards + brief flash; death-by-starvation = grey wilt motes sinking; eat = small green nibble flecks arcing to mouth; combat hit = white-yellow spark cone along spike vector; boost = trailing flame/afterimage quads; reproduction = dual-tone pulse ring. (3) Determinism: particle scheduling seeded from (tick, event ordinal, world seed) so replays produce identical VFX; particles are PURELY visual - never read back, never in any digest (test asserts digest-neutrality with particles on/off). (4) Event feed: consumes C2 VisualCue table from the typed event stream (same cues drive TUI B4 pulses) - one semantics, two renderers. (5) Tier scaling: max live particles + emission rate scaled by quality tier; overflow policy = drop oldest ambient first, never drop combat/death cues under cap. (6) Camera micro-shake hook on nearby combat (A8 consumes). Sub-tasks: A7.1 engine core, A7.2 event bindings.

ACCEPTANCE: C5 event-coverage scenes show each cue; deterministic replay hash of particle states across two runs equal; pool overflow test proves priority policy; perf within C5.3 particle budget at 10k agents + combat storm scene. Deps: A5 (creature anchors), C2 (cue table). LOGGING: debug! pool stats per second; info! on pool resize/overflow policy activation.
acceptance_criteria: 1. The production Bevy app owns and schedules the delivered ParticlePool/CueEmitter/ParticleInstance substrate, drains the canonical typed VisualCue stream exactly once, and emits visible birth, death-by-cause, eat, combat, boost, reproduction, and ambient recipes; no integration exists only in tests. 2. A real Bevy render-world pipeline uploads grow-only instance buffers, binds the atlas/WGSL/depth resources, draws camera-facing billboards with tier-appropriate blend/depth policy, and enforces fixed capacity, quality-tier budgets, observable priority drops, and zero steady-state heap allocation or an explicitly measured bounded alternative. 3. Scheduling is a pure function of seed/tick/event ordinal and remains simulation-digest neutral; same replay yields equal particle hashes/frames, while changed seed/order and disconnected event ingestion are born-red negative controls. 4. Real capture scenes through the canonical harness show each cue and prove nonempty pixels, correct anchors/lifetimes/priority, and preserved world digest; a deliberately unwired/blank pipeline must fail. 5. A 10k-agent combat-storm proof runs only through the approved visual performance lane and enforces frame, upload, allocation, memory, and dropped-cue budgets without claiming unavailable DSR evidence. 6. Comprehensive unit/property/negative/integration tests plus a mock-free production capture E2E script cover overflow, stale handles, deterministic ordering, event disconnect/reconnect, device loss, tier changes, and all recipes with detailed pool/upload/draw/drop/device logs and retained artifacts. 7. Focused format/check/clippy/tests and approved proof gates pass at one reviewed revision.

title: Particle engine core: instanced billboard renderer, WGSL motion sim, pool allocators, sprite atlas
description: The standalone engine: pool allocator (fixed rings, free-list, O(1) spawn/kill), instance buffer write-combining, WGSL billboard vertex shader (camera-facing quads with per-particle scale/rotation), motion integration in shader from spawn-time attributes (pos0/vel0/gravity/drag/life), soft-particle depth fade (scene depth read), procedural sprite atlas (spark, mote, shard, puff, ring - generated deterministically like A2.1 textures), alpha blending order (single transparent pass, back-to-front by view-space depth bucket sort on CPU at Medium+, unsorted-with-depth-fade at Low). Unit tests: allocator behavior (wrap, reuse, overflow policy), WGSL validation via naga, determinism of spawn scheduling math (given identical cue streams, identical particle tables), sprite atlas hash. Immediately executable as pure engine + tests (renderer wiring lands in A7 parent). Deps: C2.

Staged particles.rs had 3 gaps vs acceptance, finished by CyanFox: (1) WGSL billboard was axis-aligned (world-XY offset, edge-on invisible to a 3/4 camera) - now camera-facing via camera_right/camera_up uniforms; (2) added soft-particle depth fade (scene_depth textureLoad + soft_fade_scale alpha falloff; the Low tier's substitute for sort order per C1); (3) added blend ordering: BlendOrderPolicy { Unsorted, BucketSort } + blend_order_into() - true 256-bucket depth sort, back-to-front, slot-stable, NaN-safe, caller-reused order+scratch buffers (zero steady-state alloc). Also added ParticleInstance (23-f32 GPU projection, layout pinned by test) + write_instance_buffer (slot-ordered, grow-only, write-combining friendly). WGSL now validated FOR REAL via naga 26 dev-dep (same version already in lock via wgpu 26 - no new crate): parse + full semantic validation in tests. EVIDENCE: cargo test -p scriptbots-bevy (aarch64-apple-darwin): 46 lib + 2 integration tests green incl. naga validation, instance fill slot-order/grow-only, blend order identity/back-to-front/tie-stability/uniform; scriptbots-bevy clippy clean (remaining -D warnings failures are all in scriptbots-core, another agent's in-flight surface); fmt clean; UBS clean (criticals are JS-scanner false positives on Rust ==). description: Binds the C2 VisualCue table (from the world's typed event stream) to A7.1 emitters: cue -> recipe lookup, spawn transform from the cue's world position/agent anchor, intensity scaling (combat damage -> shard count), tick-exact spawn scheduling (cues queue for their tick, never wall-clock), rate limiting per family (combat storm at 10k agents must not drown the frame - documented cap + priority), boost trail emitter attached to moving agents (anchor-following emitter, bounded trail length). Tests: golden cue->particle-count vectors per recipe, rate-limit behavior, anchor-follow correctness for a moving boosted agent, determinism across replays (identical cue stream -> identical particle state hash at tick N). title: Cinematic camera: damped orbit/follow/fly-to, free-fly, combat micro-shake, photo mode, minimap, toroidal-aware motion
description:
BACKGROUND: bd-2z0.7.5 owns camera/picking CORRECTNESS (acknowledged interaction, selection). Today's rig: orbit yaw/pitch + distance + follow modes + smoothing lerp. This bead makes the camera FEEL like a game: weight, intention, and cinematic helpers - while keeping the 3/4 top-down default that keeps population dynamics readable (art direction, bd-2z0.14).

SCOPE: (1) Damped spring camera (critically damped, tunable) replacing raw lerp: no overshoot on snap, smooth follow through agent motion. (2) Fly-to transitions: selecting an agent (click, REST selection, TUI focus parity) triggers an eased fly-to framing it; Esc/right-drag cancels to free orbit. (3) Follow modes preserved + extended: Off/Selected/Oldest/FirstAgent (current set) + predator-prey 'action' follow (auto-frame current top carnivore, opt-in). (4) Combat micro-shake: impulse from A7 combat cues within camera range, decaying perlin shake, amplitude scales with zoom (never nausea-inducing; capped, disable setting). (5) Photo mode: toggle hides HUD, enables DoF (A6), frees the camera, exposes FOV/roll/exposure sliders, PNG capture via C4 harness. (6) Minimap: corner orthographic top-down inset (reuses A1 instanced pass to a small viewport, cheap) with viewport rect + click-to-jump (mouse) - restores the at-a-glance world orientation the 2D view gave for free. (7) Toroidal-aware camera: panning/follow wraps across world edges using wrapped deltas (current rig has toroidal wrap deltas - preserve and extend to fly-to paths so the camera never flies the long way around). (8) Input: mouse orbit/zoom/pan + full keyboard parity + remappable bindings (preserving the remapping feature from GPUI-era: 22 CommandActions equivalent inventory carried forward, C6 ledger).

ACCEPTANCE: C5 camera-script scenes replay exactly (deterministic keyframes); follow-through-wrap test (agent crosses seam, camera doesn't whip); shake amplitude cap unit test; photo-mode capture golden; minimap click-to-jump e2e. Deps: bd-2z0.7.5 (interaction base), A4 (so camera respects lighting/underwater hooks), A6 (DoF). LOGGING: debug! camera mode transitions; trace! per-frame pose.

REVISION (2026-07-17 self-review): dependency on A6 REMOVED - the camera is early user-facing value and must not serialize behind the post stack. Photo mode ships with FOV/roll/exposure controls; depth-of-field activation is provided BY A6 (see its revision note) and is absent until then, documented in the C6 ledger.

title: Creature + world animation: wheel spin, lean-into-turn, spike thrust, idle breathing, food growth pulse, ambient life
description:
BACKGROUND: Static critters sliding across terrain reads as 'simulation viewer'; animated critters read as 'alive'. All animation is shader/vertex-level (works with A1 instancing - no skeletal animation entities) and tick-phase driven (deterministic, replay-stable).

SCOPE: (1) Locomotion: wheels rotate at angular velocity = linear speed / wheel radius (per-instance phase accumulated in shader from tick + speed integral); body leans into acceleration/turn (pitch/roll from velocity delta, smoothed); bob scaled by speed over rough terrain (heightfield slope). (2) Idle: subtle breathing (body scale 1 +/- 0.01 at trait-scaled rate), occasional eye dart (pupil offset re-randomized on deterministic schedule), herbivore graze dip when eating. (3) Combat/attack: spike thrust animation (extend-ease-out, retract-ease-in over ~8 ticks), attack lunge (body pitch forward), hit flinch on victim (brief squash + color flash synced to A7 impact particles). title: Braille/half-block truecolor world canvas: 2x4 sub-cell density, biome ramps, day/night tint, agent glyphs, food shimmer
description:
BACKGROUND: The current Ratatui map draws ONE character per terminal cell: a 120x40 terminal shows a ~70x30 world - chunky blobs where a 5k-agent world is unreadable soup. Plan 8.4 already prescribes the fix: Braille 2x4 density rendering (8x sub-cell resolution), block 2x2 and half-block 1x2 fallbacks, grow-only painter buffers, capability-based glyph selection. bd-2z0.6.4 owns the responsive canvas+inspector MIGRATION onto FrankenTUI; THIS bead owns the VISUAL QUALITY of that canvas.

SCOPE: (1) Sub-cell painter: braille (2x4 dots = 8 pixels/cell) as the primary mode, half-block (1x2, fg/bg = two pixels) + quadrant (2x2) fallbacks; world sampled into an off-screen float 'pixel' buffer (terrain color, food glow, agent occupancy/heading, water depth, selection) then composited to cells in one pass - grow-only reusable buffers per plan. (2) Truecolor rendering with graceful degradation: 24-bit ramps on capable terminals, 256-color quantization, 16-color fallback, NO_COLOR honored; capability probe at startup (TERM/COLORTERM/locale) with the chosen tier logged (info!). (3) Biome ramps from C2 semantics: terrain kind base colors, elevation shading (hillshade from the elevation field - fake but effective terrain relief in text), fertility/moisture tinting, hydrology depth ramp + animated water shimmer (tick-phase, deterministic). (4) Agents: sub-cell dots colored by C2 diet color with heading whiskers (braille dot patterns encoding 8-sector direction), cluster heat when many agents share a cell (density -> brightness), boosted flare, spike flash on attack ticks, selection ring (braille circle). (5) Day/night: whole-canvas tint + gamma following the C2 daylight curve (same phase as Bevy sun). (6) Food: green-gold density glow with gentle pulse (C2 shimmer phase - identical phase to Bevy, cross-surface test in C5). (7) Zoom/pan: integer+sub-cell smooth zoom levels, viewport follows selection; minimap corner strip when zoomed (braille world thumbnail). (8) Preserved vocabularies: emoji/narrow/ascii modes remain selectable as an ALTERNATE vocabulary layer (same buffers, different glyph compositor) - zero feature loss; 'e'/'n' keybinds preserved.

ACCEPTANCE: buffer-cell goldens (C5.2) at all breakpoints; agent positions accurate to sub-cell within tolerance vs world coords (unit test); identical frames on identical snapshots (determinism test); 10k-agent frame build < 8ms on M4-class CPU (trace! timing field); C5 cross-surface: Bevy pixel color vs TUI cell color for same world point match C2 semantics within quantization tolerance. Deps: bd-2z0.6.4 (canvas migration), C2 (semantics). Sub-tasks: B1.1 painter core, B1.2 ramps+overlay. LOGGING: info! capability tier + canvas mode at startup; debug! frame build stats per second.
