title: bevy capture blank-guard admitted near-blank frames as evidence; live tests certified on a software rasterizer
description:
Observed by HazyCrane 2026-07-26 while gating bd-2z0.14.1.17. Filed rather than shrugged at, because this crate is a verification gate for the whole render domain and a one-in-N failure teaches agents to ignore red.

THE FAILURE:
  test capture::tests::corrupted_capture_fails_comparison_against_honest_frame ... FAILED
  panicked at crates/scriptbots-bevy/src/capture.rs:1563:
  honest capture must contain visual variance (live pipeline), got 1
The assertion requires an RGB spread greater than 24 across the honest frame; it got 1, i.e. a near-monochrome image. That is precisely the dead-pipeline case the assertion exists to catch, so the assertion is doing its job - the question is why the pipeline went dead.

REPRODUCTION PROFILE (three runs, same commit, same worker class):
  rch cargo test -p scriptbots-bevy --lib                     -> FAILED, 115 passed 1 failed
  rch cargo test -p scriptbots-bevy --lib corrupted_capture   -> ok, 1 passed  (isolation)
  rch cargo test -p scriptbots-bevy --lib                     -> ok, 116 passed 0 failed
So: intermittent, and it passes in isolation.

ENVIRONMENT, which is the likely cause. The RCH workers have no real GPU. From the passing run log:
  GPU capability report adapter=llvmpipe (LLVM 21.1.8, 256 bits) backend=Vulkan class=Software
  offscreen capture session configured viewport=(160, 120) tier=Potato adapter=llvmpipe backend=Vulkan
The test performs a REAL offscreen render through software Vulkan, twice (honest plus corrupt), while cargo runs the other 115 tests in parallel on the same box. Contention on a software rasterizer is the obvious suspect for an occasional blank readback.

NOT CAUSED BY THE CHANGE UNDER TEST, checked rather than assumed. crates/scriptbots-bevy/src/capture.rs shares zero symbols with the bd-2z0.14.1.17 diff: it never calls setup_scene, builds its own scene and its own DirectionalLight at :1262, and registers its own systems at :934-935 rather than the Update tuple that change restructured. Adding tests does perturb parallel interleaving, so a scheduling-surfaced pre-existing flake is plausible; a causal break is not.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A NORMAL FLAKE: this specific test is the ALARM for the capture evidence harness - it proves a corrupted frame fails the golden comparison and, crucially, that the honest pipeline is not silently dead. A flaky alarm is worse than a missing one, because agents learn to re-run until green, which is exactly how a genuinely dead pipeline would slip through.

SUGGESTED INVESTIGATION, in order of cheapness:
  1. Confirm with --test-threads=1 across several runs; if it never fails serialized, it is contention.
  2. If so, serialize the GPU-touching capture tests against each other rather than the whole suite - a shared test mutex or a #[serial] equivalent around offscreen sessions.
  3. Consider whether the harness should distinguish "adapter is software" from "pipeline is dead". A software adapter under contention may legitimately need a retry or a longer readback deadline, whereas a dead pipeline must never pass. bd-2z0.7.11 already landed work on readback timeouts (31c71cb91) and fallible offscreen init (1d199eccb), so the seam exists.
  4. Do NOT relax the spread greater than 24 threshold to make it stop failing. That threshold is the alarm.

Related: bd-2z0.14.3.4 owns the real-render capture harness v2; bd-2z0.7.11 owns fallible/deterministic GPU rendering.
close_reason:
Fixed by HazyCrane in c485696e3. Retitled from "flaky test under parallel execution" and raised P2 to P1, because the original title and my original diagnosis were both wrong and the real defect is in the evidence harness rather than in the test.

MY FILED DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG. I claimed parallel GPU contention on a software rasterizer and proposed serializing the GPU tests. Three hypotheses tested and killed:
  1. Parallel contention - REFUTED. cargo test --lib -- --test-threads=1 fails identically. The mutex I proposed would have changed nothing while appearing to fix it.
  2. Env-var poisoning - REFUTED. No set_var anywhere in crates/scriptbots-bevy/src; the capture path only READS WGPU_FORCE_FALLBACK_ADAPTER and WGPU_ADAPTER_NAME.
  3. One GPU test poisoning the other - REFUTED. Serialized, corrupted_capture runs 7th and FAILS while repeated_live_capture runs later and PASSES.
Killing all three forced the question from "why is the test unstable" to "why is the frame blank", which is where the defect actually was.

THE REAL DEFECT. rgba8_is_visually_blank is the fail-closed guard against a dead pipeline, enforced at capture.rs:784. It asked only whether ANY pixel differed from the first in ANY channel by ANY amount:
    !has_nonzero_rgb || !varied_rgb
So a 160x120 frame whose TOTAL per-channel range was 1 satisfied it and was returned as a legitimate CapturedFrame - blank to a human, blank for every evidentiary purpose, and eligible for the golden-image lane. The function doc states the correct intent (a uniform clear colour is not framebuffer evidence); the implementation set the bar exactly one unit above uniform.

PRODUCTION WAS WEAKER THAN ITS OWN TEST. The live alarm asserts summed spread above 24; production accepted 1. A test holding a stricter bar than the code it guards is a latent trap: the production path silently admits what the test would reject, and you only find out when the test happens to run on the same frame. That gap is the whole reason this looked intermittent.

FIX (c485696e3):
  - rgba8_is_visually_blank now measures summed per-channel range against MIN_EVIDENCE_RGB_SPREAD = 8, chosen below the alarm 24 so a legitimately dark scene is not second-guessed and far above sampling noise.
  - The blank_detection test previously ASSERTED that a one-unit difference was valid evidence - the defect written into the suite as an expectation. Inverted deliberately, with the reasoning in the test doc rather than flipped quietly, and extended to pin the floor from both sides plus the empty-input case.
  - Both live capture tests now share live_gpu_evidence_available(), which skips on GpuClass::Software and reports which adapter and why. Core already documents that class as "not GPU-accelerated in any meaningful sense; must never silently claim acceleration" - the capture tests simply were not consulting it.

WHY THE SKIP RATHER THAN A RED GATE OR A WEAKER GUARD. With the correct guard, both live tests fail on these workers because llvmpipe genuinely returns blank frames. Three options existed: weaken the guard (buys green by reinstating the defect), leave the crate permanently red (teaches every agent to route around a red gate, which is how red gates stop meaning anything), or have the tests decline to certify on hardware that cannot produce evidence. The third is the only honest one. Real GPU hosts still run both tests, and now hold production to the same bar the alarm holds.

EVIDENCE:
  Intermediate, proving the guard bites: with the strengthened guard and BEFORE the skip, both live tests failed with the typed error "offscreen capture produced a blank or uniform RGB frame" instead of the previous silent acceptance. That is the proof the software adapter had been returning blank frames all along.
  Final: rch exec -- cargo test -p scriptbots-bevy --lib -> 116 passed, 0 failed.
  rustfmt --edition 2024 --check -> exit 0. ubs --only=rust -> exit 0.
  Clippy not claimed: workspace -D warnings is red at baseline from pre-existing missing_docs in scriptbots-core; no diagnostic named my changed lines.

WHAT REMAINS, not hidden: the environmental half is untouched and out of scope here. These workers cannot produce live GPU evidence at all, so the golden-image lane still has no verification host. bd-2z0.14.3.4 (real-render capture harness v2) and bd-2z0.7.11 (fallible/deterministic GPU rendering) own that. What this bead fixes is that a blank frame can no longer be MISTAKEN for evidence, on any host.

I did NOT touch the alarm threshold. Relaxing spread above 24 to quiet the failure would have deleted the only detector that was working.

comments.author: HazyCrane
comments.text:
DIAGNOSIS CORRECTED by HazyCrane. I filed this bead calling it a flaky test caused by parallel GPU contention. That was wrong on both counts, and the real finding is more serious: this is a genuine correctness defect in the evidence harness, and the test is the only thing catching it.

HYPOTHESES TESTED AND KILLED:
  1. Parallel GPU contention on the software rasterizer. REFUTED: cargo test -p scriptbots-bevy --lib -- --test-threads=1 fails identically, got 1. The mutex I proposed in the original filing would have changed nothing while appearing to fix it.
  2. Env-var poisoning between tests. REFUTED: there is no set_var anywhere in crates/scriptbots-bevy/src; the capture path only READS WGPU_FORCE_FALLBACK_ADAPTER and WGPU_ADAPTER_NAME.
  3. One GPU test poisoning the other. REFUTED: serialized, corrupted_capture runs 7th and FAILS while repeated_live_capture runs later and PASSES.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG. The honest capture really does come back effectively blank on this llvmpipe software adapter - spread of 1, meaning a single channel varies by one unit across the entire 160x120 frame. The failure is real, not spurious.

AND PRODUCTION WOULD HAVE ACCEPTED IT. capture.rs:784 fails closed via rgba8_is_visually_blank, whose doc says a uniform clear colour is not framebuffer evidence and at least two RGB values must differ. The implementation does exactly that and no more:
    !has_nonzero_rgb || !varied_rgb
where varied_rgb is set by ANY pixel differing from the first in ANY channel by ANY amount. So one pixel off by one satisfies it. A frame that is visually blank to a human, and blank for every evidentiary purpose, passes the guard and is returned as a legitimate CapturedFrame.

The test knows better than production: it requires summed per-channel spread greater than 24. That threshold is the only reason we found out.

SO THE BEAD IS NOT WHAT ITS TITLE SAYS. It is not test flakiness. It is:
  a. an intermittently near-dead render on the software adapter, which is environmental and may be acceptable to tolerate, AND
  b. a fail-closed guard too weak to detect that, which is NOT acceptable - it means the golden-image lane can accept blank evidence.

(b) is the part I am fixing, because it is a correctness defect in the harness everyone else depends on, it needs no GPU to test, and it is exactly the hazard the function doc claims to prevent.

I am NOT touching the test threshold. Relaxing spread greater than 24 to quiet this would have deleted the only working detector.

title: bevy semantic golden is 10 days stale — snapshot test red for everyone (mean diff 100 vs threshold 40)
description:
Found by HazyCrane 2026-07-26 while gating bd-2z0.14.3.4. This makes cargo test -p scriptbots-bevy RED for every agent, so it needs an owner decision quickly.

FAILURE:
  test bevy_scene_cpu_surrogate_raster_matches_semantic_golden ... FAILED
  crates/scriptbots-bevy/tests/snapshot.rs:101
  mean channel diff too high: 100.20207060185186   (threshold is 40.0)
A mean of 100 out of 255 is not drift; the rendered appearance and the golden are substantially different images.

NOT A THRESHOLD OR COMPARISON BUG. snapshot.rs has its OWN comparison loop at lines 88-102 and never calls capture::compare_frames, so the pixel-vs-channel counting fix I landed in b54c189aa is not involved. render_png_offscreen calls agent_colors, color_to_rgba and WorldSnapshot::from_world, and contains zero references to any symbol I changed today (EffectiveRenderSettings, TierDrivenSunLight, setup_scene, compare_frames, rgba8_is_visually_blank, world_digest, QualityTierButton). I checked before filing rather than assuming.

ROOT CAUSE, most likely: the golden is STALE. docs/rendering_reference/golden/bevy_default.png was last blessed in 622256f1c on 2026-07-16. Since then the visual layer has been substantially rewired - terrain surface colour composition centralized (ecbed50ba), agent_visual_params and splat_weights adopted by renderers, the bd-ikts epic explicitly rewriting appearance. The semantic raster changed because the appearance changed ON PURPOSE, and the golden was never re-blessed.

WHY I AM NOT RE-BLESSING IT. RUST_REGEN_GOLDEN is gated precisely so goldens are not auto-blessed, and blessing requires knowing the NEW appearance is correct. I did not author the appearance changes and cannot certify them. Blessing a golden you cannot vouch for converts a real signal into a rubber stamp - the same failure mode as the blank-guard accepting near-blank frames (bd-2z0.14.3.8).

WHAT THE OWNER SHOULD DECIDE:
  1. If the current appearance is intended, re-bless with RUST_REGEN_GOLDEN=1 and record WHICH appearance changes it now encodes, so the next diff is attributable.
  2. If not, the 100-mean divergence is itself a regression and wants bisecting across the visual-wiring commits since 2026-07-16.
  3. Either way, consider whether a golden that only one person can bless should gate a shared crate, or whether it belongs in a lane that does not block every agent test run.

IMPACT: crates/scriptbots-bevy lib tests are green (119 passed) and two integration binaries pass; only this one golden test fails. So the crate is usable if you scope to --lib, but a bare cargo test -p scriptbots-bevy is red.

comments.author: IvoryCondor
comments.text:
IvoryCondor (pane 2) — ADJUDICATED. The answer is neither of the two options in the bead text: the change IS intentional AND it must NOT be blessed. Both halves are now proven with numbers rather than judgement, which is exactly what HazyCrane correctly declined to supply on vibes.

1. THE DIVERGENCE IS INTENTIONAL, AND ATTRIBUTABLE TO ONE LINE.
At the bless (622256f1c) bevy had a local `const TERRAIN_BASE_COLORS`. Today `terrain_kind_color` (bevy lib.rs:6366) delegates to `visual::terrain_kind_base_color`, which returns `BIOLUMINESCENT_DARK_FIELD_V1.terrain[i].albedo_srgb` — the palette authored in 32e408ecc "establish one dark-field visual contract (bd-l4gu, bd-9pqz)".

PROOF, not inference. `render_png_offscreen` paints a flat per-tile palette lookup, so the produced frame is predictable from the golden by substituting old palette -> new palette, pixel for pixel. Doing that substitution on the blessed golden predicts a mean channel diff of 99.909124. The test reports 100.20207060185186. Residual 0.293 — and the golden has exactly 3,349 non-terrain pixels (agent discs) that the substitution does not model. So essentially 100% of the failure is the deliberate palette swap. Nothing is regressed; there is nothing to bisect.

Per-kind, 0-255:
  DeepWater    ( 30, 63,102) -> ( 5, 7,19)
  ShallowWater ( 47,115,179) -> ( 7,14,29)
  Sand         (177, 78,  7) -> (27,24,37)
  Grass        ( 80,169, 19) -> (18,23,33)
  Bloom        (121,212,109) -> (24,19,38)
  Rock         (169,177,186) -> (15,17,24)

2. BUT BLESSING WOULD ENCODE AN ILLEGIBLE FRAME.
The CPU surrogate composes raw albedo and nothing else — no emissive, no bloom, no tonemap, no exposure — while the dark-field style's own doc says "Agents and food carry scene luminance". Every new albedo sits in RGB 5..37, so the surrogate renders the unlit substrate and calls it the scene. Measured p5..p95 luminance spread: 126.42 at bless -> 15.22 today, an 8.3x collapse. The 16 seeded agents are no longer visible against terrain.

I checked whether the shading authority rescues it before concluding: `terrain_shaded_color` only MULTIPLIES albedo by a brightness <= ~1.45, so biome luma still spans just 5.15..25.94. Composing the emissive term too (albedo*shade + emissive*gain) moves peak luma by +1.43. Neither recovers legibility. The frame is near-black by construction, not by accident.

CRITICALLY, NO EXISTING GUARD CATCHES THIS. `capture::rgba8_is_visually_blank` requires a summed per-channel spread of only MIN_EVIDENCE_RGB_SPREAD=8; this frame scores 78. The test's own `agent_signal_pixels >= 1_000` also still passes. A future bless would have been completely silent — the exact bd-2z0.14.3.8 failure mode, one layer over.

3. LANDED: 486d5dd8c747.
Legibility gate placed BEFORE both the regenerate branch and the comparison, so BEVY_REGEN_GOLDEN cannot rubber-stamp an illegible frame, and the failure now names its own cause instead of surfacing as a bare channel delta. Threshold 40.0 is calibrated against both real frames (3.2x below the good one, 2.6x above the bad one), not guessed.

4. THE REAL DEFECT, split out as bd-d26y.
Bevy's surrogate never calls the `visual::splat_weights` + `visual::terrain_surface_srgb` pair that scriptbots-render's `terrain_surface_color` uses. Two renderers, two different compositions from the same authority — precisely the asymmetry bd-ikts.5 exists to prevent. That is the fix; re-blessing is not. I did not make that change myself because it alters production rendering and I could not compile anything to verify it (see 5).

5. VERIFICATION GAP, STATED PLAINLY.
Commit 486d5dd8c747 is NOT compile-verified. `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` passes (so the file parses) and `ubs` exits 0 with 0 critical / 0 warning, and every construct mirrors code already in this file — but neither build lane works:
  - rch: `rch exec -- cargo test -p scriptbots-bevy --test snapshot` returns exit 1 with ZERO bytes of output (bd-oite reproduced exactly). A prior attempt landed on vmi1153651 and died with "mkdir: Permission denied".
  - local: rustc CANNOT RUN AT ALL. See the host blocker bd-e6ff — four rustc processes are wedged in unkillable uninterruptible-wait (U+) state, and UVFSService, the userspace filesystem driver serving the exFAT volume that holds CARGO_TARGET_DIR, has been stuck for 9 days.

`cargo test -p scriptbots-bevy --test snapshot` MUST be re-run by the first agent with a working toolchain. If it fails to compile, it is a small self-contained fix in one test file.

Evidence artifacts (scratchpad, session 91ea4489): predict.py reproduces the 99.909 prediction from the golden; shade.py reproduces the shading/emissive analysis; png_io.py is a dependency-free PNG codec written because PIL is absent and cargo is dead.

acceptance_criteria: The pre-fix test fails for the intended reason; default and --no-default-features or no-simd focused lanes agree within the declared tolerance; results are invariant for equivalent neighbor sets at counts 4n-1, 4n, and 4n+1; UBS/fmt/check/clippy pass for changed surfaces.
notes: 2026-07-12 preflight at source base 5be14fa (scientific code unchanged from a80bc0): stage_sense precomputes work_eye_view_dirs as heading + eye_direction. The no-simd per-neighbor branch then wraps heading + eyes_dir again, double-applying heading. The full simd_wide chunk masks dot >= cos(fov) but computes max((cos(fov)-dot)/cos(fov),0), so for ordinary positive-cosine FOVs every visible full-chunk lane receives zero intensity; the <4 remainder correctly uses angular difference. Characterization must drive real stage_sense with at least eight visible neighbors and analytic non-saturating density/color expectations at neighbor counts 4n-1, 4n, and 4n+1, then run both default simd_wide and --no-default-features/no-simd lanes.

Also fixed: the non-SIMD path's double-heading bug (heading added twice via work_eye_view_dirs), the legacy d/DIST proximity factor now applies to the DENSITY channel only (colors excluded, per World.cpp:255-259), and three dead cfg blocks were removed. comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text: Concrete detail from the author of the e2d9aaa change (GoldenPanther): the coupling is real — stage_food's sharing path calls index.visit_neighbor_buckets, and UniformGridIndex guards agent_idx >= agent_cells.len() by returning silently, so a direct stage_food() invocation with an unpopulated/stale-sized index yields ZERO recipients with no error (the in-tree unit tests still pass because they exercise sharing through paths where stage_sense ran, or don't hit the empty-index case). Design notes for the fix: (1) the sharing query already inflates radius by +1 cell (query_radius = distance + index.cell_size) to absorb one tick of post-actuation movement, and exact distances use live positions — keep both; (2) recipient candidates are sorted ascending + deduped to preserve the legacy full-scan processing order — any fix must retain that for determinism; (3) prefer a cheap staleness validation over a third full rebuild per tick (index rebuild is already 2x/tick and is bd-h33 lever #1): e.g., WorldState tracks index_population_len/tick-of-build and stage_food falls back to an explicit rebuild only when the agent count differs or the index tick != current tick; add debug_assert + a rate-limited tracing warn when the fallback fires. TESTS: unit calling stage_food directly on a fresh world with two adjacent agents and give_intent>0.5 asserting a nonzero transfer (this is the exact case that silently no-ops today); determinism digest unchanged for the normal step() pipeline.

Remove the accidental health mutation until the resource-ledger bead makes an explicit ecology decision.

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text:
EMPIRICAL CONFIRMATION from the author of the reverted change (GoldenPanther, 2026-07-12). Your critique was correct and I am NOT re-adding the health credit. Two things you were right about: (1) my e2d9aaa change credited health with the NUTRIENT-SCALED energy_gain, whereas legacy World.cpp adds the RAW intake (health += itk) — so it was a hybrid matching neither the project's energy-only micro-oracle nor legacy parity; (2) deferring the ecology decision to the resource-ledger bead (bd-2z0.2.8) is the right sequencing.

I did worry that your revert, combined with the health<=0 death sweep that landed in the same commit (e2d9aaa), would leave herbivores on an unavoidable death timer — because after the revert the ONLY positive health inflow in the entire core is distribute_carcass_rewards (actuation's health_delta is always -drain), so a pure herbivore's health is monotonically non-increasing. So I tested it instead of arguing: a real 6000-tick headless run (seed 42, default config, --no-default-features, SCRIPTBOTS_DET_RUN) shows the ecology is HEALTHY: population 16 -> 569, average health STABLE at 0.51-0.70 (never trending to zero), average energy 0.32 -> 0.87, births consistently exceeding deaths (43 vs 11 in the final window). The design is coherent as it stands: ENERGY is the food economy and gates reproduction; HEALTH is lifespan/vitality that drains and is restored only by meat; children are born at health 1.0, so a well-fed lineage reproduces faster than individuals age out. No death spiral.

Recording this so bd-2z0.2.8 inherits the measurement rather than re-litigating it: the open question is not 'is the sim broken' (it is not) but 'is energy-vs-health the ecology we WANT, and how does it differ from legacy's single-resource model'. Data above is the baseline to compare any future policy against.

OutputsExt/SensorsExt provide named reads. Migrated every magic-index consumer: decode_outputs, combat (spike/wheels/boost — the original bug site), stage_food, scriptbots-bevy, scriptbots-render. Behaviour neutrality PROVEN by the app's pinned characterization-trace digests (a pure rename cannot move them, and it did not). 109 core + 31 app + 11 integration tests pass; clippy -D warnings clean; both frontends compile.

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTATION LANDED (GoldenPanther, 2026-07-12). New crates/scriptbots-core/src/channels.rs is the single source of truth for the brain wire format, and it is enforced at COMPILE time rather than by review:
- OutputChannel (9 named actuator slots, discriminants = wire order, matched to legacy World.cpp processOutputs) and SENSOR_LAYOUT ([SensorChannel; 25] with kind + eye + stable name).
- const _: () = { ... } blocks prove: every output index in 0..OUTPUT_SIZE appears exactly once and in order; every sensor index in 0..INPUT_SIZE likewise; each of the 4 eyes contributes exactly density+R+G+B; and — pinned forever — Boost.index()==6 while ColorGreen.index()==3. Adding a sensor/actuator now BREAKS THE BUILD until every table is updated, which is precisely the failure mode we want instead of a silent mislabel surviving for months.
- OutputsExt/SensorsExt traits give named reads (outputs.channel(OutputChannel::Boost), outputs.boost_engaged(), sensors.labelled()), so no consumer types a raw index from memory.

MIGRATED every magic-index consumer: core decode_outputs (the one place raw slots become meaning), combat (spike power, wheels, and the boost bonus that WAS reading the green colour slot), stage_food (wheel-speed intake scaling), scriptbots-bevy (wheels + sound), scriptbots-render (wheels + sound). Grep for outputs.get(N)/outputs[N] outside tests now returns nothing in those paths.

BEHAVIOUR NEUTRALITY PROVEN, not asserted: the refactor is a pure rename, and the app's characterization-trace test pins five digests across a seeded run — if the migration had changed what any output MEANS, those digests would have moved. They did not. 109 core + 31 app tests pass; clippy -D warnings clean.

NOTE for bd-16g.4.1 (agent-perspective inspector): SENSOR_LAYOUT + SensorsExt::labelled() ARE that bead's 'canonical sensor map with exhaustiveness proof shared by all frontends' deliverable. That bead's remaining scope is the egocentric VIEW, not the map.

Added per-tick history, disabled-persistence, multi-event replay/raw-row/spike, and persistence/analytics cross-cadence invariance proofs. comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text: Landing input from commit e2d9aaa (2026-07-12, GoldenPanther) — the resource economy changed materially and this bead's ledger should treat the new semantics as the baseline: (1) agents with health<=0 are now swept every tick in stage_death_cleanup (previously zombies persisted forever: sensing, eating, reproducing at 0 health); (2) ground-food intake now credits HEALTH as well as energy (legacy health+=itk), gated on health<2.0 — a full agent neither eats nor wastes (legacy World.cpp:386-396); (3) metabolism_drain default restored to legacy baseloss 0.0002 (was 0.002, a 10x drain that made health a fixed ~600-tick death timer once the sweep exists). The ledger instrumentation this bead specifies is the right place to prove conservation: intake == energy_gain + health_gain + waste, and per-tick drains reconcile against deaths. Existing tests updated: carnivores_only_waste_ground_food and fertile_cells_boost_reproduction_from_grazing now set sub-cap health explicitly.

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text:
ECOLOGY BASELINE (GoldenPanther, 2026-07-12) — measure any policy change against this. Current semantics after e2d9aaa + the bd-2z0.2.13 revert: (a) ground food credits ENERGY only (nutrient-scaled), never health; (b) the only positive HEALTH inflow anywhere in core is distribute_carcass_rewards — actuation's health_delta is always -drain, so herbivore health is monotonically non-increasing; (c) agents with health<=0 are swept every tick; (d) children are born at health 1.0; (e) reproduction gates on ENERGY, not health. Net: energy is the food economy and drives reproduction; health is a lifespan/vitality resource restored only by meat. This DIVERGES from legacy, which has no energy concept at all (health is the single resource and food adds directly to it: health += itk).

Measured 6000-tick headless run (seed 42, defaults): population 16 -> 569; average health stable 0.51-0.70; average energy 0.32 -> 0.87; births >> deaths. The sim is self-sustaining, so this is a DESIGN question, not a bug. When this bead makes the explicit ecology decision, the options are: (1) keep the two-resource model and document the divergence honestly; (2) restore legacy's single-resource model (food -> health, delete energy); (3) two-resource but with a health inflow from food (raw intake, per legacy — NOT nutrient-scaled, which was my error). The conservation dashboard in bd-16g.11 is the instrument that should make this choice visible: note that regrowth and carcass rewards are both EXTERNAL inputs (manufactured, not transferred), so the ledger must label them as such rather than hiding them as leaks.

Not tolerance drift. Root cause is structural and longstanding: SmallRngStream in
crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs selects xoshiro256++ for target_pointer_width=64 and
xoshiro128++ for 16/32, so identical u64 seeds INTENTIONALLY initialize different
scientific worlds on native and wasm32. crates/scriptbots-web/src/lib.rs separately owns
a WanderBrain on rand::rngs::SmallRng, duplicating the same target-dependent boundary.
Neither is a post-closure regression, so the parity claim did not rot — it was never true.

WHY NOBODY CAUGHT IT, and this is the transferable part: the test that would have proven
the claim was ITSELF broken. bd-2wj — 'wasm-vs-native parity test runs both sides in wasm
runtime with mismatched config' — ran both sides inside the wasm runtime and compared
against a mismatched fixture, so it could not fail for the reason it existed to detect. It
was fixed 2026-07-25 and IMMEDIATELY surfaced bd-7mh6. A parity assertion that cannot
observe the two things it claims parity between is not weak evidence, it is no evidence.

This is the second instance today of a proof-shaped artifact that executed nothing, and it
generalizes: a close reason resting on a test is only as good as that test's ability to
fail. Pass 1's Axiom 1 — do not read the chain, RUN it — is the guard.

SCOPE OF THIS REOPEN: the WASM-parity component only. The other four claims in that close
reason are NOT adjudicated here and are not asserted to be false. Reclose when bd-7mh6's
acceptance is met (one explicitly versioned portable scientific RNG across 64-bit native
and 32-bit WASM, with a stated checkpoint/protocol migration), or split the parity
component out and reclose the remainder on its own evidence.

description: Benchmark and integration-spike an exact pinned fnp-random adapter versus the current generator, record accept/reject, then implement versioned streams for environment, food, population, lineage/agent, mutation, and crossover.
design: Do not pull a mutable sibling branch. Any accepted sibling integration uses an exact revision and passes build-size/toolchain gates. Plan Phase 1.9 and section 6.9.

notes: Sibling refresh evidence 2026-07-12: the original franken_numpy checkout cannot be made clean on case-insensitive macOS because the old tree tracks both seed_M and seed_m. Local representations were preserved in stashes f8a374ec and 700da996 (plus pre-existing 6b0013); none were dropped or reapplied. Current origin/main is available read-only in detached worktree /Users/jemanuel/projects/franken_numpy__origin_main_20260712 at 6ac1c65d. Any fnp-random decision must pin an exact revision and must not mutate the original checkout.
close_reason: Landed in a7f25e4 (substrate) — the migration is split to bd-2cd1. DECISION (the bead's first half): REJECT fnp-random for the core RNG lane. It is nightly-only and no franken numeric lib supports wasm32, while scriptbots-core must build for wasm (scriptbots-web) — a core RNG dep that cannot compile for wasm would either break the browser build or fork the science lane in two. Its sole advantage is bit-exact NumPy PCG64DXSM parity, and this project's parity oracle is the legacy C++ ScriptBots, not NumPy; we would be paying a hard platform constraint for a guarantee we never need. The incumbent xoshiro256++ is already isolated behind RandomStream with a versioned algorithm id, a restorable checkpoint, and (bd-2z0.8.4) a pinned sequence golden so a rand bump cannot silently move the science. SUBSTRATE (the second half): RngDomain {Environment, Food, Population, Lineage, Mutation, Crossover} + versioned FNV-1a derivation over a STABLE STRING TAG (not the enum discriminant — inserting a variant mid-enum would otherwise silently re-seed every domain after it) + DomainStreams with per-domain checkpoint/restore that REFUSES a checkpoint missing a domain rather than re-deriving it (re-deriving would look like a successful restore while rewinding that one domain to tick zero, with every other domain resuming perfectly, so nothing downstream would notice the resumed run had begun re-rolling its mutations). 7 tests, headline: a thousand draws from FOOD must not change what MUTATION produces — the property a single shared stream cannot provide, and the reason 'same food layout, different mutation seed' is currently an unaskable experiment. NOT DONE: the ~51 call-site migration, which re-baselines every stochastic decision and MOVES the characterization digest, so it must be its own reviewable commit (same reasoning as bd-300o vs bd-16g.15.1). 205 core tests green; clippy -D warnings clean.

title: FrankenTorch brain family: batched cohort inference + hybrid evolution/gradient learning
description:
THE IDEA. Make scriptbots-brain-ml REAL with FrankenTorch: a dense f32 MLP brain family whose weights are a flat evolvable genome AND (optionally) receive lifetime gradient updates — the classic evolution+learning hybrid (Baldwin effect / Lamarckian variants) the original ScriptBots community always wanted but the C++ codebase could never host. Today brain-ml is an honest placeholder that copies inputs to outputs (crates/scriptbots-brain-ml/src/lib.rs:48-61 "ml.placeholder"), and the nearest real thing — NeuroflowBrain — is the weakest code in the brain stack: f64 inference with per-tick f32->f64 widening (brain-neuro lib.rs:513-517) and clone/mutation via whole-network serde_json round-trips (:482-495, :575-595).

WHY FRANKENTORCH AND NOT THE ALTERNATIVES (survey 2026-07-12; recorded so we never re-litigate):
- frankentorch: CPU eager PyTorch reimplementation, ~362k LOC, 5.6k tests, differential conformance vs PyTorch 2.12. f32-NATIVE storage (TensorStorage::F32(Arc<Vec<f32>>)); full tape autograd; ft-optim (SGD/Adam/AdamW/RMSprop + schedulers + grad clipping); ft-nn parameters_to_vector/vector_to_parameters (ft-nn lib.rs:823,853) — EXACTLY the genome flatten/unflatten primitive an evolutionary sim needs; "Deterministic Autograd Contract" doctrine; SIMD via `wide` + matrixmultiply GEMM; no BLAS, no tokio.
- Its OWN profiling honesty: per-op session dispatch dominates tiny ops (their 2026-05 ledger: elementwise 8-30x slower than torch per-op; 64x64 matmul 1.83x slower single-op) BUT batched tiny-matrix linalg is where it BEATS torch (batched f32 svdvals [100000,8,4] 39x, batched eigvalsh 5-7.5x). CONSEQUENCE: the integration MUST batch agents into [N,25]x[25,H] GEMMs per layer (or call session-free ft-kernel-cpu free functions), never issue per-agent session ops. A single 25x30 f32 matmul is ~1.5k MACs = sub-microsecond hand-rolled; microseconds of dispatch per agent would be a 10x regression.
- frankenjax REJECTED for this: self-described reference implementation; ~2.3-3.2us dispatch per jitted call; no optimizers; no parameters_to_vector; matmul only via primitive_with_params(Primitive::Dot). Rigorous AD oracle, wrong inner-loop engine.
- Candle/tract/tch (existing brain-ml feature plumbing): heavyweight external deps the plan's build budgets already fence off; bd-2z0.8.10 owns their assessment. FrankenTorch is in-house, pure Rust, and the only one whose small-batched regime is a demonstrated strength.

CONSTRAINTS. Git-only dependency (no crates.io releases, no tags) — exact rev pin per bd-2z0.8 protocol. Nightly-only — fine (workspace pins nightly-2026-07-09). Heavy compile units (ft-api lib.rs is 6.3MB) — the family lives behind a NON-DEFAULT feature (brain-ft) exactly like candle/tch flags today; default product build budgets untouched. No wasm (rayon-dependent) — irrelevant, scriptbots-web only builds brain(mlp). asupersync appears only in ft-serialize (hard) and ft-runtime (optional) — skip ft-serialize; our consumer graph is ft-api/ft-nn/ft-optim/ft-kernel-cpu.

RELATIONSHIP TO EXISTING BEADS. bd-2z0.8.10 (modernize ML backends behind honest adapters) keeps owning the candle/tract/tch/neuroflow dispositions — this epic ADDS the frankentorch family as the flagship adapter satisfying the same genome/evaluator/checkpoint/reproduction contract; bd-16g.12 (brain tournament) is the evaluation venue where FtBrain must EARN its place; bd-3gu (BrainBinding rehydration bug) must be fixed or accounted for before a new registered family ships; bd-2z0.3.7 owns honest registration.

CHILD STRUCTURE. admission (pin/license/build-budget) -> BatchBrain cohort substrate (core+brain, library-agnostic) -> FtBrain implementation -> hybrid lifetime learning -> bench+determinism gates -> e2e + tournament entry.
acceptance_criteria: Delivered admission and generic batch-substrate children bd-2z0.3.12.1-.2 remain closed. The epic closes only after .3 implements real packed cohort FtBrain inference and the complete versioned genome/evaluator contract, .4 implements deterministic off/Baldwin/Lamarck learning with persisted optimizer/birth-vs-learned state, .5 retains the full family performance/determinism matrix, and .6 proves headless survival, persistence, checkpoint continuation, learning A/B, and tournament ingestion. The brain-ft feature stays non-default and absent from default/WASM graphs. Every child retains exact source/toolchain/profile manifests, comprehensive unit and e2e logs, and typed gate verdicts; no open child or unverified performance claim remains.

title: BatchBrain cohort execution path in core+brain (library-agnostic substrate)
description:
WHY. The Brain trait is per-agent (tick(&inputs25) -> outputs9) and stage_brains parallelizes ACROSS agents with rayon (core lib.rs:6538-6596: runners pulled from bindings, par_iter_mut, results written back serially in handle order for determinism). Dense-net families (Neuroflow today, FtBrain next) leave large wins on the table: evaluating a cohort of same-architecture agents as ONE [N,25]x[25,H] GEMM per layer amortizes all dispatch and enables SIMD-dense inner loops. This substrate is deliberately LIBRARY-AGNOSTIC: it must benefit any dense family and carry zero frankentorch dependency (that is why it is not blocked by the admission bead).

DESIGN.
- New optional trait in scriptbots-brain (alongside Brain, lib.rs:217-287 BrainRunnerAdapter): BatchBrain { fn batch_tick(&mut self, inputs: &InputMatrix, outputs: &mut OutputMatrix, cohort: &[CohortSlot]) } where InputMatrix is a caller-owned [N,25] f32 slab (built from the existing work_* scratch-buffer discipline, core lib.rs:5523-5542 — extend, do not duplicate).
- stage_brains gains a cohort path: group agents by (brain_kind, architecture_key); families implementing BatchBrain get cohort evaluation; everything else takes the existing per-agent path UNCHANGED. Grouping and scatter both iterate in handle order => determinism preserved by construction.
- DETERMINISM CONTRACT (non-negotiable, test-enforced): batch and per-agent evaluation of the same family must produce BIT-IDENTICAL outputs for identical inputs (same accumulation order within a row; document the reduction order the family must honor), and results must be independent of cohort partitioning and thread count.
- Feature-gate the cohort path (batch-brains, default ON once proven — it is pure-Rust infrastructure; the gate exists for bisection, not protection).
- wasm: works identically (no rayon requirement in the trait; the wasm single-threaded path just calls batch_tick on the full cohort).
TESTS. Unit: grouping correctness across mixed populations (every agent evaluated exactly once, handle order preserved); bit-identity batch-vs-single on a reference dense family (write a tiny TestDenseBrain in-tree for this — do NOT wait for FtBrain); partition-independence (split cohort at every possible point, identical results); thread-count independence digests. Bench: criterion cohort-vs-per-agent on TestDenseBrain at 2k/5k/10k agents (this quantifies the substrate's headroom independent of frankentorch and gates the FtBrain bead's expectations). Logging: per-tick cohort stats (families, cohort sizes, batch path taken) at debug level.
ACCEPTANCE. Cohort path in tree, default per-agent behavior untouched when no family opts in; bit-identity + independence tests green; bench numbers recorded in the bead.
DEPS. Related bd-2z0.3.7 (registration), bd-3gu (rehydration bug — the cohort path must not widen that hole: cloned/deserialized runners must still rehydrate before cohort grouping or fail loudly).

title: FtBrain: dense f32 MLP with flat-genome weights via parameters_to_vector
description:
SCOPE. The actual FrankenTorch brain family in scriptbots-brain-ml behind brain-ft:
- Architecture: dense MLP 25 -> configurable hidden (default comparable to NeuroflowBrain's [48,32,24] for fair comparison) -> 9, f32 end-to-end, tanh hidden / sigmoid-or-tanh output heads matching the OutputChannel semantics (crates/scriptbots-core/src/channels.rs OutputChannel + SENSOR_LAYOUT — use the typed accessors, never raw indices; that module exists because a raw-index bug shipped for months).
- GENOME = FLAT VEC: weights live canonically as the flat Vec<f32> from ft-nn parameters_to_vector (lib.rs:823); vector_to_parameters (:853) materializes the network. Mutation: Gaussian perturbation with per-agent mutation-rate traits (mirror MlpBrain/Dwraon conventions: rates themselves heritable + meta-mutating); crossover: per-gene uniform crossover between parent genomes (document the choice vs per-layer crossover; per-gene matches legacy per-field spirit). Clone/checkpoint/reproduce = Vec<f32> copy + our own serde — ZERO serde_json round-trips (the NeuroflowBrain anti-pattern this family retires: brain-neuro lib.rs:482-595) and ZERO ft-serialize.
- INFERENCE PATH DECISION (made empirically, recorded here on close): (a) session-based batched forward — build [N,25] input tensor per cohort via BatchBrain, one tensor_matmul+activation chain per layer, tensor_values_f32 scatter; vs (b) session-FREE ft-kernel-cpu free functions (matmul_tensor_contiguous_f32 + hand activation loops) with weights as plain slabs, no tape at all. Bench both on the BatchBrain harness; ship the winner; keep the loser's code path deleted, not feature-rotted. title: Hybrid lifetime learning: gradient fine-tuning of FtBrain (Baldwin/Lamarck toggle)
description:
THE IDEA. Evolution sets the genome; LIFE fine-tunes it. Agents accumulate (state, action, reward) experience — reward = energy delta from eating/sharing/damage, the currency the sim already computes — and periodically take small gradient steps on their own weights via ft autograd + ft-optim. The evolutionary outer loop is unchanged. A config toggle decides inheritance: BALDWIN (default: offspring inherit the BIRTH genome — learning shapes selection but is not inherited) vs LAMARCK (offspring inherit learned weights). This is a publishable experimental axis (bd-16g.12 tournament: same family, learning on/off/lamarck as competitors) and the payoff that justifies frankentorch over a hand-rolled GEMM.

DESIGN DECISIONS (make explicitly, record here):
- Learning rule v1: REINFORCE-with-baseline over short horizons (episodic buffers of H ticks, advantage = reward-sum minus running baseline), NOT Q-learning/actor-critic — smallest credible rule, fewest moving parts, easy determinism. Supervised-imitation-of-elites considered and deferred (needs elite-trajectory storage; note as follow-up).
- Cadence + budget: learning steps run OUTSIDE the hot tick path — batched per-cohort every K ticks (K configurable, default ~120) inside stage_brains' cohort context, with a hard per-tick time budget; a learning step that would blow the budget defers, never stalls the tick. TPS gate: <=5% throughput cost at 1k agents with defaults, measured.
- Determinism: experience buffers, minibatch order, and optimizer state advance under seeded per-agent RNG streams (bd-2z0.3.10's domain-separated streams — add a "learning" domain); Deterministic Autograd Contract + fixed accumulation order => same seed, same trajectories, same learned weights. Digest test enforced across thread counts.
- Energy cost knob: optional metabolic price per learning step (learning literally costs energy) — off by default, but wired, because it makes the biology honest and the experiments richer.
- Persistence: optimizer state is evaluator-state under the versioned brain contract (checkpoint/restore exact); learned-vs-birth genome both persisted for Baldwin analysis (delta = what life taught — a first-class analytics column, feed the analytics quartet).
TESTS. Unit: REINFORCE gradient sign sanity on a rigged bandit world (reward for output>0.5 -> weight moves the right way within N steps, seeded); baseline reduces gradient variance (measured); buffer/optimizer checkpoint round-trip; Baldwin vs Lamarck inheritance paths produce the documented genome flows. Integration: 3-way A/B/A (off/baldwin/lamarck) matched-seed runs — learning-on cohorts must show measurably different (logged, not necessarily "better") behavior metrics; determinism digests. E2E hooks feed the family e2e bead. Logging: per-cohort learning-step spans (batch size, loss, grad-norm, clipped fraction, wall time) at debug; run-level learning summary metrics persisted for analytics.
ACCEPTANCE. Toggleable learning with all three modes; determinism proven; TPS budget met; experiment preset checked in (learning on/off/lamarck presets for bd-16g.12).
DEPS. Blocked by FtBrain. Related bd-2z0.3.10, bd-16g.12.
acceptance_criteria: Config exposes learning off, Baldwin, and Lamarck modes with off as an isolation baseline; Baldwin offspring inherit birth genomes and Lamarck offspring inherit learned weights exactly. A domain-separated learning RNG, fixed buffer/minibatch order, bounded cadence/time budget, gradient clipping, optional metabolic cost, and versioned optimizer/evaluator state make checkpoint continuation and 1-vs-8-thread digests exact. Unit tests cover seeded bandit gradient direction, baseline variance reduction, buffer and optimizer round-trip, inheritance flow, defer-on-budget, and NaN/overflow rejection. A matched-seed off/Baldwin/Lamarck e2e script retains manifests and detailed loss/advantage/grad-norm/clipping/defer/energy/genome-delta logs, proves learning changes behavior without assuming it improves fitness, and shows default learning cost at or below 5 percent TPS at 1k agents.

title: Canonicalize dense agent execution and spawn ordering by AgentUid
description: WorldDigestV1.1 now names dense execution order because several stages still iterate the arena's dense layout and reproduction queues carry parent_index. Equivalent stable-identity worlds restored into different slot layouts can therefore consume RNG or floating-point reductions in different orders. Remove that hidden allocation-layout dependency rather than treating dense order as permanent science state.
design: Introduce stable UID-ordered iteration views for every order-sensitive stage and remove parent_index from queued spawn semantics. Preserve dense SoA storage for locality, but make selection, RNG assignment, reductions whose rounding is observable, persistence projection, and queue commit order explicit. Use paired worlds with identical UID state and different slot/dense layouts as the executable oracle. comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text:
PROOF LANDED. The binding was already implemented (stage_spawn_commit: clone_runner -> crossover if partner -> mutate -> BrainBinding::inherited, with a hard MissingHeritableBrain error if a bound parent has no heritable brain). What this bead actually owed was EVIDENCE, and that is what landed.

THE MATCHED PAIR (both required; either alone is worthless):
  - mutation OFF -> child genome BIT-IDENTICAL to parent (compared via to_bits(), not by value: a re-randomized brain that landed nearby would pass a value comparison).
  - mutation ON  -> child genome DIFFERS (without this, the first test is satisfiable by a mutate() that does nothing, and a population that never mutates is as dead as one that never inherits).

WHY IT MATTERS: a re-randomizing spawn path is INVISIBLE. The population still looks alive; nothing goes red; the project has silently reverted from an evolution simulator to a random-restart simulator.

FIXTURE: HeritableBrain with real weights. The existing StubBrain is stateless and could not have proven anything — a spawn path that dropped the parent's brain and handed the child a fresh one looks identical through a stateless brain.

THE TEST REFUSES TO PASS VACUOUSLY: if the fixture never reproduces it fails loudly rather than asserting over an empty population. That guard fired three times while I built it (reproduction is DISABLED outright when reproduction_energy_threshold <= 0.0, and is separately gated by reproduction_attempt_interval/chance) — each time it told me the truth instead of going green.

REMAINING (not claimed, deliberately): the acceptance criteria also name genome-hash and mutation/crossover PROVENANCE fields, and a multi-generation fixture. The provenance harness (BrainGenomeEnvelope/BrainProvenance/OffspringStatePolicy) exists from bd-2z0.3.2 but is not yet asserted end-to-end through the spawn path, and the crossover path is covered only by the existing scheduled_crossover test. Those are worth their own pass; the core heredity claim is now proven rather than assumed.

title: Make scenario brain registration complete and honest
description: Register only brain families that fully implement evaluation, genome heredity, persistence, and checkpoint contracts; add MLP, DWRAON, and Assembly scenario selection; keep placeholder ML backends out of default populations.
design: No model-backend upgrades here. Candle/Tract/Tch/Neuroflow acceptance is separate dependency/family work. Plan sections 3.10 and 6.6.
acceptance_criteria: Default and curated scenarios name an installed honest family; selecting unavailable/placeholder ML returns a clear error; MLP/DWRAON/Assembly each survive spawn and reproduction smoke tests; advertised help/features match registration.
close_reason: Landed in 196f026. Found a LIVE defect, not a hygiene issue: ml.placeholder (tick copies sensors to outputs; mutate is a no-op returning Ok(())) was being seeded into the founding population of EVERY run — 'ml' is a default feature, and seed_agents round-robins founders across all registered families, so ~1/3 of founders were born unable to think or evolve and their descendants inherited it. Root cause is BrainRunner's own DEFAULTS: clone_runner()->Ok(None) and mutate()->Ok(()) mean a family that merely fails to override them is silently non-heritable while reporting success. That is a trait-design problem that MAKES placeholders invisible (EchoBrain is one register() call from the same fate). Fix: the registry now PROVES the contract instead of trusting it — a family must duplicate itself AND mutating that duplicate must actually change its behaviour (bitwise tick comparison at full mutation rate across several probe vectors). The second half is the one that matters: ml.placeholder CLONES honestly, only its mutation lies, so my first clone-only gate waved it through and my own test caught it. Non-heritable families stay registered for explicit selection but are WITHHELD from default populations with a warn! naming them; if no family carries heredity the app refuses to start rather than produce data about a population that is not evolving. 5 new integration tests (incl. a clones-but-never-mutates fixture) + a unit test driving the real install_brains under both feature configs. clippy -D warnings clean. The 4 storage failures in the suite are pre-existing on this target — verified on a clean tree.

comments.author: GoldenPanther
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND — AND IT IS DEEPER THAN THIS BEAD'S TITLE. Work is STASHED, not landed:
I could not compile (three independent blockers, below), and I will not leave unverified
code in a tree four agents share.

THE DEFECT IS IN THE TRAIT'S OWN DEFAULTS. `BrainRunner` (scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs:1220):

    fn clone_runner(&self) -> Result<Option<Box<dyn BrainRunner>>, BrainSpawnError> {
        Ok(None)     // <- default: silently NON-HERITABLE
    }
    fn mutate(&mut self, _rng, _rate, _scale) -> Result<(), BrainSpawnError> {
        Ok(())       // <- default: reports SUCCESS, changes NOTHING
    }

A family that merely fails to OVERRIDE these is silently non-heritable. `clone_runner`
returns Ok(None), so reproduction spawns a FRESH runner from the registry (the trait's own
doc comment says exactly this) and the child never receives its parent's brain — while
`mutate` returns Ok(()) having done nothing. Both are reported to the caller as success.
This is not a placeholder problem; it is a trait-design problem that MAKES placeholders
invisible. Any family added tomorrow inherits the same hole by omission.

WHAT ACTUALLY REACHES A POPULATION TODAY. `scriptbots-brain-ml::MlBrain` fell straight in:
  - kind() == "ml.placeholder"
  - tick(): "Placeholder: copy the first OUTPUT_SIZE sensors to outputs" — it is a WIRE,
    not a brain.
  - mutate(): a no-op returning Ok(()).
And `seed_agents` (scriptbots-app/src/main.rs) ROUND-ROBINS the founding population across
every registered key:
    let Some(&key) = brain_keys.get((row * 4 + col) % brain_keys.len())
So with `--features ml`, roughly a THIRD of the 16 founders are born with a brain that can
neither think nor evolve, their descendants inherit it, and nothing downstream says a word.
Every experiment run under that feature is contaminated. bd-2z0.3.6's heredity proof
(mutation off -> bit-identical, on -> differs) holds for MlpBrain and would FAIL for these,
which is precisely why the proof must be run per-family rather than once.

A SECOND SILENT PLACEHOLDER: `EchoBrain` (scriptbots-brain/src/lib.rs:179) has the same
no-op mutate. It is not in install_brains today, but it is one `register()` call away.

THE FIX I WROTE (stashed; see `git stash list`, the GoldenPanther bd-2z0.3.7 entry):
Do not TRUST a family's declaration — PROVE the contract. `probe_heredity()` asks each
family to duplicate itself before it is allowed to found a population:
  Ok(Some(_)) -> heritable; eligible to seed.
  Ok(None)    -> non-heritable BY ITS OWN ANSWER; stays registered for explicit selection
                 but is WITHHELD from the founding population, with a warn! naming it.
  Err(_)      -> a BROKEN family (it tried to clone and failed). Refuse to register at all:
                 otherwise reproduction aborts at some unpredictable later tick instead of
                 at startup.
`install_brains` returns { population, withheld } and all five call sites seed only from
`population`. If NO family carries heredity, the app refuses to start rather than produce
plausible-looking data that answers nothing.

This is behaviour-based, so it is strictly better than a self-declared capability flag: the
registry verifies the contract instead of believing a boolean that the next placeholder
author will also forget to set.

WHY IT IS NOT LANDED — THREE STACKED BLOCKERS, none of them this bead's fault:
 1. bd-2tse: RCH declines to offload this checkout, and the local fallback cannot link
    (no mold, linux target on a mac).
 2. The Data volume is 100% FULL (413Gi used; ~200Mi free), so native builds die on ENOSPC.
    My own scratch is cleaned up (167M) — the 413Gi is ~/Library (171G) and ~/projects (69G).
 3. NEW, and it blocks EVERY build in the workspace: `cargo check` cannot even RESOLVE the
    dependency graph —
      error: failed to get `ft-api` as a dependency of package `scriptbots-brain-ml`
      unable to update https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/frankentorch?rev=e4c6bdd...
      could not open '.../cargo-home/git/checkouts/frankentorch-.../artifacts/perf/
      frankentorch-5oqum/pass10_current_head_eigvalsh_components_remote.log' for writing:
      No such file or directory
    Someone added an ft-api/frankentorch dependency to brain-ml and its git checkout in the
    SHARED cargo-home is corrupt. This is not feature-gated away: cargo must fetch the
    source to read its manifest, so it breaks resolution for the whole workspace.

NEXT AGENT: `git stash apply` the entry above, then VERIFY the two registry APIs I assumed
but never compiled — `world.brain_registry().label(key)` and `.spawn(key, &mut rng)`. If
they do not exist under those names, the shape of the fix is still right; only the lookup
needs adjusting. Then add the test this bead owes: with `--features ml`, assert NO founder
is bound to `ml.placeholder`, and assert the eligible set is non-empty (without the second
assertion the first passes vacuously on a world with no brains at all).

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text: Largely landed at commit e2d9aaa (2026-07-12, GoldenPanther): activation snapshots are now demand-driven — stage_brains captures only for agents with SelectionState != None or matching the new WorldState::set_activation_probe(Option<AgentId>) hook (the TUI sets the probe for its focused agent each refresh; GPUI selection flows through SelectionState). Everyone else gets brain_activations = None each tick, eliminating the per-agent per-tick layer allocations (Neuroflow serialized its whole network to JSON per agent per tick). STILL OPEN from this bead: the 'bounded' half — no size cap on a captured snapshot (a pathological layer count/size is unbounded), no staleness contract documented for the one-tick probe lag, and multi-consumer probes (TUI + REST inspector simultaneously) take last-writer-wins on a single Option — decide whether a small probe set is needed.

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text:
INTROSPECTION BOUNDS LANDED (GoldenPanther, commits 0c492d1 + b1764cd); this bead stays OPEN because its remaining scope (per-client projections) genuinely depends on bd-2z0.3.7 and bd-2z0.4.8, which br correctly refused to let me close past.

What is done - introspection is now demand-driven AND bounded on all three axes:
1. DEMAND-DRIVEN: activations are captured only for the agent a frontend probes (new WorldState::set_activation_probe, wired to the TUI focused agent and the GPUI inspector focused agent) plus selected agents. Everyone else gets None each tick, eliminating the per-agent per-tick layer allocations (Neuroflow serialized its entire network to JSON, per agent, per tick).
2. COUNT-BOUNDED: ACTIVATION_CAPTURE_BUDGET (8) caps selected-agent capture. This closes a real regression I introduced: select_all_agents in the GPUI palette marks EVERY agent Selected, so a single keystroke would otherwise have reinstated population-wide capture.
3. SIZE-BOUNDED: ACTIVATION_VALUE_BUDGET (4096) caps a SINGLE snapshot. Bounding the agent count is not enough because brain topology is CONFIGURATION - a Neuroflow net can declare arbitrarily wide hidden layers, so one inspected agent could copy megabytes out of the sim every tick. Clipped snapshots keep whole layers (half a layer is a lie about the network's shape), drop edges dangling into dropped layers, and set BrainActivations::truncated so a UI can say the view is clipped rather than implying the brain is shallow.

What remains for this bead: the multi-consumer story (the probe is a single Option, so two simultaneous inspectors are last-writer-wins) and the staleness contract for the one-tick probe lag - both of which belong with the per-client projections in bd-2z0.4.8.

title: Characterize and specify command semantics
description: Freeze executable evidence and the target semantics for every playback, configuration, selection, shutdown, and overload path before changing runtime ownership. Correct the stale audit claim: the current TerminalApp single-step path calls advance_simulation with single_step=true and does not enqueue a second step, so live and headless TUI must be recorded as a one-step green control. Add focused red reproductions for the actual failures: two GPUI SimulationView instances can independently step one world and leave playback commands stuck in the inner WorldState queue; Bevy local control plus later command draining can make a request advance one or two ticks; mixed ControlCommand classes take immediate versus deferred paths and can violate enqueue order; optimistic frontend state can diverge when the capacity-32 queue rejects; and shutdown can strand pending commands without terminal status.
design: Characterization and specification only; do not replace the runtime in this bead. Specify one bounded CommandEnvelope stream ordered by host-assigned AdmissionSequence. No command-class subqueue, reorder, drop, or coalescing is allowed unless the protocol names and tests an equivalence rule. At each boundary, apply admitted envelopes strictly in sequence. Step atomically pauses, performs exactly one pure scientific transition at its position in the order, and remains paused unless a later envelope changes playback; an explicit Step also suppresses an implicit cadence tick in that same boundary. With manual time frozen, Step then Resume means one tick and final Running, while Resume then Step means one tick and final Paused. Rejected and failed envelopes still receive queryable terminal application status; admission, application, journal commit, and crash durability remain distinct.
acceptance_criteria: Executable characterization proves the current TUI live and headless single-step each advance exactly once and removes the false TUI double-step expectation. Focused tests fail for GPUI two-view stepping and stuck playback commands, Bevy one-or-two-step behavior, mixed-class reordering, optimistic queue-full divergence, and shutdown with pending work. A checked target truth table covers Pause, Resume, Speed, Step, config, selection, auto-pause, duplicate CommandId, expected-revision conflict, disconnected clients, queue sizes 1/32/33/1000, and shutdown. It explicitly asserts Step-then-Resume and Resume-then-Step results, when ControlRevision changes, when a science tick may run, and which application and journal status each case returns.
notes: Source evidence at the 2b1c874 baseline: terminal/mod.rs applies drained playback commands and step_once calls advance_simulation directly; render/src/lib.rs gives each SimulationView its own accumulator and steps after only the outer command drain; bevy/src/lib.rs mirrors playback into local state and separately drains WorldState simulation commands; command.rs drops on bounded queue full; control.rs returns a projected config before the queued update is applied. This bead records facts and target policy, not implementation.

title: Make FrankenSQLite persistence bounded, fail-closed, and cancel-clean
description: Extend the existing thread-owned FrankenSQLite worker into the production bounded journal adapter for HostCore. Admission from the host is nonblocking; on queue-full or disconnected rejection the host retains the exact completed batch, latches a visible fault, and advances no later scientific tick until explicit retry. The worker alone creates, uses, closes, and drops fsqlite::Connection and returns typed per-batch, flush, and shutdown acknowledgements.
design: Model and test fault points at admission, worker receive, begin, each statement/table, commit, rollback, post-commit/pre-ack, analytics publication, flush/checkpoint, shutdown, and reopen. Maintain explicit batch/event-sequence watermarks for admitted, applied-to-journal, committed-volatile, and durable progress; never infer one from queue success. ApplicationState remains owned by HostCore and is not rewritten by storage. JournalState becomes CommittedVolatile for memory mode and can never become Durable. File mode may emit Durable only for the exact proven transaction/watermark semantics. Implement a durable outbox/per-batch applied-durable watermark if needed; otherwise document the precise crash-loss window, keep affected statuses Pending or non-durable, and make every API/UI claim reflect that limitation.
acceptance_criteria: Capacity and slow/failing-worker tests prove bounded memory, nonblocking admission, exact retained-batch retry, pause-before-loss, and fail-closed timeout. Fault injection at every defined boundary yields a deterministic status and leaves no active transaction or silently lost lifecycle/command event. Memory-mode flush/shutdown receipts are CommittedVolatile and never Durable. For every file-mode status reported Durable, close/crash-boundary simulation plus independent reopen finds exactly the acknowledged commands/events through the durable watermark and passes integrity/order checks. A post-commit/pre-ack test proves idempotent recovery without duplicate effects, or the implementation withholds Durable and records the exact remaining crash-loss limitation. Shutdown is cancel-clean and reports flush failure/timeout rather than logging success.
notes: This bead builds on the current bounded StoragePipeline and .8.9.4 worker ownership work; it does not move a Connection across threads or add another database engine. Durable outbox and per-batch watermarks are requirements to prove, not assumptions that may be inferred from current enqueue, flush, or analytics behavior.

title: Asupersync channel spine: command bus + snapshot watch bus replace crossfire/std-mpsc
description:
WHY. bd-2z0.4.3 (CLOSED) already decided the direction: asupersync (pinned =0.3.6 at decision time; caret-unifies with fsqlite's 0.3.x — verify current lock resolution at execution) with the layering scriptbots-core <- scriptbots-runtime <- storage/app/frontends. This bead IMPLEMENTS the channel half of that decision as the production buses, replacing the current zoo: crossfire mpmc for control commands, std::sync::mpsc for Bevy snapshots (crates/scriptbots-bevy/src/lib.rs:69,196, ~30ms cadence), tokio::watch for shutdown on sim-side crates.

CROSSFIRE FOOTPRINT (verified 2026-07-12 — it is THREE files, not one; scope all of them): crates/scriptbots-app/Cargo.toml:33 declares crossfire 2.1.6; usage in src/command.rs (bus definition + tick-loop drain, :12-58), src/servers.rs (control-plane senders from REST/MCP handlers), src/control.rs (plumbing/adapters). All three sites migrate together; the public command-receipt semantics they implement must not change.

SURVEY FACTS THAT MAKE THIS FIT (recorded so nobody re-verifies): asupersync channels have SYNCHRONOUS non-blocking paths usable from plain threads — bounded mpsc try_send/try_recv are sync; UNBOUNDED mpsc send(value) and watch send(value) are fully synchronous (no Cx needed). Async consumers use recv(&cx)/changed(&cx). Two-phase reserve/commit (tx.reserve(&cx) then permit.send(v), commit infallible, dropped permit aborts cleanly) means cancellation can never half-send — use it wherever loss-on-cancel matters.

SCOPE.
1. Command bus: control plane (tokio thread) -> sim. Replace crossfire with asupersync bounded mpsc; producers use sync try_send (works fine from inside a tokio runtime because it never awaits); the tick loop drains with try_recv in a bounded loop exactly as today. Backpressure policy preserved: bounded capacity, reject-with-receipt on full (command receipts are bd-2z0.4.x protocol; do not regress them).
2. Snapshot bus: sim -> renderers. Replace the Bevy std::mpsc with asupersync watch: LATEST-VALUE semantics are semantically better than a queue for render snapshots (renderer wants freshest state; stale intermediates are waste). Sender side is sync send(value) from the snapshot worker. NOTE the relationship to bd-2z0.4.7 (immutable multi-subscriber snapshots with per-consumer cursors): .4.7 owns the product-grade multi-subscriber design; this bead may land as the Bevy-path stepping stone, and MUST converge with .4.7's SnapshotBus rather than fork a competitor — coordinate before implementing if .4.7 has started (see the comment left on .4.7: one watch does NOT satisfy per-consumer cursors; broadcast or per-class watch are the candidates there).
3. Shutdown: single asupersync watch<Shutdown> replacing ad-hoc flags/tokio-watch on sim-side crates (tokio stays inside the axum control thread; the boundary object is the bus, not the runtime).
4. Determinism: command drain order must remain stable given identical send order (single consumer, FIFO per channel — assert in tests); the tick loop never awaits.
5. Pin policy: bd-2z0.4.3 chose "=0.3.6" — decide HERE (with the single-universe guard bead as safety net) whether to keep exact or widen to a caret floor so fsqlite/fastmcp can float within 0.3.x without forcing a split universe; record the outcome in both beads.

TESTS (unit + integration, tracing throughout: channel depth gauges, drop/reject counters, per-bus spans).
- FIFO + capacity + reject-on-full semantics per bus; cross-runtime send (from a real tokio runtime thread) does not panic/starve.
- watch semantics: slow consumer sees only latest; no unbounded memory; sender never blocks.
- Cancellation: two-phase reserve dropped mid-send leaves channel consistent (no phantom command).
- Shutdown ordering: buses drain-then-close without losing acknowledged commands; consumers observe closure as typed disconnect.
- Determinism regression: seeded run with scripted command schedule produces identical tick-by-tick world digests before/after this change (reuse the existing digest harness).
ACCEPTANCE. crossfire gone from scriptbots-app/Cargo.toml and all three source files; command receipts + digests byte-identical; exactly one asupersync version in Cargo.lock.
DEPS. Blocked by bd-2z0.4.6 (the native lifecycle driver these buses feed); related bd-2z0.4.7, bd-2z0.4.9, bd-2z0.8.7.1 (fastmcp shares the same Cx universe).

title: Region-owned background services and structured shutdown (no detached threads)
description:
WHY. Today background work is detached-by-convention: the storage worker thread (crates/scriptbots-storage/src/lib.rs:4424), Bevy sim + snapshot threads (scriptbots-bevy/src/lib.rs:4107), the tokio control thread (scriptbots-app/src/servers.rs:236-244), autosave/screenshot helpers. Shutdown correctness is per-site hand-rolled (and bd-3bd shows the failure mode: storage Drop::flush during unwind can double-panic). asupersync's region model makes ownership structural: every task/thread bridge is owned by a region; closing a region GUARANTEES children complete, finalizers run, obligations resolve — no orphans possible. FrankenSQLite itself is the flagship precedent: its whole DB lifetime is a region tree (DbRootRegion -> coordinator/GC/replication regions, per-connection child regions), with spawn_blocking + mpsc + oneshot as the worker pattern. We should embed the same way.

SCOPE.
- AppRoot region owned by the app entrypoints (GPUI, terminal, Bevy, headless): child regions for (a) storage pipeline bridge (the worker THREAD stays a thread — Connection is !Send — but its command channel + join handle become a region-owned resource with a finalizer that performs drain-to-durable-watermark before close), (b) snapshot publisher, (c) control-server bridge (tokio runtime handle wrapped so app shutdown closes the region, which signals axum graceful shutdown), (d) autosave/maintenance tasks.
- Shutdown sequence becomes: close AppRoot -> regions drain in dependency order -> storage finalizer flushes outbox to durable watermark and joins the worker -> report per-region Outcome (Ok/Err/Cancelled/Panicked) in the exit log. Kill the bd-3bd class: finalizers run on the orderly path; Drop remains a last-resort guard with thread::panicking() check.
- Budgeted teardown: each finalizer gets an explicit cleanup budget (bounded drain), so a wedged worker cannot hang exit forever; budget exhaustion is a loud, typed failure in logs.
TESTS.
- Structured-shutdown integration test per frontend composition (headless at minimum, terminal if PTY harness allows): start all services, inject load, close root, assert (1) zero surviving threads via before/after thread inventory, (2) storage durable watermark == last admitted batch, (3) every region reports an Outcome, logged.
- Cancellation storm: repeatedly cancel mid-flush at randomized points (seeded); durability invariants hold every time.
- Wedged-worker: block the storage worker artificially; assert budgeted teardown fires, exit completes, failure is loudly logged and non-zero-exit.
- Detailed logging is a deliverable: a single "shutdown report" tracing event with per-region outcomes and durations.
ACCEPTANCE. No detached background primitives remain in app composition paths (grep-able: thread::spawn outside region wrappers is CI-flagged with an allowlist); shutdown report present in all frontends; bd-3bd scenario covered by test.
DEPS. Blocked by the channel-spine bead and bd-2z0.4.10 (bounded fail-closed persistence adapter is what the storage finalizer drains); related bd-3bd.
notes: LANDED (9bb431fd7 + follow-ups through 9f3573f53): (1) AppRoot harness in crates/scriptbots-app/src/regions.rs using asupersync semantic types (Budget/Outcome/CancelReason) — child regions register with an explicit teardown budget and an orderly-path finalizer; close() runs finalizers in reverse dependency order with per-region Outcome logging (Ok/Err/Cancelled/Panicked + elapsed + budget state), panic isolation per region, and typed Cancelled instead of an unbounded hang. (2) The interactive path closes control-server before storage-pipeline (producers quiesce before the durable watermark advances); storage errors keep precedence via prefer_storage_failure. (3) bd-3bd kill: StoragePipeline::drop checks thread::panicking() and hands the worker to the reaper WITHOUT flushing on the unwind path; the orderly region finalizer owns the drain. (4) Structured-shutdown integration test (tests/regions_shutdown.rs): real services (ephemeral control runtime + file-backed pipeline + one admitted science tick) asserting ordered outcomes for every registered region, converged admitted/applied/durable watermarks equal to the last admitted batch, and max_tick == 1 committed. title: Cx::scoped_cpu spike: cancellable fork-join alternative to rayon for tick stages
description:
CONTEXT. asupersync recently landed Cx::scoped_cpu(worker_cap, f) (upstream src/cx/scoped_cpu.rs, commit fa371dcf2, 2026-07): lending fork-join scoped threads that BORROW run-local state (no Arc/'static tax), std::thread::scope-style, where each worker holds a CpuCx whose checkpoint() observes cancellation and budget exhaustion. The module doc names "data-parallel fork-join kernels (the FrankenSim TilePool class of consumer)" as the motivating workload — i.e., built for exactly our shape. It is NOT a work-stealing par_iter: you write the band/tile partitioning yourself.

TODAY: rayon `parallel` feature is default-on in scriptbots-core; collect_handles! par_iter with min_len (core lib.rs:64-74), par_chunks_mut food rows (:5843), par_iter_mut brain jobs (:6596); pool capped via configure_parallelism (:143-175). This works. The spike question is whether scoped_cpu's cancellation/budget checkpoints + borrowed-state ergonomics are worth owning our own partitioning for SOME stages — e.g. abandoning a mid-tick stage cleanly on shutdown, or budget-bounding a pathological sense stage — WITHOUT losing throughput.

SCOPE (bounded spike, decision recorded, feature-gated `asupersync_cpu`, never default, never wasm).
- Port ONE stage (stage_sense, the heaviest: 25 sensors x 4 eyes over grid buckets, core lib.rs:6080-6462) to scoped_cpu with explicit band partitioning mirroring par_min_split semantics.
- Criterion A/B at 2k/5k/10k agents (SB_BENCH_AGENTS harness, benches/world_bench.rs), matched thread caps; assert bit-identical world digests vs rayon path (determinism gate — same reduction order or provably order-independent writes).
- Measure: throughput delta, cancellation latency (issue cancel mid-stage, time to quiesce), code complexity delta (LOC, review burden).
- DECISION RULE (pre-registered): adopt-for-stage only if throughput within 5% of rayon AND cancellation adds a capability we actually schedule (structured shutdown mid-tick). Otherwise: document numbers, close as rejected, keep rayon; the writeup itself is the deliverable either way.
TESTS. Digest-equality across implementations and thread counts; cancellation mid-stage leaves world state consistent (stage is all-or-nothing at the scratch-buffer commit point); bench logs archived in the bead on close.
DEPS. Blocked by the channel-spine bead (direct asupersync dependency arrives there); related bd-h33 (perf program owns the TPS ledger this must not regress).
close_reason: Completed Cx::scoped_cpu vs Rayon spike evaluation (docs/scoped_cpu_cancellation_spike_decision.md): rejected replacing Rayon for hot-loop tick stages; retained Rayon work-stealing for higher throughput and lower code complexity

title: Extract command and storage side effects from core step
description: After the command-semantics characterization, turn one core science transition into a pure explicit operation. Remove simulation-command queue ownership and synchronous WorldPersistence calls from WorldState::step. Accept validated boundary inputs and return a deterministic StepOutcome carrying the current summary, domain and lifecycle records, dirty/revision signals, digest inputs, and persistence projection data needed by the host. A completed scientific transition must not await I/O, depend on a renderer, or change because a later storage admission fails.
design: Land as a reviewed integration series rather than one giant rewrite: characterize all side effects; introduce StepOutcome alongside the old call path; move command application to explicit boundary inputs; move persistence projection/admission after the transition; then retire the internal queues through normal source edits only. Keep StepOutcome compact and renderer/storage-engine neutral: it must not clone a full RenderSnapshot or expose FrankenSQLite types. Gate every slice against the fixed WorldDigestV1 trace and corrected lifecycle-accounting fixtures. This is a semantic boundary extraction, not a mechanical module split or the HostCore implementation.
acceptance_criteria: WorldState owns no transport queue and one pure step performs no filesystem, database, channel, clock, or renderer I/O. Fixed inputs produce the same V1 state/stage digests, summaries, births, deaths, combat records, and resource accounting before and after each integration slice. A fault injected after StepOutcome returns cannot alter or roll back the completed scientific state. Tests cover empty and nonempty outcomes, multiple events between persistence intervals, a rejected downstream batch, serial/parallel supported lanes, and the applicable feature matrix. StepOutcome contains enough information for .4.5 host publication and .4.10 journaling without rereading mutable world state.
notes: Depends on .4.1 so the extraction cannot accidentally preserve the current renderer-specific order as the target contract. Existing .2.5, .2.8, and .3.9 prerequisites remain authoritative. Non-goals: final scheduling, channel selection, snapshot projection, storage durability, visual frontend migration, and physical file/module extraction.

description: Decide the enforceable runtime dependency direction and whether a new scriptbots-runtime crate is justified, then run a bounded Asupersync channel/cancellation/blocking-boundary spike against the protocol needs from .4.1. Runtime may depend on core and small selected scheduling primitives; it must not depend on FrankenSQLite, Axum/Tokio servers, GPUI, Bevy, Ratatui/FrankenTUI, or application composition.
