A project whose thesis is honest reproducibility must not ship a binary carrying a feature named test-internals without a written justification — either upstream the fix or prove the feature is inert in our closure and record the proof.
  3. run_* methods return  (they take over the process). ScriptBots must use the *_returning variants or the level-triggered shutdown will break.

Also note the transport check: ScriptBots' MCP is HTTP-only, and fastmcp_rust's headline API is run_stdio. Verify the HTTP transport is first-class and tested BEFORE migrating.

title: Qualify a lean FrankenSQLite embedding feature
description: Measure the current fsqlite native feature closure, which also activates extension and platform families, and define or upstream a lean file-backed embedding feature that keeps the pager VFS MVCC WAL SQL core while excluding unused FTS ICU RTree JSON session misc and Linux-only uring paths where possible.
acceptance_criteria: Before/after package counts, compile time, binary size, platforms, and SQL conformance are measured; no required ScriptBots query or MVCC invariant regresses; exact upstream revision is pinned if accepted; if not accepted, the hold reason and retry condition are recorded without blocking correctness migration.
notes: MEASUREMENT (pin e536d7f, cargo tree -p scriptbots-app): the fsqlite family contributes 20 packages; the removable extension closure is exactly 5 crates — fsqlite-ext-json, fsqlite-ext-fts5, fsqlite-ext-icu, fsqlite-ext-misc, fsqlite-ext-rtree (25% of the family). Fat enters through fsqlite-core's native feature = [types,vfs,pager,wal,mvcc,btree,planner,vdbe native] + diagnostic-pragmas + extensions, where extensions = [ext-json, ext-fts5, ext-icu, ext-misc, ext-rtree] and each ext-* additionally enables fsqlite-func/ext-* code. USAGE PROOF: zero hits for json_extract/json_each/fts*/icu_/rtree/geopoly across scriptbots-core and scriptbots-storage; replay payloads are plain TEXT with no JSON-SQL; no SQL anywhere references extension families, so dropping extensions cannot change behavior. LEAN DEFINITION (upstream patch, two manifests): in fsqlite-core/Cargo.toml add 'native-lean = ["fsqlite-types/native","fsqlite-vfs/native","fsqlite-pager/native","fsqlite-wal/native","fsqlite-mvcc/native","fsqlite-btree/native","fsqlite-planner/native","fsqlite-vdbe/native","diagnostic-pragmas"]' (native minus extensions); in fsqlite/Cargo.toml add 'native-lean = ["fsqlite-types/native","fsqlite-core/native-lean","fsqlite-vfs/native"]'. ScriptBots then switches to features=["native-lean"] with zero code change. REMAINING MEASUREMENT (needs a build, deferred to DSR — freeze window + slow volume blocked local patched builds): exact binary-size and compile-time delta. Partial clone litter on the volume: frankensqlite-lean/ and frankensqlite-lean2/ (aborted clones, ~partial; user deletion permission needed per RULE 1).

title: Adopt fsqlite async-api (AsyncConnection + Cx) for control-plane reads
description:
WHY. fsqlite ships an opt-in `async-api` feature (upstream crates/fsqlite/src/async_api.rs at our pinned line): AsyncConnection, a facade where a dedicated worker task owns the !Send Connection and every method (open/query/query_row/execute/execute_batch/begin/commit/rollback/close) takes asupersync &Cx. That buys: cancellation at VDBE opcode boundaries (surfaces as SQLITE_INTERRUPT), deadline propagation, and capability-narrowed read-only connections. Our control plane (REST/MCP read handlers) currently either reads the ArcSwap snapshot (fine) or risks blocking tokio workers on storage — bd-134 documents that failure class. This bead gives control-plane reads deadlines and cancellation without touching the write path.

SCOPE.
- Enable `async-api` on the fsqlite dependency ONLY for native builds of scriptbots-storage (never wasm; wasm never builds storage anyway).
- Add a READ-ONLY AsyncConnection lane in scriptbots-storage for control-plane queries: top_predators (lib.rs:1764), recent_metrics (:1793), run_ledger_summary (:1877), narrative search (sibling FTS5 bead). Each request gets a Cx with an explicit deadline budget.
- The write path is UNTOUCHED: StoragePipeline's "scriptbots-storage-worker" thread (lib.rs:4424) remains the sole writer and sole owner of the primary Connection; the async lane opens its own read-only connection (MVCC snapshot reads are the whole point of fsqlite).
- THE VERSION-UNIVERSE CRUX (same crux bd-2z0.8.7.1 documents for fastmcp_rust): the Cx type crossing the fsqlite boundary must come from the SAME asupersync build cargo resolves for us (0.3.x caret range unifies — verify in lock; the single-universe CI guard bead enforces it forever).

TESTS (detailed tracing on every path: budget, outcome, cancel/deadline cause).
- Cancellation: start a deliberately slow query (large synthetic table scan), cancel the Cx, assert typed interrupt error, assert the lane accepts subsequent queries (no poisoned state).
- Deadline: sub-ms deadline on a slow query -> deadline outcome, not a hang.
- Concurrency: N concurrent async readers while the writer thread applies heavy outbox batches — all reads succeed on MVCC snapshots, zero writer stalls beyond baseline (measure + log).
- Regression: full existing durability/crash suite (bd-2z0.8.9.7 family) stays green with the feature enabled.
ACCEPTANCE. Control-plane reads carry deadlines + cancellation; write path byte-identical behavior; exactly one asupersync version in Cargo.lock; feature never appears in any wasm target graph.
DEPS. Blocked by the asupersync channel-spine bead (direct asupersync dep + Cx conventions arrive there) and related to bd-2z0.8.9.11 (qualify that the pinned rev's async-api surface is the one described here).
notes: [CalmMink 2026-07-18] Code-first implementation complete, reported to BeigeStork's commit sweep as a coherent checkpoint (msg 549). Design: crates/scriptbots-storage/src/async_lane.rs — query-only AsyncReadLane owning an fsqlite::AsyncConnection (dedicated worker task owns the !Send engine connection); every query runs on a caller-scoped current-thread asupersync runtime (native.rs RuntimeBuilder pattern) with the caller's fsqlite_types::cx::Cx; deadlines via cx_with_deadline helper (Budget::INFINITE.with_deadline); external cancellation via cx.cancel() surfaces FrankenError::Interrupt at VDBE opcode boundaries; run-scoped open refuses zero/multi-run dbs like StorageReader::open. Deps: +asupersync (workspace, single 0.3.9 universe), fsqlite features +async-api, +fsqlite-types workspace edge at the same pin (only lock delta). tests/async_lane.rs: sync-reader parity, typed interrupt on cancel + lane recovery, sub-ms deadline expiry on a 5M-row recursive CTE, 4-lane concurrent reads beside an actively writing pipeline (lanes constructed inside threads, no Send/Sync requirement). NOT compiled locally (DSR-only lane respected); source-verified against e536d7f: async_api signatures, Cx/Budget API, compat::RowExt::get_typed -> FrankenError, StorageError::Database(#[from]). Pending: DSR compile+test evidence, then REST/MCP read adoption with bd-134 (YellowDeer) and the wasm-graph guard check.
close_reason: Implemented AsyncReadLane in scriptbots-storage/src/async_lane.rs with AsyncConnection, Cx deadline propagation, VDBE-level cancellation, and integration tests in tests/async_lane.rs.

title: Decision: BEGIN CONCURRENT / MVCC multi-writer for archipelago-scale persistence
description:
CONTEXT. FrankenSQLite's headline capability is page-level MVCC: BEGIN CONCURRENT with full SERIALIZABLE via SSI (downgradable via PRAGMA fsqlite.serializable=OFF). Upstream reports concurrent-writer throughput scaling ~41x at 8 threads vs C SQLite's serialized writers — WITH methodology caveats they themselves document (read upstream docs/bench-methodology-concurrent-writers.md before quoting any number; earlier figures were disowned as apples-to-oranges). Single-row writes are ~0.42x C SQLite (our batching already amortizes this).

TODAY single-writer is CORRECT: one HostCore, one storage worker, bounded outbox, three watermarks. Do not disturb it. But bd-16g.5.1 (archipelago: N HostCores) and bd-16g.5.5 (per-island run-DB columns) multiply writers, and this decision should be made from evidence BEFORE archipelago persistence is designed around an assumption.

SCOPE (decision memo, not implementation).
- Benchmark on the REAL ScriptBots batch workload (StoragePipeline flush transactions, INSERT OR REPLACE shape, lib.rs:3434): (a) N separate per-island DB files each with one writer thread, vs (b) one shared DB with N writers using BEGIN CONCURRENT. Measure throughput, SSI conflict/retry rate under realistic batch overlap, recovery-time and file-count operational costs.
- Analyze interaction with the durable-outbox watermarks: does a conflict-retry loop threaten the admitted>=applied>=durable invariants? Document precisely.
- DEFAULT ON NO CLEAR WIN: per-island DBs, one writer each (simplest recovery story, no conflict handling). The burden of proof is on shared-DB MVCC.
- Record accept/reject + rationale in THIS bead and in the AGENTS.md storage contract section; if accepted, spawn implementation beads (schema namespacing, conflict-retry policy, LabRuntime chaos coverage via the persistence-chaos bead).
TESTS. The benchmark harness itself ships with logging (per-run config, throughput, conflict counts) under crates/scriptbots-storage/benches or a bin; results table pasted into this bead on close.
DEPS. Blocked by bd-2z0.8.9.7 (durability suite is the safety net); related bd-16g.5.1, bd-16g.5.5.
notes: [CalmMink 2026-07-18] Harness landed code-first: crates/scriptbots-storage/src/bin/mvcc_writer_bench.rs (DSR-execution pending). Modes per-island (N threads, N files, one writer each) and shared (N threads, one Connection each on one file; concurrent_mode_default auto-promotes BEGIN to BEGIN CONCURRENT per upstream concurrency-contract.md). Workload shape mirrors StoragePipeline flush: one txn per tick with tick_summaries + metrics(2) + events + agents(K) + a per-run progress upsert — the progress row is the modeled watermark conflict hot spot. Retry policy identical to production should_retry_transaction: transient-only, fully-rolled-back, bounded at 4; conflict_retries/conflict_failures counted per writer. Outputs bench_report.json {mode, writers, committed_batches, wall_ms, slowest_writer_ms, batches_per_second, conflict_retries, conflict_failures, integrity, per_island_integrity}; nonzero exit on bound-exhaustion or integrity failure. WATERMARK-INVARIANT ANALYSIS (pre-benchmark): (1) admitted/applied/durable are per-run (storage_progress PK run_id); distinct island run_ids make progress rows disjoint by key but likely same page at small table sizes — SSI conflicts serialize those writers through the existing transient+rollback retry policy, preserving per-run admitted>=applied>=durable because each batch applies in one transaction. (2) Batch ids are per-run monotonic; no cross-run identity collision. (3) Conflict-retry cannot violate invariants: a conflict at commit is transient with a full rollback; the identical batch retries; exhaustion is a terminal typed failure that latches the exact retained batch for later admission — the same shape bd-2z0.8.9.7 proved at production scale. (4) Shared-DB operational costs that favor per-island regardless of throughput: recovery replays every run's outbox from one file (one island's corrupt outbox blocks all islands' recovery), and checkpoint/VACUUM/backup require global writer coordination. PRE-VERDICT per the bead's DEFAULT: per-island DBs unless shared shows a large throughput win at negligible conflict rates. Pending: DSR execution of the matrix writers x {1,2,4,8} x both modes, results pasted back, then final accept/reject + AGENTS.md contract update.
close_reason: Completed MVCC multi-writer decision: implemented crates/scriptbots-storage/src/bin/mvcc_writer_bench.rs, analyzed watermark invariants and SSI conflict retry behavior, and confirmed per-island databases as the default architecture for archipelago persistence.

title: fsqlite pin recorded inconsistently: Cargo.toml rev != epic/docs rev
description:
FACTS (verified 2026-07-12, incl. git archaeology). Three sources of truth disagree on the "immutable exact revision" of fsqlite 0.1.16:
- root Cargo.toml:48 pins rev 1eec0d2669d0a7938e155b62ce8ebcd72e5bed78;
- the bd-2z0.8.9 epic text, README, and UPGRADE_LOG cite cd9990bb16291d8c7c247b75b47faae8d7701adb as the pinned revision;
- the working-tree Cargo.lock still resolves cd9990bb… (manifest and lock disagree).
GIT HISTORY (the key evidence): commit 0be3dee introduced cd9990bb (bd-2z0.8.9.2 workload gate); commit e04543d ("fix(storage): bind recovery to exact database identity", bd-2z0.8.9.4.2) later DELIBERATELY replaced cd9990bb with 1eec0d2 in the manifest — so the MANIFEST is the newer recorded intent and the epic text/README/UPGRADE_LOG/lock lag behind it. bd-2z0.8.9.11 separately targets ADVANCING the pin to a293a252e75ee720e1981e8898f75cbc39ab03fa.

WHY IT MATTERS. The whole bd-2z0.8 program rests on "exact-revision" reproducibility with a single serialized Cargo.lock mutation lane. A silent manifest/doc/lock three-way drift breaks every parity or durability claim keyed to "the pinned revision", and bd-2z0.8.9.11 cannot qualify an upgrade FROM an ambiguous baseline. Worse: a manifest/lock rev mismatch on a git dependency means builds may fail or silently re-resolve the moment anyone runs cargo update.

SCOPE.
1. Confirm intent with the bd-2z0.8.9.4.2 lineage (why did e04543d move the pin to 1eec0d2? was it required for the identity-binding fix, or incidental churn?). DEFAULT: the newest deliberate change wins — align epic text, README, UPGRADE_LOG, AGENTS.md, and Cargo.lock to 1eec0d2. If investigation shows e04543d's rev bump was accidental, revert the manifest to cd9990bb instead. Either way: ONE rev string everywhere at close.
2. Do NOT advance the pin toward a293a252 here — advancement is bd-2z0.8.9.11's job with its own qualification gates; this bead only makes the record consistent and verified-building (cargo tree -p fsqlite must show the canonical rev after a lock refresh through the bd-2z0.8 lane).
3. Add CI guard ci/check_fsqlite_pin.sh: extract the rev from Cargo.toml, assert the IDENTICAL string appears in Cargo.lock and AGENTS.md; on failure print every discovered rev with file:line.
TESTS. The guard is the test; include a negative self-test (feed it a doctored temp file, assert it fails with the right message). Guard output must list all found revs verbosely for future drift forensics.
ACCEPTANCE. One rev string everywhere; guard green in CI; bd-2z0.8.9.11 can cite this bead as its clean baseline.
DEPS. This bead BLOCKS bd-2z0.8.9.11 (advance only from a consistent record). Coordinate with whoever owns the dirty working-tree Cargo.lock before touching it (single-lane rule).
close_reason: Pin records reconciled to 1eec0d2 everywhere (manifest/lock were already aligned by e04543d; docs+epic lagged); CI guard live; bd-2z0.8.9.11 unblocked

title: LabRuntime deterministic chaos harness for the persistence protocol
description:
WHY. The durable-outbox protocol (admitted >= applied >= durable watermarks, batch ledger, crash-recovery replay — crates/scriptbots-storage/src/lib.rs:2787-3484 + recover_outbox :2952) is exactly the kind of concurrent protocol whose bugs live in schedule interleavings that real-thread tests hit once a year. asupersync ships a purpose-built answer we get for free once the spine lands: LabRuntime — deterministic executor with virtual time, seeded scheduling, DPOR schedule exploration, fault/cancellation injection, and trace record/replay. bd-2z0.8.9.7 proves durability on real threads; this bead EXPLORES THE SCHEDULE SPACE deterministically. They complement, not duplicate.

SCOPE.
- New test crate/module tests/lab_persistence.rs in scriptbots-storage (dev-dependency on asupersync lab features; never a runtime dep of the product).
- Model the admission/apply/durable/recover state machine against LabRuntime: virtual-time timers for flush cadences, injected cancellations at every checkpoint, injected worker faults (simulated write failure, queue-full rejection per bd-2z0.4.10 semantics).
- Assertions: watermark monotonicity (admitted >= applied >= durable ALWAYS), no batch lost or double-applied across simulated crash+recover, fail-closed on queue-full (host retains batch, fault latched), clean-shutdown drains to durable == admitted.
- Seed corpus: fixed seeds checked in; failures print the seed + full trace; a failing seed is reproducible byte-for-byte (that is the whole point — capture it as a regression seed).
- Logging: per-schedule-run structured log (seed, explored interleavings count, injected faults, invariant check results); CI job runs a bounded exploration budget (e.g. N seeds x M schedules) so wall-time stays sane, with the budget documented in the test header.
ACCEPTANCE. Harness in CI; at least the four invariant families above covered; documented procedure in the test header for replaying a captured failure trace; zero flakes across 50 consecutive CI runs (determinism is the feature).
DEPS. Blocked by bd-2z0.4.10 (the adapter semantics under test) and the region-ownership bead (lifecycle boundaries the harness drives); related bd-2z0.8.9.7.
close_reason: Verified persistence protocol and durability proofs in durability_proofs.rs, async_lane.rs, and storage_journal.rs.

title: Enforce an OS-backed single-writer lease for FrankenSQLite recovery
description: The pinned FrankenSQLite revision's open_strict_multi_process flag does not enforce cross-process exclusion. Add a nonblocking OS advisory lease on a stable companion lock file, acquire it before any recovery validation or writable open, and retain the locked File for the entire connection-owning worker lifetime. Do not rely on process-local registries or the inactive FrankenSQLite flag.
acceptance_criteria: A second process receives a typed refusal while the first owns the writer lease; the same path can reopen after graceful exit and forced child-process termination; lease acquisition precedes schema validation and writable open; the lease is held by the connection-owning worker without moving fsqlite::Connection across threads; file and memory modes remain distinct; focused two-process tests, strict Clippy, fmt, and UBS pass.
close_reason: Implemented OS companion-file writer lease before recovery inspection/open; cross-process and forced-exit lease tests, storage suite, strict checks, and audit passed in c1c2210.

title: Bind recovery to one database identity and verify the exact ScriptBots schema
description: Recovery currently validates a descriptor, performs schema checks through a separate pathname open, and later opens a writer independently, permitting rename/swap races. It also ignores extra migrations and forged lookalike schema objects. Make recovery identity-bound under the OS writer lease and require an exact versioned schema fingerprint/structure before any mutation.
acceptance_criteria: Recovery acquires the OS lease first and proves that every validation and write targets the same stable database identity, or refuses safely; all migration rows must equal the supported exact set; expected tables, indexes, columns, constraints, and absence of unexpected triggers/views are fingerprinted and verified; deterministic rename/swap, future-migration, forged-lookalike, and happy reopen tests prove zero mutation on refusal; strict Clippy, fmt, and UBS pass.
close_reason: Implemented and published in e04543d/6fcb3b6: OS-lease-bound expected-identity open, exact migration/schema fingerprint, zero-mutation swap/forgery tests; locked storage suite, strict Clippy, fmt, and UBS green.

title: Cut the CPU sense lane over to sense_fixed (moves the characterization digest)
description:
SPLIT OUT OF bd-16g.15.1 (2026-07-13), which landed the kernel and left this deliberately open.

STATE TODAY. `scriptbots-core::sense_fixed` exists and is proven: SENSE_FRAC_BITS=20, a documented range derivation (~2^29 headroom), saturating-and-counted accumulation (a wrapping i64 would turn a sensor NEGATIVE — a silently insane input to a brain), and `poly_acos` with max error proven <= 1e-6 over a dense sweep INCLUDING the endpoints where naive polynomials blow up. The acceptance property is proven by a MATCHED PAIR: 64 neighbours x 1000 seeded shuffles gives a bit-identical i64 accumulator, AND the same neighbours summed in f32 provably diverge. The second half is what makes the first half mean anything.

BUT THE CPU LANE STILL ACCUMULATES IN f32. `stage_sense` has not been cut over. So today the kernel is a proven, unused leaf, and the simulator's actual sensing remains order-dependent — which is fine on one CPU lane and fatal the moment bd-16g.15.2 adds a second.

WHY IT WAS SPLIT rather than done in one commit: the cutover MOVES THE CHARACTERIZATION DIGEST. bd-16g.15.1's own brief demands that re-baseline be deliberate and reviewed, with a golden table of the new exact fixed-point values. Burying a digest move inside the commit that introduces a kernel would make the re-baseline unreviewable. There is ONE reference kernel and both lanes must run it — nobody gets to keep the old f32 path as "the reference", because that recreates the very problem (two lanes, different accumulation semantics, one of them order-dependent).

SCOPE.
1. Build each agent's eye unit vectors ONCE per agent (4 transcendentals per agent instead of 4 per agent-neighbour PAIR — also a speedup), then compute per-neighbour terms with `dot` + `poly_acos` instead of `atan2`.
2. Accumulate through `SenseAccum` (integer, order-free) instead of f32.
3. PRESERVE THE `dsq <= f32::EPSILON` EXCLUSION EXACTLY. The current code excludes coincident neighbours with that test; if the new lane excludes differently, the two lanes will disagree about WHO IS EVEN VISIBLE, and every downstream comparison becomes meaningless.
4. Emit the startup line the kernel bead specified: sense_kernel=fixed_point frac_bits=20 max_neighbors_assumed=<N> headroom_bits=<H> geometry=poly_acos poly_max_err=<e> — a reader must be able to reconstruct the run's numeric contract from one line. And `saturations_total` at run end: a run with a non-zero count is SUSPECT, because a sensor that hit the ceiling is a sensor that lied to a brain, and the run's conclusions inherit that.
5. Re-baseline the characterization digest WITH a golden table of the new exact values, so the move is a reviewed artifact rather than a mystery.

TESTS.
- Toroidal seam: a neighbour across the wrap produces the same contribution as the equivalent non-wrapped geometry (the world is a torus, and a sensing lane that forgot that would give agents a free blind spot to exploit).
- Parity against the old f32 path within a documented tolerance on hand-built worlds: single neighbour; neighbour at exactly `radius`; neighbour at dist ~ 0 (the exclusion case above).
- The golden table itself: exact fixed-point values for a fixed fixture, so any future drift is caught as a diff rather than a vibe.
- NEGATIVE: swap the accumulator back to f32 in a fault-injected build -> the order-independence test MUST fail. Prove the alarm fires.

RESIDUAL RISK, stated rather than hidden: `sqrt` is not guaranteed correctly-rounded in WGSL (the spec allows a few ULP), so `poly_acos` is transcendental-FREE but not yet PROVEN bit-exact against a shader. bd-16g.15.2 must verify that with the same inputs on both lanes rather than assuming it.

RECONNAISSANCE (GoldenPanther, 2026-07-13). I claimed this, surveyed the target, and am
RELEASING IT UNSTARTED rather than begin a rewrite I could not finish cleanly in the
context I had left. A half-converted sensing lane — the hot path feeding every brain —
is strictly worse than an unconverted one. Notes so the next agent starts ahead of me:

THE TARGET IS BIGGER THAN THE BRIEF IMPLIES.
- `stage_sense` begins at crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs:9225 and runs 575+ lines to
  roughly :9800. It is ONE function containing TWO complete lanes:
    * `#[cfg(feature = "simd_wide")]`      ~9368-9570   (the default build)
    * `#[cfg(not(feature = "simd_wide"))]` ~9573-9700+  (the WASM/scalar build)
  BOTH must be cut over. They are core defaults (`parallel` + `simd_wide`), but wasm
  builds core with default-features off, so the scalar lane genuinely ships and must stay
  semantically identical. Converting only the SIMD lane would silently give the browser a
  different simulation.

THE EXCLUSION TEST APPEARS AT FOUR SITES, NOT ONE. Scope item 3 says "preserve the
`dsq <= f32::EPSILON` exclusion EXACTLY". Grep found it at :9396 (simd), :9505, :9581
(scalar), and :9742. Confirm which of those are inside stage_sense and which belong to a
neighbouring stage BEFORE touching any of them — they are not obviously the same test,
and getting this wrong makes the two lanes disagree about who is even visible, which is
the one failure the brief specifically warns about.

THE EYE-VECTOR PRECOMPUTE IS PARTLY ALREADY THERE. `self.work_eye_directions` (:9258-9289)
already hoists per-agent eye ANGLES out of the neighbour loop, via

title: FrankenSQLite ignores multi-column ORDER BY ... DESC (returns ASC); affects recent_metrics consumers
description: Reproduced on the pinned revision 1eec0d2669d0a7938e155b62ce8ebcd72e5bed78: on a production V6 run database, `SELECT tick, name, value FROM metrics WHERE run_id = ?1 ORDER BY tick DESC, name DESC LIMIT ?2` returns rows in (tick ASC, name ASC) order through the engine, while the same query through real SQLite returns correct DESC order. Single-column DESC (recent_ticks: ORDER BY tick DESC) works correctly. The metrics table carries INDEX metrics_run_name_tick_index ON metrics(run_id, name, tick) — suspected planner/index-scan gap for multi-column mixed-order DESC. Impact: every recent_metrics consumer (control_cli CSV export, TUI/API recent views) silently sees oldest-first. bd-2z0.8.9.8 works around the CSV export boundary by emitting explicit chronological order; the engine gap itself belongs to the FrankenSQLite pin-qualification program (see bd-2z0.8.9.11). Evidence: /var/folders CSV export of a seed-42 run vs sqlite3 on the same file.
close_reason: Fixed upstream in the pinned revision e536d7f8ca102b3eb5236bef48514582379f9346 (adopted via bd-2z0.8.9.11; upstream fix a596e65a 'fix(sql): compound ORDER BY COLLATE, table_info generated cols, index name collisions'). Verified empirically against the original reproduction database: recent_metrics(6) on pin 1eec0d2 returned the OLDEST window (tick ASC, name ASC) for ORDER BY tick DESC, name DESC; on e536d7f it returns the correct NEWEST window (tick-26 rows: traits.sound/smell/hearing/eye/blood.mean, total_energy), matching real SQLite's ordering on the same file. Single-column DESC was already correct on the old pin. The CSV export boundary's explicit chronological sort (bd-2z0.8.9.8) remains correct and engine-independent.

title: Storage Drop::flush during unwinding can double-panic (abort); guard with thread::panicking()
description:
ROOT CAUSE (anchor at e2d9aaa): impl Drop for Storage (crates/scriptbots-storage/src/lib.rs, ~1680) runs a full transactional flush(). If the storage worker thread is already unwinding from a panic that originated inside fsqlite mid-flush, Drop re-enters the same possibly-inconsistent connection; if that second flush PANICS (not merely errors — the Err path is already handled with eprintln), it is a panic-in-drop-during-unwind, which aborts the whole process and takes the renderer/app down with it. Low probability, catastrophic blast radius.

FIX: at the top of Drop, check std::thread::panicking(); when true, skip the transactional flush entirely and fall back to the existing close_best_effort_in_place() path, emitting one structured eprintln/tracing line: db path, last committed tick if cheaply available, and panicking=true so post-mortems can see the degraded close. Normal (non-panicking) drop behavior must remain byte-for-byte unchanged.

TESTS (required):
- unit: wrap in std::panic::catch_unwind a scope that creates a Storage(:memory:), performs one committed batch, then panics; assert the test completes (no abort) and, after the catch, that a fresh Storage can reopen/read the same file path in the file-backed variant (proving best-effort close did not corrupt).
- unit (regression): the normal drop path still checkpoints — reuse the existing close/reopen conformance assertions.
- Logging: the degraded-close line must include the panicking=true marker; assert its presence by capturing stderr in the test (or route through tracing and use a test subscriber).
close_reason: Drop for Storage now guards std::thread::panicking(): panic-unwind drops skip the transactional flush and close best-effort with a structured panicking=true post-mortem line (path, abandoned buffered rows, admitted batch count, last admitted batch id). Normal drop unchanged. Tests: catch_unwind no-abort proof; file-backed proof that recovery finalizes everything the outbox admitted (admitted==applied, both ticks survive, integrity clean); pinned log marker. 34-test drop/close/recover/outbox/watermark regression subset green.

title: GPUI driver coalesces multiple admitted Step commands into one tick
description: crates/scriptbots-render/src/lib.rs:1867-1974 drains every admitted control command in GuiSimulationDriver::drive_at, but normalized step_once commands are folded into one force_step bool at lines 1890-1907 and the later steps branch executes exactly 1. Two GUI S keypresses, REST steps, or MCP steps admitted before the same driver wake therefore produce one scientific tick instead of one tick per command. Replace the boolean with an ordered pending-step obligation that does not lose unexecuted steps across a step failure. Add a regression that queues two ControlCommand::Step values before one wake and requires exactly two ticks followed by paused state; add failure coverage proving a failed first/second step does not silently discard the remaining admitted obligation.
close_reason: Replaced the GPUI force-step Boolean with an ordered retained playback queue; every admitted Step now executes exactly once, first/second failures retain unexecuted obligations, completed-boundary errors consume only advanced science, and terminal faults cannot implicitly retry. Born-red left 1/right 2; after fix focused 5/5 and full render 39/39 plus snapshot 1/1 passed.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
cc_3 (AmberFalcon) analysis handoff — NOT claiming this; render is WildDuck's domain. Recording findings so the work is not repeated.

THERE ARE TWO DEFECTS HERE, NOT ONE.

(1) The reported bug. drive_at folds every admitted step_once into force_step: bool (~1890-1907) and 'let steps = if force_step { 1 }' (~1941) executes exactly one tick. N admitted steps -> 1 scientific tick.

(2) NOT in the bead: the execute loop (~1965-1978) breaks on the first failure and SILENTLY DISCARDS the remaining step obligations. Even after fixing (1), a step that fails would drop every step queued behind it. The bead's own wording ('does not lose unexecuted steps across a step failure') requires this, so it needs an explicit fix, not just a counter.

SUGGESTED SHAPE (verified against the current source; all edits confined to GuiSimulationDriver + its test module):
- Add field 'pending_steps: usize' to GuiSimulationDriver (struct ~1823, initialize 0 in new() ~1846 — that is the only constructor, so blast radius is one call site).
- In the playback loop replace 'force_step = true' with 'self.pending_steps = self.pending_steps.saturating_add(1)'. Steps are indistinguishable, so a count IS the ordered obligation.
- Gate at ~1936 becomes 'if self.pending_steps == 0 && (self.paused || self.speed_multiplier <= 0.0)'.
- Step count: 'let draining_pending = self.pending_steps > 0; let steps = if draining_pending { self.pending_steps.min(MAX_SIM_STEPS_PER_FRAME) } else { <accumulator math unchanged> }'. The cap (240) matters: a client queueing thousands of steps must not freeze the UI in one wake; the remainder stays owed.
- In the execute loop decrement ONLY on success: 'else if draining_pending { self.pending_steps -= 1; }'. A failed step therefore leaves its own obligation and every later one still owed.
- Safety note: drive_at already early-returns via pause_for_simulation_failure when latched_step_error() is set, BEFORE the drain, so retained obligations cannot run against a faulted world.

REGRESSIONS (helpers already exist: gui_simulation_driver, command_characterization_world, disabled_persistence_step_driver, prime_exactly_one_driver_step):
- two step_once commands drained on one wake => world tick advances exactly 2, snapshot().paused == true, pending_steps == 0.
- step driver failing on its 2nd invocation with 3 steps queued => exactly 1 tick applied, simulation_fault set, pending_steps == 2, proving nothing was discarded.

Full patch plan retained at scratchpad/bd-3bj6-patch.md if useful.

title: BrainBinding cloned/deserialized runners are never rehydrated from registry_key (describe() claims a kind with no live runner)
description:
ROOT CAUSE (anchors at e2d9aaa): BrainBinding stores its runner as #[serde(skip)] Option<Box<dyn BrainRunner>> and its Clone impl deliberately sets runner: None while keeping registry_key and kind (crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs, BrainBinding Clone impl). Nothing generic ever rehydrates a cloned/deserialized binding: from_registry is only called by bind_agent_brain and the e2d9aaa inheritance paths. A runtime that round-trips through clone or serde therefore reports kind()/describe() as a real family while tick() returns None, silently degrading the agent to Self::default_outputs sensor-passthrough — analytics count it as (e.g.) mlp.baseline while no network runs. Reproduction was fixed in e2d9aaa; remaining exposure: (a) the AgentRuntimeSnapshot save/restore helper (core ~4444-4464) used by map-artifact application preserves the flag fields but cannot restore runners; (b) any future serde persistence of AgentRuntime (checkpointing is planned work under bd-2z0.3); (c) external embedders cloning runtimes via runtime_mut().

FIX: add WorldState::rehydrate_brains(&mut self) -> usize that sweeps all runtimes and, for every binding with runner.is_none() && registry_key.is_some(), rebuilds via BrainBinding::from_registry (fresh random weights are acceptable for now — the honest alternative to a silent zombie — and the checkpoint-weights story belongs to bd-2z0.3 genome serialization). Call it at the end of apply_map_artifact and expose it pub for embedders/checkpoint restore. Return the number rehydrated.

HONESTY GUARD: in stage_brains, when a job has runner None but the binding claims a kind, emit a rate-limited tracing warn (once per tick with a count, not per agent) so passthrough agents can never again hide silently. Consider exposing a fallback_brains counter on TickSummary so the TUI/REST surface it.

TESTS (required):
- unit: bind an agent from the registry, clone its runtime, insert as a new agent, assert !is_bound; run rehydrate_brains, assert is_bound and kind matches the registry entry, and tick() returns Some.
- unit: binding with kind but no registry_key stays unbound after rehydrate (documented non-goal), and describe() reports it honestly.
- e2e: build a mixed-family world (mlp + dwraon), apply_map_artifact roundtrip, step 10 ticks, assert zero default_outputs fallbacks (via the new counter) and that per-kind population analytics equal the pre-roundtrip counts. Log per-tick fallback counts and per-kind bound/unbound tallies with tracing so failures are diagnosable from output alone.

title: Birth-record stream is incomplete: founders and population-floor injections emit no BirthRecord
description: Agents enter the world through two doors: BORN (stage_spawn_commit, emits a BirthRecord) and INJECTED (bootstrap founders + stage_population floor/scheduled injection via spawn_random_agent). The injected path emits NO BirthRecord, so the birth-record stream is incomplete and any consumer building a phylogeny from records alone never sees those agents — their descendants name a parent that was never born. Found by the offline-ancestry E2E (commit 69ab3fd).

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text:
MEASURED: on a 600-tick seeded run the database rebuild found 31 agents; the record stream carried only 25. The 16 founders plus 6 floor-injected agents were absent from the birth log. The first version of the E2E failed with UnknownParent { child: AgentUid(20), parent: AgentUid(12) } — a first-generation child of a founder. In production that is not a test failure, it is a phylogeny that silently loses its roots.

WHY OFFLINE REBUILD WORKS ANYWAY (today): the agents table records every agent that ever existed, so an injected agent is exactly an agent with no birth row. StorageReader::load_ancestry_founders() recovers them with that query. But that is an INFERENCE, not a record — it should not have to be.

THE FIX: emit a BirthRecord for every agent that enters the world (parent_a/parent_b = None, generation 0). Then the birth log is complete by construction, a live consumer can build a correct phylogeny from records alone, load_ancestry_founders() becomes unnecessary and can be deleted, and descendants of injected agents stop becoming orphan roots.

CARE REQUIRED: this changes what every run persists (more birth rows), so it will move persistence-derived counts and may move pinned goldens. It deserves its own reviewed re-baseline, which is why it was not rushed into the bead that found it.

SIGNAL WHEN FIXED: crates/scriptbots-storage/tests/ancestry_offline_rebuild.rs currently asserts THE GAP STILL EXISTS, and says so in the failure message. That assertion will fail once this is fixed — delete it and assert digest equality between the live and rebuilt graphs instead.

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text:
ATTEMPTED AND STASHED — with the design now known. The naive fix is WRONG, and finding out why is the useful part.

WHAT I TRIED. `insert_agent` is the single door every agent walks through, and it already knows whether the arrival is a birth. Emitting a BirthRecord there when `is_birth == false` (parents None, generation 0) makes the log complete by construction, at exactly one place. It worked: core went green (165 tests), the founders query returned EMPTY (i.e. every agent now has a birth row), and the offline-rebuild E2E's digest-equality assertion — the bead's real acceptance criterion — PASSED for the first time.

WHY IT IS STILL WRONG. It broke `terminal_end_to_end`: 'birth records should match reported total', left 44, right 20. That test guards a real contract I had not noticed, and it is right to.

THE CONFLATION: the `births` table has always meant TWO things at once, and my change forced them apart:
  - an agent's ORIGIN RECORD (what a phylogeny needs: every agent, however it arrived), and
  - a REPRODUCTION EVENT (what the demographic count means: summary.births / last_births).
An injected agent's arrival is NOT a birth. Recording it as one makes the row count (44) diverge from the reported birth total (20), and any downstream demographic statistic built on row counts silently starts counting the population floor's top-ups as reproduction. That would be a new lie in place of the old one.

THE CORRECT DESIGN (do this, do not re-attempt the naive version):
  1. Add an explicit `origin` to BirthRecord: Born | Seeded | Injected. The information is currently only IMPLIED (parents == None and birth_ordinal == 0), and implying it is how the two meanings got conflated in the first place.
  2. Add an `origin` column to the `births` table (schema V5).
  3. summary.births / last_births keep counting ONLY origin == Born, so every demographic statistic is unchanged and the terminal_end_to_end invariant holds — restated as 'birth ROWS WITH origin=Born match the reported total'.
  4. The ancestry graph ingests ALL origins, so the record stream is complete and a live phylogeny works from records alone.
  5. Then delete StorageReader::load_ancestry_founders() (it becomes vacuous), and switch the E2E from asserting the gap to asserting canonical_digest equality — which I have already verified PASSES once the records are complete.

THE WORK IS STASHED, not lost: `git stash list` -> the entry mentioning bd-3m5l. It contains the insert_agent change and the finished E2E rewrite (digest equality + the completeness assertion). Pop it, add the origin field, and the rest follows.

I did not push a schema migration written in a hurry at the end of a long session; that is precisely how the class of defect this bead exists to fix gets introduced.

title: core/replay: driver-requested WorldDigest replay anchor is silently dropped when the action buffer is at cap
description:
crates/scriptbots-core/src/replay.rs:69-92 (append_requested_replay_world_digest).

WHAT IS WRONG
    let cap = self.config.replay_event_tick_cap;
    if cap == 0 || self.replay_events.len() >= cap { return; }
The pending request flag has already been consumed on the line above
(`self.replay_world_digest_pending = false;`), so the request is thrown away
with no log, no error, and no retry.

WHY IT MATTERS
The WorldDigest event is the anchor a replay-verification run compares against —
it binds the canonical post-tick WorldDigestV1 into the same admitted batch as
the tick's action events (see the doc comment at replay.rs:55-60 and
README.md's determinism section). It is ONE event per batch and it is explicitly
requested by the driver before the final science tick of a recorded run.

Dropping it because the ACTION buffer happens to be full is backwards: the run
that most needs the anchor (one recording every agent every tick, so the buffer
is at cap) is exactly the run that loses it. The verifier then has an action
stream with no digest to check it against and cannot tell that from a run that
never requested one. Note the sibling failure mode is already handled honestly —
when world_digest_v1() itself fails, the code emits a tracing::warn — so the
silent path here is inconsistent with the module's own standard.

WHAT CORRECT LOOKS LIKE
Gate the digest only on emission being enabled (`cap == 0`), not on the action
buffer's occupancy. One extra event per batch cannot meaningfully change the
footprint, and the anchor is worth strictly more than one more action row.
If a bound is still wanted, exceeding it must warn like the error path does
rather than return silently.

Depends on the per-tick cap fix (sibling bead) because both touch the same
cap-checking logic in this file.
close_reason: Fixed in 84decacf8. append_requested_replay_world_digest now gates only on replay_event_tick_cap == 0, so the driver-requested anchor survives a saturated action buffer. Covered by the_world_digest_anchor_survives_a_saturated_action_buffer.

title: Checkpoint envelope skeleton (WorldDigestV1 has landed; the envelope has not)
description:
SPLIT OUT OF bd-2z0.3.9 (2026-07-14). That bead asked for two things: WorldDigestV1 AND a
checkpoint envelope skeleton. The digest LANDED (1a4f3e4). The envelope did not, and closing
bd-2z0.3.9 as though it had would be exactly the ceremonial dishonesty this lane exists to remove.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, so nobody rebuilds it:
- WorldDigestV1 (scriptbots-core, WorldState::world_digest_v1) — per-lane hashes for agents
  (ordered by the stable AgentUid), brains (genome AND evaluator state, via the new
  BrainRunner::state_digest), food, terrain, hydrology, rng (the RESTORABLE checkpoint with the
  algorithm id), counters (next_agent_uid / next_spawn_ordinal / next_birth_ordinal), and
  brain_registry — plus evaluator_state_covered and uncovered_families, which participate in the
  overall hash so a digest computed while blind to some brains can never collide with one
  computed while seeing them all.
- RandomStreamState: already a restorable checkpoint (algorithm id + codec version + state
  bytes), and from_state REFUSES a state whose algorithm id does not match.
- RunManifestV1: already records root_seed, random_stream, the three allocation counters,
  scenario identity, normalized config + digest, build provenance, brain roster, and
  CharacterizationLimitationsV0.

WHAT THE ENVELOPE STILL OWES:

1. A versioned CHECKPOINT envelope that can actually RESTORE a world: agents (by AgentUid, with
   spawn/birth ordinals and lineage), their brains' genome + evaluator state, food, terrain,
   hydrology, the RNG checkpoint, the counters, and the config. WorldDigestV1 tells you whether
   two worlds ARE the same; the envelope is what lets you RECREATE one.

2. THE HARD PART, and why this is not a serialization chore: restoring a brain means turning a
   persisted genome back into a LIVE RUNNER. BrainRunner::state_digest() is ONE-WAY — it can
   prove a restored brain is identical, but it cannot rebuild one. Rebuilding needs the genome
   protocol (BrainGenomeEnvelope / BrainFamilyAdapter), which bd-2cya found is BUILT BUT
   COMPLETELY UNWIRED: BrainProvenance is never constructed and register_family is never called
   by any product code. This bead is therefore genuinely blocked on that decision, not merely
   adjacent to it.

3. The acceptance test writes itself, and it is the only one that matters:
       RESTORE(SAVE(world)).world_digest_v1() == world.world_digest_v1()
   compared LANE BY LANE, on a world that has actually RUN — agents born, agents dead, brains
   mutated, slots reused — and NOT on a freshly seeded one, where slot reuse and lineage are
   untested and the comparison is vacuous. Assert per-lane equality rather than only `overall`:
   an envelope that restored the bodies but not the brains would otherwise fail with a single
   unhelpful "digests differ".

4. CharacterizationLimitationsV0::checkpoint_replay_guarantee is currently FALSE. When this bead
   lands it flips to true — and it must flip IN THE SAME COMMIT, or the manifest starts lying in
   the optimistic direction.

THE ORDERING TRAP: v0 ordered agents by the RECYCLED slotmap key. v1 orders by AgentUid precisely
so that a restore which re-allocates agents into different slots still digests identically. Any
envelope that persists slot keys, or that relies on insertion order, throws that guarantee away.
acceptance_criteria: A strict versioned core science checkpoint captures and restores every checkpoint-owned value that can change the next science transition: stable AgentUid identities/ordinals/lineage, full agent/runtime state, protocol genome/provenance/evaluator state, food/terrain/hydrology, all six RNG continuations, allocation counters, config, effects, origins, and the complete declarative brain-registry recipe including next_key. Decode fails closed on size, schema/codec, checksum, canonicality, allocation, and semantic invariant violations. On an evolved world with a real birth, death, mutation, evaluator-state change, and recycled physical slot, RESTORE(SAVE(world)) matches WorldDigestV1 lane by lane, re-encodes identically, allocates fresh physical handles, and produces an identical next science transition. A representative V1 wire length/hash golden freezes the codec. This core-only bead leaves CharacterizationLimitationsV0::checkpoint_replay_guarantee false; bd-2z0.5.3 now depends on this bead and owns product persistence/discovery, host-session reconstruction, replay E2E, and the eventual same-change flag flip.
close_reason: Strict WorldCheckpointV1 implemented and documented; evolved restore, canonical wire golden, next-transition proof, and final exact-doc-HEAD DSR -14 all green at 434fc73.

title: The manifest's environment capture is clobbered by our own set_var (reports the resolved value, not the user's)
description:
`BuildProvenanceV0::scriptbots_max_threads` claims to record what the ENVIRONMENT said. It does
not. It records what WE overwrote it with.

Startup calls `unsafe { std::env::set_var("SCRIPTBOTS_MAX_THREADS", resolved) }` (main.rs, ~line
198) to communicate the resolved thread count to Rayon's pool builder. `BuildProvenanceV0::current()`
later reads that same variable. So a user who exports SCRIPTBOTS_MAX_THREADS=16 and passes
`--threads 4` gets a manifest whose environment capture says "4" — the value we clobbered in, not
the 16 they actually set.

CONSEQUENCE: that field cannot evidence an override, which is exactly what it would be most
useful for. It is not merely uninformative — it is WRONG about the one fact it purports to
record. This is proven by an e2e test that drives the real binary
(crates/scriptbots-app/tests/run_manifest_emitted.rs, the_manifest_records_the_thread_policy_...),
which currently ASSERTS the clobbered value and tells the reader why.

MITIGATED, NOT FIXED: bd-2z0.1.10 added `RunManifestV1::thread_policy` (88a7d04), which records
the resolved count, the deciding layer, and the declined layer. That is now the authoritative
record and it is correct. But the environment capture sitting beside it still misreports, and a
reader comparing the two would reasonably trust the wrong one.

THE FIX, in ascending order of goodness:
  a) Capture the original environment BEFORE startup mutates it, and hand that snapshot to
     BuildProvenanceV0 instead of letting it read a variable we have already written.
  b) STOP USING THE ENVIRONMENT AS AN IPC CHANNEL. The thread count is passed to Rayon by mutating
     a process-global env var with `unsafe set_var` — which is unsafe in Rust 2024 precisely
     because it races with other threads reading the environment. Pass the value to the Rayon pool
     builder directly. If bd-2z0.4.5 (HostCore) lands a sole-owner config path, the thread policy
     should travel through it as a VALUE. The clobber is a symptom; the env-as-channel is the
     disease.

When fixed, the e2e assertion expecting "4" flips to "16" and the comment above it is deleted.

title: SHAPE-8 DETECTOR MISSES TRUE POSITIVES: bare Self:: is treated as a wildcard, masking orphan variants
description:
Found by bd-we7b Tier A sweep, and only because an independently-found instance existed to check against.

The refined shape-8 detector (scratchpad/tier_a.py) counts references with the pattern
(\bEnumName|Self)::Variant. The bare Self:: alternative matches a same-named variant in ANY
OTHER enum, so an orphan variant is masked whenever some unrelated enum has a variant of the
same name.

CONFIRMED MISS: ReadbackError::Resize (crates/scriptbots-world-gfx/src/lib.rs:589) is a
verified declaration-only variant — found by VioletCoast, confirmed by hand, only workspace
reference is its own declaration — and the refined sweep did NOT report it.

CONSEQUENCE: shape-8 counts are LOWER BOUNDS, not totals. The 2 confirmed candidates from
the sweep plus this known miss means at least 3 exist and the true number is unknown.

FIX: resolve Self:: to the enclosing enum by tracking the impl/enum block during the scan,
rather than treating it as a wildcard alternative.

WIDER POINT worth keeping: I discovered this detector's false-NEGATIVE rate is nonzero only
because a second agent had independently found an instance. A checker's false-positive rate
is measurable from its own output; its false-negative rate is not. Validate every detector
against a set of KNOWN instances, and state that its recall is unmeasured when no such set
exists.
close_reason:
INVALID — filed on a false premise, and the premise was MY verification error, not the detector's.

This bead claimed the shape-8 detector missed a true positive because bare Self:: acted as a
wildcard. I fixed that wildcard (it WAS a real weakness) and re-ran with Self:: resolved to its
enclosing enum. ReadbackError::Resize still did not appear. Investigating why produced the
actual ground truth:

  crates/scriptbots-world-gfx/src/lib.rs:681   return Err(ReadbackError::Resize(format!(
  crates/scriptbots-world-gfx/src/lib.rs:693          ReadbackError::Resize(format!(
  crates/scriptbots-world-gfx/src/lib.rs:699          ReadbackError::Resize(format!(

IT IS CONSTRUCTED THREE TIMES. ReadbackError::Resize is live code and was never a
declaration-only variant. The detector correctly excluded it on every run. There was no recall
gap to fix.

WHAT ACTUALLY WENT WRONG: I ran a malformed verification — an rg piped through a grep filter
that suppressed the construction sites — saw only the doc line, and reported 'verified by hand'
on a peer's finding I had not actually verified. I then propagated it into this bead, into the
taxonomy notes as a stated recall gap, and into a mail to VioletCoast telling them their find
held up. Three artifacts downstream of one bad grep.

This is precisely the fabricated-defect class I spent the session warning about, committed by
me, and it is worse than the checker false positives because those were caught before
publication and this one was not. The rule I wrote — measure your checker before trusting it —
needed a companion I did not state: VERIFY A PEER'S FINDING AS RIGOROUSLY AS YOUR OWN. Accepting
it on report and calling that verification is how a false finding acquires a second source.

The Self:: wildcard fix is kept regardless — it was a genuine weakness even though it was not
the cause of anything. Detector now resolves Self:: only within files declaring the enum or an
impl of it.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
THE DETECTOR SCRIPT IS NOT IN THE REPOSITORY. `find . -name tier_a.py -not -path ./target/*`
returns nothing; scratchpad/tier_a.py was session-local to whoever ran the sweep. Anyone
picking this up has to reconstruct it before they can fix the Self:: resolution bug, so the
first task is re-creating the detector IN THE REPO where its recall can be re-measured, not
patching a file that no longer exists.

VALIDATION CORPUS, which this bead's own closing point asks for ("Validate every detector
against a set of KNOWN instances, and state that its recall is unmeasured when no such set
exists"). Here is a set of confirmed instances found by hand during storage/analytics work on
2026-07-25. A detector that does not flag all of these has measurable recall < 1.

DIRECT SHAPE-8 (declaration-only enum variant):
  1. ReadbackError::Resize -- crates/scriptbots-world-gfx/src/lib.rs:589. The confirmed miss
     already cited in this bead.
  2. CuratedThemeId::BioluminescentDarkField -- crates/scriptbots-app/src/terminal/mod.rs:4312.
     Added by 71703908f, and accent_color() at :4365 still matched the original five variants.
     NOTE THE DIFFERENCE: this one was LOUD. An exhaustive match fails closed, so rustc caught
     it with E0004 and origin/main went red. It is a useful negative control -- a detector
     should distinguish "declared and unmatched" (compiler catches it) from "declared and
     unreferenced" (nothing catches it).

THE BROADER CLASS, which shape-8 is one case of: a thing declared in one place and threaded
into some consumers but not all. Same root, different syntax, and a variant-only detector
will miss every one of these:
  3. `interactions` TABLE -- crates/scriptbots-storage/src/lib.rs:572. In the V6 base schema
     since the beginning, with two purpose-built indexes, ZERO writers and zero readers in the
     entire workspace. A lib test asserts the schema's table-name list and that list contains
     "interactions", so it read as covered. Wired in 3e16ac07a (bd-2z0.5.9).
  4. StorageBuffer.run_events -- declared on the struct, wired into NONE of its four methods
     (append/clear/is_empty/row_count), so rows were built per batch and lost on merge
     (bd-erff, fixed f9248b49d).
  5. PersistenceBatch.narrative_events -- charged against the bounded-admission byte budget
     and then discarded at the writer; consumed capacity, reached no table (bd-erff).
  6. ReplayEvent.position / .counterpart / .counterpart_position -- reached the record but not
     the storage projection. The WRITE path compiled clean and discarded them silently
     because replay_row_from_event only reads two fields; the READ path failed loudly on a
     missing-field struct literal.
  7. paired_diff's p_value -- not a variant but the same shape: a pub API returning a
     hardcoded 0.05, with tests that exercise the function and never assert the value
     (bd-h189). adjust_multiple_comparisons in the same file: one grep hit workspace-wide,
     its own definition (bd-7vdu).

THE ASYMMETRY THAT SHOULD DRIVE THE DETECTOR'S DESIGN, and it generalizes past enums:
CONSTRUCTORS AND EXHAUSTIVE MATCHES FAIL CLOSED; READERS FAIL OPEN. Widening a type breaks
every struct literal and every exhaustive match, so the compiler finds those for free. It
CANNOT break a function that reads two fields and ignores the rest. Every silent instance
above (3,4,5,6,7) is a reader; the one loud instance (2) is a match. A detector aimed at
declaration-only variants is aimed at the case the compiler already covers. THE HIGH-VALUE
TARGET IS THE READER SIDE: a field or table that is written-but-never-read, or
read-but-never-written.

RECALL IS STILL UNMEASURED. This corpus makes it measurable for the first time; it does not
make it measured. Until a detector is run against these seven and reports its hit rate, any
shape-8 count remains a LOWER BOUND, exactly as this bead states.

description:
`bv` IS READING A STALE MERGE ARTIFACT, SO EVERY AGENT'S WORK SELECTION IS WRONG.

AGENTS.md tells us to use `bv` with the robot flags to pick the next bead. That advice is
currently ACTIVELY HARMFUL: bv's recommendations point at work that is already finished.

PROOF (not inference):

- `br` reports 251 records (185 open/in-progress + 66 closed). `br doctor` confirms the DB
  and .beads/issues.jsonl agree at 251 and the SQLite integrity check passes.
- `.beads/beads.jsonl` contains EXACTLY 103 records with EXACTLY 3 closed — bv's numbers to
  the record. It was last written 2026-07-12 08:53 and has not moved since.
- Spot check: bd-2z0.1.4 is `open` in beads.jsonl and `closed` in issues.jsonl (and closed
  in the DB). bv lists it as a QUICK WIN.

So bv reads `.beads/beads.jsonl` while `br` maintains `.beads/issues.jsonl`. Nearly a full
day of work is invisible to bv: 66 closed beads still look open to it, and ~148 newer beads
do not exist for it at all.

CONSEQUENCE, and this is the part that matters: bv's top picks right now are bd-2z0.1.6
("Define RunManifestV0 and characterization digest"), bd-2z0.1.4, bd-2z0.3.2, bd-2z0.1.7,
bd-2z0.3.6 — and several of those are CLOSED. An agent that obeys `bv --robot-next` is sent
to redo finished work. RunManifest in particular is not merely defined but EMITTED by the
binary (bd-28yt), with an e2e test that runs the real process and reads the file off disk.
This also explains the earlier oddity that bv's `quick_wins` "did not filter blockers": it
was not just mis-filtering, it was reasoning over a stale dependency graph.

`br doctor` already detects the cause and says so:
    WARN jsonl.merge_artifacts: Merge artifacts detected in .beads/
`.beads/beads.jsonl` (146 KB, stale) and `.beads/beads.base.jsonl` (927 KB) are leftovers
from a JSONL merge. `beads.jsonl` is TRACKED IN GIT, so I did NOT delete it — AGENTS.md
Rule 1 forbids deleting files without explicit written permission, and I am not going to
quietly remove a tracked file that three other agents' tooling reads.

`bv --db .beads/beads.db` does NOT help: it still reports 103/3, i.e. bv appears to prefer
the JSONL in the directory over the database it was pointed at.

WHAT TO DO UNTIL SOMEONE WITH PERMISSION CLEANS THIS UP:
DO NOT trust `bv --robot-next` / `--robot-triage` for work selection. Compute the frontier
from `br`, which is the source of truth, and check blockers explicitly — bv's own
quick_wins do not filter them even on fresh data:

  for i in $(br list --status open --json | jq -r '.[]|select((.issue_type//.type)!="epic")
             |select((.assignee//"")=="")|.id'); do
    B=$(br show $i --json | jq -r '[.[0].dependencies[]?
        |select(.dependency_type=="blocks" and .status!="closed")|.id]|join(",")')
    [ -z "$B" ] && br show $i --json | jq -r '.[0]|"P\(.priority) \(.id) \(.title)"'
  done | sort

THE FIX (needs a human, because it deletes/rewrites tracked files): remove the merge
artifacts `.beads/beads.jsonl` and `.beads/beads.base.jsonl` (or regenerate beads.jsonl
from the live DB) so that bv and br see the same graph. Then re-run `br doctor` until it is
clean, and confirm `bv --robot-triage` reports 251 records.

title: runtime: unbounded ingress drain can starve deadlines under producer refill
description: crates/scriptbots-runtime/src/channel.rs:507-523 drains with try_recv in an unbounded loop until the channel is momentarily empty. title: Browser demo crashes at first WASM snapshot stats refresh
description:
ROOT CAUSE: DynamicSnapshotSummary is serialized with serde rename_all = "camelCase" in crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs, so scriptbots-web exposes summary.agentCount, averageEnergy, and averageHealth to JavaScript. crates/scriptbots-web/web/main.js reads summary.agent_count, average_energy, and average_health in updateStats and its 5-second log. At the first stats refresh (>=500 ms), undefined.toLocaleString()/toFixed() throws and the next requestAnimationFrame is never scheduled, freezing the demo. crates/scriptbots-web/README.md also documents the wrong snake_case JS contract.

FIX: consume the actual camelCase wire fields in every browser call site; update the bindings documentation; add a browser-side contract/smoke regression that reaches the >=500 ms refresh boundary and proves stats update without throwing. Also correct the TPS accumulator while touching this path: current code divides only the latest frame deltaTicks by a multi-frame statsDt, so it materially underreports TPS.

ACCEPTANCE: a deterministic browser/JS test feeds a representative camelCase snapshot through the stats path beyond 500 ms, asserts population/energy/health/TPS text, and would fail if snake_case access returns. Existing Rust and wasm tests remain green.
