title: Complete and wire the lab statistics layer into honest matched-seed reports
description: COMPLETION DEBT FROM bd-16g.1.4. The committed lab/stats.rs contains useful paired-effect, Hedges-g, and deterministic-bootstrap substrate, but it has never had an external lab consumer and the original close omitted or misstated required statistics. Establish the intended consumer from the validated lab state machine and provenance-enforcing notebook instead of wiring by convenience. Before publication, finish every original contract: data-derived uncertainty for paired and Hedges effects; explicit undefined/underpowered outcomes; real Holm-Bonferroni and Benjamini-Hochberg adjustments; Spearman correlation with tie handling; alternative-hypothesis provenance in Effect; deterministic, order-stable and compensated reductions; and honest errors for empty, non-finite, zero-variance, zero-iteration, and unmatched-seed inputs. Reuse or centralize the sound scriptbots-analytics authority where practical; do not create a third drifting statistics implementation and do not delete the existing file without the owner permission AGENTS.md requires.
acceptance_criteria: The validated matched-seed lab calls one reviewed statistics authority and the notebook reports its typed results with correction, alternative, sample size, estimator, and undefined/underpowered reasons. Unit and known-answer tests assert numerical values for paired effects, Hedges g, data-responsive CIs, Spearman with ties, Holm and BH ordering, deterministic bootstrap, non-finite/empty/zero-variance cases, and input-order invariance; calibration/null and injected-fabrication negative controls fail if constants or label-only corrections return. A mock-free seeded lab E2E executes multiple effects through validation, analysis, and notebook rendering, retains structured inputs/results/logs, and proves the same seed is byte-stable while changed data changes the reported statistics.

comments.author: CopperCat
comments.text:
CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD, AND A LARGER FINDING. No code removed. Read before acting.

I FILED THIS BEAD PARTLY WRONG. Two of the four items are NOT declaration-only:

  Correction::HolmBonferroni and Correction::BenjaminiHochberg ARE CONSTRUCTIBLE.
  Correction derives Serialize+Deserialize (stats.rs:20) and appears as a field:
      Effect { ..., pub correction: Option<Correction>, ... }   stats.rs:72
  Effect itself derives Deserialize, so both variants round-trip through JSON. serde
  constructs them from input with no textual Enum::Variant anywhere — exactly the
  macro-construction blind spot recorded on bd-hmy4, and I carried them into this bead
  without re-applying my own refinement. REMOVING THEM WOULD BREAK DESERIALIZATION of any
  persisted Effect. Struck from this bead.

  StatsError::ZeroVariance IS declaration-only, confirmed: derives Debug/Error/PartialEq/Eq,
  no #[from], no Deserialize, and its sole workspace reference is its own declaration.

BUT THE INTERESTING PART IS WHY ZeroVariance IS NEVER RETURNED. The case it names IS
reached — and handled in-band instead:

    stats.rs:123   let cohens_dz = if sd_diff > 1e-12 { mean_diff / sd_diff } else { 0.0 };

Zero variance yields cohens_dz = 0.0, i.e. NO EFFECT. That is the strongest possible wrong
answer: zero variance with a nonzero mean_diff is a PERFECTLY CONSISTENT difference — an
unbounded effect size, not an absent one. The code reports 'no effect' precisely when the
effect is maximally consistent, and the error variant written for that case sits unused two
hundred lines above.

So this is not dead code to delete. THE VARIANT IS CORRECT AND THE CALLER IS WRONG. The
remedy is to return StatsError::ZeroVariance (or an explicit undefined marker), not to
remove the variant. A declaration-only variant can be evidence of a MISSING CHECK rather
than of surplus code — that distinction belongs in the taxonomy under shape 8 and I have
noted it there.

SEPARATE AND LARGER, FOUND WHILE READING THE SAME FUNCTION — filed as its own bead:

    stats.rs:139   p_value: 0.05,

paired_diff returns a HARDCODED p-value on every call, independent of the data, and 0.05 is
the conventional significance threshold. bd-16g.1.4 closed claiming 'effect sizes with CIs
over matched-seed runs'. A downstream significance test reads a constant.

SCOPE HELD. No files deleted, no items removed, nothing edited. AGENTS.md Rule 1 is not
engaged — I did not reach the point of removing anything, because the analysis says removal
is the wrong remedy for three of the four items.

REVISED ACCEPTANCE for this bead:
  1. paired_diff must return StatsError::ZeroVariance (or an explicit undefined effect) when
     sd_diff <= 1e-12, with a test constructing a genuine zero-variance cohort. Do NOT keep
     the 0.0 fallback.
  2. Correction::HolmBonferroni / ::BenjaminiHochberg: KEEP. Wire adjust_multiple_comparisons
     into whatever reports multiple Effects, or document that Effect.correction is currently
     recorded-but-not-applied. A config-visible knob nobody applies is worse than a dead one.
  3. adjust_multiple_comparisons (bd-7vdu) stays as filed: uncalled, untested.

comments.author: CopperCat
comments.text:
STOPPING AND REPORTING. Applying the diagnostic rule to the remaining three items resolved
the cluster into a whole-module wiring gap, which is an owner decision, not mine.

════ THE DIAGNOSTIC RULE, written down because shape 8 will recur ════

FOR A DECLARATION-ONLY ITEM, ASK "WHY DOES NOTHING CONSTRUCT OR CALL THIS" BEFORE
"SHOULD THIS EXIST".

Two responses look identical in a diff and mean opposite things:
  - DELETING the item erases the evidence that a path was never wired.
  - WIRING the site that should have used it restores an intended path.

Only reading the would-be call site tells you which. A declaration-only item is sometimes
dead weight and sometimes a handler someone forgot to connect, and the tidy-looking removal
destroys the only remaining trace of the second case.

Worked instance, this bead: StatsError::ZeroVariance had zero constructors. The tidy answer
was to delete it. Reading stats.rs:123 instead found the place that SHOULD construct it —
`if sd_diff > 1e-12 { mean_diff / sd_diff } else { 0.0 }` returns "no effect" for a
perfectly consistent difference, which is the strongest possible wrong answer. The variant
was right; the caller was wrong. Deleting it would have removed the only surviving evidence
that the error path was intended.

════ SAME TEST APPLIED TO THE REMAINING THREE ITEMS ════

VERIFIED (rg over the whole workspace):
  - NOTHING outside lab/stats.rs constructs or reports `Effect`. No Vec<Effect>, no
    [Effect], no Effect { .. } literal anywhere else in scriptbots-app.
  - NOTHING outside lab/stats.rs calls paired_diff, hedges_g, or bootstrap_ci. The single
    apparent hit is a DIFFERENT bootstrap_ci in scriptbots-analytics/src/stats.rs — a
    separate module with its own implementation — and it is a test name.
  - lab/mod.rs:17 declares `pub mod stats;` and that is the only reference to it.

So the earlier "refs = 2" for the three live-looking functions was definition + a use INSIDE
stats.rs. THE WHOLE MODULE HAS NO EXTERNAL CONSUMER.

RESOLUTION OF THE CLUSTER: this is not four dead items. It is ONE UNWIRED ANALYSIS LAYER.
adjust_multiple_comparisons is uncalled for the same reason paired_diff is: nothing consumes
lab/stats.rs at all. That is a WIRING BUG, not dead code — and per the rule above, it is the
more valuable finding, because the remedy is to connect it rather than to erase it.

Supporting context: bd-16g.1.4 closed as "Analysis layer: effect sizes with CIs over
matched-seed runs", part of the bd-16g lab epic. Its sibling modules are present —
lab/llm.rs, lab/notebook.rs, lab/spec.rs. An analysis layer built and never connected to the
lab that motivated it is exactly the shape bd-16g.1.5 (notebook renderer) and bd-16g.1.3
(lab state machine) would consume.

NOT VERIFIED, and I am not asserting it: WHICH module should be the consumer. lab/notebook.rs
and lab/llm.rs are the plausible candidates on name alone; I have not read either. Whoever
takes this should establish the intended consumer from bd-16g.1.3/.1.5 rather than picking
one that compiles.

════ WHY I STOPPED ════

The instruction was to stop and report if the cluster resolved to an empty file. It resolves
to something stronger: an entire module with no external consumer, where "remove the dead
items" would cascade to removing all of it. That is a file-level disposition and an owner
decision under AGENTS.md Rule 1, not mine and not something to reach by increments.

NOTHING DELETED. NOTHING REMOVED. NO CODE EDITED under this bead.

════ REVISED DISPOSITION ════

  1. StatsError::ZeroVariance — KEEP AND WIRE. paired_diff must return it (or an explicit
     undefined-effect marker) when sd_diff <= 1e-12, with a test on a genuine zero-variance
     cohort. Do not keep the 0.0 fallback. This one is actionable now and independent of the
     module-wiring question.
  2. Correction::HolmBonferroni / ::BenjaminiHochberg — KEEP. serde-constructible via
     Effect.correction; removal would break deserialization.
  3. adjust_multiple_comparisons (bd-7vdu) — DO NOT DELETE. Uncalled because the whole module
     is uncalled. Reclassify from "orphan deliverable" to "unwired analysis layer".
  4. THE MODULE ITSELF — owner decision. Either connect lab/stats.rs to the lab pipeline that
     bd-16g.1.3/.1.5 describe, or record explicitly that the analysis layer shipped
     unconnected and amend bd-16g.1.4's record. Do not resolve it by deletion without the
     owner's written authorization.

comments.author: CopperCat
comments.text:
ZERO-VARIANCE FIX LANDED, and the module-level resolution recorded below.

CODE CHANGE (crates/scriptbots-app/src/lab/stats.rs, no deletions):
  paired_diff now returns Err(StatsError::ZeroVariance) when sd_diff <= 1e-12. The old
  fallback set cohens_dz = 0.0, reading as NO EFFECT — the strongest possible wrong answer,
  because zero spread with a nonzero mean difference is a PERFECTLY CONSISTENT difference,
  an unbounded effect rather than an absent one. The variant existed for exactly this case
  and was constructed nowhere: it was right and the caller was wrong.

TESTS: 4 passed, 0 failed.
  paired_diff_refuses_a_degenerate_spread_instead_of_reporting_no_effect — two pairs each
    differing by exactly -10.0, so spread is zero and the mean difference is large. Fails
    loudly under the old fallback.
  paired_diff_refuses_a_single_pair — (n-1).max(1.0) makes one pair structurally zero
    variance; one pair cannot support a standardized effect size either.
  test_paired_diff_matched_seeds WIDENED, NOT INVERTED. It used a single pair, which now
    refuses. Rather than flip it to expect an error — which would have discarded its actual
    subject — it now uses two pairs and still asserts matched seeds produce mean_diff =
    -15.0, plus that cohens_dz is finite and NOT 0.0, so the old fallback cannot return.

──── MODULE-LEVEL RESOLUTION: WIRE IT. Do not record it as intentionally unused. ────

Recommendation, with the reasoning so the next person can overrule it on evidence:

  1. IT WAS NOT BUILT TO BE UNUSED. bd-16g.1.4 closed it as 'Analysis layer: effect sizes
     with CIs over matched-seed runs' — a layer, i.e. a thing other things sit on. Its
     siblings lab/llm.rs, lab/notebook.rs and lab/spec.rs all exist. Nothing in its history
     suggests a deliberate standalone utility.
  2. ITS CONTENT IS SPECIFIC, NOT GENERIC. paired_diff, hedges_g with small-sample bias
     correction, deterministic bootstrap_ci and Holm-Bonferroni correction are exactly what
     bd-16g.1.4's stated purpose needs. A module written to be optional would not carry a
     multiple-comparison correction; that only matters when many effects are reported
     together, which implies an intended reporting consumer.
  3. Effect.correction is SERDE-VISIBLE. Recording it as intentionally unused would leave a
     deserializable field that nothing applies — a config-visible knob with no consumer,
     which is worse than a dead one because it silently accepts a setting it ignores.
  4. bd-h189 (hardcoded p_value: 0.05) is currently harmless ONLY because nothing reads it.
     Wiring MUST NOT precede fixing it, or the first consumer starts publishing a fabricated
     statistic. bd-h189 is a hard prerequisite.

  NOT VERIFIED, and it is the next person's first job: WHICH module should consume it.
  lab/notebook.rs and lab/llm.rs are plausible on name alone. I have read neither. Establish
  the intended consumer from bd-16g.1.3 (lab state machine) and bd-16g.1.5 (notebook renderer
  with provenance enforcement) rather than picking whichever compiles — picking by
  compilability is how a layer ends up wired to the wrong thing and looking finished.

  RULE 1 HOLDS REGARDLESS. No file deletion. If the owner instead decides the layer is
  genuinely surplus, the resolution is an explicit record on bd-16g.1.4 saying so, not
  removing the file.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
THE CONSUMER QUESTION, ANSWERED DEFINITIVELY: lab/stats.rs WAS ALWAYS UNWIRED. This is
SPECULATIVE CODE NEVER CONNECTED, NOT A REGRESSION. No consumer was ever removed, because no
consumer ever existed.

EVIDENCE (git archaeology, read-only; I did not edit the file -- CopperCat holds it):

  Introduced by 8d0e99cfd "app: Implement lab analysis stats layer with paired diff and
  Hedges g (bd-16g.1.4)". That commit touched exactly TWO files:
      crates/scriptbots-app/src/lab/stats.rs   +305
      crates/scriptbots-app/src/lab/mod.rs     +2
  The two lines in mod.rs are, in full:
      pub mod stats;
      (blank)

  git log -S "stats::" -- crates/scriptbots-app/src/lab/mod.rs   ->  no commits, ever.
  grep for lab::stats / stats:: across crates/scriptbots-app/src/ excluding stats.rs itself
      ->  no matches today.

  So: the module was declared and never called, in the same commit that created it, and in
  every commit since. The +2 in mod.rs is the declaration, not a wiring.

WHY THE DISTINCTION CHANGES THE REMEDY. A regression would argue for restoring the caller --
find what used to consume it and reconnect. That is not this. The layer was never
load-bearing, so the real question is whether anything SHOULD consume it, and until something
does, every statistic in it is exercised only by its own tests. Removing it and re-adding it
when a consumer exists is a legitimate option here in a way it would not be for a regression.

LINK TO bd-h189, AND A CORRECTION TO THE OBVIOUS READING OF IT.

The tempting story is "an analysis layer nobody wired, plus a consumer that faked the value
instead of calling it" -- two findings meeting from opposite ends. THAT IS NOT WHAT HAPPENED,
and the evidence rules it out: there was never a consumer, so no consumer could have faked
anything. The hardcoded p_value = 0.05 was INSIDE paired_diff's own return statement, in the
analysis layer itself.

They are the same story from the SAME end: a module written speculatively, containing a
fabricated statistic, with no consumer that could ever have noticed. The absence of a
consumer is precisely WHY the constant survived -- nothing downstream ever compared a p-value
across two datasets and saw the same number twice. bd-16g.1.4 closed claiming this was
implemented "with tests"; those tests exercise the function and assert its existence rather
than its values, which is the second reason it survived.

STATUS OF THE RELATED DEFECTS IN THIS FILE, for whoever reads this next:
  bd-h189 (hardcoded p_value)              -- ALREADY FIXED by 650e9ec52 "fix(app/lab):
                                              compute the paired p-value instead of returning
                                              a hardcoded 0.05".
  bd-7453 (degenerate spread / ZeroVariance) -- addressed by c74f30c3e.
  bd-7vdu (adjust_multiple_comparisons)     -- STILL OPEN: one grep hit workspace-wide, its
                                              own definition. Zero call sites, zero tests.
  Also unaudited from the same bd-16g.1.4 close: hedges_g, bootstrap_ci, RunSummary. Same two
  questions apply to each -- is it called, and does a test assert its VALUE or its existence?

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
FULL AUDIT OF THE REMAINING bd-16g.1.4 DELIVERABLES. Requested question: for each, is the
value COMPUTED from inputs, and is it CONSUMED. Verdict: shape 10 is SYSTEMIC in this
module, not isolated -- but bootstrap_ci is genuinely correct and that is worth recording.

  symbol                          computed?                          consumed?
  ------------------------------  ---------------------------------  ---------
  paired_diff -> p_value          NOW COMPUTED (fixed 650e9ec52)     orphaned
  paired_diff -> cohens_dz        computed; refuses degenerate       orphaned
                                  spread (c74f30c3e)
  hedges_g -> statistic           computed BUT retains the           orphaned
                                  `else { 0.0 }` degenerate
                                  fallback c74f30c3e fixed in
                                  paired_diff  -> bd-gbwn
  hedges_g -> ci_95               CONSTANT: (g - 1.96*0.1,           orphaned
                                  g + 1.96*0.1). Hardcoded SE of
                                  0.1; width NEVER varies with
                                  n or variance  -> bd-gbwn
  bootstrap_ci                    GENUINELY COMPUTED. Correct.       orphaned
                                  (internal caller only)
  adjust_multiple_comparisons     NO-OP. Documented as               orphaned
                                  Holm-Bonferroni; sets
                                  effect.correction = Some(method)
                                  and adjusts nothing  -> bd-7vdu
  RunSummary, Effect              plain data, no computation         orphaned

CONFIRMED CORRECT, recorded because today has turned up enough of the opposite: bootstrap_ci
(stats.rs:252) is a real bootstrap -- LCG resampling with replacement, sorted means, 2.5/97.5
percentile bounds, deterministic by seed. Two minor robustness notes, NOT fabrications:
empty input returns (0.0, 0.0) rather than an error, and iters == 0 would index an empty
vector. Neither is a fake value.

adjust_multiple_comparisons IS WORSE THAN bd-7vdu RECORDS. That bead says "pub, uncalled and
untested", which is true. The deeper problem is that it would not work if it WERE called: it
stamps effects as corrected without adjusting any statistic. A caller would get effects
labelled "HolmBonferroni" carrying uncorrected values -- a certification of a correction that
did not happen.

CONSUMPTION: ZERO EXTERNAL CONSUMERS FOR THE ENTIRE MODULE, which corroborates this bead
comprehensively. Two apparent consumers are FALSE POSITIVES and are worth naming because a
grep audit would count them:
  - RunSummary appears 3x in crates/scriptbots-analytics/src/lib.rs -- but that is a
    DIFFERENT type, `struct RunSummary;`, a unit struct implementing Report. Unrelated.
  - crates/scriptbots-app/src/lab/notebook.rs does NOT import lab::stats. It defines its own
    EffectRef with the same field shape as stats::Effect (metric, statistic, ci_95,
    underpowered) -- a PARALLEL TYPE, duplicated rather than reused. If stats::Effect gains a
    field, EffectRef will not.

WHY THE WHOLE CLUSTER SURVIVED, one mechanism: with no consumer, nobody ever ran two datasets
through these functions and noticed that a p-value, or a CI width, or a "correction" never
changed. Fabricated values are invisible exactly when nothing consumes them. The second
mechanism is the test shape -- bd-16g.1.4 closed claiming "with tests", and those tests
assert that functions RETURN something rather than asserting what they return.

SCORECARD FOR THAT CLOSE REASON: of five named deliverables, one (bootstrap_ci) is correct,
two were fabricated (paired_diff's p_value, hedges_g's ci_95), one is a no-op
(adjust_multiple_comparisons), one is inert data (RunSummary). Zero were wired.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
CONCLUSION: lab/stats.rs IS SUPERSEDED BY crates/scriptbots-analytics. Recording the analysis
and the exact scope of the evidence. DELETION IS THE REMAINING STEP AND IT IS THE OWNER'S
DECISION, NOT MINE -- I am not proposing to take it, and AGENTS.md Rule 1 forbids it without
express written permission. This bead exists so that decision is a one-line approval rather
than an open question.

CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER WORDING: in bd-ph6w I wrote the disposition as "Either delete it,
or make it a thin re-export". Offering deletion as one of two equal options was wrong of me.
The re-export is an architecture proposal; the deletion is a request that only the owner can
grant. Amended there too.

SCOPE OF WHAT I ESTABLISHED -- STATED PRECISELY, because the two claims are not the same:

  I established NO CONSUMERS OUTSIDE ITS OWN MODULE.
  I did NOT establish "no consumers at all", and that stronger claim would be FALSE.

  Internal consumers DO exist:
    - bootstrap_ci is called by paired_diff (stats.rs:177).
    - The #[cfg(test)] module calls paired_diff at :352, :385, :435, :438 and hedges_g.
  Outside the file:
    - Zero references anywhere in crates/ to paired_diff, hedges_g, bootstrap_ci,
      adjust_multiple_comparisons, Correction, or lab::stats.
    - lab/mod.rs:17 contains `pub mod stats;` -- a DECLARATION, not a call. `git log -S
      "stats::" -- crates/scriptbots-app/src/lab/mod.rs` returns no commits, ever.
    - No `pub use` re-export of it anywhere.

REACHABILITY CAVEAT THAT MATTERS FOR ANY DELETION DECISION: lib.rs:3053 declares `pub mod
lab;`, so `scriptbots_app::lab::stats::*` is part of this crate's PUBLIC API surface. "No
in-workspace references" is not the same as "unreachable" -- an external consumer of the
crate could call it today. Whether that matters depends on whether scriptbots-app is
consumed as a library outside this repo, which I did not establish.

METHOD AND ITS LIMITS, stated because this codebase has already burned people on it: my
evidence is grep across crates/ plus git pickaxe on the symbol. That catches direct
references. It would MISS macro-generated call sites, trait-object dispatch, and reflection-
style lookups. It also produced TWO false positives during this audit that I had to run down
by hand -- `RunSummary` appeared to have 3 external consumers but those are a DIFFERENT unit
struct in scriptbots-analytics, and `Effect` appeared to have 9 but those are prose comments
plus an unrelated enum variant. The precedent worth remembering is visual_cue_for_event,
which had synthetic call sites nobody expected. Treat this as strong evidence, not proof.

WHAT WOULD RE-EXPORT CLEANLY (the architecture proposal, which is safe to act on):
Requires adding a scriptbots-app -> scriptbots-analytics dependency, which does NOT currently
exist and is also the blocker on bd-h189's suggested fix.

  lab symbol                     analytics equivalent                      status
  -----------------------------  ----------------------------------------  ---------------
  bootstrap_ci                   bootstrap_mean_difference_ci, or          direct swap
                                 moving_block_bootstrap_mean_ci for
                                 autocorrelated series
  paired_diff -> p_value         permutation_test_mean_difference          direct swap
                                 (already has the (count+1)/(n+1)
                                 correction)
  paired_diff -> cohens_dz       cohens_d                                  direct swap
  hedges_g -> statistic          cohens_d + the small-sample correction     PARTIAL: analytics
                                 factor                                     has cohens_d but
                                                                            NO hedges/small-
                                                                            sample correction.
                                                                            That factor would
                                                                            need porting INTO
                                                                            analytics.
  hedges_g -> ci_95              bootstrap over the pooled samples          needs writing;
                                                                            currently constant
                                                                            (bd-gbwn)
  adjust_multiple_comparisons    compare.rs carries `fdr` params and a      PARTIAL: analytics
                                 `significant_fdr` outcome plus a test      does FDR, not
                                 fdr_keeps_the_real_metrics_and_drops_      Holm-Bonferroni.
                                 the_null_ones                              Different method,
                                                                            not a drop-in.

  So: 3 direct swaps, 3 that need work in analytics first. The migration is real but not
  free, and nothing about it requires removing a file.

COST OF WAITING: an unreferenced 312-line file costs nothing while the decision sits. It
compiles, it is covered by its own tests, and bd-gbwn/bd-7vdu record its defects if it stays.

title: brain-neuro: advertised sigmoid is inverted by pinned NeuroFlow 0.2.0
description: Confirmed end-to-end parity defect. NeuroflowActivation::Sigmoid is documented as logistic sigmoid and maps to neuroflow::activators::Type::Sigmoid, but pinned NeuroFlow 0.2.0 implements 1/(1+exp(x)), a decreasing function. Original ScriptBots uses 1/(1+exp(-x)). Add an empty-hidden-topology test with +/-1 output bias proving positive input is above 0.5 and negative below, supply a correct local activation across construction/restore, and bind the semantic change to the adapter identity.
close_reason: Fixed in 48c87cb2b: install a correct increasing logistic custom activation for NeuroFlow sigmoid construction and snapshot restore, validate its serialized tag, and cover positive/negative bias plus clone restore. Remote proof: cargo test -p scriptbots-brain-neuro passed 15 unit and 1 integration test; cargo check -p scriptbots-brain-neuro --all-targets passed. Scoped clippy was blocked exclusively by 267 errors in concurrently modified scriptbots-core.

comments.author: WildDuck
comments.text: HISTORICAL-RESIDUAL-1 rank 5 — Bucket B, keep closed. 48c87cb2b installs a correct increasing logistic custom activation for construction and restore, validates the serialized custom tag, and retains signed-bias/clone regressions. NeuroFlow is explicitly withheld from the admitted versioned adapter roster, so no false protocol identity is published. Execution claims are unscored.

title: core/web: target-width RNG makes seeded native and WASM worlds diverge before tick 1
description:
Actual headless Chrome execution for bd-2wj is now available and proves a genuine production divergence. The uninjected native-SIMD fixture versus scalar-WASM browser lane fails at tick 1: agent[0] position.x expected 287.596893311, actual 210.409286499, absolute delta 77.187606812, config_hash 0xc314c320074babe0. This is not floating-point tolerance drift. crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs selects xoshiro256++ for target_pointer_width=64 and xoshiro128++ for target_pointer_width=16/32 in SmallRngStream, so identical u64 seeds intentionally initialize different scientific worlds on native and wasm32. crates/scriptbots-web/src/lib.rs also owns a WanderBrain with direct rand::rngs::SmallRng, duplicating the same target-dependent boundary.

Acceptance: adopt one explicitly versioned portable scientific RNG algorithm and state codec across 64-bit native and 32-bit WASM; define the checkpoint/protocol migration rather than silently reinterpreting old state; route WanderBrain and every web scientific draw through that portable stream; regenerate the native parity fixture only with a digest-change rationale; run the actual matching-ChromeDriver browser lanes and prove injected fault red plus uninjected green. The comparator must retain first tick/agent/field/value diagnostics. Do not loosen tolerances or preseed snapshots to mask different initialization streams.
close_reason: Closed by aaac3fd99: fixed seeds now use one target-independent Xoshiro256++/SplitMix64 stream and codec across native/WASM; native sequence and fixture SHA-256 69355b87 are unchanged; legacy Xoshiro128++ WASM state is typed-rejected. RCH sequence/freshness proofs pass. Real Chrome 150 plus matching ChromeDriver proves injected negative control red (12/13, exact tick/agent/field/values/allowed/config hash) and uninjected cross-runtime parity green (13/13). The original defect was a 77.187606812 tick-1 position error from selecting different algorithms by pointer width; named per-field scalar/SIMD drift bounds remain guarded by the red negative control.

comments.text: CONTRACT DECISION BEFORE IMPLEMENTATION: fixed seeds are portable across native/WASM. Evidence: README.md:523-528 defines reproducible fixed-seed runs; README.md:1002-1005 promises native/WASM snapshot comparison for fixed seeds; crates/scriptbots-web/src/lib.rs:1802+ implements true cross-architecture parity; the live acceptance explicitly requires one target-independent versioned algorithm/codec. title: Delete crates/scriptbots-app/src/terminal/paint.rs — dead duplicate painter, already out of the build (needs Rule 1 permission)
description:
Housekeeping remainder of bd-c1z8, which is closed: the crate already compiles exactly ONE
sub-cell painter. This bead is only the physical file removal, which needs a decision I am not
permitted to make.

STATE. `pub mod paint;` was removed in 2a05f8589, so paint.rs is no longer part of the build.
subcell.rs is the sole painter: wired into the live MapWidget canvas and covered by the
bd-2z0.14.2.1 tests. paint.rs remains on disk, compiling nothing, referenced by nothing.

WHY IT IS NOT ALREADY DELETED. AGENTS.md Rule 1 requires express written permission that names
the file. bd-c1z8 recorded the same constraint from the start ("DELETION IS NOT AUTHORIZED"),
and I asked twice without getting a file-naming answer, so I converged the build instead - which
achieves the engineering outcome non-destructively and leaves the irreversible step to the owner.

NOTHING IS LOST BY DELETING IT. Every item unique to paint.rs was evaluated against subcell.rs
before the declaration was dropped (full analysis in the bd-c1z8 comments): quantize_16/256,
braille_char, and DitherMode all have equal-or-better equivalents in subcell.rs that are the
wired and tested ones; blend_over is the only genuinely unique capability and is unused, because
the canvas repaints fully from world data every frame by design. subcell.rs is a strict superset.

WHEN AUTHORIZED, THREE THINGS GO TOGETHER:
  1. git rm crates/scriptbots-app/src/terminal/paint.rs
  2. remove "paint.rs" from KNOWN_DUPLICATE_MODULES in terminal/mod.rs
  3. delete the_exempt_duplicate_painter_stays_out_of_the_build, whose whole subject is the
     exemption
Step 2 is what makes this worth doing rather than leaving forever: it retires the guard's only
allowlist entry, so no_two_terminal_modules_define_the_same_item runs with NO exemptions and the
real-tree negative case is demonstrated for free (the four colliding names - ColorDepth,
quantize, SubCellMode, SubPixel - stop existing).

COST OF LEAVING IT: low but not zero. An undeclared .rs file is not compiled, so it is not
format-checked, lint-checked, or type-checked, and it will rot silently. The guard prevents it
rejoining the build, so the risk is confined to a stale file on disk.

Filed by YellowLake while closing bd-c1z8.

title: storage: bounded reads are impossible — pinned fsqlite has no interrupt for a running statement
description:
THE CAPABILITY GAP behind bd-aj12, filed separately so a read that can hang forever stays visible rather than being retired by re-scoping.

AsyncReadLane advertises deadline- and cancellation-bounded reads. It cannot deliver them, and neither can any consumer of the pinned engine, because there is no mechanism to stop a statement once it starts.

MEASURED, not inferred. Against a ~6.3 s self-join, every Budget dimension was ignored and the complete result returned:
  deadline 1 ms    6.33s  Ok, complete result (COUNT = 512000, the full 80^3 join)
  poll_quota 100   6.19s  Ok, complete result
  poll_quota 1     6.16s  Ok, complete result
  cost_quota 1     6.21s  Ok, complete result
poll_quota was isolated deliberately: Budget::MINIMAL differs from INFINITE only in that field, and a MINIMAL close is what produces the Database(Busy) of bd-qan3 — so quota enforcement exists, but only around the close handshake, never inside a running statement.

ROOT CAUSE. fsqlite/src/async_api.rs:423 query_with_params calls checkpoint_or_interrupt(cx) ONCE before dispatch, then sends the statement over an mpsc channel to a worker thread that holds no reference to the Cx. Nothing can stop it mid-scan. fsqlite-core exposes no interrupt handle, no progress callback, and no sqlite3_interrupt equivalent — grepped for interrupt/InterruptHandle/progress_handler and found none. The !Send thread-confined connection independently forecloses signalling it from another thread even if such a handle existed.

NOT A LOCAL FIX. fsqlite is pinned at version =0.1.16, rev e536d7f8ca102b3eb5236bef48514582379f9346. Requiring the capability means an upstream change and then a deliberate re-pin. UNPINNING A DELIBERATELY PINNED DEPENDENCY IS THE OWNER'S DECISION, NOT THIS SWARM'S — this bead records the gap and does not authorize that.

A TRAP FOR WHOEVER IMPLEMENTS IT. In recv_sync_response (async_api.rs:146-151) the awaiting side can already return Err(Interrupt) on cancellation, but the blocking-pool thread stays parked on the engine worker and, when the query finally completes, discards the result with:
    let _ = result_tx.send(&waiter_cx, result).map_err(blocking_wait_send_err);
No counter, no log, no error — the same silent-discard shape as the StorageBuffer defect fixed in f9248b49d. Unreachable today only because cancellation never fires. Implementing cancellation WITHOUT also handling the abandoned result would convert today's honest hang into a silent drop plus a wedged blocking slot. All three must land together: stop the statement, release the slot, account for a late-arriving result.

NO CURRENT DATA LOSS. Because no bound ever fires, every read returns its complete result or a typed error; nothing partial. The present behaviour is a hang, which is at least honest.

READY-MADE ACCEPTANCE. crates/scriptbots-storage/tests/async_lane.rs already contains the two tests, correct as written and ignored against this gap: cancelled_query_surfaces_typed_interrupt_and_lane_recovers and sub_ms_deadline_expires_a_slow_query. They will pass unchanged once a statement can be interrupted. probe_which_budget_fields_bound_a_running_query is the detector: run it after any fsqlite bump, and if any row stops returning a complete result the capability has arrived.
close_reason: Completed with honest fail-closed refusal: the unavailable async lane cannot be constructed or execute SQL, rejects before path access with exact-pin diagnostics, and directs callers to snapshots or explicitly unbounded read-only StorageReader.

title: visual-5: ART DIRECTION — bioluminescent substrate, emissive organisms, one coherent look
description:
Parent bd-ikts. Technically-correct rendering still looks amateur without a deliberate art direction, and its absence is why the current output reads as a spreadsheet even where the math is right. This bead sets ONE look and every other visual bead conforms to it.

DIRECTION: bioluminescent petri dish / dark-field microscopy. Chosen because it solves the project's actual visual problems rather than being a taste preference:
- The current captures fail mostly because everything is equally bright and equally saturated, so nothing reads as figure vs ground. A DARK substrate with LUMINOUS agents fixes figure/ground instantly.
- Agents are currently indistinguishable from terrain dither. Emissive agents against a dark field are unmissable at any zoom, which also fixes the 5k-agent legibility problem without LOD tricks.
- The post stack already implements bloom/tonemap/exposure/ACES (294 hits for bloom alone) and is currently invisible. Bloom on emissive organisms against dark terrain is exactly the case where that stack earns its keep, so this direction turns existing dead machinery into the primary visual effect.
- It suits the subject: this is artificial LIFE. Glowing cells in a dish is honest to what the simulation is, where saturated lime-green tiles are not.

SPECIFICS:
- Substrate: near-black to deep blue-violet. Terrain expressed through subtle material and depth (normal-derived shading, moisture sheen, elevation ambient occlusion), NOT through hue swaps. Biomes differ in material and value, not in crayon colour.
- Agents: emissive core, diet-driven hue on a narrow deliberate ramp (herbivore cool-cyan through carnivore hot-magenta), luminance carrying health and age. Visible orientation. Spike as a hard bright edge when extended.
- Food: soft luminous motes with falloff, denser as clusters rather than per-cell squares.
- Water: darker than land with specular response, so hydrology reads without a blue crayon.
- Events: combat as a brief hot flash, birth as a soft bloom, death as a fading ember.
- Strict palette discipline: define the ramp ONCE in visual.rs as named constants. No renderer may invent a colour.

Deliverable: the palette and material constants in visual.rs, a written one-page direction note in docs/, and a reference capture. Every later visual bead is judged against this.
close_reason: Art direction defined and landed as a single source in visual.rs (32e408ecc); appearance unvalidated — see comment, bd-lhml holds the proof

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:

The two live probes prove the backend is not the cause: GPUI 1280x720 and Bevy 1600x900 both show the same hard cell grid, lime/blue/orange hue blocks, pale-grey center, near-equal scene luminance, and agents disappearing into tile noise. Therefore establish figure/ground in one core style before renderer wiring.

TYPE SHAPE: `MaterialStyle { albedo_srgb:[f32;3], emissive_srgb:[f32;3], emissive_gain:f32, perceptual_roughness:f32, reflectance:f32, normal_strength:f32 }`; `VisualStyleV1 { substrate, terrain:[TerrainMaterialStyle;6], agents, food, events, chrome, atmosphere }`; sole literal authority `pub const BIOLUMINESCENT_DARK_FIELD_V1: VisualStyleV1`. Existing resolvers must read the style; do not add a parallel palette.

SUBSTRATE/ATMOSPHERE: abyss `[0.010,0.012,0.028]`; base `[0.022,0.028,0.070]`; depth-violet `[0.045,0.035,0.110]`; distant haze `[0.095,0.075,0.180]`; fog `[0.025,0.030,0.080]`; bloom threshold `0.70`; bloom intensity `0.55`; vignette `0.35`; exposure `1.0`. TERRAIN MATERIALS, in canonical kind order, `(albedo, emissive, gain, roughness, reflectance, normal)`:

ShallowWater `([0.028,0.055,0.115],[0.010,0.025,0.075],0.08,0.22,0.62,0.55)`;

These stay in one blue-violet family. Biome identity comes from value, roughness, reflectance, normals, moisture sheen, elevation/AO, and splat weights, never crayon hue swaps. Water is darker, smoother, and more reflective than land.

AGENTS: herbivore cool-cyan `[0.18,0.86,1.00]`; carnivore hot-magenta `[1.00,0.60,0.92]`; their Rec.709 luminances are about `0.726` and `0.708`, so diet changes hue without falsely encoding health. Body hue comes from this diet ramp; genome color is at most a constrained lineage accent, never the main body authority. Health luminance floor `0.42`; age saturation/luminance floor `0.78`; base emissive gain `2.40`; hover `3.20`; selected `4.40`; boost `5.20`. Wheel `[0.09,0.12,0.22]`; selection rim `[0.72,0.94,1.00]`; spike core `[1.00,0.82,0.96]`, spike gain `6.00`. Remove temperature hue mixing from `diet_stripe_color`; temperature may later modulate a non-hue material channel. Add `age_ticks/reference_age_ticks` to `AgentVisualInput` so health and age are resolved once in core.

FOOD: stable mint-cyan mote hue, core `[0.55,1.00,0.82]`, halo `[0.18,0.88,0.70]`; sparse-to-dense emissive gain `0.80 -> 2.80`, alpha `0.28 -> 0.92`, relative radius `0.35 -> 1.15`. Density changes count/visibility/energy, not hue. Shimmer remains tick-and-cell deterministic.

EVENTS: combat core `[1.00,0.22,0.45]`, accent `[1.00,0.78,0.34]`, gain `6.0`, duration `8`; birth core `[0.55,0.92,1.00]`, accent `[0.86,0.62,1.00]`, gain `3.5`, duration `24`; death ember `[1.00,0.32,0.12]`, ash `[0.24,0.12,0.22]`, gain `2.2`, duration `36`; eat uses food core/halo, gain `1.8`, duration `12`; reproduce `[0.72,0.70,1.00]` + `[0.40,0.92,1.00]`, gain `3.0`, duration `28`; spike flash `[1,1,1]` + spike core, gain `5.5`, duration `6`. Keep HDR gain separate from clamped sRGB and accessibility transforms.

CHROME TOKENS for bd-f4x0, defined in the same style so UI renderers do not invent colors: surface `[0.025,0.030,0.070]`; elevated `[0.045,0.050,0.105]`; border `[0.16,0.20,0.32]`; primary text `[0.88,0.92,1.00]`; muted text `[0.52,0.59,0.72]`; accent cyan `[0.18,0.86,1.00]`; accent magenta `[1.00,0.60,0.92]`; warning `[1.00,0.72,0.28]`; danger `[1.00,0.22,0.45]`.

REQUIRED TESTS: every component finite; sRGB/material coefficients in range and gains nonnegative; diet endpoint luminance delta <=0.03; health and age monotonically lower luminance/saturation without changing diet ordering; weakest visible agent brighter than brightest terrain; both water materials darker, smoother, and more reflective than land; food hue constant while visibility/gain rise with density; all event durations positive; paused shimmer stable. Deliberately replace legacy red/green diet, crayon terrain, and green/gold food goldens rather than blessing them. Rendering remains pure/read-only.

NEXT: wait for CopperCat to commit/release visual.rs, reserve it exclusively under bd-9pqz, implement the typed style and rewrite existing core resolvers/tests, then write `docs/visual_art_direction.md` and produce `docs/rendering_reference/bioluminescent_dark_field_v1.png` as a clearly labeled art-direction reference, not renderer proof. Dependent renderer adoption belongs to bd-l4gu/bd-1lls/bd-ydym/bd-bufm/bd-f4x0 and must consume this API without new scene-color literals.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
ORCHESTRATOR — closing the deliverable, flagging the direction as UNVALIDATED.

What shipped: the bioluminescent dark-field direction is defined once, numerically, and landed in core/src/visual.rs as a single visual contract (32e408ecc), with the GPUI renderer calling it (render/lib.rs 13839, 14548, 15084, 15088). That was the bead's actual scope and it is met — no renderer invents a colour any more.

What is NOT established, and this is the orchestrator's own call under test: whether the direction WORKS. The first real 1280x720 Metal captures render near-black. Terrain, food and agents are all present in code and none are legible in the image. Compare live_probes/2026-07-25/bd-l4gu_before_1280x720.png (garish saturated lime, but every element identifiable) against live_probes/bd-1lls/after_continuous_fields_1280x720.png (correct pipeline, near-black, nothing readable). The epic has traded unreadably-saturated for unreadably-dark.

The dark substrate was chosen because bloom/tonemap/exposure act on emissive bodies against dark fields — but that reasoning ASSUMES the post stack works. bd-lhml is currently establishing whether it runs and does nothing, or does not run. Until that is answered, this direction is a hypothesis with a failing observation against it.

If bd-lhml finds the post stack cannot be made to lift emissive elements off this substrate, the correct outcome is to REVISIT this direction rather than tune around it. A visual direction that only works in theory is worth less than a garish one that reads. Do not treat this closure as endorsement of the current appearance.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
ORCHESTRATOR CORRECTION — the direction is VALIDATED. I was wrong to call it a failing hypothesis.

I judged this on live_probes/bd-1lls/after_continuous_fields_1280x720.png as it stood at 05:15, which was a 12-agent fixture in a world too small to fill the viewport. That image was near-black and I concluded the dark-field direction did not read. That conclusion was drawn from a bad fixture, not from the direction.

I have now opened the 06:02 replacement — same path, 2,400x1,200 world, 96 agents, produced under bd-1lls's regression. It reads well and it looks like the thing this bead specified: food as bright cyan-mint luminous motes, clearly separable from the substrate; agents as discrete emissive bodies with visible orientation, on a cool-to-warm diet ramp; terrain a smooth continuous violet field with no cell grid anywhere. Set against live_probes/2026-07-25/bd-l4gu_before_1280x720.png — saturated lime squares with agents indistinguishable from dither — this is not a marginal improvement, it is a different quality of image.

So: my earlier note said that if the post stack could not lift emissive elements off this substrate, the direction should be revisited rather than tuned around. That contingency has not fired. Emissive elements DO lift off the substrate. Do not revisit the direction.

What remains is genuinely narrower than I claimed: terrain is underexposed and low-contrast, so the substrate carries less material detail than intended. That is bd-lhml's exposure work and it is tuning, not a rethink.

Lesson worth recording, since two of us nearly acted on it: a visual judgement made against an unrepresentative fixture is worth nothing. WildDuck fixing the fixture — 96 agents, real food, frame-filling assertion — changed the verdict completely.

title: core reproduction: aborted-birth refund restores a contaminated reproduction_counter preimage, not the transaction's true preimage
description:
Two tests are RED on main (confirmed at 47cc2bfe6 and at ced12aeb7; both fail identically):

  crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs:32283  population_factory_failure_aborts_and_refunds_queued_births
  crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs:32426  offspring_snapshot_and_mutation_failures_are_terminal_and_refunded

Both fail on the SAME assertion:
  assertion failed: (parent_runtime.reproduction_counter - 1.0).abs() < f32::EPSILON

WHICH VALUE IS NOT RESTORED
reproduction_counter. Energy IS restored correctly -- the adjacent assertion on the line
immediately above each failure (lib.rs:32282 and lib.rs:32425) PASSES. Only the counter
is wrong, and that asymmetry is the whole diagnosis.

MECHANISM (verified by reading, not inferred)
stage_reproduction mutates and then snapshots the same field in one pass:
  lib.rs:21115  runtime.reproduction_counter += reproduction_rate;   <-- per-tick accrual
  lib.rs:21197  let parent_energy_before_debit = parent_runtime_snapshot.energy;
  lib.rs:21198  let parent_reproduction_counter_before_reset = ...reproduction_counter;
  lib.rs:21250  parent_runtime.reproduction_counter = 0.0;           <-- the reset being undone
  lib.rs:21309  parent.reproduction_counter = order.parent_reproduction_counter_before_reset;

Energy's only mutation (the debit at lib.rs:21249) happens AFTER its capture at 21197, so
its preimage is clean. The counter is incremented at 21115 BEFORE its capture at 21198, so
the captured 'preimage' is already one tick's accrual past the value the transaction
started from. refund_spawn_orders (lib.rs:21300-21314) faithfully restores that
contaminated value, so a parent whose birth was aborted ends the tick closer to
reproducing than a parent that never attempted one.

TWO CANDIDATE RESOLUTIONS -- deliberately NOT choosing one
(a) The refund is incomplete: an aborted attempt should roll back the accrual too, and the
    capture must move above lib.rs:21115. The tests are then correct as written.
(b) The accrual is not part of the transaction: the agent aged a tick regardless of whether
    the birth succeeded, so retaining it is correct and both tests encode a wrong
    expectation; they should assert 1.0 + reproduction_rate.
This is a scientific-semantics call about what an aborted reproduction transaction owns.
It should be made explicitly, not by whichever side gets edited first.

DIGEST IMPACT: YES under either resolution. reproduction_counter is digest-encoded per
agent at lib.rs:4049 (encoder.f32(runtime.reproduction_counter)), and the staged preimage
is separately encoded at lib.rs:23541 (encoder.f32(spawn.parent_reproduction_counter_before_reset)).
Resolution (a) moves the world digest for any run containing an aborted birth and changes
the pending-spawn encoding. This cannot land as a drive-by.

PROVENANCE: not a regression from current swarm work. The accrual line predates the
preimage machinery -- 'runtime.reproduction_counter += reproduction_rate' comes from
a17483b7a, while parent_reproduction_counter_before_reset was introduced later by 6a9fc9a5f
(bd-1kxd, agent-keyed RNG continuations). The capture was added downstream of a mutation
that was already there.

NOT COVERED BY AN OPEN BEAD. bd-cqja recorded a full-suite run with only ONE failure
(every_injectable_fault_turns_the_gate_red, 'fault DropCombatPosting was not detected within
64 ticks' -- still red today with a byte-identical message, out of scope here). bd-cqja is
CLOSED, so these two failures currently have no owner.

RULED OUT as the cause: bd-v69t (ced12aeb7). build_child_runtime is infallible, returns only
the CHILD runtime, and is called at lib.rs:21226 -- after the captures at 21197-21198 and
before the reset at 21250. No output of it reaches parent.reproduction_counter.

REPRO: cargo test -p scriptbots-core --lib -- population_factory_failure_aborts_and_refunds_queued_births offspring_snapshot_and_mutation_failures_are_terminal_and_refunded
close_reason: Resolved stale refund expectations in b29345dfa553: completed ticks preserve per-tick reproduction accrual; production transaction boundary remains unchanged. Path fmt/diff and RCH clippy passed; full RCH test gate inconclusive twice due bd-x1ec pre-Cargo mkdir capacity, recorded in comment 920.

comments.author: QuietBeaver
comments.text:
HARNESS FINDING: these two failures silently suppress the ENTIRE integration layer of scriptbots-core.

MECHANISM
'cargo test' runs each test binary in sequence and stops at the first binary that exits
non-zero, unless --no-fail-fast is passed. The lib binary (unittests src/lib.rs) fails on
these two refund tests plus every_injectable_fault_turns_the_gate_red, so cargo aborts there
and never invokes any later target.

PROOF from a full local run of 'cargo test -p scriptbots-core' (1252.66s, exit 101):
  Running unittests src/lib.rs (.../deps/scriptbots_core-0d780e6f58c34b03)
  test result: FAILED. 503 passed; 3 failed; 2 ignored; 0 measured
...and exactly ONE 'Running' line in the whole log. Eight integration binaries never executed:
  crates/scriptbots-core/tests/clock_channel_parity.rs
  crates/scriptbots-core/tests/day_night_default_probe.rs
  crates/scriptbots-core/tests/explain_sensors_contract.rs
  crates/scriptbots-core/tests/heredity_proof.rs
  crates/scriptbots-core/tests/rng_sequence_compat.rs
  crates/scriptbots-core/tests/sense_radius_parity.rs
  crates/scriptbots-core/tests/world_digest_v1.rs
  crates/scriptbots-core/tests/world_integration.rs

WHY THIS COMPOUNDS THE BEAD
The suppressed set is precisely the oracle layer -- world digest, heredity proof, and RNG
sequence compatibility -- that would otherwise detect a determinism regression in reproduction.
So the defect recorded in this bead (an aborted birth leaving a contaminated reproduction_counter
preimage, which IS digest-encoded at lib.rs:4049 and lib.rs:23541) disables the very tests that
would catch its downstream effects. The bead is self-masking.

THE REMOTE PATH DOES NOT COVER IT EITHER. rch can only run 'cargo test -p scriptbots-core --lib';
the unfiltered invocation is exactly the one that dies on the scenarios/ rsync permission failure
recorded on bd-oite. So neither the local nor the remote documented gate has been executing these
eight binaries.

SUGGESTED MITIGATION (harness-level, independent of how this bead is resolved): make
--no-fail-fast the documented gate for this crate, so a pre-existing red binary cannot hide the
rest. That is a one-flag change and it restores visibility immediately, whereas fixing the three
red tests may take longer.

Related: bd-cqja already noted 'agents can currently only verify this crate via targeted filters,
which is how narrow verification gaps like bd-a9h1 survived in the first place.' This is the
concrete mechanism behind that observation, and it is worse than stated because the masking is
silent -- the run looks like a normal test failure, not like eight skipped binaries.

comments.author: WindySquirrel
comments.text: Scientific-semantics ruling: choose resolution (b), preserve completed-tick reproduction accrual. Current production is correct. Every live agent accrues before eligibility/cadence/admission, while the queued-birth transaction begins later and snapshots the immediate post-accrual/pre-reset value; a late spawn fault still completes bookkeeping and advances Tick(1). Legacy World.cpp likewise retains accumulated repcounter on rejected admission and resets only after reproduce() succeeds. Commit bffb1d1e8 changed these fixtures from f32::MIN_POSITIVE (whose addition rounded back to 1.0) to 1.0 but left the stale 1.0 expectations, exposing the mismatch. Planned fix: make the two failure tests expect initial + per-tick rate and pin the queued-order pre-reset value. No production state or digest changes; moving the capture would be the scientifically incorrect digest-changing alternative.

title: core/replay: replay_event_tick_cap bounds the cross-tick buffer, not the tick — 59 of every 60 ticks silently record zero action events
description:
crates/scriptbots-core/src/replay.rs:26-33 (record_replay_action_events).

WHAT IS WRONG
The cap is compared against `self.replay_events.len()`, which is the accumulated
buffer, but that buffer is drained ONLY at a persistence boundary
(crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs:21335, `std::mem::take(&mut self.replay_events)`
inside prepare_persistence). prepare_persistence returns `deferred()` without
draining whenever `next_tick % persistence_interval != 0` (lib.rs:20778-20787).
record_replay_action_events runs EVERY tick (lib.rs:21511, Actuation stage).

So with persistence_interval = N and replay_event_tick_cap = C:
  tick 1      -> records min(C, live agents) events, buffer saturates at C
  ticks 2..N  -> `self.replay_events.len() >= cap` is already true, early return,
                 records NOTHING
  tick N      -> the batch drains and the cycle repeats

WHY IT MATTERS
The shipped application default is `persistence_interval: 60`
(crates/scriptbots-app/src/main.rs:1624). A production run that opts into replay
verification therefore captures actuation decisions for 1 tick in 60 and drops
98.3% of them. The stream is still NONEMPTY, so the empty-vs-empty vacuity guard
described in README.md ('Nonzero empty-vs-empty runs now fail closed instead of
claiming verification') passes, and a replay comparison compares two equally
truncated streams and reports success. That is precisely the falsely-claimed
verification the README warns about. This is silent, not a crash.

The field name (`replay_event_tick_cap`), its doc comment (lib.rs:11016-11021,
'Maximum replay events recorded per tick'), and the module doc
(replay.rs:10-13, 'set the cap at or above their peak agent count so every live
agent is recorded every tick') all state per-tick semantics. Only
persistence_interval == 1 makes the implementation agree with them.

WHY NO TEST CAUGHT IT
crates/scriptbots-app/tests/replay_e2e.rs pins `--set persistence_interval=1`
(lines 57, and again at 239/288) — the single configuration in which the bug is
invisible. crates/scriptbots-core/src/replay.rs has no unit tests at all.

WHAT CORRECT LOOKS LIKE
Bound the number of events appended DURING THIS TICK, not the buffer length:
capture the buffer length on entry and stop after `cap` events have been pushed
this tick. Then a run with cap >= peak agent count records every live agent on
every tick regardless of persistence_interval, which is what the knob promises.
Document the resulting buffer footprint (up to cap * persistence_interval events
retained between drains) in the field doc so the memory cost is explicit rather
than paid for with silent data loss.

Companion: the same buffer-length check drops the driver-requested world digest
(see the sibling bead).
close_reason: Fixed in 84decacf8. record_replay_action_events now budgets each tick against the buffer as of tick entry, so every tick in a persistence window records its own actions regardless of persistence_interval. Regression test every_tick_in_a_persistence_window_records_its_own_actions fails against the pre-fix code and passes now.

title: offscreen harness cannot capture GPUI HUD chrome — no gpui frontend, and --dump-png bypasses the element tree
description:
Blocks visual evidence for bd-v9cz and every future bd-f4x0 chrome change. Investigated at the orchestrator's direction after being pointed at the existing harness; the harness is real and good, but it does not cover HUD chrome, and the gap is not a missing scene file.

WHAT THE HARNESS ACTUALLY COVERS
crates/scriptbots-app/src/scene.rs FrontendKind has exactly three variants:
  TerminalHeadless  - real ratatui TestBackend evidence
  Null              - synthetic deterministic driver
  BevyOffscreen     - Bevy offscreen GPU capture
There is no GPUI frontend. A scene .toml cannot select one.

WHY --dump-png IS NOT THE ANSWER EITHER
crates/scriptbots-app/src/main.rs:395-425 handles --dump-png by calling
  scriptbots_render::render_png_offscreen(&world_guard, w, h)
and lib.rs:9874 defines that as
  render_offscreen_scene(&OffscreenScene::capture(world), width, height)
which rasterizes a captured WORLD scene with its own Camera (lib.rs:9887). It takes &WorldState. It never constructs SimulationView and never calls render_overlay, render_hud_rail, render_perf_overlay or render_history_chart. It is a CPU world rasterizer that lives beside the GPUI element tree, not inside it.

The existing probe confirms this in its own words. docs/rendering_reference/live_probes/2026-07-17/gpui_offscreen.json describes gpui_offscreen_1280x720.png as: 'live GPUI world canvas: food-density field, terrain and water border cells; NOT a CPU surrogate'. That is the WORLD canvas. No HUD panel appears in it, because the code path that produced it cannot draw one.

CONSEQUENCE, AND WHY I DID NOT SHIP A SCENE ANYWAY
Adding a gpui scene through the existing path would produce an image of the world containing NONE of the docked panels, which could then be attached to bd-v9cz as 'proof' of a HUD layout it does not show. That is a convincing non-proof and is exactly the evidence class this epic exists to stamp out.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY NEEDED
A capability to render the GPUI element tree - SimulationView, not WorldState - to a pixel buffer headlessly, then a FrontendKind::GpuiOffscreen that drives it from a scene manifest at declared viewport sizes.

Starting point that already exists: the render crate's own tests drive real GPUI headlessly via gpui::TestApp::new() plus session.install(app) and window.dispatch_keystroke (see gpui_closed_world_shortcut_submits_one_intent_without_direct_mutation, lib.rs ~16300). That proves the element tree can be instantiated and driven without a display. What is missing is frame readback from that surface to RGBA.

ACCEPTANCE: a scene manifest can request a GPUI HUD capture at 1280x720 and 1600x900; the emitted PNG visibly contains the docked rail; the capture is deterministic enough to diff; and it runs in the same CI lane as the Bevy offscreen smoke scene.

Cross-refs: bd-v9cz (needs this for evidence), bd-f4x0 (every chrome change will need it), bd-2z0.14.3.4 (real-render capture harness v2 - this is the GPUI-side gap in that program).
close_reason: GPUI headless HUD capture works and is proven by images. crates/scriptbots-render/src/hud_capture.rs renders the real SimulationView through GuiSession via HeadlessAppContext + MetalHeadlessRenderer, no display. Evidence committed at 03c236b7e19b: docs/rendering_reference/live_probes/bd-v9cz/hud_docked_1280x720.png (2560x1440) and hud_docked_1600x900.png (3200x1800), both decoded by hand independently of the test. LIMIT: macOS-only, MetalHeadlessRenderer is the sole PlatformHeadlessRenderer upstream, so it cannot run on the Linux rch farm.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
PLATFORM FINDING — the harness cannot run on the rch build farm, and this is structural (cc_3).

The capture code compiles and RUNS on a Linux rch worker, then fails at readback:

  headless HUD capture failed at 1280x720:
    read back headless GPUI frame: render_to_image not available: no HeadlessRenderer configured

Cause, in gpui_platform/src/gpui_platform.rs:63-75 — current_headless_renderer() is
#[cfg(feature = "test-support")], and inside it:

  #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]     { Some(Box::new(MetalHeadlessRenderer::new())) }
  #[cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))] { None }

There is exactly one implementor of gpui::PlatformHeadlessRenderer in the whole zed tree
(gpui_macos/src/metal_renderer.rs:1783, MetalHeadlessRenderer). On any non-macOS target
the factory returns None and capture_screenshot fails. The rch workers are Linux Contabo
VPS boxes, so EVERY remote dispatch of this test will fail this way regardless of slots,
sync, or scheduling.

CONSEQUENCES THAT SHOULD SHAPE THE BEAD
1. This capability is macOS-only today. It is not a CI capability on a Linux runner, so
   the acceptance criterion 'runs in the same CI lane as the Bevy offscreen smoke scene'
   is NOT achievable as written — that lane is software/llvmpipe on Linux.
2. The test must therefore be gated to macOS. That gate has to be explicit and recorded,
   not silent: a test that quietly evaporates on the build farm is the same failure class
   this bead exists to fix.
3. Anyone extending this to Linux CI needs a second PlatformHeadlessRenderer implementor
   (Vulkan/Blade or a software rasterizer). That does not exist upstream at rev 5f8a7413;
   it is upstream work, not configuration.

Not a defect in the capture code — the GPUI path, session construction, window sizing and
run_until_parked all execute correctly right up to the readback call.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
CONFIRMED BY INSPECTION (orchestrator opened the file): docs/rendering_reference/live_probes/2026-07-25/bd-l4gu_before_1280x720.png contains NO chrome. No panels, no text, no HUD elements — pure world raster from the --dump-png path.

This settles the question this bead was opened on. The pre-existing capture route does not produce element-tree output at all, so it cannot serve as HUD-layout evidence and cannot be borrowed. bd-abu3 remains the only path to HUD chrome evidence, and the analysis in the bead description stands unamended:

  --dump-png -> render_png_offscreen(&WorldState) -> render_offscreen_scene(OffscreenScene::capture(world))
  is a CPU world rasterizer with its own Camera. It never constructs SimulationView, so no panel can
  ever appear in its output. Works on every platform precisely BECAUSE it never touches GPUI or Metal.

Corollary for anyone reading the July 17 probe: gpui_offscreen_1280x720.png is the same class of artifact. Its own gpui_offscreen.json describes the content as 'live GPUI world canvas: food-density field, terrain and water border cells'. World canvas, not chrome. The word 'gpui' in that filename refers to the app mode it was launched in, not to the element tree being rendered.

UNBLOCKED ON CONTENTION: running the capture under a dedicated CARGO_TARGET_DIR on a separate volume (/Volumes/USBNVME16TB, 5.1TiB free) removes the shared-target-lock problem entirely — no peer can block this test and it cannot block them. That is the workaround for bd-kkn7 for any test that structurally cannot be offloaded to the Linux rch farm, which this one cannot because MetalHeadlessRenderer is macOS-only.

title: Real-time WebSockets event stream and binary frame transport for sub-16ms canvas push
description:
WHY. While REST and MCP HTTP support polling and on-demand queries, high-fps web and remote TUI interfaces require a push-based binary stream for sub-16ms frame updates, live telemetry, and zero-latency client controls.

DESIGN.
- Implement an Axum WebSockets endpoint (/api/ws/stream) in scriptbots-app servers.
- Stream compact Postcard-encoded binary snapshots and EventRecord frames on tick boundaries.
- Support client backpressure handling, adaptive framerate throttling, and client subscription masks (e.g. telemetry-only, canvas-only, full-state).
- Expose bidirectional WebSocket control channel allowing remote clients to send control commands with backpressure feedback.

TESTS & ACCEPTANCE.
- Unit: Postcard frame serialization parity, subscription filtering correctness.
- Integration: Multi-client WebSocket broadcast soak test at 60 TPS without thread lock contention.
- Documentation & Swagger OpenAPI update.
close_reason: Completed WebSocket binary stream endpoint (/api/ws/stream) with Postcard frame transport and control command ingress in scriptbots-app/src/servers.rs.

title: Precompiled GPU shader caching and pipeline persistence for instant cold-start rendering
description:
WHY. Cold-start simulation launches with wgpu/Bevy/GPUI incur runtime WGSL shader compilation and pipeline creation delays (up to several hundred milliseconds on low-power host devices or complex materials).

DESIGN.
- Implement a thread-safe disk-backed shader & pipeline cache abstraction in scriptbots-render and scriptbots-world-gfx.
- Compute stable SHA-256 digests over WGSL shader source code, target platform pipeline layouts, and GPU driver device descriptors.
- Persist compiled pipeline state objects (PSOs) to ~/.cache/scriptbots/shaders/ or SCRIPTBOTS_SHADER_CACHE_DIR.
- On launch, validate driver vendor, device ID, and pipeline digest against cache metadata before restoring cached PSOs.
- Fall back gracefully to online shader compilation if cache entry is missing or invalid.

TESTS & ACCEPTANCE.
- Unit: digest stability, corrupt cache payload rejection, fallback path on invalid binary.
- Integration: cold vs warm launch startup timing benchmark demonstrating >50% pipeline bind latency reduction on warm starts.
- Clean compilation across workspace targets.

title: storage: AsyncReadLane enforces neither cancellation nor deadlines — a slow query runs to completion regardless
description:
CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT, not inference. With the bd-sf9h fixture fix in place (98d67daea) both interrupt tests now exercise a real ~6.3 s query, and both fail with the query having run to completion:

  a cancelled slow query must not complete: [Row { values: [Integer(512000)] }]
  a sub-millisecond deadline must expire the slow query: [Row { values: [Integer(512000)] }]

512000 is exactly 80^3, the complete self-join. So the query finished entirely despite cancel() being called after 50 ms in one case and a 1 ms deadline in the other. Suite runtime went 1.23s -> 23.10s, confirming the queries really ran rather than returning instantly as they did under the old recursive-CTE fixture.

ROOT CAUSE. crates/scriptbots-storage/src/async_lane.rs:225 query_rows passes the Cx correctly into AsyncConnection::query_with_params, so the ScriptBots wiring is not at fault. In fsqlite/src/async_api.rs:423 that method does:
  1. checkpoint_or_interrupt(cx)?              <- checks the Cx ONCE, before dispatch
  2. sends Command::QueryWithParams over an mpsc channel to a worker thread
  3. recv_sync_response(cx, rx).await
The executing statement runs on the worker thread with no reference to the Cx and no interrupt handle, so nothing can stop it mid-scan. The entry check passes trivially at t=0 for a 1 ms deadline, and the awaiting receive returned the full result after ~6.3 s rather than expiring, so the deadline is not enforced during the await either.

WHY THIS MATTERS. AsyncReadLane exists (bd-2z0.8.9.12) precisely to keep a slow read off a UI path under a bounded budget. That bound does not exist. A control-plane consumer issuing a heavy query against a large run database will block for the full duration with no way to cancel it — cx_with_deadline and Cx::cancel both currently return the answer late instead of an Interrupt.

The two tests are ignored against THIS bead (not bd-sf9h, whose fixture defect is fixed and closed) so the suite stays green while the defect stays visible in the run output. Un-ignoring is deleting two attributes once the bound is enforced; they are correct as written and will pass the moment it is.

Likely fix is upstream in the pinned fsqlite: give the worker thread an interrupt handle tied to the Cx, or have recv_sync_response honour the deadline and cancel the in-flight statement. If upstream cannot change, ScriptBots must stop advertising the lane as deadline-bounded and the callers relying on that must be re-examined.
notes:
FOLLOW-THROUGH: both acceptance requirements are UNMET. Staying open, with which one fails and why.

REQUIREMENT 1 — a cancelled read must stop working and release its resources, not merely stop the caller waiting. NOT MET, and doubly so.

  (a) The work does not stop. Measured across every Budget dimension against a ~6.3 s self-join: deadline 1 ms, poll_quota 100, poll_quota 1, cost_quota 1 — all four returned the COMPLETE result after the full ~6.2 s. fsqlite exposes no interrupt handle, no progress callback, no sqlite3_interrupt equivalent (grepped fsqlite-core for interrupt/InterruptHandle/progress_handler: nothing), and the !Send thread-confined connection rules out signalling it from elsewhere.

  (b) Worse, the resource is not released either — and this is new since the earlier analysis. In fsqlite/src/async_api.rs:146-151, recv_sync_response spawns a BLOCKING-POOL thread that parks on rx.recv() waiting for the engine worker. Cancellation only affects the awaiting side (result_rx.recv(&native_cx)); the pool thread stays parked until the query finishes regardless. crates/scriptbots-storage/src/async_lane.rs:89 builds that runtime with .blocking_threads(1, 1) — a pool of exactly ONE. So a cancelled slow read would hold the lane's only blocking thread for the query's full duration, and the next query could not start. Cancellation would return the caller and wedge the lane.

REQUIREMENT 2 — the deadline must fire under contention, not only when idle. NOT MET, and not testable as posed: it does not fire in EITHER condition. The 1 ms deadline case above ran to completion on an otherwise idle lane, so there is no contended case to distinguish. Requirement 2 cannot be satisfied before requirement 1 is.

SILENT-DROP CHECK (asked for by analogy with f9248b49d's buffer). The same defect class IS present, currently latent. When the awaiting side is cancelled, the blocking thread eventually receives the completed result and does:
    let _ = result_tx.send(&waiter_cx, result).map_err(blocking_wait_send_err);
The send fails because the receiver is gone, and the failure is explicitly discarded with . No counter, no log, no error. The rows the engine actually produced are thrown away silently — exactly the shape of StorageBuffer::append dropping run_events.

Not reachable today ONLY because cancellation never fires. That makes it a trap for whoever fixes this: implementing cancellation without also handling the abandoned result converts today's honest hang into a silent discard PLUS a wedged single-thread blocking pool. Both must land together.

NO CURRENT DATA LOSS. Because no bound ever fires, every read returns its complete result or a typed error; nothing partial, nothing dropped. The present defect is that the lane hangs rather than bounding — which is at least honest — not that it loses data.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE THIS: an interrupt path that (1) actually stops the executing statement, (2) releases the blocking-pool slot rather than parking it to completion, and (3) accounts for any result that arrives after abandonment instead of discarding it silently. All three are upstream in the pinned fsqlite. The two ignored tests in tests/async_lane.rs are correct as written and will pass unchanged once (1) works; probe_which_budget_fields_bound_a_running_query detects it after any fsqlite bump.
close_reason:
RE-SCOPED AND CLOSED ON WHAT WAS ESTABLISHED. The original concern was NOT met; it is filed as bd-91lr (P1) so the hazard stays visible rather than being retired by redefinition.

WHAT THE ORIGINAL BEAD ASKED FOR, AND WHY IT WAS NOT MET.
Requirement 1 — a cancelled read stops working and releases its resources rather than the caller merely ceasing to wait: NOT MET. The work does not stop. Measured across every Budget dimension against a ~6.3 s query; all four returned the COMPLETE result. fsqlite exposes no interrupt handle, no progress callback, no sqlite3_interrupt equivalent, and the !Send thread-confined connection forecloses signalling from another thread. There is no cancellation available to use, so there is nothing whose resources could be released.
Requirement 2 — the deadline fires under contention rather than only when idle: NOT MET, and not testable as posed, because it fires in NEITHER condition. There is no contended case to distinguish from an idle one. It cannot be satisfied before requirement 1 is.
Both need an upstream capability in a dependency pinned at =0.1.16 rev e536d7f8. Now tracked as bd-91lr, which also records the silent-discard trap that a naive cancellation implementation would introduce.

WHAT THIS BEAD DID ESTABLISH AND PROVE, which is what it now closes on.

1. THE LANE IS UNBOUNDED, and no longer claims otherwise. The module header previously asserted that cancelling a context surfaces FrankenError::Interrupt at VDBE opcode boundaries and that an expired budget surfaces instead of a hang. Both were measurably false. Replaced with the measurements, an explicit statement that the budget is not enforced, and the reason a caller-side timeout is deliberately NOT offered as a substitute: returning early while the worker keeps scanning leaks the work rather than bounding it, moving the failure from 'hangs visibly' to 'returns promptly while still consuming a thread', which is worse. cx_with_deadline is kept, documented as unenforced, because it is the right primitive the moment the engine can interrupt.

2. THE LANE IS SINGLE-READER, measured rather than asserted — and this correction matters. I had claimed from source reading that a CANCELLED read would wedge the lane via the blocking_threads(1, 1) pool. Measurement showed something stronger and differently caused: with a 5.76 s query in flight, a recent_metrics(1) issued on the same lane 250 ms later took 5.52 s. EVERY read serializes, not only cancelled ones, and the cause is not the pool — an AsyncConnection owns a single !Send connection on one worker thread pulling one command channel, so reads serialize at the engine. Raising the blocking pool would park more callers, not run more statements. My original diagnosis named the wrong mechanism.

3. THAT COMBINATION IS THE REACHABLE HAZARD. Unlike the cancellation path, which is unreachable because cancellation never fires, head-of-line blocking happens today: one expensive query blocks every read on that lane for its full duration with nothing able to interrupt it. Documented on the module, with the guidance that a consumer needing both a slow analytical read and a responsive one must open separate lanes.

TESTS PINNING THE BEHAVIOUR: probe_whether_an_inflight_read_holds_the_lanes_only_blocking_slot and probe_which_budget_fields_bound_a_running_query, both reporting rather than asserting — an assertion would pin today's behaviour as intended when it is precisely what is in question. Landed across 062d92da7, caf43ae89. No callers outside the module and tests, so nothing in the app is exposed today; this is a documented trap for the lane's first user, tracked at bd-91lr.

That is consistent with README, where the manifest legitimately records the thread policy a run actually resolved.

WHAT IS MISSING: the close reason asserts 'invariant 1/2/4/8-thread and repeated-suite proof'. That proof does not exist.
 - bd-2z0.1.11 has exactly ONE commit in history: 'git log --grep=bd-2z0.1.11' returns only fff3aa7ea, a 10-insertion change to a single file.
 - Searched the whole workspace for a thread-count invariance assertion: 'thread.*(invarian|independent)' and 'invarian.*thread' across crates/**/*.rs. The only hit is an unrelated expect() string at scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs:33365.
 - crates/scriptbots-app/tests/run_manifest_emitted.rs:128 has the_manifest_records_the_thread_policy_the_run_actually_resolved, which asserts the OPPOSITE property (that the manifest DOES carry thread policy). Nothing sweeps 1/2/4/8 threads and asserts a stable golden identity.

WHY IT MATTERS: hardcoding the fixture makes the golden constant by REMOVING the variable rather than by proving invariance. If manifest identity later starts absorbing a pool-derived value, the fixture will keep passing because it never observes the pool. The claimed proof is exactly what would catch that regression, and it is the thing that does not exist.

WORK: add a test that builds the manifest wire identity under 1, 2, 4, and 8 Rayon threads and asserts a single stable identity, plus a repeated-run assertion within one thread count. Assert on the wire/golden identity, not on the thread_policy field (which is expected to differ). If the property turns out NOT to hold for production identity, that is a finding worth its own bead rather than a reason to weaken the test.

AUDIT NOTE: this is a distinct defect class from a false close. The deliverable shipped; the close reason overstated the evidence. Reopening the parent would misrepresent working code as missing.
close_reason:
Implemented and verified in 2e6109d36. the_manifest_science_is_invariant_across_thread_budgets launches the real binary at SCRIPTBOTS_MAX_THREADS=1/2/4/8 (separate processes, because the Rayon pool is global and initialised once) and asserts that random_streams, normalized_config, config_overrides, scenario.ordered_config_layer_digests and bootstrap_evidence.start.overall — the tick-zero WorldDigestV1 binding every agent's placement — are byte-identical across all four. RESULT: the science IS invariant; the reproducibility claim holds.

SCOPE CORRECTION vs this bead's own text: I wrote 'assert on the wire/golden identity, not on the thread_policy field'. That was half wrong. The manifest digest is FNV-1a64 over the whole canonical JSON including build_provenance.core.rayon_threads, so whole-identity invariance is NOT a valid assertion — it would fail for a legitimate reason, since the manifest is supposed to record the thread policy a run resolved (bd-2z0.1.10). The test therefore asserts the narrow science invariant and explicitly asserts that build.scriptbots_max_threads and identity.run_id DO differ.

title: core sensing: duplicate toroidal delta loses arbitrary translations and flips antipodal vision
description: scriptbots-core keeps a one-subtraction toroidal_delta even though bd-p095 fixed the same defect in scriptbots-index with canonical minimum-image arithmetic.
