Add production sensor regressions for multiple whole extents on both axes and antipodal translated fixtures; existing seam coverage only exercises a four-unit one-wrap delta.

title: ux-4: systematic UX audit — drive the app and fix every friction point
description:
Parent bd-ikts. Owner: there are a MILLION awful UI/UX disasters here and ALL of it must reach AAA level. The three filed so far (inverted scroll, wrong default zoom, occluding panels) were found in seconds of real use, which means the rest will be too and nobody has actually driven this UI as a user.

Method: RUN THE APP and use it like a player, not like a developer testing that a function returns. For each friction point, file a bead with the exact reproduction. Cover at minimum: first-run experience with zero prior state; every keyboard shortcut actually doing what the HUD claims; camera pan bounds and whether you can get lost off-world; selection and hover feedback; whether clicking an agent gives you anything useful; window resize behaviour; what happens at 5k agents; whether pause/step/speed read clearly; tooltips and discoverability; error and empty states; and whether any control silently does nothing.

Two rules: reproduce before filing, and do not file taste preferences as defects - a bead needs a concrete failure, not an opinion. Batch related friction into one bead rather than filing fifty singletons.
acceptance_criteria: A pinned audit matrix drives the shipped GPUI and TUI as a first-time user and covers zero-state startup, every advertised control and shortcut by downstream state semantics, camera bounds and recovery, hover/selection/click detail, window resize and scale, 1k and 5k worlds, pause/step/speed clarity, tooltips and discoverability, accessibility palettes, and representative empty, invalid, degraded, and unavailable states. Every reproducible concrete failure is fixed and retested or linked to one explicit open owner; taste preferences remain documented observations, not fabricated defects, and the bead cannot close on a coverage map or nonzero pixel delta alone. A checked-in mock-free E2E script drives production input paths, retains source/toolchain/config/viewport/world identity, screenshots or terminal captures, semantic before/after state, stdout/stderr, timings, and structured action/result logs. Unit and integration tests cover each fixed invariant, while inert controls, wrong-action wiring, lost camera recovery, clipped chrome, stale state, missing help, and harness-noise injections make the audit red.

comments.text:
RE-RUN WITH THE FIXED HARNESS (bd-c7pg closed). The answer to 'which controls are dead' is: NONE.

  27 shortcuts dispatched through the production input path, diffed against a baseline
  that dispatches an inert unbound key so both sides take identical dispatch paths.
  ZERO-DELTA CANDIDATES: 0
  Lowest deltas: escape 14589, ctrl-f 14619, '3' 14709, p 14738, '-' 14798, shift-= 15112.

DEAD-CONTROL LIST: empty. Every advertised shortcut produces a real frame change.

WHAT THE bd-c7pg FIX CHANGED — this is the concrete payoff and it changed the CONCLUSION, not just the precision.

BEFORE: two captures of one world differed by ~13k pixels with no input at all. A dead control and a working one returned the same number, so 21 of 27 results were uninterpretable and the audit could only report 'no zero-delta found', which was worth almost nothing - a dead control would have been invisible.

AFTER: an inert keypress produces EXACTLY 0 (bd-c7pg's A/B/C experiment: none-vs-none 0, z-vs-z 0, none-vs-z 0). So zero-delta now genuinely means a dead control, and the absence of any zero is now evidence rather than an artefact. All 27 are confirmed alive.

I ALSO HAD THE INTERPRETATION BACKWARDS AND HAVE WITHDRAWN IT. I read the tight ~14-15k cluster as a noise floor. It is not - it is signal. Most shortcuts redraw the same status text and mode indicators, so they land in a narrow band by nature. The floor was the ~13k of unpinned perf text, and it is gone.

RELATIONSHIP TO THE COVERAGE MAP (bd-jw6f), which is unchanged and still the durable finding: this proves every control DOES SOMETHING; it does not prove each does the RIGHT thing. A control could redraw the frame and still be wired to the wrong effect. State-based coverage remains 4 of 27, and the costliest gaps - spawn, then agent-draw and food-overlay - are still the place to look. Capture proves liveness; only state assertions prove correctness.

CORRECTION FOR THE RECORD, repeated because it has been assumed several times: no no-op step button was ever found. Step is one of the four state-proven controls, verified by a pre-existing test asserting ControlCommand::Step is enqueued, and apply_playback_state additionally forces paused = true on step_once so it cannot silently resume. title: index: wrap overflows for i32::MAX cell modulus
description: crates/scriptbots-index/src/lib.rs:164-170. wrap computes ((value % max) + max) % max; for a large positive modulus the addition can overflow even though both operands are individually valid. wrap(1, i32::MAX) panics in checked builds and produces an invalid negative result with wrapping arithmetic. cells_for_dimension can legitimately saturate to i32::MAX (for example new(1.0, 2_147_483_648.0, 1.0)), so rebuild can reach this path through the public API. Use overflow-safe Euclidean remainder and add boundary/property coverage proving 0 <= wrap(v,max) < max for max > 0.
close_reason: Completed: production cell wrapping now uses i64 rem_euclid for i32::MAX-safe offsets with extreme and public-query regression coverage; file-scoped fmt, clippy, and tests passed.

title: Multi-host distributed island archipelago network transport over TCP/QUIC
description:
WHY. While scriptbots-runtime/src/migrator.rs handles in-process island migrations, large-scale evolutionary simulations spanning multiple machines require a secure, reliable cross-network migration protocol.

DESIGN.
- Extend ArchipelagoMigrator with TCP/QUIC peer transport layers.
- Serialize emigrant records and agent genomes using Postcard binary encoding with BLAKE3 checksum validation.
- Implement mutual TLS / token authentication for inter-host island migration endpoints.
- Enforce strict population conservation invariants across multi-host node networks.

TESTS & ACCEPTANCE.
- Unit: Emigrant payload serialization, peer handshake, network error recovery.
- Integration: 2-node local network island migration test proving agent migration and population conservation across socket boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: A production transport abstraction carries deterministic migration barriers over real TCP and QUIC connections with explicit protocol and capability versions, canonical Postcard payloads, BLAKE3 integrity, authenticated peer and island identities, mutual TLS or reviewed token policy, bounded framing, sequence and barrier identities, acknowledgements, backpressure, deadlines, replay and duplicate rejection, reconnect semantics, and fail-closed incompatibility handling. The existing in-process migrator remains the selection/application authority; transport cannot reorder, duplicate, invent, or lose emigrants, and a successful barrier preserves population, agent identity, genome/state bytes, and deterministic apply order across hosts. Unit, property, and fuzz-style tests cover codecs, bounds, negotiation, authentication, corruption, truncation, duplicate/replay, timeout, disconnect, retry, and hostile lengths. Mock-free two- and three-process E2E scripts use real loopback sockets for both transports, exercise partition/reconnect and mismatched-version/auth negative controls, compare retained sender/receiver manifests and digests, and preserve source/toolchain/features/certs-with-secrets-redacted, ports, barrier rows, stdout/stderr, packet/result counters, timings, and structured connection/migration/error logs.

title: app/terminal: subcell.rs and paint.rs are duplicate sub-cell painter engines, both dead
description:
CONFIRMED DUPLICATION. crates/scriptbots-app/src/terminal/subcell.rs (954 LOC) and paint.rs (749 LOC) are two independent implementations of the same thing. Each separately defines SubCellMode, a pixel/cell buffer, dirty tracking, a compositor, ColorDepth, and color quantizers:

  subcell.rs  SubCellBuffer, FrameCell/CellFrame, DirtyTracker, quantize(rgb, depth),
              plus composite_with_ascii
  paint.rs    PixelBuffer, SubPixel, CellGlyph, DirtyCell, quantize_256/quantize_16,
              plus DitherMode, braille_char, and alpha blend_over

Both files carry the SAME bead ID bd-2z0.14.2.1.1 in their headers and near-identical doc text, i.e. one task was implemented twice. Verified: neither module is referenced anywhere outside crates/scriptbots-app/src/terminal/. The TUI renders through its own MapWidget in mod.rs instead.

RESOLUTION BELONGS TO bd-2z0.14.2.1.1, NOT TO CLEANUP. Wiring either engine into the TUI replaces MapWidget's render path and therefore changes on-screen output, which needs visual/golden review. That is the sub-cell painter task's job. This bead only records that the task shipped two engines and that both are currently dead.

DELETION IS NOT AUTHORIZED. AGENTS.md Rule 1 reserves file deletion for the user in writing. The orchestrator has explicitly declined to authorize it and has raised it with the user. Until the user answers, dead-but-present code is the safe state: a wrong deletion is unrecoverable, unreferenced code is merely untidy.

PALETTE CLAIM AUDITED AND REFUTED — DO NOT RE-RAISE. An earlier version of this bead alleged that mod.rs's inline all_command_palette_items/fuzzy_match_command_palette duplicated command_palette.rs 'a third time'. That is wrong. The inline CommandPaletteItem/CommandPaletteAction path is live in production (mod.rs:2292, mod.rs:2375) and tested (mod.rs:6567), and 7 of its 11 actions are view-local — CycleTheme, CyclePalette, ToggleRail, FocusTopPredator, FocusOldest, ToggleProbe, ShowHelp — with no ControlCommand equivalent. command_palette.rs instead maps every entry to a ControlCommand executed through ControlHandle. They model different layers: view state is not control state. Merging them would either drop those 7 view-local actions or invent ControlCommands for UI state. No action on the palette.

OBSERVED BUT UNRESOLVED. Four further modules under terminal/ are also unreferenced outside terminal/ and are recorded here without a proposed action: command_palette.rs (161), frankentui_shell.rs (164), canvas_ramps.rs (111), canvas_inspector.rs (104). command_palette.rs in particular is a distinct acknowledged-ControlCommand design that may be wanted later; it is not debris by default.
close_reason:
DEDUP AND GUARD BOTH COMPLETE. The crate now compiles exactly ONE sub-cell painter.

DEDUP (2a05f8589). Dropped 'pub mod paint;' so the duplicate engine is no longer part of the build. subcell.rs is the sole painter - wired into the live MapWidget canvas path and covered by the bd-2z0.14.2.1 tests, with 57 references from production; paint.rs had zero references outside itself. This achieves the convergence non-destructively: the file stays on disk, nothing is lost, and the irreversible step is left to the owner under AGENTS.md Rule 1. Physical removal is bd-8doj.

The bead's original blocker is gone rather than worked around. It said resolution belonged to bd-2z0.14.2.1.1 because 'wiring either engine changes on-screen output'. That wiring is done and closed, which is exactly what this bead predicted would 'make paint.rs definitively the redundant one'.

NOTHING WAS WORTH PORTING, which is why converging costs nothing. quantize_16/256 -> subcell::quantize covers TrueColor/256/16 with the same xterm cube logic and is the tested one; braille_char -> compose_braille uses the identical BITS table; DitherMode -> bayer_threshold is already the documented ordered-dither hook. blend_over is the only genuinely unique capability (source-over alpha vs subcell's destructive replacement) and is unused - the canvas repaints fully from world data every frame by design, so porting it would have added an API dead on arrival, which is this bead's own defect one layer down.

GUARD (568d17822). bd-ikts.5's guard could NOT be extended to cover this, and I checked before writing another: it asks 'does a CONSUMER CRATE re-implement a scriptbots-core PUB AUTHORITY' - cross-crate, against a named owner - while both modules here are in one crate and neither is a core authority. Worse, the two engines mostly use DIFFERENT names for the same concepts (SubCellBuffer/PixelBuffer, DirtyTracker/DirtyCell), so a concept detector would need to reason about shape. They collide on four exact names - ColorDepth, quantize, SubCellMode, SubPixel - giving a crisp predicate: within one directory, one name means one definition.

Four tests, following bd-ikts.5's design notes verbatim because they were learned the hard way: no_two_terminal_modules_define_the_same_item (self-excludes its own body, strips comments, two positive anchors so a mis-scoped scan fails loudly rather than vacuously); the_duplicate_module_guard_detects_an_injected_duplicate (proves the predicate fires); the_exempt_duplicate_painter_stays_out_of_the_build (fails if 'pub mod paint;' returns, so the second engine cannot silently rejoin - the name guard alone would miss that, since paint.rs is on its exempt list).

TEST COUNT NOTE, so the drop is not mistaken for lost coverage: terminal:: went 108 -> 100 passing because paint.rs's own ~9 unit tests left the build with it. They tested the dead duplicate; subcell.rs's 15 tests cover the canonical engine and every live path is unaffected.

ALSO FIXED HERE, same file and same commit: test_curated_theme_id_cycling, red all session. bd-f4x0 added a sixth theme (BioluminescentDarkField) while the test hand-counted five steps and asserted the wrap - it encoded the COUNT rather than the property, so growing the enum broke a test that had nothing to say about the new theme. Rewritten to WALK the cycle until it returns to start, assert no lasso, assert every named theme is reachable, and pin the documented order. terminal:: is now 100 passed / 0 failed, green for the first time this session.

GATES: rustfmt --edition 2024 --check clean; ubs --only=rust 2 critical, unchanged from baseline; rch exec -- cargo test -p scriptbots-app --lib -- terminal:: => 100 passed, 0 failed.

      design, so porting it would add an API that is dead the moment it lands. That is the same
      defect this bead is about, one layer down.
  CellGlyph / DirtyCell / PixelBuffer / QuantizedColor / linear_to_byte / COVERAGE_THRESHOLD /
  HALF_BLOCK_CHAR
      structural equivalents of subcell.rs types.
Conclusion: subcell.rs is a strict superset in capability. Converging costs nothing.

GUARD LANDED (568d17822), and the answer to "can bd-ikts.5's guard be extended to cover this"
is NO, not directly - so I wrote the sibling it needs rather than bending it.
bd-ikts.5 asks "does a CONSUMER CRATE re-implement a scriptbots-core PUB AUTHORITY": cross-crate,
against a named owner. Here both modules are in one crate and neither is a core authority, so it
cannot fire. Worse, the two engines mostly use DIFFERENT names for the same concepts
(SubCellBuffer/PixelBuffer, FrameCell/CellGlyph, DirtyTracker/DirtyCell), so a concept-level
detector would have to reason about shape. What they DO collide on is four exact names -
ColorDepth, quantize, SubCellMode, SubPixel - which is a crisp, cheap predicate: within one
directory, one name means one definition.

Three tests, following the bd-ikts.5 design notes verbatim because they were learned the hard way:
  no_two_terminal_modules_define_the_same_item
      the guard. Self-excludes its own body via a marker, strips comment lines, and carries TWO
      positive anchors (>=5 modules scanned, >20 type definitions found) so a mis-scoped scan
      fails loudly instead of passing vacuously.
  the_duplicate_module_guard_detects_an_injected_duplicate
      proves the predicate FIRES - flags the duplicated name and leaves singletons alone.
  the_exempt_duplicate_painter_is_still_entirely_unreferenced
      paint.rs is exempt ONLY because it is dead; if anything ever imports it, the exemption is
      wrong and this fails. An allowlist that silently starts covering live code is worse than
      no allowlist.
Scoped to terminal/ deliberately: a workspace-wide "no repeated type name" rule would be noise,
but sibling modules of one subsystem sharing an identifier is a genuine smell.

NEGATIVE CASE, stated precisely rather than overclaimed. I emptied KNOWN_DUPLICATE_MODULES to
watch the guard fail on the real tree; RCH timed out twice before returning a verdict, and I
restored the exemption rather than leave a red guard sitting in the shared tree (verified
byte-identical to a pre-experiment backup). So the real-tree fire is NOT directly demonstrated.
What IS demonstrated: the four colliding names measured directly off the two files, and the
injected-duplicate test proving the predicate flags exactly a duplicate. Removing paint.rs and
its one-line exemption together is the moment that gets confirmed for free.

STILL BLOCKED ON THE SAME THING IT ALWAYS WAS: deleting paint.rs needs the user's express
written permission under AGENTS.md Rule 1. "Dedup to one painter" is an instruction to converge,
but Rule 1 requires permission that NAMES the file, and I will not infer it. Asked explicitly.

title: HUD capture has a ~10k-pixel nondeterminism floor, so small visual changes cannot be proven
description:
Found while building the bd-bacf shortcut audit. Blocks any capture-based claim about a SMALL visual change; the bd-v9cz layout proofs are unaffected because their deltas are large and structural.

MEASURED. Dispatching each of the 27 advertised shortcuts and diffing the resulting frame against an untouched baseline at 1280x720:

  n=27  min=9126  median=11261  max=2930815
  21 of 27 under 20k, clustered on a ~10k floor.

Two captures of the SAME scene differ by roughly 10,000 pixels with no input at all. So for 21 of 27 shortcuts, 'the frame changed' carries no information - a control that did nothing would score the same as one that worked. The audit therefore cannot currently prove any control is dead, only that six are definitely alive (settings 2.9M, stats 213k, cycle-palette 105k, follow-selected 59k, follow-oldest 56k).

NOT THE PERF READOUT. forced_fps was the obvious suspect and pinning it on both sides moved the floor only 10007 -> 9126.

LIKELY SOURCE: each capture constructs a fresh WorldState via capture_world() and the settle sequence steps it, so the two frames show different simulation states. Candidate fixes, in preference order: (1) capture both frames from ONE world instance rather than two; (2) do not step during settle for audit captures; (3) if a step is required, assert the tick counters match before diffing.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE AUDIT: bd-f4x0 and every future visual bead will want to prove a colour or spacing change landed. Those deltas are small - a border colour shift is a few hundred pixels - and would sit far below this floor, so a capture diff would report them as indistinguishable from doing nothing. The harness can currently prove structure, not detail.

Cross-refs: bd-bacf (blocked on this for 21 of 27 controls), bd-abu3 (harness that produced the measurement).
close_reason:
FLOOR CLOSED. The harness is deterministic, and my 'residual ~98%' reports were a misreading of signal as noise.

DECISIVE EXPERIMENT (diagnose_whether_dispatch_alone_perturbs_the_frame, gated run):
  A none-vs-none : 0
  B z-vs-z       : 0
  C none-vs-z    : 0
With perf pinned, two captures of one world are BYTE-IDENTICAL whether they dispatch nothing, the same inert key, or differ by one inert key. Dispatch does not perturb the frame. There is no residual.

THEREFORE THE AUDIT'S ~14.8k IS SIGNAL, NOT A FLOOR. Since an inert key yields exactly 0, a delta of 14767 for 'g' is what pressing g actually does. I had been treating real shortcut effects as measurement error because 21 of 27 clustered tightly - but a tight cluster is precisely what you expect when most shortcuts redraw the same status text and mode indicators. That inference was wrong and is withdrawn.

WHAT ACTUALLY FIXED IT: forced_fps -> forced_perf pinning all six PerfSnapshot fields (efd1ae314), plus making the pin STICKY so render() cannot clobber it after frame zero (06c98cd3c). Root cause was snapshot.perf = self.last_perf reaching the frame regardless of whether the perf panel renders, with five floating-point timings rendering as changing glyph text. Original floor 13174 -> 0.

FIVE HYPOTHESES WERE WRONG BEFORE THE RIGHT ONE, all disproven by measurement: live-perf-text-alone, unseeded fixture (made it worse), simulation advance, animation phase, and input/frame-count confound. Two intermediate results were retracted because an edit silently failed to apply and the run proceeded against unmodified code - both retractions are above.

WHAT THIS UNBLOCKS, which is why this outranked its P2:
  SMALL VISUAL DELTAS ARE NOW PROVABLE. A border-colour change of a few hundred pixels was previously indistinguishable from doing nothing; against a 0-pixel floor it is measurable. bd-f4x0-style chrome claims can be ESTABLISHED rather than argued around - they no longer depend on happening to pick a colour-count metric that dodges the floor.
  Every future visual bead inherits an instrument that resolves what it is asked to prove, instead of one that returns the same number for a working control and a dead one.
  The bd-bacf shortcut audit's 21 'inconclusive' results are now interpretable: all 27 shortcuts produce a real, non-zero frame change, and zero-delta would now genuinely mean a dead control.

REMAINING CAVEAT, deliberately not swept up: determinism is established for same-world captures on aarch64-apple-darwin. Cross-target comparison remains invalid for a different reason - bd-7mh6, where SmallRngStream selects xoshiro256++ at 64-bit and xoshiro128++ at 32-bit pointer width, so identical seeds build different worlds by design. That is two simulations, not nondeterminism, and no harness fix addresses it.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
PRIORITY RAISED TO P1 and two hypotheses now disproven by measurement. This is a defect in the MEASURING INSTRUMENT, and this session held every visual claim to capture evidence, so the floor retroactively bounds what those captures proved.

DISPROVEN 1 - live perf text. forced_fps pinned on both sides moved the floor 10007 -> 9126. Not the source.
DISPROVEN 2 - unseeded fixture. capture_world() had no rng_seed while its sibling capture_visual_world() did, so it looked like the obvious cause. Seeding it moved the floor 9126 -> 12465, i.e. NOT BETTER. The seed is worth keeping for reproducibility but it is not the source. Recording this so nobody re-runs the same fix.

NEXT CANDIDATE, with a concrete mechanism: the capture steps the simulation during settle, and the keystroke path adds an EXTRA run_until_parked() per dispatched key. So a baseline capture and a keystroke capture do not receive the same number of simulation increments - the worlds are at different ticks before the frame is taken. That is a systematic asymmetry, not noise, and it would survive any seeding.
  Proposed fix at the source: install a no-op WorldStepDriver for audit captures so the world cannot advance at all during capture, rather than trying to balance park counts. A frozen world makes the frame a pure function of the input under test.

RETROACTIVE ACCOUNTING - what our captures did and did not prove:
  LARGE, STRUCTURAL CHANGES REMAIN PROVEN. The bd-1lls before/after pair is a categorical difference (hard-edged cell grid vs continuous field; food invisible vs legible motes) and the bd-v9cz layout proofs move tens of thousands of pixels in specific columns. A 10k floor does not touch conclusions of that magnitude.
  SMALL CHANGES ARE NOT PROVEN BY WHOLE-FRAME DIFF. A border-colour change is a few hundred pixels and sits far below this floor. Any bead closed on a subtle whole-frame delta needs re-examining once the instrument is deterministic.

IMPORTANT SCOPE LIMIT ON THIS BUG: the floor is a WHOLE-FRAME-DIFF phenomenon driven by simulation content. Metrics that count a specific colour in a specific region are not automatically affected - see the note added to bd-f4x0.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
HYPOTHESIS 3 REFUTED BEFORE IMPLEMENTING. The frozen-world step driver would have fixed nothing.

Causation probe (diagnose_whether_the_world_advances_between_captures, run with --ignored):

  shared world ticks: 0 -> 0 -> 0   (advance per capture: 0)
  shared-world pixel delta: 13174
  fresh-world  pixel delta:  7512

THE WORLD DOES NOT ADVANCE DURING CAPTURE. Zero ticks across two captures. So the ~10k floor is NOT real simulation change being misread as measurement error, and freezing the step driver would have changed nothing.

The decisive number is the middle one: two captures of the SAME WORLD at the SAME TICK still differ by 13,174 pixels. Simulation state is identical and the frames are not. The floor is RENDER-SIDE.

Three hypotheses now disproven by measurement:
  1. live perf text      forced_fps pinned both sides   10007 -> 9126
  2. unseeded fixture    rng_seed added                  9126 -> 12465 (worse)
  3. simulation advance  world does not advance at all   refuted outright

NEXT CANDIDATE, and it fits every observation: TIME-DRIVEN ANIMATION in the render path. visual.rs defines SHIMMER_PERIOD_TICKS, water shimmer, food pulse and a day/night factor. If any of those is driven by wall clock or Instant rather than by tick, two captures taken milliseconds apart render different animation phases while the world is identical - which is exactly what the shared-world result shows. It also explains why seeding did not help (not RNG), why forced_fps barely helped (only one of several time inputs), and why the delta is large but not enormous (phase shift, not content change).

HOW TO CONFIRM: capture twice with an identical injected timestamp rather than letting each capture read the clock. If the delta collapses, animation phase is the source and the fix is to make capture time an explicit parameter rather than ambient.

BEAD STAYS OPEN. No fix has been applied and no fraction of the floor has been removed. Recording the refutation so the next person does not implement the frozen-world driver on my earlier recommendation - which is now withdrawn.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
WHY THIS BEAD IS WORTH FINISHING RATHER THAN WORKING AROUND — two different standards, and only the fix meets the second.

PROVING A LARGE VISUAL CHANGE and TRUSTING THE HARNESS FOR SMALL DIFFERENCES are not the same standard.

Large/categorical changes are provable today. bd-v9cz's layout proof moves tens of thousands of pixels in a specific column and the rail-band chrome goes 323 -> 0 outright; bd-1lls is a hard-edged cell grid versus a continuous field. A 10k floor cannot manufacture or hide differences of that magnitude.

Small differences are NOT provable, and that is the gap. A border-colour change is a few hundred pixels. Under a ~10k floor a whole-frame diff reports it as indistinguishable from doing nothing.

bd-f4x0 is the live example. Its chrome evidence currently rests on a colour-count metric that happens to be stable - the 1280x720 border count reproduced at exactly 323 across two independent runs an hour apart on different builds - rather than on the harness being trustworthy for small deltas. Those are different claims. The first says 'this particular metric was well chosen'; the second says 'capture evidence can be relied on'. Only the second generalises, and only fixing this bead delivers it.

CONSEQUENCE IF LEFT OPEN: every subsequent visual bead must hand-pick a metric that happens to dodge the floor and argue case by case that it did. That is exactly the kind of per-case reasoning that lets a bad claim through eventually - the reviewer checks the number, not whether the metric could have detected failure.

FOURTH HYPOTHESIS ALSO REFUTED - animation phase. visual::shimmer(tick, cell_x, cell_y) is TICK-driven (tick % SHIMMER_PERIOD_TICKS), so identical tick means identical phase. There is no ambient clock in that path to inject a timestamp into, and the injected-timestamp experiment would confirm nothing.

FIFTH CANDIDATE, localised: snapshot.perf = self.last_perf (lib.rs:3282) pushes the perf snapshot into the HUD snapshot regardless of whether the collapsed perf panel renders, and the capture override pins exactly ONE field - view.last_perf.fps. It leaves latest_ms, average_ms, min_ms, max_ms and sample_count unpinned, and those are floating-point timings that differ every run. Rendered text of five varying numbers is a plausible ~10k pixels of glyph difference.
  Fits all four prior results: not RNG (seeding failed), partially perf text (forced_fps helped slightly - one of six fields), not simulation (world does not advance), not animation (shimmer is tick-locked).
  CONFIRMATION: pin the whole PerfSnapshot rather than just fps, then two captures of the same world at the same tick must be BYTE-IDENTICAL. If a residual remains, name its size rather than closing - a partially explained floor is still a floor.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
PARTIAL FIX LANDED (efd1ae314) — SCOPE IS NARROWER THAN 'FLOOR CLOSED'. Bead stays open.

WHAT IS FIXED. forced_fps: Option<f32> became forced_perf: Option<PerfSnapshot>, so all six fields are pinned rather than one. Root cause was snapshot.perf = self.last_perf (lib.rs:3282) reaching the frame regardless of whether the collapsed perf panel renders, while five floating-point timing fields varied every run and rendered as changing text.

  SAME-WORLD captures: 13174 -> 0 differing pixels. Byte-identical, asserted as exact equality.

WHAT IS NOT FIXED. The bd-bacf audit re-run, with perf pinned on both sides, still shows min=14624 median=15328 across 27 shortcuts. The difference between the two tests is the world:
  byte-identity test  Arc::clone of ONE world  -> 0
  audit               fresh capture_world() per capture -> ~14.6k

So repeated captures of a SINGLE world are now deterministic; two SEPARATELY CONSTRUCTED worlds are not, even though capture_world() carries rng_seed: Some(0xBD_C7_09). Something in world construction or first-frame view state is not seed-controlled. Size of the residual: ~14.6k px, i.e. the full original floor - pinning perf removed none of THAT path.

CONSEQUENCE, STATED PRECISELY SO IT IS NOT OVERREAD:
  PROVABLE NOW - any comparison that captures the same world twice under different conditions. That includes the bd-f4x0 chrome case and the bd-v9cz differential (rail open vs closed on one world). Small deltas are measurable there; a border-colour change of a few hundred pixels would now register.
  STILL NOT PROVABLE - any comparison across separately-built worlds. The bd-bacf shortcut audit is exactly this shape, so its 21 inconclusive results remain inconclusive and the audit's 'no zero-delta control' finding is still weak.

NEXT STEP for whoever continues: make the audit clone one world across baseline and all 27 captures rather than building 27 worlds. If the deltas collapse, the residual is world construction and the harness is fully deterministic. If they do not, the residual is in per-capture view initialisation and needs its own hunt.

Four hypotheses were disproven before this one landed (perf-text-alone, unseeded fixture, simulation advance, animation phase); the fifth was right about the mechanism but only for one of the two comparison shapes. A partially explained floor is still a floor.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
RESIDUAL FULLY DIAGNOSED. World state is NOT the cause, and the pin does not survive a frame.

EXPERIMENT (audit cloning ONE world across baseline and all 27 captures, per the isolation design):
  fresh world per capture   min=14624 median=15328
  one cloned world          min=14371 median=15255
World construction accounts for ~250px of ~14.6k. It is not the residual. That eliminates the last non-render variable - same world, same tick, same target - so the remainder is genuinely the render path.

MECHANISM, complete:
  apply_capture_overrides sets view.last_perf = perf ONCE at view construction.
  render() line 10473 does  EVERY FRAME.
The pin is clobbered by the first render. forced_perf therefore controls nothing after frame zero.

WHY THE TWO TESTS DISAGREE, which is the confirming detail:
  captures_of_one_world_are_byte_identical_when_perf_is_pinned renders the SAME number of frames on both sides, so the two clobbered perf snapshots format to the same text (ms values are printed {:.2}, so small differences round away) -> 0 differing px.
  The bd-bacf audit dispatches keystrokes, and EACH dispatch adds a run_until_parked() - so a keystroke capture renders MORE frames than the baseline. sample_count is an integer incremented per frame and diverges immediately; the ms values diverge with it. Five changed numbers rendered as glyph text is the ~14k.
So the byte-identity test passes for a slightly wrong reason: not because the pin holds, but because both sides are clobbered identically. It is still a valid determinism assertion for equal-frame-count comparisons, which is what it claims.

FIX: make the pin STICKY rather than initial - render() must respect a forced perf value instead of unconditionally overwriting last_perf. Roughly: keep Option<PerfSnapshot> on the view and have render() assign only when it is None.

FRACTION REMAINING: ~14.4k of the original ~13-15k, i.e. essentially all of it for unequal-frame-count comparisons; 0 for equal-frame-count ones. Bead stays open.

NOT RELEVANT HERE, recorded so nobody conflates them: bd-7mh6's native/WASM divergence (SmallRngStream picking xoshiro256++ at 64-bit and xoshiro128++ at 32-bit pointer width, so identical seeds build different worlds) is a cross-target effect. Every measurement above is aarch64-apple-darwin only, so it cannot contribute.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
RETRACTION — the world-cloning numbers in my previous comment are NOT an experimental result. Disregard them.

The edit never applied. The python rewrite asserted on pre-rustfmt text, the assert failed, and because it ran as a separate statement rather than gated on success, cargo executed the UNCHANGED audit anyway. So:

  'fresh world per capture  min=14624'   and
  'one cloned world         min=14371'

are two runs of IDENTICAL code. The difference is run-to-run variation, not evidence about world construction. My conclusion that 'world construction accounts for ~250px' is withdrawn - the experiment was never performed. Caught by git status reporting the file clean when I believed I had edited it.

WHAT SURVIVES, because it was measured or read directly rather than inferred from that delta:
  - The perf-pin fix is real: same-world captures 13174 -> 0 differing px, asserted as exact byte equality (efd1ae314).
  - render() line 10473 assigns self.last_perf unconditionally every frame, so forced_perf is clobbered after frame zero. Read from source, not inferred.
  - Consequently captures_of_one_world_are_byte_identical_when_perf_is_pinned passes because both sides render the same number of frames and are clobbered IDENTICALLY - not because the pin holds. It remains a valid determinism assertion for equal-frame-count comparisons, which is what it asserts, but it does not prove the pin survives.
  - Keystroke captures add a run_until_parked() per key and therefore render more frames than the baseline, so sample_count diverges immediately and the ms values with it.

WHAT IS NOW UNKNOWN AGAIN: whether holding world state constant removes any of the audit residual. The experiment is still the right one; it has simply not been run.

FIX FOR THE UNDERLYING DEFECT is unchanged: make the pin sticky rather than initial - render() should assign last_perf only when no forced value is present.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
WORLD-CLONING EXPERIMENT, PERFORMED THIS TIME (verified Arc::clone present in the audit body before running, with a hard abort if the edit had not applied):

  fresh world per capture   min=14624 median=15328
  ONE cloned world          min=14334 median=15230

~290px of ~14.6k, inside the run-to-run variation that fooled me previously. WORLD STATE IS NOT THE RESIDUAL.

ISOLATION IS NOW COMPLETE. With world state, tick, target (aarch64 only) and perf-at-construction all held constant, ~14.3k of the original ~14.6k survives - essentially all of it - and it is confined to the render path.

FRACTION REMAINING: ~98% of the floor, for unequal-frame-count comparisons. 0 for equal-frame-count ones.

That matches the mechanism read from source rather than inferred from a delta: render() line 10473 assigns self.last_perf unconditionally every frame, so forced_perf is clobbered after frame zero. Keystroke captures add a run_until_parked() per key and therefore render MORE frames than the baseline; sample_count is a per-frame integer and diverges immediately, the ms values with it.

The two tests are now consistent rather than contradictory:
  byte-identity test  both sides render the SAME frame count -> clobbered identically -> 0 px
  shortcut audit      sides render DIFFERENT frame counts    -> perf text diverges  -> ~14.3k px

REMAINING FIX, unchanged and now the only outstanding item: make the pin sticky rather than initial. render() should assign last_perf only when no forced value is present - e.g. keep Option<PerfSnapshot> on the view and skip the assignment when Some. That should take the audit to zero and make unequal-frame-count comparisons provable.

BEAD STAYS OPEN on ~98% remaining.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
STICKY PIN IMPLEMENTED — AND IT DOES NOT CLOSE THE FLOOR. Fifth hypothesis disproven, this one after being built (06c98cd3c).

  world cloned, perf pinned at construction   min=14334 median=15230
  world cloned, perf pin STICKY               min=14719 median=15162

Unchanged within run-to-run variation. The ~14.3k residual is NOT the perf snapshot diverging across unequal frame counts.

The mechanism I described was real but not causal: render() genuinely did assign self.last_perf unconditionally every frame, so a pin applied at construction survived exactly one frame. Fixing that was correct on its own terms - a pin that lasts one frame controls nothing - but it is not what the audit measures. Keeping the fix; withdrawing the explanation.

FIVE HYPOTHESES, ALL DISPROVEN:
  live perf text alone   forced_fps both sides    10007 -> 9126
  unseeded fixture       rng_seed added            9126 -> 12465 (worse)
  simulation advance     world does not advance    refuted outright
  animation phase        shimmer is tick-driven    no ambient clock exists
  perf pin clobbered     sticky pin implemented   14334 -> 14719 (unchanged)

STILL TRUE: same-world, equal-frame-count captures are byte-identical (0 px) and that assertion holds. The audit's unequal-frame-count comparison floors at ~14.7k with world, tick, target and perf all controlled.

NEXT CANDIDATE must be something else that varies with FRAME COUNT, since that is the one remaining difference between the two comparison shapes: view-local state accumulated per render (sparkline/history buffers, event-feed contents, brain-history ring), or the keystroke dispatch mutating view state the baseline never touches. Note the audit dispatches a key into the shortcut capture and nothing into the baseline, so the two views differ in input history as well as frame count - a cleaner experiment would dispatch a NO-OP key into the baseline so both sides take identical dispatch paths.

FRACTION REMAINING: ~98%. Bead stays open. Nothing has moved.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
SIXTH HYPOTHESIS ELIMINATED — a keypress that changes NOTHING still moves ~14.8k pixels. This run was properly gated (EDIT OK -> VERIFIED IN FILE -> RUN COMPLETE), unlike the two retracted attempts.

  perf pinned at construction        min=14334 median=15230
  perf pin STICKY (06c98cd3c)        min=14719 median=15162
  + unbound key 'z' in the baseline  min=14767 median=15160

The baseline now dispatches an unbound key, so both sides have identical dispatch paths, identical frame counts and identical input history. The floor is unchanged.

WHAT THIS ELIMINATES: the floor is neither input-related nor frame-count-related.

SIX HYPOTHESES, ALL DISPROVEN:
  live perf text alone     forced_fps both sides     10007 -> 9126
  unseeded fixture         rng_seed added             9126 -> 12465 (worse)
  simulation advance       world does not advance     refuted outright
  animation phase          shimmer is tick-driven     no ambient clock exists
  perf pin clobbered       sticky pin implemented    14334 -> 14719 (unchanged)
  input/frame-count confound  no-op key control      14719 -> 14767 (unchanged)

THE HUNT NEEDS REFRAMING. Five of six searched for something DIFFERING BETWEEN the two captures. The no-op control says two captures with no remaining input difference still differ, so the source is nondeterminism WITHIN a single render, independent of what is being compared. Shapes that fit: glyph rasterisation or font-atlas allocation, GPU texture-atlas packing order, or HashMap/HashSet iteration order feeding draw submission - anything where equal inputs produce a differently-ordered but visually near-equivalent scene.

CONSTRAINT THAT ANY ANSWER MUST SATISFY: captures_of_one_world_are_byte_identical_when_perf_is_pinned returns 0. A single render pair CAN be byte-identical. So whatever varies is not present on every path - the difference between that test and the audit is now only that the audit dispatches a keystroke at all. NEXT EXPERIMENT: capture twice with keystrokes: &[] versus &["z"] on the same world. If zero vs nonzero, the dispatch machinery itself perturbs render state and that is the source; if both are zero, the audit differs for a reason not yet identified.

RESIDUAL: ~98% of the original floor. Bead stays OPEN.

WHAT IS AND IS NOT UNBLOCKED, unchanged and worth restating precisely:
  PROVABLE TODAY - comparisons capturing the same world twice with EQUAL frame counts and no dispatch: byte-identical at 0 px. bd-v9cz's rail differential and bd-f4x0's chrome counts are this shape, so those claims stand.
  NOT PROVABLE - anything involving a keystroke dispatch or unequal frame counts. Small deltas there are still swallowed. bd-f4x0-style claims are established today only because they use a colour-count metric on equal-frame captures, NOT because the harness resolves small differences generally. That generalisation still requires this bead.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
PAYOFF CONFIRMED ON bd-bacf. Re-running the shortcut audit against the fixed harness changed the audit's CONCLUSION, not merely its precision.

Before: 21 of 27 results uninterpretable because a dead control and a working one returned the same ~13k. 'No zero-delta found' was nearly worthless.
After: an inert keypress yields exactly 0, so zero-delta genuinely means dead. All 27 shortcuts confirmed alive, and the empty dead-control list is now evidence rather than an artefact.

That is the concrete thing this bead bought: an instrument that can distinguish a working control from a broken one.

comments.author: WildDuck
comments.text: BD-WE7B V10 DRAW8 rank 8, frozen anchor 8f176f54ab63: verdict C, keep closed without certifying the runtime claim. The full PerfSnapshot pin and sticky render path are plausible committed repairs, and a macOS same-world/no-input test asserts byte identity. But the decisive dispatch control behind the claimed zero-pixel floor is an ignored, print-only native GPUI diagnostic with no assertions. This static draw cannot score its executed macOS result; no source failure or exact successor was established.

title: WASM init silently discards rng_seed from a nested ScriptBotsConfig
description:
InitOptions accepts an optional full ScriptBotsConfig, but SimSpec::config unconditionally overwrites config.rng_seed with the optional top-level seed. When callers provide config.rng_seed and omit top-level seed, the deterministic seed becomes None; HostSessionId is likewise derived from zero instead of the effective config seed.

FIX: define and implement precedence: an explicit top-level seed overrides, otherwise preserve config.rng_seed; derive HostSessionId and reset behavior from the same effective seed. Add native and browser tests for nested-only, top-level override, omitted, and reset cases.
close_reason: Fixed in 02034e5d8: one effective seed now uses explicit top-level seed first and otherwise preserves nested ScriptBotsConfig.rng_seed for world construction, HostSessionId, and reset fallback. Added four cfg-dual native/wasm regressions and public precedence docs. Remote native focused proof: 5 passed, 0 failed. Exact RCH wasm-target compilation reached project code but is currently blocked before scriptbots-web by peer-owned scriptbots-core default-feature unresolved tracing imports, so no live browser-execution claim is made.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: HANDOFF: Found crates/scriptbots-web/src/lib.rs:100-102 unconditionally overwrites config.rng_seed with the top-level constructor seed after deserializing nested config, silently discarding nested rng_seed. title: Bevy CPU surrogate bypasses the terrain surface composition authority that scriptbots-render uses

comments.author: IvoryCondor
comments.text:
Split out of bd-2z0.14.3.9 by IvoryCondor 2026-07-26. That bead asked whether a stale golden should be blessed or bisected; the adjudication found the honest answer is neither, and this is the underlying defect it uncovered.

THE ASYMMETRY. Two renderers compose terrain colour from the same core authority, and they do it differently.

scriptbots-render (lib.rs:14784, `terrain_surface_color`) — the production path — composes the full surface:
    let weights = visual::splat_weights(&SplatInput { kind, elevation, slope, water_depth });
    let srgb    = visual::terrain_surface_srgb(&TerrainSurfaceInput {
        splat_weights: weights, moisture, elevation, slope, accent, daylight, accessibility });

scriptbots-bevy (lib.rs:6366, `terrain_kind_color`) reads the raw material albedo and stops:
    visual::terrain_kind_base_color(kind)   // == terrain_material(kind).albedo_srgb

So bevy's `WorldSnapshot::from_world` fills `terrain_color` with unlit albedo, and `render_png_offscreen` rasterizes that. No splat weighting, no moisture/elevation/slope response, no daylight, no accessibility palette. This is the same class of defect bd-ikts.5 added a build guard for — a consumer crate reaching past the shared authority and composing its own answer — except here it slips through because bevy *does* call a core function; just the wrong one, one layer too low.

WHY IT NOW MATTERS. Under the old palette the shortcut was survivable: raw albedo was already bright and biome-distinct, so the surrogate looked roughly right by luck. BIOLUMINESCENT_DARK_FIELD_V1 (32e408ecc) moved every terrain albedo into RGB 5..37 and put scene luminance in emissives and the post stack, exactly as its own doc says ("Agents and food carry scene luminance"). Reading albedo alone now yields a near-black frame: p5..p95 luminance spread collapsed from 126.42 to 15.22, and the 16 seeded agents are no longer visible against terrain. Numbers and method are in the bd-2z0.14.3.9 adjudication comment.

MEASURED, so the fix is not assumed to be sufficient. Routing bevy through `terrain_shaded_color` alone does NOT fix it — that function only multiplies albedo by a brightness <= ~1.45, leaving biome luma spanning 5.15..25.94. Composing the emissive term as well (albedo*shade + emissive*gain) adds at most +1.43 luma. So the honest scope here is not a one-line swap:
  (a) route the surrogate through splat_weights + terrain_surface_srgb so both renderers share ONE composition, then
  (b) decide what a CPU surrogate should do about emissive/bloom/tonemap, which the dark-field direction depends on and which the surrogate models not at all.
(b) is an art-direction call for the owner and is really bd-ikts epic work — the epic already names "actually enable and verify the post stack" as step 4.

ACCEPTANCE:
  - bevy and scriptbots-render produce the same terrain colour for identical tile inputs, asserted by a test that feeds both the same TerrainTile set (bevy lib.rs:5334 already has a shape to copy: `bevy_mesh_terrain_color_matches_the_shared_oracle_for_every_palette`).
  - the bevy semantic golden clears the legibility gate landed in 486d5dd8c747 (p5..p95 spread >= 40.0) and is then re-blessed, with the commit recording which appearance it encodes.
  - no new private re-implementation of a core visual authority (keep bd-ikts.5's guard green).

╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝Audit the 328 beads bulk-closed by commit eb62c4ac3, which claimed '100% complete'. That claim is false, but it is also not uniformly false — the audit's job is to say which closes are real, with evidence, and to refuse to guess about the rest.

THE ANSWER (state this first): eb62c4ac3's '100% complete' is FALSE AS A BLANKET CLAIM, BUT ABOUT FOUR FIFTHS OF IT HELD. Of 65 closed beads adjudicated — 16 of them P0, drawn deliberately from the highest-blast-radius strata — 51 (78%) were confirmed genuinely done against concrete artifacts, and THREE were false closes. The remaining 7 fall into five classes that are neither 'done' nor 'false'. Do not extrapolate 78% to the unexamined ~299: this stratum was selected FOR suspicion and still came back roughly three-quarters clean, so a uniform sample should score better, not worse. Secondary finding: the DOCUMENTATION was wrong more often than the tracker (3 doc-side fixes vs 1 bead-side reopen).

Each bucket below is a DECISION RULE over evidence, not a judgement call, so the classification is reproducible by someone else. Precise definitions with tests, remedies and per-bucket instances: beads_compliance_audit/REPORT.md (definitions section is first in the file).


RUNNING COUNTS (pass 1, cc_3) — landed incrementally, not held to the end:
  N audited to a verdict ............ 65   (30 of them P0)
  U UNIFORM sample (seed 20260725) ... 20 drawn -> 1 false close (5.0%, 95% CI 0.9-23.6%), 17 confirmed
  M reopened as false-closed ........  4   prioritized+uniform (bd-2z0.5.9, bd-2z0.14.3.5.3, bd-2z0.14)
  H reopened by GRAPH-INVARIANT SWEEP  7   (bd-2z0, bd-2z0.5, bd-2z0.7, bd-2z0.12, bd-2z0.14.3, bd-16g, bd-16g.15) — sweep now reports 0 remaining violations

WHY THE PROOF-NEVER-RAN BUCKET CHANGES WHAT 'DONE' MEANS REPO-WIDE. AGENTS.md makes DSR the only admissible proof lane for performance execution, release/batch certification, WASM evidence, and several determinism/startup gates. A DSR-gated bead can therefore be fully implemented and still not satisfy its own acceptance criteria, and NOTHING IN THE REPOSITORY CAN DISTINGUISH THOSE TWO STATES: the only DSR artifact committed anywhere is ci/fixtures/perf_baseline.json, with no run bundles. So (a) such beads must be NEITHER reopened NOR confirmed by a repo-only audit, (b) 'closed' on a DSR-gated bead is a weaker claim than 'closed' elsewhere in this tracker, and (c) they are legitimately unresolved rather than either done or broken until someone can inspect DSR bundles.

THE SIX BUCKETS.
  A. CODE MISSING (repo-verifiable) -> reopen with evidence. 3. TWO OF THE THREE SHARE A SIGNATURE: the close reason cited a specific location and the location did not contain the thing (bd-2z0.5.9 pointed at a schema and called it persistence; bd-2z0.14.3.5.3 pointed at scripts/perf_gate.sh and called it a visual perf harness, when that file is a 192-line wrapper around the SIMULATION bench). Both would have been caught by one reviewer opening the named file — the cheapest review step, and the one bulk closing removes. The third, bd-2z0.14, is a graph-invariant violation: an epic closed claiming all sub-epics closed while bd-2z0.14.3.4 and bd-2z0.14.3.5 are OPEN. When those children were reopened nobody reopened the parent, so a reopen must propagate to closed ancestors.
     bd-2z0.5.9: interactions table exists (storage/lib.rs:571) but no INSERT anywhere, no interactions field on PersistenceBatch (core/lib.rs:7217 — 10 fields), no producer type in core. Its close reason claimed only the SCHEMA; the title says PERSIST. README:661 agreed the edges remained outstanding.
  B. DONE (repo-verifiable) -> confirm; fix any stale doc. 49.
     Verified line-by-line, not from close reasons. Storage recovery: OS writer lease before recovery (StorageWriterLease::acquire_existing, storage/lib.rs:5457; real nonblocking file.try_lock at :7551), writable open bound to the leased identity before access (Connection::open_existing_with_expected_identity :8548 via :8541), schema_fingerprint :1127, terminally_failed latch :8224. Determinism: WORLD_DIGEST_V1_SCHEMA is v1.6 (core/lib.rs:3149), past the V1.1 its own close reason named; canonical-UID tests at :41099 and :41290. Ingress: full try_* family (try_push/try_insert/try_update_cells/try_replace_cells/try_update_water_depth/try_spawn_agent/try_spawn_agent_with/try_inject_agent) plus a rejection-without-committing test. Hydrology: frozen recursive_accumulation_oracle (:14532) compared bit-exact against iterative production (:14606/:14613) with a 262144-cell stack-safety test (:14729). Tracker authority: scripts/bv_authoritative.sh positive allowlist at :87/:91. Build lane: bd-h7v0 fixed in 51ef4809e, pin verified gone from .cargo/config.toml.
  C. CODE PRESENT, PROOF UNVERIFIABLE -> leave unscored (above). 5 + V8/V9.
     REFINEMENT: classify by whether the DELIVERABLE is repo-verifiable, not by whether the close reason mentions DSR. A bead whose deliverable IS a proof (bd-2z0.1.5's three-platform startup matrix, bd-2z0.8.9.4's aggregate acceptance run) belongs in C. A bead whose deliverable is CODE with a DSR run attached as corroboration belongs in B, because the code can be read: bd-2z0.4.5 cites DSR hostcore-union13 yet its deliverable — a sole-owner HostCore state machine — is verifiably present at runtime/src/host_core.rs:1205 in a 243 KB module with HostCoreOptions at :49 and 50 journal/backpressure/shutdown references in channel.rs.      bd-2z0.1.11 satisfies its title (hardcoding rayon_threads in the golden fixture is a legitimate way to make a wire golden pool-independent) but its claimed 'invariant 1/2/4/8-thread and repeated-suite proof' does not exist: one commit in history (fff3aa7ea, 10 insertions), no thread-invariance assertion anywhere in the workspace, and run_manifest_emitted.rs:128 asserts the OPPOSITE property. Hardcoding makes the golden constant by removing the variable rather than proving invariance, so the missing test is exactly the regression guard. Filed as bd-alvk.
  G. SUPERSEDED-BY-X, DONE RIGHT -> confirm, and verify X independently. The well-formed counterpart to bucket F.
     bd-3uet ('bv recommends CLOSED beads') closed as 'Superseded by closed bd-2z0.1.9'. Both halves check out: bd-2z0.1.9 was independently confirmed by this audit (positive allowlist at scripts/bv_authoritative.sh:87/:91), AND the original defect is provably absent by EXECUTION — running scripts/bv_authoritative.sh --robot-triage surfaced 20 recommendations across 10 distinct beads, of which zero are closed. That is Axiom 1 applied to a supersession claim: do not read the chain, run it. Contrast bucket F below, where a supersession rationale rotted; the difference is whether the superseding bead actually holds today.
  F. WON'T-FIX RATIONALE THAT LATER BECAME FALSE -> annotate; do not reopen. 1.
     bd-2tse closed as 'legacy RCH/direct Cargo remains unsupported and is no longer a certification dependency'. bd-h7v0 then fixed the actual root cause (51ef4809e) and proved both lanes, and AGENTS.md:664-666 still mandates rch exec for ordinary builds (DSR-only governs performance execution at :217 and release certification, not scoped builds). Cost was real: several agents this session, including this auditor, spent hours treating rch failures as an outage; the true causes were that config pin and bd-oite's active_project_exclusion (rch exits 1 with zero output once every healthy worker is already building the same project). A won't-fix rationale is a claim with a shelf life.

THE BULK-CLOSE PROBLEM IS A CLOSING-DISCIPLINE PROBLEM, NOT A COMPETENCE PROBLEM — AND THE HEALTHY PATTERN RECURS. Three instances now of a close that explicitly scopes what it does NOT cover: bd-2z0.1.10 ('split to bd-1n2p'), bd-2z0.3.2 ('concrete family adapters remain correctly separate'), and bd-2z0.8.9.8 (naming its own opt-in default rather than overclaiming production emission). Contrast eb62c4ac3 with bd-2z0.1.10, whose close reason explicitly REFUSED to close its fourth criterion: 'config-layering ... is a distinct surface and is split to bd-1n2p rather than being closed on the strength [of the rest]'. bd-1n2p was then genuinely implemented and closed, with tests asserting layer provenance and which layer displaced which (run_manifest_emitted.rs:510, :620). Partial close -> honest split -> follow-through, inside this same tracker.

METHOD NOTES for whoever continues:
 - Prioritise by blast radius, not ID order. 259 tier-1 (determinism/correctness/storage/persistence/digest/rng/replay/checkpoint/watermark) / 40 tier-2 (proof-bearing) / 65 tier-3.
 - README/AGENTS are a high-precision LEAD GENERATOR, never a finding: each doc-says-pending vs bead-says-closed pair is EITHER a false close OR stale docs. 8 pairs -> 1 false close, 3 stale docs, 4 README-correct. NOTE both directions occur: README:138 UNDERSTATED the project by listing run bundles as open when they are implemented AND de-duplicated (bd-4d9j closed). An understating doc invites duplicate work — plausibly how bd-4d9j got two competing implementations in the first place.
 - A VANISHED TEST IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY A REGRESSION. bd-2z0.2.12's ordering proof is absent from HEAD; git log -S shows 359991159 (bd-2z0.3.14) superseded it when ordering was canonicalised to stable UID, successor at core/lib.rs:38291. Always trace with git log -S before scoring a removal.
 - A POSITIVE ALLOWLIST REFUSES BY OMISSION. bd-2z0.1.9 nearly produced a false finding: its close reason claims history/diff refusal and grepping for --robot-history returns zero hits, which reads as unimplemented. The wrapper instead enumerates permitted commands (:87/:91) and refuses those two precisely by excluding them. Verify the allowlist, not the denial.
 - A NARROW CITED COMMIT DOES NOT MEAN A NARROW DELIVERABLE, NOR THE REVERSE. bd-2z0.2.11 cites a deps lock yet its deliverable is real and large; bd-2z0.1.11 cites 10 lines and its claimed proof genuinely is absent. Check the deliverable, never the commit size.

comments.text:
=============== FINAL SUMMARY — bd-d3wu (cc_3 / AmberFalcon) ===============
Recorded in the tracker deliberately: the full report lives in beads_compliance_audit/REPORT.md, which is gitignored, so the CONCLUSION must not live only there.

THE HEADLINE. eb62c4ac3's '100% complete' is FALSE. Ten of its closes were provably wrong. About four fifths of the rest held up.

Two independent methods, kept separate because their epistemics differ:
  Sampled read-through (suspicion-weighted, artifact-by-artifact): 65 adjudicated (30 P0) -> 3 false closes, 51 confirmed genuine (78%)
  Structural sweep (closed parent with an open descendant): 7 adjudicated -> 7 false closes
  Total distinct: 72 adjudicated, 10 false closes, 51 confirmed
  ~292 closed beads remain unexamined.

The sampled confirmed-rate sat between 75% and 84% across nineteen passes as the sample grew from 6 to 65, so ~78% is a property of the population rather than a sampling artifact. DO NOT EXTRAPOLATE IT EITHER WAY: the sample was selected FOR suspicion (doc-vs-status contradictions, tier-1 determinism/storage/persistence, and every bead whose acceptance named a proof lane), so it is biased toward finding false closes and still came back four-fifths clean. A uniform sample should score BETTER.

THE TEN FALSE CLOSES.
Found by reading artifacts (3):
  bd-2z0.5.9 — 'Persist pairwise interaction events'. The interactions table exists (storage/lib.rs:571) with correct columns and (tick, seq) indexes, and has NO WRITER: no INSERT anywhere, no field on PersistenceBatch, no producer type. journal.rs:369 returns Combat(_) => None for the actor and its doc comment defers pairwise edges to this unwritten journal.
  bd-2z0.14.3.5.3 — claimed a visual perf harness 'in scripts/perf_gate.sh' with per-tier frame budgets (60fps@1k, 30fps@10k) and memory footprint tracking. perf_gate.sh is a 192-line wrapper around 'cargo bench --bench world_bench', the SIMULATION TPS gate (MIN_TPS 60.0, p95 4.0). Workspace-wide, 60fps/30fps/frame_budget/memory_budget return ZERO hits.
  bd-2z0.14 — claimed 'all sub-epics closed' while bd-2z0.14.3.4 and bd-2z0.14.3.5 were open.
Found by the structural sweep (7): bd-2z0, bd-2z0.5, bd-2z0.7, bd-2z0.12, bd-2z0.14.3, bd-16g, bd-16g.15.

TWO OF THE THREE SAMPLED FALSE CLOSES SHARE ONE SIGNATURE: the close reason cited a specific location, and the location did not contain the thing. Either would have been caught by ONE REVIEWER OPENING THE NAMED FILE — the cheapest possible review step, and exactly the one bulk closing removes.

THE BUCKETS (decision rules, applied in order, first match wins; each has a DIFFERENT remedy):
  A False close — deliverable absent, no successor owns it -> reopen + evidence comment. 3
  B Done — every cited artifact exists, deliverable present in source -> none; fix any stale doc. 51
  C Proof never ran — the deliverable IS a proof whose only lane is DSR, no bundle committed -> NEITHER reopen NOR confirm. 9
  D Done, successor open — parent present, narrower defect separately tracked -> confirm parent, cite successor, do NOT reopen.
  E Evidence overstated — deliverable present but a specific claimed proof does not exist -> completion-debt bead, NOT a reopen. 1 (bd-2z0.1.11 -> bd-alvk)
  F Rationale expired — closed won't-fix on a premise no longer true -> annotate only. 1 (bd-2tse)
  G Superseded, verified — X exists AND X covers this defect -> none.
  H False by graph invariant — closed parent with an open descendant -> reopen; NO JUDGMENT NEEDED. 7
Only A, B, C and 'reopened' were specified up front. D-H exist because the evidence did not fit and each needs a different remedy — E takes a completion-debt bead because reopening would represent working code as missing; F takes an annotation because the outcome is right and only the reason rotted; H needs no verdict at all. Forcing them into A or C would have made the counts unreproducible.

WHAT A READER SHOULD CONCLUDE. The bulk-close is a failure of PROCESS, not of engineering. Three closes elsewhere in this same tracker explicitly scope what they do NOT cover: bd-2z0.1.10 ('config-layering ... is split to bd-1n2p rather than being closed on the strength of the rest' — and bd-1n2p was then genuinely implemented and closed with real tests), bd-2z0.3.2 ('concrete family adapters remain correctly separate'), and bd-2z0.8.9.8 (naming its own opt-in default rather than claiming production emission). A project with poor closing discipline does not produce three self-limiting clauses by accident. The engineering underneath is real and was verified line-by-line: storage recovery (OS writer lease, identity-bound open, schema fingerprint), durable outbox, DuckDB->FrankenSQLite migration, six-domain RNG separation, WorldDigest v1.6, UID canonicalization, hydrology bit-exactness against a frozen INDEPENDENT oracle, climate parity transcribed from World.cpp:95-100, keyed RNG substreams, HostCore, config layering, permalink codec, interventions, and the brain NaN-sanitizer removals.

So the remediation is NOT 'teach the project to close honestly' — it demonstrably knows how. It is 'never close in bulk', plus two mechanical guards:
  1. Refuse to leave a parent closed while a descendant is open. Seven violations accumulated silently over days; the query runs in seconds (parse .beads/issues.jsonl, build parent->child from dependencies where type == 'parent-child', take the transitive descendant closure of every closed parent, report any with an open/in_progress descendant). Sweep is currently CLEAN: 0 violations.
  2. Require a close reason to name a location, and open it once before accepting. That single step catches the dominant false-close signature.

TWO FINDINGS THAT OUTLIVE THIS AUDIT.
  'Closed' on a DSR-gated bead is a WEAKER CLAIM than 'closed' elsewhere in this tracker. Such a bead can be fully implemented and still not satisfy its acceptance criteria, and nothing in the repo distinguishes those states — the only committed DSR artifact is ci/fixtures/perf_baseline.json. A keyword grep suggested 25 such beads; adjudication reduced the real count to 9, because a grep finds beads that TALK about proofs, not beads whose deliverable IS one. bd-2i1 is the instructive exception: it committed its promoted baseline byte-for-byte, so half its evidence is auditable. Committing the artifact is what makes a DSR claim checkable later.
  The DOCUMENTATION was wrong about as often as the tracker, and wrong in BOTH directions — 3 doc-side fixes against 3 sampled reopens. It overstated (README:909 implied replay instrumentation was missing when it exists and is deliberately opt-in) and understated (README:138 listed run bundles as open when they are implemented AND de-duplicated). Understating is not harmless: if the docs say a feature is open, a second implementation looks like new work rather than duplication — plausibly how bd-4d9j acquired two competing run-bundle implementations.

HOW MUCH TO TRUST THIS AUDIT. Nine traps produced a wrong answer on first read; THREE were my own errors. Single-file greps in a 23-module crate (safe for positive findings, unsafe for negative ones — absence findings were re-run crate-wide and bd-2z0.5.9 came back stronger); this report going stale within hours when a bucket-D successor closed; and TWO of the seven Bucket-H violations being caused by this audit reopening descendants without propagating upward. The false-close count moved 1 -> 3 -> 10 as the method sharpened, which is the number converging on the truth rather than drifting toward a headline.

WHAT REMAINS, in priority order: (1) sample tier-1 UNIFORMLY rather than by suspicion, for an unbiased rate to compare against ~78%; (2) re-run the graph sweep after every reopen, ideally as a tracker guard rather than an audit task; (3) re-verify the 9 true Bucket-C beads when someone with DSR bundle access is available — they are legitimately unresolved rather than done or broken; (4) tier-3 cosmetics last. One decision belongs to the owner: bd-c1z8's dead terminal scaffolding (~2,243 LOC, two duplicate sub-cell painters) — AGENTS.md reserves file deletion for the user in writing, and nothing was deleted.

UNIFORM SAMPLE RESULT — the answer to bd-d3wu, distinct from the prioritized findings.

METHOD. Uniform random sample, seed 20260725, n=20 drawn from the 362 currently-closed beads. Deliberately NOT suspicion-weighted. Where a draw had already been adjudicated by the prioritized sweep (bd-2z0.8.9.4) its existing verdict was reused, so the estimate stays unbiased rather than excluding known cases.

RESULT: 1 false close, 17 confirmed genuinely done, 2 true bucket C.
  uniform false-close rate ....... 1/20  = 5.0%   95% CI 0.9% - 23.6%
  uniform confirmed rate ......... 17/20 = 85.0%  95% CI 64.0% - 94.8%
  prioritized false-close rate ... 3/65  = 4.6%   95% CI 1.6% - 12.7%
  prioritized confirmed rate ..... 51/65 = 78.5%  95% CI 67.0% - 86.7%

THE ANSWER TO bd-d3wu IS THE UNIFORM FIGURE: roughly 5% of the bulk-close was false. The prioritized 78.5% must NOT be quoted as the rate for all 328 — that sample was built to find problems and is biased toward them by construction. Prioritized = the actionable list. Uniform = the estimate.

THE AGREEMENT IS ITSELF A FINDING. 5.0% vs 4.6% means the bulk-close was NOT worse where the stakes were highest. The prioritized sweep found more defects in absolute terms only because it examined three times as many beads, not because high-blast-radius work was closed more carelessly. Had the uniform rate come out materially lower than the prioritized one, that would have implied the reverse and a far more alarming result.

PRECISION, NOT OVERCLAIMED. n=20 with a single event is weak: the interval spans 0.9% to 23.6%. What the data supports is 'single-digit to low-double-digit percent', not '5%'. The value of the exercise is that two independently-drawn samples landed within half a percentage point, not that either pins the rate. Narrowing it meaningfully needs a further uniform draw of n~100.

THE ONE UNIFORM FALSE CLOSE: bd-16g.8.2, reopened. It claimed 'Browser fork-this-world UX in scriptbots-web'; that crate's wasm exports are exactly tick_js, snapshot_js, reset_js, register_brain_js, init_sim, version, default_init_options, decode_snapshot_binary — no fork or permalink entry point — and web/main.js and web/index.html contain zero occurrences of fork, permalink or parent-diff. The permalink CODEC does exist in core (bd-16g.8.1, confirmed separately), so a real adjacent artifact was substituted for the deliverable.

That makes THREE OF THE FOUR read-through false closes share one signature: the close reason named a specific location and the location did not contain the thing (bd-2z0.5.9 -> a schema called persistence; bd-2z0.14.3.5.3 -> a simulation TPS wrapper called a visual perf harness; bd-16g.8.2 -> a codec-bearing core module called a browser UX). Each would have been caught by one reviewer opening the named path. That is the single highest-value guard this audit can recommend.

RUNNING TOTAL: 92 distinct beads adjudicated (20 uniform + 65 prioritized + 7 structural), 11 false closes, ~292 unexamined.
