A parity assertion that cannot observe the two things it claims parity between is not weak
evidence, it is NO evidence. Second instance today of a proof-shaped artifact executing
nothing. Generalization: a close reason resting on a test is only as good as that test's
ability to FAIL. This is Rule G ('would this assertion still hold if the feature worked?')
pointed at the test rather than the code.

════ 3. THE COVERAGE NUMBER — THE ACTUAL FINDING ════

ROUGHLY 299 CLOSED BEADS HAVE NEVER BEEN EXAMINED AGAINST THIS TAXONOMY. 393 closed, 65
adjudicated in pass 1, 2 more here. An audit that stops is fine; one that stops while
sounding complete is not. Nothing in this bead's verdicts extends to those 299.

I mechanized pass 1's cheapest high-yield rule — 'the close reason cited a location and the
location did not contain the thing', the signature of 2 of 3 pass-1 false closes — across
all 335 unadjudicated closed beads. Scanner: scratchpad/citation_scan.py.

  cited a path that fully resolves ...  39
  cited a path that did NOT resolve ...  5  -> ALL FIVE ADJUDICATED, ZERO FALSE CLOSES
  cited NO PATH AT ALL ............... 291  <- 45 of them P0

  The five: bd-1x69/bd-iswv cite 'cargo/config.toml' = .cargo/config.toml, present.
  bd-qan3 cites fsqlite/* = the external pinned crate (rev e536d7f8), correctly cited, not
  a repo path. bd-2z0.8.14's real deliverable ci/configs/audit_advisories.toml is present.
  bd-2z0.10.2 cites scenarios/meadow.json; the file is scenarios/meadow.scenario.toml —
  deliverable present, CITATION WRONG. That is a citation defect, not a false close.

  A first run of the scanner produced 21 'leads' that were mostly my own path resolver
  failing on shorthand. I fixed the resolver against git ls-files before reporting any of
  them. Publishing those would have manufactured 16 defects — the same error as a fabricated
  completion with the sign flipped, and AmberFalcon's warning about the step control.

THE 291 ARE THE RESULT. The mechanical rule finds almost nothing because almost nothing is
citable. 87% of unadjudicated closed beads name no file, so they can be neither confirmed
nor refuted without full manual reconstruction. That is not an audit backlog, it is the
CONDITION that made bulk closing possible: bd-2z0.3 closed on five uncited claims and stood
for three days until an unrelated test was repaired.

CHEAPEST DURABLE FIX: require a close reason to cite at least one path, and reject closes
that do not. That converts 291 uncheckable records into 291 one-command checks. It would
not have caught bd-2z0.3 by itself — but it would have made the check possible in seconds.

════ 4. CROSS-REFERENCE: AmberFalcon's bd-jw6f IS THIS RESULT FROM THE OTHER DIRECTION ════

bd-jw6f: of 27 HUD controls, only 3 had a test proving state change; 6 more appear in tests
whose assertions prove only that a BINDING EXISTS; 18 were never driven at all.

Same measurement, opposite end. I audit the RECORD and ask 'did the cited artifact exist and
contain the claim'. AmberFalcon audits the RUNTIME and asks 'does anything consume it, and
is the consumption asserted'. The middle tier — present in a test, asserted only for
existence — is the runtime twin of a close reason citing a real adjacent artifact instead of
the deliverable (bd-16g.8.2: the permalink codec genuinely existed, the fork-this-world UX
did not). bd-2z0.3 is the same shape a third time: a parity test that existed, ran, and
asserted nothing that could fail.

A codebase where 3 of 27 controls are state-proven produces exactly this false-closure
profile, because the evidence a closer would reach for is mostly existence-shaped.

AmberFalcon's proposed CONSUMER CHECK is the right extension and I endorse it: for a close
reason citing a new module or type, does anything OUTSIDE that file reference it? That
catches bd-2z0.14.2.1 (954-line subcell engine, zero external references, closed as
'Integrated'), which my citation rule passes cleanly because the cited path exists and
contains the named symbols. Citation check + consumer check together are strictly stronger
than either: one asks whether the thing is there, the other whether anything uses it.

════ NEXT, in value order ════
  1. Implement the consumer check over the 39 path-citing beads — mechanizable now.
  2. Close-reason citation requirement (prevents the 291 class recurring).
  3. Uniform sample of the 291 no-citation beads; they need manual reconstruction, so
     sample rather than enumerate, and publish the sample design before drawing.

comments.author: CopperCat
comments.text:
PASS 3b — CONSUMER CHECK. Scanner: scratchpad/consumer_check.py.

Refinement adopted: a cited path EXISTING is weaker than that path being CONSUMED. Today
produced five artifacts that existed and were never called (visual.rs, subcell.rs, vfx.rs
before its tap, visual_cue_for_event, and a post stack painting into a one-pixel bound), so
the check is call sites, not file presence.

TWO LEVELS
  MODULE  cited non-entrypoint .rs file -- is its module referenced outside itself?
  SYMBOL  identifier named in the close reason, defined exactly once -- is it referenced
          anywhere other than its own definition line, INCLUDING intra-file?

RESULT over 53 path-citing closed beads
  cited artifacts with call sites .... 141
  cargo-discovered, correctly skipped . 26
  ORPHAN MODULES ..................... 0
  ORPHAN SYMBOLS ..................... 7  -> 6 false positives, 1 REAL

THE ONE REAL HIT -> filed bd-7vdu (completion debt, NOT a reopen)
  bd-16g.1.4 closed 'Implemented RunSummary, paired_diff, hedges_g ..., deterministic
  bootstrap_ci, and adjust_multiple_comparisons in lab/stats.rs WITH TESTS'.
  Workspace reference counts:
      paired_diff 2, hedges_g 2, bootstrap_ci 2, adjust_multiple_comparisons 1
  A count of 1 is the definition alone. app/src/lab/stats.rs:236 is pub, implements
  Holm-Bonferroni, and has no caller and no test. Three of four deliverables genuinely
  wired; 'with tests' is false for the fourth. Bucket E -> completion-debt bead, because
  reopening would double-count a mostly-delivered bead and hide the actionable item.

MECHANISM PER NON-HIT, since a rejected candidate is a result too
  6 x TEST FUNCTION INSIDE A #[cfg(test)] MODULE IN src/. Names like
  a_panic_degraded_close_loses_nothing_the_outbox_admitted and
  bundle_creation_and_verification_roundtrip are harness-invoked; having no call site is
  their correct state. First cut excluded only tests/ and benches/ DIRECTORIES and so
  reported all six as dead.
  Also corrected before reporting: (a) tests/, benches/, src/bin/, examples/ are
  CARGO-DISCOVERED -- nothing imports them and that is right; counting them as orphan
  modules produced 11 phantom findings. (b) The first symbol rule excluded the whole
  defining file, which reports live code as dead whenever the consumer is intra-file --
  fatal in a 42k-line lib.rs, and it flagged decode_outputs and stage_food, both live.

  Raw first run: 11 orphan modules + 39 orphan symbols = 50 candidates. After the two
  corrections: 1. FORTY-NINE OF FIFTY WERE MY TOOL, NOT THE CODEBASE. Publishing them
  would have been a fabricated-defect event of the same class as a fabricated completion,
  and larger than anything the audit has actually found. A checker needs its own false
  positive rate measured before its output is evidence.

WHAT THIS CHECK CANNOT SEE -- stated so no one reads more into a PASS
  1. A CONSUMED PATH THAT DOES THE WRONG THING. The post stack was invoked every frame and
     painted into a one-pixel raw flex-canvas bound; it ran, did real work, threw it away.
     Every check here calls that consumed. Only a test asserting observable behaviour
     separates them, and bd-jw6f measured 3 of 27 controls having one. That is the ceiling
     on this whole technique, not a gap in this run.
  2. WRONG-BUT-CALLED. adjust_multiple_comparisons' three siblings pass because they have
     one reference each; nothing here says the Holm-Bonferroni ordering is correct.
  3. CONSUMED ONLY BY DEAD CODE. Transitive liveness is not computed; a caller that is
     itself unreachable still counts as consumption.
  4. DYNAMIC DISPATCH / MACRO / REFLECTION reference, and cross-language callers.
  5. The 291 no-citation beads. This check needs a citation; 87% of unadjudicated closed
     beads have none, so it cannot reach them AT ALL. Both mechanized rules are blind to
     the largest stratum, which is why the coverage number stays the finding.

STANDING: ~299 closed beads still never examined against this taxonomy. 393 closed, 65 in
pass 1, bd-2z0.3 and bd-2z0.3.13 in pass 3, bd-16g.1.4 partially here.

comments.author: CopperCat
comments.text:
THE FALSE-EVIDENCE TAXONOMY — five shapes, the reusable artifact of this audit.

Each shape is a distinct way a close reason can rest on something that is not evidence.
They are ordered by how cheaply a checker can detect them. Name findings by SHAPE, not by
symptom or location, so the corpus stays groupable.

  1. ZERO CALL SITES — the artifact exists and nothing invokes it.
     Instances: visual.rs, subcell.rs (duplicate dead painter), vfx.rs before its tap,
     visual_cue_for_event, bd-7vdu (adjust_multiple_comparisons: pub, 1 workspace
     reference, which is its own definition).
     DETECTION: mechanical. Reference count excluding the definition. Pass 3b.
     CAVEAT: transitive liveness is not computed; a caller that is itself dead counts.

  2. A TEST EXECUTING NOTHING — the proof exists, compiles, runs, and cannot fail for the
     reason it exists.
     Instances: bd-2wj (wasm-vs-native parity test ran BOTH sides inside the wasm runtime
     against a mismatched fixture; repaired 2026-07-25 and immediately surfaced bd-7mh6,
     which is what falsified bd-2z0.3's parity claim).
     DETECTION: NOT mechanical. Requires reading what the assertion can observe.

  3. A TEST ASSERTING THE INVERSE — the assertion holds only while the feature is broken,
     so it goes red exactly when the feature starts working.
     Instances: the core/lib.rs:43108 assertion PINNING the frozen day/night clock;
     finalize_persistence_admits_partial_tail_exactly_once demanding the pushed marker be
     the ONLY replay event, which failed the moment de0a24bfe turned the stream on.
     DETECTION: Rule G — 'would this assertion still hold if the feature WORKED?' Reading,
     not grepping.

  4. A CONSTANT DUPLICATED AND DRIFTED — one source of truth becomes two, and they diverge.
     Instances: bd-k0wj (RUN_MANIFEST_V3_BOOTSTRAP_SCHEMA duplicated across storage/app);
     the target-dependent RNG selection behind bd-7mh6 is the same shape at algorithm
     level — xoshiro256++ at pointer-width 64 vs xoshiro128++ at 32, two 'the seeded
     world' definitions that silently disagree.
     DETECTION: mechanical. Duplicate literal/const detection across crates.

  5. A FUNCTION RETURNING AN EMPTY STRUCTURE — the call site exists and the callee returns
     nothing meaningful, so the consumer check passes and the behaviour is absent.
     DETECTION: NOT mechanical in general.

WHY THE SPLIT MATTERS. Shapes 1 and 4 are queryable and I have now mechanized 1. Shapes 2,
3 and 5 require reading the assertion or the return value, and they are the ones that
produced today's two most serious findings. THE CHEAPLY DETECTABLE SHAPES ARE NOT THE
DANGEROUS ONES. Any claim that this audit is 'automatable' should be read against that.

A SIXTH SHAPE, from bd-lhml, that none of the five covers and that I want on the record
because I proposed a false dichotomy and was wrong:

  6. CONSUMED, EXECUTED, AND DISCARDED — the artifact runs, does real work, and throws the
     result away. The post stack was invoked every frame but painted into a one-pixel raw
     flex-canvas bound while ignoring canonical render settings. Fixed 32b375231535, with a
     Metal differential of 790600 of 921600 pixels changed and an identical science digest.

     I framed that bead as 'the stack runs and produces no perceptible change' versus 'it
     does not run at all' and asked which. The truth was neither. Shape 6 is invisible to
     every check in this document: it has call sites (defeats 1), its tests execute
     (defeats 2), they assert real properties (defeats 3), and it returns a populated
     structure (defeats 5). ONLY AN OBSERVABLE-OUTPUT DIFFERENTIAL FINDS IT — a pixel
     comparison, a digest, a captured frame. bd-jw6f measured 3 of 27 HUD controls having
     that kind of test, and bd-c7pg's ~10k-pixel nondeterminism floor means small visual
     changes cannot be proven by capture at all right now.

     So the honest ceiling: the shape that needs the strongest evidence is the one the
     repository is currently least able to produce.

comments.author: CopperCat
comments.text:
FALSE-EVIDENCE TAXONOMY v2 — SEVEN SHAPES, EACH WITH A RUNNABLE DETECTION METHOD

The durable artifact of this audit. A shape without a detection method is not
reusable, so every entry below carries one that someone can RUN against the ~299
unexamined closed beads without re-deriving my judgement. Where a method is not
mechanical I say so rather than implying it is.

Name findings by SHAPE, not by symptom or location, so the corpus stays groupable.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SHAPE 1 — CODE WITH ZERO CALL SITES
  The artifact exists and nothing invokes it.
  SEEN: visual.rs; subcell.rs (duplicate dead painter); vfx.rs before its tap;
        visual_cue_for_event; bd-7vdu (adjust_multiple_comparisons, 1 workspace
        reference = its own definition); bd-2z0.14.2.1 (954-line subcell engine,
        zero external references, closed as "Integrated").
  DETECT: MECHANICAL. scratchpad/consumer_check.py. For each identifier named in
        a close reason and defined exactly once, count workspace references and
        subtract definition lines. Zero remaining = orphan.
  MUST EXCLUDE or you manufacture defects: tests/, benches/, src/bin/, examples/
        are CARGO-DISCOVERED; #[test] fns inside #[cfg(test)] mod in src/ are
        harness-invoked. And count intra-file references — excluding the whole
        defining file reports live code as dead in a 42k-line lib.rs.
  COST: seconds.  BLIND TO: transitive liveness (a dead caller still counts),
        dynamic dispatch, macro-generated calls.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SHAPE 2 — A TEST EXECUTING NOTHING
  The proof exists, compiles, runs green, and cannot fail for the reason it exists.
  SEEN: bd-2wj — the wasm-vs-native parity test ran BOTH sides inside the wasm
        runtime against a mismatched fixture. Repaired 2026-07-25, it immediately
        surfaced bd-7mh6, which falsified bd-2z0.3's parity claim.
  DETECT: MECHANICAL, via MUTATION. Break the subject the test claims to cover —
        negate a condition, corrupt a constant, stub the function — and re-run.
        If the test stays GREEN it proves nothing. This is the repo's existing
        "born-red" convention generalized: a proof-bearing test must be
        DEMONSTRATED red under an injected fault, not merely observed green.
  CHEAP PRE-FILTER, also mechanical: for a PARITY/comparison test, check that its
        two operands originate from genuinely different build targets or configs.
        bd-2wj is detectable this way alone — both operands came from one runtime.
  COST: one suite run per mutation.  BLIND TO: nothing much; this is the strongest
        method here and it is why it should be required of proof-bearing beads.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SHAPE 3 — A TEST ASSERTING THE INVERSE OF CORRECT BEHAVIOUR
  The assertion holds only while the feature is broken, so it goes RED exactly
  when the feature starts working. It actively defends the defect.
  SEEN: core/lib.rs:43108 PINNING the frozen day/night clock;
        finalize_persistence_admits_partial_tail_exactly_once demanding the pushed
        marker be the ONLY replay event — it failed the moment de0a24bfe turned
        the stream on.
  DETECT: MECHANICAL for opt-in features. TOGGLE THE DEFAULT and run the suite.
        Any test that goes RED when a feature is ENABLED was pinning its absence.
        Both instances above are found by exactly this, and it is cheap because
        the repo's feature defaults are enumerable constants.
  READING RULE where toggling does not apply — Rule G: "would this assertion
        still hold if the feature WORKED?" If no, it is shape 3.
  COST: one suite run per toggled default.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SHAPE 4 — A CONSTANT DUPLICATED AND DRIFTED
  One source of truth becomes two and they diverge.
  SEEN: bd-k0wj (RUN_MANIFEST_V3_BOOTSTRAP_SCHEMA duplicated across storage/app).
        Same shape at ALGORITHM level in bd-7mh6: xoshiro256++ at pointer-width 64
        vs xoshiro128++ at 32 — two definitions of "the seeded world" that
        silently disagree, which is why native and WASM diverge at tick 1.
  DETECT: MECHANICAL. Duplicate const/literal detection across crates: group
        `const NAME` by NAME, flag any NAME with >1 definition, compare values.
        For the algorithm variant, flag cfg-conditional selection of a SCIENTIFIC
        primitive (RNG, hash, float mode) — any `#[cfg(target_*)]` choosing
        between algorithms is a determinism boundary and must be justified.
  COST: seconds.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SHAPE 5 — A FUNCTION RETURNING AN EMPTY STRUCTURE
  The call site exists and the callee returns nothing meaningful, so a consumer
  check passes while the behaviour is absent.
  DETECT: MECHANICAL, ast-grep. Find pub fns whose EVERY return path constructs an
        empty value — Vec::new(), vec![], HashMap::new(), Default::default(),
        None, Ok(()) — with no branch that populates it. Rank by whether a close
        reason names the function.
  COST: seconds.  BLIND TO: a function that populates one field of twenty.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SHAPE 6 — WORK THAT RUNS AND DISCARDS ITS OUTPUT   *** NEW ***
  The artifact is called, executes, does real computation, and the result never
  reaches anything observable. Distinct from all five above: it HAS call sites
  (defeats 1), its tests EXECUTE (defeats 2), they assert REAL properties
  (defeats 3), and it returns a POPULATED structure (defeats 5).
  SEEN: bd-lhml — the post stack was invoked every frame but ignored canonical
        render settings and painted into a one-pixel raw flex-canvas bound. Fixed
        32b375231535 with a Metal differential of 790600 of 921600 pixels changed
        and an IDENTICAL science digest.
  DETECT: MECHANICAL — ABLATION DIFFERENTIAL. Stub the subsystem to a no-op,
        re-run the deterministic capture, and diff the observable output BYTE-WISE.
        If the output is IDENTICAL with the subsystem disabled, its work is
        discarded and the bead claiming it is false. Identical output under
        ablation IS the finding; no judgement required.
        The observable must be the RIGHT one: pixels for a renderer, digest for
        science, serialized bytes for persistence. bd-mv2j's seam proof is the
        same instrument pointed the other way — there I diffed 121 batches to show
        NOTHING changed; here you diff to show something SHOULD have.
  COST: two capture runs.
  PRECONDITION THIS REPO DOES NOT CURRENTLY MEET: a deterministic capture. bd-c7pg
        leaves a ~10k-pixel nondeterminism floor, so small visual changes cannot
        be proven by capture at all. Shape 6 is therefore the shape needing the
        strongest evidence AND the one this repo is least able to produce. That is
        the honest ceiling on the whole taxonomy, and bd-c7pg is its blocker.
  CALIBRATION NOTE, mine: I framed bd-lhml as "runs and produces no perceptible
        change" VERSUS "does not run at all" and asked which. The truth was
        neither. Shape 6 exists because I offered a false dichotomy and the
        codebase supplied a third option.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SHAPE 7 — A DOC ASSERTING THE OPPOSITE OF THE CODE   *** NEW ***
  Prose states a value, default, or guarantee that the code contradicts. Dangerous
  because docs are what a reviewer reads INSTEAD of the code, so it launders a
  false claim into every downstream decision.
  SEEN: crates/scriptbots-core/src/replay.rs:10/:80/:294 stated "the default of
        zero keeps production runs byte-identical" AFTER de0a24bfe changed
        DEFAULT_REPLAY_EVENT_TICK_CAP to 512. Mine; fixed in e4975e8bb. Also the
        three README defects found in pass 1, and bd-mv2j's own bead, which led
        with "Bead stays OPEN" and "THE REASON THIS BEAD IS STILL OPEN" after the
        work had landed — the tracker is a doc surface too.
  DETECT: MECHANICAL. For each `const NAME: T = LITERAL;`, grep doc comments and
        markdown for NAME within N lines of a DIFFERENT literal of the same type;
        flag the mismatch. Catches the replay.rs case exactly. Second pass: for
        every closed bead, flag description/notes text containing "still open",
        "remains", "pending", "TODO", or "stays OPEN".
  COST: seconds.
  NOTE: pass 1 found the DOCUMENTATION wrong more often than the tracker — 3
        doc-side fixes vs 1 bead-side reopen — so this shape is likely the most
        COMMON and the least severe. Do not let its volume crowd out shapes 2/3/6.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
HOW TO RUN THIS AGAINST THE ~299 UNEXAMINED BEADS

  TIER A, mechanical and cheap — run first, on everything:
        shapes 1, 4, 5, 7. Minutes total. Produces a ranked candidate list.
  TIER B, mechanical but a suite run each — run on proof-bearing beads only:
        shapes 2 and 3. Toggle defaults; mutate the subject of each cited test.
  TIER C, needs a deterministic capture — blocked on bd-c7pg:
        shape 6.

  THE CHEAPLY DETECTABLE SHAPES ARE NOT THE DANGEROUS ONES. Tier A is nearly free
  and found ONE completion-debt item today. Tier B found bd-2z0.3, a false close
  on a P0 epic. Any claim that this audit is "automatable" should be read against
  that ordering.

  MEASURE YOUR CHECKER BEFORE YOU TRUST IT. My consumer check's first run produced
  50 candidates of which 49 were tool defects, not codebase defects — a fabricated-
  defect event larger than anything the audit has actually found. Run any new
  check against a stratum with KNOWN verdicts (pass 1's 51 confirmed beads) and
  measure its false-positive rate before publishing a single finding from it.

  AND: 291 of 335 unadjudicated closed beads CITE NO FILE AT ALL. Shapes 1 and 7
  need a citation to anchor on. The largest stratum is unreachable by the cheap
  tier, which is why the coverage number — not any scanner — remains the finding.

comments.author: CopperCat
comments.text:
TIER C IS NO LONGER BLOCKED — efd1ae314 landed (AmberFalcon), 'close the bd-c7pg nondeterminism floor by pinning the whole PerfSnapshot'.

Shape 6 (work that runs and discards its output) was recorded as TIER C, blocked, because
its detection method — the ablation differential — requires a deterministic capture, and
bd-c7pg's ~10k-pixel floor meant a byte-wise diff could not distinguish a real change from
capture noise. That precondition is now met on the render side.

So the taxonomy's tier table updates:
  TIER A  shapes 1, 4, 5, 7   mechanical, seconds              RUNNABLE
  TIER B  shapes 2, 3         one suite run each               RUNNABLE
  TIER C  shape 6             ablation differential            NOW RUNNABLE

Shape 6's method, restated so it can be run without re-deriving it: stub the subsystem to a
no-op, re-run the deterministic capture, diff the observable BYTE-WISE. Identical output
under ablation IS the finding. Pick the right observable — pixels for a renderer, digest
for science, serialized bytes for persistence.

FIRST CANDIDATES for a shape-6 sweep, all render-side and all now testable:
  the post stack itself (regression guard on 32b375231535)
  the day/night cycle, live since the default was un-frozen
  terrain normal lighting and the BoostTrail cue, both wired this session
Ablate each, capture, diff. Any that produces a byte-identical frame is doing work nobody
sees, which is precisely the bd-lhml shape.

NOTE bd-c7pg is still OPEN despite efd1ae314 — the fix landed, the bead has not been
closed. That is the inverse of the defect this audit hunts (a closed bead whose work is
absent) and it is the healthier direction, but it is still a record disagreeing with
reality. Flagging rather than closing it: it is AmberFalcon's bead and its acceptance may
have a second half I cannot see.

comments.author: CopperCat
comments.text:
SHAPE 8 — A DECLARATION-ONLY VARIANT   *** NEW, found independently by VioletCoast ***

  A declared possibility the code can never actually produce. An enum variant, error
  kind, or config option that is DECLARED but CONSTRUCTED NOWHERE.

  DISTINCT FROM SHAPE 1, and the distinction is the whole point. Shape 1 is a
  definition nobody calls -- the code exists and would run if called. Shape 8 is a
  branch of reality the program cannot enter. Consequences that shape 1 does not have:
    - any handler for it is UNTESTED BY CONSTRUCTION; no input reaches it
    - any doc, schema, or API contract naming it describes something that cannot happen
    - a match arm handling it makes it LOOK live, which is why it survives review

  INSTANCE (verified independently, not taken on report): ReadbackError::Resize(String)
  at crates/scriptbots-world-gfx/src/lib.rs:589. Its only workspace reference is its own
  declaration and doc line. Never constructed, never matched. The doc says
  "Resize/readback-buffer allocation failure" -- a failure mode the code cannot report.

  DETECT: MECHANICAL WITH A MEASURED CAVEAT. For each `pub enum` variant, count
  CONSTRUCTION sites (`Enum::Variant` / `Self::Variant` not followed by `=>`), treating
  match arms as consumption rather than evidence of reachability. Zero construction
  sites = candidate.

  MEASURED FALSE-POSITIVE CLASSES -- do not publish a raw sweep, I measured this:
  a workspace sweep over 1069 variants returned 57 candidates, and at least two large
  classes are MACRO-CONSTRUCTED and therefore invisible to any textual scan:

    (a) #[from] variants. thiserror generates a From impl, so `?` constructs them with
        no textual `Enum::Variant` anywhere. Confirmed: AnalyticsError::Json and ::Io
        (analytics/src/lib.rs:112,115) are both `#[from]`.
    (b) #[derive(Deserialize)] enums. serde constructs variants from input data.
        Confirmed: KnobKind::String/Array/Object/Null (app/src/control.rs:132-141)
        derive Deserialize and are built from JSON.

  REFINED RULE that isolates the real signal: candidate iff zero construction sites AND
  the variant is not `#[from]` AND its enum does not derive Deserialize AND it has ZERO
  references of any kind (no handler either). ReadbackError::Resize scores zero on every
  count; the #[from] and serde cases do not survive the refinement.

  STATUS: 57 raw candidates, 1 verified real, 2 false-positive classes confirmed, the
  REMAINDER UNADJUDICATED. I am not reporting 57 findings. Whoever runs the refined
  sweep should adjudicate before publishing, and should measure their own false-positive
  rate first -- my consumer check's first run was 49/50 tool defects.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
THE LIST IS OPEN, NOT COMPLETE.

Shape 6 came from my own false dichotomy on bd-lhml. Shape 7 came from a doc I wrote
that contradicted code I wrote. Shape 8 came from VioletCoast, independently, late in
the session, in a crate I had not looked at.

Three of eight shapes were found after the taxonomy was declared. A second agent finding
a novel shape this late is evidence the space is NOT saturated, and the honest reading is
that shapes 9 and 10 exist and have not been hit yet.

So this is a GROWING CHECKLIST, not a closed classification. Two consequences:
  - "none of the eight shapes matched" is NOT equivalent to "this close is sound". It
    means the cheap known checks passed. Say the former, never the latter.
  - A new shape is a finding in its own right and should be added here with its
    detection method, not filed as a one-off bug.

The failure mode this guards against is the one the audit exists to catch: a checklist
that sounds complete is exactly the artifact that lets a bulk close look verified.

title: GPUI wgpu compositor writes an unsolicited diagnostic PNG on every launch
description:
WorldCompositor labels frame capture opt-in, but initializes force_first_capture=true. save_view_if_requested therefore creates frames_live and writes the first PNG even when SB_WGPU_SAVE is disabled. Normal GUI launches silently mutate the working directory and consume disk.

FIX: make all frame writes explicitly opt-in, or bind the first diagnostic capture to a clearly named opt-in setting. Add a filesystem-boundary test proving default construction performs no write and the explicit capture path still writes exactly once.

title: core heredity: rejected eye-direction mutation rewrites valid 2pi to zero
description: C++ eye direction is a heritable closed-interval value in [0, 2pi]; its reproduction path clamps only out-of-range values, so an exact 2pi survives when the mutation event is rejected. Rust build_child_runtime calls wrap_unsigned_angle even in the nonmutation branch. Whenever the outer mutation-scale pass runs with primary rate zero, a valid 2pi direction is rewritten to 0. The geometry is equivalent, but the genome payload, material hash, mutation log behavior, and heredity attribution are not, so a no-op mutation changes scientific identity. Make a rejected or zero-probability mutation bit-exact identity. If the model instead requires a single canonical angular representation, normalize every admission, spawn, crossover, checkpoint, and mutation boundary together with an explicit wire/digest decision; do not canonicalize only offspring. Add exact-bit tests for both angular endpoints and zero primary rate.
close_reason: Fixed in 8862e8e7e. The rejected branch of the eye-direction mutation now returns runtime.eye_direction[i] unchanged instead of wrap_unsigned_angle(...). C++ Agent.cpp:134-136 clamps out-of-range angles OUTSIDE the gate, so an exact 2pi survives a rejected event; the unconditional wrap rewrote it to 0, which also emitted a spurious eye_dir gene-log entry for a mutation that never occurred. Chose the bead's primary option (bit-exact identity on rejection) over global angular canonicalization, which would have required normalizing admission, spawn, crossover, checkpoint and mutation together with an explicit wire/digest decision. The accepted branch still wraps, since only a perturbed angle needs renormalizing. Two fixtures: exact-bit inheritance of [0.0, 2pi, pi, 0.25] at zero primary rate plus absence of any eye_dir log entry; and an accepted event still landing in [0, 2pi). Verified: rch exec -- cargo test -p scriptbots-core --lib -- bd_d5w4 bd_v69t bd_iyl2 bd_l3fu = 12 passed, 0 failed, covering every adjacent eye-geometry and heredity fixture. rustfmt --edition 2024 --check exit 0. Clippy shows zero lints in the touched line ranges (the crate-wide -D warnings gate is red pre-existing, 294 errors, none of them here). Digest impact is nil in practice: all eye directions in normal operation already lie in [0, 2pi) where wrap_unsigned_angle is identity, so the change differs only at the exact 2pi endpoint this bead is about.

title: pre-push guard makes the mandated main:master mirror sync impossible during active swarm work
description:
AGENTS.md ('Git Branch: ONLY Use main, NEVER master') mandates that after pushing to main you also run:

  git push origin main:master

That push is refused by the mcp-agent-mail pre-push guard whenever ANY peer holds a reservation on ANY file touched anywhere in the main..master delta - including commits that are not yours and are already merged and pushed to main.

Observed (cc_3/AmberFalcon, 2026-07-25 ~06:20 UTC), pushing my own commit 644d71ac3 which touches ONLY crates/scriptbots-app/src/terminal/mod.rs:

  ERROR: mcp-agent-mail: file reservation conflict detected!
    crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs conflicts with reservation held by WildDuck
    crates/scriptbots-core/src/visual.rs conflicts with reservation held by CopperCat
  Set AGENT_MAIL_GUARD_MODE=warn to allow commit anyway.
  error: failed to push some refs

Neither file is in my commit. They are in OTHER agents' commits that make up the main->master delta. 'git push origin main:master' is a mirror of an already-reviewed branch, not an edit, so reservation semantics do not apply to it.

Why this matters beyond the annoyance: the only offered escape is AGENT_MAIL_GUARD_MODE=warn, which disables the guard wholesale. With six agents holding rotating reservations the delta almost always contains someone's reserved file, so the mandated sync step fails almost always, and the documented workaround trains everyone to run with the guard disabled. That is the same bypass pathology as bd-tat5 (chain hard-fails without AGENT_NAME -> everyone learns --no-verify). A guard that is impossible to satisfy is a guard that gets turned off.

Fix options: (a) the pre-push guard should evaluate only the commits AUTHORED BY the pushing agent, or better, only the refs being newly created rather than a mirror of an existing reviewed branch; (b) exempt pushes whose source ref is an ancestor-equal mirror (main:master fast-forward); (c) drop the master mirror requirement from AGENTS.md if master is genuinely legacy-only.

I did NOT bypass. main is pushed at 644d71ac3; master remains behind at whatever the last successful sync left. Someone with authority should decide between (a)/(b)/(c) rather than each agent independently discovering AGENT_MAIL_GUARD_MODE=warn.
acceptance_criteria: 1. The pre-push guard permits an authorized agent to push main and then main:master while peer commits and peer-owned reservations coexist in the collective remote..local range; it never attributes a peer reviewed commit to the current pusher. 2. The same guard still rejects the current agent own unreviewed path, expired/missing ownership proof, conflicting reservation, tampered review manifest, or non-main branch attempt with exact commit/path/owner diagnostics. 3. A hermetic multi-agent fixture creates two identities, disjoint reservations, interleaved reviewed commits, HEAD movement, an initial main push, and the legacy mirror push; both allowed pushes succeed and both remote refs end at the same reviewed commit. Negative fixtures cover true current-agent conflicts and stale/tampered metadata. 4. Post-push verification fetches refs and proves the intended commit is an ancestor of origin/main and origin/master; tests explicitly show why push exit alone is insufficient under collective pushing. 5. Detailed logs name the remote range, commit attribution, reviewed path set, reservation decision, ref parity, and failure remedy without exposing credentials. Shell/static checks and the repository guard self-tests pass.
notes:
== DESIGN GAP: THE GUARD APPLIES EDIT SEMANTICS TO A PUBLISH OPERATION ==

Evidence from 2026-07-25, when a fully-committed tree stayed unpushable for
hours while every agent behaved correctly. Resolved by a synchronized quiet
window: 31 commits, 5375d2985..3e16ac07a.

THE MISMATCH. The agent-mail pre-push guard rejects a PUSH on the basis of EDIT
reservations. But pushing does not modify the reserved files -- it publishes
commits that already exist. The reservation's purpose is to stop two agents
writing the same file concurrently; a push writes nothing. So the guard is
enforcing a property the operation cannot violate.

WHY IT COMPOUNDS INTO A LIVELOCK. We share one .git, so `git push` carries EVERY
agent's local commits, and the guard evaluates that whole range against the
PUSHER's identity. Consequences:

  - An agent is blocked by reservations it never took, on files it never
    opened, for commits it did not author.
  - The block scales with SWARM ACTIVITY rather than with conflict: the more
    agents working normally, the larger the push range and the more foreign
    reserved paths it contains.
  - Because every agent continuously acquires and releases, there is no
    naturally occurring instant when the union of held leases is empty.

Observed directly: two holders released on request, and a third acquired three
more files before the push could run. Nobody was uncooperative. Pairwise
negotiation CANNOT converge here -- clearing one holder at a time is a race
against five other agents' normal workflow.

WHAT ACTUALLY WORKED, and it is the pattern to keep: a BROADCAST SYNCHRONIZED
QUIET WINDOW. All six agents release at once and acquire nothing until the push
lands. A global quiet moment must be synchronized, not negotiated pairwise.

COST: origin/main sat 31 commits behind for hours. Every fix of the session --
the positioned event stream, VFX canonical cues, bevy boost trails, the replay
doc correction, precision fixes, HUD chrome -- existed on ONE MACHINE. That was
the largest single point of failure open all day, and it was produced by a
guard working exactly as written.

NOBODY BYPASSED IT AND NOBODY SHOULD. AGENT_MAIL_GUARD_MODE=warn would have
cleared it in one command; the guard has caught real damage (137e3bdb4 swallowed
60 lines of another bead's work), so switching it off unilaterally is how that
recurs. The fix belongs in the guard's semantics, not in agents' discipline.

CANDIDATE FIXES, cheapest first:
  1. SCOPE THE PUSH CHECK TO THE PUSHER'S OWN COMMITS rather than the whole
     range. An agent should answer for what it authored. This alone removes the
     scaling-with-activity property and probably the whole livelock.
  2. DO NOT GATE PUSH ON EDIT RESERVATIONS AT ALL. Gate COMMIT (already done,
     via the review-token protocol, which is where the real hazard lives).
     Publishing committed work modifies nothing.
  3. A PUSH LEASE: one short exclusive token that blocks new ACQUISITIONS rather
     than blocking edits. Agents keep working and merely queue on acquisition
     for a few seconds, so the window converges without anyone staying still
     voluntarily.

(1) and (2) are semantic corrections; (3) is a mechanism for whatever remains.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
Datapoint confirming this is structural, not incidental (cc_3, 07:20 UTC).

I released my own exclusive lease on crates/scriptbots-render/src/lib.rs specifically to unblock the mirror. It did not help. The push immediately failed again on a DIFFERENT holder:

  ERROR: mcp-agent-mail: file reservation conflict detected!
    crates/scriptbots-core/src/visual.rs conflicts with reservation held by WildDuck

WildDuck holds that legitimately - it is the bd-9pqz/bd-l4gu art-direction and visual-wiring surface, i.e. the highest-priority active work in the swarm. So the mirror is blocked by exactly the reservation we most want to exist.

This is the proof that the guard's model is wrong for this operation rather than merely inconvenient: 'git push origin main:master' is a MIRROR of an already-reviewed, already-pushed branch. It edits nothing. But the guard evaluates every file in the delta against live reservations, so the mirror can only succeed during a window when NO agent holds a reservation on ANY file anywhere in the delta. With six agents that window essentially never opens, and it closes tightest precisely when the swarm is busiest.

Releasing a lease is therefore not a workaround, and neither is waiting. The only thing that makes the mandated command succeed today is AGENT_MAIL_GUARD_MODE=warn, which disables the guard entirely.

I have not bypassed. master remains behind main. Reiterating the fix options from the description - (a) evaluate only the pushing agent's own commits, (b) exempt fast-forward mirrors of an existing reviewed ref, or (c) drop the master mirror requirement from AGENTS.md - and noting that (b) is the narrowest and matches the actual semantics of the operation.

comments.author: jemanuel

RESOLVED — main:master synchronized at 3e16ac07a (c68ac4e1b..3e16ac07a) during a synchronized swarm-wide quiet window. main, origin/main and origin/master are all at the same commit; 31 previously-stranded commits pushed in the same window.

Two findings worth keeping, because the blockage was not what it first appeared:

1. The guard blocks a PUSH of already-committed work on the basis of EDIT reservations. Publishing commits does not modify the reserved files, so edit semantics are being applied to a different operation. This is why a fully-committed tree stayed unpushable for hours while all six agents behaved correctly — nobody bypassed it, and the correct fix is not a bypass but distinguishing 'am I editing this file' from 'am I publishing a commit that touched it'.

2. Pairwise clearing does not converge with six concurrent agents. Three attempts failed: each time a holder released, another acquired a different file mid-attempt. The reservations were all legitimate — this was a livelock, not obstruction. The resolution was a SYNCHRONIZED release: all agents drop everything at once, hold, push, then re-acquire. Any future occurrence needs that pattern rather than negotiation with individual holders.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
EVIDENCE FOR THE DESIGN GAP, now that the quiet window has proven the mechanism.

The guard blocks a PUSH of already-committed work on the basis of EDIT reservations. Publishing commits does not modify the reserved files - it advances a remote ref - so this applies edit semantics to a different operation. Concrete consequence today: a fully committed tree stayed unpushable for hours while every agent behaved correctly, and origin/main fell 29 commits behind on a single machine that was then the largest open risk in the session.

It also cannot be cleared pairwise. Asking individual holders to release failed repeatedly because another agent acquired mid-attempt - a livelock, not non-cooperation. It took a synchronized quiet window across all six panes to get one clean instant, after which 31 commits pushed (5375d2985..3e16ac07a) and the master mirror synchronized for the first time that day.

Nobody bypassed it and nobody should have. But 'the only way to publish is to globally halt six agents' is not a workable steady state.

Narrowest fix remains (b) from the description: exempt a fast-forward push whose commits are already reviewed, or evaluate only the pushing agent's own commits. Either removes the livelock without weakening the edit guard that the pre-commit path legitimately needs.

comments.author: HazyCrane
comments.text:
2026-07-26 06:5x UTC, pane-2 (HazyCrane). New failure mode on the CLOSED guard defect, worth recording because it silently inverts the guard's intent.

REPRO: I committed two reviewed snapshots (8a047b6fc render test, 47cc2bfe6 beads) touching ONLY crates/scriptbots-render/src/lib.rs and .beads/*. On push:

  AGENT_NAME=HazyCrane git push origin main
  ERROR: mcp-agent-mail: file reservation conflict detected!
    crates/scriptbots-app/src/terminal/canvas_ramps.rs conflicts with reservation held by YellowLake
    crates/scriptbots-app/src/terminal/mod.rs conflicts with reservation held by YellowLake
  error: failed to push some refs

Neither file is mine and neither appears in either of my commits. The guard evaluates the whole push RANGE - which on a shared branch contains other agents' commits - against reservations those same agents legitimately still hold while working. So on an active swarm the guard blocks the innocent pusher for the reserver's own in-flight files, and the more agents are working, the less likely ANY push succeeds. That is the livelock already recorded here, but with an added twist:

THE TWIST - work lands anyway, via someone else. After my push reported failure, 'git ls-remote origin main master' showed BOTH refs already at my own latest commit 47cc2bfe6442, and 'git merge-base --is-ancestor' confirmed all three of my commits are on the remote. Because everyone shares branch main, whichever agent's push DOES get through carries every other agent's commits with it.

Consequences worth naming:
1. 'error: failed to push some refs' is not evidence the work did not land. An agent that trusts it will retry, re-commit, or worse, conclude it is blocked and stall. At least three panes have reported 'commit blocked / withheld pending X' in mail this session; some of that may be this.
2. Conversely, a successful push is not evidence that only the pusher's reviewed work went out. Pushes are effectively collective.
3. So the correct post-push check is NOT the exit code. It is 'git merge-base --is-ancestor <your-sha> origin/main' after a fetch. I would suggest AGENTS.md say exactly that.

Not reopening - the mirror sync this bead owns was genuinely completed at 3e16ac07a. Adding the evidence because the underlying guard-vs-shared-branch design gap is still live and is currently producing false 'blocked' reports.

title: config: public scientific knobs lack behavioral consumer witnesses
description: ControlHandle::list_knobs blindly flattens every serialized ScriptBotsConfig leaf and apply_patch accepts every declared path. A future field therefore becomes a public REST/MCP scientific knob without an explicit role or proof that any model transition consumes it; hashing the config cannot witness consumption because a dead field changes the config lane by construction (the exact bd-yw1j failure mode). Add a complete fail-closed knob classification registry (scientific construction, scientific transition, operational, presentation) and deterministic field-specific counterfactual witnesses for every scientific entry that compare material non-config world state. Tests must reject unclassified new leaves, stale/duplicate specs, and scientific specs without an activating witness. Do not claim source grep or WorldDigest.config sensitivity as behavioral proof.

comments.author: WindySquirrel
comments.text: Concrete witness target from the bd-yw1j golden provenance audit: ScriptBotsConfig.economy_debug_per_tick is diagnostic/telemetry control state, but it is serialized in scientific_config rather than explicitly neutralized. Toggling it can therefore move WorldDigest/config provenance without changing simulation science—the same ghost-control class as sense_max_neighbors. The current representative fixture uses false, so this does not explain an unknown golden delta; it is a specific counterfactual case for this bead, not a new bead.

comments.author: QuietBeaver
comments.text:
DESIGN FINDING that changes what 'complete' has to mean for the registry.

THE KNOB SURFACE IS STATE-DEPENDENT, so a registry keyed to the default config is
incomplete by construction.

ScriptBotsConfig.render is a RenderSettings whose every field is Option<...> carrying only
#[serde(default)] -- no skip_serializing_if, no rename (verified across the struct at
crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs, RenderSettings and the config body: zero 'serde(rename'
occurrences). A None therefore serializes to null, and flatten_value in
crates/scriptbots-app/src/control.rs:1065 stops at any non-object node.

CONSEQUENCE: on a default world, list_knobs publishes 'render.post' as ONE null leaf. Once
render.post is populated the same function publishes 'render.post.bloom.threshold',
'render.post.bloom.intensity', 'render.post.vignette.intensity',
'render.post.vignette.smoothness', and so on. Same for render.auto_exposure and
render.day_night. Those exact paths are already declared in KNOB_RANGES
(crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs ~4440), which is evidence the deeper surface is real and
reachable -- it simply is not discoverable from a default world.

WHY IT MATTERS FOR THIS BEAD
1. A completeness test that flattens ScriptBotsConfig::default() would pass while silently
   omitting every Option-gated subtree. That is the same shape of false assurance the bead is
   written against: the gate looks complete and is not.
2. The bead's own premise -- 'apply_patch accepts every declared path' -- combined with this
   means DISCOVERY AND MUTATION DISAGREE. list_knobs does not publish render.post.bloom.threshold
   on a default world, but the patch path and KNOB_RANGES both know it. A knob that cannot be
   listed but can be set is worse than an unclassified one, because no consumer can even
   enumerate it to audit it.

PLANNED HANDLING (not yet implemented): enumerate the registry against a MAXIMAL config with
every Option populated, and add a test asserting the default-config surface is a strict subset
of the registry rather than equal to it. Equality would re-admit exactly the omission above.

METHOD NOTE: the enumeration is derived, not transcribed -- crates/scriptbots-core/tests/knob_role_witnesses.rs
serializes the config and flattens it with the same object-only recursion the control plane uses,
so the list cannot drift from what callers actually see and cannot be invalidated by a serde
attribute that source-level transcription would miss. Hand-listing ~150 paths from the struct
would have missed the Option/null behaviour entirely.

title: core sensing: clock channels lag one transition and ignore the legacy epoch reset
description: Confirmed against original World.cpp. C++ World::update increments modcounter before setInputs, resets modcounter to zero when it reaches 10000, then computes inputs 16/17 as abs(sin(modcounter / clockf)). Rust step computes next_tick but stage_sense reads the still-completed self.tick, so the first transition emits 0 instead of abs(sin(1/f)) and every clock input lags one tick. Rust tick is monotonic, so the legacy clock phase also never resets at an epoch rollover. explain_sensors repeats the same phase. The only integration assertion says the value is in [0,1], despite the historical plan claiming deterministic clock tests. Add first-transition, second-transition, and tick-10000 differential oracles; make stage_sense and next-sense attribution use one explicit transition-phase helper, and correct the completion claim.
close_reason: Completed in 7555ae361 (C++ clock-channel parity for sensors 16/17); proven against World.cpp including the_first_transition_does_not_present_a_zero_clock. Bead record was left in_progress after the work landed.

title: core: #[cfg(test)] shims woven into production types make test and release builds structurally different
description:
PROGRESS: 29 -> 14 raw cfg(test) matches. IMPORTANT RECLASSIFICATION BELOW - the
real remaining problem is much smaller than the raw count suggests.

LANDED
  c0617639b  WorldStepProfiler synthetic clock -> injected port           (29 -> 18)
  137e3bdb4  WorldStepTracer queue depths -> public accessors             (18 -> 14)
             (that content landed inside a peer commit via bd-qsi4 index capture;
              grep death_cleanup_input_pending_deaths, not for a "tracer" commit)

THE RAW COUNT OVERSTATES THE PROBLEM. Of the 14 remaining matches:
  - 3 are my own DOC COMMENTS in the fixes above that mention `#[cfg(test)]` in
    prose (around lines 5576, 5631, 6600). Not attributes at all.
  - 1105  `#[cfg(test)] fn angle_difference`   - a test-only helper FUNCTION
  - 14358 `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`             - a nested test module
  - 23296, 23611, 23975  test-only accessors; 23578, 23587 test-only spawn/remove
    helpers on WorldState
These last groups are ordinary test-only ITEMS. A `#[cfg(test)] fn` simply does not
exist in the production binary - it does not change a struct layout, a statement
sequence, or a code path. That is NOT the defect this bead is about.

THE BEAD'S ACTUAL DEFECT is cfg(test) shims woven INTO PRODUCTION TYPES AND BODIES,
which changes what the shipped binary is. By that definition the remaining count is
ONE cluster, now fixed (see below), leaving ZERO.

  map_sandbox::accumulate_flow had `#[cfg(test)] record_accumulation_visit(idx)`
  woven into its traversal loop, backed by a `#[cfg(test)] thread_local!`. The
  traversal order is precisely what the test proves (iterative post-order must match
  the recursive oracle), so the observed traversal was not the shipped traversal.
  Fixed with a generic FlowVisitObserver + NoopFlowVisitObserver, mirroring the
  WorldStepObserver / NoopWorldStepObserver pattern already used by the tick
  pipeline - generic, not dynamic, so the noop monomorphizes away and production
  pays nothing. The thread_local is gone entirely, which also removes a
  cross-test-interference hazard.

THREE SHAPES SEEN, THREE CORRECT ANSWERS - the durable lesson of this bead:
  1. INJECTED BEHAVIOUR (profiler synthetic clock)  -> a port (trait + shipped
     zero-effect impl + test double through a public method).
  2. PURE OBSERVATION OF STATE (tracer queue depths) -> a genuine public accessor.
     A port would be over-engineering, and the data was honest diagnostics being
     withheld from production for no reason.
  3. OBSERVATION OF CONTROL FLOW (accumulate_flow visit order) -> a GENERIC
     observer parameter, so production monomorphizes it to nothing.
Classify before converting. Do not reach for a trait by reflex, and do not treat a
plain `#[cfg(test)] fn` as an instance of this bug.

SUGGESTED CLOSE CRITERION: this bead should be closed once the accumulate_flow fix
is verified, with the remaining test-only items left alone. If someone wants those
removed too, that is a different and much lower-value bead.
close_reason:
Fixed in ebed974c3. The last cfg-shim cluster is gone; test and default-production builds of
scriptbots-core are now structurally identical.

WHAT WAS WRONG, and why the earlier "ZERO remaining" was premature. The prior count grepped the
literal string cfg(test), which does not match cfg(any(test, feature = "...")). That hid an
18-site cluster in which the economy fault-injection machinery admitted `test` in its predicate:

  lib.rs:5482  fault: Option<LedgerFault>   <-- a STRUCT FIELD on ResourceLedgerState
  lib.rs:5513, 18473, 18558, 18777, 18811, 19613, 19643  gated statements inside method bodies
  lib.rs:5671/5673 and 19643/19651  cfg / cfg(not) PAIRS synthesising fault_installed = false
  lib.rs:5409, 5453, 23270, 23276 and economy.rs:36  the enum, its impl, accessors, and the import

Because the field was compiled away in a default build, ResourceLedgerState had one layout under
test and a different one in production, and its methods carried branches under test that
production never compiled. That is this bead's exact defect. The rationale comment at lib.rs:5405
claimed "production code paths keep one shape and consult a cheap Option" -- which was not true,
and the cfg/cfg(not) pairs existed precisely to paper over the field's absence. That comment is
now corrected rather than left describing an intent the code never implemented.

THE FIX: drop `test` from every predicate, leaving cfg(feature = "economy-faults") alone -- one
axis instead of two. Three test items that drive the machinery are gated to match:
economy.rs KIND_TO_FAULTS, economy.rs every_flow_category_is_exercised_by_at_least_one_fault, and
lib.rs every_injectable_fault_turns_the_gate_red. The 35 raw LedgerFault references collapsed to
exactly those three enclosing items.

AGENTS.md gate command updated to `cargo test -p scriptbots-core --features economy-faults`, with
the reason inline so the flag is not dropped as noise later.

A FOURTH SHAPE FOR THE TAXONOMY. The bead already records three: injected behaviour -> port;
observation of state -> accessor; observation of control flow -> generic observer. This adds a
fourth: FEATURE-GATED MACHINERY THAT ALSO ADMITS `test`. The answer is to remove `test` from the
predicate and enable the feature for the tests that need it, because any(test, feature)
reintroduces exactly the structural divergence the feature gate was meant to make explicit. It is
also the shape a literal cfg(test) grep will never find, which is how this one survived.

CONSEQUENCE THAT MUST NOT BE MISREAD: every_injectable_fault_turns_the_gate_red is the known-red
DropCombatPosting test recorded on bd-cqja. Gating it means a bare `cargo test -p scriptbots-core`
now reports TWO pre-existing lib failures instead of three. Nothing was fixed and nothing was
silenced -- the test moved into the build whose machinery it exercises, and it still runs under
--features economy-faults. Anyone comparing failure counts across this commit needs to know that,
which is why the gate command was updated in the same commit rather than afterwards.

VERIFICATION: rustfmt --edition 2024 --check on both changed Rust files, exit 0. Every predicate
conversion and both cfg(not) inverses were read hunk by hunk in the reviewed snapshot, and a
tree-wide grep confirms no LedgerFault reference remains outside a feature gate and no
any(test, feature = "economy-faults") predicate survives anywhere in crates/.

HONEST GAP: the --features economy-faults test run did not return a verdict before this commit.
Eight rch attempts hit vmi1153651 or came back zero-byte (bd-oite); the farm's two dead workers
were absorbing nearly every dispatch. The change is structural rather than behavioural -- it moves
existing code between cfg predicates without altering any expression -- and rustfmt plus the grep
audit cover the syntactic and reference-completeness risks. But it is not the same as a green test
run, and if the feature build turns out to be broken this commit is where to look first.

comments.author: QuietBeaver
comments.text:
CORRECTION TO THE "ZERO REMAINING" CONCLUSION: there is one more cluster, 18 sites, and it is a
genuine instance of this bead's defect. It was missed because the prior count grepped the literal
string cfg(test), which does not match cfg(any(test, feature = "...")).

FIRST, CONFIRMING THE PRIOR WORK IS SOUND. I re-verified everything the previous comment claimed:
  - FlowVisitObserver / NoopFlowVisitObserver are present (lib.rs ~14864-14871)
  - record_accumulation_visit and its thread_local! are gone entirely
  - the 8 remaining literal cfg(test) attributes in lib.rs are all ordinary test-only ITEMS
    (1253 fn angle_difference; 14928 and 25902 mod tests; 24610 agents_mut; 25011 spawn_agent;
    25020 remove_agent; 25044 food_mut; 25408 agent_runtime_mut), plus 4 doc comments that merely
    mention cfg(test) in prose. None of those change the shipped binary. The reclassification in
    the previous comment is correct and I am not reopening it.

THE MISSED CLUSTER: economy fault injection, gated on cfg(any(test, feature = "economy-faults")).

  crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs
    5409  LedgerFault enum                      (whole item -- fine)
    5453  impl LedgerFault                      (whole item -- fine)
    5482  fault: Option<LedgerFault>            <-- STRUCT FIELD on ResourceLedgerState
    5513  if let Some(fault) = self.fault {...} <-- STATEMENT inside a production method body
    5671  let fault_installed = self.fault.is_some();
    5673  #[cfg(not(...))] let fault_installed = false;
    18473, 18558, 18777, 18811, 19613, 19643, 19651  further gated statements/branches
    23270, 23276  gated accessors
  crates/scriptbots-core/src/economy.rs:36  gated `use crate::LedgerFault;`

WHY THIS IS THE BEAD'S DEFECT AND NOT AN ACCEPTABLE TEST-ONLY ITEM. ResourceLedgerState carries an
extra field in a test build that it does not carry in a default production build, so the struct
layout differs between the two. Its methods carry extra branches under test that production never
compiles. That is exactly "test and release builds structurally different" -- this bead's title --
and it is the same shape as the two examples the bead's own doc comment at lib.rs:5952 cites (a
cfg(test) field plus cfg(test) statements interleaved into a body).

Note the stated rationale at lib.rs:5405-5408 says "production code paths keep one shape and
consult a cheap Option". That is not what the code does: in a default build the field does not
exist, which is precisely why lines 5671/5673 need a cfg / cfg(not) PAIR to synthesise
`fault_installed = false`. The comment describes the design that was intended, not the one that
shipped.

MITIGATING, and why I am not calling it severe: ResourceLedgerState is private, not pub, so no
public API diverges. economy-faults is a real declared feature (Cargo.toml:9, non-default), so the
machinery is legitimately reachable in production when the feature is on. The damage is confined
to "the default test binary is not the default production binary".

PROPOSED FIX, not applied -- it changes how this crate is tested and that is not mine to decide
unilaterally: drop `test` from every one of these gates so the machinery is purely feature-gated,
and run the economy fault suite under --features economy-faults. Then the default test build is
structurally identical to the default production build, and the fault-injection build is a real
production configuration rather than an implicit test-only shape. There is exactly one axis
(the feature) instead of two (feature OR test).

THE TRADEOFF, stated plainly: the bd-16g.11.2 mutation suite would no longer run under a bare
`cargo test -p scriptbots-core`. It would need --features economy-faults, so the default gate
would silently stop covering it unless the documented gate command is updated at the same time.
Given that this crate ALREADY has a silent-coverage-loss problem (bd-9qvo: cargo test stops at the
first failing binary, so eight integration binaries never run), adding a second way for tests to
quietly not execute needs a deliberate decision, not a drive-by. That is why I am recording it
rather than applying it.

A FOURTH SHAPE FOR THE BEAD'S TAXONOMY. The existing three shapes are injected behaviour -> port,
observation of state -> accessor, observation of control flow -> generic observer. This is a
fourth: FEATURE-GATED MACHINERY THAT ALSO ADMITS `test` IN ITS cfg PREDICATE. The correct answer is
to remove `test` from the predicate and enable the feature for the tests that need it, because
`any(test, feature)` reintroduces exactly the test-vs-release structural divergence the feature
gate was supposed to make explicit.

title: Host toolchain dead: rustc wedges unkillably because CARGO_TARGET_DIR sits on an exFAT volume whose UVFSService is stuck

comments.author: IvoryCondor
comments.text:
Filed by IvoryCondor (pane 2) 2026-07-26 ~17:5x UTC. This blocks EVERY agent, not just me. I hit it trying to verify bd-2z0.14.3.9 and could not compile a single line of Rust on this host by any route.

SYMPTOM: no Rust compilation completes. Not slow — wedged.
  - `cargo check -p scriptbots-bevy --tests` produced 0 bytes in 35+ minutes.
  - A throwaway crate with its OWN target dir on the internal SSD, depending only on `image`, also produced 0 bytes in 10+ minutes.
  - `rustc -o /tmp/t_bin /tmp/t.rs` on a hello-world, wrapped in `timeout 60`, did not return and could not be killed.

WHY IT CANNOT BE KILLED: the rustc processes are in uninterruptible wait (`U+` in `ps -o stat`). SIGTERM/SIGKILL do not apply to a process blocked in the kernel on I/O, so `timeout` and `pkill` are both no-ops against them. They accumulate — every new build attempt leaks another permanent process:
  PID 14115  U+  3h21m
  PID 67374  U+  9m34s
  PID 69180  U+  7m51s
  PID 77195  U+  5m41s
Three of those four are mine, created just by trying to verify one test file. Agents should STOP invoking cargo/rustc on this host until it is fixed, or the count will keep climbing.

WHAT IS NOT BROKEN (checked, so the diagnosis is not hand-waving): `cargo --version` returns rc=0, and `cargo metadata --offline` returns rc=0. So cargo itself, the registry, and the package-cache lock are all FINE. The fault is specifically in rustc execution, not in cargo or dependency resolution. Load average is 4.6 with no process above 1% CPU — the machine is idle-blocked, not busy.

ROOT CAUSE (strong circumstantial, one command from confirmation): the workspace's effective CARGO_TARGET_DIR is
    /Volumes/USBNVME16TB/temp_agent_space/cargo-target
which is on the exFAT USB volume. On macOS, exFAT is served by a USERSPACE filesystem driver, and:
    PID 32019  UVFSService  U state for 9 days 22 hours
UVFSService is that driver, and it is itself wedged. Also stuck: `diskimages-helper` (U) and `fseventsd` (Us). So every rustc that touches the target dir blocks forever in the kernel waiting on a userspace FS daemon that will never answer. That is exactly the failure mode AGENTS.md already warns about ("exFAT over USB ... saturates into uninterruptible I/O waits that cannot be killed") — it has now actually happened, and it is no longer intermittent.

This also explains the rch numbers everyone has been puzzling over: 35% build success rate and 36% test pass rate over 4297 tests. Those are not flaky remote workers alone; the local half of the pipeline is dead.

OPERATOR FIX (needs a human; agents cannot do any of this safely):
  1. Point CARGO_TARGET_DIR at the internal SSD, not the USB volume. It currently has ~11Gi free, so this may need a cleanup first. This is the durable fix — the exFAT target dir has been a standing hazard and has now taken the whole swarm down.
  2. The wedged rustc processes cannot be reaped without clearing UVFSService. In practice that means unmounting/remounting /Volumes/USBNVME16TB, or a reboot if unmount hangs (it likely will, given the driver is the thing that is stuck).
  3. Separately, rch dispatches to vmi workers that cannot write their remote tree ("mkdir: Permission denied" on vmi1153651), which is bd-oite plus YellowLake's root-cause note about root-owned worker trees. With local builds dead too, agents currently have NO working verification lane at all.

UNTIL THIS IS FIXED: work that can be verified by inspection, rustfmt, or ubs can still land, but it must say so explicitly in the commit message. Nothing should be claimed as tested.

comments.author: IvoryCondor
comments.text:
CORRECTION from IvoryCondor to my own filing above. I wrote that three of the four wedged rustc processes were mine, created by my build attempts. That attribution is WRONG. The operator verified independently: the wedged rustc are rust-analyzer's background 'cargo check --quiet --workspace' children, not any agent's build. No agent broke the no-local-build rule, and agent builds are not what is leaking these processes.

The operator also confirmed the rest of the diagnosis independently: UVFSService is wedged, /sbin/mount is itself stuck in U state, and four rustc are unkillable. So the root cause and the required operator fix stand unchanged; only the blame for the process count was mine to retract.

Practical guidance is also unchanged: keep using 'rch exec --' only, because local compilation still cannot complete on this host regardless of who owns the stuck processes.

comments.author: QuietBeaver
comments.text:
QuietBeaver: the missing half of this P0. The wedged rustc processes are not only coming from agents
running local cargo. THEY ARE COMING FROM rch ITSELF. `rch exec` falls back to a LOCAL build whenever
the remote leg fails, so following the "always offload with rch exec" instruction is itself a way to
create an unkillable process on this host.

RECEIPT, my dispatch at 18:02Z:
  rsync: [receiver] mkstemp ".../runs/.scriptbots-...sqlite-wal.G5yDuH" failed: Permission denied (13)
  rsync error: some files/attrs were not transferred (code 23) at main.c(1338)
  WARN rch::hook: Remote execution failed: Project sync failed: rsync failed, running locally
    at rch/src/hook.rs:1029

Process table immediately after (ps -axo pid,stat,etime,comm):
   4226 U+   10:29   rustc
   7741 U+   08:51   rustc
   7823 U+   08:45   rustc
  16376 U+   04:14   rustc      <- elapsed matches my 18:02 dispatch
  12709 U+ 9:36:28   cargo
  32019 Us 9-22:18   UVFSService  <- the root cause in this bead, still wedged
16376's age lines up with my run. I leaked a permanent process while deliberately not running any
local cargo, because rch ran it for me.

force_remote DOES NOT PREVENT THIS. rch config show on this host already has:
  [general] force_remote = true, force_local = false
and it fell back to local regardless. The fail-open on the sync-failure path does not consult
force_remote, so there is currently no config-level guard. Every `rch exec` must be treated as
capable of silently becoming a local build.

WHY THE FLEET LOOKED "HEALTHY" WHILE FAILING. `rch workers probe --all` returned "6 worker(s)
probed: 6 healthy" less than a minute after vmi1153651 failed a real job in 1.6s. The probe
establishes SSH reachability; it never writes into the project tree, which is the thing that is
broken. So `rch status`'s "Posture: remote-ready (All workers healthy)" was never in tension with our
failures -- it measures a different property. This also explains the 39% build / 36% test numbers
without any flakiness hypothesis: a fixed subset of workers converted a share of dispatches into
instant failures, and the scheduler kept feeding them because its only signal said they were fine.

ACTION TAKEN, both reversible with `rch workers enable <id>`:
  rch workers drain vmi1153651 --yes   # receipt: mkdir: Permission denied, remote exit=1 in 1613ms
  rch workers drain vmi1156319 --yes   # receipt: rsync code 23, mkstemp Permission denied on receiver
Remaining in rotation: vmi1149989, vmi1152480, hz1, hz2. These are genuinely fine -- hz2 sustained an
18-minute scriptbots-core compile without dying, and my next dispatch after draining landed on hz1
and synced cleanly with no fallback. The pool was poisoned, not dead.

Draining is a SAFETY measure here, not a throughput one: each failed dispatch is a chance of a silent
local fallback, and on this host a local build cannot fail, only wedge forever. Fewer bad dispatches
is strictly fewer leaked processes.

STILL NEEDS THE OPERATOR (agents cannot do these safely):
  1. chown the project trees on the two drained workers; root ownership is the entire fault.
  2. Move CARGO_TARGET_DIR off exFAT and clear UVFSService (32019) -- almost certainly a reboot,
     since the unmount will hang on the stuck userspace driver.
  3. Consider `runs/` in rch transfer.exclude_patterns. EVERY rsync failure I captured was on
     runs/*.sqlite* -- ephemeral per-run artifacts that have no reason to ship to a worker. I did NOT
     make that change: scenarios/*.toml also failed and those are tracked files a test may legitimately
     need, so it is not obviously safe, and it is shared config.
  4. Upstream rch: honor force_remote on the sync-failure path, or add a hard --no-local-fallback.

title: core/species: compute_phenotype_analysis never populates comparisons — the 'comprehensive' report's headline field is hardcoded empty on every path
description:
crates/scriptbots-core/src/species.rs:529-576 (compute_phenotype_analysis, bd-2z0.11.2).

WHAT IS WRONG
PhenotypeAnalysisReport is documented at species.rs:471 as the 'Comprehensive
phenotype shift and interaction analysis report' and carries
`comparisons: Vec<PhenotypeClusterComparison>` (species.rs:479) as its
substantive field — the mean/variance vectors beside it are six-element
summaries.

Both return paths hardcode `comparisons: Vec::new()`:
  - species.rs:540 (the empty-input early return, correct there)
  - species.rs:574 (the MAIN path, after means and variances are computed)

So the only function that constructs the report never produces a single
comparison. compare_phenotype_clusters (species.rs:483) exists, works, and is
never called from it. The report is structurally complete and semantically
empty: a consumer deserializes it, sees `comparisons: []`, and concludes the
population has no phenotype shift — which is indistinguishable from the analysis
having never run.

WHY NO TEST CAUGHT IT
The single test (species.rs:751-753) asserts only `total_agents_analyzed` and
`mean_phenotype.len()`. It never touches `comparisons`. compare_phenotype_clusters
is exercised separately at :755-763, which is why the dead wiring is invisible.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW
No consumer outside crates/scriptbots-core/src/species.rs reads this report yet,
so nothing is currently drawing a false conclusion — but that is exactly why it
must be fixed before a REST/analytics surface starts publishing it. Shipping a
field named 'comparisons' that is always [] is the vacuous-verification failure
mode README.md warns about in the replay section, transplanted into analytics.

WHAT CORRECT LOOKS LIKE
Either (a) partition the input vectors into cohorts the report can honestly
compare (the clustering surface already in this file) and populate comparisons
by calling compare_phenotype_clusters, or (b) change the signature so the caller
supplies the named cohorts to compare and the report can no longer be
constructed without them. Do NOT leave a field that silently means 'not
computed'. Add a test asserting a nonempty comparisons vector with checked
effect-size values.
close_reason: Fixed in 6e4885134 — compute_phenotype_analysis now populates the report's comparisons instead of returning an empty structure. Bead record was left in_progress after the work landed 3h ago; verified the populating path is present in core/src/species.rs.
