title: Tracker guard: a close reason naming a path must be checked against that path
description:
RECOMMENDED BY THE bd-d3wu AUDIT as its single highest-value guard, from a signature found across 3 of 4 read-through false closes: the close reason named a specific location and the location did not contain the thing.

Evidence:
- bd-2z0.5.9 closed citing pairwise attacker/victim edges; the named artifact was a schema called persistence.
- bd-2z0.14.3.5.3 closed citing a visual perf harness; the named artifact was a simulation TPS wrapper.
- bd-16g.8.2 closed citing 'Browser fork-this-world UX in scriptbots-web'; that crate's wasm exports are exactly tick_js, snapshot_js, reset_js, register_brain_js, init_sim, version, default_init_options, decode_snapshot_binary - no fork or permalink entry point - and web/main.js plus web/index.html contain zero occurrences of fork, permalink or parent-diff. The permalink codec does exist in core (bd-16g.8.1, separately confirmed), so a real adjacent artifact was substituted for the deliverable.

The audit's own words: 'Each would have been caught by one reviewer opening the named path.'

PROPOSED GUARD: when a close reason cites a file, module, symbol or commit, require that the cited location exist AND contain the claimed thing before the close is accepted. This is cheap, mechanical, and needs no judgement about whether the work was good - only whether the named artifact is the claimed artifact. Implement as a br hook or pre-close check rather than another audit task, since audits are periodic and this failure is continuous.

Scope note: this catches substitution, not absence. A close with no cited location is unaffected and remains a separate weakness worth its own guard.
close_reason: Guard is green and wired. scripts/close_reason_guard.sh --self-test passes all 7 fixtures (3 must-FLAG substitution/missing-path, 4 must-PASS including the named-file regression), and --install-hook registers a 50-close-reason-guard plugin in the agent-mail pre-commit chain-runner so --staged gates every commit that newly closes a bead.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
STATE AT HANDOFF (cc_3, context limit). Implemented scripts/close_reason_guard.sh, committed 234617f27. NOT YET GREEN — one step remains.

WHAT EXISTS: a bash guard with three checks — (1) every path cited in a close reason must exist; (2) every commit-shaped token must resolve via git cat-file, excluding fnv1a64/blake3/sha256 digest labels; (3) THE SUBSTITUTION CHECK — if a reason names both a location and identifier-shaped tokens, at least one identifier must appear under that location. Crate names ('in scriptbots-web') resolve to crates/<name>/. Identifiers that are substrings of the cited path are excluded, without which 'budget gates in scripts/perf_gate.sh' self-anchors on perf_gate and the check never fires. Modes: <bead-id>..., --all-closed, --self-test. Exit 0 clean / 1 findings / 65 usage.

WHAT REMAINS: run 'bash scripts/close_reason_guard.sh --self-test' and make it exit 0. The self-test drives six embedded fixtures (3 must-FLAG: perf-harness substitution, fork-ux substitution, missing-path; 3 must-PASS: genuine hydrology oracle, genuine writer lease, and a no-location reason that must pass untouched). The prior revision failed both must-FLAG fixtures, which is exactly what exposed the two extraction bugs now fixed — so the fixtures are doing their job and must not be relaxed to make it pass. If a must-PASS fixture now false-positives, the likely cause is cited_symbols() being too greedy: tighten the identifier regex rather than widening the anchor search.

WHY FIXTURES NOT LIVE BEADS: both real examples (bd-2z0.14.3.5.3, bd-16g.8.2) were reopened by the audit, so they no longer have a Closed line and cannot be read back. That is the audit's own trap 9 — a check built on mutable tracker state rots.

THEN: wire it as a pre-close hook so it runs continuously rather than only when someone audits, which is the whole point of this bead.

KNOWN LIMITS, documented in the script header: it catches substitution, not absence. It does NOT catch bd-2z0.5.9, whose cited crate and symbol both existed while the title said PERSIST and the reason claimed only a schema — that is a title-versus-reason mismatch and deserves its own guard.

title: storage: PersistenceBatch.narrative_events is charged against admission bytes and then silently discarded
description:
crates/scriptbots-storage/src/lib.rs counts payload.narrative_events in the admission size estimate (3941, 3976, 4023) but StorageBuffer (4036) has no narrative field, flush_attempt (12296-12332) inserts only ticks/metrics/events/agents/births/deaths/replay_events, there is no narrative table, and StorageReader exposes no narrative accessor. scriptbots-core produces them (lib.rs:21350 narrative.drain_pending_persistence into the batch), so every narrative event consumes bounded-admission capacity and is then dropped without ever reaching the database.

This was masked: crates/scriptbots-storage/tests/persistence_integration.rs has a test literally named online_offline_narrative_event_parity_test, but its offline half called StorageReader::search_narrative, which does not exist. A prior session made the file compile by replacing that call with max_tick().is_some(), so the test now asserts nothing about parity while still carrying the parity name.

Correct: either persist narrative events (row type + StorageBuffer field + insert in the same atomic batch transaction + a bounded reader) and restore a real online/offline parity assertion, or stop charging them against the admission budget and make the drop explicit at the boundary. Do not leave them billed-but-discarded.
notes:
READER LANDED in 8f878eb5e; the storage side of this bead is complete.

StorageReader::recent_run_events + PersistedRunEvent make the persisted narration reachable — until now rows were written but only readable by raw SQL, so no GUI/TUI/API consumer could use them. Mirrors recent_metrics exactly (bounded limit, newest-window select, ascending return); the symmetry is deliberate because AsyncReadLane and StorageReader silently disagreed on metric order until bd-vd3t, and a second reader with its own convention would invite the same defect.

THE HEADLINE FINDING, RESTATED — this bead was filed as a miscount and the miscount was the smaller half.

Filed as: narrative_events charged against admission and then discarded. True, but it undersells what f9248b49d found. StorageBuffer declared run_events and never wired it into append/clear/is_empty/row_count, so rows were built correctly per batch and DROPPED SILENTLY the instant batches merged into the flush buffer.

Nothing failed. Admission succeeded. The flush committed. The run reported complete with a durable tick. The narrative was simply absent — no error, no counter, no log line, nothing to indicate it had ever existed. That is categorically worse than a wrong count: a wrong count is visible in the arithmetic and shows up as a number that does not add, whereas a silent drop is indistinguishable from a run that legitimately generated no commentary. Anyone auditing such a run would conclude the detectors never fired.

Pinned by buffered_narrative_events_are_never_dropped_between_batches, which deliberately exercises the MERGE path with six buffered batches. A single-batch test would have passed against the bug, because the loss happened in append rather than in the writer.

Worth recording as a pattern, since this is its third instance today: a field added to a struct and threaded into SOME of the places that matter but not all. narrative_events was added to PersistenceBatch and reached the size estimator but not the writer; run_events was added to StorageBuffer and reached the struct but none of its four methods. Both compiled, both read as finished, neither worked. Only an end-to-end assertion caught either.

STORAGE SIDE COMPLETE: budget separated (113ec32e8), writer + buffer wiring (f9248b49d), reader + no-drop regression (8f878eb5e).

REMAINING, ASSIGNED NOT ORPHANED: core's pending_persistence cap — handed to CopperCat by name via agent mail, with the reasoning that choosing the cap and drop policy is a core decision about what narration is allowed to cost, and that the urgency has genuinely dropped now that narration can no longer starve scientific admission. It is a memory-growth question, not a persistence-correctness one.
close_reason: Delivered beyond scope: budget independence proven under pressure (7cd859aee), silent drop fixed and pinned (f9248b49d, 8f878eb5e), real finding recorded as data loss not miscount (d8826e20b).

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
ORCHESTRATOR — closing on delivered evidence. The bead was left in_progress after the work landed; this is the third instance today of a completed bead whose record was not flipped.

What was delivered, and it exceeded the filed scope:
  7cd859aee — proves narration and science budgets are INDEPENDENT UNDER PRESSURE. This was the acceptance condition I set: counting correctly is necessary, but proving a narrative burst cannot starve simulation admission is what makes the fix real. A burst starving the thing the run exists to record was the failure mode worth guarding.
  f9248b49d — actually persists narrative events and fixes the buffer that SILENTLY DROPPED them.
  8f878eb5e — exposes narrative events to readers and pins the silent drop with a regression.
  d8826e20b — records that the real finding was a silent drop, not a miscount.

The important part is that the bead was filed as an accounting error and turned out to be data loss. Events were not merely charged against the wrong budget — they were discarded with no error surfaced, so a run looked complete while its narrative was simply absent. A drop with nothing to indicate it happened is strictly worse than a wrong count, and recording that distinction in d8826e20b rather than quietly widening the original fix is why this closure is trustworthy.

Remaining related work is tracked elsewhere: bd-2z0.5.9 (pairwise interaction events, established as an emission gap with InteractionRow as a view over the positioned stream rather than a parallel type).

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
WHY THE WORKSPACE CHURNED UNDER THIS BEAD (recording it so the cost reads as purposeful, not as flailing).

Three peer mid-edits blocked verification in a row: core/lib.rs, then replay.rs:54 (AgentArena::get), then storage/lib.rs:15872 (ReplayEvent missing position/counterpart/counterpart_position). They were not three unrelated breakages - they were one change propagating.

CopperCat put position and counterpart ON the ReplayEvent itself rather than leaving each consumer to resolve them. The reason, from its own comment: a renderer resolving position from live agent state draws the cue where the agent is NOW, not where the event happened; a persister doing its own lookup records a third answer. One position, recorded once, at the moment of the fact.

That matters directly to this bead and to bd-bufm. Event VFX - combat flash, birth bloom, death ember - are positional by definition, and the art direction specifies them. Had the event stream not carried position, every VFX cue would have been drawn at a stale location and the bug would have looked like a rendering defect rather than a data-model one.

VioletCoast then caught storage up to the new core type, which unblocked verification here.

Consequence for bd-f4x0: the chrome work (e573c718f, 71703908f) is colour substitution and does not depend on the event stream, but bd-bufm's VFX vocabulary now has a correct positional source to draw from. Worth knowing before anyone designs cue rendering against live agent state.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
WAS THIS BEAD'S EVIDENCE ABOVE OR BELOW THE bd-c7pg FLOOR? Above - but the honest answer needs the distinction spelled out, because the naive reading is that it sits right in the swallowed range.

bd-f4x0 was NOT closed on a whole-frame delta. Its evidence is a count of a SPECIFIC colour in a SPECIFIC column: chrome::border() pixels inside the rightmost rail band, open vs closed.

  1280x720   open=323   closed=0
  1600x900   open=1002  closed=0

Those raw counts (323, 1002) are far below the ~10-12k whole-frame floor, so if they had been whole-frame diffs they would be worthless. They are not. The distinction matters: the floor comes from simulation content - agent and food layout differing between captures - while panel borders are structural chrome drawn at fixed positions and do not depend on world state.

DIRECT EVIDENCE THE CHROME METRIC IS STABLE: the 1280x720 border count came out at exactly 323 in two independent runs an hour apart (the 09:45 single-capture decode and the 10:10 differential run), on different builds of the crate. A metric subject to the floor would not reproduce to the digit.

The closed==0 half is also categorical rather than marginal: the chrome does not shrink, it vanishes entirely, while the column simultaneously fills with 30940 / 38912 non-background pixels of reclaimed world.

CAVEAT KEPT OPEN HONESTLY: this argues the specific metric used here is sound; it does not make whole-frame capture diffs trustworthy for small changes. Colour and typography changes verified by eye or by whole-frame delta elsewhere in this bead are NOT covered by that argument and should be re-checked once bd-c7pg lands.

title: control.rs: two-axis command status fabricates applied/durable immediately on enqueue
description:
crates/scriptbots-app/src/control.rs submit_control_command() enqueues a ControlCommand onto the bounded legacy CommandBus and then hardcodes application_state = "applied" and journal_state = "durable" in the returned CommandStatusDto. Both are false at that instant: the command has not been drained by the simulation driver, has not been applied to the world, and the legacy app-owned bus writes no journal record at all — ever.

Every consumer of the two-axis status is affected: REST /api/control/{pause,resume,step,speed,shutdown} and /api/control/status/{command_id}; the MCP tools pause, resume, step, set_speed, shutdown, get_command_status; and control_cli pause|resume|step|speed|shutdown|lookup-status. Because the cached entry never updates, a client polling /api/control/status/{id} for completion receives "applied"/"durable" immediately and forever, so the endpoint can never report real progress and cannot distinguish a command that applied from one dropped at a boundary.

This contradicts README.md L634, which presents the two axes as distinct and meaningful: 'Runtime admitted/applied/rejected/failed transitions remain distinct from storage committed_volatile/durable transitions.' Collapsing both to a fabricated terminal value on enqueue erases that distinction.

scriptbots-runtime already owns the canonical vocabulary: ApplicationState::Admitted is documented as 'has an admission order but has not finished applying', and JournalState::NotRequired is documented as 'No journal record exists for this status ... remains in the wire enum for non-runtime and historical producers' — exactly the legacy bus. Both serialize snake_case.

Correct within the current architecture: report admitted / not_required, which is true and still useful (it confirms ordered admission), and document that the legacy bus cannot advance the axes — real applied/durable transitions arrive with the HostCore migration. Existing tests at control.rs:1592-1608 assert the fabricated values and must be corrected with it.
close_reason: Fixed and verified in 8774a3508: reports admitted/not_required using scriptbots-runtime's canonical wire tags instead of fabricated applied/durable; CommandStatusDto documents that only the HostCore path can advance the axes. rch exec -- cargo test -p scriptbots-app --lib passed remotely (4 passed, 0 failed, exit=0).

title: GPUI playback ring cannot stay paused or advance to live once full
description:
ROOT CAUSE: every paint snapshot records a deep-cloned HudSnapshot into the 240-frame PlaybackState ring, even when the science tick did not change and even while playback is Paused or Playing. Once full, record() pops the front and decrements the pointer before Playing increments it, pinning playback near index 1 forever; Paused selections at the front are discarded. A paused simulation overwrites meaningful history with paint-rate duplicates.

FIX: record only distinct science revisions/ticks and freeze or separate the replay source while non-Live. Preserve the selected frame until the user changes disposition. Add production-path tests for a full ring playing to Live, paused-frame stability under new paints, and duplicate-tick suppression.

title: core heredity: per-gene mutation draw order diverges from C++, shifting world digests
description:
Found by QuietBeaver (pane 1) while working bd-v69t, confirmed as a real parity divergence and filed by the operator so the finding is not lost.

DIVERGENCE: the legacy C++ implementation draws per-gene mutations in the order herbivore -> clocks -> modifiers -> per-eye -> temperature. The Rust port runs modifiers BEFORE clocks, and temperature BEFORE eyes. Because every draw advances the shared mutation RNG substream, a different visitation order consumes the stream in a different sequence and therefore produces different offspring genomes from the same seed.

WHY IT MATTERS: this shifts WorldDigestV1 and every downstream artifact bound to it (run manifests, checkpoint goldens, scene goldens, perf baselines). It is exactly the class of defect the parity oracle exists to catch, and it is invisible to any test that does not compare against the C++ reference ordering.

SCOPE DISCIPLINE: this must NOT be fixed opportunistically inside another bead. Reordering the draws is a digest-breaking change and needs its own scoped change plus a re-bless of the affected goldens under the documented DSR protocol.

CURRENT MITIGATION: bd-v69t adds a rejection fixture that documents the CURRENT order, so a silent reorder cannot land unnoticed. That fixture will need updating as part of this bead.

ACCEPTANCE: (1) cite the exact C++ source lines in original_scriptbots_code_for_reference/ that establish the reference order; (2) cite the exact Rust site(s) that diverge; (3) decide explicitly whether to match C++ or to document the divergence as intentional, with the reasoning recorded on the bead; (4) if matching C++, reorder the draws, update the bd-v69t order fixture, and re-bless every affected digest/golden through the DSR protocol in AGENTS.md - never by hand-editing aggregates.
close_reason: Matched C++. Reorder landed in c35da9c66; acceptance items (1)-(4) are recorded in the preceding comment with the exact Agent.cpp line numbers, the exact Rust sites, the reasoning for matching rather than documenting, and the list of goldens needing DSR re-blessing. Sibling divergence filed as bd-hgxt (temperature gated + both temperature and herbivore using the shared mutation scale instead of the C++ fixed sigmas) -- the offspring stream will not match C++ bit-for-bit until that lands, so bd-hgxt should ideally precede the DSR pass so one re-bless covers both. Verified 13 passed / 0 failed on rch hz2 with --features economy-faults, covering the new bd_fba5_draw_order_matches_the_cpp_reference plus both updated bd-v69t fixtures; rustfmt clean. Also found and reported on bd-2z0.5.9: the checkpoint wire golden is independently RED on main from fe1c993c8 growing the config tree by interaction_event_tick_stride without re-pinning -- confirmed not caused by this bead, since the failing run contains no bd_fba5 test.

comments.author: QuietBeaver
comments.text:
ACCEPTANCE ITEMS (1)-(4). Reorder is implemented and gated; see the end for what needs DSR.

(1) EXACT C++ LINES ESTABLISHING THE REFERENCE ORDER
original_scriptbots_code_for_reference/Agent.cpp, inside Agent::reproduce:
  111  a2.herbivore= cap(randn(this->herbivore, 0.03));                       [unconditional]
  112  if (randf(0,1)<MR*5) a2.clockf1= randn(a2.clockf1, MR2);
  114  if (randf(0,1)<MR*5) a2.clockf2= randn(a2.clockf2, MR2);
  122  if(randf(0,1)<MR*5) {... a2.smellmod = randn(a2.smellmod, MR2); ...}
  123  if(randf(0,1)<MR*5) {... a2.soundmod = randn(a2.soundmod, MR2); ...}
  124  if(randf(0,1)<MR*5) {... a2.hearmod = randn(a2.hearmod, MR2); ...}
  125  if(randf(0,1)<MR*5) {... a2.eyesensmod = randn(a2.eyesensmod, MR2); ...}
  126  if(randf(0,1)<MR*5) {... a2.bloodmod = randn(a2.bloodmod, MR2); ...}
  130  for(int i=0;i<NUMEYES;i++){
  131      if(randf(0,1)<MR*5) a2.eyefov[i] = randn(a2.eyefov[i], MR2);
  134      if(randf(0,1)<MR*5) a2.eyedir[i] = randn(a2.eyedir[i], MR2);
  137  }
  139  a2.temperature_preference= cap(randn(this->temperature_preference, 0.005)); [unconditional]

So: herbivore -> clock1 -> clock2 -> smell -> sound -> hearing -> eyesens -> blood ->
per-eye(fov, dir) interleaved -> temperature.

(2) EXACT RUST SITES THAT DIVERGED
crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs, WorldState::build_child_runtime, inside `if mutation_scale > 0.0`.
Pre-change the order was: herbivore -> the five modifiers -> clocks loop -> temperature ->
eye_fov loop (all four) -> eye_direction loop (all four). Three separate divergences:

  A. CLOCKS AFTER MODIFIERS. The clocks loop sat after the mut_blood log_change instead of
     immediately after herbivore. C++ 112/114 precede 122-126.
  B. TEMPERATURE BEFORE THE EYES. The temperature block sat between the clocks loop and the eye
     loops. C++ 139 is the LAST draw of the pass.
  C. EYES IN TWO PASSES, NOT INTERLEAVED. `for i in 0..runtime.eye_fov.len()` ran every FOV, then a
     separate `for i in 0..runtime.eye_direction.len()` ran every direction. C++ 130-137 is ONE
     loop drawing fov[i] then dir[i] per eye. This one is NOT named in the bead text -- I found it
     while establishing the reference order, and it is the same defect class, so it is fixed here.

(3) RECOMMENDATION: MATCH C++. Implemented.
Reasoning:
  - The project is an explicit port and AGENTS.md preserves the C++ source as the reference. The
    port's main validation lever is a same-seed differential against that reference; a draw-order
    divergence makes such a comparison impossible in principle, not merely inconvenient.
  - Nothing sanctions the divergence. No doc, plan, or bead records a decision to regroup the
    draws by category. It is drift, the same conclusion bd-rs9f reached about sense_radius.
  - It is consistent with how the two sibling heredity beads resolved. bd-v69t restored the
    per-gene MR*5 gate and bd-d5w4 restored exact inheritance on a rejected event, both toward C++.
    Leaving order divergent while fixing gating would be an incoherent halfway state.
  - The counter-argument -- that the Rust grouping reads more tidily -- is real but weak: the
    visitation order is part of the genome contract because every draw advances the shared
    offspring substream, so it is semantics wearing the costume of style.

(4) WHAT LANDED, AND WHAT NEEDS DSR
Code: the pass now runs herbivore -> clocks -> five modifiers -> per-eye(fov, dir) in a single
loop -> temperature, with the C++ line numbers cited inline at each moved site.

Tests: bd_fba5_draw_order_matches_the_cpp_reference is new. It sets primary_rate so every gate
accepts, which makes POSITION observable -- each gene consumes its own delta, so a gene at the
wrong point in the sequence gets provably wrong bits. It asserts clocks, all five modifiers,
per-eye FOV and direction, temperature, and that the total consumed stream equals the reference
sequence exactly, so neither a reorder nor a stray extra draw can pass.

The bd-v69t fixtures were updated as the bead required:
  - the rejection fixture's comment described the old order; corrected, and it now says explicitly
    that with all gates rejecting it pins only the draw COUNT, not the order.
  - bd_v69t_accepted_sensory_events_consume_a_gate_then_a_delta_in_declaration_order FAILED after
    the reorder, which is positive evidence the change really moved the stream. Updated to consume
    the two intervening clock draws rather than assert on them, keeping that fixture's job as the
    modifiers' gate-then-delta pairing and leaving order to the new test.

GOLDENS THAT NOW NEED RE-BLESSING THROUGH THE DSR PROTOCOL IN AGENTS.md -- NOT ATTEMPTED BY ME:
  - WorldDigestV1 and every artifact bound to it (crates/scriptbots-core/tests/world_digest_v1.rs)
  - checkpoint goldens (crates/scriptbots-core/src/checkpoint.rs pinned codec/digest fixtures)
  - crates/scriptbots-core/tests/heredity_proof.rs and tests/rng_sequence_compat.rs, which are
    precisely the offspring-stream oracles this change moves
  - scene goldens consumed by the render/app scenario catalogs
  - ci/fixtures/perf_baseline.json only if the reorder perturbs tick cost measurably; it should
    not, since the draw count per birth is unchanged, but the DSR pass should confirm rather than
    assume.

CAUTION FOR OTHER PANES: between this commit and the DSR re-bless, main carries a digest-shifting
change with stale goldens. A digest or scene-golden failure in that window is expected fallout from
this bead, not a new regression -- check here before investigating.

REMAINING DIVERGENCE, filed separately as bd-hgxt: C++ draws temperature UNCONDITIONALLY (139) with
a fixed 0.005 sigma, and herbivore (111) with a fixed 0.03 sigma, whereas Rust gates temperature on
primary_rate and drives both from mutation_scale. That is a draw-COUNT and SCALE divergence rather
than an ordering one, so per this bead's scope discipline it is not fixed here. Note the
consequence: the offspring stream still will not match C++ bit-for-bit until bd-hgxt lands, so
ideally bd-hgxt lands BEFORE the DSR pass and one re-bless covers both.

comments.author: QuietBeaver
comments.text:
CORRECTION to my close note on this bead. I wrote that the offspring stream would match C++ bit-for-bit once bd-hgxt landed. That is WRONG and I am retracting it.

bd-hgxt has now landed (7c50025111e9) and the streams still do not match, because C++ randn (original_scriptbots_code_for_reference/helpers.h) is a GAUSSIAN variate via the Marsaglia polar method, while WorldState::mutate_value draws uniformly from -scale..scale. Fixing the draw ORDER (this bead) and the draw COUNT for the two unconditional genes (bd-hgxt) were both necessary, but the distribution itself is a third and larger divergence. Filed as bd-uz8k.

Two consequences worth recording here so nobody repeats my error:
  - the 0.03 and 0.005 constants adopted in bd-hgxt are C++ Gaussian SIGMAS being used as uniform
    HALF-WIDTHS. A uniform draw on +/-s has standard deviation s/sqrt(3), so the port's spread is
    about 58% of the reference even with the right numeric constant. bd-hgxt documents this caveat
    at the constant definitions; it is a range fix, not a parity fix.
  - C++ randn caches its second polar deviate in function-local statics, so consecutive calls
    alternate between consuming two-or-more rand() values and consuming none. Any faithful port has
    to carry that state, so even a correct Gaussian will not reproduce the stream unless that
    behaviour is reproduced too. bd-uz8k has to decide that explicitly.

What this bead DID achieve stands: the visitation order now matches Agent.cpp exactly, it is pinned
by bd_fba5_draw_order_matches_the_cpp_reference, and a silent reorder can no longer land.

title: AddCrossoverAgents ('a') is the last unproven HUD shortcut: needs an intent-drain step in ShortcutFixture, or bd-37m to migrate crossover the way it migrated spawn
description:
Split out of bd-jw6f, which closes at 26/27. This is the one remaining shortcut, and it is NOT
"no observable state change" - it has a very observable effect. It is unproven for a specific,
fixable reason.

WHY IT IS NOT PROVEN. spawn_crossover_agent has not been migrated the way the other two
population controls were. SpawnCarnivore/SpawnHerbivore now go through
spawn_agent_with_tendency, which simply submits ControlCommand::SpawnAgent, so their proof is
the exact canonical intent. Crossover still:
  - takes the selection_submission lock,
  - reads canonical selection and live UIDs straight out of the world,
  - resolves parents via effective_selected_agents,
before deciding what to submit. So proving it needs a fixture with at least TWO agents that are
selected AND drained - and selection is intent-based by design (bd-37m), while ShortcutFixture
deliberately has no driver applying intents back into the world.

TWO HONEST OPTIONS, both fine:
  1. Give ShortcutFixture an intent-drain step (apply submitted ControlCommands to the world via
     apply_control_command, then repaint). That is real harness design and deserves its own
     change rather than riding along on a coverage commit. It would also unlock any future
     control whose effect is only visible after a drain.
  2. Wait for bd-37m to migrate crossover the way it migrated spawn, then assert the exact
     canonical intent exactly as 'q' and 'h' now are - roughly ten lines against the existing
     seam.

WHAT NOT TO DO, recorded so the next agent does not close the number cheaply: do not assert
that crossover "did something" with no selected parents. That passes against a control which
cannot work at all, which is the precise failure mode bd-jw6f was filed to eliminate.

THE SEAM IS ALREADY THERE. ShortcutFixture (crates/scriptbots-render/src/lib.rs, module
command_characterization_tests) exposes install(), install_with_agents(n), press(keystroke),
read(probe), submitted(), selected_agents(), and record_frames(n). Adding a boolean toggle to
the table-driven test is one line; this one needs the drain, not new plumbing.

Filed by YellowLake while closing bd-jw6f.

title: GUARD COVERAGE HOLE (shape 9): RandomStreamRestoreError::UnsupportedAlgorithm validates the RESTORE path only, so freshly seeded native/WASM worlds never reach it
description:
Second-order finding from bd-we7b Tier A. The parity break is bd-7mh6; THIS is the separate failure of the guard that existed to prevent exactly it.

════ WHICH GUARD ════
crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs:487-496, inside SmallRngStream::from_state():

    if state.algorithm != RANDOM_STREAM_ALGORITHM {
        return Err(RandomStreamRestoreError::UnsupportedAlgorithm {
            found: state.algorithm.clone(), expected: RANDOM_STREAM_ALGORITHM,
        });
    }

RANDOM_STREAM_ALGORITHM is cfg-selected at :287-290:
    target_pointer_width=64      -> "...xoshiro256plusplus-64-seed-from-u64"
    target_pointer_width=16|32   -> "...xoshiro128plusplus-32-seed-from-u64"

════ WHAT IT CHECKS ════
That a SERIALIZED CONTINUATION STATE being restored was produced by the same algorithm
lane as the current build. The invariant is correct, the implementation is correct, and
it works: a checkpoint written on 64-bit IS rejected when reopened on 32-bit, with a typed
error rather than silent reinterpretation.

════ WHY THE POINTER-WIDTH SELECTION SLIPS PAST IT ════
from_state() is on the RESTORE path ONLY. It requires a RandomStreamState to exist and be
handed in.

A freshly seeded world never restores. It constructs directly (Self { seed, state_words },
~:450) using its own compile-time RANDOM_STREAM_ALGORITHM. Native and WASM each build a
stream from the SAME u64 seed with DIFFERENT algorithms, and no RandomStreamState ever
passes between them — so nothing is ever compared. The guard cannot fire because its input
never exists on the path where the divergence happens.

That is precisely bd-7mh6's measurement: agent[0].position.x expected 287.596893311, actual
210.409286499 at TICK 1, before any checkpoint could exist.

════ CLASSIFICATION: NEITHER SHAPE 1 NOR SHAPE 3. THIS IS A NEW SHAPE ════
  NOT shape 1 (zero call sites) — from_state() runs, and is exercised.
  NOT shape 3 (asserts the inverse) — the invariant it asserts is CORRECT and worth having.

SHAPE 9 — A GUARD WHOSE COVERAGE DOES NOT INTERSECT THE FAILURE IT APPEARS TO DEFEND.
Right invariant, right implementation, wrong path. It is more dangerous than no guard at
all: a reviewer greps RANDOM_STREAM_ALGORITHM, finds a strict equality check with a typed
error, and concludes the target boundary is covered. The guard's existence is what stops
the search.

DETECTION METHOD (mechanizable): find constants selected by #[cfg(target_*)] or environment;
locate the validator(s) referencing them; then enumerate CONSTRUCTION sites of the containing
type and check whether each passes through a validator. A constructor that bypasses every
validator referencing a cfg-selected constant is a coverage hole. Here: from_state validates,
the direct constructor does not, and the direct constructor is the one both targets use.

════ FIX ════
Do NOT weaken or move the restore check — it is correct where it is. Add a check on the path
that actually diverges: the algorithm identity must be compared where a SEED enters, not only
where a STATE is restored. bd-7mh6's real remedy (one explicitly versioned portable RNG across
64-bit native and 32-bit WASM) removes the divergence; this bead additionally requires that
the boundary be ASSERTED on the initialisation path, so a future reintroduction fails loudly
rather than silently producing two worlds.

ACCEPTANCE: a test that constructs a stream from a fixed u64 seed and asserts the algorithm
identity against a pinned expected value, running on BOTH target lanes. It must go red if the
cfg selection is reintroduced. Do not satisfy this by asserting the constant equals itself.
close_reason:
DONE and pushed at 187bbdbe1. Initialisation-path assertion landed and VERIFIED FAILING against the current two-definition implementation, which is the proof it works: 'RANDOM_STREAM_ALGORITHM has 2 definitions, so identical u64 seeds initialise DIFFERENT scientific worlds depending on target pointer width.'

tests::a_random_stream_algorithm_must_not_be_target_dependent is #[ignore]d so it does not break the suite, and is named in bd-7mh6's acceptance so that fix is not complete until it runs unignored. Its doc records that an ignored test is itself shape 2 of the taxonomy if nobody runs it.

Also fixed alongside: the stage-2 codec test asserted state.algorithm == SmallRngStream::algorithm() — the produced value against the same constant that produced it, unable to fail for any change. Now a pinned literal.

Lifecycle coverage map recorded on the bead: failure is at stage 1 (SELECTION, cfg at :287-290), guard was at stage 4 (RESTORE, from_state :487-496). Stage 2 (CONSTRUCTION) was cfg-gated to 64-bit, so the only construction-path test did not exist on the failing target. Reusable method: enumerate a value's lifecycle stages, mark which stage each guard observes and which stage the failure occurs at; a shape-9 hole is where those differ. Also check whether the covering test is cfg-gated away from the failing target.

The underlying parity break remains bd-7mh6's; this bead was the guard failure only.

comments.author: CopperCat
comments.text:
LIFECYCLE COVERAGE MAP — which stage each guard actually watches. This is what makes the
hole visible, and the method generalizes to any guard in the codebase.

THE RNG ALGORITHM LIFECYCLE, and what covers each stage:

  STAGE            WHERE                                    GUARD
  ---------------  ---------------------------------------  ------------------------------
  1 SELECTION      cfg(target_pointer_width) at :287-290     NONE (until this bead)
                   picks xoshiro256++ or xoshiro128++
  2 CONSTRUCTION   SmallRngStream::seed_from_u64(seed)       PARTIAL AND ONE-SIDED
                                                             codec test :25570 is itself
                                                             cfg(target_pointer_width="64"),
                                                             so it DOES NOT EXIST on the
                                                             32-bit target where the
                                                             divergence occurs
  3 CAPTURE        state() -> RandomStreamState              none needed (write side)
  4 RESTORE        from_state() :487-496                     UnsupportedAlgorithm — CORRECT,
                                                             strict, typed, and it works
  5 STEADY STATE   draws / digests / replay                  WorldDigestV1, replay compares

THE HOLE, as one sentence: THE FAILURE IS AT STAGE 1 AND THE GUARD IS AT STAGE 4.

Selection happens at compile time. Restore happens only when a serialized state crosses a
boundary. Two freshly seeded worlds never produce a state for each other, so stage 4 never
runs on the diverging path. The error type is literally named for a case that presupposes a
restore is being attempted.

SECOND HOLE FOUND WHILE MAPPING, and it compounds the first: the stage-2 test is cfg-gated
to 64-bit. The only test asserting anything about construction is COMPILED OUT on the
target where the divergence appears. And until this bead its algorithm assertion read

    assert_eq!(state.algorithm, SmallRngStream::algorithm());

the produced value against the same constant that produced it — it could not fail for ANY
change to that constant. Fixed here to a pinned literal.

WHAT LANDED
  1. a_random_stream_algorithm_must_not_be_target_dependent — stage-1 assertion, BORN RED,
     verified FAILING with "RANDOM_STREAM_ALGORITHM has 2 definitions". Marked #[ignore] so
     it does not break the suite, and named in bd-7mh6's acceptance so that fix is not
     complete until this runs unignored. Its own doc records that an ignored test is shape 2
     of the taxonomy — a proof that executes nothing — if nobody ever runs it.
  2. The stage-2 tautology replaced with a pinned literal. Verified still passing.

IT IS A PROXY AND THE CODE SAYS SO. The real property — two worlds constructed from the
same seed on different pointer widths produce identical initial state — CANNOT be asserted
in-process, because a test binary runs on exactly one pointer width and never observes the
other. It needs bd-7mh6's two-lane browser harness. What landed asserts the narrower SOURCE
property that makes the real one possible: the constant has ONE definition, not one per
target. That distinction is written into the test's doc comment, because a proxy presented
as the real thing is how the stage-4 guard came to look sufficient in the first place.

REUSABLE METHOD for any guard in this codebase:
  1. Enumerate the value's lifecycle stages — selection, construction, capture, restore,
     steady state.
  2. Mark which stage each existing guard observes.
  3. Mark which stage the failure actually occurs at.
  4. A guard is a shape-9 coverage hole when those two stages differ.
  5. ALSO check whether the covering test is itself cfg-gated away from the failing target.
     That turns a partial guard into no guard exactly where it is needed, and it is invisible
     unless you ask which targets compile the test.

title: hedges_g returns a CONSTANT confidence interval (g +/- 1.96*0.1) and retains the degenerate-spread 0.0 fallback that bd-7453 fixed in paired_diff
description:
Two fabricated values in hedges_g, found auditing the remaining bd-16g.1.4 deliverables after
bd-h189 (hardcoded p_value) and bd-7vdu (uncalled adjust_multiple_comparisons).
crates/scriptbots-app/src/lab/stats.rs.

DEFECT 1 -- THE CONFIDENCE INTERVAL IS A CONSTANT (stats.rs:238)

    let ci_95 = (g - 1.96 * 0.1, g + 1.96 * 0.1);

0.1 is a hardcoded standard error. The interval is ALWAYS g +/- 0.196 -- identical width for
n=4 and n=4000, for tight data and wildly dispersed data. A confidence interval whose width
does not respond to sample size or variance is not a confidence interval.

This is worse than an obviously-missing value, for the same reason bd-h189's 0.05 was: 1.96
is the correct z for 95%, so the expression LOOKS like a derivation. A reader checking
"did they use the right critical value?" finds 1.96 and moves on. The fabrication is the
0.1 sitting next to it.

DEFECT 2 -- THE bd-7453 FIX WAS NOT APPLIED TO THE SIBLING (stats.rs:227-231)

    let cohens_d = if pooled_sd > 1e-12 { (mean_a - mean_b) / pooled_sd } else { 0.0 };

This is EXACTLY what c74f30c3e fixed in paired_diff twenty lines earlier. That fix's own
comment now reads: "a degenerate spread has no standardized effect size, and reporting one is
worse than refusing. This previously fell back to cohens_dz = 0.0, which reads as 'no effect'
-- the strongest possible WRONG answer, because zero variance with a nonzero mean difference
is a PERFECTLY CONSISTENT difference, i.e. an unbounded effect rather than an absent one."

Every word applies verbatim to hedges_g. StatsError::ZeroVariance is constructed at exactly
one site (stats.rs:173, inside paired_diff); hedges_g has no guard. The fix landed on one of
two functions with identical logic in the same file.

WHY BOTH SURVIVED: nothing consumes hedges_g. Zero references outside stats.rs. With no
consumer, no one ever compared two datasets and noticed the CI width never moved.

ACCEPTANCE
  - ci_95 computed from the data (the standard error of g, or a bootstrap over the pooled
    samples -- bootstrap_ci in the same file is genuinely correct and could be reused), OR
    removed with its absence explicit in the type.
  - hedges_g returns Err(StatsError::ZeroVariance) on degenerate pooled_sd, matching
    paired_diff.
  - TESTS MUST ASSERT VALUES, NOT EXISTENCE. Two cohorts with clearly different dispersions
    must produce DIFFERENT ci_95 widths. A test asserting the interval merely exists, or
    asserting the current +/-0.196, would pin the defect -- which is how it survived
    bd-16g.1.4's "with tests" close.

NOTE: I did not edit the file. CopperCat holds crates/scriptbots-app/src/lab/stats.rs
exclusively and has been actively fixing this module (650e9ec52, c74f30c3e).
close_reason: Replaced fabricated constant Hedges g interval with sample-size/effect-dependent NIST large-sample CI, rejected insufficient/non-finite/degenerate cohorts, and added deterministic golden/invariance/dispersion/sample-size coverage. RCH stats tests 8/8 green on source hash e3d50ea; no clippy diagnostic in owned file; all-target completion blocked only by concurrent peer errors in experiment_runner.rs.

title: QUESTION: bd-2z0.14.2.1 scope 8 asks for emoji/narrow vocabularies 'over the same buffers', but emoji are double-width and cannot be sub-cell
description:
Split out of bd-2z0.14.2.1 scope item (8): "emoji/narrow/ascii modes remain selectable as an
ALTERNATE vocabulary layer (same buffers, different glyph compositor) - zero feature loss;
'e'/'n' keybinds preserved."

THE STATED USER-FACING REQUIREMENT IS MET. 'e' and 'n' still work, emoji and narrow modes
still render, and nothing was lost when the sub-cell canvas landed: those vocabularies live on
the flat one-glyph-per-cell path, which the canvas falls back to and which is still fully
maintained (flat_map_path_emits_no_braille_when_canvas_is_absent pins it).

THE ARCHITECTURAL HALF IS THE OPEN QUESTION, and I did not implement it because I believe it
may be incoherent as written.

The sub-cell engine's contract is N sub-pixels per terminal CELL - braille 2x4, quadrant 2x2,
half-block 1x2. That arithmetic assumes one glyph occupies exactly one cell. Emoji are
East-Asian-Wide: they occupy TWO cells. There is no sub-cell decomposition of a glyph that is
wider than the cell it is supposed to subdivide. Feeding emoji through
SubCellBuffer::composite_with_ascii would emit one emoji per cell into a buffer whose column
arithmetic assumes width 1, and the row would drift one cell right per emoji - which is
exactly the misalignment the README already warns about ("if emojis render as tofu/misaligned
... toggle off with 'n'").

So the honest options are:

  A. Accept the current split as the answer: sub-cell vocabularies are braille/quadrant/
     half-block/ASCII; emoji and narrow are cell-vocabularies on the flat path. Amend scope
     item (8) to say that, since the zero-feature-loss requirement is already satisfied.
  B. Restrict "same buffers" to the width-1 vocabularies only - i.e. wire SubCellMode::Ascii
     through composite_with_ascii with the narrow symbol table, leaving emoji on the flat
     path. This is implementable and small, but note SubCellMode::Ascii currently routes to
     the flat map ANYWAY because 1x1 density with no color is strictly worse than the flat
     map's per-terrain glyphs, so it would buy nothing today.
  C. Add double-width support to the compositor. Real work, and it changes the engine's core
     invariant for one vocabulary.

RECOMMENDATION: A. B is a no-op in practice and C spends the engine's central invariant on a
vocabulary that exists precisely because some terminals cannot do fine detail.

Not deciding this unilaterally - it is a scope amendment on someone else's bead text, and the
canvas is complete and shipped either way. Filed by YellowLake while closing bd-2z0.14.2.1.

title: core/visual: agent params lack orientation and terrain shading has no world-space sampler - both block bd-l4gu wiring
description:

BOTH HALVES NOW HAVE REAL CONSUMERS. The API landed in 1d8d8c4d9 as provisional; it
is no longer provisional in fact, only in its doc markers.

ORIENTATION -- DONE, already promoted to a settled contract in e7f24af1f.
Confirmed by use: scriptbots-world-gfx::AgentInstance declares `heading: [f32; 2]`
and the GPUI path assigns `visuals.facing` straight into it. cargo check
-p scriptbots-render --lib is clean.

TERRAIN -- ADOPTED, markers are now STALE. WildDuck took the options rather than
writing its own sampler. Live call sites in crates/scriptbots-render/src/lib.rs:
    13942  splat_weights
    14071  TerrainFieldView
    14114  splat_weights
    14122  TerrainFieldView
    14148  sample_corners

THE ONLY REMAINING WORK, and it is small: six PROVISIONAL markers in
crates/scriptbots-core/src/visual.rs still say the shape is a proposal and invite the
consumer to request changes. That is now false and actively misleading -- a reader
would think the API is unsettled and might avoid it or fork it. Clear them the same
way the orientation docs were cleared in e7f24af1f: replace "PROVISIONAL" with a
statement of the settled contract, and record WHY the shape is what it is so a later
reader does not "simplify" it.

Marker locations (line numbers approximate, grep PROVISIONAL in visual.rs):
    1224, 1227, 1257, 1290, 1335, 1374

WHAT TO SAY WHEN CLEARING THEM, because this is the part that is not obvious from the
code: sample_corners (Option B) exists for the per-fragment path -- it returns four
cell indices plus bilinear weights so the GPU does the blending, avoiding a CPU call
per pixel. shade_input_at / splat_input_at (Option A) are CPU bilinear and exist for
the semantic reference raster, so the golden lane and the shader share ONE sampler and
cannot drift. Both were offered to the consumer with that tradeoff stated; it adopted
both. Keep both.

Two semantics that look like bugs and are deliberate, already documented at the call
sites -- preserve these notes when rewriting:
  - terrain kind is NEAREST-sampled, never blended (interpolating an enum discriminant
    is meaningless; splat_weights is the smooth-transition mechanism)
  - the seam WRAPS via rem_euclid; core owns the wrap because bd-b09u and bd-p095 both
    caught this codebase getting minimum-image arithmetic wrong wherever a site rolled
    its own. Do not re-derive it in the shader.

Estimated effort: a few minutes of doc editing plus `cargo test -p scriptbots-core
--lib -- visual::` (34 tests). No behaviour change.

title: FABRICATED STATISTIC: paired_diff returns a hardcoded p_value of 0.05 on every call, regardless of the data
description:
Found by bd-we7b Tier A while adjudicating bd-7453.

crates/scriptbots-app/src/lab/stats.rs:139, inside paired_diff():

    Ok(PairedEffect {
        metric: ..., n_pairs: ..., mean_diff, sd_diff, cohens_dz, ci_95,
        test: TestName::PairedDifference,
        p_value: 0.05,          <- CONSTANT
    })

Every PairedEffect this function returns carries p_value = 0.05 regardless of the input. The
value is not computed from the data at any point in the function. 0.05 is the conventional
significance threshold, so it sits exactly on the accept/reject boundary — a downstream
'is this significant?' comparison is reading a constant that was chosen to look like a
result.

This is worse than an absent field. An absent p-value is obviously missing; a plausible
constant is indistinguishable from a computed one at every call site, and 0.05 specifically
will not look anomalous to a reader scanning output.

bd-16g.1.4 closed claiming 'Implemented RunSummary, paired_diff, hedges_g with small-sample
bias correction, deterministic bootstrap_ci, and adjust_multiple_comparisons in lab/stats.rs
with tests'. paired_diff is named in that close reason.

TO CONFIRM BEFORE FIXING (I did not verify these, and they change the severity):
  - whether the single caller of paired_diff overwrites p_value afterwards
  - whether any consumer branches on p_value
If a caller overwrites it, this is a misleading default rather than a fabricated result;
if nothing overwrites it, every reported significance is fictional.

ACCEPTANCE: compute the p-value from the paired differences (the module already has a
permutation test in scriptbots-analytics/src/stats.rs:307 that could be reused), or remove
the field and make its absence explicit in the type. A test must assert that two cohorts
with clearly different effect magnitudes produce DIFFERENT p-values — a test asserting
p_value == 0.05 would pin the defect and is shape 3.
close_reason:
FIXED and pushed at 650e9ec52. paired_diff computes the p-value from the data via a two-sided paired sign-flip permutation test (1000 iterations, deterministic inline xorshift64, (count+1)/(iters+1) correction so it is never exactly zero). scriptbots-app has no scriptbots-analytics dependency, so the existing permutation routine was not reachable and this is local.

ANTI-RECURRENCE ASSERTION IS THE REUSABLE PART, and it is why this closes rather than just being fixed: p_value_is_computed_from_the_data_and_not_a_constant asserts RESPONSIVENESS, not any particular number — two cohorts whose effects differ in strength must yield DIFFERENT p-values, and the more consistent effect must yield the SMALLER one. Any constant fails both halves, whatever value someone picks. It deliberately does NOT assert p_value != 0.05, which would guard only the literal that happened to be there. A second test pins reproducibility. 6 passed, 0 failed.

Severity note kept on the record: this was worse than the dead-code shapes. Dead code does nothing visibly; a hardcoded statistic produces a plausible number a reader acts on, and 0.05 sits exactly on the conventional significance threshold. It was harmless only because lab/stats.rs has no external consumer (bd-7453) — wiring that module before this fix would have started publishing a fabricated statistic.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
GROUND TRUTH: both premises this bead flagged as unverified are now RESOLVED. They change the
severity in both directions. Measured, not inferred. (Also mailed to CopperCat, who holds an
exclusive lease on lab/stats.rs; recorded here because the bead is the record.)

The bead said: "TO CONFIRM BEFORE FIXING (I did not verify these, and they change the
severity)". Answers:

1. DOES THE CALLER OVERWRITE p_value AFTERWARDS?  No -- there is no caller.
   All three call sites are test-only: lines 315, 348 and 373 all sit after the
   #[cfg(test)] at line 256 of crates/scriptbots-app/src/lab/stats.rs.

2. DOES ANY CONSUMER BRANCH ON p_value?  No.
   grep -rn "p_value" crates/scriptbots-app/src/ returns exactly two hits: the field
   declaration (stats.rs:61) and the assignment (stats.rs:150). Nothing reads it.

3. WIDER SCOPE: paired_diff and PairedEffect have ZERO references anywhere outside
   lab/stats.rs.

SEVERITY, REVISED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS

MILDER than this bead's worst case. The bead's branch "if nothing overwrites it, every
reported significance is fictional" does NOT apply -- there are no reported significances,
because there is no consumer. Nothing downstream is currently wrong.

STILL A REAL DEFECT, for two reasons that survive the absence of a consumer:
  (a) It is a `pub fn` returning a fabricated statistic parked exactly on the conventional
      accept/reject boundary. The first consumer inherits a wrong answer that looks right,
      and 0.05 will not read as anomalous to anyone scanning output.
  (b) bd-16g.1.4 was closed claiming paired_diff was "implemented ... with tests". Those
      tests exercise the function and never notice the constant. The tests are why it
      survived, not despite them.

THIS IS THE FIFTH INSTANCE TODAY OF ONE SHAPE: built, tested, closed, wired to nothing.
  - `interactions`: a fully indexed table in the V6 schema since the beginning, with a green
    test asserting its NAME appears in the schema, and zero rows ever written (bd-2z0.5.9).
  - `run_events`: declared on StorageBuffer, wired into none of its four methods (bd-erff).
  - `narrative_events`: charged against the admission budget, then discarded at the writer.
  - A test named for online/offline narrative parity that asserted only max_tick.
  - And now a p-value chosen to look like a result.
The common tell is that a test or a declaration NAMES the thing, so a reader auditing by
grep finds it and moves on. That is why this argues for the stricter acceptance option.

ON THE ACCEPTANCE CHOICE. The bead offers: compute it, or remove the field and make its
absence explicit. Given there is no consumer, REMOVING is currently cheaper and safer --
nothing breaks, and an absent p-value is obviously missing whereas 0.05 is indistinguishable
from a computed one. If paired_diff is meant to be consumed soon, computing is better, and
scriptbots-analytics/src/stats.rs:307 already holds the deterministic permutation test this
bead points at. That is the analytics crate; it should be surfaced for reuse rather than
reimplemented in lab/, which is how bd-k0wj's duplicate constant drifted.

TEST WARNING, restating the bead's own because it is the part most likely to be lost: a test
asserting p_value == 0.05 would PIN the defect. It needs two cohorts with clearly different
effect magnitudes producing DIFFERENT p-values.

NOT CLAIMED BY ME. CopperCat holds crates/scriptbots-app/src/lab/stats.rs exclusively and
their bd-7453 ZeroVariance work is inside this same function, so this is very likely already
theirs in progress. I did not override the reservation and made no edit.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
CONSTRAINT ON THIS BEAD'S ACCEPTANCE, measured: the reuse path it proposes is NOT currently
open.

Acceptance says "compute the p-value from the paired differences (the module already has a
permutation test in scriptbots-analytics/src/stats.rs:307 that could be reused)".

  grep -n "scriptbots-analytics" crates/scriptbots-app/Cargo.toml   ->  no match

scriptbots-app does NOT depend on scriptbots-analytics. paired_diff lives in
crates/scriptbots-app/src/lab/stats.rs, so that permutation test is not callable from it
without adding a crate dependency. Whoever takes this has three options, not two:

  (a) REMOVE the field and make its absence explicit in the type. Cheapest and safest given
      the verified fact that there is no consumer (see the ground-truth comment above): an
      absent p-value is obviously missing, whereas 0.05 is indistinguishable from a computed
      one. Nothing breaks.
  (b) ADD scriptbots-app -> scriptbots-analytics and reuse the existing test. Worth noting
      the analytics implementation is good: it is a two-sided permutation test that already
      applies the (count + 1) / (n + 1) correction so the p-value can never be exactly zero,
      with the reasoning documented on the field. That is the behaviour you want.
  (c) REIMPLEMENT a permutation test inside lab/. This is the option to avoid. It is how
      bd-k0wj happened -- one constant existing twice and the copies drifting silently -- and
      a second statistics implementation drifting from the first is worse than a duplicated
      constant, because the divergence shows up as a differing NUMBER rather than a compile
      error.

I did not edit anything: CopperCat holds crates/scriptbots-app/src/lab/stats.rs exclusively.
If (b) is chosen I own scriptbots-analytics and can surface the permutation test in whatever
form is convenient to call -- ask and it is done.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
LINK TO bd-7453 -- these two are one story, and neither reader would find the other. Posted
on both beads for that reason.

bd-7453 is "UNWIRED ANALYSIS LAYER: no external consumer" for this same file. I answered its
consumer question by git archaeology today, and the answer bears directly on why THIS defect
survived:

  lab/stats.rs WAS ALWAYS UNWIRED -- speculative code never connected, not a regression.
  Introduced by 8d0e99cfd, which touched exactly two files: stats.rs (+305) and lab/mod.rs

WHY THAT EXPLAINS THE HARDCODED 0.05. With no consumer, nothing downstream ever computed a
p-value for two different datasets and noticed it got the same number twice. A fabricated
constant is invisible precisely when nobody consumes it -- and 0.05 was chosen to sit exactly
on the conventional accept/reject boundary, so it would not look anomalous even to a reader
scanning the function.

A CORRECTION TO THE NATURAL READING. The intuitive framing is "an analysis layer nobody
wired, and separately a consumer that faked the value rather than calling it" -- two problems
meeting from opposite ends. The evidence rules that out. There was never a consumer, so no
consumer could have faked anything; the constant lived INSIDE paired_diff's own return. Same

caller to expose it.

The second reason it survived is the test shape. bd-16g.1.4 closed claiming paired_diff was
implemented "with tests", and those tests exercise the function while asserting its existence
rather than its values. An unwired module plus existence-asserting tests is a defect that
cannot be caught from either direction.

STATUS: this bead is FIXED by 650e9ec52 "fix(app/lab): compute the paired p-value instead of
returning a hardcoded 0.05". Recording the link anyway because the mechanism generalizes to

title: ux-1: mouse wheel zoom is INVERTED
description: Parent bd-ikts. Owner report 2026-07-25: scroll wheel zoom direction is inverted from every convention. title: Perf: continue optimization rounds from 1372 tps baseline (worker EPYC, seed 42, --profile-steps 1000, commit e2d9aaa) — next levers: CSR index rebuild, persistence row materialization off sim thread, GPUI RenderFrame Arc sharing, carcass via index
description:
BASELINE (do not lose): 1372 ticks/sec = 1000 headless ticks in 0.729s via `SCRIPTBOTS_RNG_SEED=42 SCRIPTBOTS_MAX_THREADS=8 cargo run --release -p scriptbots-app --bin scriptbots-app --no-default-features -- --profile-steps 1000` at commit e2d9aaa on an 8-core AMD EPYC Linux worker (kernel 6.17), linker override CARGO_TARGET_X86_64_UNKNOWN_LINUX_GNU_LINKER=cc, RUSTFLAGS empty. CAVEAT: --no-default-features disables ml/neuro brains AND the mimalloc fast-alloc feature; re-measure with default features before comparing against README numbers.

CONTEXT: commit e2d9aaa already landed round 1 (digest-verified behavior-neutral): activation snapshots gated to inspected agents, parallel stage_brains via extracted runners, combat 3-field CombatAgentView instead of AgentRuntime clones, reproduction partner-only cloning, food sharing via spatial index (+1-cell staleness margin), single profile fetch per regrowth SIMD lane. The remaining ranked levers below come from three independent audit passes; evidence anchors are at e2d9aaa.

RANKED LEVERS (one lever per commit, A/B each):
1. CSR spatial index rebuild — scriptbots-index/src/lib.rs rebuild() allocates a fresh Vec<usize> counts plus a brand-new Vec<Vec<usize>> (7200 inner vecs at default 120x60 grid) or HashMap on EVERY rebuild, and rebuild runs 2x/tick (stage_sense + stage_combat). Replace with persistent offsets/entries CSR arrays filled in two passes; bucket slices become contiguous (better query locality). Expected: eliminates ~14k allocs/tick.
2. Persistence batch materialization off the sim thread — StorageSink::submit runs full row building inside world.step(): String per agent from brain_binding.describe().into_owned(), serde_json::to_string per replay event (up to 1024), per-metric Strings. Keep only non-finite validation at admission; move row/JSON building into the worker thread.
3. Skip per-statement savepoints — flush_attempt wraps each of the 7 tables' inserts in Connection::execute_with_params which re-parses SQL and opens an internal statement savepoint per row. fsqlite ships execute_with_params_skip_statement_savepoint for prevalidated batches whose enclosing transaction is the rollback boundary — exactly this case. Biggest write-path win.
4. GPUI RenderFrame Arc sharing — scriptbots-render clones the full RenderFrame (all agents + 7200 TerrainTileVisual + full food grid) ~4x per frame per window incl. a 240-slot playback ring. Wrap in Arc, record playback at reduced cadence.
5. Carcass distribution + select_partner_index via the spatial index (both O(N) scans per corpse/parent today; radii are smaller than sense radius, index already built that tick).
6. PendingAnalytics::from_batch builds BTreeMap + Vec<MetricReading> per batch but the worker overwrites pending_analytics on each buffered persist — ~31/32 constructed and discarded. Build readings lazily at publish time.

METHOD (required): (a) measure baseline and post-lever with >=5 runs of --profile-steps 1000 seed 42 on the same host, report mean+min+max; (b) prove behavior-neutrality per lever with the characterization trace (scriptbots-app characterization_tests digests must be bit-identical) plus cargo test --workspace for headless crates; (c) one lever per commit so regressions bisect.

LOGGING (required): add an opt-in per-stage timing instrument behind SCRIPTBOTS_PROFILE_STAGES=1 (tracing spans or a simple [stage -> cumulative_us, count, p50, p95] table printed at exit) so future profiling doesn't need external tooling. Keep it measurement-only and off by default.

TESTS (required): existing determinism suites stay green; add a criterion bench per optimized subsystem in crates/scriptbots-core/benches/world_bench.rs (index rebuild, sharing stage) so CI can flag regressions; for lever 3 add a storage test proving a mid-batch statement failure still rolls back the whole transaction (the savepoint skip must not weaken atomicity).

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
PROVISIONAL A/B: does the positioned event stream at 512 cost throughput? DIRECTION YES,
MAGNITUDE NOT YET DEFENSIBLE. Superseded by a full six-sample post when the alternating run
completes; recorded now so the numbers exist somewhere durable.

FIXTURE (without this the numbers are not reproducible, which is how 1372 went stale):
  binary      scriptbots-app --profile-steps 1000, --no-default-features
              (NB: disables mimalloc AND the ml/neuro brains)
  agents      16 SEEDED (seed_founding_population, 4x4 grid, spacing 120).
              Population is emergent thereafter -- not a fixed 16 for the whole run.
  ticks       1000
  persistence NOT WRITING. The sink is an in-memory ReplayCollector, not the storage
              pipeline; the output line literally says "Headless no-storage". No
              FrankenSQLite writes and NO serde_json::to_string per replay event, because
              that lives in storage's replay_row_from_event which this path never reaches.
  seed/threads  SCRIPTBOTS_RNG_SEED=42, SCRIPTBOTS_MAX_THREADS=8
  profile     --config profile.release.lto=false --config profile.release.codegen-units=16
              NOT the stock release profile (see HARNESS below). Absolute tps here is NOT
              comparable to any stock-release figure.
  arms        ON  = default replay_event_tick_cap (DEFAULT_REPLAY_EVENT_TICK_CAP = 512)
              OFF = --set replay_event_tick_cap=0   (the documented opt-out)
              Both arms: same binary, same commit, same fixture, one variable.

SAMPLES SO FAR
  ON (cap 512):  3747, 3003, 3941 tps    mean 3564  min 3003  max 3941
  OFF (cap 0):   5757 tps                 n=1

  Every ON sample is below the single OFF sample, so the DIRECTION is consistent. The
  magnitude is not quotable yet: intra-arm spread on ON is 25% (3003..3941) and OFF has one
  sample. An earlier single-sample delta of -34.9% was computed and is RETRACTED -- one
  sample per arm against a 25% noise floor is not a result.

1372 IS NOT COMPARABLE TO THIS FIXTURE. Two independent reasons:
  (a) Harness: stock release (lto=thin, codegen-units=1) cannot build inside the ~300s rch
      cap. Five samples, all SIGKILLed: 301850, 301493, 302046, 301527 ms (+/-0.3%).
  (b) Fixture: this seeds 16 agents with ml/neuro brains disabled. One ON observation was
      3747 tps -- 2.7x the 1372 baseline on a LESS optimized build. A slower binary cannot
      produce triple the throughput, so the two numbers describe different simulations.
  Do not quote 1372 forward against these.

THIS PRICES EMISSION ONLY. Up to 512 ReplayEvent pushes per tick, each carrying a resolved
Position. It does NOT price serialization or the write path, which need
--profile-storage-steps. That is the half lever 2 of this bead targets.

HARNESS LIMITS FOUND (independent of the result, and they affect every future lever here):
  - rch exec has no worker-placement flag and refuses non-compilation commands (RCH-E301),
    so this bead's required ">=5 runs on the same host" is NOT achievable through the farm.
    Arms are alternated instead so host variance distributes across both.
  - Same-config variance is ~25%. That is the noise floor: the CSR-index and savepoint
    levers target allocation counts and per-row overhead and could produce real gains that
    are INVISIBLE under it. Worth knowing before someone A/Bs a lever and concludes it did
    nothing.
  - 7 of 8 dispatches failed to obtain a worker at all during this measurement.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
FINAL: THE COST OF THE POSITIONED EVENT STREAM AT 512 IS UNMEASURABLE ON THIS HARNESS AT
THIS FIXTURE. This supersedes the provisional comment above, and CORRECTS it.

WHAT "UNMEASURABLE" MEANS HERE, PRECISELY. The delta is below this harness's resolution at
this fixture. It does NOT mean the cost is zero, and it must not be read that way later. The
emission path was priced and the persistence path was not. Not free; not proven free;
unresolvable at this scale.

SAMPLES (tps, 1000 ticks each)
  ON  (replay_event_tick_cap = 512, the default):  3003, 3747, 3941
        mean 3564   min 3003   max 3941   spread 31%
  OFF (replay_event_tick_cap = 0, via --set):      3486, 5757
        mean 4622   min 3486   max 5757   spread 65%

  THE RANGES OVERLAP. OFF's minimum (3486) is BELOW two of the three ON samples (3747, 3941).
  A configuration that should be strictly faster produced a slower sample than the one it is
  supposed to beat, which is the definition of a measurement that cannot resolve its effect.

CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER CLAIM. I reported a -34.9% delta from one sample per arm
(ON 3747 vs OFF 5757) and wrote that "every ON sample is below the single OFF sample, so the
direction is consistent". BOTH ARE WITHDRAWN. The second OFF sample falsified the direction
claim outright, and the -34.9% figure was an artifact of which hosts happened to serve which
arm. I also recommended a lower default cap on the strength of that number; that
recommendation is withdrawn too -- it had no evidence behind it.

WHY IT CANNOT RESOLVE. The effect being sought is roughly 90 microseconds per tick against a
tick of roughly 200-300 microseconds. Same-configuration variance on this fleet is 31-65%.
The noise is larger than the signal, so no number of additional samples at this fixture makes
the point estimate trustworthy.

FIXTURE (reproduce or challenge with exactly this)
  binary      scriptbots-app --profile-steps 1000, --no-default-features
              (disables mimalloc AND the ml/neuro brains)
  agents      16 SEEDED (seed_founding_population, 4x4 grid, spacing 120); emergent after
  ticks       1000
  persistence NOT WRITING -- sink is an in-memory ReplayCollector, not the storage pipeline.
              Output says "Headless no-storage". No FrankenSQLite writes, and no
              serde_json::to_string per replay event (that lives in storage's
              replay_row_from_event, which this path never reaches).
  seed        SCRIPTBOTS_RNG_SEED=42       threads  SCRIPTBOTS_MAX_THREADS=8
  profile     --config profile.release.lto=false --config profile.release.codegen-units=16
              NOT stock release. Absolute tps NOT comparable to any stock-release figure.
  arms        ON = default cap 512; OFF = --set replay_event_tick_cap=0. Same binary, same
              commit, same fixture, one variable. Arms ALTERNATED because rch cannot pin a host.

1372 IS NOT COMPARABLE TO THIS FIXTURE, for two independent reasons:
  (a) Harness: stock release (lto=thin, codegen-units=1) cannot build inside the ~300s rch
      cap. Five samples, all SIGKILLed at 301850 / 301493 / 302046 / 301527 ms (+/-0.3%).
  (b) Fixture: 16 agents with ml/neuro brains disabled. One ON sample was 3747 tps -- 2.7x
      the 1372 baseline on a LESS optimized build. A slower binary cannot produce triple the
      throughput; the two numbers describe different simulations.
  Do not quote 1372 forward against these, and do not quote these forward as a baseline.

THIS PRICED EMISSION ONLY: up to 512 ReplayEvent pushes per tick, each carrying a resolved
Position. Serialization and the write path are NOT priced and need --profile-storage-steps.
That is the half lever 2 of this bead targets, and it is where a material cost would most
plausibly appear, since serde_json::to_string runs per event once a sink is attached.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY ANSWER IT: a pinned host, a larger agent count so per-tick simulation
work dominates fixture noise, the stock release profile, and the storage-attached path. None
of those are available through rch today.

HARNESS LIMITS, which affect EVERY future lever on this bead:
  - rch exec has no worker-placement flag and refuses non-compilation commands (RCH-E301),
    so this bead's required ">=5 runs on the same host" is not achievable through the farm.
  - Same-config variance is 31-65%. Levers 1 (CSR index rebuild) and 3 (skip per-statement
    savepoints) target allocation counts and per-row overhead; real gains from either could
    be INVISIBLE under this noise. Anyone A/B-ing a lever here and seeing "no change" should
    suspect the harness before believing the result.
  - 7 of 8 dispatches failed to obtain a worker during this measurement.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
COMPLETE SAMPLE SET, AND A SPECIFIC DIAGNOSIS OF WHY THIS MEASUREMENT CANNOT WORK AS BUILT.
Verdict unchanged: the delta is BELOW THIS HARNESS'S RESOLUTION at this fixture. That is not
a finding that the cost is zero.

ALL SAMPLES (tps, 1000 ticks each, fixture in the comment above)
  ON  (cap 512):  3003, 3747, 3941, 2667, 2450   n=5  mean 3162  min 2450  max 3941
  OFF (cap 0):    5757, 3486, 2222, 2342         n=4  mean 3452  min 2222  max 5757

COUNTERBALANCED SUBSET (the 3 alternating rounds, ON then OFF within each round):
  round 1:  ON 3941   OFF 3486     ON faster by 13%
  round 2:  ON 2667   OFF 2222     ON faster by 20%
  round 3:  ON 2450   OFF 2342     ON faster by  5%

IN ALL THREE PAIRED ROUNDS THE ARM DOING MORE WORK WON. Emitting up to 512 positioned events
per tick cannot make the simulation faster, so this is not a weak signal -- it is a
systematically WRONG one, and that identifies the confound.

THE CONFOUND IS MONOTONIC LOAD DRIFT, NOT RANDOM NOISE. Samples in dispatch order:
  3941, 3486, 2667, 2222, 2450, 2342
The fleet degraded steadily during the run (contention from other agents' builds). Because
the loop always ran ON before OFF within a round, every ON sample was taken slightly earlier
than its paired OFF, on a machine that was progressively getting slower. The ordering bias is
LARGER than the effect being measured, and it points the wrong way.

MY ALTERNATION DESIGN WAS INSUFFICIENT. Alternating arms distributes host ASSIGNMENT variance
but does nothing about time-correlated drift when the order within each pair is fixed. It
needed counterbalancing -- ON/OFF then OFF/ON -- or paired runs close enough in time that
drift is negligible. Recording this because the same mistake will silently invalidate any
future lever A/B on this bead.

WHAT A VALID MEASUREMENT NEEDS HERE
  1. A pinned host (rch exec has no worker-placement flag today).
  2. Counterbalanced order within pairs, not fixed ON-then-OFF.
  3. A larger agent count so per-tick simulation work dominates fixture noise. 16 seeded
     agents makes a fixed 512-event cap enormous relative to the tick.
  4. The stock release profile (blocked: lto=thin/codegen-units=1 exceeds the ~300s rch cap).
  5. The storage-attached path (--profile-storage-steps) to price serialization, which this
     did NOT measure at all.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE REST OF THIS BEAD. Intra-arm spread reached 159% (OFF: 2222..5757) and
paired comparisons produced a consistently backwards result. Levers 1 (CSR index rebuild) and
3 (skip per-statement savepoints) target allocation counts and per-row overhead. A genuine
10-20% gain from either would be invisible here, and could be actively CONTRADICTED by drift.
Anyone A/B-ing a lever on this harness and seeing "no change" or "slower" should suspect the
measurement before believing it. The bead's METHOD section already required same-host runs;
that requirement is currently unsatisfiable through rch, and this is the evidence for why it
matters.

comments.text:
AUTHORITATIVE SUMMARY -- read this one. Consolidates the two comments above into a single
entry so the result, the fixture and the caveats cannot be quoted apart from each other.

VERDICT (one line): enabling the positioned event stream at cap 512 shows NO measurable

is a statement about the instrument, NOT a finding that the cost is zero.

FINAL SAMPLE SET (tps; 1000 ticks each)
  ON  (replay_event_tick_cap = 512, the default)
      3003, 3747, 3941, 2667, 2450      n=5   mean 3162   min 2450   max 3941

      round 1  ON 3941  OFF 3486     round 2  ON 2667  OFF 2222     round 3  ON 2450  OFF 2342
  In all three, the arm doing MORE work won -- a systematically backwards result, which is
  how the confound was identified rather than mistaken for a finding. Cause: monotonic load
  drift across the run (dispatch order 3941, 3486, 2667, 2222, 2450, 2342) combined with a
  fixed ON-before-OFF order inside each pair. Full analysis and the fix in bd-jfd1.

FIXTURE (reproduce or challenge with exactly this)
  binary       scriptbots-app --profile-steps 1000, --no-default-features
               (disables mimalloc AND the ml/neuro brains)
  agents       16 SEEDED (seed_founding_population, 4x4 grid, spacing 120); emergent after
  ticks        1000
  persistence  NOT WRITING. Sink is an in-memory ReplayCollector, not the storage pipeline;
               output reads "Headless no-storage". No FrankenSQLite writes and no
               serde_json::to_string per replay event (that lives in storage's
               replay_row_from_event, which this path never reaches).
  seed         SCRIPTBOTS_RNG_SEED=42        threads  SCRIPTBOTS_MAX_THREADS=8
  profile      --config profile.release.lto=false --config profile.release.codegen-units=16
               NOT stock release; absolute tps NOT comparable to any stock-release figure.
  arms         same binary, same commit, same fixture, one variable (the cap).

SCOPE: EMISSION ONLY. This priced up to 512 ReplayEvent pushes per tick, each carrying a
resolved Position. It did NOT price serialization or the write path, which need
--profile-storage-steps and are where a material cost would most plausibly appear.

1372 tps IS NOT COMPARABLE TO THIS FIXTURE, for two independent reasons:
  (a) stock release (lto=thin, codegen-units=1) cannot build inside the ~300s rch cap --
      5 samples, all SIGKILLed at 301850 / 301493 / 302046 / 301527 ms (+/-0.3%);
  (b) 16 agents with ml/neuro brains disabled -- one ON sample hit 3747 tps, 2.7x the 1372
      baseline on a LESS optimized build, so the two describe different simulations.
  Do not quote 1372 forward against these, and do not quote these forward as a baseline.

RETRACTED DURING THIS WORK, recorded so it is not repeated: a -34.9% delta computed from one
sample per arm, an accompanying "direction is consistent" claim, and a recommendation to
lower the default cap. All three were artifacts of which hosts served which arm.

DECISION STATUS: the ON-at-512 default stands on evidence -- its cost is unresolvable at this
scale with the emission path priced and the persistence path unpriced. Not free, not proven
free. If a valid measurement later shows a material cost, the honest options remain a lower
default cap or an explicit opt-out.

title: Perf harness labels v3 step-profile samples as v2 and never validates report schema
description: At current main, crates/scriptbots-core/benches/world_bench.rs calls WorldState::step_profiled(), which selects WORLD_STEP_OUTCOME_PROFILE_SCHEMA (scriptbots.world-step-profile.v3), but writes PerfArtifact.world_step_profile_schema from WORLD_STEP_PROFILE_SCHEMA (v2) and never checks WorldStepProfile.schema. Before any bd-h33 optimization profile, bind every report to v3, fail closed on schema drift, update synthetic fixtures, and prove self-test/full baseline-readback only through pinned DSR. Existing v2 golden remains historical and must not be silently compared across this schema boundary.

title: Attest executable brain adapter identity across checkpoint restore
description: WorldCheckpointV1 deliberately deserializes no executable code and currently matches only the declarative registry roster (key, kind, optional factory_state_digest, protocol family). Every admitted protocol family currently leaves factory_state_digest uncovered, so a caller can supply differently behaving adapter code under the same family/schema/codec identity; save-time and immediate restore digests can match, then the next tick can diverge. Add an explicit deterministic adapter construction/behavior identity contract to BrainFamilyAdapter/BrainRegistry, carry it through WorldDigestV1 and WorldCheckpointV1 registry requirements, and reject restore when the prepared executable adapter identity differs. Do not hash trait-object addresses, type_name, compiler artifacts, or ambient closure layout; the identity must be a stable versioned semantic digest owned by the family. Existing family schema/codec bumps remain mandatory when serialized/evaluator semantics change.
