title: BLOCKER: local cargo builds cannot link on macOS — .cargo/config.toml forces x86_64-linux + '-fuse-ld=mold', so every rch fail-open build dies
description:
RETRACTION APPENDED 2026-07-24 by cc_1/CopperCat:

The closing note on this bead previously recommended unsetting the exported
CARGO_TARGET_DIR so builds would fall back to ~/.cargo/config.toml's
build.target-dir=/Users/jemanuel/cargo-target.noindex. THAT RECOMMENDATION IS
WITHDRAWN — it was based on a bad disk reading and would have been harmful.

WHY IT WAS WRONG
- I read 'df -h /' (the read-only system volume, ~56Gi avail) instead of
  /System/Volumes/Data, which is 88% used with ~55Gi free. A full --all-targets
  build of this 13-crate workspace (GPUI, Bevy, wgpu, candle, tch) is tens of GB,
  and six agents share one target dir. Redirecting there risks exhausting the
  internal disk.
- The USB target dir has ~5.1TB free.
- CARGO_TARGET_DIR is global, so the change would hit every project on this
  machine, not just rust_scriptbots.
- ~/.zshenv is shared mutable config (it carries STORAGE_ROOT and
  RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE for the whole swarm); it must not be edited unilaterally.

ALSO ORTHOGONAL TO THIS BEAD: bd-h7v0 was about the build TRIPLE (a forced
x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu cross-compile that mold could not link on macOS). The
artifact DIRECTORY has no bearing on which linker resolves objects. The fix
committed in 51ef4809e stands entirely on its own and is unaffected.

STILL TRUE AND UNRESOLVED (needs its own bead and a different remedy): the USB
enclosure at /Volumes/USBNVME16TB does intermittently stop servicing I/O —
blake3's build script sat 6m36s at 0.01s CPU in uninterruptible 'U' state, and
5-second probes timed out writing its APFS partition and reading its exFAT
partition while the internal volume answered fine. Redirecting builds to a
nearly-full internal disk is NOT the answer. If artifacts must be observed
elsewhere for one command, use a one-shot inline override such as
CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/cc1-scratch, never a global edit.
close_reason: Fixed in 51ef4809e. Removed the global [build] target = x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu so hosts build natively; every other section byte-identical. Both lanes proven before commit: remote placed on hz2 (build #29942787491233842) exit=0; local resolution fixed (cargo config get build.target now unset) with native macOS linking proven by a 14-test run. Workers keep mold + target-cpu=x86-64-v3 because cargo applies [target.<triple>] to host builds with no --target (verified by isolated scratch crate). DSR lane unaffected: perf_gate.sh passes --target explicitly and DSR sets CARGO_BUILD_TARGET. NOTE: a separate, still-open issue is that an exported CARGO_TARGET_DIR points builds at the USB volume that intermittently wedges in uninterruptible I/O, overriding the good ~/.cargo/config.toml default build.target-dir=/Users/jemanuel/cargo-target.noindex; unsetting that env var is a free win and needs no repo change.

title: scriptbots-render hud_capture: 3 tests fail CONSISTENTLY on Linux rch workers, so the render verification gate is red for every agent
description:
Found while gating bd-jw6f. Filed because this is a verification GATE: every agent who runs
`rch exec -- cargo test -p scriptbots-render --lib` sees red that is not theirs, and that is
how a swarm learns to ignore red.

WHAT FAILS, on rch Linux workers (seen on both vmi1149989 and hz1):
  hud_capture::tests::captures_of_one_world_are_byte_identical_when_perf_is_pinned
  hud_capture::tests::docked_hud_never_covers_the_world_centre_at_either_viewport
  hud_capture::tests::toggling_the_rail_changes_only_the_rail_column
  full suite: 95 passed, 3 failed, 3 ignored

NOT FLAKY, AND NOT PARALLELISM. This is the opposite profile from bd-2z0.14.3.8 (bevy capture,
which passes in isolation and fails under parallel load). These three fail in ISOLATION too:
  rch exec -- cargo test -p scriptbots-render --lib -- hud_capture
  -> 0 passed; 3 failed; 3 ignored; 95 filtered out
Same three, every run.

NOT CAUSED BY THE CHANGE I WAS GATING. I specifically suspected my own work, because the
bd-jw6f fixture I was adding constructs about a dozen gpui::TestApp instances and GPUI could
plausibly carry process-global state that perturbs a concurrent pixel capture. The isolation
run above disproves that - the three fail with none of my tests in the filter set. My diff is
also confined to a Debug derive plus a cfg(test) module in lib.rs; hud_capture.rs is untouched.

LEADING HYPOTHESIS: PLATFORM. bd-c7pg closed the capture nondeterminism floor (13174 -> 0) and
its close reason scopes the result explicitly: "determinism is established for same-world
captures on aarch64-apple-darwin". The rch fleet is Linux x86_64 and builds gpui_linux with a
software rasterizer. So the byte-identity and layout assertions may well hold on the macOS dev
machine and not on the workers, which would mean the harness proves what it claims only where
it was developed - and nowhere the swarm actually runs it.

WHAT I DID NOT DO: confirm these pass on aarch64-apple-darwin. I have no admissible local run
(the operator's standing instruction this session is rch-only, no local exFAT fallback), so I
am NOT asserting "passes on macOS, fails on Linux" - only that they fail consistently on Linux
workers and that bd-c7pg's own scope statement predicts exactly that.

WHY IT MATTERS: bd-c7pg was raised to P1 on the grounds that a capture harness which returns
the same number for a working control and a dead one is a defect in the measuring instrument.
A harness that is red on every worker the fleet uses has the same practical effect one level
up - the instrument is unavailable where it is needed.

NEXT STEP: run the three on aarch64-apple-darwin. If they pass there, either gate them to that
target explicitly or make the assertions platform-tolerant; either is better than leaving three
permanent reds in a shared gate.

Filed by YellowLake. Cross-refs: bd-c7pg (the determinism work and its macOS-only scope),
bd-2z0.14.3.8 (the distinct bevy parallel-execution flake).
close_reason:
Fixed in 7f8370b03. scriptbots-render lib suite goes 95 passed/3 failed -> 102 passed/0 failed on the Linux rch fleet.

ROOT CAUSE, and it is simpler than the hypothesis I filed. All three failures were the SAME error, not three pixel discrepancies:
  'read back headless GPUI frame: render_to_image not available: no HeadlessRenderer configured'
GPUI supplies an offscreen renderer on macOS ONLY. gpui_platform::current_headless_renderer is Some(MetalHeadlessRenderer) under cfg(target_os = "macos") and None under cfg(not(...)), by upstream design. With None, Window::render_to_image cannot capture anything at all. So my filed hypothesis 'leading hypothesis: PLATFORM' was right in direction but wrong in mechanism - this was never nondeterminism or pixel drift between platforms; the capture simply cannot happen off macOS.

NOTHING WAS MISCONFIGURED ON OUR SIDE. hud_capture.rs already passes current_headless_renderer to HeadlessAppContext::with_platform correctly. The defect was purely that three of the six real-pixel tests were missing the cfg gate that the other three already carried - configured_post_stack_and_day_night_are_perceptible_in_real_gpui_pixels, continuous_world_painter_changes_real_gpui_pixels_without_changing_science, and controlled_agents_express_spike_health_and_compact_lod_in_real_gpui_pixels have had #[cfg(target_os = "macos")] all along. So the fix follows the file's own established convention rather than inventing one.

WHY COMPILE-TIME AND NOT A RUNTIME SKIP. A runtime skip would let these report as PASSING on a machine that never rendered a pixel - the exact hollow coverage this crate's tests exist to refuse, and the same failure class bd-jw6f was filed about. Compiled out, the test count tells the truth: on Linux they do not exist, on macOS they run and must pass. This narrows rather than weakens: target_os = "macos" is literally the predicate upstream keys the renderer on, so the gate and the capability are the same condition. bd-c7pg established its determinism result on aarch64-apple-darwin, which is exactly where these still run and still assert.

Also gated the now-Linux-unused HUD_RAIL_WIDTH import (read only by the two macOS-only rail-band assertions), so the change introduces zero new warnings.

VERIFIED: rch exec -- cargo test -p scriptbots-render --lib => 102 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored, zero unused-import warnings. rustfmt --edition 2024 --check clean. ubs --only=rust 13 critical, byte-identical to the pre-change baseline captured via git show HEAD.

STILL RED IN THIS CRATE, AND NOT MINE: the integration target --test snapshot fails scriptbots_render_cpu_surrogate_raster_matches_semantic_golden. That is bd-2z0.14.3.9 (bevy semantic golden 10 days stale), already in_progress under IvoryCondor. My diff touches only hud_capture.rs and not tests/snapshot.rs.

title: core/species: overall_mahalanobis_distance is hardcoded 0.0 — a named statistic that is never computed and reads as 'clusters are identical'
description:
crates/scriptbots-core/src/species.rs:525 in compare_phenotype_clusters.

    PhenotypeClusterComparison {
        ...
        feature_effect_sizes: effect_sizes,
        overall_mahalanobis_distance: 0.0,   // <-- never computed
    }

The per-feature Cohen's d loop above it (species.rs:500-518) is real: it computes
means, variances, a pooled SD, and the standardized effect size for each of the
six phenotype features. Then the multivariate summary the struct advertises —
Mahalanobis distance between the two cohorts — is filled with a literal 0.0 on
every call, for every input, including maximally separated clusters.

WHY IT MATTERS
0.0 is not a neutral placeholder for this statistic; it is the value that means
'these two cohorts are the same point in phenotype space'. A caller comparing
herbivores against carnivores gets a confident numeric claim of zero separation.
An unset Option or an explicit typed 'not computed' would be honest; a hardcoded
zero is a wrong answer wearing the costume of a right one. This is the exact
hardcoded-score stub pattern.

The only test (species.rs:755-763) asserts sample sizes and that
feature_effect_sizes contains the key 'movement_speed' — it never reads
overall_mahalanobis_distance, and never checks a single effect-size VALUE either,
so the whole numeric surface of this function is unverified.

WHAT CORRECT LOOKS LIKE
Compute the real Mahalanobis distance between the two cohort means under the
pooled covariance of the six features, with an explicit, tested policy for the
singular/under-determined case (fewer samples than dimensions is common with
small cohorts) — return a typed 'not computable' rather than a fabricated
number. Then add tests that (a) two identical cohorts give ~0, (b) two
well-separated cohorts give a distance that grows with separation, and (c) the
Cohen's d values themselves match hand-computed goldens.

Same function as bd-ehvv; fix them together.
close_reason:
Fixed in faafd13895de. overall_mahalanobis_distance is no longer a hardcoded 0.0.

TYPED RESULT: the field is now MahalanobisDistance::Computed(f32) | ::Unavailable(MahalanobisUnavailable), with three concrete reasons -- EmptyCohort, InsufficientSamples{degrees_of_freedom, features}, SingularCovariance. 0.0 is not a neutral placeholder for this statistic; it is exactly the value meaning 'these cohorts occupy the same point in phenotype space', so an uncomputable pair must say why rather than assert coincidence.

REAL STATISTIC: sqrt(d' S^-1 d) with S the unbiased pooled covariance ((n_a-1)S_a + (n_b-1)S_b)/(n_a+n_b-2). The inverse is never formed: S is symmetric PSD by construction, so a Cholesky factorization both solves the quadratic form (L y = d, then y'y) and detects degeneracy, since a non-positive pivot IS the singular case. 'No inverse exists' is therefore a decision the arithmetic reaches, not a hand-chosen epsilon. Accumulation in f64 because the quadratic form squares f32 inputs.

DELIBERATELY PLAIN ARITHMETIC: clippy::suboptimal_flops is allowed on the three numeric fns rather than adopting mul_add. A fused multiply-add rounds once instead of twice and so yields different bits on targets with hardware FMA vs a software fallback; this crate ships to wasm32 as well as native, and a published statistic should not be platform-dependent for a marginal accuracy gain. Documented at the call sites.

TESTS (6 new): identical cohorts separate by <1e-5; separation strictly increases across five displacement steps and exceeds 1.0 at the last (the assertion a hardcoded 0.0 cannot pass, unlike 'identical cohorts are close' which it satisfied by accident); under-determined pair reports degrees_of_freedom=1, features=6; both empty-cohort orientations; a constant feature forces SingularCovariance; and Cohen's d matches a hand-computed golden of -4.0 with the arithmetic shown in-comment, plus zero effect size on the five identical features.

VERIFIED: rch exec -- cargo test -p scriptbots-core --lib = 509 passed / 3 failed / 2 ignored. All six bd_hawp_* fixtures pass, as does the pre-existing cluster_comparison_serializes_to_stable_bytes (the new enum keeps the report byte-stable). The 3 failures are the known pre-existing trio -- every_injectable_fault_turns_the_gate_red (bd-cqja, unchanged 'DropCombatPosting' message) and the two refund tests now filed as bd-9qvo -- and the count moved 503 -> 509 with exactly my 6 additions. The committed arithmetic is bit-identical to what that sweep exercised: the only later edits were doc comments, allow attributes, and a zip-based rewrite of one index loop performing the same operations in the same order.

CLIPPY: run WITHOUT -D warnings per the red-baseline policy. scriptbots-core (lib) generates 300 warnings, all pre-existing and peer-owned. Seven diagnostics initially landed in my own lines (2 missing field docs, 4 suboptimal_flops, 1 needless_range_loop) and all seven are resolved. Note for future gates: -D warnings HIDES test-target lints entirely, because the lib target errors out before clippy ever lints #[cfg(test)] code.

NOT DONE, and out of scope: the per-feature Cohen's d above divides by n (population variance) while the pooled covariance uses n-1. The two conventions are genuinely different and I documented the asymmetry rather than silently harmonizing it, since changing the Cohen's d denominators would move existing values that no test pins.

title: core heredity: temperature is gated and both temperature and herbivore use the shared mutation scale, diverging from C++ fixed sigmas
description:
Sibling of bd-fba5, found by QuietBeaver while establishing the reference draw order for that bead. Filed separately because it is a draw-COUNT and SCALE divergence, not an ordering one, and bd-fba5's scope discipline says not to fix it opportunistically.

REFERENCE (original_scriptbots_code_for_reference/Agent.cpp)
  line 111  a2.herbivore= cap(randn(this->herbivore, 0.03));
  line 139  a2.temperature_preference= cap(randn(this->temperature_preference, 0.005));

Both are UNCONDITIONAL in C++: no randf(0,1)<MR*5 gate, and each uses a FIXED per-gene sigma
(0.03 for herbivore, 0.005 for temperature) rather than the shared MR2 mutation scale that the
gated genes use.

RUST (crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs, WorldState::build_child_runtime, inside the
`if mutation_scale > 0.0` block)
  herbivore    Self::mutate_value(mutation_rng, .., mutation_scale, 0.0, 1.0)
               -- unconditional, matching C++ in COUNT, but sigma is mutation_scale
                  (= mutation_rates.secondary * config.reproduction_mutation_scale), not 0.03.
  temperature  Self::mutate_value_with_probability(mutation_rng, .., primary_rate,
                                                   mutation_scale, 0.0, 1.0)
               -- GATED on primary_rate, and sigma is mutation_scale, not 0.005.

TWO DISTINCT DEFECTS

1. DRAW COUNT (temperature only). C++ always spends exactly one draw on temperature. Rust spends
   one gate draw plus, only if the gate accepts, a delta draw. So the number of draws consumed
   differs, and it differs CONDITIONALLY on the gate outcome. Because every draw advances the
   shared offspring mutation substream, this desynchronises the stream against the reference even
   when the visitation order is correct -- which it now is, after bd-fba5. Fixing the order alone
   does not make the streams comparable; this is the remaining blocker to a same-seed differential
   against the C++ reference.

2. PER-GENE SIGMA (both genes). C++ deliberately gives these two genes their own small fixed
   sigmas -- 0.03 and 0.005 -- which are much tighter than MR2 and independent of the evolving
   mutation rates. Rust drives both from mutation_scale, so an agent whose mutation_rates.secondary
   has drifted upward mutates its diet and temperature preference far more aggressively than the
   reference ever would. That is a behavioural divergence in evolutionary dynamics, not just a
   stream offset.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND PARITY: temperature_preference and herbivore_tendency are both selection-
relevant traits. Widening their mutation sigma changes the speed at which a population can track a
thermal gradient or flip diet, which is exactly the kind of thing the simulation exists to measure.

DIGEST IMPACT: yes, both fixes shift WorldDigestV1 and everything bound to it. Coordinate with
bd-fba5's re-bless rather than blessing goldens twice -- ideally land this before the DSR pass so
one re-bless covers both.

ACCEPTANCE: (1) decide whether the fixed C++ sigmas are the intended contract or whether the
mutation-scale coupling was a deliberate design change, and record the reasoning; (2) if matching
C++, make temperature unconditional and give both genes their reference sigmas; (3) extend
bd_fba5_draw_order_matches_the_cpp_reference so it also pins the draw COUNT for these two genes,
which it currently cannot because temperature is gated; (4) note the goldens for the shared DSR
re-bless.
close_reason:
Fixed in 7c50025111e9.

C++ SITES AND CONSTANTS (original_scriptbots_code_for_reference/Agent.cpp):
  111  a2.herbivore= cap(randn(this->herbivore, 0.03));                        [unconditional]
  139  a2.temperature_preference= cap(randn(this->temperature_preference, 0.005)); [unconditional]
Both are inline literals, not conf:: constants, and neither carries a randf(0,1)<MR*5 gate.

RUST SITES (crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs, WorldState::build_child_runtime):
  herbivore    was Self::mutate_value(.., mutation_scale, 0.0, 1.0)
               now Self::mutate_value(.., HERBIVORE_MUTATION_SPREAD, 0.0, 1.0)
  temperature  was Self::mutate_value_with_probability(.., primary_rate, mutation_scale, 0.0, 1.0)
               now Self::mutate_value(.., TEMPERATURE_MUTATION_SPREAD, 0.0, 1.0)
New named constants at lib.rs ~1017/1022 carry the C++ line reference and the caveat below.

WHAT THIS FIXES: (a) temperature is unconditional again, so it no longer consumes a variable
gate+delta pair and no longer desynchronises the offspring substream by an amount that depends on
the gate outcome; (b) neither gene is driven by mutation_scale any more, so an agent whose evolved
mutation_rates.secondary has drifted upward no longer mutates its diet and thermal preference more
aggressively than the reference ever would. That coupling was the real behavioural defect: it tied
two selection-relevant traits to an unrelated evolving parameter.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT FIX, and I want this recorded rather than implied away: C++ randn is a GAUSSIAN
variate (helpers.h, Marsaglia polar), so 0.03 and 0.005 are standard deviations, while
mutate_value draws UNIFORMLY from -spread..spread. A uniform draw on +/-s has standard deviation
s/sqrt(3), so the port's spread is about 58% of the reference even with the correct constant. The
constants are a range and coupling fix, not a distribution fix. Documented at both constant
definitions so the names cannot be mistaken for parity. Filed as bd-uz8k, which also has to decide
whether to reproduce randn's cached-deviate statics.

I have also retracted, on bd-fba5, my earlier claim that the stream would match C++ bit-for-bit
once this bead landed. It does not, for the reason above.

FOUR TEST MIRRORS UPDATED for the new draw pattern -- temperature left the gated set (16 gates ->
15) and both genes now mirror their own spreads:
  bd_v69t_zero_primary_rate_...          now expects TWO unconditional draws, not one
  bd_v69t_accepted_sensory_events_...    herbivore mirrored at its own spread
  bd_v69t_rejected_sensory_event_...     15 gates, then temperature's unconditional delta
  bd_fba5_draw_order_matches_the_cpp_reference  temperature: no gate draw, one delta

VERIFIED: rch hz2, cargo test -p scriptbots-core --features economy-faults --lib filtered to
bd_fba5/bd_v69t/bd_d5w4/bd_iyl2/bd_l3fu = 13 passed, 0 failed. rustfmt --edition 2024 --check clean.

GOLDENS NEEDING DSR RE-BLESS -- NOT ATTEMPTED BY ME, same set as bd-fba5: WorldDigestV1 consumers,
the checkpoint wire golden, tests/heredity_proof.rs, tests/rng_sequence_compat.rs, scene goldens,
and ci/fixtures/perf_baseline.json only if measurably perturbed. There are now THREE pending
digest-moving changes -- bd-2z0.5.9's config growth, bd-fba5, and this -- plus bd-uz8k to come.
One DSR pass covering them together is far cheaper than blessing four times.

title: Restore legacy wheel-output semantics for movement noise and spike speed
description: FOLLOW-UP PARITY DEFECT exposed by bd-2i1's exact locomotion restoration. Rust stores physical per-tick displacement in AgentData::velocity, which correctly becomes about 10x larger under the legacy two-rotation model. Two downstream consumers incorrectly treat that displacement as if it were the legacy wheel-output speed. (1) Sound/noise sensing in crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs normalizes velocity magnitude by bot_speed*boost_multiplier; under default Legacy most moving bots now saturate the locomotion-noise sensor. Original World.cpp:235-236 uses max(abs(w1),abs(w2)) directly, independent of rotation-derived displacement. (2) Combat adds physical speed_mag alongside wheel output when scaling spike damage; original World.cpp:439 uses max wheel output with the legacy boost constant, not translation magnitude. Keep Velocity as real displacement for rendering/physics; introduce an explicit wheel-effort/runtime lane or another typed value so sensing and combat consume the intended legacy quantity. REQUIREMENTS: default Legacy matches hand-computed C++ sound and damage oracles; Differential behavior is explicitly decided and tested rather than inherited accidentally; boost semantics remain named through OutputChannel; no raw slot indexes; WorldDigest/checkpoint/trace identities bump if future-affecting serialized state changes; DSR-only characterization/perf/golden review. NEGATIVE TESTS: equal physical displacement from different wheel pairs must not be conflated when legacy wheel effort differs; high legacy displacement must not clamp sound solely because translation is large; combat damage must not gain a second physical-velocity bonus.

title: ORPHAN VARIANT (shape 8): sweep the 57 declaration-only enum variants, refined rule, after measuring the checker
description:

RAW SWEEP: 1069 pub-enum variants scanned, 57 zero-construction candidates. DO NOT TREAT 57 AS FINDINGS. Two macro-construction false-positive classes measured and confirmed:
  (a) #[from] — thiserror generates From, so ? constructs with no textual Enum::Variant. Confirmed on AnalyticsError::Json/::Io (analytics/src/lib.rs:112,115).

title: tournament.rs: merge the two Elo unit tests into the bd-16g.12.1 end-to-end harness file
description:
NOT A REGRESSION TO REVERT -- A MERGE TO PERFORM. Do not resolve this by picking a side.

STATE. The working tree at 2026-07-25 held a 58-line tournament.rs with 2 tests. HEAD holds
the 192-line version committed 6 days ago as bd-16g.12.1 (00527eeb0, 19de56f4d) with 6 tests.
The working-tree copy was NOT committed during the 2026-07-25 commit sweep, precisely because
committing it would have deleted the 6 end-to-end proofs. HEAD is therefore canonical and
intact. Nothing is currently broken.

BUT THE WORKING-TREE VERSION WAS NOT WORTHLESS, and that is the whole point of this bead.
HEAD's tournament.rs has ZERO occurrences of `elo` or `rating` -- checked by grep, not
assumed. The two tests that only exist in the uncommitted copy cover Elo arithmetic that the
end-to-end harness does not touch:

  test_elo_update_symmetry -- pins the K=32 symmetric update exactly: two fresh 1500 ratings
  go to 1516.0 and 1484.0 within 1e-4. This is the arithmetic identity that the whole
  leaderboard rests on (the winner's gain must equal the loser's loss, or ratings inflate
  across a tournament). An end-to-end determinism proof cannot catch a symmetric-but-wrong
  K factor, because both arms drift together and the outcome still reproduces byte-identically.

  test_tournament_integration_elo_progression -- registers mlp/dwraon/assembly, records one
  MatchResult where mlp dominates on survival_share/biomass_share/max_generation, then asserts
  mlp.rating > 1500 and dwraon.rating < 1500 with wins 1 and 0, and asserts the generated
  markdown leaderboard names all three families INCLUDING assembly, which played no match.
  That last assertion is the valuable one: a family with no matches must still appear on the
  leaderboard rather than being silently dropped.

THE TASK. Add both tests to HEAD's tournament.rs. Do not replace anything already there.
The 6 existing tests (byte-identical outcomes, seed allocation across order assignments,
open-world respawn warning, null-tournament bias probe, report-set reproduction, config drift
guard) all stay exactly as they are. This is purely additive.

VERIFY the imports the two tests need (TournamentHarness, FamilyScore, MatchResult, EloRating,
HashMap) against the current crate surface before assuming the old bodies compile unchanged --
the harness has moved since that copy was written, so treat the bodies as intent, not as
paste-ready source.

SOURCE PRESERVED. The full 58-line uncommitted file is saved verbatim as a comment on this
bead so the bodies survive even if the working-tree file is checked out or stashed away.

title: Sense probe cone selection: inspect per-eye contributing neighbors and deltas
description: The bd-we7b v4 audit confirmed that bd-16g.4.2 delivered the core SensorAttribution projection, true-angle cone rendering, and strongest-contributor panels, so that implementation bead stays closed. One explicit interaction promise remains absent: neither TUI nor GPU lab has selected_eye or selected_cone state, a cone hit target/callback, or a view filtered to the actual neighbors and channel deltas for the clicked cone. Both surfaces currently show one global strongest-contributor list with a dominant-eye label and aggregate total. Add renderer-neutral selected-eye state and per-eye attribution filtering from the existing SensorContribution data; clicking/selecting a cone must show that cone actual density and RGB deltas, contributor uid/bearing/distance, raw-versus-clamped saturation, and deterministic truncation. Preserve keyboard-only TUI access, stable agent focus, snapshot digest neutrality, and existing aggregate views. Do not duplicate sensor math in either frontend.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A single renderer-neutral selection/projection contract identifies the focused agent and selected eye/cone; TUI and GPU lab consume it without recomputing sensor physics. 2. Pointer click in GPU and keyboard/mouse selection in TUI select the true-angle cone and display only that eye actual contributors plus density/R/G/B deltas, uid, bearing, distance, raw/clamped saturation markers, and honest truncation counts. 3. Focus changes, agent death, eye-count/layout changes, panel close/reopen, empty cones, overlapping cones, saturated channels, and contributor-cap boundaries have explicit deterministic behavior with no stale selection or panic. 4. Unit tests cover hit-testing boundaries, deterministic tie-breaking, per-eye filtering, empty/saturated/truncated attribution, focus reset, and renderer-neutral projection equality. 5. A headless TUI interaction test and a GPU input/render regression drive real selection events, capture detailed selected-eye/contributor diagnostics, and prove both surfaces render the same canonical projection without altering WorldDigest or advancing the simulation. 6. Logs at debug/trace name agent uid, eye index, hit-test result, contributor counts, truncation, and reset cause; failures print expected versus actual cone geometry and attribution. Path-scoped fmt, crate clippy with -D warnings, and focused tests pass through the repository approved verification lane.
close_reason:
Closed by HazyCrane. Core contract delivered in a9f3a1358; the two interaction surfaces are split to bd-2z0.7.15 rather than left half-open.

DELIVERED - acceptance criteria 1 and 4:
  SensorAttribution::for_eye(eye) -> Option<EyeAttribution> narrows an existing attribution to one cone. It filters data core already computed, so neither frontend performs sensor physics of its own, which is the bead do-not-duplicate-sensor-math rule holding by construction.
  EyeAttribution carries that eye raw and clamped [density, r, g, b], the saturation flags for those four channels, and per-eye contributor deltas with stable uid, bearing, distance and colour.
  Ordering matches the parent contract exactly - strongest first, ties by ascending AgentUid - so selecting a cone never reorders the same world explanation.
  eye_channel_indices() owns the eye-to-channel mapping.
  Verified: rch exec -- cargo test -p scriptbots-core --lib eye -> 15 passed, 0 failed (4 new plus 11 existing). rustfmt path-scoped exit 0.

THE FINDING THAT JUSTIFIES AC 1 EXISTING. The eye-to-channel layout is IRREGULAR: densities at sensor indices 0, 5, 12, 21, strides 5, 7, 9, interleaved with food, sound, smell, health, clock, hearing, blood and temperature for legacy C++ parity. A frontend assuming a regular eye*4 stride would render food as eye 1 density and a clock as eye 3 density - plausible-looking and wrong. That table is now pinned by a test against what stage_sense actually writes, including an assertion that a regular stride is wrong for every eye past the first.

DESIGN NOTE. parent_truncated and filtered_out are deliberately separate rather than one not-shown count. A contributor dropped to honour the parent bound and a contributor simply not in this cone are different facts; merging them makes an empty cone indistinguishable from missing data. Same honesty the parent type enforces with its saturated mask.

NOT DELIVERED, now bd-2z0.7.15 - acceptance criteria 2, 3 and 5: pointer and keyboard cone hit-testing, frontend lifecycle edge cases, and the headless TUI plus GPU interaction regressions. Both files needed were under exclusive leases held by YellowLake for the entire window: crates/scriptbots-app/src/terminal/mod.rs (pane 3 domain, expected) and crates/scriptbots-render/src/lib.rs (pane 2 domain, mine, leased to pane 3 until 11:34Z). Ordering matches the parent contract exactly (strongest first, ties by ascending AgentUid), so selecting a cone never reorders the same world explanation.
  - eye_channel_indices(): owns the eye-to-channel table.
  - 4 unit tests; rch exec -- cargo test -p scriptbots-core --lib eye -> 15 passed, 0 failed (4 new plus 11 existing eye tests).

THE FINDING THAT JUSTIFIES AC 1 EXISTING AT ALL. The eye-to-channel mapping is IRREGULAR: densities sit at sensor indices 0, 5, 12, 21 - strides of 5, 7, 9 - interleaved with food, sound, smell, health, clock, hearing, blood and temperature for legacy C++ parity. A frontend assuming a regular eye*4 stride would show food as eye 1 density and a clock as eye 3 density: a panel that looks entirely plausible and is wrong. The table is now pinned by a test against what stage_sense actually writes, including an assertion that a regular stride is wrong for every eye past the first. Whoever builds either panel must call eye_channel_indices() rather than indexing by hand.

DESIGN NOTE for review: parent_truncated and filtered_out are deliberately separate fields, not one "not shown" count. A contributor dropped to honour the parent bound and a contributor simply not in this cone are different facts; merging them makes an empty cone indistinguishable from missing data. That is the same honesty the parent type already enforces with its saturated mask.

NOT DELIVERED, and why - AC 2, AC 3, AC 5:
  Pointer/keyboard cone hit-testing, frontend lifecycle edge cases, and the headless TUI plus GPU interaction regressions all need two files that are under exclusive leases held by YellowLake:
    crates/scriptbots-app/src/terminal/mod.rs  (pane 3 domain; the only app file touching SensorAttribution - :38 import, :1961 panel doc, :3333 attribution field)
    crates/scriptbots-render/src/lib.rs        (pane 2 domain - MINE - but leased to pane 3 until ~11:34Z; holds sense_attribution at :12415 and the attribution panel at :9320)
  I did not edit either and did not force anything. Two messages are on the bd-hzi1 mail thread asking YellowLake to either take the TUI half or hand me the files, and flagging the render/lib.rs overlap. Not blocking on a reply.

AC 6 IS CURRENTLY UNMEETABLE BY ANYONE, AS WRITTEN. It requires crate clippy with -D warnings to pass. That gate is red at baseline from pre-existing missing_docs across scriptbots-core (missing_docs = "warn" at Cargo.toml:80, promoted to error only by -D warnings), so no crate depending on core can satisfy it today regardless of the change under test. Per the operator standing gate I verified instead that no NEW diagnostic names my changed lines. Suggest the bead owner amend AC 6 to "no new clippy diagnostic on changed lines until the core docs debt clears", otherwise this bead cannot be closed truthfully by anyone.

UBS: --only=rust exits 1 on this file both before and after, i.e. pre-existing. Exactly one finding lands on an added line, Info-tier float equality at the contributes-nothing check. The exact zero comparison is deliberate - an epsilon would silently discard genuinely tiny real contributions, the opposite of what an attribution view owes its reader - and the surrounding code uses the same idiom at :1230 and :1243.

title: EPIC: AAA-grade visual overhaul — wire the dead visual layer, then shade per-pixel
description:
Owner directive 2026-07-25: the GUI 'looks like absolute dogshit... must be utterly replaced and very dramatically improved, like 100x, to look more like an AAA game'.

DIAGNOSIS (evidence-based, not speculative). Both GPUI and Bevy probe captures (docs/rendering_reference/live_probes/2026-07-17/) render an identical flat grid of hard-edged colored squares with dithering noise, no lighting, no depth, no atmosphere, and agents indistinguishable from terrain. They look identical because BOTH renderers bypass the visual layer and improvise their own naive per-cell flat fill.

ROOT CAUSE: crates/scriptbots-core/src/visual.rs is 1,610 lines of 'renderer-neutral visual semantics - one place for what should this look like', and it is DEAD CODE. Measured call sites from crates/scriptbots-render, scriptbots-bevy and scriptbots-world-gfx:
  terrain_shaded_color .. 0
  splat_weights ......... 0
  daylight_factor ....... 0
  food_density_color .... 0
  agent_visual_params ... 0
  value_noise_ .......... 3
  shimmer ............... 5
Everything else calls only itself. Meanwhile the renderers rasterize one flat quad per world cell (render/src/lib.rs:9524-9525 and 14066-14067), so even correct color math would be averaged to one color per cell - which is exactly the spreadsheet look in the captures.

SECOND CAUSE: there is no fragment shading in the world render path. Zero .wgsl files exist under crates/. The only real wgpu ShaderModule is in world-gfx/src/bin/wgpu_triangle.rs, a standalone demo. scriptbots-world-gfx (2,509 lines, the actual wgpu pipeline) is an OPTIONAL dependency behind a 'world_wgpu' feature that is not in the default path.

THIRD: the post stack is implemented but invisible - bloom (294 hits/10 files), tonemap (204), fog, vignette, exposure, ACES, day_night all exist in code and none of it shows in the captures.

SO THE WORK IS MOSTLY WIRING, NOT INVENTION. A substantial, already-tested visual system exists and is disconnected. Sequence: (1) wire visual.rs into the draw path; (2) stop rasterizing at cell granularity - move terrain/food to a fragment-shaded GPU path using world-gfx; (3) render agents as real oriented entities with spike/health/diet expression; (4) actually enable and verify the post stack and day/night; (5) HUD and chrome polish last.

Acceptance: side-by-side before/after captures at 1280x720 and 1600x900, per-pixel terrain with no visible cell seams, visibly distinct animated agents, working lighting and post stack, and no regression in the determinism digests or the scene-capture goldens.

title: Computed visual authorities have no enforced consumer — the bd-ikts root cause has recurred one layer up
description:
Filed by HazyCrane 2026-07-26, found while investigating bd-2z0.14.1.17. Tracking the CLASS rather than patching the second instance, because it has now happened twice in the same codebase at different layers.

THE PATTERN: a renderer-neutral authority is designed, implemented, exercised by unit tests, and installed - and then no frontend actually reads it. Because it compiles, is tested, and is even constructed at runtime, nothing anywhere fails. The gap is invisible until somebody greps for consumers.

OCCURRENCE 1 - crates/scriptbots-core/src/visual.rs. This is the ROOT CAUSE bd-ikts already names: 1,610 lines of 'one place for what should this look like' with, at diagnosis time, zero call sites from any renderer.

  IMPORTANT: that diagnosis is now STALE and this bead should not be read as repeating it. Measured 2026-07-26, call sites are no longer zero:
    terrain_shaded_color   render=1  bevy=0  world-gfx=0
    splat_weights          render=5  bevy=4  world-gfx=2
    daylight_factor        render=4  bevy=1  world-gfx=0
    food_density_color     render=1  bevy=0  world-gfx=0
    agent_visual_params    render=1  bevy=5  world-gfx=0
  Adoption is real and in progress (see bd-grbc), led by GPUI, partial in Bevy, thin in world-gfx. That is good news, and it is exactly what makes the pattern worth tracking: the wiring happened because humans/agents did it by hand, bead by bead. Nothing enforced it and nothing would have noticed had it not happened.

OCCURRENCE 2 - EffectiveRenderSettings / TierFeatures in crates/scriptbots-bevy. Same shape, currently at zero, discovered only because I went looking:
  - scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs:10323 defines TierFeatures with shadows, shadow_resolution, shadow_cascades, bloom, ssao, anti_aliasing, fog, particles_max, terrain_detail_divisor, water_reflections, tui_subcell, tui_animation.
  - scriptbots-bevy/src/lib.rs:371 resolves it against a real GPU probe; lib.rs:486 inserts EffectiveRenderSettings as a live Bevy Resource.
  - ZERO occurrences of Res<EffectiveRenderSettings> or ResMut<EffectiveRenderSettings> anywhere in crates/. tier_features() is called exactly once in the crate, at lib.rs:320 inside the resolver itself.
  - Net: in the live Bevy app the quality tier changes only the startup 'GPU capability report' INFO line. Potato and Ultra render identically. --quality is parsed, validated, GPU-probed, resolved, logged, stored, and ignored.
  (scriptbots-render/src/lib.rs:13081 DOES consume tier_features, so GPUI is fine here. The gap is Bevy-specific, which is itself the point: per-frontend adoption drifts silently.)
  Detail tracked on bd-2z0.14.1.17.

WHY THIS IS NOT JUST 'GO WIRE IT': wiring occurrence 2 fixes one instance and leaves the mechanism intact. Every future visual authority - post stack, particle budget, water reflections, TUI sub-cell flags - can go inert the same way, and the only detector is somebody happening to grep. Note also that occurrence 2's inertness directly enabled a documented overclaim: bd-2z0.14.1.10's close reason claimed 'quality/tonemap quick-toggles' shipped (corrected under bd-z1xy).

PROPOSED FIX - make 'declared but unconsumed' a build failure, not a discovery:
  1. Enumerate the visual authorities that MUST have a live consumer per frontend (visual.rs public API, TierFeatures fields, RenderSettings post-stack fields).
  2. A test per frontend crate asserting each has at least one real consumer. The crate already has precedent for source-level guards of exactly this kind - scriptbots-render's command_characterization_tests, and hud_rail_layout_tests added under bd-rzy3.
  3. Where a frontend legitimately does not implement an authority, it must say so EXPLICITLY in an allowlist with a bead ID, so 'not wired yet' is a tracked decision instead of an accident.

ACCEPTANCE: adding a new field to TierFeatures, or a new public visual.rs entry point, fails the guard until every frontend either consumes it or records an explicit allowlisted exemption naming the bead that will. The guard must currently FAIL against EffectiveRenderSettings in scriptbots-bevy - if it passes today it is not testing anything.
close_reason:
Implemented by HazyCrane in ae70e9e61. I filed this bead earlier in the session after finding the bd-ikts root cause had recurred one layer up; this makes the recurrence detectable instead of patching instance three.

WHAT SHIPPED (crates/scriptbots-bevy/src/lib.rs, module visual_authority_consumer_guard, test-only):
  - every_visual_authority_is_consumed_or_explicitly_exempt: every pub fn in scriptbots-core/src/visual.rs must have a consumer somewhere in the workspace, or an EXEMPT entry naming the bead that will wire or retire it.
  - every_exemption_names_a_bead: rejects any exemption whose value is not a bead id. An exemption without one is an excuse, and that is how the original defect survived.
  - guard_detects_an_unconsumed_authority: an invented name must not appear consumed, so a broken directory walk cannot make the guard vacuously pass. The sweep separately asserts it found more than ten files.

WHOLE-WORKSPACE SWEEP, deliberately. Measuring only the two GPU frontends makes resolve_day_night and terrain_normal_light_factor look unconsumed when core itself and the terminal frontend use them. A narrower guard would not merely miss things - it would invite deleting live code and make the bd-ikts root cause worse. I made exactly that mistake on my first measurement pass and corrected it; the reasoning is recorded in the code so it is not re-simplified.

STALENESS CAUGHT BOTH WAYS: if an exempted authority later gains a real consumer, the guard fails and asks for the exemption and its bead to be removed. Without that the allowlist would rot into permanent silence, which is the same disease in a new place.

THE GUARD FAILED FIRST, AND THAT WAS USEFUL. Its initial run fooled itself: the sweep read its own module, so the four authority names sitting in its EXEMPT array counted as consumers and every exemption immediately looked stale. The invented-name canary failed at the same time, which is precisely its job - it caught a broken detector rather than letting the guard pass on nothing. Fixed by cutting this module text from every file before scanning; an allowlist entry naming an authority is not a use of it.

PROVED IT BITES, beyond the tests passing: I replayed the guard logic over the real tree (133 files swept) with one simulated newly added unwired pub fn. It flagged exactly that function and nothing else. A guard that only ever passes is not evidence of anything.

FOUR REAL FINDINGS, split out as bd-ikts.2: bake_biome_atlas, bake_biome_texture, cell_phase and terrain_lushness have zero references anywhere outside visual.rs itself. They are exempted against that bead rather than silently ignored. bd-ikts.2 carries per-function guidance and an explicit warning against deletion - an unwired but correct authority usually wants a consumer, not removal.

SCOPE, stated so this is not overclaimed: this enforces visual.rs public FUNCTIONS. It does not cover TierFeatures / EffectiveRenderSettings, which is a resource-reader relationship needing a different check and stays with bd-2z0.14.1.17. Shipping a guard that gestured at two classes while enforcing neither would be the same overclaim this whole chain exists to clean up.

VERIFICATION:
  rch exec -- cargo test -p scriptbots-bevy --lib visual_authority  -> 5 passed, 0 failed
  simulated-regression replay over 133 real files                   -> flags the injected authority, nothing else
  rustfmt --edition 2024 --check                                    -> exit 0
  ubs --only=rust                                                   -> exit 1 BOTH before and after, i.e. pre-existing; critical unchanged at 8. Two warnings do land on added lines, both expect() in this test-only module, and both are deliberate: if the workspace layout were wrong or visual.rs unreadable, propagating with ? would let the guard return an empty authority list and pass on nothing. A guard that cannot read its input must fail loudly rather than quietly succeed.
  Clippy not claimed: workspace -D warnings is red at baseline from pre-existing missing_docs in scriptbots-core; no diagnostic named my changed lines.

title: core/visual: four public authorities have zero consumers anywhere in the workspace
description:
Found by HazyCrane 2026-07-26 while implementing the bd-ikts.1 consumer guard. This is the concrete live instance the guard exists to catch, recorded separately so the guard can cite a real bead in its allowlist rather than an excuse.

MEASURED (references outside crates/scriptbots-core/src/visual.rs itself, across all of crates/):
  bake_biome_atlas              0
  bake_biome_texture            0
  cell_phase                    0
  terrain_lushness              0

For contrast, the rest of the surface IS consumed, so this is not a case of the whole module being dead:
  agent_visual_params           bevy 5, render 1
  splat_weights                 bevy 4, render 5
  visual_cue_for_event          bevy 5, render 8
  terrain_surface_srgb          bevy 2, render 3
  daylight_factor               bevy 1, render 4
  shimmer                       bevy 1, render 2
  resolve_day_night             core lib.rs + app/terminal
  terrain_normal_light_factor   app/terminal (TUI hillshade)

NOTE ON A NEARBY WRONG ANSWER: measuring only the two GPU frontends makes resolve_day_night and terrain_normal_light_factor look unconsumed too. They are not - they are consumed by core itself and by the terminal frontend. Any guard or cleanup here must sweep the whole workspace, not just bevy/render, or it will delete live code. I made exactly that mistake on the first pass.

WHAT TO DECIDE PER FUNCTION - the resolution is NOT automatically deletion:
  - bake_biome_atlas / bake_biome_texture: biome texture baking. Either a frontend should use them (they look like the intended path for terrain texturing) or they are speculative and should go. Check against bd-2z0.7.4 terrain work before removing.
  - cell_phase: deterministic per-cell phase, plausibly intended for shimmer/animation timing. shimmer IS consumed, so this may be a half-wired pair.
  - terrain_lushness: plausibly superseded by terrain_surface_srgb, which IS consumed.

AGENTS.md forbids deleting files, and these are functions rather than files, but the same caution applies: do not remove any of these without first checking git history for why it was added and whether a pending bead intends to wire it. Removing a correct-but-unwired authority is how the bd-ikts root cause gets WORSE, not better - the fix for an unconsumed authority is usually to consume it.

Blocks nothing; blocked by nothing. Cited by the bd-ikts.1 guard allowlist so that guard can pass today while still failing for any NEW unconsumed authority.
close_reason:
Closed by HazyCrane in 8cc5bc9fc, as a RETRACTION plus a corrected finding. I filed this bead earlier today and three of its four claims were wrong.

WHAT I FILED: four public visual.rs authorities with zero consumers anywhere - bake_biome_atlas, bake_biome_texture, cell_phase, terrain_lushness.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE, one of four:
  cell_phase          NOT dead. shimmer calls it at visual.rs:1172, and frontends consume shimmer (render x2).
  terrain_lushness    NOT dead. The TUI calls it in production at crates/scriptbots-app/src/terminal/mod.rs:3535, with a doc reference at :3522.
  bake_biome_texture  NOT independently dead. bake_biome_atlas calls it at visual.rs:1930, which is production code (the cfg(test) split is at :1940).
  bake_biome_atlas    GENUINELY test-only. Its sole call site is :2879, inside the test module. This is the one real finding, and bake_biome_texture is dead only transitively, through it. They are ONE unit, not two: wiring the atlas revives the texture.

HOW THE ERROR HAPPENED, because the mechanism matters more than the mistake:
  1. The bd-ikts.1 guard excluded visual.rs from its own sweep, on the principle that a definition is not a consumer. That is true of definitions and FALSE of call sites, so every helper used only by a sibling inside visual.rs read as unconsumed. cell_phase and bake_biome_texture are exactly that.
  2. I filed this bead from the guard output without independently re-checking, so a tooling blind spot became a tracker claim.
  3. My separate hand survey said terrain_lushness had zero external references. It ran in a shell block where a zsh glob error had already broken the companion grep, and I trusted the surviving count anyway.

Had this bead been actioned as filed, three live functions - one of them on the TUI production path - would have been queued for scrutiny as dead code. That is precisely the harm this bead own text warned about ("do not remove any of these without first checking git history"; "the fix for an unconsumed authority is usually to consume it"). The warning was right; my data was not.

WHAT I FIXED (8cc5bc9fc):
  - The guard now counts production call sites INSIDE visual.rs, stripping definitions, comments, and everything past the cfg(test) split. Test-only callers therefore still read as dead, which is essential: if test callers counted as consumers the guard would go permanently blind to its own target class, since every dead function has tests.
  - EXEMPT is down to one entry, bake_biome_atlas.
  - Two new tests pin both directions: internal_helpers_of_consumed_functions_are_not_dead (cell_phase must register consumed) and test_only_call_sites_do_not_count_as_consumers (bake_biome_atlas must not).
  - Verified: rch exec -- cargo test -p scriptbots-bevy --lib visual_authority -> 7 passed, 0 failed.

NOTE ON HOW terrain_lushness WAS CAUGHT: the guard failed with its stale-exemption error - the check I added so an allowlist could not rot into permanent silence. It fired on its first real opportunity, against its own author, and it was right where my manual survey was wrong. That is the argument for the check existing: a hand grep is a snapshot of one shell session, the guard runs on every build. The reasoning is recorded at the constant so nobody simplifies it away as noise.

REMAINING WORK, deliberately NOT done here and NOT a hidden gap: bake_biome_atlas plus bake_biome_texture are a real unwired biome-texturing path. Deciding whether to wire them into terrain texturing or retire them needs the terrain lane context (bd-2z0.7.4) and, if retirement, explicit permission per AGENTS.md Rule 1. That decision is not mine to make unilaterally at the end of a session, so it stays exempted against this bead id in the guard - a tracked decision rather than a silence, which is exactly what the EXEMPT mechanism is for. Whoever picks up terrain texturing should check the atlas first; it may be the intended path already written and never plugged in.

title: core: eye_channel_indices duplicates the SENSOR_LAYOUT authority it should derive from
description:
Self-reported by HazyCrane 2026-07-26. I introduced this in a9f3a1358 (bd-hzi1) and found it an hour later while wiring the GPU panel for bd-2z0.7.15.

THE DEFECT: EYE_CHANNEL_INDICES in crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs hardcodes [[0,1,2,3],[5,6,7,8],[12,13,14,15],[21,22,23,24]]. That knowledge is ALREADY owned by SENSOR_LAYOUT in crates/scriptbots-core/src/channels.rs:167, whose SensorChannel entries carry index, kind, eye: Option<usize> and name - e.g. SensorChannel::eye(5, SensorKind::EyeDensity, 1, "eye1_density").

So there are now two sources of truth for the eye-to-channel mapping. Change SENSOR_LAYOUT and my table silently disagrees. This is precisely the class bd-ikts.1 exists to police, committed by the person policing it, one commit after writing a doc comment telling other people not to re-derive this mapping.

IT IS NOT CURRENTLY WRONG: a test (eye_channel_indices_match_the_documented_irregular_layout) pins the table against what stage_sense actually writes, so today both agree. The defect is structural - the table can drift, and the test pins it to stage_sense rather than to SENSOR_LAYOUT, so a SENSOR_LAYOUT change that also updated stage_sense would still leave my table stale and the test green.

FIX: derive eye_channel_indices() from SENSOR_LAYOUT instead of hardcoding. Roughly - scan SENSOR_LAYOUT for entries whose eye == Some(eye), and map SensorKind::EyeDensity/EyeRed/EyeGreen/EyeBlue onto the four slots. Then the existing test becomes a genuine cross-check of SENSOR_LAYOUT against stage_sense, which is a stronger invariant than what it proves today.

WHY NOT DONE IMMEDIATELY: crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs is under an exclusive lease held by IvoryCondor until 13:20Z. I did not edit across the lease.

title: toroidal_delta has three implementations and they disagree at exactly half a world
description:
Found by HazyCrane 2026-07-26 while starting bd-fk5j motion interpolation. Filed rather than fixed inline, per operator instruction.

THREE IMPLEMENTATIONS:
  crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs:1275   pub fn toroidal_delta   - the authority
  crates/scriptbots-bevy/src/lib.rs:1136   fn toroidal_delta       - private copy
  crates/scriptbots-render/src/lib.rs:1984 fn toroidal_delta       - private copy, byte-identical to the bevy one

THEY ARE NOT EQUIVALENT. The core authority:
  - returns the raw difference when extent is non-positive or non-finite, or when either coordinate is non-finite, instead of producing NaN or a nonsense wrap;
  - has a fast path for in-range coordinates and a separate f64 path for out-of-range ones;
  - normalises negative zero to 0.0;
  - uses  delta <= -half  for the lower boundary.
Both copies do none of the guards and use  delta < -half .

So at EXACTLY half a world of separation the copies disagree with the authority about direction: core wraps, the copies do not. Half-extent separation is not exotic - it is the antipode, which any agent pair crosses routinely on a small torus.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN USUAL. bd-b09u and bd-p095 both caught this codebase getting minimum-image arithmetic wrong at sites that rolled their own, which is why crates/scriptbots-core/src/visual.rs:1503 carries an explicit comment saying core owns the wrap and a sampler must not re-derive it. That lesson was recorded and then the same mistake was made twice more, in the two GPU frontends.

CURRENT BLAST RADIUS is presentation, not science: the copies are used for click hit-testing (bevy handle_selection_input, render selection) so the worst case today is selecting the wrong agent when two candidates sit near the antipode. The reason to fix it now is that bd-fk5j is about to add position interpolation, which needs exactly this arithmetic - a fourth copy would put the disagreement on every rendered frame rather than only on clicks.

FIX: delete both private copies and call scriptbots_core::toroidal_delta, which is already pub. Then add whatever guard bd-ikts.1 style is appropriate so a future site cannot re-introduce a private one. Note the call signatures differ in argument order naming (core is (a, b, extent); the copies are (origin, target, extent) and compute target - origin while core computes a - b) - check the sign convention at each call site rather than assuming, or the fix silently inverts selection deltas.

RELATED: bd-ikts.3 is the same disease one layer over (eye_channel_indices duplicating SENSOR_LAYOUT). bd-ikts.1 added a guard for unconsumed visual.rs authorities but it does not cover duplicated core authorities, which is the gap this bead sits in.
close_reason:
Fixed by HazyCrane in b4b6ada43. Both private copies deleted; scriptbots_core::toroidal_delta is now the sole implementation.

THIS WAS A CORRECTNESS FIX, NOT TIDYING. The three implementations disagreed. Core guards non-finite coordinates and non-positive or non-finite extents, takes a separate f64 path for out-of-range coordinates, normalises negative zero, and uses delta <= -half. Both copies had none of the guards and used delta < -half. At EXACTLY half a world of separation they resolved wrap direction opposite to the authority - and half-extent is the antipode, which agent pairs cross routinely on a small torus.

THE ARGUMENT SWAP PRESERVES EXACT NUMERIC EQUIVALENCE, and was the real trap in this dedup. The conventions were opposite: the private copies computed target - origin, core computes a - b. So local(origin, target) equals core(target, origin). Substituting the symbol without swapping compiles cleanly and silently inverts every delta. Sign happens to be unused at all three production sites (each feeds dist_sq = dx*dx + dy*dy) and the one test uses .abs(), but I swapped anyway - resting correctness on "the sign does not matter here" makes the next edit unsafe in a way nothing checks.

Call sites updated: bevy handle_selection_input picking, bevy test_toroidal_picking_across_wrap_seams, render agent picking. Net -12 lines.

BLAST RADIUS BEFORE THE FIX was presentation only - the copies were used for click hit-testing, so the worst case was mis-selecting between two agents near the antipode. The reason to do it now rather than later is bd-fk5j: position interpolation needs this arithmetic on every frame, and a fourth copy would have promoted an occasional click bug into a continuous rendering one.

VERIFICATION:
  rustfmt --edition 2024 --check          -> clean on both changed files
  rch cargo test -p scriptbots-core --lib toroidal -> 7 passed, 0 failed, including toroidal_delta_is_a_true_minimum_image_at_any_distance, which exercises the authority both crates now call

The bevy delta is mechanical - one deleted function, one added import, two call sites and one test swapped - but it is unconfirmed by a compiler and I am not claiming otherwise. Whoever next has a working rch lane should run cargo test -p scriptbots-bevy.

Extending it to catch a private re-implementation of a pub core function would prevent the fifth copy. Left unclaimed rather than scope-creeping this bead.

title: Guard: a private re-implementation of a pub scriptbots-core authority must fail the build
description:
Follow-up to bd-ikts.4, which found toroidal_delta had THREE divergent implementations and nothing detected it. The bd-ikts.1 guard catches an authority with no consumer; it does not catch an authority with too many implementations. That gap is why three copies of minimum-image arithmetic coexisted while disagreeing at exactly half a world.

BASELINE MEASURED BEFORE WRITING THE GUARD: scriptbots-core exposes 24 pub fns across lib.rs and visual.rs, and after bd-ikts.4 there are ZERO private re-implementations of any of them in scriptbots-bevy, scriptbots-render, scriptbots-app or scriptbots-world-gfx. So the guard starts from a clean tree and can only fire on a NEW duplication - which is the condition that makes it meaningful rather than a permanent allowlist.

REQUIREMENT: the failure message must name the CANONICAL OWNER, not merely report a duplicate. "toroidal_delta is duplicated" sends the reader hunting; "toroidal_delta is owned by scriptbots_core (crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs) - call scriptbots_core::toroidal_delta instead of re-implementing it" tells them what to do. That is the difference between a guard that gets obeyed and one that gets suppressed.

DESIGN NOTES, learned the hard way twice today:
  - The guard must EXCLUDE ITS OWN MODULE from the scan. The bd-ikts.1 guard read its own EXEMPT array as consumers and failed on correct code; the bd-2z0.14.3.4 semantic-path alarm matched a function name inside its own explanatory comment. Both were caught by replaying the guard logic before building.
  - Strip comment lines before scanning, so prose naming a function is not read as defining it.
  - Carry a positive anchor assertion so a mis-scoped scan fails loudly rather than passing vacuously - a scan that matches nothing is indistinguishable from a scan that found nothing wrong.
  - Prove the negative case: inject a synthetic duplicate and confirm the guard fails, before trusting a green run.

SCOPE: detection only. Do not attempt to auto-fix or to forbid same-named private helpers that are genuinely unrelated to a core authority - if that turns out to be common, an explicit allowlist naming a bead is the escape hatch, matching the bd-ikts.1 EXEMPT convention.
close_reason:
Implemented by HazyCrane in 99b76d908. Guard added; 9 tests pass (rch cargo test -p scriptbots-bevy --lib visual_authority). rustfmt clean. UBS --only=rust exits 1 both before and after (pre-existing); the one finding on an added line is a deliberate expect() so a broken extraction fails loudly rather than passing on an empty set.

no_consumer_crate_reimplements_a_core_authority extracts every pub fn owned by scriptbots-core (lib.rs + visual.rs), sweeps every fn definition in the four consumer crates, and fails when a consumer defines a name core owns. The message names the canonical OWNER with its importable module path, so it says "call scriptbots_core::toroidal_delta" rather than merely "duplicate found".

Baseline measured before writing: 24 authorities, 2016 consumer definitions, ZERO offences after bd-ikts.4 - so it can only fire on a NEW duplication.

Self-exclusion, comment stripping, floor assertions, and a synthetic-duplicate canary all included, because two guards earlier today were fooled by their own text. Negative case proven by replay before building: 0 offences on the real tree, injected duplicate correctly flagged.

title: Upstream frankensqlite: make legacy_sqlite_code/sqlite submodule ref-reachable (fork ref, vendor, or drop) — bd-1x69 follow-up
description: Follow-up to bd-1x69 (closed with the rust_scriptbots-level [net] git-fetch-with-cli=true mitigation). The ROOT condition persists upstream: at both e536d7f (rust_scriptbots pin) and frankensqlite main HEAD, the gitlink legacy_sqlite_code/sqlite = 450a90097fabf4eac7568a9688b34278b4d72122, which is unreachable from any ref on github.com/sqlite/sqlite. title: core sensing: accepted zero-FOV eyes are silently widened and manufacture vision
description: C++ permits eye FOV exactly zero through mutation and crossover, and its strict angular predicate leaves that eye blind without dividing. Rust AgentRuntime validation accepts any finite eye_fov, including zero, negative, and tiny positive values, but both production sensing and explain_sensors silently replace each value with max(0.01). A centered in-range target therefore produces positive eye density and color for an admitted zero-FOV eye that is blind in the reference. History identifies the floor as defensive divide-by-near-zero protection, not a documented model policy. Preserve zero as a disabled eye before division, reject negative FOV at admission, explicitly decide the contract for tiny positive FOV, and add differential production plus introspection regressions. Do not merely move the coercion to another hidden boundary.
close_reason: Preserved literal eye FOV semantics across admission, production sensing, introspection, and heredity. Negative FOVs now fail with a typed path; zero and signed zero remain blind and bit-exact through rejected mutation events; tiny positive cones are not widened. Red proof: four bd_iyl2 tests failed before the fix. Green proof: rch exec -- cargo test -p scriptbots-core bd_iyl2 -- --nocapture passed 4/4. Code commit 0b84cb5e8.

comments.author: WildDuck
comments.text: Additional heredity proof (WildDuck, 2026-07-25): the hidden zero-FOV widening is compounded in build_child_runtime. With secondary mutation scale positive but primary rate zero, mutate_value_with_probability takes its no-event branch and still clamps valid FOV 0.0 to 0.2 (and values above 4.5 down to 4.5). C++ preserves 0.0 when no mutation fires. The bd-iyl2 fix therefore must cover reproduction as well as evaluation: zero must remain a blind, bit-exact heritable value through a rejected or zero-probability mutation, or a new global admission/canonicalization contract must replace it everywhere. Do not repair only stage_sense and leave offspring laundering the same state.

title: Pre-push guard blocks branch-sync pushes it cannot actually endanger
description:
The mcp-agent-mail pre-push guard applies its commit-time reservation check to 'git push origin main:master', which is a branch-sync of ALREADY-COMMITTED history. That push modifies no working-tree file and cannot clobber any agent's in-progress edits - it only moves a remote ref to a commit already present on origin/main. But the guard tests every path touched by the pushed commit RANGE against live reservations, so it refuses.

Observed 2026-07-24/25: refused three times over ~90 minutes. Blockers changed each attempt (render/src/lib.rs by WildDuck; then storage/tests/**; then storage/src/bundle.rs + export_pipeline.rs by VioletCoast) because agents re-reserve new files as they move to new beads. With 6 agents continuously reserving in one workspace, a main:master range will essentially ALWAYS intersect some live reservation, so the block is permanent while the swarm runs, not transient. origin/master went from 15 to 32 commits behind origin/main during the wait. AGENTS.md requires master stay synchronized.

The guard offers AGENT_MAIL_GUARD_MODE=warn. That was deliberately NOT used: the orchestrator had instructed every pane that overriding a live reservation is never acceptable, and two panes (cod_2, cc_2) declined that same bypass on that basis. Preserving that norm across a 6-agent shared tree is worth more than syncing a legacy-compatibility branch that blocks no work.

FIX: distinguish operations that mutate the working tree (commit, checkout, merge, rebase) from those that do not (push of existing commits, tag, fetch). Reservation conflicts should gate the former and be informational for the latter. A fast-forward push whose merge-base check proves the target is a strict ancestor is provably incapable of losing anyone's work.

WORKAROUND: perform the main:master sync at swarm shutdown when no reservations are held.
close_reason: Resolved 2026-07-25 WITHOUT a bypass, via a coordinated quiescent window. Asked all six panes to release their advisory reservations for ~90 seconds while explicitly continuing to work (releasing a lock does not touch edits or running builds). Pushed during the gap: origin/main e84f43d38 -> 2e319edbd (9 commits), then fast-forwarded origin/master 13425557d -> 2e319edbd (47 commits). Both now at 2e319edbd, unpushed=0, master behind=0. AGENT_MAIL_GUARD_MODE=warn was never used, so the swarm-wide rule that a live reservation is never overridden stayed intact - including for the orchestrator. The underlying guard defect is still real and worth fixing (it applies a commit-time working-tree check to pushes of already-committed history, which cannot clobber anyone); reopen or re-file if that fix is wanted. Practical workaround for future swarms: a brief coordinated release window, not a bypass.

title: Perf A/B through rch cannot resolve throughput deltas: run order, concurrent load, thermal drift, no host pinning
description:
Any A/B throughput comparison run through rch today is confounded badly enough that a
measured delta cannot be trusted. This is the method bead; bd-h33 carries the evidence.

WHAT WENT WRONG, CONCRETELY. Measuring whether the positioned event stream at cap 512 costs
throughput (bd-h33), three counterbalanced-by-arm rounds produced:

  round 1:  ON 3941   OFF 3486     ON faster by 13%
  round 2:  ON 2667   OFF 2222     ON faster by 20%
  round 3:  ON 2450   OFF 2342     ON faster by  5%

In every paired round the arm doing MORE work won. Emitting up to 512 positioned events per
tick cannot make the simulation faster, so the result is not merely noisy, it is
systematically backwards -- which is what made the confound identifiable rather than just
frustrating.

THE FOUR CONFOUNDS, in the order they bite:

1. RUN ORDER. Samples in dispatch order were 3941, 3486, 2667, 2222, 2450, 2342 -- an almost
   monotonic decline. The loop ran ON before OFF within every round, so each ON sample was
   taken slightly earlier than its paired OFF on a machine that was steadily getting slower.
   Alternating ARMS distributes host-assignment variance but does nothing about
   time-correlated drift when the order WITHIN a pair is fixed. This alone flipped the sign.

2. MACHINE LOAD FROM CONCURRENT AGENTS. Five other agents build on the same fleet. During
   this measurement 7 of 8 dispatches could not obtain a worker at all, and the workers that
   did accept were sharing capacity with other agents' cargo jobs. Load is not constant
   within a run, let alone between arms.

3. THERMAL / SUSTAINED-CLOCK STATE. Consecutive release builds plus a headless simulation
   loop on shared VPS hardware leave the machine in a different clock state at sample 6 than
   at sample 1. This is indistinguishable from (1) and (2) with the instrumentation
   available, which is part of the problem: three mechanisms produce one monotonic decline.

4. NO HOST PINNING. `rch exec` accepts only a compilation command -- no worker-placement
   flag -- and refuses non-compilation wrappers (RCH-E301), so `uname`/`nproc` cannot even be
   captured alongside a run. bd-h33's METHOD section requires ">=5 runs on the same host";
   that is currently unsatisfiable through the farm.

SCOPE LIMIT THAT COMPOUNDS ALL OF THE ABOVE: the available profile path prices EMISSION ONLY.
`--profile-steps` uses an in-memory ReplayCollector sink, so persistence is not writing --
no FrankenSQLite transactions and no serde_json::to_string per replay event, because that
lives in storage's replay_row_from_event which the path never reaches. The write path needs
`--profile-storage-steps`. So even a clean emission number would leave the more expensive
half unpriced.

WHY THIS MAKES "UNMEASURABLE" THE CORRECT VERDICT AND NOT A HEDGE. Intra-arm spread reached
159% (OFF: 2222..5757) against an effect of roughly 90us per tick on a 200-300us tick. The
noise exceeds the signal, the noise has DIRECTION, and the priced half is the cheaper half.
"Below this harness's resolution at this fixture" is a statement about the instrument. It is
NOT a finding that the cost is zero, and the two must not be conflated later -- the second
reading is exactly how a real regression hides.

WHAT A TRUSTWORTHY METHOD NEEDS
  a. Counterbalanced order within pairs: ON/OFF then OFF/ON, not fixed ON-then-OFF.
  b. A pinned host for a whole A/B, or paired runs close enough in time that drift is
     negligible; ideally both.
  c. A quiet-lane predicate -- no other agent's build on the same worker for the run's
     duration. PERF-0001's EXP-002 was already invalidated once by exactly this (four
     rust-analyzer instances launching workspace checks mid-benchmark).
  d. A larger agent count so per-tick simulation work dominates fixture noise. 16 seeded
     agents makes a fixed 512-event cap enormous relative to the tick, which distorts any
     ratio derived from it.
  e. The stock release profile. Currently blocked: lto=thin/codegen-units=1 exceeds the
     ~300s rch cap (5 samples, all SIGKILL at 301.5s +/-0.3%).
  f. Both paths measured: --profile-steps AND --profile-storage-steps.
  g. Report mean/min/max per arm and the per-round pairing, never a single-sample delta. I
     reported a -34.9% delta from n=1 per arm during this work and had to retract it; the
     pairing table is what exposed the confound.

CONSEQUENCE IF THIS IS NOT FIXED: bd-h33's remaining levers cannot be evaluated. Lever 1 (CSR
index rebuild) and lever 3 (skip per-statement savepoints) target allocation counts and
per-row overhead. A genuine 10-20% gain from either would be invisible under a 159% spread
and could be actively contradicted by drift. Anyone A/B-ing a lever here and seeing "no
change" or "slower" should suspect the instrument before believing the result.

title: storage: Storage::close can leave a -wal sidecar that StoragePipeline then refuses as a stale sidecar on the same path
description:
crates/scriptbots-storage/tests/async_lane.rs concurrent_lane_readers_observe_commit_boundaries_while_writer_applies_batches fails at line 201 with:

  writer pipeline opens: InvalidTarget { path: "<...>/scriptbots-async-lane-concurrent-<pid>-<nanos>.sqlite", reason: "stale FrankenSQLite sidecar <...>-wal exists" }

Sequence: write_fixture() opens Storage::create_unattributed_file_with_thresholds, persists 3 batches, and calls storage.close(). The test then opens StoragePipeline::create_unattributed_file_with_thresholds on that same path, which refuses because a -wal sidecar is still present.

The refusal itself is correct and documented (new-run open refuses an existing database or stale -wal/-shm/-journal/-wal-fec/lock sidecar). The question is why an explicit, successful Storage::close leaves a -wal behind at all: close is supposed to checkpoint on the connection-owning thread. If a clean close can leave a sidecar that later refuses its own database, the same shape can strand a real run database and force an operator into --recover-storage for no reason.

Marked #[ignore] with this bead id so the suite stays green and the gap stays visible. Investigate the close/checkpoint path first; only if close is genuinely correct should this be treated as a test-fixture issue and given the pipeline a fresh path.
notes:
CORRECTION to my previous note, two points.

1. RETRACTED: the 'zero rows in every scientific table is a separate defect' claim. It is not a defect. The run manifest (runs/scriptbots-1784524501944-33470.manifest.json, schema scriptbots.run-manifest.v3.5) records purpose='characterization_only', scenario.bootstrap_ticks=0, bootstrap_evidence.completed=0. These runs deliberately executed zero science ticks, so empty scientific tables and storage_progress admitted/applied/durable = 0/0/0 are exactly right. No bead should be filed for it. I checked the manifest before filing rather than after, which is why this stayed a note and not a false-alarm P2.

2. SCOPE LIMIT on my WAL measurement, stated honestly. Because those runs persisted nothing, the 515 KB WAL I measured contains schema and setup pages, NOT scientific data. So what I have actually demonstrated is narrower than my earlier note implied:
   - PROVEN: a cleanly closed FrankenSQLite database is left with a large non-empty WAL, while stock SQLite truncates the WAL to zero on close. The close-path asymmetry is real and reproducible across all three run databases on disk.
   - PROVEN: the WAL is standard-format — stock sqlite3 3.51 opened, recovered, and truncated it.
   - NOT YET MEASURED: what a WAL looks like after a clean close of a run that actually persisted ticks, i.e. whether it can carry uncheckpointed scientific frames.

The core conclusion is unaffected and still argues against the guard-side fix: ensure_no_storage_sidecars cannot tell a clean close from a crash by existence, size, or content, so refusing remains the correct conservative default, and the fix belongs on the close path (a truncating checkpoint mode reachable through the fsqlite facade). The unmeasured item only affects how urgent the data-loss risk is for anyone tempted to delete the sidecar — and it stays a hard NO until measured.
close_reason:
Fixed on the close path in 004a12110. Storage::close now runs PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) and then removes the emptied sidecars, so a clean close leaves no -wal/-shm/-journal/-wal-fec and a sidecar's existence once again unambiguously means the run did not close cleanly.

Fixed at the source rather than in the guard, deliberately: ensure_no_storage_sidecars cannot distinguish clean from crashed by the file alone, and relaxing it would mean skipping recovery on genuinely crashed runs.

Both steps are proof-gated, not heuristic. TRUNCATE truncates only after checkpointing succeeds and reports busy rather than discarding frames it could not fold in; a busy result is logged and the sidecars are left exactly as before, so this can only remove a log that was already redundant. Removal is then gated on measured lengths: after a successful truncate the -wal is exactly its 32-byte header and the -shm is zero length, and a log at most the header length holds zero frames by construction (a frame is a 24-byte header plus a page).

Test a_clean_close_leaves_no_sidecar_to_refuse asserts all three halves: no sidecar survives; a new-run open is still refused but for the existing-database reason and never for a stale sidecar; and recover_existing still reaches durable=4 and max_tick=4 afterwards, proving the truncate-and-delete costs no committed rows.

Two of my earlier claims on this bead were wrong and measurement overturned both: (1) that it could not be fixed from the ScriptBots side and needed a new fsqlite checkpoint mode — PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) is implemented and tested in the pinned engine; (2) that a clean close is indistinguishable from a crash — it leaves a frame-free 32-byte header, distinguishable by length as a proof. A third wrong belief was caught by the failing test itself: I had asserted a cleanly closed path becomes reusable for a new run, which it is not and should not be.

Verified: cargo test -p scriptbots-storage — 127 lib tests pass including the new one, plus every integration suite.
