title: Control coverage map: only 3 of 27 HUD shortcuts are proven by state; 18 are never driven by any test
description:
bd-bacf audit output. Not a list of complaints - a coverage map. A control with no state-based test is a control nobody has proven does anything, and this codebase has produced several artifacts today that looked functional and were not.

METHOD. For each of the 27 shortcuts in the README's generated table, search all five cfg(test) modules in scriptbots-render for (a) any test that DRIVES it, by dispatching its keystroke or invoking its CommandAction, and (b) whether the surrounding assertions check STATE - a ControlCommand enqueued, a controls/hud/playback field changed, world.is_closed() - rather than merely that a handler ran.

The (b) distinction is the whole point: a test asserting a handler fired would pass for a control that does nothing downstream.

RESULTS

STATE-PROVEN (3 of 27):
  StepSimulation           s        asserts &[ControlCommand::Step] enqueued
  ToggleClosedEnvironment  c        asserts one intent, no direct world mutation
  SelectAll                ctrl-a   asserts selection state

DRIVEN BUT NOT STATE-PROVEN (6): TogglePlayback (space), GoLive (g), CyclePalette (ctrl-p), ToggleSimulationPause (p), FollowSelected (shift-s), FitWorld (0).
  These appear in tests - mostly keybinding-registry and no-duplicate-shortcut checks - which prove the BINDING exists, not that pressing the key changes anything.

NEVER DRIVEN BY ANY TEST (18): ToggleBrush, ToggleNarration, ToggleAgentDraw, ToggleFoodOverlay, ToggleAgentOutline, IncreaseSimulationSpeed, DecreaseSimulationSpeed, AddCrossoverAgents, SpawnCarnivore, SpawnHerbivore, FollowOldest, ToggleDebugOverlay, ClearSelection, FocusFirstSelected, ToggleSettings, ToggleStatsPanel, ToggleHistoryPanel, TogglePerfPanel.

WHERE A SILENT NO-OP WOULD COST MOST, in priority order:
  1. SIMULATION CONTROL - IncreaseSimulationSpeed, DecreaseSimulationSpeed (never driven); TogglePlayback, ToggleSimulationPause (driven, unproven). If these are inert the app feels broken on first contact, which is exactly the class the owner reported.
  2. POPULATION MUTATION - SpawnCarnivore, SpawnHerbivore, AddCrossoverAgents. These change scientific state; a silent failure is invisible and corrupts what an experimenter believes they ran.
  3. WHAT THE OWNER LOOKS AT - ToggleAgentDraw, ToggleFoodOverlay. Directly on the visual complaint.
  The three panel toggles (1/2/3) are lower risk: bd-f4x0's differential capture drove them through the production path and showed the rail appearing and vanishing, which is state evidence even though no unit test asserts it.

WHY CAPTURE CANNOT SUBSTITUTE. The bd-bacf capture sweep measured all 27 and found no zero-delta control, but bd-c7pg's ~10k-pixel nondeterminism floor swallows 21 of 27 - the instrument reports the same number for a working control and a dead one. Only 6 clear the floor. Verification must be by STATE until bd-c7pg is fixed.

NOT WRITING 18 TESTS HERE. The gap is recorded; the tiers above say where to start.

Cross-refs: bd-bacf (this is its first concrete output), bd-c7pg (why capture cannot close this).
close_reason:
26 of 27 HUD shortcuts state-proven; the last one is split out to bd-fjs5 with its exact blocker.

The map this bead produced said 3 of 27 were proven by state and 18 were never driven by any test. Every one of those 18 is now either proven or explicitly accounted for, through a production GPUI session that dispatches real keystrokes into the HUD window and reads back the state each control names - not a keybinding-registry check, which passes for a control that does nothing.

COMMITS: 95359af3d (12 controls + the ShortcutFixture seam), 8df9518a5 (CyclePalette, FitWorld), 9d8bf1b20 (speed pair), b1e7b7ac8 (TogglePlayback, GoLive, FocusFirstSelected, ToggleSimulationPause), 093045eb1 (SpawnCarnivore, SpawnHerbivore).

ASSERTIONS ARE DELIBERATELY STRONGER THAN 'IT CHANGED', because the weak form passes on real breakage: toggles must toggle BACK (a latching control is as broken as a no-op); CyclePalette must return to start after five presses (pins cycle length and wrap together); FitWorld pans the camera off-centre FIRST and asserts that as a precondition, so it cannot pass trivially on an already-fitted camera; the two follow shortcuts must reach DIFFERENT modes; the two spawn shortcuts must carry DIFFERENT tendencies (a carnivore key that quietly seeds herbivores is invisible to an experimenter); speed and pause intents must carry the current pause state and speed through.

TWO CORRECTIONS MADE RATHER THAN INHERITED. (1) bd-zlmc, my own filed finding that TogglePlayback was dead, is WITHDRAWN - it was my harness. snapshot_for_render returns Playing to Live when pointer+1 == timeline.len(), so a ONE-frame timeline finishes the instant it starts; record_frames(n) steps the world between repaints because record() drops any snapshot whose tick matches the newest. (2) The July deferral of the population controls was obsolete: spawn_agent_with_tendency now submits ControlCommand::SpawnAgent, so q and h are provable against the post-migration contract rather than the direct-mutation shape the deferral was protecting against. I checked instead of inheriting.

A near-miss worth recording: my first ClearSelection test asserted world selection changed after ctrl-a and FAILED. That was the test being wrong about the contract, not the product - bd-37m requires the renderer to submit intent and never write selection. Rewritten to assert the intent bus plus that world selection stays untouched pre-drain. It would have been easy to file that as a defect.

GATES: rustfmt --edition 2024 --check clean; ubs --only=rust 2 critical, unchanged from the pre-work baseline captured via git show HEAD; rch exec -- cargo test -p scriptbots-render => 102 passed, 3 failed, 3 ignored. The 3 failures are the pre-existing hud_capture trio filed as bd-h9ca; they fail in isolation with none of my tests in the filter set and hud_capture.rs is untouched by every commit above.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
SPEED NOW STATE-PROVEN. simulation_speed_multiplier_changes_the_observed_tick_rate drives GuiSimulationDriver's accumulator with fabricated instants (drive_at takes now as a parameter) and asserts 2x executes exactly twice the ticks of 1x over the same advance. Ratio rather than absolute rate, so it cannot flake under load. Coverage moves 3/27 -> 4/27 state-proven.

Also resolved BY INSPECTION of the consumer, all three correct:
 - step never silently resumes (Step yields paused: None; apply_playback_state forces paused=true on step_once)
 - a paused world does not free-run (tick gate returns early AND zeroes sim_accumulator, so unpausing does not discharge stored ticks)
 - speed set while paused persists (speed_multiplier assigned unconditionally, not gated on running)

So the simulation-control tier is now the BEST-verified area examined, not the worst. Recording that explicitly because '3 of 27' invites the opposite reading: this map measures TEST COVERAGE, not correctness. An untested control is unproven, not presumed broken.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: State-level speed proof banked in ca6639bfb after AmberFalcon explicitly transferred the self-contained green hunk during a shared render/lib.rs collision. The test drives GuiSimulationDriver with fabricated Instants and pins exactly 2x observed ticks at 2x speed; no wall-clock sleep.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
SPAWN DEFERRED, AND THE REASON IS A FINDING IN ITSELF.

Spawn was next on this map's priority list. It is not written, deliberately: spawn is a DIRECT AGENT-SCIENCE WRITE FROM THE RENDER LAYER, and it is one of the paths making WildDuck's production_renderer_has_no_direct_agent_science_writes_or_rng born-red.

  lib.rs:5671  spawn_agent_with_tendency locks the world and calls
  lib.rs:5680  spawn_agent_with_bias_internal(&mut WorldState, ..) which mutates it directly.
               No ControlCommand, no intent, no drain. It also samples RNG render-side -
               the guard at 5682 warns 'rejected before RNG sampling'.

Three controls route this way: SpawnCarnivore (q), SpawnHerbivore (h), AddCrossoverAgents (a). Step, Pause and Resume all correctly go through submit_control_command, so spawn is the exception rather than the house style.

Writing a population-count test against that path today would pin the behaviour of a direct-mutation shape that the routing work is about to replace. Mailed WildDuck to sequence it: either they route spawn to an intent and I assert population across the new path, or they want a born-red test pinning the intended behaviour first and I write it against the intent so it greens as the routing lands.

WHY POPULATION IS THE RIGHT ASSERTION whenever it is written: spawn changes population, population drives every downstream metric, and a spawn control that silently did nothing would look IDENTICAL to a simulation that is simply not reproducing. The debugger goes hunting in evolution or energy, finds nothing wrong there because nothing is, and the actual broken control is never suspected. That is the specific cost of this gap.

STOPPING HERE per direction. 24 controls remain untested; the map stands as the finding rather than being converted into 24 tests. Current state: 4 of 27 state-proven (Step, ToggleClosedEnvironment, SelectAll, and speed once its hunk lands), 6 driven-but-unproven, 17 never driven.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
SPAWN NOW STATE-PROVEN — coverage 4 of 27 -> 5 of 27.

The deferral resolved itself: WildDuck routed spawn while I was on bd-c7pg. It is no longer a direct render-layer agent-science write:
  spawn_agent_with_tendency -> submit_control_command(ControlCommand::SpawnAgent { herbivore_tendency })
  apply_control_command     -> world.try_inject_control_agent(..) -> ControlDisposition::WorldApplied

spawn_shortcut_increases_population_through_the_control_path asserts agent_count before and after for both biases plus the disposition - the END of the chain, not that a command was enqueued. Enqueueing is precisely what the old direct-mutation path could have faked.

Holding off was the right call: a test written a few hours ago would have pinned the shape that has since been removed.

STATE-PROVEN (5): StepSimulation, ToggleClosedEnvironment, SelectAll, speed (tick-rate ratio), spawn (population count).
NEXT COSTLIEST: agent-draw and food-overlay. Both gate EMISSION rather than appearance (lib.rs 'if controls.draw_food {' and 'if controls.draw_agents {' wrap the whole emission block), so an emitted-count assertion is available and would catch the failure that matters - a toggle that stops painting but still builds geometry costs the same frame time and looks like it works.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
EMITTED-COUNT SEAM: PROTOTYPED, PROVEN TO WORK FOR AGENTS, REVERTED UNFINISHED. Not committed - the tree is clean at HEAD.

DESIGN THAT WORKS, for whoever picks it up:
  #[cfg(test)] thread_local Cell<(usize, usize)> in scriptbots-render, with
  note_food_emitted() / note_agent_emitted() called at the paint sites inside the
  'if controls.draw_food {' and 'if controls.draw_agents {' gates, and

So the SEAM ITSELF WORKS - a thread-local incremented inside paint_frame is visible to

with 'col' at ~16223 is not on the food emission path, or food is not painted through

  capture_world() has population_minimum: 0 and no seeded food, so NOTHING is drawn -
  the first run reported food=0 agents=0 and the vacuity guard correctly refused.
  capture_visual_world() is the populated one (96 agents, seeded food hotspots) and is
  what any emission test must use.
The vacuity guard - requiring both counters non-zero with toggles ON before asserting
zero with them OFF - did its job twice and is the reason neither wrong result was
mistaken for a pass.

WHY PIXELS CANNOT SUBSTITUTE, restated because it is the whole point: geometry built
but not painted is pixel-identical to geometry never built, so a pixel diff passes for
the failure worth catching - a toggle that stops painting while still paying the build
cost. Same shape as bd-rzy3's perf panel mounting one frame in four.

STATE: 5 of 27 state-proven (Step, ToggleClosedEnvironment, SelectAll, speed, spawn).

comments.text:

now proven against the state they name, through the real production GPUI session.

METHOD, and why it is not the hollow coverage this bead was filed to expose. Every test below
installs both production windows via GuiSession::install, forces a production repaint, and then
calls window.dispatch_keystroke into the HUD - the same harness the existing
gpui_s_shortcut_* test uses. Nothing calls invoke_action directly, so a binding that never
reaches its handler fails. Then each asserts the specific field the control names, and asserts
it TOGGLES BACK on a second press. That second half matters: a control that latches on and
cannot be undone is just as broken from the user's seat as one that does nothing, and neither
a registry check nor a "did the handler fire" test can see either failure.

NEWLY STATE-PROVEN (12):
  d              ToggleAgentDraw       controls.draw_agents
  f              ToggleFoodOverlay     controls.draw_food
  ctrl-shift-o   ToggleAgentOutline    controls.agent_outline
  shift-f        ToggleDebugOverlay    debug.enabled
  1              ToggleStatsPanel      hud.stats_open
  2              ToggleHistoryPanel    hud.history_open
  3              TogglePerfPanel       hud.perf_open
  ,              ToggleSettings        settings_panel.open
  n              ToggleNarration       accessibility.narration_enabled
  b              ToggleBrush           inspector.lock().brush_enabled

  shift-s        FollowSelected        controls.follow_mode
The two follow shortcuts get a stronger assertion than "it changed": follow_mode is a
tri-state, so the test also proves 'o' and 'shift-s' reach DIFFERENT modes. Otherwise one of
them could silently be the other and both would still "work".

escape / ClearSelection is proven against the CONTROL BUS, not a view field, because that is
its real contract. bd-37m established that the renderer submits selection INTENT and must not
write selection itself; the existing SelectAll test pins exactly that. So the new test asserts
ctrl-a submits an UpdateSelection intent naming agents, escape submits a further intent with
state None, and - critically - that world selection is still untouched afterwards. My first
version of this test asserted world.selected_count() > 0 after ctrl-a and FAILED. That was my
test being wrong about the contract, not the product being wrong; recording it because the
failure looked exactly like a defect and it would have been easy to file one. This is the same
reason the bead's own spawn deferral was right.

REUSABLE FIXTURE, so the remaining controls are cheap: ShortcutFixture in
command_characterization_tests, with install(), install_with_agents(n), press(keystroke),
read(probe), submitted(), selected_agents(). Adding a control to the table test is one line.

ONE FINDING SPLIT OUT -> bd-zlmc. TogglePlayback does not move playback.mode() in this harness
even with a recorded timeline, and I could not close the question of whether that is a product
defect or a harness artifact, so I did not ship a claim or a red test. What is measured: the
timeline had 1 frame, bindings.action_for("space") returned Some(TogglePlayback), and the mode
stayed Live. I eliminated the obvious confound - that GPUI never delivers the space key,
plausible since a focused button often eats space - by rebinding TogglePlayback to 'shift-p'
and dispatching that instead; the mode still stayed Live. And dispatch itself demonstrably
works in the same fixture, since the nine table controls above all flip. The bead has the exact
next step. Note TogglePlayback is one of the six this map classified as "driven but not
state-proven" - it appears only in binding-registry checks - so nobody has ever confirmed the
space bar works.

STILL UNPROVEN AFTER THIS PASS (11 of 27): TogglePlayback and GoLive (-> bd-zlmc);
CyclePalette, FitWorld, FocusFirstSelected; IncreaseSimulationSpeed and DecreaseSimulationSpeed
(state-proven separately per this bead's earlier comment, via the driver ratio test, not via
keystroke); and the three population controls SpawnCarnivore, SpawnHerbivore,
AddCrossoverAgents, which remain deliberately deferred per this bead's own note - they are

pin a shape that is being replaced.

PlaybackMode gained a Debug derive so assertion failures print a mode instead of a type error.
That is the only production line in the change; the other 277 are inside cfg(test).

comments.author: YellowLake
comments.text:
16/27 -> 18/27. Two more of the six "driven but not state-proven" controls now have real proofs
(commit 8df9518a5, verified on rch worker hz2).

  ctrl-p  CyclePalette   accessibility.palette
  0       FitWorld       camera offset/zoom

BOTH ASSERTIONS ARE DELIBERATELY STRONGER THAN "IT CHANGED", because for these two the weak
form would pass on a broken control:

CyclePalette walks a FIVE-entry enum. Asserting only that one press changed the palette would
pass for a control that advances by two, or that saturates on the last entry and never wraps.
So the test presses once and asserts it advanced, then presses four more times and asserts it
is back exactly where it started - which pins the cycle length and the wrap together.

pass trivially whenever the camera happened to already be fitted, which for a freshly installed
session is most of the time - vacuous coverage of exactly the kind this bead exists to replace.
So the test first pans the camera off-centre through the public start_pan/update_pan/end_pan
path, asserts as a FIXTURE PRECONDITION that the offset really did move, and only then presses
'0' and asserts the offset returns to (0,0). If the perturbation ever stops working the test
fails on the precondition rather than silently going hollow.

Note fit_world() is a no-op until a render has recorded a base scale, so this also confirms the
production repaint in ShortcutFixture::install() is doing its job; without it the test would be
asserting against the guard instead of against the control.

STILL UNPROVEN (9 of 27):

  FocusFirstSelected                          needs an APPLIED selection, and selection is
                                              intent-based by design (bd-37m) - the fixture has

  IncreaseSimulationSpeed, DecreaseSimulationSpeed

comments.text:
24 of 27 (commit b1e7b7ac8). THREE remain, and all three are the deferral this bead itself
already declared - not shortcuts I ran out of time on.

the WRONG SHAPE. This bead's own 2026-07-25 comment established it: all three route through

it directly from the render layer, sampling RNG render-side. No ControlCommand, no intent, no
drain. bd-37m is migrating exactly that path. A population-count assertion written against
today's direct-mutation shape would have to be rewritten the moment that lands, and worse, it
would be a test asserting that the renderer DOES write agent science directly - the opposite of
the contract bd-37m is establishing. So they stay deferred until bd-37m reroutes them, at which
point the assertion is population across the new intent path.

COUNT CORRECTION, stated because the running number in my earlier comments was loose. The
bead's own baseline of "3/27, moved to 4/27" counted the speed pair as ONE item, but the map
lists IncreaseSimulationSpeed and DecreaseSimulationSpeed as two of the 27. Against the literal
27-shortcut list the honest tally is now 24 proven / 3 unproven. Full enumeration:

  PROVEN BEFORE THIS SESSION (3)
    s  StepSimulation · c  ToggleClosedEnvironment · ctrl-a  SelectAll
  PROVEN THIS SESSION (21)
    space  TogglePlayback        g       GoLive              ctrl-p  CyclePalette
    p      ToggleSimulationPause shift-s FollowSelected      0       FitWorld
    b      ToggleBrush           n       ToggleNarration     d       ToggleAgentDraw
    f      ToggleFoodOverlay     ctrl-shift-o ToggleAgentOutline
    shift-=  IncreaseSimulationSpeed      -  DecreaseSimulationSpeed
    o      FollowOldest          shift-f ToggleDebugOverlay  escape  ClearSelection
    ctrl-f FocusFirstSelected    ,       ToggleSettings
    1      ToggleStatsPanel      2       ToggleHistoryPanel  3       TogglePerfPanel

NEW IN THIS COMMIT, and one of them corrects a finding I filed earlier:

TogglePlayback + GoLive. bd-zlmc IS WITHDRAWN — it was my harness, not the product. Root cause:
PlaybackTimeline::snapshot_for_render, in Playing mode, checks `pointer + 1 < timeline.len()`
and on failure concludes playback ran off the end and sets mode back to Live. With a ONE-frame
timeline that is true immediately, so toggle_play correctly sets Playing and the very next
render correctly returns it to Live - a one-frame timeline finishes the instant it starts. My
earlier fixture recorded exactly one frame, observed Live after pressing space, and read a
working control as dead. The fix is record_frames(n), which STEPS the world between repaints,
because PlaybackTimeline::record drops any snapshot whose tick matches the newest one it holds
- repainting a frozen world records one frame no matter how often you call it. With 4 frames:
space -> Playing, space -> Paused, g -> Live. All three assertions pass.

FocusFirstSelected. Driven through the realistic flow, ctrl-a then ctrl-f, because it resolves
its target via effective_selected_agents, which prefers the pre-drain selection PROJECTION over
the world's canonical selection. So this doubles as proof that the projection bd-37m's intent
routing publishes is actually consumable downstream, not merely recorded. Also asserts ctrl-f
with nothing selected focuses NOTHING - a focus that invents a target is worse than no focus -
and that the resulting handle names a live agent rather than a stale one.

ToggleSimulationPause. Bus-routed like the speed pair, so the proof is the exact canonical
intent. Pins that the intent carries the CURRENT speed through: a pause that silently reset
speed to a default would be a real regression.

THE DEFERRAL ON THE OTHER TWO WAS OBSOLETE AND I CHECKED RATHER THAN INHERITED IT. This bead

title: app: reqwest pulled openssl-sys via default-tls, breaking every build on hosts without OpenSSL dev headers
description:
crates/scriptbots-app/Cargo.toml:16 declared reqwest with features = ["json", "rustls-tls"] but left default features enabled. reqwest's default feature set includes default-tls, which pulls native-tls -> openssl v0.10.81 -> openssl-sys v0.9.117. Requesting rustls-tls does not displace it.

Because .cargo/config.toml pins [build] target = "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu", every cargo invocation in this repo cross-compiles, and openssl-sys cannot configure through pkg-config for a cross target ('pkg-config has not been configured to support cross-compilation'). Result: cargo build/check/test -p scriptbots-app fails on this macOS host both locally and through rch, which is consistent with 'rch status' reporting Builds: 8 total, 0% success rate.

reqwest is declared by exactly one crate (scriptbots-app), so this is a self-contained fix: set default-features = false and re-state the defaults actually used (charset, http2) alongside json and rustls-tls. Verified after the change that 'cargo tree -p scriptbots-app -i openssl-sys' reports no matching package and reqwest resolves through hyper-rustls/rustls 0.23.41 instead.
close_reason: Fixed and verified in 48c87cb2b; rch exec -- cargo test -p scriptbots-app --lib passed (test_openapi_spec_conformance, poisoned_derived_caches_keep_serving_knobs_and_command_status).

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: bd-we7b V11 verdict B. Commit 48c87cb2b disables reqwest default features and explicitly selects rustls-related features; it is the sole direct reqwest declaration. The committed lock contains rustls/hyper-rustls and no openssl-sys, native-tls, hyper-tls, or tokio-native-tls package. Historical RCH output was not scored.

title: storage/app: RUN_MANIFEST_V3_BOOTSTRAP_SCHEMA is duplicated and has drifted — app emits v3.6, storage still validates v3.5
description:
ff937dec6 (fix(app): retire ghost sensing provenance, bd-yw1j) bumped the manifest bootstrap contract from scriptbots.run-manifest.v3.5/WorldDigestV1.6 to v3.6/WorldDigestV1.7, but only in crates/scriptbots-app/src/lib.rs:29. crates/scriptbots-storage/src/lib.rs:1241 defines its OWN copy of the same constant, still v3.5, and storage does not import app's (verified: no 'use scriptbots_app' in storage). Two independent definitions of one wire contract, now disagreeing.

Consequence: the app emits manifests tagged v3.6 while storage's validation accepts only v3.3 or v3.5 and explicitly rejects anything else as 'continuation-incomplete' or as embedding a superseded digest contract. Storage's error text at lib.rs:1540 also still names WorldDigestV1.5 against a v3.5 expectation.

THE MANIFEST CHANGE ITSELF IS CORRECT. bd-yw1j retired sense_max_neighbors, a hashed GUI knob with no simulation effect, and ff937dec6 asserts normalized_config['sense_max_neighbors'].is_null() with the message 'the retired neighbor normalizer must not survive in run provenance'. Provenance dropping a ghost it never legitimately recorded is right, and a genuine change to manifest content correctly bumps the embedded digest contract V1.6 -> V1.7 and the schema tag v3.5 -> v3.6. Nothing real was lost alongside the ghost.

So the five failing tests in crates/scriptbots-storage/tests/multi_run_schema.rs (continuation_incomplete_v3_and_v32_manifests_are_refused, v34_/v35_ superseded-digest rejections, v36_manifest_requires_explicit_world_digest_v1_7_bootstrap_evidence, v3_config_overrides_...) are CORRECT and are catching real drift. They must not be updated to match storage, and must not be ignored — the fix is to bring storage's constant and acceptance set up to v3.6/V1.7 so both crates state one contract.

Better still, remove the duplication: one crate should own the constant and the other consume it, so this cannot drift again. storage cannot depend on app, so the shared definition likely belongs in storage (or core) with app consuming it.

Found while running the storage suite; the five failures were briefly misread as a regression and then as pre-existing bad tests, and were neither.
notes:
GUARD VERIFIED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS (the closure above said it had compiled but not been run; it has now run, and been exercised against the condition it guards).

Positive: cargo test -p scriptbots-app --test manifest_schema_single_definition = 3 passed, 0 failed.

Negative control: I deliberately reintroduced the exact defect this bead fixed — replaced the re-export with a convenience copy in the app,
    pub const RUN_MANIFEST_V3_BOOTSTRAP_SCHEMA: &str = "scriptbots.run-manifest.v3.5";
which is literally the value that had drifted — re-ran, and the guard failed with 2 failed, 1 passed:

  app_and_storage_share_one_bootstrap_schema_definition FAILED
    'the app and storage disagree on the bootstrap manifest schema tag — this is the exact drift of bd-k0wj'
    left: "scriptbots.run-manifest.v3.5"
  the_shared_bootstrap_tag_is_one_storage_accepts FAILED
    'the shared bootstrap tag "scriptbots.run-manifest.v3.5" is one storage treats as superseded, so the app would emit manifests storage refuses'

The deliberate copy was then removed; git status for crates/scriptbots-app/src/lib.rs is empty (tree matches origin) and the guard is back to 3 passed, 0 failed.

Two things the control established that inspection would not have:

1. The third assertion is NOT redundant with the equality checks. It caught the duplicate independently, via the superseded-tag table rather than via disagreement. So a copy diverging toward a tag storage rejects trips two separate mechanisms, and a lockstep bump of both constants to a rejected tag would still trip the third alone.

2. app_and_storage_share_one_manifest_schema_definition correctly stayed GREEN, because only the bootstrap constant was duplicated and the non-bootstrap one still resolved through the re-export. The guard localises the fault instead of going uniformly red, which is what makes a failure actionable.

This is therefore not a guard that has only ever seen its passing case.
close_reason:
Fixed as de-duplication in 65983e7b4. Storage now owns RUN_MANIFEST_V3_SCHEMA and RUN_MANIFEST_V3_BOOTSTRAP_SCHEMA; the app re-exports them. The app already depends on storage and the dependency cannot go the other way, so storage is the correct owner. The superseded-tag table moved with them into superseded_bootstrap_world_digest (gaining v3.5 -> WorldDigestV1.6 beside v3.4 -> V1.5), so which tags are stale is also stated once, and refusals now name the exact digest contract a stale tag embeds.

Deliberately NOT a version bump: bringing storage to v3.6 alone would have made the tests pass and left the next bump free to break them identically.

Drift guard: crates/scriptbots-app/tests/manifest_schema_single_definition.rs. Comparing the two crates' constants is a tautology while the re-export stands and a failure the moment anyone reintroduces a diverging const; a third case asserts the shared tag is one storage actually accepts, so bumping both in lockstep to a tag storage rejects fails there rather than at a distant call site. Stated limit: it cannot catch a duplicate holding the same value today — divergence is the failure mode that bit.

The five manifest tests were CORRECT and the constant was wrong. bd-yw1j retired sense_max_neighbors, a hashed GUI knob with no simulation effect; provenance dropping a ghost it should never have recorded is right, and a genuine change to manifest content correctly bumps V1.6 -> V1.7 and v3.5 -> v3.6. Nothing real was lost with the ghost, so the resolution was to move storage forward, never to relax the tests. Recorded explicitly in the commit message so the expectation changes are not later misread as papering over a regression.

Verified: cargo check -p scriptbots-storage -p scriptbots-app --all-targets clean; cargo test -p scriptbots-storage --test multi_run_schema 19 passed, 0 failed (was 5 failing). Not verified: the new app-side guard test compiled but was not run, and the wider suites were not re-run.

title: analytics cohens_d has no small-sample bias correction: real computation, wrong in a specific regime — material below n~15, and the only correction in-tree lives in the orphaned lab layer
description:
DIFFERENT CLASS FROM SHAPE 10, and worth separating. A hardcoded statistic is a fake number
and greppable. This is a REAL computation that is systematically wrong in a specific regime:
it produces a plausible, data-dependent, correctly-varying value that is biased high when the
sample is small. No sweep for literals will ever surface it.

THE GAP. crates/scriptbots-analytics/src/stats.rs has `cohens_d` (independent groups, pooled
SD) and compare.rs has an inline `cohens_dz` (paired). NEITHER applies the small-sample bias
correction. Cohen's d is a BIASED estimator of the population effect size, overestimating it
by roughly 1/J where

    J(df) = 1 - 3 / (4*df - 1),    df = n1 + n2 - 2

Hedges' g is exactly `d * J`. grep for hedges / small.sample / correction_factor across
crates/scriptbots-analytics/src returns nothing -- the correction exists nowhere in the crate.

Note the correction factor DOES exist in the codebase, in the orphaned layer:
crates/scriptbots-app/src/lab/stats.rs computes `1.0 - (3.0 / (4.0*df - 1.0).max(1.0))`. So
if bd-7453's supersession proceeds and lab/ is re-exported onto analytics, this correction is
the thing that would be LOST rather than gained. That is the reason this is filed now.

THE REGIME -- at what n it matters (equal n per group, so df = 2n - 2):

    n per group    df     J        d overstates the effect by
    -----------    ---    ------   --------------------------
        3            4    0.800    +25.0%
        5            8    0.903    +10.7%
       10           18    0.958     +4.4%
       15           28    0.973     +2.8%
       20           38    0.980     +2.0%
       30           58    0.987     +1.3%
       50           98    0.992     +0.8%
      100          198    0.996     +0.4%

Practical reading: MATERIAL below about n=15 per group (>2.5% inflation), SERIOUS below n=10
(>4%), SEVERE below n=5 (>10%). Immaterial at n>=30.

DOES THIS PROJECT FALL IN THE REGIME? At default parameters, NO -- but it is one config knob
away from YES.

  The single production consumer is certify.rs:143, `let d = cohens_d(before, after)?`, inside
  event certification. Its sample size is governed by `CertificationParams::window`, whose
  DEFAULT IS 30 (certify.rs:72). At n=30 per side the inflation is ~1.3% -- immaterial for
  effect-size reporting, and I would not change a number over it.

  Two ways it enters the material regime:
    (a) `window` is a public parameter. Any caller setting it below ~15 lands in the >2.5%
        band, and below 10 in the >4% band, with no warning.
    (b) SEGMENTS CAN BE TRUNCATED. certify.rs:133 computes
        `params.block_len.min(after.len()).max(1)` -- the code explicitly anticipates
        `after.len()` being smaller than block_len (default 5). Near a series boundary, or
        for closely spaced changepoints, the actual window is shorter than the configured
        one. Those are precisely the cases where the bias is largest, and nothing reports
        the realised n alongside the effect size.

IS IT CONSUMED? YES -- and that is what makes this a correctness question about outputs rather
than a latent bug. `d` is returned in `EventCertification` from certify.rs and is part of
reported certification results. Contrast lab/stats.rs's hedges_g, which HAS the correction but
has zero external consumers (bd-7453): the codebase applies the correction exactly where
nobody reads it and omits it exactly where somebody does.

ACCEPTANCE
  1. Add the small-sample correction to scriptbots-analytics -- either as `hedges_g` alongside
     `cohens_d`, or as a corrected variant, so the choice is explicit at the call site rather
     than implicit.
  2. certify.rs reports the REALISED n (or df) alongside the effect size, so a truncated
     window is visible in the output instead of silently inflating d.
  3. Test asserting the corrected and uncorrected values DIVERGE at small n and CONVERGE at
     large n -- e.g. n=5 differs by ~10%, n=100 by <0.5%. A test asserting only that the
     function returns a number would not catch a J that was accidentally 1.0.

NOT URGENT AT DEFAULTS, and I want that recorded plainly rather than overstated: at
window=30 this is a 1.3% effect. It is filed because it is invisible to inspection, it is
consumed, its magnitude is configuration-dependent, and the correction that exists today
lives in the module slated for supersession.
close_reason:
IMPLEMENTED AND LANDED in 6da3a4630. Verified: cargo test -p scriptbots-analytics --lib ->
43 passed, 0 failed, including the new shape test.

WHAT LANDED
  - stats::hedges_g -- Cohen's d with the small-sample correction, offered ALONGSIDE cohens_d
    rather than replacing it, so the choice is explicit at the call site. Its doc carries the
    regime table (n=5 -> +10.7%, n=30 -> +1.3%, n=100 -> +0.4%).
  - stats::EffectSizeEstimator { CohensD, HedgesG }.
  - EventCertification::effect_estimator.

WHY BOTH FIELDS, NOT JUST n. n_before/n_after already existed and say whether the
small-sample regime APPLIES; only the estimator identity says whether the correction was
ALREADY APPLIED. Applying it twice is exactly as wrong as never applying it, so a reader who
sees n_before = 6 and discounts an already-discounted number is misled in the other
direction. Together they make the statistic self-describing; either alone leaves it something
that has to be trusted.

DELIBERATELY NOT SWITCHED, and this is the part to review. Certification still reports
EffectSizeEstimator::CohensD. Adding a correction is safe; changing what certification
REPORTS alters effect sizes that may already have been published, and that is a decision with
consequences past this bead. It is now a one-line change that the estimator field makes
self-documenting. IF THE OWNER WANTS certification to use the corrected estimator, that is a
follow-up, not an omission.

THE TEST PINS THE SHAPE, NOT THE EXISTENCE: g/d in 0.900..0.906 at n=5 and 0.995..1.0 at
n=100, sign preserved, magnitude shrunk, and the small-sample penalty dominating the
large-sample one by 10x. A test merely asserting hedges_g returns a finite number would pass
with the correction factor accidentally equal to 1.0 -- with the bug still present. That is
the same failure mode that let bd-16g.1.4 close "with tests" over a hardcoded p_value.

CORRECTIONS I MADE TO MY OWN FILING, recorded so the bead is not read as originally written:
  - Acceptance item 2 ("report realised n") was WITHDRAWN: EventCertification already carried
    n_before/n_after. I proposed it without checking. The crate already follows the
    provenance convention throughout -- ConfidenceInterval reports `resamples`,
    PairedComparison `n_pairs`, DistributionSummary `n` plus a `degenerate` flag.
  - Consequently the severity was OVERSTATED in the original description. This was never "a
    number whose validity depends on a sample size nobody can see" -- the sample size was
    always visible. It was an uncorrected number, ~1.3% at defaults, with the information
    needed to spot the exception already present.

ONE IMPLEMENTATION NOTE worth keeping. My first attempt derived Serialize/Deserialize on
EffectSizeEstimator, copied from lab/stats.rs. That is wrong here: this module is
dependency-free by design and its sibling result types derive only Debug/Clone/PartialEq. I
imported a convention from the layer this audit found to be the WORSE implementation into the
one it found sound. The compiler caught it instantly -- the loud-failure side of the
asymmetry this session kept meeting: a missing derive is a hard error, a silently dropped
field is not.

CLOSING. Acceptance items 1, 3 and 4 are done; item 2 was withdrawn as already satisfied.
Remaining open work is bd-gbwn (lab/stats.rs's constant CI and its unguarded degenerate
spread), which is a different layer and tracked separately.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S OWN ACCEPTANCE, and it reduces the severity. I wrote acceptance
item 2 -- "certify.rs reports the REALISED n (or df) alongside the effect size" -- without
checking whether it already did. IT ALREADY DOES.

    EventCertification (certify.rs:85) already carries:
        pub n_before: usize,   /// Number of samples in the before window that was tested.
        pub n_after: usize,    /// Number of samples in the after window that was tested.

These are the REALISED sizes of the windows actually tested, in the returned struct, not a
log line. So the truncated-window concern I raised is DISCLOSED, not hidden: a reader who
gets an EventCertification can see n_before = 6 and judge for themselves that a small-sample
correction would matter at that size. ACCEPTANCE ITEM 2 IS WITHDRAWN -- there is nothing to
add.

THE CRATE ALREADY FOLLOWS THE CONVENTION, consistently, and it is worth recording as an
established practice to PRESERVE rather than a change to make:

    EventCertification    n_before, n_after
    ConfidenceInterval    confidence, resamples -- documented "so a reader can judge the
                          Monte-Carlo error of the bounds themselves"
    PairedComparison      n_pairs
    DistributionSummary   n, and a `degenerate` flag when the sample is constant

Every statistic in scriptbots-analytics travels with the provenance needed to judge it. That
is the generalisation of this defect class done right, and it is already done here. The
contrast is instructive: lab/stats.rs's hedges_g returns a ci_95 of g +/- 1.96*0.1 with no n,
no confidence level, and no indication the width is fixed (bd-gbwn). Same statistic family,
opposite discipline.

REVISED SEVERITY. With n disclosed in the output, this is NOT "a number whose validity depends
on a sample size nobody can see". It is a number that is uncorrected, at defaults by ~1.3%,
with the information needed to spot the exception present in the result. That is a real gap
but a modest one, and I overstated it by assuming the disclosure was missing.

REMAINING ACCEPTANCE (items 1 and 3 stand):
  1. Add the small-sample correction to scriptbots-analytics -- as `hedges_g` alongside
     `cohens_d`, or a corrected variant -- so the choice is explicit at the call site. This is
     the substance of the bead and is unaffected by the above.
  3. Test asserting corrected and uncorrected values DIVERGE at small n and CONVERGE at large
     n (n=5 differs by ~10%, n=100 by <0.5%). A test asserting only that the function returns
     a number would not catch a J accidentally equal to 1.0.

  New item, and it is the only thing the n-reporting discussion actually leaves open:
  4. If a corrected variant is added, EventCertification should say WHICH estimator produced
     `cohens_d` -- corrected or not. n_before/n_after let a reader compute the correction
     themselves, but only if they know it has not already been applied. Following the crate's
     own convention, that belongs in the struct, not in documentation.

comments.author: WildDuck
comments.text: HISTORICAL-RESIDUAL-1 rank 11 — Bucket B, keep closed. 6da3a4630 adds Hedges g with the small-sample J correction alongside Cohen d, publishes estimator identity and realized sample counts, and pins divergence at n=5 plus convergence at n=100. n_before/n_after was the citation-pattern false positive. Open lab-layer defects own different scope.

title: Shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR lock stalls git and bead operations, not just builds - long br/git chains get killed mid-write
description:
Observed 2026-07-25 by cc_1/CopperCat. Reported by the orchestrator as a failure mode not previously seen from their side.

SYMPTOM
A chained command of the form
    br update <id> -d "<long description>" ; br sync --flush-only ; git add .beads/ ; git commit ; git push
blocked on
    Blocking waiting for file lock on build directory
and was killed at the 2-minute tool timeout (exit 143). The damage was PARTIAL and
therefore easy to miss: .beads/issues.jsonl and .beads/last-touched were written,
so git status showed the sync had happened, but the bead's DESCRIPTION never
landed. Verifying afterwards returned 0 matches for the new text while everything
looked superficially fine.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN A SLOW BUILD
The shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR lock is reaching into git and bead operations, not
just compilation. A half-applied bead update is worse than a failed one: the
tracker looks updated (timestamps move, JSONL changes) while the content that
explains the work is silently missing. In a swarm whose premise is that beads
carry the handoff context, that is a quiet correctness problem in the
coordination layer itself.

WORKAROUND THAT WORKS
Split the chain and give each step its own timeout:
    timeout 100 br update <id> -d "..."
    br show <id>   then grep for a distinctive phrase   # VERIFY IT LANDED
    timeout 60  br sync --flush-only
    git add .beads/ then timeout 110 git commit -m "..."
    timeout 110 git push
Always verify the description landed before committing. Do not infer success from
br update printing "Updated <id>" - that printed even when the description was lost.

GUIDANCE
Do not chain bead and git operations while a build is in flight. Run them as
separate, individually time-boxed commands, preferably in a quiet window between
builds.

RELATED
- bd-ln8e: rust-analyzer contends on this same target dir; the orchestrator is
  auto-reaping its deadlocked cargo children every few minutes.
- bd-h7v0 (closed): same shared target dir, on a USB volume that intermittently
  stops servicing I/O, with build scripts observed wedged in uninterruptible U
  state. This lock contention is a distinct symptom of the same shared resource.

POSSIBLE REAL FIX
Bead and git operations have no reason to touch the cargo build lock at all. Worth
checking whether a git hook (the pre-commit guard, or a fmt/check hook) invokes
cargo on commit; if so that hook is the actual coupling, and it could be made
lock-free or skipped for .beads/-only commits.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
Corroborating datapoint (cc_3/AmberFalcon): with rch's test path dead (see bd-oite), the local fallback 'cargo test -p scriptbots-app --lib terminal::' parked on 'Blocking waiting for file lock on build directory' and stayed there.

Combined effect worth recording: when rch refuses AND the shared target dir is locked by a peer build, an agent has NO working verification path at all. That is what blocked me from validating a P0-adjacent change this session. Also note build slots cannot be used to coordinate around it - acquire_build_slot returns 'Build slots are disabled. Enable WORKTREES_ENABLED to use this tool.'

comments.author: Operator
comments.text:
OPERATOR MEASUREMENT + PROPOSAL 2026-07-26T07:35Z. Measured under a live 6-agent swarm: routing per-agent CARGO_TARGET_DIR to /Volumes/USBNVME16TB (exFAT over USB) removes Cargo build-directory lock contention but replaces it with I/O starvation. Peak observed: ~150 concurrent rustc across 4 cold-start builds, 25 rustc/cargo processes simultaneously in macOS U state (uninterruptible I/O wait), one openssl-sys build-script wedged 41 minutes with 0.97s CPU. U-state processes cannot be killed until their I/O returns, so a wedged gate is unrecoverable by retry. A plain du against the volume timed out at 2m30s. Metadata ops (ls/stat) stay fast; sustained many-small-file I/O is the bottleneck - which is exFATs known weakness (no journaling, expensive directory ops).

PROPOSAL for this bead: give agent builds an APFS sparseimage on the USB device instead of writing to exFAT directly. APFS-inside-an-image converts thousands of small file creates into large sequential writes to a single backing file, which is what USB is actually good at. Precedent already exists on this host: /Volumes/USBNVME16TB/temp_agent_space/dsr-volumes/rust_scriptbots_bd_2z0_5_2_ff21cdfc4ce8_02.sparseimage (512Gi APFS, DSR-owned) and /Volumes/USBNVME16TB/temp_agent_space/rch_scratch_wave18.sparsebundle (32Gi APFS, rch-owned). Do NOT commandeer either of those - they belong to the DSR and rch lanes. Create a dedicated agent-build image instead.

INTERIM MITIGATION now in force: one cold-start local build at a time across the swarm (warm-target rebuilds exempt), and a cargo -j parallelism cap so a single build cannot queue 100+ rustc against one USB device. Related: bd-ln8e (rust-analyzer holding the shared target lock, which is why builds were moved off it in the first place) and bd-oite (rch silent empty exit 1, which is why local fallback was needed at all). All three compound into one story: this host has no fast, uncontended place to build.

title: docs: cross-kind fallback claim conflates scheduled spawn and natural reproduction
description: README.md:1047 says all cross-kind parents fall back to random spawns, but that is only true for scheduled population-floor crossover: spawn_crossover_agent returns None on a family mismatch and stage_population calls spawn_random_agent. Natural mixed-kind mating intentionally still crosses body/runtime genes while the child's brain clones/mutates the primary parent's same-family genome and excludes the incompatible partner from brain provenance; existing heredity tests codify this. No path fabricates a hybrid brain, but the public contract is overbroad and can make experimenters misread mixed-family lineage. Correct README lines 544/1047 to distinguish the two paths and add a focused scheduled-fallback regression proving random registry selection rather than a hybrid; preserve the existing natural-reproduction barrier proof.
close_reason: Fixed in b9bd527e2: docs now distinguish scheduled fresh-spawn fallback from natural unary brain heredity, with a remote-tested regression proving the scheduled path.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Fixed in b9bd527e2. Verified the two distinct contracts in source: scheduled mixed-family crossover rejects the pair before constructing a parent-derived child and stage_population routes that attempt through spawn_random_agent; natural mixed-family mating can retain two-parent body/runtime lineage but excludes the incompatible partner from brain provenance and clones/mutates only the primary family's brain. Corrected README.md and the historical GPUI plan, and added a metamorphic integration test proving scheduled mismatch is bit-for-bit the same fresh registry Founder as the direct random-spawn path. Remote proof: targeted regression 1/1 passed; full heredity_proof integration suite 10/10 passed; rch cargo check -p scriptbots-core --all-targets passed (with pre-existing scoped core warnings outside this bead).

comments.author: WildDuck
comments.text: Audit correction: comment 492 was written and submitted by WildDuck; br defaulted its author field to the local OS user because --author was omitted. This note preserves the actual authorship without altering the completed technical record.

title: core heredity: crossover excludes the partner eye geometry while claiming a hybrid
description: C++ Agent::crossover independently chooses the whole eye-FOV vector and the whole eye-direction vector from either parent. Rust build_child_runtime clones the primary parent and never crosses eye_fov or eye_direction at all; those arrays can change only in the later mutation pass. With mutation disabled, a child marked hybrid can therefore never inherit the partner visual geometry, even when the parents have disjoint FOV/direction genomes. This is an undetected heredity failure, not a cosmetic numeric difference. The scalar eye-sensitivity blend is an explicit Rust body/runtime policy and is not part of this defect. Restore an explicit geometry crossover contract with deterministic RNG-domain accounting, add mutation-off fixtures proving each parent geometry can found offspring and that vector grouping matches the chosen documented policy, and make the gene log/provenance state which parent supplied the geometry.
close_reason: Completed C++-parity eye-geometry heredity. Hybrid offspring now independently inherit each whole eye_fov and eye_direction vector from either parent, log both sources, and preserve exact crossover RNG accounting (blend -> clock 0 -> clock 1 -> FOV -> direction). Pre-fix remote proof: rch cargo test -p scriptbots-core --lib bd_l3fu produced 2 expected failures (partner geometry unreachable; provenance absent). Final remote proof: same scoped command passed all 3 bd_l3fu tests, including continuation-state draw-count/order fixture. cargo fmt -p scriptbots-core --check and path diff check passed. Shared-working-tree capture placed implementation/first tests in d16fb2685 and RNG-accounting/lint follow-up in 7555ae361; history was not rewritten, and both captures were recorded with CopperCat.

comments.author: WildDuck
comments.text: Audit boundary / negative results (WildDuck, 2026-07-25): spawn eye count and ranges match the reference (four eyes; sensitivity 1..3, FOV 0.5..2, direction 0..TAU). C++ interleaves FOV/direction draws while Rust samples all FOVs then all directions, but the ports do not share an RNG algorithm/seed contract, so no order-parity bead was filed. Gaussian C++ mutation versus bounded-uniform Rust mutation is an explicit historical design choice, not rediscovered debt. Clone, serde, checkpoint capture/restore, and world-digest encoding preserve sensitivity/FOV/direction exactly; the C++ save/load path is only a TODO, so there is no serialization oracle to claim. title: HUD panel state does not persist across restarts — needs serde + a config-dir dependency in scriptbots-render
description:
Q3 of the bd-v9cz layout policy: 'what does a panel remember across restarts'. The policy answers it; the implementation does not yet honour it. Filed separately so the policy note is not mistaken for a description of what shipped.

CURRENT STATE (bd-v9cz, commit 077f76851)
HudLayout is constructed exactly once, at SimulationView initialisation:
  crates/scriptbots-render/src/lib.rs:2401  hud: HudLayout::default()
Nothing reads saved UI state anywhere. Consequence: toggling a panel with 1/2/3 works within a session, but every launch is a first launch. The defaults - stats open, history open, perf collapsed - are currently the ONLY state the app can be in at startup.

WHY IT WAS NOT IMPLEMENTED WITH THE LAYOUT
crates/scriptbots-render/Cargo.toml has no serde and no dirs/directories dependency. Persisting state means adding at least two dependencies to a crate manifest in a workspace six agents are editing concurrently, which also touches the shared Cargo.lock. That is a dependency decision with blast radius beyond this bead, so it was not taken unilaterally mid-swarm.

WHAT TO PERSIST (from the bd-v9cz policy, unchanged)
Per panel id: collapsed (bool), and size for resizable docks. Nothing else.
Explicitly NOT persisted: dock site (sites are fixed); transient auto-collapse from the resize rule - hud_rail_forced_closed is window geometry, not intent, and writing it would let one narrow resize destroy the saved layout; scroll offsets; modal open state (settings always opens closed).

HARD CONSTRAINTS
1. Storage must be entirely separate from ScriptBotsConfig. UI state must never reach simulation config or it perturbs science and determinism.
2. Versioned schema.
3. Fail-safe: unknown, corrupt, or older-version state falls back to HudLayout::default() silently. A HUD preference file must never be able to stop the app from starting.

DEPENDENCIES NEEDED: serde + serde_json (or toml) in scriptbots-render, plus a platform config-dir crate (dirs or directories). Both are already workspace dependencies used elsewhere, so this is about crate-level opt-in rather than new third-party code.

Depends on bd-v9cz (landed).

comments.author: IvoryCondor
comments.text:
IvoryCondor: claimed and released within a minute, no work done, no partial state. crates/scriptbots-render/src/lib.rs — which is where HudLayout, its Default impl, and the sole construction site at :2830 all live — is held exclusively by IndigoTiger (reservation expires 2026-07-26T19:33Z). This bead is essentially entirely in that one file, so there is no honest slice to take without stepping on an active lease.

Recording what I established before backing off, so the next taker does not redo it:

DEPENDENCY QUESTION IS SMALLER THAN THE BEAD FEARED. serde AND serde_json are already workspace dependencies (serde 1.0.228 with derive, serde_json 1.0.150 with float_roundtrip) and both are already in Cargo.lock. Adding them to crates/scriptbots-render/Cargo.toml is a crate-level opt-in with no new third-party code and no new lock entries — only the scriptbots-render package's own dependency list changes. That is a much smaller blast radius than 'adding two dependencies mid-swarm' implies.

THE CONFIG-DIR CRATE IS THE PART TO AVOID. 'dirs' appears in Cargo.lock but is purely transitive: it is NOT in [workspace.dependencies] and NO crate in crates/*/Cargo.toml depends on it directly. 'directories' is not in the lock at all. So a config-dir crate genuinely would be a new direct dependency decision.
I also checked whether the workspace already resolves a config dir anywhere — it does not. rg for dirs::, config_dir(), XDG_CONFIG_HOME, APPDATA and home_dir across crates/ returns nothing outside tests. There is no existing authority to reuse, so whoever does this establishes the first one.
My recommendation: resolve the path with std (XDG_CONFIG_HOME then HOME on unix, APPDATA on windows) rather than taking the new dependency, keeping the crate-level opt-in to serde/serde_json only. That satisfies the bead's storage requirement while leaving the dependency decision it deliberately declined to make still unmade. If a second crate later needs the same path, promote the helper then rather than now.

title: runtime: shutdown reserved ID collides with archived client command
description: crates/scriptbots-runtime/src/host_core.rs:1413-1437 checks shutdown ID candidates only against SharedHostState.commands, but submit at :700-721 also rejects payload collisions in archived_idempotency. A client can use the public lifecycle namespace/sequence ID for a normal command, let it reach the archived idempotency cache, then request_shutdown chooses the same candidate and returns CommandIdCollision instead of admitting the ordered shutdown. Candidate selection must skip both live and archived identities; add a regression that archives the colliding command before shutdown.
notes: Same lifecycle-ID allocator has a second boundary failure: HostCore initializes next_lifecycle_command_sequence from session_id and increments before forming the candidate. HostSessionId::new(u64::MAX) therefore makes the first request_shutdown fail with lifecycle command sequence exhausted even without a collision. Acceptance must cover max session identity by either admitting the current max candidate before exhausting or rejecting that session at construction.
close_reason: Lifecycle shutdown allocation now skips both live and archived command identities and admits a free u64::MAX candidate before requiring a successor; both born-red regressions pass remotely.

again just now: `resolved_day_night` has NO call site anywhere in
crates/scriptbots-render/src/lib.rs. Until this edit lands, day/night cannot be
observed and NOBODY SHOULD TUNE TERRAIN EXPOSURE -- the entire reason for
fixing the clock first is to stop choosing constants against a single frozen
sample of a range nobody has seen.

FILE: crates/scriptbots-render/src/lib.rs
ANCHOR: search for the literal `map_or((0, 0.25)` -- ONE hit. Do not trust a
line number; it was 13083, then 13122, and it moves every time the file is
edited. It sits inside `RenderFrame`'s constructor, just above `Some(Self {
tick: world.tick().0,`.

REPLACE:

        let (day_night_cycle_ticks, day_night_start_phase) = config
            .render
            .day_night
            .as_ref()
            .map_or((0, 0.25), |settings| {
                (
                    settings.cycle_ticks.unwrap_or(0),
                    settings.start_phase.unwrap_or(0.25),
                )
            });

WITH:

        let (day_night_cycle_ticks, day_night_start_phase) =
            config.render.resolved_day_night();

That is the whole change. `RenderSettings::resolved_day_night()` is public and
landed in f696b4005; it returns the same `(u32, f32)` tuple, so no other line
in the function changes. No import is needed (it is an inherent method on the
already-in-scope `config.render`).

WHY IT MUST BE THE CALL AND NOT AN INLINE DEFAULT: this inline `.map_or` WAS
the bug. It was the only place in the workspace that answered "what does an
unset day/night block mean?", and it answered "no cycle". Re-inlining a
different constant here just moves the defect. Core owns the answer now.

═══ WHAT THE RE-BLESS WILL REQUIRE (read BEFORE regenerating anything) ═══

Expect goldens to move. This is DELIBERATE, and the direction is the part that
will mislead you if nobody says it first:

  With the clock live, a golden captured at a FIXED TICK now samples a PHASE of
  a cycle instead of a constant. Its direction depends on where that tick falls
  in the 10,000-tick cycle. A golden whose tick lands near midnight gets
  DARKER. That reads exactly like a rendering or determinism regression. IT IS
  NOT ONE.

Concretely, before/after for any fixed tick T:
  before: daylight == 0.65 always (DAYLIGHT_STATIC)
  after:  daylight == daylight_factor(T, 10_000, 0.25), which sweeps
          0.15 (midnight) .. 1.00 (noon)

WHEN RE-BLESSING, STATE IN THE COMMIT: the golden's tick T, the resulting
daylight value at T, and that the change is expected. An unexplained golden
diff is indistinguishable from a determinism regression -- that is the standard
this repo already holds itself to (bd-yw1j/bd-k0wj bumped manifest v3.6 /
WorldDigestV1.7 for exactly this reason).

Also expect run-provenance movement: render settings are hashed, so the config
lane advances. Science lanes must NOT move -- if a transition/tail/ledger lane
changes, that IS a real regression and this edit is not the cause.

VERIFY IT WORKED: capture two frames whose ticks are half a cycle apart (e.g.
T and T+5000) and diff them. Identical frames mean the mapping did not take
effect. The probe at crates/scriptbots-core/tests/day_night_default_probe.rs
covers the CORE half only -- it cannot see the renderer, so a green core suite
is NOT evidence this landed.

title: rust-analyzer contends with agent builds on the shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR
description: Observed 2026-07-24 17:35. title: Align default sense_radius to World.cpp's 150 and re-bless the digest, scene and perf artifacts (bd-rs9f follow-through)
description:
Align ScriptBotsConfig::default's sense_radius from 120 to World.cpp's conf::DIST of
150, and re-bless the three artifact families that move as a result.

WHY THIS IS NOT A REGRESSION FIX. 150 NEVER EXISTED in the Rust port. `sense_radius:
120` arrived with c79e9590f ("feat: implement spatial indexing and agent sensing
pipeline") and was never subsequently changed. A future reader seeing the word
"restore" would go looking for a regression that does not exist. This INTRODUCES C++
parity for the first time; it is a behaviour change, not a repair.

DRIFT, NOT A DECISION -- evidence gathered under bd-rs9f:
  - c79e9590f is exhaustively documented (hundreds of lines covering grid hashing,
    inv_cell_size caching, squared-distance comparison) and says NOTHING about the
    radius, conf::DIST, or any reason to diverge. An author who documented a
    reciprocal-multiply micro-optimisation would have justified departing from the
    reference constant.
  - No bead, no doc, no plan entry sanctions 120 or records an intentional divergence.
  - Repository history calls 120 "a typical perception range"; that is a description,
    not an approval.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY CHANGES. conf::DIST is BOTH the cutoff and the attenuation
normalizer in World.cpp (`smaccum += (conf::DIST-d)/conf::DIST`), and Rust mirrors
this with `distance_factor = (radius - distance) / radius`. So the radius does not
only decide WHO is visible -- it rescales HOW STRONGLY every in-range neighbour is
sensed across smell, sound, hearing and blood. Every simulation trajectory shifts.

EVIDENCE ALREADY IN THE TREE. crates/scriptbots-core/tests/sense_radius_parity.rs
holds two tests, currently #[ignore]d with the reason printed by the runner. They
were landed RED first (75d04276f) to prove the divergence, then ignored (c5d1c5f72)
so the suite is not permanently failing. Removing the two #[ignore] attributes is the
acceptance proof for this bead; no new test needs writing.
  - a_neighbor_inside_the_legacy_range_is_perceived -> currently "got 0" at 135 units
  - the_attenuation_curve_matches_the_legacy_normalizer -> currently 3.000 vs 2.000

REQUIRED RE-BLESSES -- this is why the bead exists rather than a one-line commit.
Each is a deliberate act and must state its reason; a goldens diff appearing without
explanation is indistinguishable from a determinism regression, which is exactly what
this project's machinery exists to catch.

  1. WORLD DIGEST GOLDEN. The six-point trace gated by SCRIPTBOTS_WORLD_DIGEST_GOLDEN
     (scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs). Its `traced_world()` builds from
     ..ScriptBotsConfig::default() and overrides only world size, food cell size,
     population and seed -- so it INHERITS sense_radius and will move. Env-gated, so
     ordinary test runs stay green. Needs the pinned DSR lane.

  2. SCENE GOLDENS. crates/scriptbots-app/tests/scenes/goldens/{empty_world,
     hydrology_flood,bevy_offscreen_smoke}. All three carry `kind = "agent_count"`
     assertions and run 6-90 ticks with agents, so shifted trajectories move the
     captures. Regeneration needs RUST_REGEN_GOLDEN=1 with --features bevy_render and
     a real GPU (--dump-scene-png). Never auto-bless; a missing golden must stay an
     explicit failure.

  3. PERF BASELINE -- THE ONE MOST LIKELY TO BITE. ci/fixtures/perf_baseline.json
     (total_tps 70.2, max_tps_regression_pct 10.0). Sensing cost scales with the AREA
     swept per neighbour query, and (150/120)^2 = 1.5625, i.e. ~56% more neighbours
     tested and accumulated per agent per tick in the dominant cost of the tick loop.
     A 10% regression gate will very likely trip. Re-baselining is a reviewed DSR
     operation requiring a nonempty `Perf-Baseline-Justification:` trailer per
     AGENTS.md and must never be self-approved.

     NOTE THE REAL TRADEOFF: this is parity versus throughput, not a free correctness
     win. Whoever takes this should decide explicitly whether the project accepts a
     materially slower tick for C++ sensing parity, and record that decision. If the
     answer is no, the honest outcome is to document 120 as an intentional divergence
     and close bd-rs9f as invalid instead -- that is a legitimate result, not a
     failure.

WHO CAN TAKE THIS: an agent or session with BOTH the scene-regen lane (GPU + bevy
feature) and the DSR lane. cc_1/CopperCat has neither, which is why the constant was
not landed alongside the tests.

title: brain-dwraon: zero-scale bias mutation rewrites signed-zero genome bits
description: Confirmed metamorphic identity defect in crates/scriptbots-brain/src/dwraon.rs. A valid DWRAON bias may be -0.0 and is encoded bit-for-bit, but mutate_nodes always executes bias += gaussian * scale. When the bias gate selects a positive Gaussian and scale is 0.0, -0.0 becomes +0.0, changing the genome payload/material hash despite zero continuous mutation magnitude. Structural mutation draws must remain unchanged, and the Gaussian draw must still be consumed; skip only the continuous arithmetic at zero scale, add a scripted signed-zero/RNG-continuation regression, and bump the adapter semantic identity.
close_reason: Fixed zero-scale DWRAON continuous mutation to preserve signed-zero genome bits while retaining the exact RNG draw schedule; scoped scriptbots-brain tests pass remotely.

title: shared_tree_commit message guard false-positives on git's own blank-line normalization
description:
shared_tree_commit.py compares the approved commit message byte-for-byte against what git
actually stored, but git NORMALIZES messages on the way in (it strips and collapses blank
lines). Any message git renormalizes therefore trips the mismatch check even though the
commit is exactly correct.

CONCRETE EVIDENCE, commit 3e16ac07a. The guard printed:

  shared-tree-commit: REFUSED: commit landed with a message different from approval;
  stop and inspect 3e16ac07a4101162d3544152a5a5b5c70526e21a.

Diffing the approved text against `git log -1 --format=%B`:

  90d89 <     (one blank line)
  118a118 >   (one blank line)

That is the ENTIRE difference: git moved one blank line. No content differs. No mangling.
The commit was correct and the refusal was spurious.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. The check exists to catch real message corruption --
the backtick/command-substitution mangling that produced commit 1de69a471 earlier in this
session was exactly that, and the guard catching it was valuable. A check that also fires on
correct commits trains agents to read "REFUSED" as noise, which is precisely how the real
corruption gets waved through next time. A safety guard with a routine false positive is
worse than a strict one, because it spends its credibility.

It also fires AFTER the commit has already landed, so the operator is left with a committed
tree and an instruction to "stop and inspect" -- there is no safe automatic action, only a
manual diff every time.

FIX: normalize both sides before comparing -- strip trailing whitespace per line, collapse
runs of blank lines, and strip leading/trailing blank lines -- or compare against
`git stripspace` output of the approved message rather than the raw text. Either makes the
check fire only on genuine divergence.

REPRODUCE: approve any message whose blank-line layout git will renormalize (for example one
with a trailing blank line before the trailer block) and commit it.

NOT the same as bd-donj, which is about the agent-mail push guard applying EDIT reservation
semantics to a PUSH operation. Different component, different mechanism; filed separately so
closing bd-donj does not close this.

title: brain-assembly: public legacy runner still launders NaN outputs
description: Residual surface adjacent to closed bd-mk5q. crates/scriptbots-brain/src/assembly.rs tick_with_budget rewrites NaN sensors and NaN outputs to 0.0. A deterministic finite two-instruction program can compute MAX*MAX -> Inf then Inf*0 -> NaN into output cell 199; raw AssemblyBrain::tick/runner returns 0 as if evaluation succeeded while retaining a poisoned NaN cell, whereas the C++ reference propagates NaN because its clamp comparisons are false. The protocol evaluator correctly rejects and rolls back, so default product runs are safe. Make the public legacy path honest by preserving non-finite values instead of laundering them, and add a differential regression proving raw output/state expose NaN while the protocol path remains typed and transactional.
close_reason: Removed legacy Assembly NaN laundering so infallible evaluation exposes invalid values while protocol evaluation rejects them transactionally; scoped scriptbots-brain tests pass remotely.

title: brain-assembly: interpreter sanitizer hides generated NaN and commits corrupted transition
description: Confirmed against original ScriptBots C++. crates/scriptbots-brain/src/assembly.rs performs unchecked arithmetic, then rewrites NaN cells to zero before its transactional validation. A finite two-instruction sequence can create Inf and then Inf * 0 -> NaN; current Rust returns Ok and commits the sanitized cell, while C++ only caps values outside +/-10 and does not rewrite NaN. Add a two-instruction regression requiring InvalidPayload plus an unchanged checkpoint, fail before commit, and update semantic identity if transition semantics change.
close_reason: Stopped Assembly interpreter NaN laundering; a real two-instruction Inf*0 transition now returns typed evaluator-state InvalidPayload with byte-identical rollback, semantic identity v2. Verified by remote scriptbots-brain and scriptbots-brain-ml tests.

title: rch exits 1 with zero output when no workers are admissible
description: Observed 2026-07-24 23:50. 'rch exec -- cargo test -p scriptbots-index' exits 1 producing ZERO bytes on stdout and stderr, giving the caller no indication why. 'rch diagnose' reveals the real reason: 'no admissible workers: insufficient_slots=1, hard_preflight=1, active_project_exclusion=2'. rch excludes workers already running a build for the same project, so a 6-agent swarm on one project can starve itself down to zero admissible workers whenever healthy worker count is low. Two agents (cod_1, cc_3) independently concluded 'rch is disabled' and stalled - one for over an hour - because the failure is silent. Worse, the orchestrator initially dismissed the first report as a phantom outage on the strength of a passing 'cargo check', which still worked because check landed before the exclusions bit. IMPACT: silent exit-1 is indistinguishable from a disabled service and directly caused lost agent-hours. FIX: emit the diagnose reason on the failure path, non-zero-exit with a message naming insufficient_slots / hard_preflight / active_project_exclusion counts. WORKAROUND USED: 'rch daemon restart' recovered free slots 15 -> 25 and dispatch resumed (verified exit 0, artifacts retrieved). Related: bd-x1ec (2 workers persistently cached offline though they probe OK).

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
Reproduced hard today (cc_3/AmberFalcon), and it is narrower than 'no admissible workers' - rch is HEALTHY while this happens.

  rch doctor            -> 22 passed, all checks green
  rch status            -> 4/6 workers healthy (vmi1156319, vmi1153651 unreachable)

Split by subcommand, same shell, same minute:
  rch exec -- cargo check -p scriptbots-app                 -> WORKS. 261s, full diagnostics, found a real compile error.
  rch exec -- cargo check -p scriptbots-app --all-targets   -> exit 1, ZERO bytes on both stdout and stderr.
  rch exec -- cargo test  -p scriptbots-app --lib terminal:: -> exit 1, ZERO bytes. 4 consecutive attempts.
  rch exec -- cargo test  -p scriptbots-app --lib            -> exit 1, ZERO bytes.

So the failing axis appears to be the 'test' subcommand and/or --all-targets, not worker admissibility. A plain check on the same crate succeeds immediately before and after.

The zero-output part is the damaging bit: exit 1 with no diagnostics is indistinguishable from a compile failure, so an agent cannot tell 'your code is broken' from 'the build system declined'. Whatever the cause, rch should emit the reason on stderr - RCH-E301 style - rather than exiting silently.

Note the documented contract in AGENTS.md is 'If rch or its workers are unavailable, it fails open - builds run locally as normal.' It is not failing open here; it is failing closed and silent.

comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-07-26T07:45Z - the silent empty exit 1 is an rsync artifact-sync failure, NOT a compiler failure and NOT (only) transient.

Reproduction from the operator shell: `rch exec -- cargo check -p scriptbots-core --message-format=short` returned exit 1 with 0 bytes on stdout and 71,980 bytes on stderr. Grepping that stderr for real rustc diagnostics (`^error:` / `^error[`) yields ZERO matches. What it actually contains is 36 instances of:

  rsync: [generator] failed to set times on "/Users/jemanuel/projects/rust_scriptbots/<path>": Operation not permitted (1)

Affected paths include .beads/.br_recovery, captures/, captures/bevy_offscreen_smoke, captures/empty_world, captures/hydrology_flood, ci/fixtures/, crates/scriptbots-analytics/. All are owned by jemanuel:staff with no special flags, and the invoking user IS jemanuel - so this is not simple ownership.

Most probable mechanism: rsync preserves mtimes on directories during the sync, and with a 6-agent swarm continuously writing into this working tree, those directories are being mutated concurrently while rsync tries to utime them. That makes the failure LOAD-DEPENDENT, which explains the observed "transient" behavior perfectly: success rate tracked swarm build concurrency (100% at 0 builds, 12-15% under 4 concurrent cold-start builds, 40% once load dropped).

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN THE COSMETIC BUG: because rch surfaces this as a bare exit 1 with no diagnostic, agents cannot distinguish "your code does not compile" from "the remote compile was fine but sync-back failed". Three separate panes independently concluded RCH was dead, and one built an elaborate (and wrong) macOS code-signing theory around it. The compile result in this mode is INCONCLUSIVE, not negative.

SUGGESTED FIX SHAPE: (1) separate the transfer stage exit code from the compile stage exit code and report which stage failed; (2) treat rsync utime failures on directories as non-fatal (rsync --omit-dir-times / --no-t for the sync-back, or ignore exit 23/24 selectively); (3) always emit a typed reason on nonzero exit - never exit 1 with zero bytes of diagnostic. Related: bd-kkn7 (host has no fast uncontended build location), bd-ln8e (rust-analyzer holds the shared target lock), bd-x1ec (worker storage pressure).

ROOT CAUSE EVIDENCE (QuietBeaver, pane 1). The silent empty/bare-nonzero rch failures are not a flaky daemon; they trace to a permission failure on ONE directory.

CAPTURED FROM 'rch exec -- cargo clippy -p scriptbots-core --all-targets':
  rsync: [receiver] mkstemp "/Users/jemanuel/projects/rust_scriptbots/scenarios/.cooperation_kinship.scenario.toml.MZIagj" failed: Permission denied (13)
  rsync: [receiver] mkstemp ".../scenarios/.drought_recovery.scenario.toml.o7zXXV" failed: Permission denied (13)
  rsync: [receiver] mkstemp ".../scenarios/.islands_closed.scenario.toml.TdU5fa" failed: Permission denied (13)
  rsync: [receiver] mkstemp ".../scenarios/.meadow.scenario.toml.iyyCqY" failed: Permission denied (13)
  rsync: [receiver] mkstemp ".../scenarios/.predator_prey.scenario.toml.yFwN2E" failed: Permission denied (13)
  rsync error: some files/attrs were not transferred (see previous errors) (code 23) at main.c(1338) [sender=3.4.2]
  WARN rch::hook: Remote execution failed: Project sync failed: rsync failed, running locally

Every failing path is under scenarios/. That single failure produces BOTH observed symptoms:
  (a) clippy -> 'rsync failed, running locally' and rch FAILS OPEN into a local build;
  (b) 'cargo test -p scriptbots-core' -> 'mkdir: Permission denied', exit 1 in ~1.4s, no other diagnostic.

DISCRIMINATING OBSERVATION that supports this: 'cargo test -p scriptbots-core --lib -- <filter>'
succeeds remotely EVERY time (three separate runs today, 12/12 and 14/14 passing), while the
unfiltered 'cargo test -p scriptbots-core' fails instantly. The --lib target does not need
scenarios/; the integration-test targets do. So the failure is selective by target, not random.

LIKELY FIX (untested, not attempted by me): correct ownership/permissions of scenarios/ on the
worker(s), so rsync can write its temp files there.

SECOND, SEPARATE DEFECT WORTH ITS OWN DECISION: rch's fail-open. Under the current disk-pressure
policy 'rch first, local only as fallback', a sync failure silently runs the build LOCALLY against
/Volumes/USBNVME16TB/temp_agent_space/cargo-target -- the exact saturated volume the policy exists
to protect. An agent complying with the policy can therefore still land a cold build on that
volume and only discover it by reading a WARN line buried in the tail of the log. A hard-fail mode
on sync failure would make the priority order enforceable rather than advisory.

comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE ISOLATED TO ONE WORKER: vmi1153651. This is not intermittency.

Correlating worker identity against outcome across every rch run I made this session
(10 runs, worker read from the .rch-target-<worker>-pool path and the transfer logs):

  vmi1149989   3 runs   ALL SUCCEEDED

    - cargo test -p scriptbots-core --lib -- <3 filters>   ran to completion
