    - cargo test -p scriptbots-core --test knob_role_...   'mkdir: Permission denied', exit 1
    - cargo clippy -p scriptbots-core --all-targets        rsync scenarios/ Permission denied -> local fallback
    - cargo test -p scriptbots-core (full)                 'mkdir: Permission denied', exit 1

  unknown      2 runs   exit 1 with ZERO bytes (failed before logging a worker; almost
                        certainly the same host)

ZERO exceptions in either direction. Eight of ten runs split perfectly by worker.

THIS REVISES MY EARLIER COMMENT ON THIS BEAD. I previously attributed the failures to the
scenarios/ rsync permission error as though it were a project-wide or pool-wide condition. It is
not: those rsync 'mkstemp .../scenarios/.NAME.scenario.toml.XXXXXX failed: Permission denied (13)'
lines and the bare 'mkdir: Permission denied' are the SAME underlying permission fault, and it
lives on vmi1153651 specifically. The --lib vs --test discrimination I reported was a coincidence
of which worker each invocation happened to land on, NOT a property of the cargo target. I have
since had --lib fail on vmi1153651 and --lib succeed on vmi1149989, which breaks that theory
cleanly.

WHY IT LOOKS LIKE A FLAKY DAEMON: rch load-balances, so an agent gets a coin flip between a good
worker and a broken one. That is exactly the shape of a 40%-ish success rate with no other
pattern, and it is why retrying 'sometimes works'.

SUGGESTED FIX (not attempted by me, no rch config touched): drain or repair vmi1153651 --
correct the ownership/permissions of the checkout root and scenarios/ for the build user there.
If the same fault exists on other pool members, the same correlation method will find them: read
the worker from the .rch-target-<worker>-pool path in the log and bucket by outcome.

LOCALLY (WARN 'Project sync failed: rsync failed, running locally'), against the saturated exFAT

comments.author: QuietBeaver
comments.text:
SECOND BAD WORKER ISOLATED, with the exact failing paths: vmi1156319.

Distinct failure mode from vmi1153651. Reproduced on 5 separate runs today:

  rsync: [generator] failed to set times on ".../rust_scriptbots/.beads/.br_history": Operation not permitted (1)
  rsync: [generator] failed to set times on ".../rust_scriptbots/.beads/.br_recovery": Operation not permitted (1)
  rsync: [generator] failed to set times on ".../rust_scriptbots/captures": Operation not permitted (1)
  rsync error: some files/attrs were not transferred (code 23)
  WARN rch::hook: Remote execution failed: Project sync failed: rsync failed, running locally

The rsync GENERATOR runs on the receiver, so these are stale remote copies of those three paths
whose ownership does not match the build user on that host. It is narrower than a checkout-root
permission problem: only paths that a previous run created as another user fail. Likely fix is
chown of the remote checkout on vmi1156319, or deleting those three stale paths so rsync recreates
them.

RUNNING TALLY across ~25 rch invocations this session, worker read from the
.rch-target-<worker>-pool path:
  vmi1149989  SUCCEEDS
  hz2         SUCCEEDS
  vmi1153651  ALWAYS FAILS - 'mkdir: Permission denied', exit 1 in ~1.4s
  vmi1156319  ALWAYS FAILS - rsync 'failed to set times', then FALLS BACK TO LOCAL
Two of the six pool members are unusable, which matches the ~40% success rate observed at the
swarm level. 'rch status' reports 6/6 healthy throughout: its probe does not exercise write
access to the checkout path, so the pool looks healthy while a third of it is not.

WORTH SEPARATE ATTENTION -- FAIL-OPEN DEFEATS force_remote. The rch config already sets
force_remote = true, yet the vmi1156319 path still logs 'running locally' and executes the build
on the local machine. force_remote is not honoured on the sync-failure branch. Under the current
disk-pressure policy that is actively harmful: an agent instructed to use rch exclusively still
gets a local build on the saturated volume, and only discovers it by reading a WARN line in the
log tail. 'rch exec' also exposes no worker-selection flag, so an agent that lands on a bad worker
cannot steer off it.

PRACTICAL WORKAROUND for other panes until the hosts are fixed: retry and read the worker name out
of the log; a run that names vmi1149989 or hz2 is trustworthy, one that names vmi1153651 or
vmi1156319 is not a real result. Classify by worker before classifying by exit code.

title: index: toroidal delta fails for coordinates more than one extent apart
description: crates/scriptbots-index/src/lib.rs:181-188 adjusts delta by at most one world extent, while rebuild accepts unnormalized coordinates and cell_from_point wraps their bucket coordinates. In a 100x100 world positions (1,50) and (201,50) are the same toroidal point and land in the same wrapped cell, but toroidal_delta returns 100 after one subtraction, so even radius 0 misses. Use a true Euclidean-remainder minimum image or canonicalize/reject coordinates; add translation properties for arbitrary integer multiples of each extent.
close_reason: Completed in 5e49b61c3: f64 canonical minimum-image geometry handles arbitrary whole-extent translations; born-red translation properties added. scriptbots-index 11/11 passed; scriptbots-core 460 passed, 1 unrelated bd-cqja failure, 2 ignored.

title: runtime: driver wait paths consume and drop command ingress
description: crates/scriptbots-runtime/src/channel.rs:596-632. ChannelHostDriver::run waits with receiver.recv()/recv_timeout() after each step but only checks for Disconnected; every Ok(IngressMessage::Command { .. }) is consumed and discarded before drain_ingress can admit it. The dropped reply Sender makes the submitting client observe Disconnected even though its bounded send succeeded, and the command never enters the authoritative lifecycle. Correct behavior must retain or process the exact received message on the owner thread, preserve ordering, and count it once. Add a deterministic paused/WakeOnly threaded regression plus coverage for timed waits.
close_reason: Fixed ChannelHostDriver wait paths to retain the exact received ingress message for ordered admission; added a paused WakeOnly regression covering the command that wakes the owner.

title: AUDIT: two statistics layers — the wired one (analytics) is sound 9/9, the orphaned one (app/lab) fabricates 3 of 6 outputs
description:
Cross-layer audit prompted by bd-h189 (hardcoded p_value). Question asked of every statistic
in both layers: is the value COMPUTED from its inputs, and is it CONSUMED by anything?

HEADLINE, AND IT IS GOOD NEWS FOR REPORTED OUTPUTS: this project has TWO statistics layers.
The one that is wired is sound. The one that is not wired is the unsound one. No number this
project currently reports comes from a fabricated statistic.

  crates/scriptbots-analytics/src/  -- CONSUMED, and uniformly computed. 9/9 genuine.
  crates/scriptbots-app/src/lab/    -- ORPHANED (zero external consumers), and 3 of its 6
                                       outputs are not computed.

LAYER 1: scriptbots-analytics (the wired one)

  function                            computed?                          consumed?
  ----------------------------------  ---------------------------------  ---------
  mean                                computed                           yes
  std_dev                             computed                           yes (18)
  quantile                            computed                           yes (8)
  bootstrap_mean_difference_ci        computed; confidence + n_resamples yes (2)
                                      are PARAMETERS, and the resample
                                      count is recorded in the result
  moving_block_bootstrap_mean_ci      computed; documented rationale     yes (2)
                                      for block resampling preserving
                                      autocorrelation
  permutation_test_mean_difference    computed; applies the              yes (3)
                                      (count + 1)/(n + 1) correction so
                                      a p-value can never be exactly 0
  cohens_d                            computed; degenerate case          yes (13)
                                      handled CORRECTLY (see below)
  cliffs_delta                        computed; genuine pairwise         yes (9)
                                      dominance counting
  distribution summary                computed; constant sample returns  yes
                                      zeros AND sets `degenerate: true`

  Supporting evidence of discipline: 12 finite_guard call sites in stats.rs; the two
  `confidence: 0.95` literals are Default impls for PARAMETER structs (the confidence LEVEL),
  not computed outputs. I checked both -- they are correct.

LAYER 2: scriptbots-app/src/lab/stats.rs (the orphaned one)

  function                            computed?                          consumed?
  ----------------------------------  ---------------------------------  ---------
  paired_diff -> p_value              NOW computed (was 0.05, fixed      orphaned
                                      650e9ec52 under bd-h189)
  paired_diff -> cohens_dz            computed; refuses degenerate       orphaned
                                      spread (c74f30c3e, bd-7453)
  hedges_g -> statistic               computed BUT blanket `else{0.0}`   orphaned
                                      on degenerate spread   -> bd-gbwn
  hedges_g -> ci_95                   CONSTANT: g +/- 1.96*0.1. Width    orphaned
                                      never varies with n or variance
                                                             -> bd-gbwn
  bootstrap_ci                        computed; genuine resampling       orphaned
  adjust_multiple_comparisons         NO-OP: stamps                      orphaned
                                      correction = Some(method) and
                                      adjusts nothing        -> bd-7vdu

DENOMINATOR: 15 statistics audited. 11 genuine, 1 fixed during this session, 3 defective --
and all 3 defective are in the layer nothing consumes.

THE SHARPEST EVIDENCE THAT THIS IS DUPLICATION, NOT IGNORANCE. Cohen's d exists in BOTH
layers. Analytics handles the degenerate case with explicit reasoning:

    if pooled_sd == 0.0 {
        // Both groups are constant. The effect is either zero (equal constants) or infinite
        // (different constants); report 0.0 for equal and a large sentinel for different,
        // rather than dividing by zero.
        return Ok(if (mean(after)? - mean(before)?) == 0.0 { 0.0 } else { f64::INFINITY });
    }

lab/hedges_g returns a blanket 0.0 for both cases -- which reads as "no effect" when the truth
may be an unbounded one. THE CORRECT ANSWER ALREADY EXISTED IN THIS CODEBASE. lab/ is a
parallel reimplementation that is worse, and this is bd-k0wj's drift with a far worse failure
mode: a duplicated CONSTANT diverges into a compile error or a wrong label, a duplicated
STATISTIC diverges into a wrong number that still looks like a number.

RECOMMENDED DISPOSITION (owner's call)
  1. Do not fix lab/stats.rs statistic-by-statistic. It has no consumer (bd-7453 confirms it
     was NEVER wired -- introduced by 8d0e99cfd which added `pub mod stats;` and nothing
     else, and `git log -S "stats::" -- lab/mod.rs` returns no commits ever). Fixing each
     defect preserves a second, weaker implementation of statistics that already exist.
  2. Either delete it, or make it a thin re-export of scriptbots-analytics. The latter needs
     a scriptbots-app -> scriptbots-analytics dependency, which does NOT currently exist and
     is the real blocker on bd-h189's suggested fix.
  3. If it must stay standalone, bd-gbwn and bd-7vdu are the outstanding defects.

WHY THIS WAS INVISIBLE, one mechanism for the whole cluster: with no consumer, nobody ever
ran two datasets through these functions and noticed that a CI width, a p-value, or a
"correction" never changed. Fabricated values are invisible exactly when nothing consumes
them. Compounded by test shape -- bd-16g.1.4 closed claiming "with tests", and those tests
assert that a function RETURNS something rather than asserting WHAT it returns.

AUDIT RULE WORTH KEEPING: for any reported statistic, ask both questions. A statistic that is
computed but unconsumed is dead weight; a statistic that is consumed but constant is a lie
with a decimal point. Only the second is urgent, and this audit found none of them in the
consumed layer.
close_reason: Audit complete and source-reverified at 95359af3d. Corrected durable table is comment 711; current verification comment records computed/reporting paths, public-but-unwired lab surface, and successor defects bd-gbwn, bd-7vdu, and bd-7453. No source change required for this evidence deliverable.

  cliffs_delta                      computed; genuine pairwise        consumed (9)
                                    dominance counting
  compare.rs cohens_dz (inline)     computed; same correct            consumed
                                    degenerate handling as cohens_d
  distribution summary              computed; constant sample         consumed
                                    returns zeros AND sets
                                    `degenerate: true`

  10 statistics. 10 computed. 0 constant.

LAYER 2 -- crates/scriptbots-app/src/lab/stats.rs (NEVER WIRED, see bd-7453)

  paired_diff -> p_value            NOW computed (was 0.05;           orphaned
                                    fixed 650e9ec52, bd-h189)
  paired_diff -> cohens_dz          computed; refuses degenerate      orphaned
                                    spread (c74f30c3e, bd-7453)
  hedges_g -> statistic             computed BUT blanket else{0.0}    orphaned
                                    on degenerate spread -> bd-gbwn
  hedges_g -> ci_95                 CONSTANT: g +/- 1.96*0.1; width   orphaned
                                    never varies with n or variance
                                                          -> bd-gbwn
  bootstrap_ci                      computed; genuine resampling      orphaned (internal only)
  adjust_multiple_comparisons       NO-OP: stamps                     orphaned
                                    correction = Some(method) and
                                    adjusts nothing       -> bd-7vdu

  6 outputs. 3 sound, 3 defective.

TOTALS: 16 statistics audited. 13 genuine, 3 defective, and ALL 3 DEFECTIVE ARE IN THE LAYER
NOTHING CONSUMES. One (bd-h189's p_value) was fixed during this session; one gap in the
consumed layer (no small-sample correction, bd-k3f3) was closed by 6da3a4630.

"ORPHANED" MEANS NO CONSUMERS OUTSIDE ITS OWN MODULE, not none at all -- bootstrap_ci is
called by paired_diff (stats.rs:177) and the test module calls paired_diff and hedges_g. And
lib.rs:3053 declares `pub mod lab;`, so these are part of the crate's PUBLIC API surface:
unreferenced in-workspace is not the same as unreachable.

METHOD AND LIMITS: grep across crates/ plus git pickaxe. Catches direct references; would
miss macro-generated call sites and trait-object dispatch. It produced TWO false positives
during this audit that had to be run down by hand -- `RunSummary` appeared to have 3 external
consumers (a DIFFERENT unit struct in analytics) and `Effect` appeared to have 9 (prose
comments plus an unrelated enum variant). Strong evidence, not proof.

THE CONVENTION THAT MADE LAYER 1 TRUSTWORTHY, worth preserving explicitly: every result type
carries what a reader needs to judge it. ConfidenceInterval reports `confidence` and
`resamples` ("so a reader can judge the Monte-Carlo error of the bounds themselves");
EventCertification reports `n_before`, `n_after` and now `effect_estimator`; PairedComparison
reports `n_pairs`; DistributionSummary reports `n` and a `degenerate` flag. Contrast
lab/hedges_g, which returns g +/- 1.96*0.1 with no n, no confidence level, and no indication
the width is fixed. Same statistic family, opposite discipline -- and the disciplined one is
the one that is wired.

AUDIT RULE: for any reported statistic ask BOTH questions. Computed-but-unconsumed is dead
weight. Consumed-but-constant is a lie with a decimal point. Only the second is urgent, and
this audit found none of them in the consumed layer.

title: storage: AsyncReadLane::close fails with Database(Busy) when a writer is active
description:
crates/scriptbots-storage/src/async_lane.rs:238 AsyncReadLane::close closes with Cx::with_budget(Budget::MINIMAL). Under an actively-writing StoragePipeline that budget is not enough, and closing a READ-ONLY lane returns Err(Database(Busy)).

Observed in crates/scriptbots-storage/tests/async_lane.rs concurrent_lane_readers_observe_commit_boundaries_while_writer_applies_batches, where four reader lanes close while the writer is submitting batches:

  thread '<unnamed>' panicked at tests/async_lane.rs:288:30:
  reader lane closes: Database(Busy)
  thread '...' panicked at tests/async_lane.rs:303:34: reader joins: Any { .. }

TIMING-DEPENDENT, which is why it needs a bead rather than a quick tweak: the same test PASSES when the whole file runs (2 passed, 2 ignored) and FAILS when run alone with a filter. Different scheduling, different contention window.

Why this is a product issue and not just a test issue: a lane is the control-plane read path for GUI/TUI/API consumers. A consumer closing its lane should not fail because some other connection is mid-commit — there is nothing to contend over, the lane holds no write intent. Budget::MINIMAL gives close no room to make progress, so the failure surfaces to a caller that has no sensible recovery other than retrying a close.

Cannot attribute to my change: this test had never executed before, because it was blocked by the stale-sidecar refusal now fixed under bd-jjxe (004a12110). Unblocking it is what exposed this. The seeding rework I made (baseline written through the pipeline rather than a separate Storage, required because a new run refuses an existing database path) changes contention timing but not reader lifecycle, and the failure is in lane.close(), not in any assertion the test is about.

Same shape as bd-aj12: fixing a fixture defect revealed a real defect underneath it.

Fix direction: give close a bounded budget with retry rather than MINIMAL, or make a read-only close non-contending. Then un-ignore the concurrent test — it is correct as written.
close_reason:
Fixed in 870e525ab. Root cause was neither of the two obvious readings.

AsyncReadLane::close called AsyncConnection::close, whose worker runs Connection::close_in_place = close_internal(best_effort: false, checkpoint_on_close: true), which attempts a passive WAL checkpoint (the engine's own comment at fsqlite/src/async_api.rs:206 says so). That is a WRITE, performed for a lane that has never written anything, so under an active StoragePipeline it returns Busy.

Worse than a spurious error: with best_effort false the ? propagates BEFORE release_connection (fsqlite-core/src/connection.rs:14384-14403), so a Busy close also left the connection unreleased. A leak, not a complaint.

Not 'close racing a writer it should wait for': it needed nothing from the writer. Not 'caller wrong to close while work is outstanding': closing a read lane during a write is entirely legitimate. It was close attempting work it had no business doing.

The engine skips the checkpoint when pager.is_readonly(), which is what this lane morally is, but the async API has no read-only open — ConnectionEnv carries no such flag — so the handle cannot be opened that way.

Fix: teardown drops instead. AsyncConnection::drop sends Command::Shutdown and joins the worker; the worker's Connection::drop runs close_internal(best_effort: true, checkpoint_on_close: false) — no checkpoint to contend over, and it still reaches release_connection, so teardown always completes. That is a property the checkpointing path could not offer even on success.

Rejected alternatives, both explicitly: awaiting quiescence would make a read-only teardown block on an unrelated writer, and a blocking close needs a bound the engine cannot enforce (bd-aj12), rebuilding that hang in teardown. A retry loop would retry work the lane should never attempt, papering over the real problem.

concurrent_lane_readers_observe_commit_boundaries_while_writer_applies_batches is un-ignored as the regression guard — four readers closing against a live writer is the contended teardown that reproduced this. Verified: the isolated invocation that previously failed (--test-threads=1 concurrent_lane) now passes; full file 2 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored.

title: storage: orphaned journal.rs edit weakens a determinism assertion to accept a blocker the precedence chain cannot produce
description:
Uncommitted working-tree edit in crates/scriptbots-storage/src/journal.rs (dated 07-23, from a session that never returned) widens two assertions in the receipt-timeout test:

  assert_eq!(blocked.blocker, Some(HostBlocker::ScientificFault))
    -> assert!(matches!(blocked.blocker, Some(JournalClosed{..}) | Some(ScientificFault)))
  assert_eq!(second_status.journal(), &JournalState::Pending)
    -> match { Pending => {}, Failed(f) => assert_eq!(f.code, "journal_closed"), .. }

The test's own expect message says the latched failure rejects later science DETERMINISTICALLY, and HostCore::current_blocker (crates/scriptbots-runtime/src/host_core.rs:1964) is a const fn with strict precedence: retained_blocker, then event_pressure, then health.blocker(), then ScientificFault. Exactly one answer is possible for a given state; there is no branch that could return either.

retained_blocker is set only by fail_closed_batch (host_core.rs:1727), which also writes the journal_closed failure code. The test asserts just above that core.pending_journal_batch().is_none() and retry_retained_journal() is None on this accepted-timeout path, i.e. fail_closed_batch did not run, so the blocker should be exactly ScientificFault and the journal state exactly Pending. Accepting the JournalClosed/journal_closed alternative therefore admits an outcome this scenario cannot legitimately produce, and would hide a regression where a receipt timeout starts latching a retained blocker.

VioletCoast/cc_2 left the file uncommitted rather than landing the weakening under a recovery commit. Resolve by restoring the two exact assertions and confirming they pass; if they do not pass, the nondeterminism is a real host defect and should be raised to P1 rather than absorbed into the test.
notes:
Tried to settle this empirically: put both strict assertions back (assert_eq on blocked.blocker == Some(HostBlocker::ScientificFault), and assert_eq on second_status.journal() == JournalState::Pending) in stuck_live_worker_times_out_once_releases_batch_and_stops_later_science, intending to commit the strict form if it passed and escalate to P1 if it did not. Could not get a build: rch returned exit 1 with zero bytes on four consecutive attempts across --lib, --lib with a filter, and whole-crate forms. Put journal.rs back byte-for-byte to the orphaned state rather than leave a self-modified untested file in the shared tree; git diff is again exactly the original 9-insert/2-delete orphan diff.

Resolution is one test run: apply the two strict assertions and run cargo test -p scriptbots-storage --lib stuck_live_worker. If it passes, commit the strict form and close this. If it fails, HostCore::current_blocker's strict precedence (retained_blocker, then event_pressure, then health.blocker(), then ScientificFault) means the host is returning a blocker this accepted-timeout path should not be able to produce, which is a real defect and this should go to P1 rather than be absorbed into the test.
close_reason:
Settled empirically in d14bc2133 rather than by inspection. Put the strict ScientificFault assertion back and ran it: left = Some(JournalClosed { batch_id: ... sequence: 2 }), right = Some(ScientificFault). The receipt timeout runs fail_closed_batch, which latches retained_blocker and writes the journal_closed failure; the accepted timed-out batch leaves no retryable retained batch (which is what made ScientificFault look correct) but the blocker latch is separate state and persists. HostCore::current_blocker checks retained_blocker first, so JournalClosed preempts the ScientificFault fallback arm and the journal axis is Failed, not Pending.

Both prior forms were wrong. The committed assert_eq against ScientificFault was stale and has been failing on main — that is what the orphaned session was actually fixing. Its accept-either widening did make it pass but admitted an outcome that would hide a regression in either direction. Now pinned to the single correct variant per axis (matches! on JournalClosed, and on Failed with code journal_closed) with the precedence reasoning recorded inline. My original bead analysis was right that accept-either was wrong and wrong about which single answer is correct. Verified: cargo test -p scriptbots-storage --lib stuck_live_worker = 1 passed, 0 failed.

title: Shared git index across six agents: one agent's staged files get swept into another agent's commit
description:
UPDATE 2 (2026-07-25, cc_1/CopperCat): a pathspec commit can be ATOMIC AND STILL WRONG.
The existing note treats this bead as an attribution problem. It is not only that.

THIRD INCIDENT, AND THE WORST ONE
A peer pathspec commit captured cc_1's HALF-FINISHED edit of the bd-7u5a diagnostic
facade and shipped it to main. HEAD's four forwarding arms read:

    ($($arg:tt)*) => { ::diag_error!($($arg)*) };   // lib.rs:29
    ($($arg:tt)*) => { ::diag_warn!($($arg)*) };    // lib.rs:38
    ($($arg:tt)*) => { ::diag_info!($($arg)*) };    // lib.rs:47
    ($($arg:tt)*) => { ::diag_debug!($($arg)*) };   // lib.rs:56

Each should forward to `::tracing::<level>!`. As committed they are self-referential,
so `scriptbots-core` DOES NOT COMPILE off-wasm: 4x E0433. Verified independently by
the orchestrator. The repair existed in cc_1's working tree at the moment of capture
but had not been committed yet.

WHY THIS IS A DIFFERENT FAILURE FROM THE FIRST TWO
137e3bdb4 (60 lines of core) and 48c87cb2b (109 lines of brain-neuro) absorbed peer
work that was COMPLETE and WORKING. The damage was bookkeeping: right code, wrong
commit message. Here the captured content was mid-repair, so the damage is a BROKEN
BUILD ON MAIN. Same mechanism, categorically worse outcome.

THE PRECISE DISTINCTION TO RECORD
  pathspec (`git commit -m MSG -- <paths>`) protects the INDEX from peers: it builds a
  temporary index from the named paths and ignores whatever else is staged. It does NOT
  protect the WORKING TREE: it commits whatever those paths currently contain. So a
  pathspec commit is atomic with respect to the index and still arbitrary with respect
  to time -- it faithfully ships whatever half-written state a peer happens to be in.
An agent following the rule perfectly can therefore still publish a broken build that
is not theirs, and will not notice, because the content compiles in THEIR context.

SECOND LESSON, FROM THE SAME INCIDENT: PER-TARGET VERIFICATION IS NOT OPTIONAL
The broken state passed `cargo check -p scriptbots-web --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`
cleanly, because the broken arm is `#[cfg(not(wasm32))]` and is compiled out there. A
wasm-only check would have certified a commit that cannot build natively. The bd-7u5a
commit message predicted this outcome in the abstract; it then happened for real,
within minutes, to that same change. Neither target substitutes for the other, IN
EITHER DIRECTION.

MITIGATION, revised and ordered
  1. DIFF BEFORE YOU COMMIT A SHARED FILE. `git diff -- <file>` and confirm every hunk
     is yours. This is still the cheapest guard and it catches both mechanisms.
  2. DO NOT COMMIT A SHARED FILE WHILE ANOTHER AGENT IS MID-EDIT IN IT. A live
     reservation held by someone else is the signal; if the guard refuses you, that is
     the system working, not an obstacle to route around.
  3. KEEP EDIT WINDOWS SHORT. The exposure is the interval between "file is
     inconsistent" and "repair is committed". cc_1's window here was about two minutes
     and that was enough.
  4. VERIFY EVERY TARGET THE CHANGE TOUCHES before committing, not just the convenient
     one.
  5. Private worktrees remain the only structural fix for the working-tree half.
     Rejected for this session (six agents mid-flight, separate target dirs, ~11% disk);
     correct call, but record it as the option for a session that STARTS clean.
close_reason: Implemented and installed the immutable reviewed-tree protocol in scripts/shared_tree_commit.py: review_candidate freezes a fresh private-index tree, commit_review enforces mutex plus stale-HEAD/tree/path/message checks, hook_check blocks raw commits, and self_test proves index isolation, frozen bytes, stale rejection, tamper rejection, and hook composition; AGENTS.md now mandates the commands. Landed as a639287fa.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: ORCHESTRATOR VERIFICATION - CONFIRMED, with evidence. 137e3bdb4 ('refactor(storage,app): converge the two competing run-bundle implementations on RunBundleV1 (bd-4d9j)', VioletCoast/cc_2) contains crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs with 60 changed lines. That file is cc_1/CopperCat's bd-dz37 work. So cc_1's staged content was committed under cc_2's commit message. Full file list of 137e3bdb4: experiment_runner.rs, core/src/lib.rs, storage/src/bundle.rs, storage/src/export_pipeline.rs, storage/src/lib.rs. Only the storage/app files belong to bd-4d9j. IMPACT: work is not lost, but (1) the commit message does not describe the core change, (2) bead traceability is broken - bd-dz37 work now lives inside a bd-4d9j commit, and (3) reverting bd-4d9j would also revert unrelated determinism work in core. CONSEQUENCE FOR POLICY: 'stage only your own files' is INSUFFICIENT as a rule, because .git/index is itself shared mutable state - an agent can follow that rule perfectly and still have its content swept into a peer's commit, or lose its staged set when a peer commits. MITIGATION BROADCAST TO SWARM: use the pathspec form 'git commit -m MSG -- <explicit paths>', which commits the named paths from the working tree using a temporary index and ignores whatever else is staged. STRUCTURAL FIX for consideration: per-agent GIT_INDEX_FILE, git worktrees per agent, or a commit mutex.

comments.text: IMPLEMENTED WORKING PROTOCOL (a639287fa). scripts/shared_tree_commit.py now freezes each declared path set into a fresh private index based on a recorded HEAD, prints the complete binary/full-index diff, and binds an explicit review token to agent + base tree + candidate tree + literal paths + commit message. title: brain-neuro: zero mutation scale still perturbs selected weights
description: crates/scriptbots-brain-neuro/src/lib.rs:746 computes sigma as scale.max(1e-5). With rate > 0 and scale == 0.0, every selected weight receives a nonzero Gaussian perturbation even though the mutation magnitude is explicitly zero. This violates the zero-magnitude metamorphic identity enforced by FtBrain and the C++-derived randn(0, MR2) semantics, and can silently change scientific heredity when users set mutation.secondary to zero. Correct behavior: preserve the exact network at zero scale while retaining the documented deterministic RNG draw schedule; add a regression test that compares serialized state bit-for-bit and checks continuation.
close_reason: Implemented exact zero-scale identity while preserving the deterministic per-weight RNG draw schedule; added byte-exact state and continuation regression coverage. rustfmt/diff checks pass. Scoped RCH execution was attempted repeatedly with the required plain command but the installed helper normalized this checkout outside its canonical root and tried local fallback, which was interrupted before Cargo ran.

title: app/terminal: hover tooltip labels a reusable slotmap key as an AgentUid, and shows a different number than the brain panel for the same agent
description:
Hit while wiring the canvas selection ring for bd-2z0.14.2.1. The TUI carries TWO agent
identities and displays them interchangeably; one of the two labels is wrong.

THE MISMATCH

  crates/scriptbots-app/src/terminal/mod.rs:3716
      AgentViz { id: id.data().as_ffi(), .. }
    AgentViz.id is the SLOTMAP KEY's FFI encoding - a physical handle.

  crates/scriptbots-app/src/terminal/mod.rs:2265
      self.hover_tooltip = Some(MouseHoverTooltip { agent_uid: agent.id, .. })
    The field is NAMED agent_uid and is fed the slot key.

  crates/scriptbots-app/src/terminal/mod.rs:2394
      format!(" Agent #{} ", tooltip.agent_uid)
    Rendered to the user as the agent's identity.

  crates/scriptbots-app/src/terminal/mod.rs:2802
      snap.focused_agent_uid = Some(agent_uid.get())   // via world.agent_uid(id)
    The brain/insights panel's "uid N" is the REAL stable AgentUid.

So hovering an agent and focusing the same agent show two different numbers, and the one
labelled uid in the tooltip is not a uid.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND COSMETICS. AGENTS.md is explicit that these are two identity layers and
that AgentUid is 'the stable scientific identity used by digests, lineage, replay, and
persistence', while AgentId is a generational handle whose slots are REUSED after death. A
slot key is therefore not stable across a run: note an agent as 'Agent #5' from the tooltip,
let it die, and a later unrelated agent can be presented under the same number. An
experimenter correlating a tooltip observation against a persisted uid, a digest, or a replay
is silently correlating against the wrong identity. This is precisely the confusion the two
layers exist to prevent.

SCOPE OF THE FIX. Give AgentViz the stable uid alongside its handle - world.agent_uid(id) is
already in scope at the snapshot build site - and have the tooltip render that. Rename
MouseHoverTooltip.agent_uid only if it keeps carrying a uid; if a caller genuinely needs the
slot handle, name that field for what it is. Do not just rename the field and leave the slot
key flowing into it.

BLOCKS: the bd-2z0.14.2.1 selection ring. The canvas paints from AgentViz, focus is tracked as
focused_agent_uid, and with no shared identity between them the ring cannot be matched to a
dot without an identity comparison that is wrong by construction. Filing rather than widening
that bead, because the correct fix touches the snapshot builder and the tooltip contract,
which is a different surface from the canvas painter.

Found by YellowLake (pane 3). Not fixed in place because the snapshot builder is shared
surface and the rename has callers; wanted it recorded with exact line evidence first.
close_reason: Fixed in 68e0043d3. AgentViz now carries the stable AgentUid alongside the arena handle; every user-facing identity (hover tooltip, click-select toast, Top Predators and Oldest Agents rows) renders the uid, while the handle is retained only where focus-lock resolves a row back to a live agent. LeaderboardEntry.label was doing double duty as both display text and lookup key and is now split into handle + uid. A missing uid renders as '?' rather than 0, so an invariant violation stays visible instead of being presented as agent zero. Two tests: displayed_agent_identity_is_the_stable_uid_not_the_arena_handle drives a real 3-agent world and asserts every AgentViz and every leaderboard row carries the arena's own uid for the agent that row resolves to; a_missing_agent_identity_renders_as_a_visible_placeholder pins the placeholder. title: storage: watermark monotonicity is spot-checked, never proven across a full failure+recovery lifecycle
description: AGENTS.md storage contract: three separate monotonic watermarks (admitted/applied/durable). PersistenceWatermarks::from_raw (lib.rs:3327) enforces durable<=applied<=admitted on every READ, but no test observes the triple at every boundary of one lifecycle and proves it never regresses componentwise. Existing coverage checks single endpoints: lib.rs:19563 public_file_persist_preserves_one_identity_and_monotonic_watermarks compares a few discrete snapshots; durability_proofs.rs:687 asserts only final convergence. A regression that briefly published a lower applied/durable between two of those checkpoints would go unseen. Correct: a witness that records every observation across create->persist->flush->close->reopen->duplicate->conflict-refusal->reopen and asserts ordering plus componentwise non-decrease at each step.
close_reason: Added WatermarkWitness + watermarks_stay_ordered_and_never_regress_across_refusal_and_recovery to durability_proofs.rs. The witness records all 11 watermark observations of one lifecycle (fresh -> 3 admissions -> flush -> exact duplicate -> conflicting-payload refusal -> post-refusal admit/flush -> close -> StoragePipeline::recover_existing shutdown -> StorageReader) and asserts durable<=applied<=admitted within every observation plus componentwise non-decrease between consecutive ones. Also pins that admission is not application (applied stays None after 3 admissions) and that neither the duplicate nor the refusal moves any watermark or adds a scientific row. Verified: 10/10 pass.

comments.text:
PROGRESS: 5 of the contract items are landed across two commits. Bead stays OPEN.

LANDED IN b2973fa5f (verified 10 passed / 0 failed, rch worker vmi1149989):

1. REMOVED THE FORBIDDEN SMALL-N I.I.D.-SHUFFLE FALLBACK, in both compute_mi and compute_te.
   Both now return a typed InfoTheoryError::SurrogateInfeasible instead. The two nulls are not
   interchangeable: a circular shift preserves each series' autocorrelation and destroys only the
   cross-series alignment, so it asks "is this dependence more than the series' own structure
   explains". A shuffle destroys the autocorrelation too, narrowing the null and making the
   p-value anti-conservative -- it manufactures significance for autocorrelated signals, which is
   the population-dynamics case this module exists to measure. The substitution was also silent
   and sample-size-dependent, so the p-value's meaning changed on a branch no caller could see.

2. TE BIN VALIDATION BEFORE DENSE ALLOCATION. calc_te_mm builds a dense bins^3 histogram and
   compute_te never range-checked bins, despite being the path that cubes it: bins = 1024 asks for
   a billion cells from caller-supplied input. compute_mi already enforced 2..=32; compute_te now
   enforces the same, BEFORE anything allocates. Constant MAX_ESTIMATOR_BINS.

3. CORRECTED A MISLEADING ERROR PAYLOAD. compute_te's short-input guard reported
   need: bins^3 * 5 (2560 at default bins) when it actually needed 2. It now reports the real
   requirement, derived from the surrogate constraint via MIN_CIRCULAR_SURROGATE_SAMPLES = 3
   (the shift range max(n/10,1)..=n-max(n/10,1) is empty until n > 2).

4. FOUR NEGATIVE TESTS, including a boundary test asserting that three samples ARE accepted. A
   refusal guard that over-refuses is its own defect, so the boundary is pinned from both sides.

LANDED IN 10d4d402c (verified 11 passed / 0 failed, rch worker vmi1149989):

comments.author: QuietBeaver
comments.text:
HANDOFF NOTES for WindySquirrel -- the five things in my two commits that are NOT obvious from the diff and that a reasonable cleanup would undo.

1. THE SURROGATE NULL IS A POSITIONAL ARGUMENT, NOT A MiParams FIELD, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE.
   compute_mi_with_surrogate takes SurrogateKind as an argument; compute_mi is the safe default.
   I built it as a MiParams field first and reverted. Two reasons: it would have churned 17
   existing struct literals, and more importantly choosing PairingPermutation is a scientific
   ASSERTION THAT THE SAMPLES ARE I.I.D. An assertion that consequential belongs where a reader
   can see it -- at the call site -- not defaulting silently inside a struct literal three scopes
   away. Moving it into MiParams 'for consistency' would quietly restore the failure mode the
   bead is about.

2. THE OPT-IN PERMUTATION NULL IS NOT A REVERSAL OF THE SHUFFLE-NULL REMOVAL, THOUGH IT LOOKS
   LIKE ONE. What b2973fa5f removed was a SILENT, SAMPLE-SIZE-DEPENDENT substitution: below a
   length threshold the estimator swapped the null without telling anyone, so a p-value's meaning
   changed on a branch no caller could see. What 106b73d66 adds is the same technique made
   explicit, caller-chosen, unconditional, and RECORDED on the estimate as surrogate_kind. The
   defect was the silence, never the technique. Both facts are documented on the SurrogateKind
   enum so this cannot be 'simplified' back.

3. compute_te REFUSES PairingPermutation with a typed SurrogateUnsupported rather than falling
   back to a circular shift. Transfer entropy is a statement about temporal structure and a
   pairing permutation destroys exactly that, so the result would not be a null for the quantity
   being measured. I added compute_te_with_surrogate specifically so that refusal is REACHABLE
   AND TESTED rather than an unexercisable comment.

4. USE bits_corrected_unclamped, NEVER bits_corrected, FOR ANY BIAS FIGURE. On independent noise
   the floored mean is 0.0398 versus 0.0325 unclamped, with 29 of 100 runs truncated at the zero
   floor. A bias number taken from the floored field measures truncation, not bias. This matters
   directly for the communication study if it reports MI on channels that are near-independent
   under the null. Note also that the surrogate and bootstrap sites clamp EXPLICITLY, so exposing
   the raw value moved no p-value and no confidence interval by a single bit -- keep that property
   if you touch those loops.

5. DO NOT RELAX bd_r4ja_iid_shuffle_null_manufactures_significance_the_circular_null_avoids. It
   asserts the shuffle null returns p < 0.05 on genuinely INDEPENDENT AR(1) series -- it is
   supposed to be wrong, and the test proves the anti-conservatism rather than asserting it. If
   that assertion ever fails, the fixture has stopped demonstrating the trap and needs REBUILDING,
   not loosening. The failure message says so, but it is the kind of thing that gets 'fixed' at
   3am.

One correction I already posted on bd-270k and repeat here because it bears on any bias work: I

title: storage: async_lane cancellation and deadline tests cannot fire — recursive-CTE fixture is capped at 1000 rows by the engine
description:
crates/scriptbots-storage/tests/async_lane.rs cancelled_query_surfaces_typed_interrupt_and_lane_recovers and sub_ms_deadline_expires_a_slow_query both build their slow workload as WITH RECURSIVE cnt(x) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT x+1 FROM cnt LIMIT 5000000/8000000) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cnt.

The pinned FrankenSQLite caps recursion at RECURSIVE_CTE_MAX_RECURSION = 1000 (fsqlite-core/src/connection.rs:785, applied at 57865, 57926, 58904), so both queries return COUNT(*) = 1001 in microseconds. The observed failures are literally 'a cancelled slow query must not complete: [Row { values: [Integer(1001)] }]' — the query finished before cancel() or the 1 ms deadline could matter.

This is NOT evidence that lane cancellation or deadline enforcement is broken. It is evidence that neither has ever been exercised: the tests have been asserting against an instant query. AsyncReadLane's whole purpose (bd-2z0.8.9.12) is to keep a slow read off a UI path under a bounded deadline, and that bound is currently unproven in both directions.

Both are marked #[ignore] with this bead id in the attribute so the suite stays green and the gap stays visible. Fix: replace the recursive CTE with a workload that is genuinely slow on this engine — e.g. a wide self-join over a fixture large enough that the row count dominates (write_fixture writes 2 rows per tick, so a 3-way join over a few hundred ticks is millions of combinations) — then confirm the typed FrankenError::Interrupt actually arrives and un-ignore.
notes:
FIXTURE FIXED AND LANDED in 98d67daea. The recursive CTE is gone; both tests now run a measured self-join. Remaining work is one verification run, then delete two #[ignore] attributes.

Measured on the pinned engine (rch worker), ~80k row-combinations/sec:
  metric rows | join  | combinations | elapsed
  40          | 3-way | 64k          |  0.86 s
  80          | 3-way | 512k         |  6.3 s
  40          | 4-way | 2.6M         | 49.7 s

Chose 80 rows (SLOW_FIXTURE_TICKS = 40, two metrics per tick) at 3-way: ~6.3 s is thousands of times the 1 ms deadline and ~126x the 50 ms cancellation delay, while short enough that a FAILED interrupt ends the test in seconds rather than hanging the suite. Assertion changed from elapsed < 30s (which an instant 1001-row query passed trivially) to elapsed < 3s, which separates a working interrupt (milliseconds) from a broken one (~6.3 s).

WHY STILL IGNORED: rch refused ten consecutive dispatches with 'no admissible workers' (composition varied: insufficient_slots, hard_preflight, active_project_exclusion — see bd-oite). Whether lane cancellation and deadline enforcement actually work is exactly the open question, so un-ignoring unverified is a coin flip on turning cargo test -p scriptbots-storage red for every other agent. cargo check -p scriptbots-storage --all-targets is clean (0 errors) so this compiles; only runtime behaviour is unknown.

TO FINISH (one line each): delete the #[ignore] on cancelled_query_surfaces_typed_interrupt_and_lane_recovers and sub_ms_deadline_expires_a_slow_query, run cargo test -p scriptbots-storage --test async_lane. If they pass, close this bead. If they fail, the fixture is no longer the suspect — AsyncReadLane is not enforcing its bounds, which is a P1 for a lane whose entire purpose (bd-2z0.8.9.12) is keeping a slow read off a UI path; file that separately rather than re-ignoring.
close_reason:
Fixture defect fixed in 98d67daea; follow-through in 18804d9e7. The recursive CTE (truncated to 1001 rows by RECURSIVE_CTE_MAX_RECURSION) is replaced with a measured self-join: 80 metric rows at 3-way = 512k combinations = ~6.3s, chosen from a real timing table so a 50ms cancel and a 1ms deadline have thousands of times the room they need, while a failed interrupt still ends the test in seconds rather than hanging the suite. Assertion tightened from elapsed<30s (which an instant query passed trivially) to elapsed<3s.

The fix did its job: running the honest fixture proved AsyncReadLane enforces NEITHER cancellation NOR deadlines — both tests returned COUNT(*)=512000, the complete join, and suite runtime went 1.23s to 23.10s confirming the queries genuinely ran. Filed as bd-aj12 (P1) with the root cause: fsqlite async_api.rs:423 checks the Cx once at entry, then executes on a worker thread holding no reference to it.

Both tests are now ignored against bd-aj12 rather than this bead, with reasons saying they are correct and fail against that defect, so nobody is sent to a closed bead. They will pass unchanged once the bound is enforced. Closing this: the fixture is no longer the suspect, which is exactly what this bead asked for.

title: pre-commit chain hard-fails without AGENT_NAME, so every commit-time guard is skipped or bypassed
description:
Found while wiring the bd-emmm close-reason guard into .git/hooks/hooks.d/pre-commit/.

The mcp-agent-mail chain-runner at .git/hooks/pre-commit runs every executable in .git/hooks/hooks.d/pre-commit/ in sorted name order and aborts on the first nonzero exit. The first plugin, 50-agent-mail.py, exits 2 with 'mcp-agent-mail: AGENT_NAME environment variable is required.' when AGENT_NAME is unset.

Reproduce:
  env -u AGENT_NAME .git/hooks/pre-commit   -> exit 2, no plugin after agent-mail runs
  AGENT_NAME=AmberFalcon .git/hooks/pre-commit -> exit 0, all plugins run

Consequences, both bad:
1. An agent whose shell lacks AGENT_NAME cannot commit at all through the normal path, so it reaches for 'git commit --no-verify' - which skips BOTH the file-reservation guard and the close-reason guard. The guards are then decorative.
2. Any plugin sorting after 50-agent-mail.py (including 50-close-reason-guard) never executes in that state, silently. Nothing reports that a guard was skipped.

Claude Code Bash tool sessions do NOT have AGENT_NAME exported by default - confirmed unset in this pane - so this is the default condition, not an edge case.

Correct fix is one of: (a) have the agent-mail plugin treat a missing AGENT_NAME as 'not an agent commit' and exit 0 rather than 2; (b) export AGENT_NAME from the swarm launcher into every pane; or (c) have the chain-runner continue past a plugin that reports 'not applicable' while still failing on real findings. (a) or (b) is preferable - silently continuing past errors is how we got here.

Cross-refs: undermines bd-emmm (guard is only continuous if the chain runs) and bd-qsi4 (shared git index - the reservation guard is the mitigation being bypassed).

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
Also affects pre-push, not just pre-commit. 'git push origin main:master' with AGENT_NAME unset fails with the same 'mcp-agent-mail: AGENT_NAME environment variable is required.' and refuses the push ('failed to push some refs'). The chain-runner pattern is duplicated at .git/hooks/pre-push with its own hooks.d/pre-push directory, so the fix has to cover both.

Note the failure mode is especially misleading here: git reports 'failed to push some refs to <url>', which reads as a remote/network or non-fast-forward problem. Nothing in that message points at a local hook or at AGENT_NAME.

title: core heredity: every mutation draws uniformly where C++ draws from a Gaussian (randn), so no same-seed differential is possible
description:
Found by QuietBeaver while implementing bd-hgxt. This is the largest of the heredity parity divergences found today and it subsumes part of what bd-fba5 and bd-hgxt were trying to achieve.

THE DIVERGENCE: C++ mutates with a GAUSSIAN variate; the Rust port mutates with a UNIFORM one.

REFERENCE (original_scriptbots_code_for_reference/helpers.h):
  //normalvariate random N(mu, sigma)
  inline double randn(double mu, double sigma) { ...Marsaglia polar method... }
Every per-gene mutation in Agent::reproduce calls randn(value, sigma) -- clocks (112, 114), the
five sensory modifiers (122-126), eye FOV (131), eye direction (134), herbivore (111) and
temperature (139).

RUST (crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs, WorldState::mutate_value):
  let delta = rng.random_range(-scale..scale);
  (value + delta).clamp(min, max)
A uniform draw on a closed interval. Every mutation in the port goes through this, so the
divergence is total rather than per-gene.

WHY IT MATTERS, in order of importance:

1. DIFFERENT EVOLUTIONARY DYNAMICS. A Gaussian has unbounded tails: rare large jumps are possible
   and are precisely what lets a population escape a local optimum. A uniform draw is hard-bounded
   at +/-scale and can never produce them. Two populations under these two schemes explore the
   fitness landscape differently, which is a scientific difference, not an implementation detail.

2. SIGMA AND HALF-WIDTH ARE NOT THE SAME QUANTITY. For the uniform draw the standard deviation is
   scale/sqrt(3) ~= 0.577*scale, so reusing a C++ sigma as a Rust half-width silently narrows the
   spread to about 58% of the reference. bd-hgxt adopted 0.03 and 0.005 from Agent.cpp:111 and 139
   for exactly this reason and documented the caveat at the constant definitions -- those constants
   are in the right RANGE but are not the reference distribution.

3. IT BLOCKS THE SAME-SEED DIFFERENTIAL. bd-fba5 fixed the draw ORDER and bd-hgxt fixed the draw
   COUNT for the two unconditional genes, both toward making a same-seed comparison against the C++
   reference possible. Neither achieves it while the distribution differs. THIS IS A CORRECTION TO
   MY OWN EARLIER CLAIM on bd-fba5, where I wrote that the stream would match bit-for-bit once
   bd-hgxt landed. It will not.

4. THE DRAW ACCOUNTING ALSO DIFFERS, and awkwardly. C++ randn caches its second polar deviate in
   function-local statics (deviateAvailable / storedDeviate), so consecutive calls alternate:
   the first consumes at least two rand() values through a rejection loop, the next consumes none.
   A faithful port therefore cannot be a stateless per-call helper -- the generator state has to
   carry the stored deviate, and the rejection loop's variable consumption has to be reproduced.
   That statefulness is also a cross-agent hazard in the original: the cached deviate leaks between
   whichever agents reproduce consecutively.

SCOPE: this is deliberately NOT folded into bd-fba5 or bd-hgxt. It changes every mutation in the
simulation, it needs a decision about whether to reproduce randn's cached-deviate statefulness
exactly or only its distribution, and it will shift WorldDigestV1 again.

ACCEPTANCE: (1) decide explicitly whether the port adopts the Gaussian, including whether it
reproduces the cached-deviate behaviour or uses a stateless normal draw and accepts a stream that
is distributionally but not bitwise identical; (2) if adopting, implement it in mutate_value and
its gated variants so every gene inherits it; (3) extend
bd_fba5_draw_order_matches_the_cpp_reference to pin the distribution as well as the order;
(4) coordinate the golden re-bless with bd-fba5 and bd-hgxt so one DSR pass covers all three.

GOLDENS: same set as bd-fba5 -- WorldDigestV1 consumers, checkpoint wire, heredity_proof.rs,
rng_sequence_compat.rs, scene goldens, and the perf baseline if a Gaussian draw measurably changes
tick cost (it may: the polar method has a rejection loop).
close_reason:
Fixed in 54619f802b8f. This was the BLOCKER of the three parity findings, and it is worth being
precise about why: bd-fba5 (order) and bd-hgxt (count and scale) were necessary but not sufficient.
Order and scale are alignment problems -- given the right sequence and the right sigma, two streams
can in principle be compared. A DIFFERENT DISTRIBUTION is not an alignment problem. No amount of
seed alignment makes a uniform draw reproduce a Gaussian one, so the parity oracle could not work
at all until this landed, and any same-seed differential against the reference was meaningless.

C++ randn CALL SITES (original_scriptbots_code_for_reference)
  helpers.h            inline double randn(double mu, double sigma)  -- Marsaglia polar
  Agent.cpp:107,108    MUTRATE1 / MUTRATE2 meta-mutation
  Agent.cpp:111        herbivore
  Agent.cpp:112,114    clockf1 / clockf2
  Agent.cpp:122-126    smellmod, soundmod, hearmod, eyesensmod, bloodmod
  Agent.cpp:131        eyefov[i]
  Agent.cpp:134        eyedir[i]
  Agent.cpp:139        temperature_preference
Every per-gene mutation in Agent::reproduce is a randn call. randf is used ONLY for the
`randf(0,1) < MR*5` gates, never for a mutation magnitude.

RUST UNIFORM SITES NOW CONVERTED (crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs)
  WorldState::mutate_value          was rng.random_range(-scale..scale)
                                    now normal_deviate(rng, scale)
                                    -- this alone covers clocks, all five modifiers, eye FOV,
                                       herbivore and temperature, since they all route through it
  meta-mutation delta_primary       was random_range(-meta_scale..meta_scale) -> normal_deviate
  meta-mutation delta_secondary     same
  eye_direction delta               was random_range(-mutation_scale..mutation_scale) -> normal_deviate

DECISION: implement the Gaussian, using C++'s own Marsaglia polar algorithm including the rejection
loop, so the shape and the tails match rather than approximating with Box-Muller.

TWO DELIBERATE DEPARTURES, both documented at normal_deviate:

1. NO CACHED DEVIATE. C++ randn keeps storedDeviate/deviateAvailable in function-local statics, so
   consecutive calls alternate: one runs the rejection loop, the next consumes nothing and returns
   the cached partner. That cache is process-global and shared by every caller including brain
   mutation, so it leaks across whichever agents reproduce consecutively. This port deliberately
   isolates each birth in its own offspring_substream; a global cache would undo exactly that, and
   it is the same class of hidden cross-agent coupling bd-dz37 removed a thread_local to eliminate.
   Each call here runs its own loop and discards the second deviate.

2. BIT-EXACT PARITY IS UNREACHABLE ANYWAY, so it is not the target. C++ draws from C rand(); this
   port draws from a project-owned Xoshiro256++. No algorithm matching makes those emit the same
   bytes. The achievable and meaningful goal is DISTRIBUTIONAL parity -- same family, same sigma,
   same unbounded tails -- and that is what this restores. Anyone later attempting a bitwise
   differential should read this paragraph first rather than rediscovering it.

STREAM CONSUMPTION IMPLICATION, recorded explicitly as required. A uniform draw consumed exactly
one value. The Gaussian consumes TWO per rejection-loop attempt, and retries whenever the sampled
point falls outside the unit circle -- probability 1 - pi/4, about 21% per attempt, so the expected
cost is about 2.55 draws per mutation. Consumption is therefore both LARGER and VARIABLE, which
shifts every downstream draw in the offspring substream. The variability is also why the test
mirrors now call normal_deviate directly instead of open-coding draws: no hand-written mirror can
reliably replicate a rejection loop, and one that tried would be silently wrong the first time a
draw landed outside the circle.

WHY THIS IS A SCIENTIFIC CHANGE, NOT A REFACTOR: a uniform draw is hard-bounded at +/-scale, so
large mutations were not merely rare, they were IMPOSSIBLE. A Gaussian has unbounded tails, and
those rare large jumps are the mechanism by which a population escapes a local optimum. The port
was structurally incapable of a class of evolutionary event the reference exhibits.

VERIFIED: rch hz2, cargo test -p scriptbots-core --features economy-faults --lib filtered to
bd_fba5/bd_v69t/bd_d5w4/bd_iyl2/bd_l3fu/heredity = 13 passed, 0 failed. rustfmt clean.

FOLLOW-UP NOT IN SCOPE HERE: randn is also used for BRAIN mutation in the reference --
DWRAONBrain.cpp:144,149,157 and MLPBrain.cpp:138,143,150,157, all randn(0, MR2) -- while the Rust
brain crate mutates uniformly (crates/scriptbots-brain/src/{mlp,dwraon,assembly}.rs). Same defect,
different crate and different mutation path. Worth its own bead; I have not filed one because I do
not own that domain and the owner should scope it.

GOLDENS -- ONE DSR PASS SHOULD COVER ALL THREE PARITY FIXES. bd-fba5 (order), bd-hgxt (count and
scale) and this (distribution) each shift WorldDigestV1, and bd-2z0.5.9's config growth has already
left the checkpoint wire golden red on main independently. Blessing after each would mean four
passes over the same artifact set. The set is: WorldDigestV1 consumers, the checkpoint wire golden,
tests/heredity_proof.rs, tests/rng_sequence_compat.rs, scene goldens, and ci/fixtures/perf_baseline.json
-- and the perf baseline genuinely does need checking this time rather than assuming, because the
rejection loop makes each mutation cost about 2.55 draws instead of 1. I have NOT attempted any
re-bless; per AGENTS.md that is a reviewed golden-file operation under DSR, never a hand edit.

title: core heredity: sensory trait mutation ignores the documented per-gene probability
description: MutationRates.primary is documented as the probability of mutating each heritable attribute, and the C++ offspring path perturbs smell, sound, hearing, eye sensitivity, and blood only when randf is below MR times five. Rust build_child_runtime computes primary_rate but calls mutate_value unconditionally for all five sensory modifiers whenever secondary times reproduction_mutation_scale is positive. Minimal proof: parent eye sensitivity 1.5, primary 0, secondary 1, reproduction scale 1, meta mutation disabled. C++ preserves 1.5 exactly; Rust consumes a mutation delta and changes it, then shifts the downstream mutation RNG stream. Apply the per-gene probability consistently to these five modifiers, prove primary zero is bit-exact identity and consumes no trait-mutation draws, and add seeded boundary tests for rejected and accepted events so the RNG order is explicit.
close_reason: Fixed in ced12aeb7. The five sensory modifiers (smell, sound, hearing, eye sensitivity, blood) now go through the C++ randf(0,1) < MR*5 per-gene gate instead of mutating unconditionally. New mutation_event_accepted() is the single definition of that gate and draws nothing when rate or scale is zero; new mutate_modifier_with_probability() makes a rejected event bit-exact identity, kept distinct from mutate_value_with_probability() whose clamp-on-reject is correct only for genes C++ clamps outside the gate. The open-coded gates at the eye_fov and eye_direction sites now call the shared helper. Three seeded fixtures cover zero-rate identity with zero draws consumed, accepted events consuming gate-then-delta in declaration order, and rejected events consuming only the gate; the last pins the full per-gene draw order. Verified: targeted 3/3 pass remotely on vmi1149989; full crate run 501 passed / 3 failed, all three failures pre-existing fault-injection tests (every_injectable_fault_turns_the_gate_red is documented red on main in bd-cqja; the two refund tests assert parent scalars captured in stage_reproduction before build_child_runtime is called and restored from saved copies, so they are structurally unreachable from this change). rustfmt and ubs clean.

title: ux-3: stats panels occlude the world; HUD has no layout discipline
description: Parent bd-ikts. Owner report: the stats panels cover up the stuff. The HUD currently overlays the world with opaque panels and no reserved-space discipline, so the subject of the application is hidden behind its own instrumentation. Fix: give the world a viewport that panels do not overlap, or make panels genuinely translucent with the world still readable beneath and collapsible to an edge. Panels must be dismissible and remember their state. No panel may sit over the world centre by default. This is layout policy, not styling - it is separate from bd-f4x0 which handles typography and palette, and it must land first because a beautiful panel in the wrong place is still covering the simulation.
close_reason: Panels can no longer cover the world, proven on pixels rather than by inspection. Docked chrome is now flex siblings of the world canvas, and the rail is a first-class sibling of canvas_row (not nested in render_canvas), so overlap is structurally impossible. Verified in both production viewports by decoding the captures by hand: rail border occupies exactly the rightmost 320 logical px at 1280x720 (x 960-1279) and at 1600x900 (x 1280-1575), and the measured world-canvas column span contains no docked-panel border. Evidence at 03c236b7e19b via the bd-abu3 harness. SCOPE: Q1/Q2/Q4 of the layout policy shipped. Q3 - panel state across restarts - is NOT implemented and lives in bd-lelp; HudLayout::default() is built once and nothing reads saved state, so every launch is a first launch. Do not read this closure as the full layout policy having shipped.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
LAYOUT POLICY (cc_3/AmberFalcon). Written before touching the file, so implementation is mechanical. Grounded in the current code, not in the abstract.

CURRENT STATE, for the record:
- canvas_stack (lib.rs:4116) is .relative() with the world canvas_element as flex_1, then absolutely-positioned children painted over it.
- render_overlay (7535): .absolute().top(12).left(12).bg(rgb(0x0b1120)) - fully opaque.
- render_perf_overlay (7791): .absolute().top(12).right(12).bg(rgb(0x111b2b)) - fully opaque, and effectively always on (see bd-rzy3).
- render_history_chart (7827): third floating child.
- There is NO UI-state persistence anywhere in the crate. No config file, no serde of UI prefs. 'Panels remember their state' is net-new storage, not a flag.
- The only sizing constraint that exists is min_h(px(400.0)) at 4128. There is no resize policy.

=== Q1. RESERVED VIEWPORT, not translucency. ===
Two panel classes, and the distinction is what makes the rule enforceable:

(a) DOCKED CHROME - every persistent readout. Laid out as FLEX SIBLINGS of the world canvas, never as absolute children. The world viewport is exactly the space left over. Overlap becomes structurally impossible rather than a rule future code has to remember.

(b) WORLD-ANCHORED TRANSIENTS - hover tooltip, selection callout, drag affordances. These may sit over the world because they are ABOUT a world position. Absolute, translucent, cursor- or agent-anchored, auto-dismissed, never persistent, and offset so they never cover their own subject.

Why not the translucency option: at the agent densities this app is for, a translucent panel over a dark field loses BOTH readings - the world is muddied and the text is unreadable. It trades one defect for two. Translucency is also a promise that erodes: the next panel someone adds will be absolute because the surrounding code is. Docking cannot erode. Note that render_overlay and render_history_chart are not spatially tied to any world position, so neither has any business being absolute - making them so was the original mistake.

=== Q2. FIRST-RUN DEFAULT, no saved config ===
- Right rail: EXPANDED, 320 logical px, holding the stats readout and the history chart - both of which float today.
- Perf overlay: COLLAPSED to an edge tab. It is a diagnostic, not a first-run readout. This also gives it one stable home instead of the strobe in bd-rzy3.
- Bottom footer: docked, unchanged - it already is.
- Left edge: empty. No second rail by default.
- Settings drawer: closed. It stays a modal overlay when invoked; a user-summoned modal is allowed to cover the world, that is what it is for.
- Net: zero absolute panels over the world on first run. The world centre is clear by construction, not by policy.
- Below the narrow-window threshold (Q4) the right rail starts collapsed instead of expanded.

=== Q3. WHAT PERSISTS ===
Per panel, keyed by a stable panel id: collapsed (bool), and size for resizable docks (rail width). Nothing else.

NOT persisted, deliberately: dock site (sites are fixed, so there is no position to remember); transient auto-collapse caused by resize (Q4); scroll offsets; modal open state - settings always opens closed.

Storage constraints: this is new, so it must be (1) entirely separate from ScriptBotsConfig - UI state must never reach simulation config, or it perturbs science and determinism; (2) versioned; (3) fail-safe - unknown, corrupt, or older-version state silently falls back to defaults and never blocks startup. A HUD preference file must not be able to stop the app from opening.

=== Q4. RESIZE WHEN THE RESERVED VIEWPORT NO LONGER FITS ===
- The world viewport has absolute priority and a hard floor: 640x400 logical px (extends the existing min_h 400).
- As width drops, docked panels auto-collapse to edge tabs in a FIXED order: perf, then history, then the stats rail. Deterministic, so a given window size always produces the same layout.
- If the floor cannot be met even with everything collapsed, the world keeps its floor and the surrounding content area clips/scrolls. The world never shrinks below the floor to make room for chrome.
- AUTO-COLLAPSE IS TRANSIENT AND MUST NEVER OVERWRITE PERSISTED INTENT. Growing the window back restores the user's remembered state. Without this rule a single narrow resize silently destroys the saved layout - which is the bug people actually hit in shipped apps.
- Hysteresis: collapse at width W, restore at W + margin, so dragging a window edge does not strobe the panels.

=== NON-NEGOTIABLE ===
Nothing sits over the world centre by default. Under this policy that is guaranteed structurally: class (a) cannot overlap because it is not absolute, and class (b) is cursor-anchored and transient.

=== MECHANICAL WORK LIST once the lease frees ===
1. Restructure canvas_stack (4116-4215) from .relative() + absolute children into a row: [world canvas flex_1] [right rail].
2. Convert render_overlay and render_history_chart into rail content instead of absolute panels.
3. Give render_perf_overlay an edge-tab collapsed form; fix bd-rzy3 while there.
4. Add a HudLayout state struct (collapsed + width per panel id) and the versioned, fail-safe load/save.
5. Threshold + hysteresis on the resize path, with the transient/persisted split from Q4.
Constraint: bd-f4x0 owns typography and palette. This bead changes WHERE things are, not what they look like. Colours stay as-is here so bd-9pqz can land the ramp once, in one place.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
SCOPE CORRECTION — what landed at 077f76851 vs what the policy note describes (cc_3).

The layout policy comment above answers four questions. THREE are implemented; Q3 is not. Recording this so the note is not read as a description of shipped behaviour.

IMPLEMENTED:
 Q1 reserved viewport - docked flex siblings, no absolute chrome over the world.
 Q2 first-run defaults - 320px rail, stats+history open, perf collapsed.
 Q4 resize - 640px world floor, force-close at 960 / restore at 1040 with hysteresis, and the transient-vs-intent split (hud_rail_forced_closed is separate from HudLayout and the resize rule never writes intent).

NOT IMPLEMENTED:
 Q3 persistence across restarts. HudLayout::default() is constructed once at lib.rs:2401 and nothing reads saved state, so every launch is a first launch. Toggles work within a session only. Split out as its own bead because scriptbots-render has neither serde nor a config-dir dependency, and adding both to a shared manifest mid-swarm is a decision with wider blast radius. See the new bead for the exact persistence contract.

VISUAL EVIDENCE — STILL OUTSTANDING, AND BLOCKED
No screenshot is attached because none can currently be produced for HUD chrome:
 - my session runs in the launchd Background domain (launchctl managername = Background), so screencapture returns 'could not create image from display' and a GPUI window has nowhere to appear;
 - the offscreen scene harness has no GPUI frontend (FrontendKind is TerminalHeadless | Null | BevyOffscreen only);
 - --dump-png calls render_png_offscreen(&WorldState), i.e. render_offscreen_scene(OffscreenScene::capture(world)) - a CPU world rasterizer that never constructs SimulationView, so it cannot draw a panel. The existing gpui_offscreen_1280x720.png is a WORLD CANVAS capture, as its own gpui_offscreen.json states.

I deliberately did not add a scene through that path. It would emit a world image containing none of the docked panels, which attached here would read as proof of a layout it does not show. Capability gap filed as its own bead; until it lands, the layout claim in this bead rests on code inspection and the passing shortcut-table test, NOT on a rendered image, and should be treated as unproven visually.
