title: storage: recovering tests/async_lane.rs exposes 4 real failures, including AsyncReadLane returning metrics in the opposite order from StorageReader
description:
crates/scriptbots-storage/tests/async_lane.rs could not compile for ~29 hours (missing PersistenceBatch.narrative_events), so nothing ran it. With the one-line fix applied, all 4 of its tests fail. The diff is correct; the failures are pre-existing defects it was written to catch. VioletCoast/cc_2 held the file back rather than turning cargo test -p scriptbots-storage red for every agent.

1. lane_reads_match_the_sync_reader (async_lane.rs:91) — ORDERING DIVERGENCE, root cause identified. StorageReader::recent_metrics and AsyncReadLane::recent_metrics run byte-identical SQL (ORDER BY tick DESC, name DESC LIMIT ?2), but the sync reader ends with readings.reverse() while the lane does not. Sync returns oldest-first, lane returns newest-first. Test output confirms: lane [5,5,4,4,3,3] vs sync [3,3,4,4,5,5]. The lane doc comment claims it mirrors StorageReader and is newest-first, which is wrong on both counts. The lane is documented as a drop-in for GUI/TUI/API consumers, so any caller swapping between them gets reversed charts. A one-line fix (reverse after decode, plus correcting the doc) is written and reserved in the working tree but is NOT committed: rch cargo test began silently failing again (exit 1, zero bytes on both streams) before it could be verified.

2. cancelled_query_surfaces_typed_interrupt_and_lane_recovers (async_lane.rs:144) — 'a cancelled slow query must not complete: [Row { values: [Integer(1001)] }]'. Cancellation does not interrupt an in-flight lane query.

3. sub_ms_deadline_expires_a_slow_query (async_lane.rs:180) — 'a sub-millisecond deadline must expire the slow query: [Row { values: [Integer(1001)] }]'. Same shape: the deadline does not expire the query.

4. concurrent_lane_readers_observe_commit_boundaries_while_writer_applies_batches (async_lane.rs:201) — InvalidTarget, 'stale FrankenSQLite sidecar <path>-wal exists'. Test-isolation/cleanup issue against the rch scratch dir, not necessarily a product defect.

2 and 3 together suggest lane cancellation/deadline enforcement is not wired at all, which matters because those are the bounds that keep a slow read off a UI path. Fix 1 first (cheap, proven), then 2/3, then 4; commit tests/async_lane.rs once green.
notes:
ROOT CAUSES IDENTIFIED for all 4. Fix written and reserved in the working tree, NOT committed: rch is refusing every build from this pane (see blocker note at the end).

1. ORDERING DIVERGENCE — real product bug, fixed in src/async_lane.rs. StorageReader::recent_metrics and AsyncReadLane::recent_metrics run byte-identical SQL (ORDER BY tick DESC, name DESC LIMIT ?2) but the sync reader ends with readings.reverse() and the lane did not. Sync returned oldest-first, lane newest-first; the failing assertion showed exactly reversed vectors. StorageReader is the canonical authority (older, more depended-on surface), so the lane now reverses to match, and its doc comment — which claimed both 'newest-first' AND 'mirroring StorageReader', contradictory and wrong on both counts — is corrected. tests/async_lane.rs now also pins the direction (windows(2) ascending-tick assertion), not just agreement, so a future flip of BOTH surfaces together cannot pass.

2+3. CANCELLATION AND DEADLINE TESTS CANNOT FIRE — split out as bd-sf9h, both #[ignore]d with that bead id in the attribute. Their slow workload is a recursive CTE with LIMIT 5000000/8000000, but the pinned FrankenSQLite caps recursion at RECURSIVE_CTE_MAX_RECURSION = 1000 (fsqlite-core/src/connection.rs:785), so both queries return COUNT(*) = 1001 in microseconds. The failures literally read 'a cancelled slow query must not complete: [Row { values: [Integer(1001)] }]'. This is NOT evidence cancellation is broken — it is evidence the workload is instant and cancellation/deadline enforcement has never been exercised. Unproven in both directions, which matters because bounding a slow read off a UI path is the lane's entire purpose.

4. STALE -wal SIDECAR — split out as bd-jjxe, #[ignore]d with that bead id. write_fixture's explicit successful Storage::close leaves a -wal behind, and StoragePipeline then refuses the same path with InvalidTarget 'stale FrankenSQLite sidecar ...-wal exists'. The refusal is correct documented policy; the question is why a clean close leaves a sidecar at all, since close is supposed to checkpoint on the connection-owning thread. Same shape could strand a real run database.

BLOCKER: rch refuses every build from this pane. 'rch exec -- cargo test' and now also 'rch exec -- cargo check' exit 1 immediately with ZERO bytes on stdout and stderr. RUST_LOG=debug shows execution stopping right after 'project identity normalization: verified_within_root', never reaching worker selection (the working case logged 'Selected worker: hz2'). Meanwhile rch doctor reports 22/22 checks passed and peer builds are actively running on hz1/hz2/vmi1149989. 'rch exec -- echo hello' DOES print '[RCH] remote required; refusing local fallback [RCH-E301] (non-compilation command)', so the error channel works on that path — the cargo path fails silently. Not committing unverified code into a shared main that five other agents build from; that is the failure mode that just cost the swarm an hour when scriptbots-core landed a non-exhaustive match.
close_reason: Landed in cc4cf09f9. Fixed the ordering divergence with StorageReader as canonical: AsyncReadLane::recent_metrics now reverses to match, and its doc comment (which claimed both newest-first AND mirroring StorageReader) is corrected. The test pins the direction with an ascending-tick assertion, not just agreement, so a future flip of both surfaces together cannot pass. The other three are ignored with their bead id in the attribute so the suite stays green and the defects stay visible: bd-sf9h (cancellation and deadline fixtures cannot fire — recursive CTE capped at 1000 rows by RECURSIVE_CTE_MAX_RECURSION, so both queries return COUNT(*)=1001 instantly and neither bound has ever been exercised) and bd-jjxe (a clean Storage::close leaves a -wal sidecar the pipeline then refuses on the same path). Verified: cargo test -p scriptbots-storage --test async_lane = 1 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored.

title: core/replay: replay.rs has zero unit tests; the only coverage pins persistence_interval=1, the one config where the cap defect is invisible
description:
crates/scriptbots-core/src/replay.rs (93 lines, production replay instrumentation for bd-2z0.8.9.8) contains no #[cfg(test)] module and no tests.

The sole coverage is crates/scriptbots-app/tests/replay_e2e.rs, which pins
`--set persistence_interval=1` (lines 57, 239, 288). That is the single value of
persistence_interval under which record_replay_action_events' buffer-length cap
coincides with its documented per-tick semantics, so the e2e suite cannot
observe the truncation bug filed as the sibling bead — the tests pass while the
shipped default (persistence_interval: 60, crates/scriptbots-app/src/main.rs:1624)
drops 98.3% of the stream.

WHAT TO ADD (core-level, deterministic, no storage dependency)
1. Multi-tick emission under persistence_interval > 1: run enough ticks to span
   more than one interval with a cap >= live agent count and assert every tick
   contributed one Action event per live agent — the direct regression test for
   the cap defect. Must FAIL against the pre-fix implementation.
2. Per-tick cap enforcement: cap strictly below the live agent count must record
   exactly `cap` events per tick, every tick, not `cap` events total.
3. Disabled default: replay_event_tick_cap == 0 records nothing and leaves the
   world digest byte-identical to a run with the field absent, which is the
   'byte-identical to pre-instrumentation baselines' claim in the module doc.
4. Digest-neutrality: emission is documented as a read-only projection that never
   mutates science state. Assert world_digest_v1() is identical between a capped
   and an uncapped run of the same seed. This claim is currently unproven.
5. WorldDigest anchor: request_replay_world_digest() followed by a boundary
   appends exactly one WorldDigest event, including when the action buffer is at
   cap (the sibling bead's fix).
6. Canonical order: recorded events follow ascending stable AgentUid, matching the
   normalization the module doc relies on for determinism.

Every assertion must be observable through the world's public/crate surface so
the tests are mock-free per the project's testing policy.
close_reason: Done in 84decacf8. Six tests added to replay.rs covering multi-tick window recording, per-tick truncation, zero-cap silence, digest neutrality, anchor survival under saturation, and ascending-UID order. The digest-neutrality test immediately found a real P1 (bd-zpoa), which is the point of the bead.

title: brain-ml ft: zero-sigma mutation changes valid negative-zero genome bits
description: Confirmed metamorphic identity defect. The FtBrain codec accepts finite -0.0 and preserves parameter bits, but mutation always executes parameter += gaussian * 0.0. For a selected -0.0 parameter and positive signed-zero delta this becomes +0.0, changing payload and material hash despite zero mutation magnitude. Add a scripted-stream negative-zero fixture, preserve the full RNG draw schedule, and skip arithmetic when sigma is zero.
close_reason: Ft zero-sigma mutation now consumes the unchanged per-gene Box-Muller schedule but skips arithmetic, preserving signed-zero genome bits and material hashes; semantic identity bumped to v2 and the full remote brain-ft suite passes 10/10.

title: DB-backed lineage locus tracing with CSV/PNG export (bd-16g.13.2 remainder)
description: Split out of bd-16g.13.2. The heredity proof suite landed (8/8 green, crates/scriptbots-core/tests/heredity_proof.rs). title: bd-d3wu successor: ~299 closed beads unexamined — Tier A ran (2 confirmed, floors), Tier B/C unrun; ten-shape taxonomy with detection methods
description:
╔══ STATED CONCLUSION (CopperCat) — READ THIS FIRST ════════════════════════════╗
║ ALL COUNTS BELOW ARE FLOORS, NOT TOTALS. Recall was never measured for any    ║
║ detector (bd-hmy4). One detector also OVER-reported once from my manual       ║
║ verification error (ReadbackError::Resize, retracted, bd-3t3y INVALID).       ║
╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

TIER A — RAN. 58 candidates -> 2 CONFIRMED.
  shape 4  25 -> 1   RANDOM_STREAM_ALGORITHM, core/lib.rs:288+290. Two cfg-gated
                     definitions of one concept. FOUND FROM THE CODE with no knowledge
                     of bd-7mh6, which measured the same thing as a 77.19-unit
                     divergence at tick 1. Best evidence the taxonomy generalises.
  shape 8  57 -> 1   ScenarioError::NotATable, app/lib.rs:267. Zero construction sites.
                     (StatsError::ZeroVariance was a second, now RESOLVED by c74f30c3e.)
  shape 5   9 -> 0   all `new() -> Self { Self::default() }`, idiomatic.
  shape 7  22 -> 0   all numbers in arithmetic/range/list context. AND THE RULE WOULD
                     MISS ITS OWN FOUNDING INSTANCE: replay.rs said "the default of
                     ZERO" while the constant was 512 — stated as a WORD. Shape 7 is
                     real but NOT detectable this way. Reclassified TIER A -> TIER B.
  shape 2  1579 tests -> 0. "No assertions" WOULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT bd-2wj, which had
                     assertions comparing two values from the same runtime.
  shape 10 20 -> 0   detector VALIDATED not unproductive: the known instance
                     (bd-h189, p_value: 0.05) matches its pattern.

TIER B — ATTEMPTED, NO RESULT. Four visual.rs defaults mutated; the suite stalled in
  uninterruptible I/O on the USB volume (state U, 7m29s elapsed / 0.43s CPU). Killed and
  ALL FOUR REVERTED, git diff verified empty. No test output was produced, so nothing is
  claimed about what detects what. Retry through rch, not locally.
  MANDATORY FOR THE RETRY: a POSITIVE CONTROL — one constant with a known pinning test.
  Without it a null result is meaningless rather than informative.

TIER C — SPECIFIED, NOT RUN. Ablation differential. Unblocked by efd1ae314 (bd-c7pg
  floor closed). Not run because every candidate lives in render files leased by peers,
  and editing a peer's leased file to run an audit is not acceptable. Method, four ranked
  candidates, and blind spots are in this bead's comments; mailed to WildDuck/AmberFalcon.

MECHANISM PER HIT
  RANDOM_STREAM_ALGORITHM  cfg(target_pointer_width) selects xoshiro256++ at 64-bit and
    xoshiro128++ at 32-bit, so identical seeds initialise different scientific worlds BY
    DESIGN. Guarded — but at RESTORE (from_state) while the failure is at SELECTION. That
    guard hole is shape 9, filed and fixed as bd-g4aw with a born-red stage-1 assertion.
  ScenarioError::NotATable  declared, constructed nowhere, so any handler is unreachable.
  StatsError::ZeroVariance  declared-only BECAUSE A CHECK WAS MISSING, not because it was
    surplus. paired_diff returned cohens_dz = 0.0 for zero spread — "no effect" for a
    perfectly consistent difference. The variant was right and the caller was wrong.

WHAT THE SWEEPS CANNOT SEE
  1. A CONSUMED PATH THAT DOES THE WRONG THING. The ceiling on all of Tier A. Needs
     ablation (shape 6) or a behavioural test.
  2. Shapes 6 and 1 are INDISTINGUISHABLE by ablation alone — code nobody calls gives the
     same null as code whose output is discarded. Interpret Tier C against call-site counts.
  3. TIER B CANNOT SEPARATE "genuinely unconstrained" from "hollow tests" on its own.
     Ask what the constant FEEDS: if it reaches a consumed output, a null is hollowness.
  4. MACRO-CONSTRUCTED CODE in every static shape: #[from], derive(Deserialize), serde.
  5. THE 291 NO-CITATION BEADS. Shapes 1/7/8 need a citation to anchor on, and 291 of 335
     unadjudicated closed beads name no file. The cheap tier cannot reach the largest
     stratum. THIS REMAINS THE HEADLINE FINDING.
  6. Its own false negatives, absent an independent set of known instances.

THE ORDERING THAT MATTERS MOST: THE CHEAPLY DETECTABLE SHAPES ARE NOT THE DANGEROUS ONES.
Tier A over the whole codebase confirmed 2. Tier B, over a handful of beads by hand, found
bd-2z0.3 — a false close on a P0 epic. Any claim this audit is automatable should be read
against that.

STILL OPEN: ~299 closed beads never examined. Tier B and C unrun. Successors bd-hmy4
(shape-8 sweep), bd-7453 (unwired lab/stats.rs, owner decision, NO DELETION).bd-d3wu adjudicated 67 of 393 closed beads. THIS BEAD OWNS THE REMAINING ~299, which have NEVER been examined against the taxonomy. Nothing in bd-d3wu's verdicts extends to them.

THE STRUCTURAL OBSTACLE, measured: 291 of 335 unadjudicated closed beads CITE NO FILE AT ALL (45 of them P0). Shapes 1, 7 and 8 need a citation to anchor on, so the cheap tier CANNOT REACH the largest stratum. This is not an audit backlog — it is the condition that made bulk closing possible in the first place.

PLAN, in value order:
1. CLOSE-REASON CITATION REQUIREMENT (prevents recurrence, cheapest durable fix). Reject a close whose reason names no path. Converts uncheckable records into one-command checks. Would not by itself have caught bd-2z0.3, but would have made the check possible in seconds.
2. TIER A sweep over the 44 citable beads: shapes 1, 4, 5, 7, 8. Minutes.
3. TIER C is NOW UNBLOCKED by efd1ae314 (bd-c7pg PerfSnapshot pinning). Shape 6 ablation differential over render-side subsystems: the post stack (regression guard on 32b375231535), day/night, terrain normal lighting, BoostTrail.
4. TIER B on proof-bearing beads only: shape 2 mutation, shape 3 toggle-the-default.
5. UNIFORM SAMPLE of the 291 no-citation beads. They need manual reconstruction, so sample rather than enumerate, and PUBLISH THE SAMPLE DESIGN BEFORE DRAWING.

RULES INHERITED FROM bd-d3wu, do not re-derive:
- MEASURE YOUR CHECKER FIRST. My consumer check's first run was 49/50 tool defects, a fabricated-defect event larger than anything the audit found. Validate against pass 1's 51 known-confirmed beads.
- THE CHEAPLY DETECTABLE SHAPES ARE NOT THE DANGEROUS ONES. Tier A found one completion-debt item; tier B found a false close on a P0 epic.
- THE LIST IS OPEN. Three of eight shapes were found after the taxonomy was declared, one by a second agent late in the session. 'None of the eight matched' means the cheap known checks passed, NOT that the close is sound.
- A reopen must PROPAGATE to closed ancestors (bd-2z0.14 was the instance).
- Do not publish a rate from a suspicion-selected stratum.

comments.author: CopperCat
comments.text:
TIER A SWEEP — RESULT (bd-we7b, CopperCat). Scanner: scratchpad/tier_a.py
Detection pass over 90 non-test .rs files. Shapes 4, 5, 7, 8. Shape 1 ran in bd-d3wu 3b.

COUNT
  shape 4  constant duplicated and drifted ....  25 candidates ->  1 CONFIRMED + 3 to adjudicate
  shape 5  fn returning an empty structure ....   9 candidates ->  0 CONFIRMED  (9/9 false)
  shape 7  doc asserting the code's opposite ..  22 candidates ->  0 CONFIRMED  (22/22 false)
  shape 8  declaration-only variant (refined) .   2 candidates ->  2 CONFIRMED  (+1 known, MISSED)
  ────────────────────────────────────────────  58 candidates ->  3 confirmed + 1 missed

════ THE ONE THAT MATTERS: SHAPE 4 REDISCOVERED bd-7mh6's ROOT CAUSE MECHANICALLY ════

  RANDOM_STREAM_ALGORITHM, crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs:288 and :290
      "rand-0.9.5-smallrng-xoshiro256plusplus-64-seed-from-u64"   (64-bit)
      "rand-0.9.5-smallrng-xoshiro128plusplus-32-seed-from-u64"   (32-bit)

  Two cfg-gated definitions of THE SAME NAMED CONCEPT with different values. That is
  shape 4 exactly, and it is the root cause bd-7mh6 measured from the other end as a
  77.187606812-unit divergence in agent[0].position.x at TICK 1.

  SIGNIFICANCE: the detector found this from the CODE with no knowledge of bd-7mh6,
  bd-2z0.3, or the browser lane. An independently-derived mechanical rule rediscovered
  the session's most important finding. That is the strongest evidence so far that the
  taxonomy generalizes rather than just describing what was already known.

  Note the constant is CONSUMED at :457, :476, :493, :496 including a guard
  `if state.algorithm != RANDOM_STREAM_ALGORITHM`, which REJECTS a checkpoint written on
  the other target. So the divergence is caught at the checkpoint boundary and NOT at
  world initialisation — the two worlds still start differently. Detection at the wrong
  layer is why this survived: it looks defended.

  Owned by bd-7mh6; not double-filed.

  THREE MORE WORTH ADJUDICATING (not filed as defects, cross-crate same-name drift):
      DEFAULT_COMMAND_CAPACITY   32 runtime/host_core.rs   vs   8 storage/lib.rs
      MAX_SIM_STEPS_PER_FRAME     8 bevy/lib.rs            vs 240 render/lib.rs   (30x)
      ADAPTER_SEMANTIC_VERSION    2 ft/assembly/dwraon     vs   3 mlp

════ MEASURED FALSE-POSITIVE CLASSES — per detector, before anything is called a finding ════

  SHAPE 4, ~22 of 25 false. Two classes:
    (a) PER-MODULE NAMESPACING. Each brain family legitimately owns GENOME_MAGIC,
        STATE_MAGIC, KIND, ACTIVATION_LAYER_NAME, ADAPTER_SEMANTIC_DESCRIPTOR. Same
        name, different module, different value BY DESIGN.
    (b) FN-LOCAL TEST CONSTANTS. AGENTS, INTERVAL, COUNT, STEPS, SAMPLES, WARMUPS appear
        3-5 times in different test functions in one file. Different scopes entirely.
    REFINEMENT NEEDED: require the name to cross a CRATE boundary and both values to be
    literals of the same type; or restrict to names denoting a shared contract (schema,
    magic, protocol, algorithm). RANDOM_STREAM_ALGORITHM survives either refinement.

  SHAPE 5, 9 of 9 false — 100% FP RATE ON THIS CODEBASE.
    Every candidate is `pub fn new() -> Self { Self::default() }`, the idiomatic Rust
    constructor. Not a stub; the type's real content is in its Default impl. The rule
    must exclude new()->Self delegating to Default. AS WRITTEN THIS DETECTOR IS USELESS
    HERE and should not be run again without that exclusion.

  SHAPE 7, 22 of 22 false. The rule flags a const name near a different number; every hit
    was a number in ARITHMETIC, RANGE, or LIST context, not a claimed value:
        "3^4 = 81 > MAX_ARMS"                     81 is the comparand
        "0..INPUT_SIZE"                           0 is a range bound
        "HUD_RAIL_COLLAPSE_WIDTH is 960 (WORLD_MIN_WIDTH 640 + HUD_RAIL_WIDTH)"  640+320=960
        "sqrt(0.08) — see DEFAULT_TEMPERATURE_COMFORT_BAND"   sqrt(0.08)=0.2828427, correct
        "2. Waterline: below SPLAT_WATERLINE_ELEVATION"        2 is a list number
    AND WORSE, IT WOULD MISS ITS OWN FOUNDING INSTANCE: replay.rs said "the default of
    ZERO keeps production runs byte-identical" while the constant was 512. The false value
    was stated as an ENGLISH WORD, which no numeric matcher catches. Shape 7 is real — I
    committed the instance myself — but it is NOT mechanically detectable by this rule.
    Reclassify shape 7 from TIER A to TIER B pending a rule that works.

  SHAPE 8, 0 of 2 false, and the refinement worked: 57 raw -> 2 candidates, both real.
      ScenarioError::NotATable     app/src/lib.rs:267        zero refs workspace-wide
      StatsError::ZeroVariance     app/src/lab/stats.rs:46   zero refs workspace-wide
    Both are declared failure modes the code cannot produce, so every handler for them is
    unreachable and any doc naming them describes an impossible state.
    StatsError::ZeroVariance sits in the same file as bd-7vdu's uncalled
    adjust_multiple_comparisons and Correction::HolmBonferroni/BenjaminiHochberg — that is
    now four dead items in lab/stats.rs, i.e. ONE DEAD CLUSTER, not four findings.

    *** THE DETECTOR MISSED A KNOWN TRUE POSITIVE ***
    ReadbackError::Resize (world-gfx/src/lib.rs:589), verified by hand and by VioletCoast,
    did NOT appear. Cause: my reference pattern is `(\bEnum|Self)::Variant`, and the bare
    `Self::` alternative matches a same-named variant in ANY other enum, masking the
    orphan. FALSE-NEGATIVE RATE IS NOT ZERO AND I ONLY KNOW THAT BECAUSE I HAD AN
    INDEPENDENTLY-FOUND INSTANCE TO CHECK AGAINST. Fix: resolve Self:: to the enclosing
    enum instead of treating it as a wildcard. Until then, treat shape-8 counts as LOWER
    BOUNDS.

════ WHAT THIS SWEEP CANNOT SEE ════

  1. SHAPES 2, 3, 6 — not in Tier A. A test executing nothing, a test asserting the
     inverse, and work that runs but discards its output all need execution: mutation, a
     default toggle, or an ablation capture. Tier A is text analysis and is blind to all
     three. This matters because tier B found the P0 false close and tier A found none.
  2. SEMANTIC CORRECTNESS. Nothing here says a consumed constant is the RIGHT constant or
     a called function computes the right answer.
  3. THE 291 NO-CITATION BEADS. This sweep scans code, so it is not limited by citations —
     but it also cannot ATTRIBUTE what it finds to a bead. RANDOM_STREAM_ALGORITHM is a
     real defect found in code; mapping it back to which close reason overclaimed still
     needs the citation link that 291 beads do not have.
  4. MACRO-CONSTRUCTED AND MACRO-GENERATED CODE, in every shape. Confirmed classes:
     #[from] and derive(Deserialize) for shape 8; the same blindness applies elsewhere.
  5. Its own false negatives, except where an independent source supplies an instance —
     see the ReadbackError::Resize miss above.

════ CALIBRATION ════

  58 candidates -> 3 confirmed. A 95% candidate-rejection rate, and two detectors (5 and 7)
  produced NOTHING BUT NOISE on this codebase. The value of Tier A is not its yield; it is
  that RANDOM_STREAM_ALGORITHM was found without knowing where to look.

  Consistent with bd-d3wu's finding and worth restating: THE CHEAPLY DETECTABLE SHAPES ARE
  NOT THE DANGEROUS ONES. Tier A, run over the whole codebase, confirmed one defect already
  known from the other direction plus one dead cluster. Tier B, run over a handful of
  beads, found a false close on a P0 epic.

  no assertion, first regex ............   30

  CONFIRMED HOLLOW ..................... 0

  (a) ASSERTION HELPER FUNCTIONS. assert_locomotion_oracle(...) is a plain fn call, not a
      macro, so \bassert\w*! missed it. This alone was 23 of the first 30 — and it hit the

comments.text:
SHAPE 9 ADDED — A GUARD WHOSE COVERAGE DOES NOT INTERSECT THE FAILURE IT APPEARS TO DEFEND.

Filed as bd-g4aw. Found by the Tier A shape-4 hit on RANDOM_STREAM_ALGORITHM, then by
reading what actually guards it rather than assuming nothing did.

  THE GUARD   SmallRngStream::from_state(), core/src/lib.rs:487-496
              if state.algorithm != RANDOM_STREAM_ALGORITHM -> UnsupportedAlgorithm
  IT CHECKS   that a serialized continuation state being RESTORED came from the same
              algorithm lane as the current build. Correct invariant, correct code, and it
              works — a 64-bit checkpoint IS rejected on 32-bit with a typed error.
  IT MISSES   from_state() is the RESTORE path only. A freshly seeded world constructs
              directly (Self { seed, state_words }) and never produces a RandomStreamState
              for the other target to validate. Native and WASM build from the same u64
              seed with different algorithms and nothing ever compares them.

CLASSIFICATION, and the reason this is worth its own shape: it is NEITHER of the two the
orchestrator offered.
  NOT shape 1 — from_state runs and is exercised; it is not dead code.
  NOT shape 3 — its invariant is correct; it does not assert the inverse of anything.
It is right invariant, right implementation, WRONG PATH.

WHY IT IS WORSE THAN NO GUARD: a reviewer greps RANDOM_STREAM_ALGORITHM, finds a strict
equality check with a typed error, and concludes the target boundary is covered. The
guard's existence terminates the search. That is the same mechanism as shape 2 — bd-2wj's
parity test made people believe parity was tested — expressed in production code rather
than in a test. Shapes 2 and 9 are the same disease in different tissue: an artifact whose
APPEARANCE of coverage is what prevents real coverage.

DETECTION (mechanizable): find constants selected by #[cfg(target_*)] or environment;
locate validators referencing them; enumerate CONSTRUCTION sites of the containing type;
flag any constructor that reaches no validator. Here from_state validates and the direct
constructor does not — and the direct constructor is the one both targets actually use.

THIRD NOVEL SHAPE FOUND AFTER THE TAXONOMY WAS DECLARED — shape 6 from my own false
dichotomy, shape 8 from VioletCoast, shape 9 from this sweep. The list is not converging
on eight. Every serious look produces a shape the previous look did not have, and the
honest reading remains that shapes 10 and 11 exist. 'None of the nine matched' means the
known cheap checks passed, NOT that a close is sound.

comments.author: CopperCat
comments.text:
SHAPE 10 — A COMPUTED-LOOKING VALUE THAT IS ACTUALLY CONSTANT   *** NEW ***

  A field that presents as the output of a computation and is a literal. The call site
  reads a number, uses it, and nothing about it looks wrong.

  THIS IS THE MOST DANGEROUS SHAPE ON THE LIST, and the entry says so deliberately.
  Every other shape fails toward silence: dead code does nothing and is eventually
  noticed; an unreachable variant never fires; a discarded computation produces no
  output. Shape 10 fails toward CONFIDENT WRONGNESS. It emits a plausible value that a
  reader acts on, and there is no symptom at the call site — no panic, no empty result,
  no missing row. It is only visible by reading the producer.

  INSTANCE (bd-h189, fixed 650e9ec52): crates/scriptbots-app/src/lab/stats.rs:139
      p_value: 0.05,
  returned by paired_diff on EVERY call, never computed from the data, and sitting
  exactly on the conventional significance threshold. Anyone who consulted it made a
  decision on a literal. It was harmless only because the module has no external
  consumer (bd-7453) — wiring it would have started publishing a fabricated statistic.

  DETECT: MECHANICAL. Grep for literal assignments to fields named like statistics,
  probabilities, scores or rates:

    rg -n -g '!*/tests/*' -g '!*/benches/*' \
      '\b(p_value|p_val|score|rate|ratio|confidence|significance|alpha|power|likelihood|
        probability|prob|mean|median|stddev|std_dev|variance|correlation|r_squared|
        effect_size|magnitude|coverage|accuracy|precision|recall)\s*:\s*-?[0-9]+\.?[0-9]*\s*[,}]' \
      crates/*/src

  MEASURED ON THIS CODEBASE: 20 raw hits, 0 NEW confirmed findings. The detector is
  VALIDATED rather than unproductive — the known instance matches its pattern, so it
  would have caught bd-h189 before a human did.

  FALSE-POSITIVE CLASSES, all three seen in the 20:
    (a) TEST FIXTURES inside #[cfg(test)] mod in src/. Literal statistics in test data are
        the point. Excluding tests/ and benches/ DIRECTORIES does not exclude these.
    (b) PARAMETERS, not outputs. certify.rs:75 and compare.rs:102 carry confidence: 0.95 —
        a chosen confidence LEVEL, an input to the procedure, not a result of it.
    (c) DOCUMENTED DEGENERATE-CASE CONSTRUCTORS. distribution.rs:115 returns
        variance: 0.0, std_dev: 0.0 for a constant sample, with the comment "A constant
        sample: no shape. Report zeros and flag it rather than divide by zero," and
        jb_p_value: 1.0, which is the CORRECT p-value for no evidence against normality.

  THE DISCRIMINATOR, which is what makes this actionable rather than 20 things to read:
  ask whether the field is an OUTPUT of the computation ON THE SUCCESS PATH. A parameter
  is an input. A degenerate-case constructor is an explicit refusal to compute, and is
  legitimate when it says so. Shape 10 is a literal standing in the place where a computed
  result belongs, on the path a caller treats as a real answer.

  WORTH RECORDING AS A CONTRAST, because it is the same situation handled both ways in one
  codebase: analytics/src/distribution.rs meets a constant sample, refuses to compute,
  returns explicit zeros WITH a comment explaining why, and emits the honest p-value of 1.0.
  app/src/lab/stats.rs met the same class of case and fabricated cohens_dz = 0.0 plus a
  constant p_value. Same problem, one honest treatment and one fabricated. The honest one is
  the model.

  THE FIX IS NOT ENOUGH BY ITSELF. Computing the value does not prevent recurrence; the
  reusable part is an assertion that distinguishes computed from constant. bd-h189's is
  p_value_is_computed_from_the_data_and_not_a_constant, which pins RESPONSIVENESS rather
  than any number: two inputs with different effect strengths must produce DIFFERENT
  outputs, and the stronger effect the more significant one. Any constant fails both halves
  whatever value is chosen. Deliberately does NOT assert p_value != 0.05 — that guards only
  the literal that happened to be there and passes for the next one.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
TEN SHAPES NOW, AND THE LIST IS STILL OPEN.

Four of the ten arrived after the taxonomy was declared: 6 from my own false dichotomy on
bd-lhml, 7 from a doc I wrote contradicting code I wrote, 8 from VioletCoast in a crate I
never opened, 9 from the Tier A sweep, 10 from reading one function while adjudicating a
different bead. Not one of the last four came from the previous list predicting it.

"None of the ten matched" means the known cheap checks passed. It does not mean a close is
sound, and a checklist that sounds complete is exactly the artifact that lets a bulk close
look verified.

comments.text:
TIER C SHAPE-6 ABLATION: SPECIFIED AND HANDED OFF, NOT RUN. Saying so rather than reporting a sweep I did not execute.

WHY NOT RUN: the ablation differential requires stubbing a render subsystem to a no-op and
re-running the deterministic capture. Every candidate lives in files I do not own and that are
actively leased — crates/scriptbots-render/src/lib.rs (WildDuck, bd-37m) and
crates/scriptbots-render/src/hud_capture.rs (AmberFalcon). Core owns visual.rs, but the
OBSERVABLE for shape 6 here is pixels, which only the render harness produces. I am not going
to edit a peer's leased file mid-slice to run an audit.

THE METHOD, precise enough to run without re-deriving it:
  1. Stub ONE subsystem to a no-op (return early / identity transform). One at a time.
  2. Re-run the deterministic capture at a fixed size and seed.
  3. Diff the frame BYTE-WISE against the unablated capture.
  4. IDENTICAL OUTPUT UNDER ABLATION IS THE FINDING. No judgement required: the subsystem ran,
     did work, and nothing downstream can observe the result.
  Precondition now met: efd1ae314 (AmberFalcon) pinned the whole PerfSnapshot and closed
  bd-c7pg's ~10k-pixel nondeterminism floor. Before that a byte-wise diff could not separate a
  real change from capture noise, which is why this tier was blocked.

CANDIDATES, in order of suspicion:
  1. the post stack — REGRESSION GUARD on 32b375231535. It was the shape-6 instance; an
     ablation that shows no diff means it regressed to painting nowhere again.
  2. day/night — live only since the default was un-frozen; never verified to reach pixels.
  3. terrain normal lighting (visual.rs terrain_normal_light_factor) — wired this session.
  4. BoostTrail — cue defined in core this session, consumer in vfx.rs.
  Expected signal for a healthy subsystem: a large diff. 32b375231535's own fix measured
  790600 of 921600 pixels changed with an IDENTICAL science digest — that pairing (big pixel
  delta, zero digest delta) is the signature of a correctly wired visual-only subsystem.

WHAT ABLATION CANNOT SEE:
  1. A DOC THAT IS CORRECT ABOUT BEHAVIOUR NOBODY EXERCISES. Ablating code nothing calls
     produces no diff, which is indistinguishable from ablating code whose output is
     discarded. Shape 6 and shape 1 give the SAME ablation result; only a call-site count
     separates them. Run the shape-1 check first and interpret the ablation against it.
  2. A SUBSYSTEM WHOSE OUTPUT IS WRONG BUT PRESENT. A large diff proves the work reaches
     pixels, NOT that the pixels are right. Ablation answers 'does this matter', never 'is
     this correct'.
  3. PARTIAL DISCARD. A subsystem that correctly paints 90% of its effect and drops the rest
     still shows a large diff and reads as healthy.
  4. ANYTHING OUTSIDE THE CHOSEN OBSERVABLE. Pixels miss audio, logs, journal rows; a digest
     misses everything visual-only. Choosing the wrong observable makes a live subsystem look
     dead. The bd-mv2j seam proof is the same instrument on serialized bytes.
  5. NON-DETERMINISM REINTRODUCED ANYWHERE UPSTREAM. The whole method rests on bd-c7pg
     staying closed; if the floor returns, every ablation reads as a diff and the method
     silently inverts from precise to useless.

HANDOFF: whoever holds render/lib.rs and hud_capture.rs next should run candidate 1 first — it
is a regression guard on a fix that already landed, so it is the cheapest way to validate that
the method works before spending captures on the other three.

SHAPE-8 RECALL: CORRECTED COUNTS, AND A CORRECTION TO MY OWN REPORTING

════ THE FIX ════
The shape-8 detector matched references with (\bEnum|Self)::Variant. The bare Self::
alternative matched a same-named variant in ANY other enum. Fixed: Self::Variant now counts
only inside files that declare the enum or an `impl Enum`. Real weakness, worth fixing.

I fixed it expecting ReadbackError::Resize to appear. It did not. Investigating why produced
the ground truth I should have had at the start:

    world-gfx/src/lib.rs:681   return Err(ReadbackError::Resize(format!(
    world-gfx/src/lib.rs:693          ReadbackError::Resize(format!(
    world-gfx/src/lib.rs:699          ReadbackError::Resize(format!(

CONSTRUCTED THREE TIMES. It is live code and was never a shape-8 instance. The detector
excluded it correctly on every run. THERE WAS NO RECALL GAP.

The error was mine: a malformed verification (an rg piped through a filter that suppressed the
construction sites) let me report "verified by hand" on a peer's finding I had not verified. I
propagated it into bd-3t3y, into these taxonomy notes as a stated recall gap, and into a mail
telling VioletCoast their find held up. Three artifacts downstream of one bad grep.

════ CORRECTED COUNTS ════
  shape 8, as previously reported ... 2 confirmed (+1 "known miss")
  shape 8, ACTUAL .................. 1 confirmed

  ScenarioError::NotATable   app/src/lib.rs:267   — stands, zero construction sites
  StatsError::ZeroVariance   app/lab/stats.rs:46  — WAS valid; no longer, because I fixed it
                                                    in c74f30c3e. paired_diff now constructs
                                                    it. A resolved instance, not a false one.
  ReadbackError::Resize      world-gfx:589        — NEVER VALID. Retracted.

  Tier A total, as reported ......... 3 confirmed
  Tier A total, CORRECTED ........... 2 confirmed
    RANDOM_STREAM_ALGORITHM (shape 4) and ScenarioError::NotATable (shape 8).

════ WHAT THIS MEANS FOR EVERY OTHER COUNT I REPORTED ════
The user's framing is right and applies to my own instrument: a detector with unknown recall
produces FLOORS, not totals. But the direction here is the opposite of the one assumed — the
detector did not undercount. I over-reported by adding an instance it correctly rejected.

So, stated precisely:
  - Counts from shapes 1, 4, 5, 7, 8, 10 remain LOWER BOUNDS on what exists, because recall
    was never measured for any of them. That is unchanged and was already stated.
  - The CONFIRMED counts were an OVER-count by one, from a manual verification error rather
    than from any detector. Corrected above.
  - No re-run of the other tiers is needed: the wildcard bug could only cause FALSE NEGATIVES
    (a live-looking variant wrongly excluded), never false positives, so no reported finding
    from shapes 1/4/5/7/10 is invalidated by it. Shape 8's re-run is done and is the corrected
    figure above.

════ THE TAXONOMY LINE THIS EARNS ════
A DETECTION METHOD MUST STATE ITS OWN RECALL, OR THE SWEEP INHERITS EXACTLY THE
FALSE-CONFIDENCE PROBLEM IT WAS BUILT TO FIND.

There is something apt about the detector for "declared but never constructed" having its
blind spot examined and found innocent while its operator was not. The lesson generalises past
tooling:

  1. A checker's FALSE-POSITIVE rate is measurable from its own output. Its FALSE-NEGATIVE
     rate is not, and cannot be, without an independent set of known instances.
  2. Therefore every count from these sweeps is a FLOOR. "N found" never means "N exist".
  3. VERIFY A PEER'S FINDING AS RIGOROUSLY AS YOUR OWN. This is the companion rule I had not
     written, and its absence is what let one bad grep become three published artifacts.
     Accepting a report and calling that verification is how a false finding acquires a
     second source and starts looking corroborated.
  4. A retraction must be as loud as the finding was. bd-3t3y is closed INVALID rather than
     quietly dropped, and VioletCoast is being told directly, because they were told the
     opposite by me.

comments.text:
TIER B ATTEMPTED, NO RESULT. Mutations reverted, tree clean, lease released.

WHAT I DID: mutated four visual.rs defaults in one build so detection would be attributable by
which tests failed — DAYLIGHT_NIGHT_FLOOR 0.15->0.37, DEFAULT_DAY_NIGHT_START_PHASE 0.25->0.61,
FERTILITY_LUSHNESS_WEIGHT 0.25->0.73, TERRAIN_LIGHT_HEIGHT 0.85->0.41.

WHAT HAPPENED: the core lib suite stalled in uninterruptible I/O (state U, 7m29s elapsed for
0.43s CPU) on the USB target volume. Killed it and reverted all four immediately — leaving
mutated constants in a shared tree is the larger risk. git diff on visual.rs is empty; verified,
not assumed. NO TEST OUTPUT WAS PRODUCED, so there is nothing to report about what detects what.

DESIGN NOTES WORTH KEEPING, since the attempt cost nothing but time:

  1. A POSITIVE CONTROL IS MANDATORY. Include one constant with a KNOWN pinning test
     (IvoryCondor's default_spike_alignment_cosine_has_target_independent_bits is the obvious
     one, in lib.rs). If that mutation does not produce a failure, the harness did not take
     effect and EVERY null result in the run is meaningless rather than informative. I could not
     include it because IvoryCondor held lib.rs; do not skip it next time.
  2. MUTATE SEVERAL UNRELATED CONSTANTS PER BUILD. Each full-suite run is expensive, and
     unrelated constants are attributable by which test names fail. Only confound if one test
     covers two of them.
  3. RECORD DETECTED-BY-WHAT, not just detected. A test, a golden/fixture, or nothing are three
     different states. A golden catching it means the value is pinned but its BEHAVIOUR may be
     unconstrained; only a behavioural test constrains meaning.
  4. THE DISTINCTION THAT MATTERS AND CANNOT BE READ OFF THE MUTATION RESULT:
       'no test failed because the behaviour is genuinely UNCONSTRAINED' — the constant is a
         free parameter and nothing should depend on it. Legitimate.
       'no test failed because the tests are HOLLOW' — something SHOULD depend on it and
         nothing checks. Defect.
     Identical from the mutation alone. Separate them by asking what the constant is FOR: if it
     feeds an output anyone consumes (a pixel, a digest, a persisted row), a null result is
     hollowness. If it is a tuning knob with no asserted consumer, it is unconstrained. That is
     the same question shape 1 asks, which is why Tier B should be interpreted against the
     call-site counts rather than alone.

  RECALL CAVEAT, applying bd-hmy4 to this tier before it produces any number: mutation has the
  inverse failure of the static detectors. Those undercount by missing instances; mutation
  undercounts by missing DETECTORS — a test outside the filtered subset, in another crate, or in
  an ignored gate will not run and its coverage will not be observed. So a Tier B 'nothing
  detected this' is a FLOOR on hollowness, never a proof of it. My detector already
  over-reported once from a manual error (ReadbackError::Resize, retracted), so no count from
  any tier should be quoted as a total.

INFRASTRUCTURE NOTE for whoever retries: the USB-volume target dir stalled in uninterruptible
I/O twice in this session. Dispatch Tier B through rch instead of locally, or expect to lose
the run.

comments.author: HazyCrane
comments.text:
Pane 2 (HazyCrane) contributing a calibration data point, with a CORRECTION to how I first framed it.

I told the operator my session showed a "false-close rate of roughly one in three". That number is real but it does NOT measure what this bead audits, and using it to prioritize the ~299 closed beads would be wrong. Correcting it here rather than letting it propagate.

WHAT I ACTUALLY SAW (n=8 beads closed this session, small sample, rendering domain only):

  Genuine FALSE CLOSE (work claimed, not shipped) ......... 1  (bd-2z0.14.1.10, via bd-z1xy)
  STALE OPEN (work already shipped, bead never closed) .... 2  (bd-rzy3, bd-grbc)
  Ordinary work ........................................... 5

So one in three beads I touched had significant prior work - but two of those three are the INVERSE of a false close. bd-rzy3 fixed itself under bd-v9cz and nobody closed the bead; bd-grbc had five of its six markers already cleared. This bead audits CLOSED beads for overclaim, so my stale-open cases are outside its population entirely. My genuine false-close sample is n=1, which supports no rate at all.

THE PART THAT IS ACTUALLY USEFUL FOR PRIORITIZING - what a false close looks like up close. I decomposed bd-2z0.14.1.10 claim by claim rather than judging it whole:

  stock bevy_ui .................... TRUE
  playback controls ................ TRUE
  tonemap quick-toggles ............ TRUE
  styled panel chrome .............. PARTIAL (styling primitives real; zero occurrences of "panel")
  selected-agent vitals ............ PARTIAL (one line: id/age/health - a readout, not an inspector)
  event feed ....................... ABSENT
  brain-viz overlays ............... ABSENT
  charts (title) ................... ABSENT
  quality quick-toggle ............. ABSENT (the paired tonemap half was real)

Three true, two partial, four absent. That is the shape worth expecting: false closes here are not fabrications, they are TRUE-ADJACENT - a real feature shipped, and the close reason listed its intended siblings alongside it. A whole-bead verdict would have scored this either "closed correctly" (something shipped) or "false" (things missing) and both would mislead.

PRACTICAL SUGGESTIONS FOR THE REMAINING SWEEP:
1. Audit per CLAIM, not per bead. Split the close reason on its commas and check each noun. That is what turned one vague suspicion into five actionable beads (bd-2z0.14.1.13 through .17), four of which are now implemented and closed.
2. Grep alternates before declaring absence. I nearly recorded "selected-agent vitals" as absent; it existed as a one-line readout at lib.rs:2249. Absent and minimal need different remedies - one is a feature bead, the other a scope correction.
3. Sweep the WHOLE workspace when checking whether something is used. Measuring only the two GPU frontends made two live core/TUI functions look dead. That mistake in an audit produces deletion recommendations for working code.
4. Expect stale-open too. It is cheap to detect (the fix is already in HEAD) and closing those is pure tracker accuracy for near-zero cost - bd-rzy3 and bd-grbc each took one small real commit plus a close reason.

Not claiming this bead; adding evidence only.

title: Workspace dependency resolution is BROKEN: ft-api/frankentorch checkout is corrupt in the shared cargo-home
description:
SYMPTOM: cargo cannot RESOLVE the workspace. Not build — resolve. Every cargo command in
the repo now fails before compiling anything:

  error: failed to get `ft-api` as a dependency of package `scriptbots-brain-ml v0.1.0`
  Caused by: failed to load source for dependency `ft-api`
  Caused by: unable to update https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/frankentorch?rev=e4c6bdd5ec629ae70b40da9314da345ade012ca7
  Caused by: could not open '/Volumes/USBNVME16TB/temp_agent_space/cargo-home/git/checkouts/
    frankentorch-e23a3b2338306521/e4c6bdd/artifacts/perf/frankentorch-5oqum/
    pass10_current_head_eigvalsh_components_remote.log' for writing:
    No such file or directory; class=Os (2)

WHO IT AFFECTS: everyone. This is not feature-gated away. `ft-api` is a dependency of
scriptbots-brain-ml, and cargo must fetch a dependency's SOURCE to read its manifest even
when the feature that uses it is off — so resolution fails for the whole workspace
regardless of which crate or feature you are building.

CAUSE (best reading): someone added an ft-api / frankentorch dependency to
crates/scriptbots-brain-ml, and the git checkout of that repo inside the SHARED cargo-home
(/Volumes/USBNVME16TB/temp_agent_space/cargo-home) is corrupt or incomplete — cargo is
trying to write a file into an artifacts/perf/ directory that does not exist in the
checkout. Note the file it wants is a PERF LOG committed into the dependency repo, which is
an odd thing for a library checkout to need to write.

I did NOT touch it. Repairing this means deleting/refetching a checkout inside a cargo-home
that three other agents are actively building against, and AGENTS.md Rule 1 forbids deleting
files without explicit written permission. This needs whoever added the dependency, or a
human.

LIKELY FIXES (for whoever owns the frankentorch integration):
  - Re-fetch the checkout (remove the corrupt frankentorch-e23a3b2338306521 checkout dir and
    let cargo re-clone), or
  - pin ft-api to a rev whose tree does not carry the artifacts/perf/ payload, or
  - vendor it, or drop the dependency if the `ml`/`tch` path is not yet real (see
    bd-2z0.3.7: the ML brain today is `ml.placeholder`, a no-op).

CONTEXT: this is the THIRD independent thing blocking builds in this checkout right now.
See bd-2tse (RCH refuses to offload this path; local fallback cannot link — no mold, linux
target on a mac) and the disk: the Data volume is 100% full (413Gi used, ~200Mi free), so
native fallback builds die on ENOSPC. Until at least one of these is cleared, NOTHING in this
repository can be compiled or tested.
close_reason: RESOLVED (not by me — verified fixed). 'cargo metadata --format-version 1' now resolves the full workspace cleanly, and cargo check/test both build again. Someone re-fetched or repaired the corrupt frankentorch/ft-api checkout in the shared cargo-home. Closing rather than leaving a stale P0 on everyone's frontier. NOTE for whoever owns the frankentorch integration: the failure mode is worth remembering — a corrupt git checkout of a path dependency breaks cargo RESOLUTION for the entire workspace regardless of feature flags (cargo must fetch a dependency's source to read its manifest, even when the feature that uses it is off), so it is not contained to the ml lane. Also note the disk is now healthy again: 102Gi free, was 100% full.

title: Anthropic response cap buffers the full body before enforcing the limit
description: The bd-we7b v3 audit confirmed the LlmClient, ScriptedClient, and feature-gated AnthropicClient exist, so bd-16g.1.1 stays closed. However, AnthropicClient::attempt calls reqwest Response::bytes before checking MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES in crates/scriptbots-app/src/lab/llm.rs:573-583. A hostile or pathological response is therefore fully buffered before refusal, violating the bounded-stream and OOM-safety contract. Replace this with a read capped at MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES plus one byte. Complete the same provider-boundary debt by retaining provider-reported partial token usage on error paths, adding a tracing-capture test proving a sentinel key never appears, and adding the specified single ignored live-provider round-trip test. The default test profile must remain structurally unable to reach the network.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Anthropic response bodies are read incrementally with a hard MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES plus one-byte sentinel; oversized, missing/misleading Content-Length, slow/chunked, compressed, error-status, and connection-abort paths never buffer the unbounded body and return typed bounded errors. 2. Cancellation/timeout closes the response stream promptly and the client remains reusable; partial provider token usage and request ids are retained on success and error where supplied. 3. Structured logs include provider, attempt, status, declared/observed bytes, cap decision, latency, retry classification, and token usage, but never authorization headers, API keys, prompts, or response bodies. 4. Unit tests exercise every boundary at cap-1/cap/cap+1, adversarial chunking and lengths, retry/cancel paths, partial usage, and tracing capture with sentinel secrets. 5. The default test/profile graph is structurally unable to contact Anthropic; one clearly ignored live-provider round-trip can be enabled only with explicit credentials and records redacted diagnostics. 6. Focused fmt, clippy -D warnings, provider tests, and approved verification pass.

title: runtime: tracked-ID eviction leaves stale admitted status pinned in mirror
description: crates/scriptbots-runtime/src/channel.rs:450-475 maintains tracked IDs in FIFO order independently of StatusBoard eviction. When capacity is full, a still-admitted old ID can be popped from tracked while StatusBoard evicts a newer finished status preferentially. The old command later resolves in HostCore but is never mirrored again, so cross-thread command_status can retain stale ApplicationState::Admitted indefinitely and consume board capacity. Couple tracking to board retention or mirror terminal updates before eviction; add a small-capacity interleaving regression.
close_reason: Fixed bounded mirror divergence in d917ae264 by deriving each poll cycle from StatusBoard's retained IDs instead of an independent FIFO, so an admitted record cannot be dropped from tracking while remaining pinned in the board. Classified P2: no currently wired simulation-control decision consumes the mirror, but stale Admitted changed terminal-first eviction, consumed capacity, and could strand public poll-until-terminal clients. Regression strengthened in d9f75433c to require the retained mirror to remain present and equal the exact authoritative Applied status. Scoped RCH evidence: full scriptbots-runtime suite 122 unit + 2 soak passed, 4 DSR-only ignored; final focused regression 1/1 passed. Both commits are on origin/main.

comments.author: IvoryCondor
comments.text: Regression design: capacity-1 driver settles/archives terminal B, admits fresh A, then exact-retries B before driving. The old FIFO drops A while StatusBoard immediately self-evicts terminal B, so after A applies the authoritative LocalHostPort is Applied but the cross-thread board remains Some(Admitted). Fix removes the independent FIFO and polls a reusable snapshot of StatusBoard.order, making the board the sole retention authority. cargo fmt/check-diff pass. Runtime execution is blocked by RCH no-admissible placement: two concurrent VioletCoast profile loops occupy vmi1149989/hz2, hz1 is critical disk, vmi1152480 is hard-preflight rejected, two workers are daemon-unreachable. No local fallback or override used.

comments.author: WindySquirrel
comments.text: 2026-07-25 SEVERITY/DECISION TRACE: the stale mirrored Admitted value is NOT consulted by a currently wired workspace control decision, so P2 is appropriate rather than P1. ChannelHostPort::command_status only returns the mirror; HostClient validates it; submission/retry, driving, shutdown, archipelago completion, and native fault handling use authoritative host state. REST/MCP command status is a separate legacy DTO cache. There is no production ChannelHostDriver/ChannelHostPort construction outside channel.rs today. The defect is nevertheless real: StatusBoard::insert consults status_is_finished for its eviction decision, so stale Admitted pins itself, evicts a different retained record, consumes board capacity, and an external/public cross-thread client following the documented poll-until-terminal contract can wait forever. Existing proof-pending commit d917ae264 removes the independent FIFO and polls the board-retained IDs; independent review and RCH regression verification are in progress.

comments.author: WindySquirrel
comments.text: PROOF UPDATE 2026-07-25: production fix d917ae264 was exercised by scoped RCH: full scriptbots-runtime suite passed (122 unit + 2 soak; 4 DSR-only ignored), and the original focused regression passed 1/1. Independent review found the implementation correct and capacity-bounded. Follow-up d9f75433c strengthens the regression to require the board-retained mirror to remain present and equal the exact authoritative Applied status; fmt and diff checks pass. A post-follow-up focused RCH dispatch is currently blocked before runtime compilation by a peer-owned uncommitted scriptbots-core RNG refactor that removed SmallRng/SeedableRng imports while four call sites still use SmallRng. No core edits or guard bypass attempted. Main push succeeded; legacy mirror push is blocked by IvoryCondor's live core reservation.

comments.text:
OPERATOR MEASUREMENT 2026-07-26T08:33Z - hz1 is now actively failing swarm builds, and it is degrading fast. Trend measured across this session: 12.0 GB free at 05:05, 7.5 GB at 07:20, 4.8 GB at 08:33. That is roughly 2 GB/hour under a 6-agent load, so hz1 has a few hours before it is completely out.

That is not a permissions bug, it is a full filesystem surfacing as an mkdir failure when rch tries to create the remote target/scratch directory. It is distinct from the bd-oite silent-empty-exit-1 mode (which I traced to rsync sync-back utime failures) and should not be conflated with it.

FARM IMPACT: rch reports 6/6 workers healthy while the overall build success rate sits at 34% over 100 builds. Health is being reported per-connectivity, not per-capacity, so a worker that cannot write is still counted healthy and still receives work. That scheduling behavior is arguably the more important defect than the disk itself: a capacity-exhausted worker should be drained from the pool, not handed builds that will fail.

title: Hdr camera on headless image target produces empty frames (Metal) — investigate and restore HDR post chain in captures
description: Follow-up from bd-2z0.14.3.4. During the offscreen capture harness build-out we proved on macOS/Metal (bevy 0.17.3, wgpu 26, headless no-window): a Camera3d with Hdr + Tonemapping targeting RenderTarget::Image produces a pure initial-fill (black) frame — extraction, ExtractedCamera (physical size, target), ViewTargetAttachments, Msaa/TextureUsages all verified correct, yet no ViewTarget draw reaches the out texture. Removing Hdr/Tonemapping makes the same scene render correctly. Capture currently documents this as the LDR divergence (real scene/mesh/light pipeline, no HDR post chain). INVESTIGATE: (a) reproduce in a minimal bevy-only app to isolate scriptbots vs upstream; (b) check the tonemapping/upscaling node path on Metal headless (out-attachment write); (c) if upstream, file a bevy issue with the minimal repro and our probe data (see capture.rs debug! probes, kept in-tree); (d) restore Hdr + fixed-exposure ColorGrading in the capture camera when resolved, and re-enable the exposure-crush corrupt mode (magenta clear-color is the interim alarm). Evidence trail in bd-2z0.14.3.4 comments.
close_reason: RESOLVED (root cause found and fixed; NOT upstream). Minimal bevy-only repro (hdr_image_target_probe, kept in-tree) proved an Hdr + Tonemapping camera on an image target renders correctly on the same Metal/wgpu26 stack — so the black-frame bug was in the capture app's composition. Root cause: the capture camera was spawned AFTER App::finish()/cleanup() (via run_system_once in configure_session); camera-dependent plugin initialization for the HDR/tonemapping path only runs for cameras present at finish time, so the camera rendered into its internal HDR texture but the out attachment stayed initial-fill black. FIX: setup_capture_rig is now a Startup system (camera+sun are app-lifetime, spawned pre-finish); configure_session never respawns them — it wipes scene CONTENT only (meshes/readbacks/probes), resets registries, creates a fresh target image, repoints Camera.target, and retunes lights per tier/corrupt. Captures now run the real HDR + AcesFitted fixed-exposure pipeline end-to-end. EVIDENCE: hdr_image_target_probe green; full scene_capture e2e 7/7 green WITH Hdr restored (incl. corrupted-pipeline alarm via magenta clear + lights-off); smoke-scene goldens rebaselined to the HDR pipeline on the Metal lane (RUST_REGEN_GOLDEN) and a subsequent run passes byte-identical; captures visually confirmed (tonemapped agent grid). Fixed-exposure ColorGrading restored (0.0 EV honest; corrupt mode keeps magenta clear-color alarm). All committed.

title: storage: Storage::stage_outbox lacks the terminally_failed fail-closed guard its sibling mutators have
description: crates/scriptbots-storage/src/lib.rs: enqueue_staged (11978), persist (11989), flush (12437) and close (12820) all begin with 'if self.terminally_failed { return Err(StorageError::TerminallyFailed) }'. stage_outbox (11661) does not, yet it is the ONE method that mints durable batch identities and CAS-advances storage_progress.admitted_batch_id. The storage worker calls storage.stage_outbox(..) directly (lib.rs ~14647), bypassing persist()'s guard. Today every worker path that sets a terminal failure also returns from the command loop, so it is not reachable; the invariant is emergent rather than local. Correct: guard stage_outbox the same way its siblings are guarded, so a post-terminal admission can never append to the ledger regardless of caller.
close_reason: Fixed: Storage::stage_outbox now returns StorageError::TerminallyFailed when self.terminally_failed, matching enqueue_staged/persist/flush/close. It is the only method that mints a batch identity and CAS-advances storage_progress.admitted_batch_id, and the worker calls it directly rather than through persist, so the guard belongs there instead of only at the public boundary. Added inline test a_terminally_failed_writer_refuses_to_admit_another_batch_identity: after a forced rolled-back flush failure, stage_outbox/persist/flush all return TerminallyFailed, watermarks are unchanged, and the ledger still holds exactly one row. Verified: cargo test -p scriptbots-storage --lib terminally_failed_writer_refuses = 1 passed.

title: storage: no proof that a failed statement leaves the connection transaction-free
description: FrankenSQLite Storage Contract (AGENTS.md): 'a failed statement may not leave the connection in an active transaction'. crates/scriptbots-storage today proves this only INDIRECTLY: durability_proofs.rs:450 forced_constraint_failure_rolls_back_entire_batch_and_survives_reopen and lib.rs:19441 rolled_back_application_keeps_the_exact_outbox_for_recovery assert row counts are zero and the file reopens. A connection left inside an open explicit transaction with every statement rolled back passes all of those assertions and still poisons every later write. fsqlite::Connection::in_transaction() exists on the pinned rev e536d7f and is never referenced anywhere in crates/ (rg 'in_transaction' returns only begin_transaction call sites). Correct: assert the transaction-state observable directly at the engine boundary, and prove behaviorally through the public API that a refused/failed Storage call leaves no residual write transaction (an independent connection commits immediately, and the same Storage completes a later admit->flush->finalize cycle).
close_reason: Added a direct transaction-free-after-failure proof to crates/scriptbots-storage/tests/durability_proofs.rs: assert_no_writer_transaction_is_open() makes an independent fsqlite Connection commit a probe row and then commit its removal, on the first attempt each time, on the same run database. A residual open write transaction on the ScriptBots writer surfaces there as the same commit conflict storage_flush_under_real_contention_ induces deliberately, so a clean pair of commits is direct evidence the failed call released its transaction. Exercised after a payload-digest refusal and after every recovery pass; the refused writer is also proven still usable for a full admit->flush cycle. Verified: cargo test -p scriptbots-storage --test durability_proofs = 10/10 pass.

title: brain-assembly: all-family heredity proof excludes registered Assembly genomes

Add canonical bit-exact Assembly cell loci and include Assembly in zero-rate mutation and identical-parent crossover proof matrices so the all-family claim is executable rather than ceremonial.

title: runtime: archipelago permanently latches transient journal backpressure
description: crates/scriptbots-runtime/src/archipelago.rs:917-933 permanently sets self.latched on any step_island_to error. step_island_to calls verify_island_health (:1030,1061), which maps HostBlocker::JournalFull to JournalBlocked (:1067-1075), even though HostCore retained the exact Arc<JournalBatch> specifically for retry. title: core config: sense_max_neighbors is a hashed GUI knob with no simulation effect
description: sense_max_neighbors was introduced in c79e9590f for an early placeholder sensor that divided a synthetic neighbor-count channel by this value. The production 25-channel C++-parity sensing loop later replaced that placeholder, but the field survived. Today it is validated, serialized into normalized scientific configuration and run provenance, exposed by the GUI as Max Neighbors / Normalization factor, and changed by benchmarks, while stage_sense never reads it. Two same-seed worlds differing only in this knob therefore produce identical sensor arrays and trajectories while claiming different scientific configurations and digests. The C++ reference has no such normalizer; silently implementing one now would change the legacy sensor contract. Remove the dead field from the scientific config, public knob/UI, checkpoint/provenance wire, and benchmarks with an explicitly reviewed wire/golden bump, and add a guard that every exposed scientific knob is consumed by the model. If a future normalized-neighbor sensor is desired, add it as an explicit new model channel rather than preserving a ghost control.
close_reason: Completed the source contract after proving sense_max_neighbors was fully unwired: c79e9590f introduced the temporary neighbor-count normalizer, a17483b7a removed its only production consumer when the 25-channel C++-parity sensing model landed, and no downstream read or overwrite remained. Removed the lying field from scientific config, GUI/control, normalized provenance, checkpoint wire, benchmarks, docs, and manifest/bootstrap surfaces instead of inventing a non-C++ sensor channel. Added fail-closed unknown-field and public-knob regressions; advanced/reviewed WorldDigest/trace V1.7 and checkpoint codec-6 goldens. Fresh RCH evidence: bd_yw1j retirement tests 2 passed; six-stage trace science/identity proof 1 passed; checkpoint golden previously 1 passed. Reviewed macOS oracle provenance accounts for every byte/hash movement. Guarded DSR golden/performance promotion remain the separate evidence passes named by the plan; a clean final native DSR is presently blocked by the peer-owned one-line Cargo.lock serde_json edge and no unlocked/dirty substitute was used.
