title: TogglePlayback does not change playback mode when driven through the production HUD, even with a recorded timeline
description:
Found while state-proving HUD shortcuts for bd-jw6f. Recording it as a finding with the exact
evidence rather than shipping a red test or a guess, because I could not fully separate
product defect from harness artifact and I am not willing to claim either.

WHAT WAS MEASURED, through the real production GPUI session (gpui::TestApp, both windows
installed via GuiSession::install, a forced production repaint, then window.dispatch_keystroke
into the HUD - the same harness the existing gpui_s_shortcut_* test uses):

  timeline frames recorded            1        (non-empty, so toggle_play's guard is satisfied)
  bindings.action_for("space")        Some(TogglePlayback)   (the binding resolves correctly)
  playback.mode() before 'space'      Live
  playback.mode() after  'space'      Live     <-- expected Playing

toggle_play() at lib.rs:12794 reads:
    PlaybackMode::Live => { if !self.timeline.is_empty() { self.mode = Playing; self.pointer = 0; } }
so Live + 1 frame should become Playing.

I ELIMINATED THE OBVIOUS CONFOUND. The first hypothesis was that GPUI does not deliver the
space keystroke - plausible, since a focused button often eats space. So I rebound
TogglePlayback to 'shift-p' via bindings.assign and dispatched THAT instead. Mode still stayed
Live. So the space key is NOT the problem; the action path is.

AND DISPATCH ITSELF WORKS IN THIS HARNESS. In the same fixture, nine other shortcuts driven
identically DO flip the state they name, and each toggles back on a second press:
'd' draw_agents, 'f' draw_food, 'ctrl-shift-o' agent_outline, 'shift-f' debug.enabled,
'1'/'2'/'3' the three hud panels, ',' settings_panel.open, 'n' narration_enabled. Those all
route through the same handle_key_down -> bindings.action_for -> invoke_action path. So
handle_key_down is reached and invoke_action dispatches; what differs about TogglePlayback is
that it delegates to self.playback.toggle_play() rather than writing a view field directly.

WHAT I DID NOT DETERMINE: whether the SimulationView entity that receives the keystroke is the
same one whose playback field I read back, or whether a production repaint between press and
read resets mode to Live. Either would make this a harness artifact. Equally, a playback
toggle that genuinely does nothing in production would make it a user-facing defect - and note
this control is exactly one of the six bd-jw6f classified as "driven but not state-proven",
i.e. it appears only in keybinding-registry checks, which pass for a control that does nothing.
Nobody has ever confirmed the space bar works.

NEXT STEP for whoever picks this up: instrument handle_key_down to record the last keystroke
and last action it actually invoked, then re-run the fixture. That distinguishes the three
remaining cases in one build. The fixture is committed and reusable - ShortcutFixture in
command_characterization_tests, with install()/install_with_agents()/press()/read()/
submitted()/selected_agents().

Filed by YellowLake. bd-jw6f stays open; 12 controls were proven in the same pass.
close_reason: WITHDRAWN - my harness, not the product. Root cause: PlaybackTimeline::snapshot_for_render, in Playing mode, checks 'pointer + 1 < timeline.len()' and on failure concludes playback ran off the end and returns mode to Live. With a ONE-frame timeline that is true immediately, so toggle_play correctly sets Playing and the very next render correctly returns it to Live - a one-frame timeline finishes the instant it starts. My fixture recorded exactly one frame, observed Live after pressing space, and read a working control as dead. The rebind-to-shift-p experiment did not distinguish this because the reset happens on render, not on dispatch, so it reproduced identically. Fix is ShortcutFixture::record_frames(n), which STEPS the world between repaints - PlaybackTimeline::record drops any snapshot whose tick matches the newest it holds, so repainting a frozen world records one frame no matter how often it is called. With 4 frames: space -> Playing, space -> Paused, g -> Live, all passing in playback_shortcuts_move_the_playback_mode (commit b1e7b7ac8). TogglePlayback and GoLive are now state-proven; no product defect exists.

title: runtime: NativeRunner into_parts drops commands still queued in receiver
description: crates/scriptbots-runtime/src/native.rs:863-868 NativeRunner::into_parts(self) returns only the existing unresolved vector and then drops the NativeMessage receiver. Any Command envelopes successfully queued by NativeHandle but not yet observed are silently destroyed by Receiver::drop, contradicting the API promise that returned parts retain every unreconciled envelope. Drain queued commands into unresolved in FIFO order (handling control messages explicitly); regression: submit then immediately into_parts and require the exact envelope in returned unresolved state.
close_reason: NativeRunner::into_parts now seals ingress and drains buffered command envelopes in FIFO order into caller-owned unresolved work; born-red native feature test proved the prior loss and passes after the fix.

comments.author: WildDuck
comments.text: bd-we7b V8 verdict B at af8cb1e. NativeRunner::into_parts seals ingress, drains queued command envelopes in receiver FIFO, explicitly consumes Wake/JournalReady, and the regression proves exact unresolved work plus closed post-extraction ingress. Keep closed.

title: core: replay_event_tick_cap leaks into world_digest_v1's scientific config — a recorded run's digest can never match the production run it verifies
description:
crates/scriptbots-core/src/lib.rs ~22264-22278 (world_digest_v1, scientific_config normalization).

FOUND BY a digest-neutrality test added under bd-vden, which failed with
  left:  0900b4d99f2cea61   (replay_event_tick_cap = 0)
  right: ef05c32ce60ab0dc   (replay_event_tick_cap = 64)
for two worlds identical in seed, config and tick count.

WHAT IS WRONG
The normalization block exists precisely to neutralize knobs that do not change the
next core transition, and it lists: initial_food, rng_seed, chart_flush_interval,
history_capacity, narrative_interval, narrative_capacity, persistence_interval,
analytics_stride, neuroflow, control, render.

replay_event_tick_cap is NOT in that list, so it flows into the digested config.

The codebase already classifies it correctly elsewhere — crates/scriptbots-core/src/
checkpoint.rs:2912 describes it verbatim as 'replay_event_tick_cap (a persistence-
recording knob, default 0)'. It simply was not added to the digest normalization
when it joined the serialized config tree under bd-2z0.8.9.8.

WHY IT MATTERS (this is the sharp edge)
The replay stream's WorldDigest anchor exists so a recorded run can be compared
against a production run. Production runs have replay_event_tick_cap = 0; a
recorded run has it nonzero by definition. Their digests therefore CANNOT match
even when the science is bit-identical. Replay verification against a production
baseline is structurally impossible, and the failure presents as 'science
diverged' — the most misleading possible error, because it will be believed.

It also contradicts the module contract in crates/scriptbots-core/src/replay.rs:6-8:
'Emission is a read-only projection ... it never mutates science state, so identical
configurations produce identical streams and the world digest is unaffected.'
That claim was simply untrue and untested until now.

FIX (applied)
    scientific_config.replay_event_tick_cap = 0;
placed beside persistence_interval, which is the same class of knob.

WIRE IMPACT: none for production. The default is 0, so zeroing it is a no-op for
every run that does not opt into recording; no existing golden or pinned digest
changes. The checkpoint's pinned V1.3/codec-5 byte-identity test is untouched —
that serializes the full config, not this normalized copy.

Compounds bd-a9h1: the stream was both truncated AND anchored to an incomparable
digest.
close_reason: Fixed in 84decacf8. scientific_config.replay_event_tick_cap = 0 added beside persistence_interval, so enabling replay recording no longer changes world_digest_v1. Found by the digest-neutrality test added under bd-vden, which failed 0900b4d99f2cea61 vs ef05c32ce60ab0dc and now passes. No production wire impact: default is 0.

title: stage_combat: sustained combat does not terminate, and the 0.5 spike floor has been hiding it (DropCombatPosting unreachable)
description:
TWO DEFECTS, AND THE FIRST IS WHY NOBODY EVER SAW THE SECOND. Split out of bd-16g.11.2, where both
were found; the revert rationale lives in a299e3c71a8e but must not live only there.

=== HALF ONE: Combat is unreachable by construction in the economy mutation suite ===

stage_combat hard-gates attack eligibility on the PHYSICAL spike extension (crates/scriptbots-core/
src/lib.rs ~20828):

    if spike_lengths[idx] <= 0.5 { result.energy = energy_before; return result; }

Agents start at spike_length 0 (AgentData::default()), and stage_actuation only walks spike_length
toward the brain-commanded target at config.spike_growth_rate, whose default is 0.005/tick
(lib.rs ~11743, applied at ~18686-18691). Over the mutation suite's 64-tick window the maximum
attainable length is therefore ~0.32 -- BELOW THE FLOOR. Every agent returns early from stage_combat
on every tick, no matter what any brain commands.

Consequence for the economy gate: Combat is posted as a DERIVED delta --
    observed_stage!(WorldStepStage::Combat, {
        let before = self.capture_resource_amounts();
        self.stage_combat();
        self.record_resource_change(ResourceFlowKind::Combat, before);
    });
(lib.rs ~23121). If combat moves nothing, the posted flow is zero. LedgerFault::DropCombatPosting
works by SUPPRESSING that posting, so it suppresses a zero and the conservation gate cannot go red.

That is why every_injectable_fault_turns_the_gate_red has been failing with
"fault DropCombatPosting was not detected within 64 ticks" -- it is not a flaky test and not a gate
bug. The fault is unreachable.

WORSE, AND THE REASON THIS IS FILED AS A BUG RATHER THAN A TEST CHORE: economy.rs's KIND_TO_FAULTS
maps Combat -> DropCombatPosting, and the fault_coverage completeness test PASSES. So the suite has
reported full category coverage for its entire life while the Combat category has never once been
exercised. The completeness test proves a fault is MAPPED to every category, not that the fault is
REACHABLE, and a mapping-only check cannot tell a covered category from an unexercisable one. The
conservation gate has never been observed to catch a combat leak.

A SECOND, INDEPENDENT TRAP for whoever fixes this: you cannot stage the commanded spike by writing
runtime.outputs[SpikeTarget] between ticks. stage_brains (lib.rs ~23075) runs BEFORE Combat (~23121)
and writes back unconditionally for every agent, bound or not --
    runtime.brain.restore_execution(job.execution);
    runtime.outputs = job.outputs;
with job.outputs = Self::default_outputs(&job.sensors) for unbound agents (lib.rs 18017-18022, i.e.
a copy of the first OUTPUT_SIZE sensors). Any value staged into outputs is gone before combat reads
it. The commanded spike must come from a BOUND BRAIN. The existing test-only LedgerAggressorBrain
(lib.rs ~42181) commands SpikeTarget = 1.0 every tick and is already used by
resource_ledger_attributes_ecology_combat_and_interventions to earn its asserted non-zero Combat
attribution. Note also that the equivalent flag trick fails for the same class of reason:
stage_reset_events clears runtime.spiked before stage_combat runs.

=== HALF TWO: with combat actually reachable, the world step does not terminate ===

WHAT I OBSERVED. I seeded spike_lengths[attacker] = 5.0 (clears the floor and holds -- the same
0.005/tick walk needs ~900 ticks to decay back), bound LedgerAggressorBrain to the attacker, set
herbivore_tendency = 0.0 (carnivore), and dropped config.spike_min_length and
config.spike_alignment_cosine to 0.0. Landed as dfaca98aa448, run remotely on hz1 (confirmed genuinely
remote: "Executing command remotely" present, zero "running locally" matches, which matters because
rch fails open per bd-e6ff):

    test tests::every_injectable_fault_turns_the_gate_red ...        <- printed, never completed
    Remote command finished: exit=137 in 1800469ms
    RCH_EXIT=137

SIGKILL by rch's 1800s external timeout. The worker was healthy and had just compiled the crate and
started the test; other agents' tests completed normally on the same fleet in that window. The
process was alive and not finishing. Reverted in a299e3c71a8e (comment-only against 608b3fad2, so
prior behavior is exactly restored) because AGENTS.md names
`cargo test -p scriptbots-core --features economy-faults` as THE command for this crate, and a
30-minute hang for every agent is strictly worse than a fast red.

CAUSALITY IS INFERRED, NOT PROVEN. Recording both directions honestly:
  FOR: the test completed historically, on record failing fast with the "not detected" message; the
    worker was healthy and mid-test; the only change was making combat reachable.
  AGAINST/UNKNOWN: no controlled A/B was run. An earlier variant (which ALSO seeded spike_length) was
    killed manually at 20m24s on hz2, so it was never observed to terminate either -- consistent with
    the hang being tied to the spike seed common to both variants, but equally consistent with a
    pre-existing suite-level problem.
  WHY NOT PROVEN: under bd-e6ff rch fails open to a local build and a local rustc on this host wedges
    unkillably. My one control attempt did exactly that and leaked four permanent U-state processes
    (count went 11 -> 16). Each further attempt costs the host another. I stopped rather than buy it.

CANDIDATE MECHANISMS, none confirmed, ordered by my suspicion:
  1. Mass simultaneous death feeding carcass distribution -- carcass_distribution_radius with
     carcass_neighbor_exponent over a growing population.
  2. The death/respawn interaction: population_minimum 8 with population_spawn_interval 5 against
     combat killing faster than the floor refills, in a world that also has reproduction_cooldown 1,
     reproduction_attempt_interval 1 and reproduction_attempt_chance 1.0.
  3. The fixture's spike_alignment_cosine = 0.0 making every agent in the attacker's forward
     hemisphere a hit target every tick (spike_radius defaults to 40.0, so reach ~45 covers a 120x120
     world entirely) -- i.e. the hang may need only unusually WIDE combat, not sustained combat.
Mechanism 3 is cheap to discriminate from 1 and 2: rerun with a realistic alignment threshold.

=== HOW TO WORK THIS ===

Do NOT start by re-adding a DropCombatPosting fixture arm; a warning comment now sits at the fixture
site saying so. Reproduce half two in isolation first: a minimal world, one carnivore with
spike_length above 0.5 and a bound aggressor brain, one victim, NO ledger and NO faults, a bounded
tick budget, and a wall-clock assertion. That separates simulation non-termination from anything
economy-related and gives a test that fails in seconds instead of hanging for thirty minutes.

Only once the world survives sustained combat should the mutation-suite arm return; at that point the
reachability recipe above is already solved and can be applied directly.

BLOCKED ON bd-e6ff for verification. This needs compilation to investigate, and there is currently no
safe lane: rch fails open to a local build and local rustc wedges unkillably on this host.

comments.author: QuietBeaver
comments.text:
QuietBeaver: MECHANISM FOUND, by code reading alone -- no compile, so this cost the host nothing.
I am now fairly confident the non-termination is a POSITIVE-FEEDBACK POPULATION EXPLOSION with an
O(N^2) cost term, not an infinite loop. Every ingredient is a default or a value already in the
fixture.

THE DECISIVE FACT, and it explains why this never surfaced before. distribute_carcass_rewards
(lib.rs 21163) begins each victim iteration with:

    let Some(victim_runtime) = self.runtime.get(*agent_id) else { continue };
    if !victim_runtime.spiked { continue; }        // lib.rs 21201

Carcass rewards are gated on the victim having been SPIKED, i.e. killed by combat. Combat is
unreachable in this suite (the 0.5 spike-length floor, per this bead's first half), so
THE ENTIRE CARCASS REWARD PATHWAY HAS BEEN DEAD CODE in the economy mutation suite for its whole
life. Making combat reachable does not merely add combat -- it switches on a large dormant subsystem
that had never once executed here. That is why one fixture change flipped a fast-failing test into a
30-minute non-termination.

THE FEEDBACK LOOP, all defaults unless noted:
  carcass_distribution_radius = 100.0   (lib.rs 11790) in a 120x120 world -> EVERY agent is a
                                        "neighbor" of EVERY carcass; this is not a local effect
  carcass_health_reward       = 5.0     (11791)
  carcass_reproduction_reward = 5.0     (11792)
  carcass_neighbor_exponent   = 1.25    (11793)
  carcass_maturity_age        = 5       (11794)
  no population cap exists anywhere -- `max_agents` (lib.rs 1894/1899, default 4) is CaptureBudget
    for snapshots, NOT a population limit. I checked for population_maximum / population_cap /
    agent_limit / population_limit: none exist.
and from mutation_suite_world (lib.rs ~42439):
  reproduction_energy_threshold = 0.8, reproduction_cooldown = 1,
  reproduction_attempt_interval = 1, reproduction_attempt_chance = 1.0, population_minimum = 8

The rewards land on reproduction directly -- health_add, energy_add and reproduction_bonus are
accumulated per neighbor and then applied, with reproduction_bonus feeding the reproduction counter.
So: one combat death -> +5.0 health and +5.0 reproduction bonus to EVERY agent in a world-sized
radius -> with threshold 0.8, cooldown 1, interval 1 and chance 1.0 they all reproduce on the next
tick -> population multiplies -> more bodies inside the attacker's reach (spike_radius 40 + length 5
= 45, again world-sized) -> more deaths -> more rewards. Deaths ACCELERATE reproduction instead of
damping it. There is no cap and no negative feedback term.

THE COST TERM THAT TURNS GROWTH INTO A HANG. distribute_carcass_rewards does NOT use the spatial
index. It takes a full snapshot of handles/positions/ages/healths (21175-21182) and then, for EVERY
dead agent, scans EVERY live agent (21197 onward). That is O(dead x agents) per tick. With deaths
scaling with population, cost is ~O(N^2) per tick against a population that is itself multiplying,
across 64 ticks -- and the mutation suite pays it for 17 faults. Superlinear growth times quadratic
per-tick work is more than sufficient to blow a 1800s budget without any infinite loop.

WHY MY FIXTURE MAXIMIZED IT, worth stating so the next attempt does not repeat it: I set
spike_alignment_cosine = 0.0, which makes the whole forward hemisphere hittable, so the attacker
killed broadly rather than singly. Combined with a world-sized carcass radius, essentially every
death fed every agent. A realistic alignment threshold would slow this down -- but it would not
remove the feedback loop, only its constant factor.

WHAT I HAVE NOT PROVEN. I have not executed any of this; under bd-e6ff there is still no safe lane
and I will not buy proof in wedged processes. Specifically unverified: (a) that population growth is
in fact unbounded rather than food-limited -- carcass rewards recycle energy from the dead into the
living, which is what defeats the usual food-limiting argument, but I have not traced the energy
accounting end to end; (b) the exact growth rate; (c) that no other stage clamps population.

CHEAPEST DISCRIMINATING EXPERIMENT, when a lane exists -- in this order, each is seconds not minutes:
  1. Run the reachable-combat scenario with carcass_distribution_radius = 0.0 (the function early-
     returns at 21171). If it terminates, the carcass pathway is confirmed as the driver.
  2. If it still hangs, set carcass_reproduction_reward = 0.0 but keep health_reward: separates
     "reproduction amplification" from "carcass work is simply expensive".
  3. Instrument agent count per tick. A monotone climb settles it immediately and is the single most
     informative number here.
  4. Only then attack the real fix.

LIKELY REAL FIXES, not for me to choose unilaterally since they are scientific knobs:
  - A population ceiling with a documented eviction rule. Its absence is arguably the root defect:
    any positive-feedback ecology can run away, and nothing currently stops it.
  - Route carcass neighbor lookup through the existing spatial index instead of a full scan. That
    removes the O(N^2) term regardless of the ecology question, and is a clean standalone
    improvement.
  - Revisit carcass_distribution_radius = 100.0 against typical world sizes; a "radius" that spans
    the entire world is not a radius, and it makes the reward global rather than local. This one
    smells like the actual bug rather than a tuning preference.

NOTE FOR bd-16g.11.2: if the fix changes carcass rewards, the economy gate's CarcassReward category
and MislabelCarcassAsTransfer fault are both downstream of it.

comments.author: QuietBeaver
comments.text:
QuietBeaver: CORRECTING MY OWN PREVIOUS COMMENT. I kept reading after posting it and found two damping
terms I had not accounted for. The "positive-feedback population explosion" mechanism I proposed is
substantially WRONG and nobody should chase it. Correcting now rather than leaving a plausible-but-
false lead in a bug report someone will act on.

WHAT I MISSED. The carcass reward is NORMALIZED BY NEIGHBOR COUNT, and it is CARNIVORE-ONLY
(lib.rs ~21283-21300):

    let norm = carcass_neighbor_normalizer(neighbor_indices.len(), exponent);   // count^1.25
    ...
    let carnivore_factor = (1.0 - herb) * (1.0 - herb);
    if carnivore_factor <= f32::EPSILON { continue; }
    let share = health_base * carnivore_factor * age_multiplier / norm;
    let bonus = reproduction_base * carnivore_factor * age_multiplier / norm;

with carcass_neighbor_normalizer(count, exponent) = count^exponent, exponent = max(1.25, ...)
(lib.rs 1251-1257).

So per death, each of N neighbors receives base/N^1.25, and the TOTAL distributed is
N * base/N^1.25 = base / N^0.25 -- which DECREASES as the population grows. That is negative
feedback, not positive. My claim that "deaths accelerate reproduction instead of damping it" and that
"there is no negative feedback term" is simply false: the normalizer IS the damping term, and it was
sitting fourteen lines above the code I quoted.

Second damper: carnivore_factor = (1 - herbivore_tendency)^2 gates the reward to carnivores, with a
hard `continue` for anything at/below epsilon. In mutation_suite_world the agents are
AgentData::default() and my fixture made exactly ONE of them a carnivore. So the reward was reaching
essentially one agent, not "every agent in a world-sized radius" as I wrote.

WHAT STILL STANDS, all directly checked:
  1. THE `!spiked` GATE IS REAL AND IS STILL THE HEADLINE (lib.rs 21201). distribute_carcass_rewards
     early-returns for any victim not killed by spiking, so the entire carcass pathway is dead code
     while combat is unreachable. Turning combat on executes a subsystem that had never run in this
     suite. That remains the strongest link between "made combat reachable" and "suite stopped
     terminating", independent of my broken explosion story.
  2. IT IS AN O(dead x agents) FULL SCAN THAT BYPASSES THE SPATIAL INDEX. It snapshots
     handles/positions/ages/healths (21175-21182) and rescans every live agent for every dead one.
     With carcass_distribution_radius = 100.0 in a 120x120 world, no candidate is ever filtered out
     by distance, so the scan is always the full population. This is a genuine and separable defect:
     the index exists and this path ignores it.
  3. There is no population cap anywhere; `max_agents` is CaptureBudget, not a limit. Still a fact,
     just no longer load-bearing for my (withdrawn) explosion argument.

CONFIDENCE NOW, stated honestly: I have a strong candidate for WHY the hang is newly reachable (1),
and a real cost defect (2), but I NO LONGER HAVE A CREDIBLE MECHANISM FOR 30 MINUTES OF NON-
TERMINATION. A quadratic scan over a modest population across 64 ticks x 17 faults should not take
that long. So either the population does grow substantially for some reason I have not found, or the
hang is somewhere else entirely and the carcass pathway is a red herring. I am not going to invent a
third story to fill the gap.

REVISED FIRST EXPERIMENT, and it is now diagnostic rather than confirmatory: INSTRUMENT THE AGENT
COUNT PER TICK before touching anything else. That single number decides between "population grows"
and "population is stable and the hang is elsewhere", and it costs one run. My earlier ordering put
the carcass ablation first; that was built on the mechanism I have just withdrawn. If the count is
flat, drop carcass entirely as a suspect and bisect the step stages instead.

Everything in this bead's original description -- the 0.5 spike floor, the unreachability, the
stage_brains/outputs trap, and the observed SIGKILL at 1800469ms -- is unaffected by this correction.
Those were measured or read directly. Only my proposed explanation for the hang was wrong.

title: Reconcile the 2026-07-11 executable baseline into an immutable per-lane evidence manifest
